items.title: NativeHTMLKit
items.text: Native desktop windows from HTML and CSS, driven by a shell script, Python or PowerShell. No browser engine, no JavaScript, no local web server: a small Rust host renders your page and sends your program the user's events over a private local connection.

items.title: Choose what you build with
items.text:
• UI library

    The quickest way to an app: reactive state and ready-made components (layouts, buttons, inputs, lists, themes). Write a few lines of Python or PowerShell, not HTML.

    Python · PowerShell

  • SDK

    Full control: your own HTML and CSS, events, page updates, native dialogs, clipboard, live bitmaps. The UI library is built on it.

    Python · PowerShell

  • Command line (CLI)

    One executable for shell scripts: pick rows, view text or fill in a form in a native window and get the answer on stdout. Every command and option with examples.

    Linux · Windows · Reference

The UI library and the SDK work the same on Linux and Windows (the few differences are on Linux and Windows); each has a Python and a PowerShell section with the same shape: getting started, step-by-step tutorials, task guides, complete examples with screenshots and source, and the full API reference. Python and PowerShell mirror each other one to one. The CLI has separate Linux and Windows sections because shell scripts differ per system.

Start here: Try the demo · Install and first steps · Choose an entry point · Platform requirements · Linux and Windows

More on the window, and how to check an installation: Try the demo.

items.title: A complete app in a few lines
Packages
items.text:
Entry point Package For CLI nativehtmlkit / nhk 0.1.2 Select rows, view text or fill a form from any shell Python SDK nativehtmlkit 0.1.2 (uv add nativehtmlkit) Windows, documents, events, dialogs, clipboard and live bitmaps Python UI nativehtmlkit_ui 0.1.1 (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui) Reactive state and compact components on the Python SDK PowerShell SDK NativeHTMLKit 0.1.2 The same features as cmdlets, plus background tasks PowerShell UI NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1 Reactive components on the PowerShell SDK Demo nativehtmlkit-demo / NativeHTMLKit.Demo 0.1.1 Browse and run every example (Try the demo)

All of them bundle the native host, Core 1.0.3 (wire protocol v1, stable). Target desktops are KDE Plasma on Wayland (Linux) and Windows; see the capability matrix and limitations. Every example on this site is run against the released packages before it is published.

items.title: What it is not
items.text: NativeHTMLKit is not a web browser, not a web UI framework and not a plugin platform. It runs no JavaScript, loads nothing from the network, and implements a documented HTML and CSS profile rather than the whole web platform. See Why native? and Concepts.

items.title: Limitations and qualifications
items.text: This page lists what the released packages (Core 1.0.3, CLI 0.1.2, Python SDK 0.1.2, PowerShell SDK 0.1.2, UI 0.1.1) do not do, or do only with qualifications. For per-feature availability see the matrix. A feature appearing in source code is not automatic proof of support on every OS/runtime combination.

items.title: Platforms and runtimes
items.text:
• Targets: Linux with KDE Plasma on Wayland, and Windows x64. macOS is not a target of the current releases.
  • Python SDK on Linux: the released x64 wheel uses a manylinux_2_39_x86_64 tag. Systems with glibc older than 2.39 do not meet that wheel's compatibility floor; the source package has no native host.
  • PowerShell: Windows PowerShell 5.1 is Windows only. Linux uses PowerShell 7.2+.

items.title: UI library
items.text:
• Version: NativeHTMLKit UI 0.1.1 is an early (pre-1.0) release with a deliberately small component set. Its 0.1.1 packages passed the real-input GUI suite at 100% scaling against Python SDK 0.1.2 / PowerShell SDK 0.1.2 / Core 1.0.3 on KDE Plasma Wayland (Python, PowerShell 7) and Windows Server 2022 (Python, PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell 5.1). IME, 125/150% scaling and screen-reader checks were last run against UI 0.1.0 with SDK 0.1.0 / Core 1.0.2.
  • Fixed tree: components are declared before mounting; afterwards only bound state changes the page. Lists are text-only (text_list / Add-NHKUiTextList).
  • Reactive state: Python Computed can race when multiple threads mutate its dependencies concurrently. Avoid such concurrent patterns until fixed; update related state from one thread.
  • Lifecycle: repeatedly creating and disposing UI windows can accumulate shutdown callbacks; limit repeated create/dispose loops until fixed.
  • No modal wrapper: HTML dialogs, native file dialogs, extra windows, clipboard and live bitmaps are SDK calls made next to the UI library.

items.title: Accessibility
items.text:
• Core 1.0.3 has a reported Linux Orca collapsed-select announcement issue (NHK-CROSS-0010).
  • UI-specific screen-reader coverage remains incomplete. See accessibility basics.

items.title: Headless test mode
items.text:
With NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 (SDKs) or NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1 (CLI) the host runs the protocol without a window. In that mode:

  • there is no synthetic user input — only document operations you call (for example request_submit, which fires submit, or replace_control_range, which fires input) produce events; set_value, set_checked and set_selected_values fire none;
  • the clipboard and native file/folder dialogs are unavailable and fail with RPC error -32001;
  • opening external targets and revealing files are unavailable;
  • desktop preferences report no observed values.

Headless runs prove startup, rendering, DOM state, readiness and clean shutdown — not real input, focus, IME or screen-reader behaviour.

items.title: Not included
items.text: JavaScript and browser APIs, network resource loading, an HTTP server, a general-purpose plugin framework, a UI modal wrapper, web-style routing, video/audio playback, and full Chrome-level HTML/CSS support.

items.title: Command-line tool
items.text:
nativehtmlkit gives shell scripts a native window: pick rows from a list, view text, or fill in a form, and get the answer on stdout with a meaningful exit status. One executable, no runtime to install.

  • Linux

    bash/zsh on KDE Plasma Wayland: install, every command and option with examples, recipes, scripting with exit codes, a tutorial.

  • Windows

    PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 (cmd.exe notes): the same commands and recipes with Windows examples.

The reference is the exact, system-independent specification of every command, format, limit and exit code.

items.title: CLI architecture
items.text:
How nativehtmlkit 0.1.2 turns a pipe into a native window and back into an exit status. This page explains; the exact contract is in the reference.

The CLI is a standalone Rust program. It does not draw anything itself: it supervises one Core host session per command over Core's local, authenticated wire protocol v1 (stable since Core 1.0.3). It depends only on that public protocol, not on Core's source. Command parsing, input framing, the generated page, output encoding and exit statuses are owned by this repository; rendering and GUI events are owned by Core. The SDKs neither use nor ship the CLI.

items.title: Process model
items.text:
One command runs three processes:

flowchart LR
  STDIN[stdin records] --> L["launcher<br/>nativehtmlkit select ..."]
  L -- "spawns: nativehtmlkit-host run --app <session>/app.toml" --> H["Core host<br/>nativehtmlkit-host"]
  H -- "spawns (manifest): nativehtmlkit __backend <session>" --> B["backend<br/>same executable"]
  B <-- "wire v1: Unix socket / named pipe,<br/>launch token" --> H
  H --> W[native window]
  B -. "files in the private session directory" .-> L
  L --> OUT[stdout result + exit status]
  1. Launcher (the process you start). It parses the arguments, reads and validates all input, builds the page, and refuses anything the host would refuse (sizes, node count, title, missing nhk-form) before any other process exists. It then writes a private session directory and starts the host with run --app <dir>/app.toml; the host's stdin and stdout are closed, its stderr is shared with yours.
  2. Core host. It reads the generated manifest, which names the CLI executable itself as the application backend (__backend <dir>, a hidden command), with instance = "multiple" and max_windows = 1, so concurrent commands get independent sessions. It starts the backend with the wire-v1 launch variables (UI4ME_ENDPOINT, UI4ME_TOKEN, ...).
  3. Backend. It removes the launch variables from its environment first, reads and deletes session.json, connects to the host's endpoint (Unix stream socket on Linux, named pipe on Windows) and authenticates with the launch token. Then: host.hello -> host.diagnostics (to learn the real host process id) -> window.create (900 x 610) -> document.load (the generated page) -> app.ready. From then on it waits for document.event notifications: clicks on nhk-cancel, nhk-submit or nhk-done.

On Submit the backend asks the document for its state with document.command: get_form_data (the ticked selection inputs, or the form's successful controls) and, for forms, check_validity; it shows problems in #nhk-error with set_text and keeps the window open. An accepted result is committed atomically to result.json, then the backend asks the host to quit (app.request_quit), answers the host's app.before_quit with allow, and ends at app.shutdown.

The launcher meanwhile only watches files and the host process. When the host has exited successfully it reads the committed outcome, encodes stdout itself (the selected indices are mapped back to the original rows, so the result is byte-exact input data), writes it in one piece and exits. No result committed means Cancel (exit 2), or for view simply closed (exit 0).

items.title: The session directory
items.text:
Created per command in the temporary directory as nativehtmlkit-cli-*, mode 0700 on Unix, and removed when the launcher exits (also on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP; only a SIGKILLed launcher leaves it behind, by then without the piped data):

File Written by Holds app.toml launcher the host manifest ({app_dir} resolves to this directory) session.json launcher mode, title, parsed rows, CSS/HTML, timeouts; deleted by the backend right after reading ready backend the host's process id, once the window is ready heartbeat backend a progress counter, bumped (at most every 200 ms) while frames arrive from the host result.json backend the outcome: selected indices, form entries, viewed, or timed out error.json backend a classified, payload-free failure done backend the session ended normally diag.ndjson backend the backend's diagnostic records, relayed to stderr by the launcher (max 1 MiB)

items.title: Security model: escaped data, trusted markup
items.text:
There are exactly two kinds of content in a window:

Content Source Treatment Records from stdin, --title untrusted every character & < > " ' is HTML-escaped; it can only ever be text in a cell, a <pre> or the heading. A line <img src=x onerror=...> is displayed literally and returned byte-exact. --css file, --html fragment trusted, written by the script author inserted verbatim into the page; a fragment can contain any markup

Consequences for script authors:

  • Never build --html/--css from untrusted data without escaping it (jq -rn --arg s "$v" '$s|@html', [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode). Putting data in through stdin rows is always safe.
  • Core runs no JavaScript, so markup cannot execute code; the remaining risk of unescaped data is a misleading or broken form.
  • The result never contains HTML from the page: select returns your original rows, form returns Core's form-data entries.

Other protections:

  • Wire-v1 credentials (UI4ME_*) exist only in the backend's environment and are removed before it does anything else; the token is never logged.
  • Diagnostics are privacy-safe by construction: records accept only fixed event names, identifier-shaped strings, numbers and booleans, so stdin data, selections, form values, titles, paths and the token cannot be recorded. Error lines never quote host-authored text, which could contain form values.
  • Fail closed: once any failure is recorded, nothing is written to stdout, even if a result had been committed before.
  • No network: the CLI talks only to its own host over a local endpoint.

items.title: Lifecycle and watchdogs
items.text:
A person may take as long as they like; a hung host must not block a pipeline. These are different controls:

Control Who enforces it Default On expiry --timeout (the person) backend, from window ready none window closed, result.json = timed out, exit 124 --rpc-timeout (one request) backend 30 s rpc.timeout (remote outcome unknown), exit 1 liveness probe (host.diagnostics after --liveness-interval idle) backend every 5 s, answer within 2 x 30 s host.unresponsive, exit 1 --startup-timeout launcher (+5 s margin), also the host's own backend start-up limit 15 s host.startup_timeout, exit 1 backend progress (heartbeat) launcher stale after interval + 3 x rpc timeout + 5 s backend.unresponsive, exit 1 host exit after the session ended launcher 5 s host shutdown allowance + 5 s host.shutdown_timeout, exit 1 quit acknowledged but no app.shutdown backend rpc timeout + 5 s host.shutdown_timeout, exit 1 a failure the backend recorded launcher up to 2 s for the host to end by itself the recorded failure, exit 1

Any frame from the host counts as progress, and all waits charge only time actually spent waiting, so a suspended machine is not mistaken for a hang. When the launcher has to stop the host it kills the process it started and, on Linux, also the real host process (Core runs it in a systemd user unit), after checking through /proc/<pid>/exe that the id still belongs to that host executable.

sequenceDiagram
  participant L as launcher
  participant H as Core host
  participant B as backend
  L->>H: run --app session/app.toml
  H->>B: start __backend session (launch token)
  B->>H: host.hello, host.diagnostics, window.create, document.load, app.ready
  B-->>L: ready (host pid)
  loop while the window is open
    H-->>B: document.event (clicks)
    B->>H: host.diagnostics after each idle interval (liveness)
    B-->>L: heartbeat
  end
  B->>H: document.command get_form_data / check_validity
  B-->>L: result.json
  B->>H: app.request_quit
  H->>B: app.before_quit -> allow
  H-->>B: app.shutdown
  B-->>L: done
  H-->>L: process exit 0
  L->>L: encode stdout, exit 0

items.title: Lifetime binding
items.text:
The host must not outlive the launcher, or an orphaned window would hold your data with nobody to receive the result:

  • Linux: the host is started with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG = SIGKILL; if the launcher dies for any reason, the host is killed, and Core's own supervision ends the window and backend.
  • Windows: the host is assigned to a kill-on-close Job Object whose only handle the launcher owns; the kernel ends the host tree when the launcher exits.

Signals: SIGINT (Ctrl+C) gives the host up to 3 s to end by itself (a terminal Ctrl+C reaches the whole process group), SIGTERM and SIGHUP stop it at once; the exits are 130, 143, 129, never with a result.

Known limits of this design (see the release notes): a hung host is noticed late on purpose (about 65 s with the defaults) because ending a busy but healthy session would discard the user's input; with --liveness-interval 0 a hang is only noticed at the next request; if the host process is stopped as a whole (SIGSTOP) and the CLI is killed at the same time, the window and its unit remain.

items.title: NativeHTMLKit CLI on Linux
items.text:
nativehtmlkit (alias nhk) puts a native window into a shell pipeline: pipe records in, let a person pick, view or fill in something, and read the result from stdout. This section documents CLI 0.1.2 (bundled with Core host 1.0.3) for bash on Linux x86-64. For Windows and PowerShell see the Windows section.

git branch --format='%(refname:short)' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Switch branch'

items.title: Install
items.text:
Download the Linux archive and the checksum file from the v0.1.2 release (in the browser, or with the GitHub CLI as below) and check the archive:

gh release download v0.1.2 -R nativehtmlkit/nativehtmlkit-cli -p '*linux-x64*' -p SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS

nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-linux-x64.tar.gz: OK

Without gh: curl -fLO https://github.com/nativehtmlkit/nativehtmlkit-cli/releases/download/v0.1.2/nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-linux-x64.tar.gz and the same for SHA256SUMS.

Extract it and check the files inside against the archive's own SHA256SUMS:

tar -xzf nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-linux-x64.tar.gz
cd nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-linux-x64
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
./nhk doctor

The directory contains:

File What it is nativehtmlkit the CLI nhk a symbolic link to nativehtmlkit (the short alias) nativehtmlkit-host Core host 1.0.3, the program that draws the window; keep it beside the CLI manifest.json, SHA256SUMS versions, source commits, protocol version and hashes examples/sample-form.html the smallest form for nativehtmlkit form LICENSE, licenses/ licences of the CLI, Core and third-party components

items.title: Put it on PATH
items.text:
Move the directory somewhere permanent and link the executables into a directory on your PATH. Leave nativehtmlkit-host where it is: the CLI resolves its own symbolic link and finds the host beside the real file.

sudo mv nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-linux-x64 /opt/nativehtmlkit-cli
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
ln -s /opt/nativehtmlkit-cli/nativehtmlkit ~/.local/bin/nativehtmlkit
ln -s /opt/nativehtmlkit-cli/nativehtmlkit ~/.local/bin/nhk

Check it (open a new terminal if ~/.local/bin was not on PATH yet):

nativehtmlkit doctor

NativeHTMLKit CLI 0.1.2
Core host: /opt/nativehtmlkit-cli/nativehtmlkit-host
nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3

Needs a graphical session (Wayland or X11). The CLI writes no configuration files; to uninstall, delete the directory and the links.

items.title: First command
items.text:
printf 'alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n' | nativehtmlkit select --multi

A window lists the three lines with a checkbox each. Tick some and click Submit selection: they are printed, one per line, and the exit status is 0. Click Cancel: nothing is printed and the status is 2.

alpha
gamma

items.title: The four commands
items.text:
Command Reads stdin stdout on success Page select records the chosen rows select view records nothing (read-only) view form no one JSON line with the form values form doctor no which host is used, and its version doctor, help, version

Global options (--timeout, --host, --diagnostics, --rpc-timeout, --liveness-interval, --startup-timeout) work with every command, before or after its name. Each command page shows each of them with that command.

items.title: How the examples are verified
items.text:
The examples on these pages run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository:

git clone https://github.com/nativehtmlkit/nativehtmlkit-cli.git
cd nativehtmlkit-cli/examples

Every bash block that calls the CLI is run by scripts/test-docs.py against the released Linux archive (CLI 0.1.2, Core host 1.0.3) with its real host, in headless mode (no window and nobody to click). That proves the input and options are accepted, the page renders, and the documented exit status and output follow; since nobody clicks, each window ends by its deadline. Three kinds of results are shown:

  • stdout / stderr blocks: the text the example printed in that run.
  • "Submit prints" blocks: what the CLI writes when the user ticks the named rows. They are checked by running the release's own parsing, selection and output code on the exact stdin and options the example gave the CLI.
  • Replayed results: a recorded Submit result, in the exact output format, handed to the script after the real CLI call was accepted, to show what the script does with it.

What a person sees and clicks (layout, keyboard, Cancel, closing the window) is covered by the release's GUI qualification on KDE Plasma (Wayland) and Windows.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/index.md · edit the page there.

items.title: CSS and forms (Linux)
items.text:
Two options insert your own trusted content into the page the CLI generates: --css FILE (every window command) adds a style sheet, and --html FILE (form) is the form itself. This page shows how to write both, and how to generate them from data safely. The generated page, its element ids and the built-in style sheet are documented in page structure.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how). How the windows look is checked by the release's GUI qualification, not here.

items.title: Trusted means: written by you
items.text:
• --css and --html are inserted verbatim. Write them yourself; never paste data into them without escaping it (below).
  • Core runs no JavaScript: <script> does nothing. Keep the files self-contained: no remote fonts, images or @import URLs.
  • Each file is UTF-8 and at most 256 KiB.
  • Do not hide the footer or reuse the CLI's ids (nhk-form, nhk-error, nhk-cancel, nhk-submit, nhk-done, nhk-selection-form, nhk-row-N): the CLI's buttons are the only way to submit.

Data piped into select and view, and the --title, are always escaped by the CLI: they can never become markup.

items.title: --css: themes
items.text:
The built-in style sheet takes its colours from custom properties on :root (--background, --panel, --border, --text, --accent); your file comes after it, so overriding them is enough for most themes. The repository's css/light.css:

:root {
  color-scheme: light;
  --background: #f6f7f9; --panel: #ffffff; --border: #c9d1dc; --text: #1d2430; --accent: #2f6fd0;
}
th { background: #e8edf4; }
tr:hover { background: #eef3fb; }
button.primary { background: #2f6fd0; border-color: #2f6fd0; color: #ffffff; }
.error { color: #b3261e; }

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --css css/light.css < data/servers.csv

The same file works for view and form:

nativehtmlkit view --css css/light.css < data/app.log

A small accent change, written on the fly:

cat > accent.css <<'CSS'
:root { --accent: #3fa37a; }
h1 { font-size: 18px; letter-spacing: .02em; }
button.primary { background: #2f8a63; border-color: #3fa37a; }
CSS
printf 'keep\nremove\n' | nativehtmlkit select --css accent.css --title 'Green'

Files over 256 KiB, unreadable files and non-UTF-8 files are refused before a window opens:

head -c 300000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' ' ' > huge.css
echo a | nativehtmlkit select --css huge.css

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: custom HTML or CSS file exceeds 256 KiB

items.title: --html: writing a form
items.text:
The fragment must contain <form id="nhk-form">. Put every control inside it and give each a name. Do not add a submit button; the CLI adds Cancel and Submit below your fragment. Core validates these constraints when the user clicks Submit and keeps an invalid form open with Some required fields are invalid:

Attribute / type Checked required text, select, checkbox, radio group minlength, maxlength text, textarea pattern the whole value must match type="number" with min, max, step number range type="email", type="url" format date/time types with min, max range

A deployment form using most of them (the repository's deploy-form.sh generates this):

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

cat > deploy.html <<'HTML'
<form id="nhk-form">
  <label>Service <select name="service" required>
    <option value="">Choose...</option><option value="api">api</option><option value="web">web</option>
  </select></label>
  <fieldset><legend>Environment</legend>
    <label><input type="radio" name="environment" value="staging" required checked> Staging</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="environment" value="production"> Production</label>
  </fieldset>
  <label>Version <input name="version" required value="v1.0.0"
         pattern="v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" title="a version such as v1.4.2"></label>
  <label>Replicas <input name="replicas" type="number" min="1" max="20" value="2" required></label>
  <label>Notify <input name="notify" type="email" placeholder="team@example.com"></label>
  <label>Change notes <textarea name="notes" maxlength="500" rows="3"></textarea></label>
  <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" name="dry_run" value="yes" checked> Dry run only</label>
</form>
HTML
nativehtmlkit form --html deploy.html --css css/form.css --title 'Deploy'

css/form.css lays it out as a grid of labelled fields using the page's colour variables:

#nhk-form { display: grid; gap: 12px; max-width: 520px; }
#nhk-form label { display: grid; gap: 4px; }
#nhk-form input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]), #nhk-form select, #nhk-form textarea {
  background: var(--panel); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 6px; padding: 7px 9px; font: inherit;
}

items.title: Reading the result
items.text:
Submit prints one line {"entries":[...]}: one entry per named control that has a value, in document order. All values are strings; an unticked checkbox has no entry; an empty text field is "". A jq helper reads one field:

result=$(nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html) || exit
field() { jq -r --arg n "$1" 'first(.entries[] | select(.name == $n) | .value) // ""' <<<"$result"; }
[[ $(field confirm) == yes ]] || { echo 'not confirmed' >&2; exit 1; }
echo "creating $(field project) for $(field environment)"

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"project","value":"Demo App"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"production"}]}

not confirmed

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"project","value":"Demo App"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"production"},{"kind":"text","name":"confirm","value":"yes"}]}

creating Demo App for production

Rules HTML cannot express (for example "production needs change notes") are checked by the script after Submit; see the deployment form recipe.

items.title: Generating a form from data
items.text:
Anything that comes from outside the script (file names, Git tags, user names, API data) must be HTML-escaped before it goes into the fragment, or a value such as <b> or " would change the markup. jq's @html escapes & < > " ':

esc() { jq -rn --arg s "$1" '$s | @html'; }
{
  echo '<form id="nhk-form"><p>These files will be deleted:</p><ul>'
  for f in 'a <b>.txt' 'notes & "more".log'; do echo "<li>$(esc "$f")</li>"; done
  echo '</ul><label><input type="checkbox" name="sure" value="yes" required> I understand</label></form>'
} > confirm.html
grep '<li>' confirm.html >&2
nativehtmlkit form --html confirm.html --title 'Confirm deletion' > /dev/null

<li>a <b>.txt</li>
<li>notes & "more".log</li>

Do not use bash ${var//</<}: in bash 5.2 an unquoted & in the replacement means "the matched text". Python's html.escape is a good alternative to jq.

Options for a select built from data need no escaping: pipe the data in and the CLI escapes it.

items.text:
form, deployment form recipe, page structure.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/css-and-forms.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Environment and diagnostics (Linux)
items.text:
This page shows the environment variables the CLI reads, how it finds the Core host, and how to get a timeline of a session with --diagnostics. Specifications: environment, diagnostics, host discovery.

The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
Variable Effect NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY the Core host to use when --host is not given (an empty value is ignored) NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS default for --diagnostics: off, normal, debug, trace; the host reads it too NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID correlation id put into every CLI and host record (1-128 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -) PATH the last place the CLI looks for nativehtmlkit-host TMPDIR where the private, per-session directory nativehtmlkit-cli-* is created and removed again

The CLI reads no configuration files.

items.title: Which host is used
items.text:
The first match wins: --host PATH, then NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY, then nativehtmlkit-host in the directory of the real CLI executable (symbolic links resolved), then each PATH directory. doctor shows the result:

host=$(nativehtmlkit doctor | sed -n 's/^Core host: //p')
NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY=$host nativehtmlkit doctor | tail -n 1

nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3

A variable that names no file is an error; --host wins over it:

echo a | NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY=/opt/missing/nativehtmlkit-host nativehtmlkit select

nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: /opt/missing/nativehtmlkit-host

host=$(nativehtmlkit doctor | sed -n 's/^Core host: //p')
echo a | NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY=/opt/missing/nativehtmlkit-host nativehtmlkit select --host "$host"

The CLI 0.1.2 is qualified with Core host 1.0.3, the one in its release archive; use the override for development builds only.

items.title: --diagnostics levels
items.text:
The CLI writes structured records, one JSON object per line, to stderr; stdout only ever carries the result. The Core host writes its own JSON log records to the same stderr ("target":"nativehtmlkit_host..."); the CLI's carry "component":"nativehtmlkit-cli".

Level CLI records off none normal (default) failures only debug the session's lifecycle with timings trace also every request, host event and liveness probe

Count the CLI's records per level for the same window:

printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select --diagnostics off 2> off.log
jq -cR 'fromjson? | select(.component == "nativehtmlkit-cli")' off.log | wc -l

0

printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select --diagnostics normal 2> normal.log
jq -cR 'fromjson? | select(.component == "nativehtmlkit-cli")' normal.log | wc -l

A deadline is not a failure, so normal writes nothing here either:

0

printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select --diagnostics debug 2> debug.log
jq -rR 'fromjson? | select(.component == "nativehtmlkit-cli") | .event' debug.log | sort -u | grep -c .
jq -rR 'fromjson? | select(.event == "session.completed") | .context | "\(.outcome) \(.exit_code)"' debug.log

11
deadline 124

printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select --diagnostics trace 2> trace.log
jq -rR 'fromjson? | select(.component == "nativehtmlkit-cli") | .event' trace.log | grep -m1 -x rpc.started

rpc.started

NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS sets the default; the flag wins:

export NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS=debug
printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select 2> env.log
jq -rR 'fromjson? | select(.component == "nativehtmlkit-cli") | .event' env.log | grep -m1 -x window.ready

window.ready

items.title: A timeline of one session
items.text:
Keep the result and the log apart, then read the CLI's records:

printf 'one\ntwo\nthree\n' > items.txt
nativehtmlkit --diagnostics debug select < items.txt > choice.txt 2> session.log
jq -cR 'fromjson? | select(.component == "nativehtmlkit-cli" and .event != "rpc.completed") | {role, event}' session.log

{"role":"launcher","event":"session.started"}
{"role":"launcher","event":"host.spawned"}
{"role":"backend","event":"backend.started"}
{"role":"backend","event":"handshake.completed"}
{"role":"backend","event":"window.ready"}
{"role":"backend","event":"deadline.expired"}
{"role":"backend","event":"host.request"}
{"role":"backend","event":"session.shutdown"}
{"role":"launcher","event":"host.exited"}
{"role":"launcher","event":"session.completed"}

With a Submit instead of a deadline you would see submit.accepted where deadline.expired is. rpc.completed records carry the protocol operation and duration_ms of each request. Records never contain your data, titles, paths or form values; the host's records are a separate log, so review those before sharing one.

items.title: Correlate with your own logs
items.text:
NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID puts your id into every CLI record (session_id) and every host record (diagnostic_session_id):

echo 'build ok' > build.log
NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID="nightly-42" nativehtmlkit --diagnostics debug view < build.log 2>> all.log || [[ $? -eq 124 ]]
jq -rR 'fromjson? | .session_id // .diagnostic_session_id' all.log | sort -u

nightly-42

An id with other characters is replaced by a generated one, and a session_id.replaced record says so:

echo 'x' | NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID='my id/1' nativehtmlkit view --diagnostics normal 2> replaced.log || true
jq -rR 'fromjson? | select(.component == "nativehtmlkit-cli") | .event' replaced.log

session_id.replaced

items.title: Temporary files
items.text:
Each session uses a private directory nativehtmlkit-cli-* under TMPDIR (or /tmp) and removes it when the command ends, whatever the outcome:

mkdir -p session-tmp
echo x | TMPDIR=$PWD/session-tmp nativehtmlkit view || true
ls -A session-tmp | wc -l

0

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/environment-and-diagnostics.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Exit codes and scripting (Linux)
items.text:
Every nativehtmlkit command reports what happened through its exit status, and only a successful Submit writes anything to stdout. This page shows how to use that in bash. The complete specification, including every error[<code>], is the exit status reference.

Status Meaning stdout Typical reaction 0 submitted (select, form), closed (view), done (doctor, --help, --version) the result use it 1 error: usage, input, host missing or failed; one nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: ... line on stderr empty fail 2 Cancel, or the window was closed without submitting empty stop quietly, change nothing 124 --timeout expired empty stop, maybe say so 130 SIGINT (Ctrl+C) empty stop 143 SIGTERM empty stop 129 SIGHUP (the terminal went away) empty stop

Usage errors exit 1 (not 2), so 2 always means the user said no.

The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how). Headless, nobody clicks, so windows end with 124; replayed results show the 0 and 2 paths.

items.title: Capture the status under set -e
items.text:
var=$(command) gives $? the command's status, but with set -e a 2 would end the script before you could look at it. Capture it explicitly:

set -euo pipefail
status=0
size=$(printf 'small\nmedium\nlarge\n' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Size' --timeout 60) || status=$?
case $status in
  0)   echo "size: $size" ;;
  2)   echo 'cancelled' >&2; exit 2 ;;
  124) echo 'no answer within 60 s' >&2; exit 124 ;;
  *)   exit "$status" ;;    # the CLI already explained the error on stderr
esac

no answer within 60 s

When the user clicks Cancel:



cancelled

When the user picks large:

large

size: large

Inside $( ... ) the status is the pipeline's: the last command's, or with pipefail the last non-zero one. Both are the CLI's when it is the last command.

items.title: A helper that ends the script on anything but Submit
items.text:
Its exit runs in the command substitution's subshell; set -e then ends the script with the same status, so a cancelled script exits 2 and a timed-out one 124:

set -euo pipefail
choose() {
  local status=0 out
  out=$(nativehtmlkit select "$@") || status=$?
  [[ $status -eq 0 ]] || { echo "${0##*/}: nothing chosen" >&2; exit "$status"; }
  printf '%s' "$out"
}
colour=$(printf 'red\ngreen\n' | choose --title 'Colour')
echo "colour: $colour"

After Cancel the script exits 2 without printing anything:

After picking green:

green

colour: green

items.title: The CLI in the middle of a pipeline: PIPESTATUS
items.text:
A pipeline's status is the last command's. Read the CLI's own status from PIPESTATUS right after the pipeline:

printf 'a.txt\nb.txt\n' | nativehtmlkit select --multi | xargs -r -d '\n' wc -l
status=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")        # printf, nativehtmlkit, xargs
case ${status[1]} in
  0)   ;;
  2)   echo 'cancelled' >&2 ;;
  124) echo 'timed out' >&2 ;;
  *)   echo 'selection failed' >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

timed out

After Cancel or a timeout the CLI writes nothing, so xargs -r runs nothing. Without -r, GNU xargs would run wc -l once with no file and read its own stdin.

items.title: Errors: status 1 and the error code
items.text:
Each failure writes exactly one line nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: <message> to stderr. stderr also carries the Core host's own log records, so match the line, never parse stderr for results:

status=0
printf 'a,b\n1,2,3\n' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv 2> err.log || status=$?
code=$(grep -o 'error\[[a-z_.]*\]' err.log | head -n 1)
echo "status $status, $code"

status 1, error[input.invalid]

A usage error from the argument parser has no code but also exits 1:

echo a | nativehtmlkit select --input-format xml

error: invalid value 'xml' for '--input-format <INPUT_FORMAT>'

items.title: Write files only after success
items.text:
nativehtmlkit select ... > out.csv creates (or empties) out.csv even when the user cancels. Write to a temporary file and move it into place on 0 only:

tmp=$(mktemp out.csv.XXXXXX)
if nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format csv < data/servers.csv > "$tmp"; then
  mv -- "$tmp" out.csv
else
  status=$?; rm -f -- "$tmp"; ls out.csv* 2>/dev/null; exit "$status"
fi

Nothing is left behind after Cancel or a timeout (the block ended with 124 and listed no file). csv-report.sh does the same with a trap.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: --timeout is for people, not for hangs
items.text:
Without --timeout a window waits as long as the person needs. Add it when an unattended window must not block a job forever:

printf 'deploy\nskip\n' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Nightly deploy?' --timeout 900

nativehtmlkit: no decision before the --timeout deadline; the window was closed

You do not need --timeout against a hung host: the CLI notices that itself (liveness probes) and exits 1 with error[host.unresponsive] (environment and diagnostics).

items.title: Signals: 130, 143, 129
items.text:
Ctrl+C in the terminal closes the window and exits 130; SIGTERM exits 143, SIGHUP 129. stdout stays empty, even if the user had just clicked Submit. timeout --preserve-status sends a signal after a delay and returns the command's own status, which shows all three:

printf 'a\nb\n' | timeout --preserve-status -s INT 3 nativehtmlkit select
echo "after SIGINT: $?"

after SIGINT: 130

printf 'a\nb\n' | timeout --preserve-status -s TERM 3 nativehtmlkit select
echo "after SIGTERM: $?"

after SIGTERM: 143

printf 'a\nb\n' | timeout --preserve-status -s HUP 3 nativehtmlkit select
echo "after SIGHUP: $?"

after SIGHUP: 129

A trap in your own script runs as usual; the CLI cleans up its window and host itself.

items.title: view and doctor
items.text:
view has no Cancel: closing it is 0, and 124 is "the deadline closed it". Treat both as done:

nativehtmlkit view --timeout 120 < data/app.log || [[ $? -eq 124 ]] || exit 1
echo 'carry on'

carry on

doctor exits 0 or 1 and suits a start-of-script check:

nativehtmlkit doctor > /dev/null || { echo 'NativeHTMLKit CLI is not installed correctly' >&2; exit 1; }
echo 'ready'

ready

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/exit-codes-and-scripting.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Input formats (Linux)
items.text:
select and view read all of stdin, then parse it as --input-format lines (default), csv, tsv, json or ndjson. This page shows each format with bash examples; the complete rules are in the input formats reference.

Common rules:

  • stdin must be piped or redirected (not a terminal), UTF-8, at most 8 MiB.
  • At most 2,000 rows and 32 columns.
  • Any problem exits 1 with nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: ... before a window opens. Messages give positions, never your data.
  • Every cell is shown as text: markup in the data is never interpreted.

The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how); "Submit prints" blocks are the exact output of the released code for the rows named.

items.title: lines (default)
items.text:
One row per line, one column named Value. A \r before the \n is removed, so Windows text files work; a last line without \n is still a row; empty lines are rows too.

printf 'first\r\n\nthird\nlast-without-newline' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format lines --multi

Four rows: first, an empty row, third, last-without-newline. Submit prints, after ticking rows 1 and 4:

first
last-without-newline

Lines are kept exactly, including leading spaces and markup:

printf '  indented\n<b>not bold</b>\nPříliš žluťoučký kůň 😀\n' | nativehtmlkit select --multi

  indented
<b>not bold</b>
Příliš žluťoučký kůň 😀

Empty stdin has no rows: select refuses it, view shows an empty viewer:

printf '' | nativehtmlkit select

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: no selectable input rows; stdin was empty or contained no records

Text that is not UTF-8 is refused; convert it first:

printf 'caf\xe9\n' | nativehtmlkit select

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: stdin must contain UTF-8; use ConvertTo-Json or UTF-8 output

printf 'caf\xe9\n' | iconv -f latin1 -t utf-8 | nativehtmlkit select

items.title: csv
items.text:
Comma-separated values with a header row, RFC 4180 quoting: inside "..." commas and line breaks are data and "" is one ". Blank lines are skipped. A UTF-8 byte-order mark before the header is ignored.

cat > notes.csv <<'CSV'
name,comment,n
plain,"has, comma",1

quote,"say ""hi""",2
multi,"line one
line two",3
CSV
nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --multi < notes.csv

Three rows (the blank line is skipped), columns name, comment, n. Submit prints, after ticking all three (CSV output is re-quoted where needed):

name,comment,n
plain,"has, comma",1
quote,"say ""hi""",2
multi,"line one
line two",3

Every record must have as many fields as the header, and header names must be unique:

printf 'host,role\nweb-01,frontend,extra\n' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: malformed CSV/TSV record: CSV error: record 1 (line: 2, byte: 10): found record with 3 fields, but the previous record has 2 fields

printf 'name,name\na,b\n' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: duplicate CSV/TSV column names cannot be represented as JSON objects

Only , is a delimiter: a;b is one column named a;b. Convert semicolon files first, for example with Python's csv module:

printf 'host;status\nweb-01;healthy\nweb-02;degraded\n' |
  uv run python -c 'import csv,sys; csv.writer(sys.stdout, lineterminator="\n").writerows(csv.reader(sys.stdin, delimiter=";"))' |
  nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv

A header without data rows: select refuses it, view shows an empty table:

printf 'host,status\n' | nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv

items.title: tsv
items.text:
Tab-separated values, otherwise like csv (same header and quoting rules):

printf 'branch	updated	subject
main	2 hours ago	Merge fix/typo
feature/login	3 days ago	Add login form
' |
  nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv

branch  updated subject
feature/login   3 days ago  Add login form

Pitfall: TSV uses CSV quoting, so a field that starts with " is read as a quoted field. A " inside a field is data, but at the start the quotes are removed, and a quote that is never closed swallows the following tabs and lines:

printf 'branch	subject
main	"quoted" start
' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv

branch  subject
main    quoted start

printf 'branch	subject
main	"unclosed quote
feature	second row
' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv

Two data lines, but only one row: the second line became part of the first row's subject. For free text such as commit subjects build JSON with jq instead (see pick a Git branch), or replace the quotes first:

printf 'branch	subject
main	"unclosed quote
feature	second row
' | tr '"' "'" |
  nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv

items.title: --no-headers
items.text:
For csv and tsv: the first record is data; columns are named column_1 ... column_N. (Accepted, without effect, for the other formats.)

printf 'web-01\thealthy\nweb-02\tdegraded\ndb-01\thealthy\n' |
  nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv --no-headers --multi --output-format json

[{"column_1":"web-01","column_2":"healthy"},{"column_1":"web-02","column_2":"degraded"}]

items.title: json
items.text:
Exactly one JSON document. An array gives one row per element; any other value is one row. If every row is an object, the columns are the union of their keys in order of first appearance; otherwise there is one column Value. Cells show strings as they are, null as empty, numbers and booleans as JSON text, nested arrays and objects as compact JSON.

echo '[{"id":1,"name":"web","tags":["a","b"]},{"id":2,"name":"db","owner":null}]' |
  nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

Columns id, name, tags, owner. The result is the original element, unchanged: key order, nesting and number text are kept.

[{"id":2,"name":"db","owner":null}]

A single object is one row; an array of strings is a one-column table:

echo '{"name":"api","replicas":3}' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

jq -c '[.[].title]' data/issues.json | jq -c '.[:3]' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --output-format lines

Document the <form> limits

Big numbers and trailing zeros survive the round trip:

echo '[{"id":12345678901234567890123,"price":2.50}]' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

[{"id":12345678901234567890123,"price":2.50}]

Only one document is accepted; a byte-order mark is refused:

echo '[1] [2]' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: invalid JSON input: trailing characters at line 1 column 5

printf '\xef\xbb\xbf[1]' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: invalid JSON input: expected value at line 1 column 1

jq output and REST responses are usually json. Pick the fields you want to see first:

jq -c 'map({"#": .number, Title: .title, Author: .user.login, url: .html_url})' data/issues.json |
  nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json

items.title: ndjson
items.text:
One JSON value per line (JSON Lines). Blank lines are skipped; a line holding an array is one row. Columns, cells and values follow the json rules.

nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson --multi < data/app.ndjson

{"time":"2026-11-16T09:01:12Z","level":"warn","msg":"slow query","duration_ms":812}
{"time":"2026-11-16T09:02:40Z","level":"error","msg":"upstream timeout","retry":1,"upstream":{"host":"api-01"}}

Tools that print one JSON object per line feed it directly:

docker ps --all --format '{{json .}}' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson

Pretty-printed JSON is not NDJSON; compact it with jq -c:

printf '{\n  "a": 1\n}\n' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: invalid NDJSON line 1: EOF while parsing an object at line 1 column 1

printf '{\n  "a": 1\n}\n' | jq -c . | nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson

items.title: Limits
items.text:
seq 1 2000 | nativehtmlkit select --multi

jq -nc '[range(33) | {key: "k\(.)", value: 1}] | from_entries' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: 33 columns exceeds the 32-column limit

Also refused: more than 8 MiB on stdin, and a page over 1 MiB or 65,536 elements (the message says how many rows would fit). See the limits reference.

items.title: Which format to use
items.text:
Your data Format names, paths, one item per line lines a spreadsheet export, --format csv of a tool csv jq output, a REST response json docker ps --format '{{json .}}', kubectl ... -o json \| jq -c '.items[]', JSON log files ndjson fields that may contain tabs, quotes or newlines json/ndjson built with jq (not tsv)

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/input-formats.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Output formats (Linux)
items.text:
After Submit selection, select writes the chosen rows to stdout in the format named by --output-format: same (default), lines, csv, tsv, json or ndjson. view never writes to stdout; form always writes one JSON line (form). The complete rules are in the output formats reference.

Common rules:

  • Rows are written in input order, whatever order they were ticked in.
  • The result is written in one piece after the window has closed, and only on exit 0. On Cancel (2), timeout (124), error (1) or a signal stdout stays empty, so out=$(nativehtmlkit select ...) never holds half a result.
  • UTF-8, \n line ends, a newline at the end.

Every "Submit prints" block below is the exact output of the released code for the stdin of the example above it and the rows named, checked by scripts/test-docs.py (how). The examples use the sample file data/servers.csv from the repository's examples directory:

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes
web-01,frontend,eu-west,4,8,healthy,
web-02,frontend,eu-west,4,8,degraded,"disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled"
api-01,backend,eu-west,8,32,healthy,
api-02,backend,us-east,8,32,healthy,"canary for ""v2"" API"
db-01,database,eu-west,16,128,healthy,primary
db-02,database,us-east,16,128,maintenance,"replica, patching until 18:00"
cache-01,cache,eu-west,2,16,healthy,

items.title: same (default)
items.text:
The format of the input: lines in, lines out; csv in, csv out; and so on.

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format same < data/servers.csv

Submit prints, after ticking api-02 and web-02:

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes
web-02,frontend,eu-west,4,8,degraded,"disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled"
api-02,backend,us-east,8,32,healthy,"canary for ""v2"" API"

items.title: lines
items.text:
One line per chosen row. A lines row is written as it was read; a row whose value is a JSON string is written as that string; any other row is written as its cells joined by a tab.

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format lines < data/servers.csv

web-01  frontend    eu-west 4   8   healthy 
db-01   database    eu-west 16  128 healthy primary

cut then takes a column; here the host names of the chosen rows go to xargs:

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format lines < data/servers.csv |
  cut -f1 | xargs -r -d '\n' printf 'checking %s\n'

web-01  frontend    eu-west 4   8   healthy 
db-01   database    eu-west 16  128 healthy primary

checking web-01
checking db-01

A lines result can never turn one row into two: if a chosen value contains a line break, nothing is written and the command fails with exit 1. Use json or ndjson for such data:

printf 'name,comment\nplain,ok\nmulti,"line one\nline two"\n' |
  nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --output-format lines

Submit after picking multi:

nativehtmlkit: error[output.failed]: selected value contains newline: use --output-format json or ndjson

JSON strings come back as plain lines:

echo '["red","green","blue"]' | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json --output-format lines

red
blue

items.title: csv
items.text:
The header line, then each chosen row's cells, quoted where needed:

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format csv < data/servers.csv

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes
db-02,database,us-east,16,128,maintenance,"replica, patching until 18:00"

From json or ndjson input the columns are the union of the keys; nested values are written as compact JSON and null as an empty field:

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format ndjson --output-format csv < data/app.ndjson

time,level,msg,port,duration_ms,retry,upstream
2026-11-16T09:00:01Z,info,server listening,8080,,,
2026-11-16T09:02:40Z,error,upstream timeout,,,1,"{""host"":""api-01""}"

Write the result to a file only after a successful Submit (see exit codes and scripting).

items.title: tsv
items.text:
Like csv with a tab as delimiter (and the same quoting):

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format tsv < data/servers.csv

host    role    region  cpu_cores   memory_gib  status  notes
web-02  frontend    eu-west 4   8   degraded    disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled
api-01  backend eu-west 8   32  healthy

items.title: json
items.text:
One JSON array with the chosen rows' values on one line. A lines row is a string, a csv/tsv row an object of strings keyed by the header, a json/ndjson row the original value unchanged (key order, nesting, null, booleans and number text are kept).

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json < data/servers.csv

[{"host":"api-01","role":"backend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"8","memory_gib":"32","status":"healthy","notes":""}]

printf 'a.txt\nb c.txt\nit'"'"'s.txt\n' | nativehtmlkit select --multi --output-format json

["b c.txt","it's.txt"]

jq reads it by field name:

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json < data/servers.csv |
  jq -r '.[] | "\(.host) has \(.memory_gib) GiB"'

[{"host":"api-01","role":"backend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"8","memory_gib":"32","status":"healthy","notes":""}]

api-01 has 32 GiB

items.title: ndjson
items.text:
The same values as json, one per line; convenient for while read loops:

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format ndjson < data/servers.csv

{"host":"web-01","role":"frontend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"4","memory_gib":"8","status":"healthy","notes":""}
{"host":"db-01","role":"database","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"16","memory_gib":"128","status":"healthy","notes":"primary"}

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format ndjson < data/servers.csv |
  while IFS= read -r row; do
    echo "would restart $(jq -r .role <<<"$row") on $(jq -r .host <<<"$row")"
  done

{"host":"web-01","role":"frontend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"4","memory_gib":"8","status":"healthy","notes":""}
{"host":"db-01","role":"database","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"16","memory_gib":"128","status":"healthy","notes":"primary"}

would restart frontend on web-01
would restart database on db-01

items.title: Nothing chosen (--allow-empty)
items.text:
With --allow-empty, Submit with nothing ticked is a valid answer (exit 0). lines and ndjson print nothing, json prints [], csv/tsv print the header line only:

nativehtmlkit select --multi --allow-empty --input-format csv --output-format csv < data/servers.csv

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes

nativehtmlkit select --multi --allow-empty --input-format csv --output-format ndjson < data/servers.csv

items.title: Which one to use
items.text:
You need Output format one value per line for xargs, while read lines (single-column input) fields by name in jq json or ndjson a spreadsheet file csv exactly the records you put in same values that may contain line breaks json or ndjson

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/output-formats.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Troubleshooting (Linux)
items.text:
On failure the CLI exits 1 and writes one line to stderr:

nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: <message> (<details>)

Find the line in the table, or reproduce the error with the example below it. Every code is listed in the exit status reference. The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

You see Cause Fix error[host.not_found]: NativeHTMLKit Core host not found... no nativehtmlkit-host beside the CLI or on PATH keep the extracted archive together; run nativehtmlkit doctor; or set NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: <path> --host or NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY points nowhere correct or unset it error[host.not_found]: cannot start the Core host (...) the file is not executable chmod +x, or extract the archive again with tar error[input.invalid]: stdin is a terminal; pipe records in... select/view without piped input pipe or redirect records in error[input.invalid]: no selectable input rows... the command before the CLI printed nothing check for empty input first error[input.invalid]: stdin must contain UTF-8... Latin-1 or UTF-16 text iconv -f latin1 -t utf-8 error[input.invalid]: invalid JSON input: ... not JSON, two documents, or a byte-order mark validate with jq .; strip the BOM error[input.invalid]: malformed CSV/TSV record: ... ragged rows, a TSV field starting with " fix the data, or build JSON error[input.invalid]: input is too large to display: ... over the 1 MiB page or 65,536-node limit the message says how many rows fit; filter first error[input.invalid]: ... exceeds the 2000-row ... / too many records more than 2,000 rows head -n 2000, or filter error[usage.invalid]: --title must be nonempty... empty, over 128 characters, or a tab/newline ${title:0:128} error[output.failed]: selected value contains newline... lines output of a value with a line break --output-format json or ndjson error[host.startup_timeout] no window within --startup-timeout (+5 s) slow first start on a busy machine: raise --startup-timeout error[host.unresponsive] the host stopped answering while the window was open it has been stopped; report it with a --diagnostics debug log error[host.failed]: ... the host process failed run with --diagnostics debug, read the host's records error: unexpected argument ... (no code) a typo in an option nativehtmlkit <command> --help

items.title: Check the installation
items.text:
nativehtmlkit doctor

If that fails with host.not_found, the host is not beside the CLI. A symbolic link to nativehtmlkit is fine (the CLI resolves it); a copy of the executable elsewhere is not:

cp "$(realpath -- "$(command -v nativehtmlkit)")" ./nativehtmlkit-copy
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ./nativehtmlkit-copy doctor

nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: NativeHTMLKit Core host not found. Install a qualified release beside the CLI or set NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY.

ln -s "$(realpath -- "$(command -v nativehtmlkit)")" ./nativehtmlkit-link
./nativehtmlkit-link doctor | tail -n 1

nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3

A host file without the execute bit:

cp "$(nativehtmlkit doctor | sed -n 's/^Core host: //p')" ./host-copy
chmod -x ./host-copy
nativehtmlkit doctor --host ./host-copy

nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: cannot start the Core host (permission denied)

items.title: Input problems
items.text:
Nothing was piped in. In a terminal select would wait for typing, so it refuses instead (here script provides a terminal):

script -qec 'nativehtmlkit select' /dev/null | tr -d '\r' | grep -o 'error\[input.invalid\]: stdin is a terminal'

error[input.invalid]: stdin is a terminal

An empty pipe (the previous command found nothing). Check before calling select:

matches=$(find . -name '*.nothing-here')
if [[ -z $matches ]]; then echo 'no files to choose from'; exit 0; fi
nativehtmlkit select <<<"$matches"

no files to choose from

Too large to display. The message says how many rows fit at this width:

jq -nc '[range(1871) | [range(16) | {key: "c\(.)", value: "v"}] | from_entries]' |
  nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --multi

at most 1870 rows fit

Long lines push a page over 1 MiB; shorten them by characters (not bytes):

for i in $(seq 2000); do printf '%0600d\n' "$i"; done | nativehtmlkit view

the host accepts 1048576 (1 MiB)

for i in $(seq 2000); do printf '%0600d\n' "$i"; done | perl -CSD -pe 's/^(.{400}).+/$1.../' | nativehtmlkit view

items.title: "Nothing happens when I click Submit"
items.text:
• select: something must be ticked, unless --allow-empty is given. The window says select at least one row before submitting.
  • form: a constraint failed; the window says Some required fields are invalid. Check required, pattern (it must match the whole value), min/max.
  • With --diagnostics debug the stderr log shows submit.rejected with the reason (empty_selection, invalid_form).

items.title: The script stops at the CLI
items.text: That is by design: the window waits for the person. Add --timeout for unattended runs (exit codes and scripting).

items.title: Get a log to report a problem
items.text:
printf 'a\nb\n' | NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID=report-1 nativehtmlkit --diagnostics trace select 2> report.log || true
jq -cR 'fromjson? | select(.component == "nativehtmlkit-cli") | {role, event, operation, error_code}' report.log | head -n 3

{"role":"launcher","event":"session.started","operation":null,"error_code":null}
{"role":"launcher","event":"host.spawned","operation":null,"error_code":null}
{"role":"backend","event":"backend.started","operation":null,"error_code":null}

The CLI's records contain no data from your input; the host's records (also in the file) are a separate log, review them before you share it. More in environment and diagnostics.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/troubleshooting.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Tutorial: a Git branch picker (Linux)
items.text:
You will write git-pick, a bash script that lists your local Git branches in a native window, switches to the one you pick, and can delete merged branches in a multi-select list. It shows how to use nativehtmlkit select safely in scripts: input formats, output, exit statuses and timeouts.

Time: about 20 minutes. You need: bash, Git, and nativehtmlkit on your PATH (install). Final code: examples/tutorial-branch-picker/git-pick.sh. The same tutorial for PowerShell: Windows.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The runs below were made in the examples directory of a clone of this repository (a Git work tree with the branches main, feature/login, fix/typo and release/1.4) against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py, headless and with replayed results (how).

items.title: Step 1: pick a branch
items.text:
step1-pick.sh:

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Branch picker tutorial, step 1: offer the local branches in a native list and report the choice.
#
# Teaches: piping lines into `nativehtmlkit select`, capturing stdout, and the exit statuses
#          0 (chosen), 2 (cancelled), 124 (--timeout expired) and anything else (error).
# Run:     bash step1-pick.sh [--timeout SECONDS]     (inside a Git work tree)
# Guide:   docs/linux/tutorial-branch-picker.md (step 1 of 2)
set -euo pipefail

status=0
choice=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ \
  | nativehtmlkit select --title "Pick a branch" "$@") || status=$?

case $status in
  0) echo "You chose: $choice" ;;
  2) echo "Cancelled" >&2 ;;
  124) echo "No choice made in time" >&2 ;;
  *) echo "nativehtmlkit select failed with exit status $status" >&2 ;;
esac
exit "$status"
  • git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ prints one branch per line, which is the default lines input format.
  • nativehtmlkit select opens the window and blocks. On success it prints the chosen line and exits 0.
  • choice=$(...) || status=$? keeps set -e from ending the script when the user cancels: the exit status is captured instead.
  • "$@" passes extra options through, for example --timeout 30.

Run it inside any Git work tree:

bash tutorial-branch-picker/step1-pick.sh --timeout 30

Nobody chose within the deadline:

No choice made in time

After picking release/1.4:

release/1.4

You chose: release/1.4

After Cancel:



Cancelled

items.title: Step 2: a table, switching, and deleting merged branches
items.text:
git-pick.sh:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# git-pick: choose a local Git branch in a native window and switch to it (CLI tutorial final code).
#
# Teaches: feeding TSV to `nativehtmlkit select`, reading the selection from stdout, handling every
#          exit status (0 chosen, 2 cancelled, 124 timed out, anything else an error), multi-select
#          with --multi, and keeping the shell script safe with `set -euo pipefail`.
# Run:     bash git-pick.sh [--timeout SECONDS]                 switch to the chosen branch
#          bash git-pick.sh --delete-merged [--timeout SECONDS] delete chosen branches already merged
#          bash git-pick.sh --print                             show the table that would be offered
#          (inside a Git work tree; needs `nativehtmlkit` on PATH)
# Guide:   docs/linux/tutorial-branch-picker.md
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  sed -n '2,11p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
}

die() { echo "git-pick: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

mode=switch
select_options=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --timeout)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--timeout needs a number of seconds"
      select_options+=(--timeout "$2"); shift 2 ;;
    --delete-merged) mode=delete; shift ;;
    --print) mode=print; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "git-pick: unknown option: $1 (try --help)" >&2; exit 64 ;;
  esac
done

command -v nativehtmlkit >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "nativehtmlkit is not on PATH (see the CLI install guide)"
git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "not inside a Git repository"
current=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD || echo "(detached HEAD)")

# One TSV row per branch, most recently committed first. The CLI treats a double quote as CSV/TSV
# quoting, so quotes in commit subjects are replaced by apostrophes.
branch_table() {
  printf 'branch\tupdated\tlast commit\n'
  git for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate \
    --format='%(refname:short)%09%(committerdate:relative)%09%(subject)' "$@" | tr '"' "'"
}

# Runs `nativehtmlkit select`, prints the chosen branch names (first column), returns its status.
pick() {
  local title=$1; shift
  local output status
  set +e
  output=$(nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv --output-format lines --title "$title" \
    "${select_options[@]}" "$@")
  status=$?
  set -e
  case $status in
    0) printf '%s\n' "$output" | cut -f1 ;;
    2) echo "git-pick: cancelled; nothing changed" >&2 ;;
    124) echo "git-pick: no choice made in time; nothing changed" >&2 ;;
    *) echo "git-pick: nativehtmlkit select failed with exit status $status" >&2 ;;
  esac
  return $status
}

case $mode in
  print)
    branch_table refs/heads/
    ;;
  switch)
    branch=$(branch_table refs/heads/ | pick "Switch branch (current: $current)") || exit $?
    [ -n "$branch" ] || die "no branch selected"
    if [ "$branch" = "$current" ]; then
      echo "Already on $branch"
    else
      git switch --quiet -- "$branch"
      echo "Switched to $branch"
    fi
    ;;
  delete)
    if [ -z "$(git for-each-ref --merged HEAD --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ | grep -vxF -- "$current" || true)" ]; then
      echo "No merged branches to delete"
      exit 0
    fi
    # Offer every merged branch except the one you are on (row 1 is the header).
    chosen=$(branch_table --merged HEAD refs/heads/ | awk -F'\t' -v current="$current" 'NR == 1 || $1 != current' \
      | pick "Delete merged branches" --multi) || exit $?
    while IFS= read -r branch; do
      if [ -n "$branch" ]; then
        git branch --quiet -d -- "$branch"
        echo "Deleted $branch"
      fi
    done <<< "$chosen"
    ;;
esac
  • branch_table prints TSV with a header row (branch, updated, last commit), and --input-format tsv shows it as a table with columns. TSV uses CSV quoting, so " in commit subjects is replaced (input formats).
  • --output-format lines prints each selected row as its cells joined by tabs, without the header; cut -f1 keeps the branch name.
  • pick turns every exit status into a clear message and returns it unchanged, and || exit $? makes the script exit with the same status: 2 when cancelled, 124 when --timeout expired.
  • --delete-merged offers only branches merged into HEAD (minus the current one) and passes --multi, so the user can tick several rows. Each is deleted with git branch -d, which refuses anything not merged.
  • --print shows the table without opening a window, useful when you change the format.

items.title: Try it
items.text:
The table that would be offered (no window):

bash tutorial-branch-picker/git-pick.sh --print | cut -f1

branch
main
fix/typo
feature/login
release/1.4

Switch branch, giving up after 20 seconds (exit 124):

bash tutorial-branch-picker/git-pick.sh --timeout 20

git-pick: no choice made in time; nothing changed

With feature/login picked, the CLI prints that row's cells joined by tabs and the script switches:

bash tutorial-branch-picker/git-pick.sh

feature/login   2 minutes ago   Add the example scripts

Switched to feature/login

Tidy up merged branches (--multi):

bash tutorial-branch-picker/git-pick.sh --delete-merged

fix/typo    2 minutes ago   Fix the 'quick start' typo
release/1.4 2 minutes ago   Add the example scripts

Deleted fix/typo
Deleted release/1.4

Make it a Git command by saving it as git-pick somewhere on your PATH and marking it executable; then git pick works.

items.title: What you learned
items.text:
• Feed lines or tsv input, read lines output, and keep stdout trustworthy: it is only written on success.
  • Handle 0, 2, 124 and other exit statuses explicitly under set -euo pipefail.
  • Use --multi and --timeout.

items.title: Where next
items.text:
• form collects several values at once from trusted HTML; the project picker tutorial uses select, form and view together.
  • Recipes, and every option on select.
  • For anything more interactive than one decision, use the Python or PowerShell SDK (see nativehtmlkit.github.io).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/tutorial-branch-picker.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Tutorial: build a project picker (Linux)
items.text:
In this tutorial you build proj, a small bash tool that remembers project directories and lets you jump to one by picking it in a native window:

proj add ~/src/website     # a form asks for name and tags
cd "$(proj pick)"          # a table of projects; pick one, Submit
proj list                  # a read-only table
proj remove                # tick projects, confirm

On the way you use all three interactive commands (select, form, view), two input formats, the exit contract, escaping for trusted HTML, and a stylesheet. The finished script is examples/tutorial/proj.sh (about 100 lines); every step below is a part of it.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

You need: the CLI release extracted and nativehtmlkit on PATH (install), bash 4 or later, and jq.

items.title: Step 1: a first picker
items.text:
select reads records from stdin, one per line by default, and prints the chosen one:

printf '%s\n' ~/src/website ~/src/cli ~/notes | nativehtmlkit select --title "Open project"

A window lists the three paths with a radio button each. Pick one and press Submit selection: the path is printed and the exit status is 0. Press Cancel: nothing is printed and the status is 2. Try echo $? after each.

That is already a usable tool, but a path alone is a poor label, and we want to store more (a name, tags, the date added).

items.title: Step 2: store projects as JSON lines
items.text:
Keep one JSON object per line in a file. NDJSON is both easy to append to and an input format of the CLI, so the file can be piped straight into select:

{"name":"website","path":"/home/me/src/website","tags":"work, web","added":"2026-11-16"}
{"name":"cli","path":"/home/me/src/cli","tags":"rust","added":"2026-11-16"}

With --input-format ndjson the window shows a table with the columns name, path, tags, added. With --output-format json the result is a JSON array holding the chosen record exactly as stored, so jq can read any field:

store=${PROJ_FILE:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/proj/projects.ndjson}

cmd_pick() {
  need_projects
  local picked
  picked=$(ui select --input-format ndjson --output-format json --title "Open project" <"$store")
  jq -r '.[0].path' <<<"$picked"
}

select refuses empty input (exit 1, no selectable input rows), so check first:

die() { echo "proj: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
need_projects() { [[ -s $store ]] || die "no projects yet; add one with: proj add [DIR]"; }

items.title: Step 3: one place for the exit contract
items.text:
Every call of the CLI can end in four ways: 0 (a result on stdout), 2 (Cancel), 124 (--timeout), or 1 and others (an error already explained on stderr). Handle that once:

set -euo pipefail

# ui ARGS... - run the CLI with ARGS and print its result. Cancel and timeout end the
# script with the CLI's status (called inside $(...), so set -e carries the exit through).
ui() {
  local status=0 out
  out=$(nativehtmlkit "$@" "${style[@]}") || status=$?
  case $status in
    0)   printf '%s' "$out" ;;
    2)   exit 2 ;;
    124) echo "proj: no answer in time" >&2; exit 124 ;;
    *)   exit "$status" ;;
  esac
}

ui is always called as x=$(ui ...). Its exit ends only that command substitution, but the substitution then fails with the same status and set -e ends the script with it. So a cancelled proj pick exits 2 and prints nothing, and the caller can tell. (style is filled in step 7; until then define style=().)

items.title: Step 4: add projects with a form
items.text:
form --html FILE shows your own HTML form and prints {"entries":[...]} on Submit. The fragment is trusted HTML, so the directory name and path, which come from the file system, must be escaped before they go into it. jq's @html does that:

esc() { jq -rn --arg s "$1" '$s | @html'; }

cmd_add() {
  local dir result record path
  dir=$(cd -- "${1:-.}" && pwd) || die "no such directory: ${1:-.}"
  html=$(mktemp --suffix=.html)          # global: the EXIT trap runs after this function
  trap 'rm -f -- "$html"' EXIT
  cat >"$html" <<HTML
<form id="nhk-form">
  <p><label>Name <input name="name" required maxlength="60" value="$(esc "$(basename -- "$dir")")"></label></p>
  <p><label>Directory <input name="path" required value="$(esc "$dir")"></label></p>
  <p><label>Tags <input name="tags" placeholder="work, rust" pattern="[A-Za-z0-9 ,_-]*"
         title="letters, digits, spaces, commas, - and _"></label></p>
</form>
HTML
  result=$(ui form --html "$html" --title "Add project")

The form element must have id="nhk-form". Core checks required, maxlength and pattern when the user presses Submit; an invalid form stays open with a message. The result looks like this:

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"name","value":"website"},{"kind":"text","name":"path","value":"/home/me/src/website"},{"kind":"text","name":"tags","value":"work, web"}]}

One jq expression turns it into the stored record, then the script checks it:

  # {"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"name","value":"..."},...]} -> {"name":"...",...}
  record=$(jq -c --arg added "$(date +%F)" \
             '(.entries | map({(.name): .value}) | add) + {added: $added}' <<<"$result")
  path=$(jq -r '.path' <<<"$record")
  [[ -d $path ]] || die "not a directory: $path"
  mkdir -p -- "$(dirname -- "$store")"
  touch -- "$store"
  if jq -e --arg p "$path" 'select(.path == $p)' "$store" >/dev/null; then
    die "already bookmarked: $path"
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$record" >>"$store"
  echo "proj: added $path" >&2
}

Messages go to stderr; stdout is reserved for results (that is what makes cd "$(proj pick)" work).

items.title: Step 5: list them
items.text:
view shows the same file read-only. It has no result; closing it exits 0:

cmd_list() {
  need_projects
  ui view --input-format ndjson --title "Projects ($(wc -l <"$store"))" <"$store"
}

items.title: Step 6: remove with confirmation
items.text:
--multi turns the radio buttons into checkboxes. --output-format ndjson returns the chosen records one per line, exactly as stored. A second select asks for confirmation; its safe answer is first and nothing is preselected:

cmd_remove() {
  need_projects
  local picked count answer tmp
  picked=$(ui select --multi --input-format ndjson --output-format ndjson \
             --title "Remove projects" <"$store")
  count=$(wc -l <<<"$picked")
  answer=$(printf 'Keep them\nRemove %d project(s)\n' "$count" |
           ui select --title "Remove $count project(s)?")
  [[ $answer == Remove* ]] || { echo "proj: nothing removed" >&2; return 0; }
  tmp=$(mktemp "$store.XXXXXX")
  jq -c --slurpfile drop <(printf '%s\n' "$picked") \
     'select(.path as $p | any($drop[]; .path == $p) | not)' "$store" >"$tmp"
  mv -- "$tmp" "$store"
  echo "proj: removed $count project(s)" >&2
}

The store is rewritten through a temporary file and mv, so an interrupted run never leaves half a file.

items.title: Step 7: give it a look
items.text:
--css adds a stylesheet after the built-in one. The page's colours are CSS custom properties, so small overrides go a long way (examples/tutorial/proj.css):

:root { --accent: #3fa37a; }
h1 { font-size: 18px; letter-spacing: .02em; }
td { color: #dfe7f1; }
button.primary { background: #2f8a63; border-color: #3fa37a; }

Pass it on every call through ui:

here=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
style=(--css "$here/proj.css")

items.title: Step 8: the command dispatcher
items.text:
case ${1:-pick} in
  pick | add | remove | list) cmd_"${1:-pick}" "${@:2}" ;;
  *) echo "usage: proj.sh [pick | add [DIR] | list | remove]" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

Put the script on your PATH as proj and add a shell function, because a script cannot change its caller's directory:

p() { local dir; dir=$(proj pick) && cd -- "$dir"; }

After Cancel, proj pick exits 2 with no output and p stays where it is.

items.title: Step 9: try it
items.text:
The examples below run proj.sh from the repository's examples directory with a store in the current directory. They were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py, headless and with replayed results (how).

Add a project. The form opens with the directory's name and path filled in:

export PROJ_FILE=$PWD/projects.ndjson
./tutorial/proj.sh add /tmp

When the user submits it, the record is stored:

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"name","value":"scratch"},{"kind":"text","name":"path","value":"/tmp"},{"kind":"text","name":"tags","value":"temp, demo"}]}

proj: added /tmp

Pick one (the store here has two projects):

export PROJ_FILE=$PWD/projects.ndjson
printf '%s\n' '{"name":"scratch","path":"/tmp","tags":"temp","added":"2026-11-16"}' \
               '{"name":"system","path":"/usr","tags":"","added":"2026-11-16"}' > "$PROJ_FILE"
./tutorial/proj.sh pick

[{"name":"system","path":"/usr","tags":"","added":"2026-11-16"}]

/usr

After Cancel, proj pick prints nothing and exits 2, so cd "$(proj pick)" and the p function stay where they are:

List and remove:

export PROJ_FILE=$PWD/projects.ndjson
printf '%s\n' '{"name":"scratch","path":"/tmp","tags":"temp","added":"2026-11-16"}' \
               '{"name":"system","path":"/usr","tags":"","added":"2026-11-16"}' > "$PROJ_FILE"
./tutorial/proj.sh list

export PROJ_FILE=$PWD/projects.ndjson
printf '%s\n' '{"name":"scratch","path":"/tmp","tags":"temp","added":"2026-11-16"}' \
               '{"name":"system","path":"/usr","tags":"","added":"2026-11-16"}' > "$PROJ_FILE"
./tutorial/proj.sh remove
status=$?
wc -l < "$PROJ_FILE"
exit "$status"

2

Tick scratch, then confirm with Remove 1 project(s):

{"name":"scratch","path":"/tmp","tags":"temp","added":"2026-11-16"}

Remove 1 project(s)

1

proj: removed 1 project(s)

To test your own tools like this, see test your scripts without a desktop.
