items.title: doctor, help and version (Linux)
items.text:
nativehtmlkit doctor reports which Core host executable the CLI would use and checks that it starts. help, --help and --version print information. None of them opens a window or reads stdin. Exact rules: OS-neutral reference.

The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

items.title: doctor
items.text:
nativehtmlkit doctor

prints three lines, for example:

NativeHTMLKit CLI 0.1.2
Core host: /opt/nativehtmlkit-cli/nativehtmlkit-host
nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3

The third line is the host's own --version output. Check it in a script:

if nativehtmlkit doctor | grep -qx 'nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3'; then
  echo 'qualified host found'
else
  echo 'install the release archive, or set NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY' >&2; exit 1
fi

qualified host found
Situation Exit stderr host found and it answered --version 0 no host anywhere 1 error[host.not_found]: NativeHTMLKit Core host not found. ... --host/NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY names no file 1 error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: <path> the file cannot be started 1 error[host.not_found]: cannot start the Core host (<reason>) it failed, printed nothing, or took over 10 s 1 error[host.failed]: ...

items.title: doctor --host PATH
items.text:
Check a specific host executable:

nativehtmlkit doctor --host /opt/missing/nativehtmlkit-host

nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: /opt/missing/nativehtmlkit-host

A file that is not a working host fails the version check:

printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 3\n' > fake-host && chmod +x fake-host
nativehtmlkit doctor --host ./fake-host

nativehtmlkit: error[host.failed]: Core host version check failed with exit status: 3

items.title: doctor --diagnostics LEVEL
items.text:
doctor writes no diagnostic records of its own at any level; the option is accepted so that the same global options work for every command:

nativehtmlkit doctor --diagnostics trace > /dev/null 2> doctor.log
wc -c < doctor.log

0

items.title: doctor --timeout, --rpc-timeout, --liveness-interval, --startup-timeout
items.text:
Accepted and ignored by doctor: it never opens a window, and its version check has its own fixed 10-second limit. They are useful when one options array is passed to every command:

opts=(--timeout 120 --rpc-timeout 10 --liveness-interval 2 --startup-timeout 30)
nativehtmlkit doctor "${opts[@]}" > /dev/null && echo 'doctor ok'
printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select "${opts[@]}" || echo "select ended with $?"

doctor ok
select ended with 124

items.title: --version, -V
items.text:
nativehtmlkit --version
nhk -V

nativehtmlkit 0.1.2
nativehtmlkit 0.1.2

items.title: --help, -h, help COMMAND
items.text:
--help prints the full help, -h a summary; after a command they describe that command. help COMMAND is the same as COMMAND --help:

nativehtmlkit --help | tail -n 1

Exit status: 0 submitted/viewed, 1 error, 2 cancelled, 124 --timeout expired, 130 Ctrl+C/SIGINT, 143 SIGTERM, 129 SIGHUP.

nativehtmlkit doctor --help | head -n 1
nativehtmlkit -h | head -n 1
nativehtmlkit help select | head -n 1

Usage: nativehtmlkit doctor [OPTIONS]
Native HTML/CSS windows for shell pipelines (alias: nhk)
Usage: nativehtmlkit select [OPTIONS]

help takes a command name, not options: nativehtmlkit help --help is a usage error (exit 1).

items.title: The nhk alias
items.text:
The release archive contains nhk, a symbolic link to nativehtmlkit. It behaves exactly the same, including finding the host beside the real file:

nhk doctor | head -n 1

NativeHTMLKit CLI 0.1.2

items.title: form: collect values with an HTML form
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: form: collect values with an HTML form (Linux)
items.text:
nativehtmlkit form --html FILE shows your own HTML form with the CLI's Cancel and Submit buttons below it. When the user submits a valid form, one line of JSON with the values is written to stdout. stdin is not read. Exact rules: OS-neutral reference.

nativehtmlkit form [OPTIONS] --html FILE
Outcome Exit status stdout Submit, every constraint satisfied 0 {"entries":[...]} and a newline Cancel, or the window closed 2 empty --timeout expired 124 empty error (missing file, no nhk-form, ...) 1 empty

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how). How to write and style forms: CSS and forms.
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --html FILE (required)
items.text:
A trusted UTF-8 HTML fragment (at most 256 KiB) that contains <form id="nhk-form">. Give every control a name; do not add a submit button of your own. sample-form.html (also in the release archive) is the smallest useful one:

<form id="nhk-form">
  <label>Project name <input id="project" name="project" required placeholder="My NativeHTMLKit App"></label>
  <p><label>Environment
    <select name="environment"><option value="development">Development</option><option value="production">Production</option></select>
  </label></p>
  <p><label><input type="checkbox" name="confirm" value="yes"> I confirm the details</label></p>
</form>

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html

After typing Demo App, keeping Development and ticking the checkbox, Submit prints this line (the exact result the release's GUI qualification asserts on Linux and Windows):

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"project","value":"Demo App"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"development"},{"kind":"text","name":"confirm","value":"yes"}]}

Read single values with jq. A checkbox that is not ticked has no entry, so give first(...) a default:

result=$(nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html) || exit
field() { jq -r --arg n "$1" 'first(.entries[] | select(.name == $n) | .value) // ""' <<<"$result"; }
echo "project=$(field project) environment=$(field environment) confirm=$(field confirm)"

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"project","value":"Demo App"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"development"}]}

With that result (checkbox not ticked) the script prints:

project=Demo App environment=development confirm=

Or turn all entries into one object:

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html | jq -c '.entries | map({(.name): .value}) | add'

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"project","value":"Demo App"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"development"},{"kind":"text","name":"confirm","value":"yes"}]}

{"project":"Demo App","environment":"development","confirm":"yes"}

The fragment must contain the form element nhk-form; otherwise nothing opens:

printf '<form><input name="a"></form>\n' > no-id.html
nativehtmlkit form --html no-id.html

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: --html must contain <form id="nhk-form"> with the controls to submit

--html is required:

nativehtmlkit form

error: the following required arguments were not provided:
  --html <HTML>
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: Generated forms: escape every value
items.text:
The fragment is trusted markup. Anything that comes from data (file names, Git tags, user names) must be HTML-escaped before it goes in. jq's @html escapes & < > " ':

esc() { jq -rn --arg s "$1" '$s | @html'; }
version='v1.2.3 <rc> & "beta"'
cat > release.html <<HTML
<form id="nhk-form">
  <label>Version <input name="version" required value="$(esc "$version")"></label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="publish" value="yes"> Publish now</label>
</form>
HTML
grep -o 'value="[^"]*"' release.html | head -n 1 >&2
nativehtmlkit form --html release.html

value="v1.2.3 <rc> & "beta""
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --title TITLE
items.text:
Window title and heading (default Input form), 1-128 characters, shown as text:

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --title 'New project'
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --css FILE
items.text:
A trusted style sheet added after the built-in one. css/form.css lays the form out as a grid of labelled fields:

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --css css/form.css --title 'New project'
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --timeout SECONDS
items.text:
A form left open is closed after the deadline, with exit 124 and no output:

status=0
result=$(nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --timeout 600) || status=$?
case $status in
  0)   echo "$result" ;;
  2)   echo 'cancelled' >&2; exit 2 ;;
  124) echo 'the form was left open for 10 minutes' >&2; exit 124 ;;
  *)   exit "$status" ;;
esac

the form was left open for 10 minutes
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --host PATH
items.text:
host=$(nativehtmlkit doctor | sed -n 's/^Core host: //p')
nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --host "$host"
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --diagnostics LEVEL
items.text:
nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --diagnostics debug 2> form.log || true
jq -rR 'fromjson? | select(.event == "session.started") | .context.mode' form.log

form
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --rpc-timeout SECONDS, --liveness-interval SECONDS, --startup-timeout SECONDS
items.text:
Host watchdogs; they never limit the person filling in the form:

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --rpc-timeout 15

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --liveness-interval 15

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --startup-timeout 30
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: -h, --help
items.text:
nativehtmlkit form --help | head -n 1

Usage: nativehtmlkit form [OPTIONS] --html <HTML>
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: What the result contains
items.text: entries are the form's successful controls in document order, as HTML form submission defines them: one {"kind":"text","name":...,"value":...} per named, enabled control that has a value. All values are strings. Unticked checkboxes and radio groups have no entry; a <select multiple> has one entry per chosen option; names may repeat; a file input gives {"kind":"file","name":...,"path":...,"filename":...}. Core checks required, pattern, min/max/step, minlength/maxlength and type="email"/"url" when the user clicks Submit; an invalid form stays open with Some required fields are invalid. Details: form reference.

items.title: select: choose rows (Linux)
items.text:
nativehtmlkit select shows the records piped into it as a table with a pick column and writes the rows the user submits to stdout. This page shows every option of the command with a bash example. The exact rules are in the OS-neutral reference.

nativehtmlkit select [OPTIONS] < records
Outcome Exit status stdout Submit selection 0 the chosen rows, in input order Cancel, or the window closed 2 empty --timeout expired 124 empty error (bad input or option, no host) 1 empty; nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: ... on stderr

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository, which has the sample files data/servers.csv, data/issues.json and css/light.css. Each example on this page was run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py; a "Submit prints" block shows the exact bytes the released code writes when the user ticks the rows named above it (how the examples are verified).

items.title: Without options: one line
items.text:
stdin is read as lines (--input-format lines). The window has one radio button per line; the chosen line is printed.

printf 'small\nmedium\nlarge\n' | nativehtmlkit select

Submit prints, after picking medium:

medium

Capture it in a variable and check the status. || status=$? keeps set -e from ending the script on Cancel:

status=0
size=$(printf 'small\nmedium\nlarge\n' | nativehtmlkit select) || status=$?
case $status in
  0)   echo "size: $size" ;;
  2)   echo "cancelled" ;;
  124) echo "no answer in time" ;;
  *)   echo "failed with $status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

medium

After the user picks medium the script prints:

size: medium

items.title: --multi
items.text:
Checkboxes instead of radio buttons: any number of rows. The chosen rows come back in input order, whatever order they were ticked in.

printf 'alpha
beta
gamma
delta
' | nativehtmlkit select --multi

Submit prints, after ticking delta, then alpha:

alpha
delta

Without --multi, Submit with nothing picked is refused: the window stays open and says select at least one row before submitting. With --multi the same applies:

printf 'a
b
' | nativehtmlkit select --multi

items.title: --allow-empty
items.text:
Accept Submit with nothing ticked. stdout is then empty for lines (and ndjson), [] for json, the header line for csv/tsv. Useful for "also do this" questions where "nothing" is a valid answer:

extras=$(printf 'clear cache\nrotate logs\nvacuum database\n' |
  nativehtmlkit select --multi --allow-empty --title 'Also run') || exit
printf 'extra: %s\n' $extras

Submit with nothing ticked prints nothing and exits 0:



printf 'name,size\na.txt,1\nb.txt,2\n' |
  nativehtmlkit select --multi --allow-empty --input-format csv --output-format json

[]

items.title: --input-format FORMAT
items.text:
How stdin is parsed: lines (default), csv, tsv, json, ndjson. Every format is shown in detail on input formats.

nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv < data/servers.csv

docker ps --all --format '{{json .}}' | jq -c '{Names, Image, State, Status, Ports, ID}' |
  nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson

items.title: --no-headers
items.text:
For csv and tsv: the first record is data, and the columns are named column_1 ... column_N:

printf 'web-01,healthy\nweb-02,degraded\ndb-01,healthy\n' |
  nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --no-headers --output-format json

Submit prints, after picking web-02:

[{"column_1":"web-02","column_2":"degraded"}]

items.title: --output-format FORMAT
items.text:
What Submit writes: same (default: the input format), lines, csv, tsv, json, ndjson. Each is shown on output formats. CSV in, JSON out, then jq by column name:

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json < data/servers.csv |
  jq -r '.[].host'

[{"host":"web-02","role":"frontend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"4","memory_gib":"8","status":"degraded","notes":"disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled"},{"host":"db-02","role":"database","region":"us-east","cpu_cores":"16","memory_gib":"128","status":"maintenance","notes":"replica, patching until 18:00"}]

The replayed result above is what Submit prints after ticking web-02 and db-02; the pipeline then prints:

web-02
db-02

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json < data/servers.csv

[{"host":"web-02","role":"frontend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"4","memory_gib":"8","status":"degraded","notes":"disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled"},{"host":"db-02","role":"database","region":"us-east","cpu_cores":"16","memory_gib":"128","status":"maintenance","notes":"replica, patching until 18:00"}]

items.title: --title TITLE
items.text:
The window title and the heading of the page (default Select an item). 1 to 128 characters, no control characters; it is shown as text, never as markup:

printf 'main\nfeature/login\n' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Switch to <branch> & pull'

An empty title is refused before any window opens:

echo a | nativehtmlkit select --title ''

nativehtmlkit: error[usage.invalid]: --title must be nonempty, at most 128 characters, with no control characters

items.title: --css FILE
items.text:
A trusted UTF-8 style sheet (at most 256 KiB) added after the built-in one. The page uses CSS custom properties for its colours, so a theme is a few lines (CSS and forms):

printf 'Europe/Prague
America/New_York
Asia/Tokyo
' |
  nativehtmlkit select --title 'Time zone' --css css/light.css

items.title: --timeout SECONDS
items.text:
Give the user a deadline. Without it the window waits as long as it takes. When the deadline passes the window is closed, stderr says so, stdout stays empty and the exit status is 124:

printf 'deploy\nskip\n' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Deploy now?' --timeout 60
echo "exit status: $?"

Nobody answered within the deadline (60 s here; the test uses a shorter one):

exit status: 124

nativehtmlkit: no decision before the --timeout deadline; the window was closed

items.title: --host PATH
items.text:
Use this Core host executable instead of the one beside the CLI. The release archive has the qualified host next to nativehtmlkit, so you only need this for development builds:

host=$(nativehtmlkit doctor | sed -n 's/^Core host: //p')   # the host found the normal way
printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select --host "$host"

A path that does not exist is an error, before anything else happens:

echo a | nativehtmlkit select --host /opt/missing/nativehtmlkit-host

nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: /opt/missing/nativehtmlkit-host

items.title: --diagnostics LEVEL
items.text:
off, normal (default), debug, trace: structured JSON records about the session on stderr, separate from the result on stdout (environment and diagnostics):

printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select --diagnostics debug 2> session.log
jq -rR 'fromjson? | select(.component == "nativehtmlkit-cli") | .event' session.log | grep -x -m1 window.ready

window.ready

items.title: --rpc-timeout SECONDS
items.text:
How long the CLI waits for the host to answer one request before it treats the host as hung (default 30). Lower it for unattended scripts that should fail fast; the person in front of the window is never affected by it:

printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select --rpc-timeout 10

items.title: --liveness-interval SECONDS
items.text:
Idle time between the CLI's "are you alive?" probes to the host while the window is open (default 5; 0 turns probing off). Together with --rpc-timeout it decides how soon a hung host is noticed:

printf 'a
b
' | nativehtmlkit select --liveness-interval 2 --rpc-timeout 5

printf 'a
b
' | nativehtmlkit select --liveness-interval 0

items.title: --startup-timeout SECONDS
items.text:
How long the host may take to open the window (default 15). Raise it on a slow, loaded machine:

printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select --startup-timeout 60

items.title: -h, --help
items.text:
nativehtmlkit select --help | head -n 3

Usage: nativehtmlkit select [OPTIONS]

Options:

-h prints the same options in one line each.

items.title: Options in any order
items.text:
Options can come before or after the command name; each may be given once:

printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit --rpc-timeout 10 select --multi --allow-empty

A repeated or unknown option is a usage error, exit 1:

echo a | nativehtmlkit select --multi --multi

items.title: view: show records read-only (Linux)
items.text:
nativehtmlkit view shows the records piped into it in a window with a single Close button. It never writes to stdout. Plain lines are shown as one wrapping, scrolling text block; every other input format as a table. Exact rules: OS-neutral reference.

nativehtmlkit view [OPTIONS] < records
Outcome Exit status stdout Close, or the window closed 0 empty --timeout expired 124 empty error 1 empty; nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: ... on stderr

view blocks until the window is closed. Unlike select it accepts no records: an empty viewer is fine. It has no --multi, --allow-empty or --output-format.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

items.title: Without options: text
items.text:
nativehtmlkit view < data/app.log

Markup in the text is shown literally: the <script> in that log stays text.

Command output works the same way:

ps -eo pid,user,pcpu,args --sort=-pcpu | head -n 200 | nativehtmlkit view

Nothing to show is not an error:

printf '' | nativehtmlkit view

items.title: --input-format FORMAT
items.text:
lines (default), csv, tsv, json, ndjson; every format except lines is shown as a table (input formats):

nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv < data/servers.csv

nativehtmlkit view --input-format ndjson < data/app.ndjson

nativehtmlkit view --input-format json < data/issues.json

issues.json has nested values (user, labels): they appear as compact JSON in their cells. Reshape with jq first for a readable table:

jq -c '[.[] | {"#": .number, Title: .title, Author: .user.login, Labels: ([.labels[].name] | join(", "))}]' data/issues.json |
  nativehtmlkit view --input-format json

printf 'name\tsize\tmodified\nreport.pdf\t120 KiB\t2026-11-14\nnotes.txt\t2 KiB\t2026-11-16\n' |
  nativehtmlkit view --input-format tsv

items.title: --no-headers
items.text:
For csv/tsv without a header row; columns are named column_1 ... column_N:

printf 'alice,admin,2026-01-04
bob,dev,2026-03-17
carol,ops,2026-06-30
' |
  nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --no-headers

items.title: --title TITLE
items.text:
Window title and heading (default Output viewer), 1-128 characters, shown as text:

nativehtmlkit view --title "app.log ($(wc -l < data/app.log) lines)" < data/app.log

items.title: --css FILE
items.text:
A trusted style sheet added after the built-in one (CSS and forms):

nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --css css/light.css < data/servers.csv

items.title: --timeout SECONDS
items.text:
Close the viewer by itself after a while. Exit 0 (closed) and 124 (deadline) both mean "done looking", so a script can carry on after either:

nativehtmlkit view --timeout 300 --title 'Build log' < data/app.log || [[ $? -eq 124 ]] || exit 1
echo 'continuing'

continuing

items.title: --host PATH
items.text:
host=$(nativehtmlkit doctor | sed -n 's/^Core host: //p')
echo 'pinned host' | nativehtmlkit view --host "$host"

items.title: --diagnostics LEVEL
items.text:
echo 'hello' | nativehtmlkit view --diagnostics debug 2> view.log || true
jq -rR 'fromjson? | select(.event == "session.started") | .context | "\(.mode) \(.rows)x\(.columns)"' view.log

view 1x1

items.title: --rpc-timeout SECONDS, --liveness-interval SECONDS, --startup-timeout SECONDS
items.text:
The host watchdogs (defaults 30, 5 and 15 seconds). They limit how long the CLI waits for a host that stopped working, never the person reading (global options):

nativehtmlkit view --rpc-timeout 10 < data/app.log

nativehtmlkit view --liveness-interval 10 < data/app.log

nativehtmlkit view --startup-timeout 45 < data/app.log

items.title: -h, --help
items.text:
nativehtmlkit view --help | head -n 1

Usage: nativehtmlkit view [OPTIONS]

items.title: Options that view does not have
items.text:
echo a | nativehtmlkit view --multi

error: unexpected argument '--multi' found

items.title: Limits
items.text:
At most 2,000 lines or records, 32 columns and an 8 MiB stdin; the generated page must stay under 1 MiB. More is an error, never a silent truncation, so cut first:

seq 1 100000 | tail -n 2000 | nativehtmlkit view --title 'last 2000'

seq 1 2001 | nativehtmlkit view

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: 2001 rows exceeds the 2000-row initial GUI limit

See view logs for long lines and the limits reference.

items.text:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Branch picker tutorial, step 1: offer the local branches in a native list and report the choice.
#
# Teaches: piping lines into `nativehtmlkit select`, capturing stdout, and the exit statuses
#          0 (chosen), 2 (cancelled), 124 (--timeout expired) and anything else (error).
# Run:     bash step1-pick.sh [--timeout SECONDS]     (inside a Git work tree)
# Guide:   docs/linux/tutorial-branch-picker.md (step 1 of 2)
set -euo pipefail

status=0
choice=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ \
  | nativehtmlkit select --title "Pick a branch" "$@") || status=$?

case $status in
  0) echo "You chose: $choice" ;;
  2) echo "Cancelled" >&2 ;;
  124) echo "No choice made in time" >&2 ;;
  *) echo "nativehtmlkit select failed with exit status $status" >&2 ;;
esac
exit "$status"

items.title: Source: tutorial-branch-picker/git-pick.sh
items.text:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# git-pick: choose a local Git branch in a native window and switch to it (CLI tutorial final code).
#
# Teaches: feeding TSV to `nativehtmlkit select`, reading the selection from stdout, handling every
#          exit status (0 chosen, 2 cancelled, 124 timed out, anything else an error), multi-select
#          with --multi, and keeping the shell script safe with `set -euo pipefail`.
# Run:     bash git-pick.sh [--timeout SECONDS]                 switch to the chosen branch
#          bash git-pick.sh --delete-merged [--timeout SECONDS] delete chosen branches already merged
#          bash git-pick.sh --print                             show the table that would be offered
#          (inside a Git work tree; needs `nativehtmlkit` on PATH)
# Guide:   docs/linux/tutorial-branch-picker.md
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  sed -n '2,11p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
}

die() { echo "git-pick: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

mode=switch
select_options=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --timeout)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--timeout needs a number of seconds"
      select_options+=(--timeout "$2"); shift 2 ;;
    --delete-merged) mode=delete; shift ;;
    --print) mode=print; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "git-pick: unknown option: $1 (try --help)" >&2; exit 64 ;;
  esac
done

command -v nativehtmlkit >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "nativehtmlkit is not on PATH (see the CLI install guide)"
git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "not inside a Git repository"
current=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD || echo "(detached HEAD)")

# One TSV row per branch, most recently committed first. The CLI treats a double quote as CSV/TSV
# quoting, so quotes in commit subjects are replaced by apostrophes.
branch_table() {
  printf 'branch\tupdated\tlast commit\n'
  git for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate \
    --format='%(refname:short)%09%(committerdate:relative)%09%(subject)' "$@" | tr '"' "'"
}

# Runs `nativehtmlkit select`, prints the chosen branch names (first column), returns its status.
pick() {
  local title=$1; shift
  local output status
  set +e
  output=$(nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv --output-format lines --title "$title" \
    "${select_options[@]}" "$@")
  status=$?
  set -e
  case $status in
    0) printf '%s\n' "$output" | cut -f1 ;;
    2) echo "git-pick: cancelled; nothing changed" >&2 ;;
    124) echo "git-pick: no choice made in time; nothing changed" >&2 ;;
    *) echo "git-pick: nativehtmlkit select failed with exit status $status" >&2 ;;
  esac
  return $status
}

case $mode in
  print)
    branch_table refs/heads/
    ;;
  switch)
    branch=$(branch_table refs/heads/ | pick "Switch branch (current: $current)") || exit $?
    [ -n "$branch" ] || die "no branch selected"
    if [ "$branch" = "$current" ]; then
      echo "Already on $branch"
    else
      git switch --quiet -- "$branch"
      echo "Switched to $branch"
    fi
    ;;
  delete)
    if [ -z "$(git for-each-ref --merged HEAD --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ | grep -vxF -- "$current" || true)" ]; then
      echo "No merged branches to delete"
      exit 0
    fi
    # Offer every merged branch except the one you are on (row 1 is the header).
    chosen=$(branch_table --merged HEAD refs/heads/ | awk -F'\t' -v current="$current" 'NR == 1 || $1 != current' \
      | pick "Delete merged branches" --multi) || exit $?
    while IFS= read -r branch; do
      if [ -n "$branch" ]; then
        git branch --quiet -d -- "$branch"
        echo "Deleted $branch"
      fi
    done <<< "$chosen"
    ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# csv-report.sh - review a CSV report in a native table, then export only the rows you tick.
#
# Teaches: `view` for read-only tables, `select --input-format csv --output-format csv`
# (the header is written back and every cell is re-quoted as needed), and writing the result
# through a temporary file so a Cancel never leaves a truncated or empty output file behind.
#
# Run:   ./csv-report.sh data/servers.csv [OUTPUT.csv]
#        Without OUTPUT only the viewer is shown.
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH.
# Exit:  0 viewed / exported, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
set -euo pipefail

report=${1:?usage: csv-report.sh REPORT.csv [OUTPUT.csv]}
output=${2:-}
title="Report: $(basename -- "$report")"

if [[ -z $output ]]; then
  # A viewer has no result: closing it exits 0 and prints nothing.
  exec nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --title "${title:0:128}" <"$report"
fi

tmp=$(mktemp "${output}.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f -- "$tmp"' EXIT

status=0
nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format csv \
  --title "Rows to export" <"$report" >"$tmp" || status=$?
case $status in
  0)   mv -- "$tmp" "$output"
       echo "csv-report: wrote $(( $(wc -l <"$output") - 1 )) row(s) to $output" >&2 ;;
  2)   echo "csv-report: cancelled, $output not written" >&2 ;;
  124) echo "csv-report: no decision in time, $output not written" >&2 ;;
esac
exit "$status"

items.text:
Tick files, confirm in a second window, then delete exactly the ticked files.

Same example in Windows: Delete files with confirmation

What it teaches: NUL-safe or literal paths; a confirmation select; nothing changes unless submitted.

items.title: Run it
items.text: ./delete-files.sh DIRECTORY [GLOB]

items.title: Source: delete-files.sh
items.text:
View on GitHub

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# delete-files.sh - tick files in a directory, confirm, and delete exactly those files.
#
# Teaches: NUL-safe file lists (find -print0 -> jq), multi-select with JSON output, a second
# `select` as a confirmation dialog whose safe answer is the default, and passing the chosen
# paths to rm NUL-separated so spaces, quotes and newlines in names cannot split them.
#
# Run:   ./delete-files.sh DIRECTORY [GLOB]       e.g. ./delete-files.sh ~/Downloads '*.iso'
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH, GNU find, jq, xargs.
# Exit:  0 deleted or nothing to do, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
set -euo pipefail

dir=${1:?usage: delete-files.sh DIRECTORY [GLOB]}
glob=${2:-*}

# size<TAB>mtime<TAB>path<NUL>; only the path can contain a tab, and it is the last field.
rows=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -printf '%s\t%TY-%Tm-%Td %TH:%TM\t%p\0' |
  jq -R -s -c 'split("\u0000") | map(select(length > 0) | split("\t") | (.[2:] | join("\t")) as $path | {
      Name: ($path | split("/") | last), "Size (KiB)": ((.[0] | tonumber) / 1024 | ceil),
      Modified: .[1], Path: $path
    }) | sort_by(.Modified) | .[:2000]')     # the CLI shows at most 2,000 rows

if [[ $(jq length <<<"$rows") -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "delete-files: nothing in $dir matches $glob" >&2
  exit 0
fi

# Run one picker; on anything but a submitted choice, leave without deleting. `pick` runs in
# a command substitution, so its `exit` ends only that subshell; `set -e` then ends the
# script with the same status.
pick() {
  local status=0 out
  out=$(nativehtmlkit select "$@") || status=$?
  case $status in
    0)   printf '%s' "$out" ;;
    2)   echo "delete-files: cancelled, nothing deleted" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    124) echo "delete-files: no decision in time, nothing deleted" >&2; exit 124 ;;
    *)   exit "$status" ;;
  esac
}

picked=$(pick --multi --input-format json --output-format json \
              --title "Files to delete in $(basename -- "$dir")" <<<"$rows")
count=$(jq length <<<"$picked")

answer=$(printf 'No, keep them\nYes, delete %d file(s)\n' "$count" |
         pick --title "Delete $count file(s)?")
if [[ $answer != Yes* ]]; then
  echo "delete-files: kept all files" >&2
  exit 0
fi

jq -j '.[].Path + "\u0000"' <<<"$picked" | xargs -0 rm -v --

items.text:
Collect validated deployment parameters, confirm production, return them typed.

Same example in Windows: A deployment form

What it teaches: generated and escaped --html; Core form validation; parsing entries; a confirmation step.

items.title: Source: deploy-form.sh
items.text:
View on GitHub

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# deploy-form.sh - collect deployment parameters in a native form and print them as JSON.
#
# Teaches: generating a trusted `--html` form from a script while escaping every dynamic
# value (jq's @html), Core's HTML constraint validation (required, pattern, min/max,
# type=email, maxlength) that runs before Submit is accepted, parsing the
# {"entries":[...]} result, an extra check in the script, and a confirmation step for
# production.
#
# Run:   ./deploy-form.sh [SERVICE...]            e.g. ./deploy-form.sh api web worker
#        ./deploy-form.sh api web | your-deploy-tool --params -
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH, jq; git (optional, to prefill the version).
# Exit:  0 parameters printed, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
set -euo pipefail

here=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
services=("$@")
[[ ${#services[@]} -gt 0 ]] || services=(api web worker)

esc() { jq -rn --arg s "$1" '$s | @html'; }    # escapes & < > " ' for HTML text and attributes

version=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || echo v1.0.0)

form=$(mktemp --suffix=.html)
trap 'rm -f -- "$form"' EXIT
{
  echo '<form id="nhk-form">'
  echo '<label>Service <select name="service" required><option value="">Choose...</option>'
  for s in "${services[@]}"; do
    printf '<option value="%s">%s</option>' "$(esc "$s")" "$(esc "$s")"
  done
  echo '</select></label>'
  echo '<fieldset><legend>Environment</legend>'
  echo '<label><input type="radio" name="environment" value="staging" required checked> Staging</label>'
  echo '<label><input type="radio" name="environment" value="production"> Production</label>'
  echo '</fieldset>'
  printf '<label>Version <input name="version" required value="%s" pattern="v?[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+" title="a version such as v1.4.2"></label>\n' "$(esc "$version")"
  echo '<label>Replicas <input name="replicas" type="number" min="1" max="20" value="2" required></label>'
  echo '<label>Notify <input name="notify" type="email" placeholder="team@example.com"></label>'
  echo '<label>Change notes <textarea name="notes" maxlength="500" rows="3"></textarea></label>'
  echo '<label class="check"><input type="checkbox" name="dry_run" value="yes" checked> Dry run only</label>'
  echo '</form>'
} >"$form"

status=0
result=$(nativehtmlkit form --html "$form" --css "$here/css/form.css" \
           --title "Deploy" --timeout 600) || status=$?
case $status in
  0)   ;;
  2)   echo "deploy-form: cancelled" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  124) echo "deploy-form: the form was left open for 10 minutes; closed" >&2; exit 124 ;;
  *)   exit "$status" ;;
esac

# {"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"service","value":"api"}, ...]}: one entry per
# successful control, in document order. An unchecked checkbox has no entry at all.
field() { jq -r --arg n "$1" 'first(.entries[] | select(.name == $n) | .value) // ""' <<<"$result"; }

service=$(field service) environment=$(field environment) version=$(field version)
replicas=$(field replicas) notify=$(field notify) notes=$(field notes)
dry_run=false; [[ $(field dry_run) == yes ]] && dry_run=true

# A rule HTML cannot express: production deploys need change notes.
if [[ $environment == production && -z ${notes//[[:space:]]/} ]]; then
  echo "deploy-form: production deploys need change notes" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ $environment == production && $dry_run == false ]]; then
  status=0
  answer=$(printf 'No, stop here\nYes, deploy %s %s to production\n' "$service" "$version" |
           nativehtmlkit select --title "Really deploy to production?") || status=$?
  [[ $status -eq 0 && $answer == Yes* ]] || { echo "deploy-form: not confirmed" >&2; exit 2; }
fi

jq -n --arg service "$service" --arg environment "$environment" --arg version "$version" \
      --argjson replicas "$replicas" --arg notify "$notify" --arg notes "$notes" \
      --argjson dry_run "$dry_run" \
      '{service: $service, environment: $environment, version: $version, replicas: $replicas,
        notify: (if $notify == "" then null else $notify end), notes: $notes, dry_run: $dry_run}'

items.title: Choose a Docker container
items.text:
Pick a container, then show its logs, restart, stop it or open a shell.

Same example in Windows: Choose a Docker container

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

What it teaches: NDJSON from docker ps; chained selections; view for logs.

items.title: Run it

items.title: Source: pick-container.sh
items.text:
View on GitHub

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pick-container.sh - choose a Docker container, then choose what to do with it.
#
# Teaches: NDJSON input (`docker ps --format '{{json .}}'` prints one object per line),
# projecting a wide record down to the columns worth showing, chaining two selections, and
# showing command output in a read-only `view` window.
#
# Run:   ./pick-container.sh
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH, docker, jq, perl.
# Exit:  0 action done, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
set -euo pipefail

# Stop on anything but a submitted choice (Cancel 2, timeout 124, error 1).
choose() {
  local status=0 out
  out=$(nativehtmlkit select "$@") || status=$?
  [[ $status -eq 0 ]] || { echo "pick-container: no action taken" >&2; exit "$status"; }
  printf '%s' "$out"
}

rows=$(docker ps --all --format '{{json .}}' |
       jq -c '{Name: .Names, Image, State, Status, Ports, ID}')
if [[ -z $rows ]]; then
  echo "pick-container: no containers" >&2
  exit 0
fi

container=$(choose --input-format ndjson --output-format json --title "Containers" <<<"$rows")
id=$(jq -r '.[0].ID' <<<"$container")
name=$(jq -r '.[0].Name' <<<"$container")

action=$(printf 'logs\nrestart\nstop\nshell\n' |
         choose --title "Container ${name:0:80}")     # --title allows at most 128 characters

case $action in
  logs)    docker logs --tail 1000 --timestamps "$id" 2>&1 | perl -CSD -pe 's/^(.{400}).+/$1.../' |
             nativehtmlkit view --title "Logs: ${name:0:80}" ;;
  restart) docker restart "$id" ;;
  stop)    docker stop "$id" ;;
  shell)   docker exec -it "$id" sh ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pick-from-api.sh - choose issues from a JSON API response and print their URLs.
#
# Teaches: reshaping nested API JSON with jq into flat rows (one column per key, at most 32),
# keeping a hidden-in-plain-sight key (`url`) for the follow-up step, multi-select with JSON
# output, and printing a pipe-friendly result (one URL per line on stdout).
#
# Run:   curl -fsS 'https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/issues?per_page=100' | ./pick-from-api.sh
#        ./pick-from-api.sh data/issues.json          (the sample response in this directory)
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH, jq.
# Exit:  0 printed the chosen URLs, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
set -euo pipefail

source=${1:--}     # a file name, or - for stdin

# GitHub lists pull requests as issues too; they carry a "pull_request" key.
rows=$(jq -c '[.[] | select(has("pull_request") | not) | {
          "#": .number,
          Title: .title,
          Author: .user.login,
          Labels: ([.labels[].name] | join(", ")),
          Updated: .updated_at[:10],
          url: .html_url
        }]' "$source")

if [[ $(jq length <<<"$rows") -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "pick-from-api: the response contains no issues" >&2
  exit 0
fi

status=0
picked=$(nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json --output-format json \
           --title "Open issues" <<<"$rows") || status=$?
[[ $status -eq 0 ]] || exit "$status"

# Records come back exactly as they went in (key order, number text), in input order.
jq -r '.[].url' <<<"$picked"

items.text:
Switch to a branch chosen from a table of recent branches with their last commit.

Same example in Windows: Pick a Git branch

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

What it teaches: JSON rows built from tab-separated tool output; single choice; reading a field of the chosen record.

items.title: Run it

items.title: Source: pick-git-branch.sh
items.text:
View on GitHub

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pick-git-branch.sh - choose a local Git branch in a native window and switch to it.
#
# Teaches: turning tab-separated command output into JSON rows with jq, a single-choice
# `select`, reading one field of the JSON result, and telling Cancel (2) and --timeout (124)
# apart from errors (1).
#
# Run:   ./pick-git-branch.sh [REPOSITORY]        (default: the current directory)
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH, git, jq.
# Exit:  0 switched, 2 cancelled, 124 no choice before the deadline, 1 error.
set -euo pipefail

repo=${1:-.}

# One JSON object per branch, newest first. The subject is the last field, so a tab inside
# it is joined back instead of shifting the columns.
rows=$(git -C "$repo" for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate \
    --format='%(HEAD)%09%(refname:short)%09%(committerdate:relative)%09%(upstream:short)%09%(subject)' \
    refs/heads |
  jq -R -s -c 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {
      Current: .[0], Branch: .[1], Updated: .[2], Upstream: .[3], "Last commit": (.[4:] | join("\t"))
    })')

if [[ $(jq length <<<"$rows") -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "pick-git-branch: no local branches in $repo" >&2
  exit 1
fi

status=0
picked=$(nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --output-format json \
           --title "Switch branch" --timeout 120 <<<"$rows") || status=$?
case $status in
  0)   ;;
  2)   echo "pick-git-branch: cancelled; still on $(git -C "$repo" branch --show-current)" >&2
       exit 2 ;;
  124) echo "pick-git-branch: no branch chosen within 120 s" >&2
       exit 124 ;;
  *)   exit "$status" ;;   # the CLI already printed "nativehtmlkit: error[...]" on stderr
esac

branch=$(jq -r '.[0].Branch' <<<"$picked")
git -C "$repo" switch "$branch"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pick-timezone.sh - choose a time zone from a long list in a light-themed window.
#
# Teaches: restyling the CLI's window with a trusted --css file (css/light.css overrides the
# page's colour custom properties) and using a single `lines` selection as a value.
#
# Run:   ./pick-timezone.sh                  prints e.g. Europe/Prague
#        TZ=$(./pick-timezone.sh) date
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH; timedatectl or /usr/share/zoneinfo.
# Exit:  0 printed the zone, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
set -euo pipefail

here=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

zones() {
  if timedatectl list-timezones 2>/dev/null; then return; fi
  (cd /usr/share/zoneinfo && find . -type f -name '[A-Z]*' | sed 's|^\./||' | grep '/' | grep -v '^right/\|^posix/' | sort)
}

zones | head -n 2000 |
  nativehtmlkit select --title "Time zone" --css "$here/css/light.css"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# kill-process.sh - pick processes from a table, choose the signal, and send it.
#
# Teaches: turning `ps` output into correctly quoted CSV, multi-select over CSV input with
# JSON output (field access by column name), and a second `select` that chooses an action.
#
# Run:   ./kill-process.sh [NAME-FILTER]           e.g. ./kill-process.sh python
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH, procps `ps` (Linux), awk, jq.
# Exit:  0 signal sent, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
set -euo pipefail

filter=${1:-}

# Take the snapshot first, then filter it: a filter running while ps runs would list itself.
listing=$(ps -eo pid=,user=,pcpu=,pmem=,etime=,args= --sort=-pcpu)

# CSV with a header row. The command is the only free-text field; it is quoted and any "
# inside it doubled, as RFC 4180 requires, so the CLI parses it as one cell.
rows=$(awk -v filter="$filter" -v self=$$ '
    BEGIN { print "PID,User,CPU %,Mem %,Running,Command" }
    $1 == self || n >= 500 { next }
    {
      cmd = $6; for (i = 7; i <= NF; i++) cmd = cmd " " $i
      if (filter != "" && index(cmd, filter) == 0) next
      if (length(cmd) > 160) cmd = substr(cmd, 1, 157) "..."
      gsub(/"/, "\"\"", cmd)
      printf "%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,\"%s\"\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5, cmd; n++
    }' <<<"$listing")

if [[ $(wc -l <<<"$rows") -le 1 ]]; then
  echo "kill-process: no process matches '${filter}'" >&2
  exit 0
fi

status=0
picked=$(nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json \
           --title "Processes to signal" <<<"$rows") || status=$?
[[ $status -eq 0 ]] || { echo "kill-process: nothing signalled" >&2; exit "$status"; }

mapfile -t pids < <(jq -r '.[].PID' <<<"$picked")

status=0
signal=$(printf 'TERM  - ask the process to exit\nINT   - like Ctrl+C\nKILL  - force, cannot be caught\n' |
         nativehtmlkit select --title "Signal for ${#pids[@]} process(es)") || status=$?
[[ $status -eq 0 ]] || { echo "kill-process: nothing signalled" >&2; exit "$status"; }

signal=${signal%% *}
kill -s "$signal" -- "${pids[@]}"
echo "kill-process: sent SIG$signal to ${pids[*]}" >&2

items.title: Project picker (tutorial)
items.text:
Bookmark project directories, pick one to jump to, list and remove them.

Same example in Windows: Project picker (tutorial)

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

What it teaches: select, form and view in one tool; NDJSON as storage and CLI format; one wrapper for the exit contract; escaped generated forms; --css.

items.title: Run it
items.text: ./tutorial/proj.sh [pick | add [DIR] | list | remove]

items.title: Source: tutorial/proj.sh
items.text:
View on GitHub

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# proj.sh - a small project-directory bookmark tool, built step by step in
# docs/linux/tutorial.md.
#
# Teaches: one storage format (NDJSON) used directly as CLI input and output, a shared
# wrapper for the exit contract, a generated and escaped form, multi-select with
# confirmation, a read-only table, and a custom stylesheet.
#
# Run:   ./proj.sh add [DIR]      bookmark DIR (default: the current directory)
#        cd "$(./proj.sh pick)"   jump to a bookmarked project
#        ./proj.sh list           show all bookmarks
#        ./proj.sh remove         tick bookmarks to remove, then confirm
# Store: $PROJ_FILE, default ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/proj/projects.ndjson
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH, jq.
# Exit:  0 done, 2 cancelled, 124 no answer in time, 1 error.
set -euo pipefail

here=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
store=${PROJ_FILE:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/proj/projects.ndjson}
style=(--css "$here/proj.css")

die() { echo "proj: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
esc() { jq -rn --arg s "$1" '$s | @html'; }

# ui ARGS... - run the CLI with ARGS and print its result. Cancel and timeout end the
# script with the CLI's status (called inside $(...), so set -e carries the exit through).
ui() {
  local status=0 out
  out=$(nativehtmlkit "$@" "${style[@]}") || status=$?
  case $status in
    0)   printf '%s' "$out" ;;
    2)   exit 2 ;;
    124) echo "proj: no answer in time" >&2; exit 124 ;;
    *)   exit "$status" ;;
  esac
}

need_projects() { [[ -s $store ]] || die "no projects yet; add one with: proj add [DIR]"; }

cmd_pick() {
  need_projects
  local picked
  picked=$(ui select --input-format ndjson --output-format json --title "Open project" <"$store")
  jq -r '.[0].path' <<<"$picked"
}

cmd_add() {
  local dir result record path
  dir=$(cd -- "${1:-.}" && pwd) || die "no such directory: ${1:-.}"
  html=$(mktemp --suffix=.html)          # global: the EXIT trap runs after this function
  trap 'rm -f -- "$html"' EXIT
  cat >"$html" <<HTML
<form id="nhk-form">
  <p><label>Name <input name="name" required maxlength="60" value="$(esc "$(basename -- "$dir")")"></label></p>
  <p><label>Directory <input name="path" required value="$(esc "$dir")"></label></p>
  <p><label>Tags <input name="tags" placeholder="work, rust" pattern="[A-Za-z0-9 ,_-]*"
         title="letters, digits, spaces, commas, - and _"></label></p>
</form>
HTML
  result=$(ui form --html "$html" --title "Add project")
  # {"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"name","value":"..."},...]} -> {"name":"...",...}
  record=$(jq -c --arg added "$(date +%F)" \
             '(.entries | map({(.name): .value}) | add) + {added: $added}' <<<"$result")
  path=$(jq -r '.path' <<<"$record")
  [[ -d $path ]] || die "not a directory: $path"
  mkdir -p -- "$(dirname -- "$store")"
  touch -- "$store"
  if jq -e --arg p "$path" 'select(.path == $p)' "$store" >/dev/null; then
    die "already bookmarked: $path"
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$record" >>"$store"
  echo "proj: added $path" >&2
}

cmd_remove() {
  need_projects
  local picked count answer tmp
  picked=$(ui select --multi --input-format ndjson --output-format ndjson \
             --title "Remove projects" <"$store")
  count=$(wc -l <<<"$picked")
  answer=$(printf 'Keep them\nRemove %d project(s)\n' "$count" |
           ui select --title "Remove $count project(s)?")
  [[ $answer == Remove* ]] || { echo "proj: nothing removed" >&2; return 0; }
  tmp=$(mktemp "$store.XXXXXX")
  jq -c --slurpfile drop <(printf '%s\n' "$picked") \
     'select(.path as $p | any($drop[]; .path == $p) | not)' "$store" >"$tmp"
  mv -- "$tmp" "$store"
  echo "proj: removed $count project(s)" >&2
}

cmd_list() {
  need_projects
  ui view --input-format ndjson --title "Projects ($(wc -l <"$store"))" <"$store"
}

case ${1:-pick} in
  pick | add | remove | list) cmd_"${1:-pick}" "${@:2}" ;;
  *) echo "usage: proj.sh [pick | add [DIR] | list | remove]" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

Tick files in a window, then search only those for a pattern.

Same example in Windows: Search only the files you tick

What it teaches: select --multi as a pipeline stage; the CLI's own exit status inside a pipeline.

items.title: Source: grep-selected.sh
items.text:
View on GitHub

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# grep-selected.sh - tick files in a window, then search only those files with grep.
#
# Teaches: using `select --multi` as one stage of a pipeline into xargs, and reading the
# CLI's own exit status from PIPESTATUS, because a pipeline's status is normally that of its
# last command (here grep/xargs), which would hide a Cancel or a timeout.
#
# Run:   ./grep-selected.sh PATTERN [DIRECTORY]      e.g. ./grep-selected.sh TODO src
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH, GNU find and xargs (-d), grep.
# Exit:  0 matches found, 1 no match or error, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time.
set -uo pipefail     # no -e: every status of the pipeline is inspected below

pattern=${1:?usage: grep-selected.sh PATTERN [DIRECTORY]}
dir=${2:-.}

# `lines` input and output: one path per line. A file name that itself contains a newline
# cannot be represented in this format (use JSON or NDJSON for such names).
find "$dir" -type f -not -path '*/.git/*' -size -2M | sort | head -n 2000 |
  nativehtmlkit select --multi --title "Search for: ${pattern:0:100}" |
  xargs -r -d '\n' grep -n -H -e "$pattern" --
status=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")      # find, sort, head, nativehtmlkit, xargs

case ${status[3]} in
  0)   [[ ${status[4]} -eq 0 ]] && exit 0 || exit 1 ;;   # xargs: 123 = grep found nothing
  2)   echo "grep-selected: cancelled" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  124) echo "grep-selected: no files chosen in time" >&2; exit 124 ;;
  *)   exit 1 ;;
esac

items.title: View logs
items.text:
Show the end of a text or JSON-lines log (Windows: also the event log).

Same example in Windows: View logs

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

What it teaches: view for text and NDJSON; staying inside the page limit.

items.title: Run it
items.text: ./view-logs.sh data/app.log

items.title: Source: view-logs.sh
items.text:
View on GitHub

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# view-logs.sh - show the end of a log file (plain text or JSON lines) in a native viewer.
#
# Teaches: `view` for plain text (a scrolling, wrapped text pane) and for NDJSON (a table
# with one column per key), and keeping input inside the CLI limits: at most 2,000 rows
# and a generated page of at most 1 MiB, so long lines are shortened first.
#
# Run:   ./view-logs.sh data/app.log
#        ./view-logs.sh data/app.ndjson
#        journalctl -n 500 --no-pager | ./view-logs.sh -
# Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH, tail, perl.
# Exit:  0 viewer closed, 124 closed by the deadline, 1 error.
set -euo pipefail

file=${1:?usage: view-logs.sh FILE|-}
lines=${LINES_SHOWN:-1000}

if [[ $file == - ]]; then
  name=stdin
else
  name=$(basename -- "$file")
fi

case $file in
  *.ndjson | *.jsonl)
    # JSON lines are not shortened (that would break them); keep the row limit only.
    tail -n "$lines" -- "$file" |
      nativehtmlkit view --input-format ndjson --title "Log: ${name:0:100}" ;;
  *)
    # Shorten by characters, not bytes: cutting bytes could split a UTF-8 sequence, and
    # the CLI refuses input that is not valid UTF-8.
    tail -n "$lines" -- "$file" | perl -CSD -pe 's/^(.{400}).+/$1.../' |
      nativehtmlkit view --title "Log: ${name:0:100}" ;;
esac

items.title: Review and export CSV reports (Linux)
items.text:
Look at a CSV file in a table, or tick rows and export them as a new CSV file. Script: examples/csv-report.sh, sample examples/data/servers.csv.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

items.title: Look at it
items.text:
./csv-report.sh data/servers.csv

The first record is the header; quoted fields ("disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled", "canary for ""v2"" API") are shown unquoted. Without the script:

nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --title 'Servers' < data/servers.csv

items.title: Export the rows you tick
items.text:
./csv-report.sh data/servers.csv degraded.csv
status=$?
ls degraded.csv* 2>/dev/null
exit "$status"

On Cancel or a timeout no output file, and no temporary file, is left behind (the ls found nothing):

After ticking web-02 and Submit, degraded.csv exists:

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes
web-02,frontend,eu-west,4,8,degraded,"disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled"

degraded.csv

csv-report: wrote 1 row(s) to degraded.csv

The script writes through a temporary file and moves it into place only on exit 0:

tmp=$(mktemp "${output}.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f -- "$tmp"' EXIT
status=0
nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format csv \
  --title "Rows to export" <"$report" >"$tmp" || status=$?
case $status in
  0)   mv -- "$tmp" "$output"

items.title: Other shapes of the same rows
items.text:
--output-format You get csv header and chosen rows, re-quoted where needed tsv the same, tab-separated json [{"host":"web-02","role":"frontend",...}], all values strings lines each row's fields joined by a tab, no header

Only the host names of the chosen rows:

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json < data/servers.csv | jq -r '.[].host'

A file without a header row needs --no-headers (columns column_1, ...):

tail -n +2 data/servers.csv | nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --no-headers

Semicolon-separated files are not supported; convert them first (input formats).

Windows: Review and export CSV reports (Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/recipes/csv-report.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Delete files with confirmation (Linux)
items.text:
Tick files in a window, confirm in a second window, then delete exactly the ticked files. Cancel, closing a window or the deadline delete nothing. Script: examples/delete-files.sh (needs GNU find, jq, xargs).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

items.title: Run it
items.text:
mkdir -p scratch
printf 'one\n' > 'scratch/a b.txt'
printf 'two\n' > "scratch/it's \"quoted\".log"
printf 'three\n' > scratch/notes.md
printf 'four\n' > scratch/-rf.txt
./delete-files.sh scratch

A table of the four files (Name, Size (KiB), Modified, Path) opens. Suppose the user ticks a b.txt and -rf.txt, then picks Yes, delete 2 file(s) in the confirmation window:

[{"Name":"a b.txt","Size (KiB)":1,"Modified":"2026-11-16 09:00","Path":"scratch/a b.txt"},{"Name":"-rf.txt","Size (KiB)":1,"Modified":"2026-11-16 09:00","Path":"scratch/-rf.txt"}]

The script then asks in a second window (here nobody answers, so it ends with 124 and deletes nothing):

delete-files: no decision in time, nothing deleted

With Yes, delete 2 file(s) picked in the second window, exactly those two files go:

Yes, delete 2 file(s)

removed 'scratch/a b.txt'
removed 'scratch/-rf.txt'

With No, keep them the script exits 0 and deletes nothing:

No, keep them

delete-files: kept all files

Only a file glob:

mkdir -p scratch && printf 'x\n' > scratch/old.iso && printf 'y\n' > scratch/keep.txt
./delete-files.sh scratch '*.iso'

Nothing matches: the script says so and exits 0 without opening a window:

mkdir -p empty-dir
./delete-files.sh empty-dir

items.title: How it works
items.text:
1. List without breaking on odd names. File names may contain spaces, quotes or newlines, so the script lists the directory NUL-separated and builds JSON rows with jq:
rows=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -printf '%s\t%TY-%Tm-%Td %TH:%TM\t%p\0' |
  jq -R -s -c 'split("\u0000") | map(select(length > 0) | split("\t") | (.[2:] | join("\t")) as $path | {
      Name: ($path | split("/") | last), "Size (KiB)": ((.[0] | tonumber) / 1024 | ceil),
      Modified: .[1], Path: $path
    }) | sort_by(.Modified) | .[:2000]')
  1. Pick, then confirm. The confirmation is a single-choice select whose safe answer comes first; nothing is preselected, so deleting needs a deliberate choice and Submit:
answer=$(printf 'No, keep them\nYes, delete %d file(s)\n' "$count" | pick --title "Delete $count file(s)?")
  1. Delete exactly what was chosen, NUL-separated and after --, so no name can be split or read as an option (-rf.txt stays a file name):
jq -j '.[].Path + "\u0000"' <<<"$picked" | xargs -0 rm -v --

items.title: A form as the confirmation
items.text:
For a stronger confirmation use form with a required checkbox; Submit is only accepted with the box ticked. Escape the names you put into the HTML:

picked='[{"Path":"scratch/a <b>.txt"},{"Path":"scratch/notes & more.md"}]'
esc() { jq -rn --arg s "$1" '$s | @html'; }
{
  echo '<form id="nhk-form"><p>These files will be deleted:</p><ul>'
  jq -r '.[].Path' <<<"$picked" | while IFS= read -r p; do echo "<li>$(esc "$p")</li>"; done
  echo '</ul><label><input type="checkbox" name="sure" value="yes" required> I understand</label></form>'
} > confirm.html
nativehtmlkit form --html confirm.html --title 'Confirm deletion' > /dev/null || exit
echo 'confirmed'

Exit 0 means confirmed; anything else ends the script before deleting.

Windows: Delete files with confirmation (Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/recipes/delete-files.md · edit the page there.

items.title: A deployment form (Linux)
items.text:
Collect deployment parameters in a form with validation, check a rule HTML cannot express, ask for confirmation before production, and print the parameters as typed JSON for the next tool. Script: examples/deploy-form.sh with css/form.css (needs jq; git optional, to prefill the version).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how). Writing forms in general: CSS and forms.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
./deploy-form.sh api web worker

The form offers the services given on the command line, Staging or Production, a version (prefilled from git describe, checked with a pattern), replicas (1-20), an optional e-mail address, change notes and a Dry run only checkbox. Service names are HTML-escaped into the form, so hostile names are harmless:

./deploy-form.sh '<script>x</script>' 'a"b' "it's&more"

After a staging Submit the CLI prints the entries, and the script turns them into typed JSON (numbers as numbers, the checkbox as a boolean, an empty e-mail as null):

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"service","value":"api"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"staging"},{"kind":"text","name":"version","value":"v1.4.2"},{"kind":"text","name":"replicas","value":"3"},{"kind":"text","name":"notify","value":""},{"kind":"text","name":"notes","value":""},{"kind":"text","name":"dry_run","value":"yes"}]}

{
  "service": "api",
  "environment": "staging",
  "version": "v1.4.2",
  "replicas": 3,
  "notify": null,
  "notes": "",
  "dry_run": true
}

Production without change notes is refused by the script (exit 1):

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"service","value":"api"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"production"},{"kind":"text","name":"version","value":"v1.4.2"},{"kind":"text","name":"replicas","value":"3"},{"kind":"text","name":"notify","value":""},{"kind":"text","name":"notes","value":"  "}]}

deploy-form: production deploys need change notes

A real production deploy (no dry run) asks once more in a select. Anything but Yes (here: nobody answered in time) stops with exit 2:

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"service","value":"web"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"production"},{"kind":"text","name":"version","value":"2.0.0"},{"kind":"text","name":"replicas","value":"4"},{"kind":"text","name":"notify","value":"ops@example.com"},{"kind":"text","name":"notes","value":"Rollout of the new login"}]}

deploy-form: not confirmed

Answering Yes, deploy web 2.0.0 to production prints the parameters:

Yes, deploy web 2.0.0 to production

{
  "service": "web",
  "environment": "production",
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "replicas": 4,
  "notify": "ops@example.com",
  "notes": "Rollout of the new login",
  "dry_run": false
}

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Every dynamic value is escaped with jq's @html while the form is written:

esc() { jq -rn --arg s "$1" '$s | @html'; }    # escapes & < > " ' for HTML text and attributes
for s in "${services[@]}"; do
  printf '<option value="%s">%s</option>' "$(esc "$s")" "$(esc "$s")"
done
printf '<label>Version <input name="version" required value="%s" pattern="v?[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+" title="a version such as v1.4.2"></label>\n' "$(esc "$version")"

Core validates required, pattern, min/max and type="email" before it accepts Submit. The script reads the entries with one helper; an unticked checkbox has no entry, so // "" supplies the default:

field() { jq -r --arg n "$1" 'first(.entries[] | select(.name == $n) | .value) // ""' <<<"$result"; }
dry_run=false; [[ $(field dry_run) == yes ]] && dry_run=true

Use the output as input for the next step:

params=$(./deploy-form.sh api web) || exit
jq -r '"deploying \(.service) \(.version) x\(.replicas) to \(.environment)"' <<<"$params"

Windows: A deployment form (Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/recipes/deploy-form.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Choose a Docker container (Linux)
items.text:
Pick a container, then an action: show its logs, restart, stop, or open a shell. Script: examples/pick-container.sh (needs docker, jq, perl).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how) with a stand-in docker that lists two containers (web, and db <primary>), so no real Docker daemon was touched.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
./pick-container.sh

The first window lists the containers (Name, Image, State, Status, Ports, ID). After the user picks web:

[{"Name":"web","Image":"nginx:1.27","State":"running","Status":"Up 2 hours","Ports":"0.0.0.0:8080->80/tcp","ID":"3f2a9c1d7b44"}]

a second window asks for the action; nobody answers here, so nothing is done:

pick-container: no action taken

With restart chosen, the script runs docker restart 3f2a9c1d7b44 and exits 0:

restart

With logs chosen, a third window shows the container's last 1,000 log lines:

logs

items.title: How it works
items.text:
docker ps --format '{{json .}}' prints one JSON object per container per line: exactly the ndjson input format. The objects have many keys; project the useful ones with jq so the table stays narrow:

docker ps --all --format '{{json .}}' | jq -c '{Name: .Names, Image, State, Status, Ports, ID}' |
  nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson --output-format json --title 'Containers'

[{"Name":"db <primary>","Image":"postgres:17","State":"exited","Status":"Exited (0) 3 minutes ago","Ports":"5432/tcp","ID":"9b8e7d6c5a43"}]

The name db <primary> is shown as text, never as markup. jq -r '.[0].ID' then gives the id. Logs are shown with view, each line cut to 400 characters (by character, with perl -CSD, so UTF-8 stays valid) to stay inside the 1 MiB page limit:

docker logs --tail 1000 --timestamps 3f2a9c1d7b44 2>&1 | perl -CSD -pe 's/^(.{400}).+/$1.../' |
  nativehtmlkit view --title 'Logs: web'

--title allows 128 characters, so the script cuts container names to 80 (${name:0:80}). The same pattern works for any tool that prints JSON: kubectl get pods -o json | jq -c '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, phase: .status.phase}' is ndjson too.

Windows: Choose a Docker container (Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/recipes/docker.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Pick a Git branch (Linux)
items.text:
Show the local branches, newest first, with their last commit, and switch to the one the user picks. Script: examples/pick-git-branch.sh (needs git and jq). For a step-by-step version with TSV and deleting merged branches, see the branch picker tutorial.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository (a Git work tree) and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

items.title: Quick version
items.text:
branch=$(git branch --format='%(refname:short)' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Switch branch') &&
  git switch "$branch"

&& runs git switch only after a Submit; on Cancel (2) or a timeout (124) nothing happens and the line ends with the CLI's status.

items.title: With columns
items.text:
./pick-git-branch.sh

The window shows Current, Branch, Updated, Upstream and Last commit. When the user picks feature/login, the CLI returns that record as a JSON array (the record exactly as it went in) and the script switches:

[{"Current":" ","Branch":"feature/login","Updated":"2 minutes ago","Upstream":"","Last commit":"Add the example scripts"}]

Switched to branch 'feature/login'

After Cancel nothing changes and the script exits 2:



pick-git-branch: cancelled; still on main

items.title: How it works
items.text:
git for-each-ref prints tab-separated fields. Do not feed that to --input-format tsv: a commit subject may begin with ", which TSV parsing treats as a quote (input formats). jq builds JSON, which no character can break:

rows=$(git -C "$repo" for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate \
    --format='%(HEAD)%09%(refname:short)%09%(committerdate:relative)%09%(upstream:short)%09%(subject)' \
    refs/heads |
  jq -R -s -c 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {
      Current: .[0], Branch: .[1], Updated: .[2], Upstream: .[3], "Last commit": (.[4:] | join("\t"))
    })')

status=0
picked=$(nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --output-format json \
           --title "Switch branch" --timeout 120 <<<"$rows") || status=$?
case $status in
  0)   ;;
  2)   echo "pick-git-branch: cancelled; still on $(git -C "$repo" branch --show-current)" >&2
       exit 2 ;;
  124) echo "pick-git-branch: no branch chosen within 120 s" >&2
       exit 124 ;;
  *)   exit "$status" ;;   # the CLI already printed "nativehtmlkit: error[...]" on stderr
esac

branch=$(jq -r '.[0].Branch' <<<"$picked")
git -C "$repo" switch "$branch"

.[0].Branch is the branch name whatever characters it contains.

items.title: Variations
items.text:
Remote branches, then track the chosen one:

git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads refs/remotes |
  nativehtmlkit select --title 'Check out' --timeout 120

Delete merged branches: tick several with --multi, and git branch -d refuses anything that is not merged:

git branch --merged main --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -vx main |
  nativehtmlkit select --multi --title 'Delete merged branches' |
  xargs -r git branch -d --

Here feature/login, fix/typo and release/1.4 are merged into main. Submit prints, after ticking fix/typo:

fix/typo

The Windows counterpart is Pick a Git branch (Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/recipes/git-branch.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Test your scripts without a desktop (Linux)
items.text:
A script that opens a window is hard to test in CI: nobody clicks. This repository tests its examples and these pages headless; you can do the same for your own scripts.

NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS is a test-only switch, not part of the user contract of CLI 0.1.2, and may change in a later release. Never set it for real use.

The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).
path: Test your scripts without a desktop

items.title: What headless mode proves
items.text:
With NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1 the CLI starts the real Core host with --headless: the host runs the whole protocol (handshake, window, document, events, shutdown) without showing anything. With no input, every session ends by --timeout:

export NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1
printf 'a\nb\n' | nativehtmlkit select --timeout 0.5 2> /dev/null
echo "exit $?"

exit 124

Exit 124 with empty stdout shows that the input was parsed, the page was accepted by the host and the exit contract held. --diagnostics debug shows how the input was understood:

export NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1
printf 'a,b\n1,2\n3,4\n' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --timeout 0.5 --diagnostics debug 2>&1 |
  grep -o '"event":"session.started".*'

"event":"session.started","context":{"mode":"select","rows":2,"columns":2}}

Input errors still fail at once with exit 1, so a headless run also proves your data is acceptable (UTF-8, valid JSON, row, column and page limits):

export NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1
printf 'a,b\n1,2,3\n' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --timeout 0.5 2> /dev/null
echo "exit $?"

exit 1
path: Test your scripts without a desktop

items.title: Testing a whole script
items.text:
Your script probably sets its own --timeout (or none). Put a small wrapper named nativehtmlkit first on PATH that replaces the deadline with a short one and records each call; optionally it hands the script a recorded result instead, to test what happens after a Submit ("replay"):

real=$(command -v nativehtmlkit)
mkdir -p shim
cat > shim/nativehtmlkit <<SH
#!/usr/bin/env bash
args=(); skip=0
for a in "\$@"; do
  if ((skip)); then skip=0; continue; fi
  case \$a in --timeout) skip=1 ;; --timeout=*) ;; *) args+=("\$a") ;; esac
done
NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1 "$real" "\${args[@]}" --timeout 0.5 2>/dev/null
rc=\$?
echo "call: \${args[0]} -> \$rc" >> "$PWD/calls.log"
if [[ -n \${REPLAY:-} ]]; then printf '%s\n' "\$REPLAY"; exit 0; fi
exit \$rc
SH
chmod +x shim/nativehtmlkit
PATH=$PWD/shim:$PATH ./pick-timezone.sh; echo "headless: $?"
PATH=$PWD/shim:$PATH REPLAY=Asia/Tokyo ./pick-timezone.sh
cat calls.log

headless: 124
Asia/Tokyo
call: select -> 124
call: select -> 124

The first run proves the script's window opened and that it passes 124 on; the second, with a recorded result in the exact output format (output formats), what it does after a Submit.

This repository's harnesses do the same with more checks (rows x columns per call, document ready, no stdout on a non-zero status, no leftover processes):

scripts/test-examples.sh --cli /opt/nativehtmlkit-cli/nativehtmlkit           # the example scripts
python3 scripts/test-docs.py --cli /opt/nativehtmlkit-cli/nativehtmlkit       # every example on these pages

What this does not prove: anything that needs a person or a real screen (clicking, keyboard focus, layout, colours). The CLI release's GUI qualification covers those.

Windows: Test your scripts without a desktop (Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/recipes/headless-testing.md · edit the page there.
