items.title: Choose from JSON API output (Linux)
items.text:
Reshape a REST response with jq, let the user pick records, and use fields of the chosen records. Script: examples/pick-from-api.sh with the sample response examples/data/issues.json (GitHub's issue list format; needs jq).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

items.title: Run it
items.text:
With the saved response, or with a live one piped in (curl -fsS 'https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/issues?per_page=100' | ./pick-from-api.sh):

./pick-from-api.sh data/issues.json

The response has four entries; one is a pull request, so three issues are offered. The script prints the URLs of the chosen issues:

[{"#":42,"Title":"Window opens off-screen on a second monitor","Author":"ada","Labels":"bug, windows","Updated":"2026-11-12","url":"https://example.invalid/issues/42"},{"#":39,"Title":"Příliš žluťoučký kůň: Unicode in titles & \"quotes\"","Author":"zoë","Labels":"i18n","Updated":"2026-11-01","url":"https://example.invalid/issues/39"}]

https://example.invalid/issues/42
https://example.invalid/issues/39

items.title: How it works
items.text:
The CLI shows one column per top-level key and nested values as compact JSON, so flatten first, and keep the field you need afterwards (url) even if it is dull to look at:

jq -c '[.[] | select(has("pull_request") | not) | {
         "#": .number, Title: .title, Author: .user.login,
         Labels: ([.labels[].name] | join(", ")), Updated: .updated_at[:10], url: .html_url
       }]' data/issues.json |
  nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json --output-format json --title 'Open issues' |
  jq -r '.[].url'

In this one-line form a Cancel just produces no output; the script checks the status and exits 2 or 124 instead. What comes back is the array of the chosen records exactly as they went in: key order, numbers (42, not 42.0) and Unicode are kept:

jq -c '[.[] | select(has("pull_request") | not) | {
         "#": .number, Title: .title, Author: .user.login,
         Labels: ([.labels[].name] | join(", ")), Updated: .updated_at[:10], url: .html_url
       }]' data/issues.json |
  nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json --output-format json --title 'Open issues'

[{"#":41,"Title":"Document the <form> limits","Author":"grace","Labels":"docs","Updated":"2026-11-10","url":"https://example.invalid/issues/41"}]

items.title: Variations
items.text:
A one-column list of strings and lines output, for example to open the chosen URLs:

jq -c '[.[].html_url]' data/issues.json |
  nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json --output-format lines |
  xargs -r -n1 echo open

Large responses: the CLI refuses more than 2,000 rows or 32 columns rather than cutting them, so page or filter in jq (.[:2000], a smaller object).

Windows: Choose from JSON API output (Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/recipes/json-api.md · edit the page there.

items.title: View logs (Linux)
items.text:
Show a text log in a scrolling, wrapping pane, or JSON lines as a table. view has no result: closing it exits 0. Script: examples/view-logs.sh (needs tail, perl), samples data/app.log and data/app.ndjson.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

items.title: Plain text
items.text:
./view-logs.sh data/app.log

The script shows the last 1,000 lines (LINES_SHOWN changes that), each cut to 400 characters. Markup in log lines is shown literally (<script> stays text). From stdin:

for i in $(seq 3000); do printf 'line %d: %0700d\n' "$i" 0; done | ./view-logs.sh -

Two limits matter for logs (limits):

  • at most 2,000 lines; more is an error, not a truncation, so use tail -n;
  • the page must stay under 1 MiB: 2,000 lines of 500 characters fit, 2,000 of 600 do not. Shorten by characters (perl -CSD as below), not with cut -c, which counts bytes and could split a UTF-8 character; invalid UTF-8 is refused.
tail -n 1000 data/app.log | perl -CSD -pe 's/^(.{400}).+/$1.../' | nativehtmlkit view --title 'app.log'

The system journal (journalctl -n counts entries, and one entry can span lines, so cut lines too):

journalctl -n 500 --no-pager | tail -n 2000 | ./view-logs.sh -

items.title: JSON lines
items.text:
./view-logs.sh data/app.ndjson

Columns are the union of all keys in order of first appearance (at most 32); nested objects appear as compact JSON. Never shorten JSON lines (a cut line is invalid JSON); choose columns with jq instead:

tail -n 1000 data/app.ndjson | jq -c '{time, level, msg}' | nativehtmlkit view --input-format ndjson --title 'app.ndjson'

Only warnings and errors:

jq -c 'select(.level != "info") | {time, level, msg}' data/app.ndjson | nativehtmlkit view --input-format ndjson

items.title: Keep the script going
items.text:
view blocks until the window is closed. Exit 0 (closed) and 124 (--timeout) both mean "done looking":

nativehtmlkit view --timeout 300 --title 'Build log' < data/app.log || [[ $? -eq 124 ]] || exit 1
echo 'next step'

next step

To show a log and continue at once, start the viewer in the background:

nativehtmlkit view --title 'Build log' < data/app.log &
viewer=$!
echo 'building...'
wait "$viewer"

Windows (text files and the Windows event log): View logs (Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/recipes/logs.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Multi-select in pipelines and xargs (Linux)
items.text:
select --multi writes one line per chosen row, in input order, and nothing at all on Cancel or a timeout. That makes it a filter stage in a pipeline. Script: examples/grep-selected.sh (GNU find and xargs).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

items.title: Search only the files you tick
items.text:
./grep-selected.sh 'nativehtmlkit view' .

The window lists the files under . (at most 2,000). Suppose the user ticks two scripts:

./csv-report.sh
./view-logs.sh

./csv-report.sh:20:  exec nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --title "${title:0:128}" <"$report"
./view-logs.sh:28:      nativehtmlkit view --input-format ndjson --title "Log: ${name:0:100}" ;;
./view-logs.sh:33:      nativehtmlkit view --title "Log: ${name:0:100}" ;;

After Cancel the script exits 2 and grep never runs:



grep-selected: cancelled

items.title: The rules that keep such pipelines safe
items.text:
printf 'first\n' > one.log; printf 'second\n' > two.log
ls *.log | nativehtmlkit select --multi --title 'Compress' | xargs -r -d '\n' gzip --
ls *.gz 2>/dev/null | wc -l

0
  • xargs -r: run nothing when nothing was chosen (nothing was compressed above).
  • xargs -d '\n' (GNU): split on newlines only, so spaces and quotes in names survive. Names containing newlines cannot be represented in lines; use JSON and NUL separators (jq -j '.[].Path + "\u0000"' | xargs -0 ..., see delete files).
  • head -n 2000 before the CLI: more than 2,000 rows is an error, not a truncation.
  • -- before the arguments, so a name that starts with - is not an option.
  • The CLI's own status is in PIPESTATUS, not $?:
find . -type f -name '*.sh' | sort | head -n 2000 |
  nativehtmlkit select --multi --title 'Lint' |
  xargs -r -d '\n' bash -n --
status=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")      # find, sort, head, nativehtmlkit, xargs
[[ ${status[3]} -eq 0 ]] || exit "${status[3]}"

items.title: Rows with several fields
items.text:
Choose an output format that keeps the fields apart. CSV in, one column of the chosen rows out, one ssh per host:

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json < data/servers.csv | jq -r '.[].host' |
  xargs -r -d '\n' -I{} ssh -o BatchMode=yes {} uptime

ndjson gives one JSON object per line, handy for while read loops:

nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format ndjson < data/servers.csv |
  while IFS= read -r row; do
    echo "would restart $(jq -r .role <<<"$row") on $(jq -r .host <<<"$row")"
  done

{"host":"api-01","role":"backend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"8","memory_gib":"32","status":"healthy","notes":""}

would restart backend on api-01

Windows: Multi-select in pipelines (Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/recipes/pipelines.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Choose processes to signal (Linux)
items.text:
Pick processes in a table, then pick the signal to send them. Script: examples/kill-process.sh (needs procps ps, awk, jq).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).

items.title: Run it
items.text:
Start a harmless process to practise on, then offer only the processes whose command line contains sleep 300:

sleep 300 & sleeper=$!
./kill-process.sh 'sleep 300'
status=$?
kill "$sleeper"
exit "$status"

The table shows PID, User, CPU %, Mem %, Running and Command. After Submit a second window offers TERM, INT and KILL; only then is the signal sent. On Cancel or a timeout nothing is signalled:

kill-process: nothing signalled

No match: the script exits 0 without a window:

./kill-process.sh 'no-such-process-name-42'

kill-process: no process matches 'no-such-process-name-42'

items.title: How it works
items.text:
ps output is aligned by spaces and the command line contains spaces, so the script turns it into CSV, quoting the free-text field and doubling any " in it as CSV requires. It takes the snapshot first and filters afterwards, so the filter does not list itself:

listing=$(ps -eo pid=,user=,pcpu=,pmem=,etime=,args= --sort=-pcpu)
rows=$(awk -v filter="$filter" -v self=$$ '
    BEGIN { print "PID,User,CPU %,Mem %,Running,Command" }
    $1 == self || n >= 500 { next }
    {
      cmd = $6; for (i = 7; i <= NF; i++) cmd = cmd " " $i
      if (filter != "" && index(cmd, filter) == 0) next
      if (length(cmd) > 160) cmd = substr(cmd, 1, 157) "..."
      gsub(/"/, "\"\"", cmd)
      printf "%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,\"%s\"\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5, cmd; n++
    }' <<<"$listing")

status=0
picked=$(nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json \
           --title "Processes to signal" <<<"$rows") || status=$?
[[ $status -eq 0 ]] || { echo "kill-process: nothing signalled" >&2; exit "$status"; }
mapfile -t pids < <(jq -r '.[].PID' <<<"$picked")

--output-format json turns each chosen CSV row into an object keyed by the header, so .[].PID reads the column by name. The signal is a second, single-choice select whose first word is the signal name:

printf 'TERM  - ask the process to exit\nINT   - like Ctrl+C\nKILL  - force, cannot be caught\n' |
  nativehtmlkit select --title 'Signal for 2 process(es)'

TERM  - ask the process to exit

The script keeps ${signal%% *} (TERM) and runs kill -s TERM -- PID....

items.title: A quick one-liner
items.text:
pgrep -a already prints PID command; cut keeps the PID of each chosen line:

sleep 301 & sleeper=$!
pgrep -a -f 'sleep 301' | nativehtmlkit select --multi --title 'Stop' | cut -d' ' -f1 | xargs -r kill
status=${PIPESTATUS[1]}
kill "$sleeper"
exit "$status"

Windows: Choose processes to stop (Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/linux/recipes/processes.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Choose a time zone in a light theme (Linux)
items.text:
Choose one value from a long list in a window restyled with --css, and use it in the next command. Script: examples/pick-timezone.sh with css/light.css (needs timedatectl or /usr/share/zoneinfo).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples directory of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.py (how).
path: Choose a time zone in a light theme

items.title: Run it
items.text:
./pick-timezone.sh

The list holds every zone timedatectl list-timezones knows (about 600; at most the first 2,000 are offered). Use the choice for one command:

zone=$(./pick-timezone.sh) && TZ=$zone date '+%H:%M in '"$zone"
echo "status $?"

Asia/Tokyo
path: Choose a time zone in a light theme

items.title: How it works
items.text:
The whole script is a list and one select with a style sheet:

printf '%s\n' Europe/Prague Europe/London America/New_York Asia/Tokyo |
  nativehtmlkit select --title 'Time zone' --css css/light.css

Asia/Tokyo

css/light.css overrides the page's colour custom properties and a few fixed colours (CSS and forms). Single choice is the default, so exactly one zone comes back.

items.title: Command reference
items.text:
Reference for nativehtmlkit 0.1.2 (alias nhk), built for and bundled with Core host 1.0.3. Everything here was taken from the released binary's --help, from the source of the release commit, and checked against the released Linux and Windows archives (see Verification).

nativehtmlkit [GLOBAL OPTIONS] <COMMAND> [COMMAND OPTIONS]
Command Purpose stdin stdout on success Page select choose one row (or several with --multi) from piped records records, required, not a terminal the chosen rows, in input order select view show piped records read-only records, required, not a terminal nothing view form show a trusted HTML form and return its values not read one JSON object {"entries":[...]} form doctor show which Core host would be used and its version not read three lines of text doctor help [COMMAND] print help not read help text Topic Page Options every command accepts (--host, --timeout, --rpc-timeout, ...) Global options lines, csv, tsv, json, ndjson: exact parsing rules Input formats same, lines, csv, tsv, json, ndjson: exact output bytes Output formats Exit statuses, the error[<code>] line, stdout/stderr discipline Exit status and errors Size limits (8 MiB, 2,000 rows, 32 columns, 1 MiB page, 65,536 nodes, 256 KiB files) Limits Environment variables Environment --diagnostics records on stderr Diagnostics The generated page (element ids and classes) for --css and --html authors Page structure

items.title: Contract in one table
items.text:
Outcome Exit stdout stderr Submitted (select, form) or viewer closed (view) 0 the result (nothing for view) host log only Error: bad input or option, host missing, host failure or hang 1 empty one line nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: <text> (usage errors: the usual error: ... help text) Cancel button, or window closed without submitting 2 empty nothing extra --timeout expired before a decision 124 empty nativehtmlkit: no decision before the --timeout deadline; the window was closed SIGINT / Ctrl+C 130 empty SIGTERM 143 empty SIGHUP 129 empty

--help, -h, --version, -V exit 0. The result is written in one piece after the window has closed, never partially, and never after an error or an interruption.

items.title: Usage by operating system
items.text:
This reference is the exact, OS-neutral specification. Every command, option, format and exit status is shown with verified examples in the shell of each OS:

Linux (bash) Windows (PowerShell 5.1 / 7, cmd.exe) Start here: install, first command Linux Windows select select select view view view form form form doctor, help, --version doctor doctor Input formats input formats input formats Output formats output formats output formats Exit codes in scripts exit codes exit codes Environment, diagnostics environment environment --css, --html CSS and forms CSS and forms Troubleshooting troubleshooting troubleshooting Recipes recipes recipes Tutorials project picker, branch picker project picker, branch picker

Runnable scripts: example catalogue (catalog.toml). Internals: architecture.

items.title: Verification
items.text:
The statements in this reference that concern input parsing, limits, option validation, exit statuses and the stderr lines are asserted by scripts/test-examples.sh against the released nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-linux-x64 archive with its bundled Core 1.0.3 host, headless (NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1). Every example of the Linux and Windows sections is run by scripts/test-docs.py (bash, Linux archive) and scripts/test-docs.ps1 (Windows PowerShell 5.1 with the Windows archive, and PowerShell 7), which also check the exact output shown for a Submit against the release's own formatting code. The GUI behaviour (selection order, Cancel, window close, form validation, keyboard use, Ctrl+C) is asserted by the release's GUI qualification on KDE Plasma Wayland and Windows Server 2022 (tests/gui/, 49/49 per platform). See QUALIFICATION.md.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/REFERENCE.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Diagnostics
items.text: --diagnostics off|normal|debug|trace (or NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS; the flag wins) sets the level of the CLI's own records on stderr. When given as a flag it is also exported to the Core host, which has its own, separate log on the same stderr.

items.title: Record format
items.text:
One JSON object per line, schema version 1:

{"schema_version":1,"timestamp":"2026-11-16T14:14:45.106Z","session_id":"nhk-2322069-18e88c17ba30360d","component":"nativehtmlkit-cli","role":"backend","pid":2322075,"level":"debug","event":"rpc.completed","request_id":"nhk-4","operation":"document.load","duration_ms":41}
Member Always Meaning schema_version yes 1 timestamp yes UTC, ISO 8601 with milliseconds session_id yes correlation id (environment); generated as nhk-<pid>-<hex> unless inherited component yes nativehtmlkit-cli role yes launcher (the process you started) or backend (the process the host started for the session; its records are written to a private file and relayed to stderr by the launcher, at most 1 MiB per session) pid yes process id of that role level yes the record's level event yes event name, below request_id, operation, duration_ms, error_code, context when known request correlation (nhk-1, nhk-2, ...), protocol method, timing, the stable error[<code>], small numeric or fixed-text details

Records can only contain fixed event names, identifier-shaped strings, numbers and booleans. They never contain stdin data, selections, form values, HTML, titles, paths or the launch token. The host's records are a separate channel ("target":"nativehtmlkit_host..."); review them before sharing a log.

items.title: Levels and events
items.text: Level Adds off no CLI records normal (default) failures only: session.failed, backend.failed, rpc.timeout, rpc.failed, host.watchdog, host.killed, session_id.replaced, diagnostics.dropped, and host.notifications_dropped (the host discarded window/document events because the backend was not reading: a click may have been lost). session.failed for usage and input errors appears only at debug. debug lifecycle and timings: session.started (context.mode, rows, columns), host.spawned, backend.started, handshake.completed (context.host_version), rpc.completed, window.ready, host.request, submit.rejected (context.reason: empty_selection or invalid_form), submit.accepted, submit.superseded_by_shutdown, host.already_shutting_down, user.cancelled, deadline.expired, session.shutdown, host.exited, session.completed (context.outcome: submitted, viewed, cancelled, deadline, interrupted, terminated, hangup; context.exit_code) trace every request start (rpc.started), every host notification (event.received), every liveness probe answer (liveness.ok)

items.title: Using it
items.text:
Reading the records, a session timeline and correlation ids, with verified examples: Linux, Windows.

A debug session that reached the window and timed out looks like this (CLI records only): session.started -> host.spawned -> backend.started -> rpc.completed for host.hello, host.diagnostics, window.create, document.load, app.ready -> window.ready -> deadline.expired -> host.request (app.before_quit) -> rpc.completed (app.request_quit) -> session.shutdown -> host.exited -> session.completed (deadline, 124).

See also troubleshooting (Linux, Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/diagnostics.md · edit the page there.

items.title: nativehtmlkit doctor
items.text:
Report which Core host executable the CLI would use, and that it starts.

nativehtmlkit doctor [--host <PATH>]

doctor finds the host exactly as every other command does (host discovery), runs it once with --version (stdin closed, at most 10 seconds) and prints three lines to stdout:

NativeHTMLKit CLI 0.1.2
Core host: /opt/nativehtmlkit-cli/nativehtmlkit-host
nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3

The third line is the host's own --version output. No window is opened and no session is started; the other global options are accepted and ignored.

Situation Exit stderr host found, --version succeeded 0 no host found anywhere 1 nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: NativeHTMLKit Core host not found. Install a qualified release beside the CLI or set NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY. --host / NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY names no regular file 1 nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: <path> the file cannot be started (e.g. not executable) 1 nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: cannot start the Core host (<reason>) it ran but failed or printed nothing 1 nativehtmlkit: error[host.failed]: Core host version check failed with <status> it did not exit within 10 s (it is killed) 1 nativehtmlkit: error[host.failed]: the Core host did not answer --version in time (after 10000 ms)

Use it first when a command reports host.not_found, and to confirm which host a pinned installation uses. Examples: Linux, Windows.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/doctor.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
Variable Read by Effect NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY CLI host executable to use when --host is not given; an empty value is ignored (host discovery) NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS CLI and host diagnostics level when --diagnostics is not given: off, normal, debug, trace (case-insensitive, surrounding spaces ignored); anything else means normal. The host reads the same variable. NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID CLI, passed to the host correlation id put into every CLI record (session_id) and every host record (diagnostic_session_id). Accepted when it is 1-128 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : - (after trimming spaces); otherwise a fresh id is generated and a session_id.replaced record is written. PATH CLI last step of host discovery TMPDIR (Unix), TMP/TEMP (Windows) CLI where the private session directory nativehtmlkit-cli-* is created

Set by the CLI for the host process (not for you to set):

Variable Value NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID the session id in use NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS the level given with --diagnostics, only when the flag was given

The Core host passes wire-v1 launch variables (UI4ME_ENDPOINT, UI4ME_TOKEN, UI4ME_APP_ID, UI4ME_PROTOCOL_VERSION; the names are fixed by protocol v1) to the CLI's internal backend, which removes them from its environment before doing anything else.

items.title: Test-only switches
items.text:
Not part of the user contract; they may change without notice:

Variable Effect NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS any value: start the host with --headless, so the whole protocol runs without a window. Nobody can click, so every session ends by --timeout (124), Ctrl+C or an error. Used by scripts/test-examples.sh and the release qualification. NATIVEHTMLKIT_WATCHDOG_GRACE_MS shortens the launcher watchdog margins (default 5000 ms)

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/environment.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Exit statuses
items.text:
Status Meaning stdout 0 select/form: submitted; view: closed; doctor, --help, --version: done the result (empty for view) 1 any error: usage, input, host not found, host failure or hang, protocol violation, output write failure empty 2 Cancel, or the window was closed without submitting (select, form) empty 124 --timeout passed before a decision empty 130 interrupted by SIGINT / Ctrl+C empty 143 SIGTERM empty 129 SIGHUP empty

Notes:

  • Usage errors (unknown option, invalid value, missing --html) exit 1, not clap's usual 2, so that 2 always means the user cancelled.
  • view has no Cancel: closing it is exit 0.
  • On 143 and 129 the window is closed at once; on 130 the CLI gives the host up to 3 s to end by itself (a terminal Ctrl+C reaches the whole process group), then stops it.
  • Exit statuses 124/130/143/129 never come with a result, even if the user had just clicked Submit.

items.title: stdout and stderr
items.text:
• stdout carries only the result, written once after the window has closed. Never parse stderr for results.
  • stderr is shared by the CLI and the Core host:
  • the host's own JSON log records (one object per line, "target":"nativehtmlkit_host...");
  • the CLI's diagnostic records ("component":"nativehtmlkit-cli"), as chosen by --diagnostics (diagnostics);
  • on failure exactly one human line nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: <message>;
  • on exit 124 the line nativehtmlkit: no decision before the --timeout deadline; the window was closed;
  • clap's error: ... text for usage errors.
  • Every line is written with a single write, so lines from the CLI and the host cannot be interleaved inside one another.
  • Error lines never quote stdin data, selections, form values, host-authored messages or the launch credential.

items.title: The error line
items.text:
nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: <message>[ (<details>)]

<details> is a comma-separated list of what is known: operation <protocol method>, request <id>, host code <n>, after <n> ms, remote outcome unknown. Example:

nativehtmlkit: error[rpc.timeout]: the Core host did not answer the request in time (operation document.load, request nhk-4, after 30000 ms, remote outcome unknown)

The <code> is stable and meant for scripts:

Code Meaning usage.invalid an option value clap accepted but the CLI rejects (--title empty, over 128 characters, or with control characters) input.invalid stdin, the --html or the --css file cannot be used: terminal stdin, not UTF-8, too large, parse error, limits, missing nhk-form output.failed the result could not be encoded (lines and a value with a newline) or written to stdout host.not_found no Core host executable, or it cannot be started host.startup_timeout the host did not get the window ready within --startup-timeout (+5 s) host.unresponsive the window was open but the host stopped answering liveness probes host.shutdown_timeout the host accepted the quit request, or the session ended, but the host did not exit host.failed the host process ended unsuccessfully without a more specific cause; doctor's version check failed backend.unresponsive the CLI's own backend process stopped reporting progress rpc.timeout a request got no response within --rpc-timeout rpc.rejected the host answered a request with a JSON-RPC error (host code N) transport.connect_failed the local connection to the host could not be made transport.disconnected the connection ended (the host exited or closed it) protocol.truncated_frame, protocol.invalid_frame, protocol.violation, protocol.handshake_failed the host broke the wire-v1 contract, or the launch credentials were not accepted document.error the host reported a renderer/document error session.invalid the CLI's private session files are missing or inconsistent internal unclassified: a CLI defect, please report it

A usage error printed by the argument parser has no code; it looks like this and also exits 1:

error: unexpected argument '--bogus' found

Usage: nativehtmlkit select [OPTIONS]

For more information, try '--help'.

items.title: Handling it in scripts
items.text:
Capturing the status, helpers that stop on Cancel, the CLI inside a pipeline, writing files only after success, signals: Linux (bash), Windows (PowerShell, cmd.exe).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/exit-status.md · edit the page there.

items.title: nativehtmlkit form
items.text:
Show a trusted HTML form fragment and print its values as JSON when the user submits.

nativehtmlkit form [OPTIONS] --html <HTML>
Option Default Meaning --html <PATH> required trusted UTF-8 HTML fragment, at most 256 KiB, containing <form id="nhk-form"> --title <TITLE> Input form 1-128 characters, no control characters, shown as text --css <PATH> none trusted UTF-8 CSS file, at most 256 KiB global options global options

stdin is not read; form has no --input-format/--output-format.

items.title: The fragment
items.text:
• The file is inserted as-is into the page body, after the heading and before an error line and the buttons Cancel and Submit that the CLI adds itself (page structure). It is trusted markup: never paste untrusted text into it without HTML-escaping it first (bash: jq -rn --arg s "$v" '$s|@html', PowerShell: [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($v)).
  • It must contain the form element with id nhk-form. Before a window opens the CLI checks, after removing all whitespace, that the text contains id="nhk-form", id='nhk-form' or id=nhk-form; otherwise: error[input.invalid]: --html must contain <form id="nhk-form"> with the controls to submit, exit 1. (This is a text check, not an HTML parse.)
  • Put the controls to submit inside that form and give each a name. Do not add your own submit button: only the CLI's Submit button ends the session.
  • The file must be valid UTF-8 (error[input.invalid]: <path> is not UTF-8: ...), readable (error[input.invalid]: read <path>: ...) and at most 256 KiB (custom HTML or CSS file exceeds 256 KiB). Core runs no scripts; there is no JavaScript.

items.title: Submit, validation and the result
items.text:
Submit asks Core to check the form's HTML constraints (check_validity on nhk-form). Core 1.0.3 implements required (text, select, checkbox, radio group), minlength, maxlength, pattern (whole-value match), type="email", type="url", type="number" with min/max/step, and the date/time input types with min/max. Disabled, read-only and hidden controls are not validated.

  • Any constraint fails: the window stays open and shows Some required fields are invalid.
  • All valid: the window closes and stdout receives one line:
{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"project","value":"Demo App"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"development"},{"kind":"text","name":"confirm","value":"yes"}]}

That line is the exact result the release's GUI qualification asserts for examples/sample-form.html after typing Demo App, keeping the default environment and ticking the checkbox.

entries are Core's successful controls in document order, as HTML form submission defines them: one entry per named, enabled control that contributes a value. A checkbox or radio button that is not checked has no entry, a checked one without a value attribute reports "on"; a <select multiple> contributes one entry per selected option; buttons contribute nothing; names may repeat. Each entry is an object with kind ("text" for ordinary controls), name and value. A file input produces {"kind":"file","name":...,"path":...,"filename":...} instead ("path":null,"filename":"" when no file was chosen). Parse the line as JSON; do not rely on key order.

Outcome Exit stdout Submitted, form valid 0 {"entries":[...]} and a newline Cancel or window closed 2 empty --timeout expired 124 empty Error (missing/invalid file, no nhk-form, host failure) 1 empty

items.title: Reading the result
items.text:
Parse the line as JSON and look entries up by name: Linux (bash, jq), Windows (PowerShell, ConvertFrom-Json). Writing and generating forms safely: CSS and forms (Linux, Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/form.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Global options
items.text:
These options are accepted by every command, before or after the command name (nativehtmlkit --timeout 60 select and nativehtmlkit select --timeout 60 are the same). Each may be given once; a repeated option is a usage error (exit 1).

Option Value Default Meaning --host <PATH> path discovery, below the Core host executable to use --diagnostics <LEVEL> off, normal, debug, trace $NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS, else normal structured records on stderr for the CLI, and exported to the host (diagnostics) --timeout <SECONDS> 0.01-86400 none: wait indefinitely the user's deadline: when it passes without Submit/Cancel/Close, the window is closed, exit 124 --rpc-timeout <SECONDS> 0.01-86400 30 longest wait for the host to answer one request, finish a frame it started, or accept a write --liveness-interval <SECONDS> 0-86400 5 idle time between liveness probes while the window is open; 0 disables probing --startup-timeout <SECONDS> 0.01-86400 15 longest wait from starting the host until the window is ready -h, --help print help (exit 0); -h prints a summary -V, --version print nativehtmlkit 0.1.2 (exit 0)

items.title: Seconds
items.text:
A value is a decimal number of seconds, fractions allowed (0.5, 90, 1e2), surrounding spaces ignored. Out of range or not a number is a usage error, exit 1:

error: invalid value '0' for '--timeout <SECONDS>': expected at least 0.01 seconds
error: invalid value '90000' for '--timeout <SECONDS>': expected a number of seconds between 0 and 86400

items.title: --timeout: waiting for a person
items.text:
There is no default limit on how long a person may look at a window. --timeout adds one. It is counted from the moment the window is ready (document loaded), not from the start of the command. When it passes:

  1. the CLI asks the host to close the window,
  2. writes nativehtmlkit: no decision before the --timeout deadline; the window was closed to stderr,
  3. exits 124 with empty stdout (the convention of coreutils timeout).

A submit that was accepted before the deadline wins; nothing is written after the deadline.

items.title: Host watchdogs: --rpc-timeout, --liveness-interval, --startup-timeout
items.text:
These bound the host, not the person. They exist so a pipeline never hangs on a host that has stopped working, while a slow user never trips them:

  • While the window is idle, the CLI's backend asks the host host.diagnostics every --liveness-interval seconds. Any answer proves the host is alive. A probe may take up to 2 x --rpc-timeout (a busy host, a native modal loop); with the defaults a hung host is therefore reported about 65 s after it stopped answering, as error[host.unresponsive] (exit 1), and the host is stopped.
  • Every other request must be answered within --rpc-timeout, or the session fails with error[rpc.timeout] (remote outcome unknown).
  • The host must have the window ready within --startup-timeout (the launcher adds a 5 s margin): otherwise error[host.startup_timeout]. The value is also given to the host as its own backend start-up limit; extremely small values make the host itself give up (error[host.failed]).
  • With --liveness-interval 0 there is no probing: a host that hangs while the window is idle is only noticed at the next request (for example when the user clicks Submit).

All waits count time actually spent waiting, so a suspended laptop is not mistaken for a hung host. See architecture for the full lifecycle.

items.title: Host discovery
items.text:
The first match wins:

  1. --host <PATH>
  2. NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY (ignored when set to an empty string)
  3. nativehtmlkit-host (nativehtmlkit-host.exe on Windows) in the directory of the running CLI executable (symbolic links resolved, so the nhk alias finds it too)
  4. the same file name in each PATH directory, in order

1 and 2 must name an existing regular file (error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: <path>); 3 and 4 are skipped when absent. Nothing found: error[host.not_found]: NativeHTMLKit Core host not found. Install a qualified release beside the CLI or set NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY. Release archives contain the exact host the CLI was qualified with next to the CLI, so step 3 finds it; the override is for development. nativehtmlkit doctor shows the result.

The CLI 0.1.2 is qualified with Core host 1.0.3 only. An older 1.0.x host speaks the same protocol version and runs, but that combination is not qualified.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/global-options.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Input formats
items.text:
select and view read all of stdin, then parse it with --input-format (default lines). Common rules for every format:

  • stdin must not be a terminal; at most 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes) is read; it must be UTF-8 (error[input.invalid]: stdin must contain UTF-8; use ConvertTo-Json or UTF-8 output: invalid utf-8 sequence ...).
  • At most 2,000 rows and 32 columns; the generated page must also fit the host's 1 MiB / 65,536-node limits (limits).
  • Each row keeps its original value (a string for lines, an object of strings for csv/tsv, the JSON value itself for json/ndjson) and a list of display cells. The table shows the cells, escaped as text; the output formats write values or cells (output formats).
  • Every error exits 1 with nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: <message> before a window opens. Messages quote positions, never data.

items.title: lines (default)
items.text:
Rule Detail Row boundary ; a before it is removed ( files work) Last line a final line without is a row; a final does not create an empty row Empty lines are rows (an empty or whitespace-only line is a selectable row) Columns one, named Value Value the line text, unchanged (no trimming) Byte-order mark not removed: it becomes part of the first line

printf 'a b last' gives 4 rows: a, (empty), b, last.

items.title: csv and tsv
items.text:
RFC 4180-style parsing with , (csv) or a tab (tsv) as delimiter:

Rule Detail Header the first record names the columns, unless --no-headers (then column_1 ... column_N, N from the first record) Quoting " quotes a field; inside quotes the delimiter and line breaks are data and "" is one ". This also applies to TSV: a field that starts with " is parsed as quoted, so its quotes are removed ("quoted" start becomes quoted start), and a quote that is never closed swallows the following delimiters and lines (two data lines can become one row; "x<TAB>y with too few fields is an error). A " inside an unquoted field is data (say "hi" is fine). Record boundary \n or \r\n outside quotes Blank lines skipped Field count every record must have as many fields as the first one: malformed CSV/TSV record: CSV error: record 1 (line: 2, byte: 4): found record with 3 fields, but the previous record has 2 fields Header names must be unique (duplicate CSV/TSV column names cannot be represented as JSON objects); an empty name is allowed Empty input expected at least one header column (also for view) Header only zero rows: select refuses it (no selectable input rows), view shows an empty table Byte-order mark a UTF-8 BOM before the header is ignored Other delimiters not supported: a;b is one column named a;b Value / cells value: object {header: field} of strings; cells: the fields Limits more than 2,000 records: too many records; more than 32 columns: too many columns

items.title: json
items.text:
Rule Detail Document exactly one JSON document; trailing content is an error (invalid JSON input: trailing characters at line 1 column 5) Array each element is a row Any other value (object, string, number, ...) is a single row Empty or whitespace-only stdin zero rows (select refuses it, view shows an empty viewer); [] is the same Byte-order mark not accepted: invalid JSON input: expected value at line 1 column 1 Columns, all rows objects the union of keys, in order of first appearance across rows; a row without a key shows an empty cell Columns, otherwise one column Value (scalars, arrays, or arrays mixing objects and other values) Cells strings as-is; null as an empty cell; numbers and booleans as JSON text; arrays and objects as compact JSON Value the element exactly as given: key order and number text (big integers, 2.50) are kept Limits more than 2,000 rows: 2001 rows exceeds the 2000-row initial GUI limit; more than 32 distinct keys: 33 columns exceeds the 32-column limit

Note: in an array that mixes objects and non-objects, the single Value column shows each object's "Value" member, which is usually absent, so those rows look empty. Use arrays of one kind.

items.title: ndjson
items.text:
One JSON document per line (JSON Lines):

Rule Detail Lines each non-blank line is parsed as one JSON value; whitespace-only lines are skipped Pretty-printed JSON not supported: a value must fit on one line (invalid NDJSON line 1: EOF while parsing an object at line 1 column 1) Errors name the 1-based physical line: invalid NDJSON line 2: ... A line holding an array is one row (its value is the array) Columns, cells, values as for json Limits more than 2,000 rows: too many NDJSON rows; more than 32 keys as for json

items.title: Choosing a format
items.text:
Source Use plain names, paths, one item per line lines spreadsheet exports, --format csv of a tool csv docker ps --format '{{json .}}', kubectl ... -o json items via jq -c '.items[]', log files in JSON Lines ndjson jq output, ConvertTo-Json, REST responses json fields that may contain tabs or quotes json/ndjson (build with jq -R/ConvertTo-Json), not tsv

PowerShell: send objects as JSON (Select-Object ... | ConvertTo-Json | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json), choosing the properties first: a raw object easily has more than 32 properties. In Windows PowerShell 5.1 set $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false) first; [Text.Encoding]::UTF8 would prepend a BOM, which the json format rejects (Windows input formats).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/input-formats.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
All limits are checked before a host process or a window exists; exceeding one exits 1 with error[input.invalid] (or usage.invalid for the title) and empty stdout.

Limit Value Applies to Message stdin size 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes) select, view input exceeds 8 MiB; use a prefiltered pipeline or smaller selection rows 2,000 select, view 2001 rows exceeds the 2000-row initial GUI limit (lines, json); too many records (csv/tsv); too many NDJSON rows columns 32 select, view too many columns (csv/tsv); 33 columns exceeds the 32-column limit (json/ndjson) --html / --css file 256 KiB (262,144 bytes), UTF-8 form, every --css custom HTML or CSS file exceeds 256 KiB --title 1-128 characters, no control characters (tab, newline, ...) all error[usage.invalid]: --title must be nonempty, at most 128 characters, with no control characters generated page 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes) of HTML all input is too large to display: the generated page is N bytes, the host accepts 1048576 (1 MiB); prefilter the input document nodes 65,536 select, view tables input is too large to display: R rows x C columns need about N document nodes, the host accepts 65536; at this width at most M rows fit (prefilter the input or select fewer columns)

items.title: Document nodes
items.text:
The host refuses documents with more than 65,536 nodes (elements and text nodes). The CLI counts the nodes of its generated page the way the page is built:

select table:  48 + 2 x (columns + 1) + rows x (3 + 2 x columns)
view table:    48 + 2 x columns       + rows x (1 + 2 x columns)

(an empty cell needs one node less). Some sizes that fit and do not fit:

Rows x columns select view (table) 2,000 x 14 fits fits 1,870 x 16 fits fits 1,871 x 16 refused ("at most 1870 rows fit") fits 976 x 32 fits fits 1,000 x 32 refused fits 2,000 x 32 refused refused

view of lines input is one text block, not a table: only the 1 MiB page limit applies. A form page is not counted; the host's own limits apply to your fragment.

items.title: The 1 MiB page
items.text: The page contains the built-in style sheet (about 1.3 KB), your --css, the escaped title and every escaped cell. Escaping grows &, <, >, ", ' to 4-5 bytes each. In practice 2,000 lines of 500 characters still fit in a view; 2,000 lines of 600 do not. Shorten long lines before piping them in (viewing logs: Linux, Windows).

items.title: No limit
items.text:
• How long a person may take: unlimited unless --timeout is given.
  • Cell length: only the page limit.
  • The number of concurrent CLI windows: each invocation is its own host session.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/limits.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Output formats
items.text:
What select writes to stdout after a successful Submit (exit 0). view never writes to stdout; form always writes one JSON line (form). On every other exit status stdout is empty.

Common rules:

  • The chosen rows are written in input order, whatever order they were ticked in.
  • The whole result is encoded first and written in one piece, then stdout is flushed; a failed write is error[output.failed], exit 1.
  • Output is UTF-8; every format ends with a newline.
  • With --allow-empty and nothing ticked: lines, ndjson write nothing; json writes [] and a newline; csv/tsv write the header line only.

--output-format same (the default) means: the format named by --input-format.

items.title: lines
items.text:
One line per chosen row, each ending in \n:

  • a lines row: the original line text;
  • any other row whose value is a string (a JSON string, an NDJSON string line): that string;
  • any other row: its display cells joined with a tab (a CSV row web-01,frontend becomes web-01<TAB>frontend; a JSON object row its cell texts in column order).

If a value to be written contains \n or \r, nothing is written and the command fails: error[output.failed]: selected value contains newline: use --output-format json or ndjson, exit 1. A line therefore never turns into two records downstream.

items.title: json
items.text:
One JSON array of the chosen rows' values, on one line:

Input Element written lines the line as a JSON string csv/tsv an object {"header": "field", ...}, all values strings, keys in header order json/ndjson the original value: key order, nesting, null, booleans and number text are kept (12345678901234567890123, 2.50); only an exponent is normalised (1e3 is written 1e+3, the same number) 
$ printf '[{"id":1,"name":"x"},{"id":2.50,"name":"y"}]' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --multi
[{"id":1,"name":"x"},{"id":2.50,"name":"y"}]        # both ticked

items.title: ndjson
items.text: The same values as json, one compact JSON document per line.

items.title: csv and tsv
items.text:
A header line with the column names, then one record per chosen row with its display cells, quoted where needed ("has, comma", "say ""hi""", a field with a line break is quoted and keeps it). tsv uses a tab as delimiter and the same quoting rules. Line ends are \n.

For json/ndjson input the columns are the union of keys and the cells are the display texts described in input formats (nested values as compact JSON, null as an empty field).

items.title: Examples of exact output
items.text:
These are the byte sequences the release's GUI qualification asserts after real clicks:

Command (input) Rows ticked stdout select --multi (alpha beta gamma ) gamma, then alpha alpha gamma select --input-format json (objects with number, boolean, string, array, null) row 2 [{"id":2.5,"ok":false,"name":"Příliš 😀","tags":[],"none":null}] select --input-format ndjson --multi ({"a":1}, {"a":"two"}, blank line, {"a":[3]}) rows 1 and 3 {"a":1} {"a":[3]} select --input-format csv --multi (header name,comment, fields with comma, quotes, line break) first three name,comment plain,"has, comma" quote,"say ""hi""" nl,"line1 line2" select --input-format csv --output-format tsv (same input) first name comment plain has, comma select --input-format csv --output-format lines (same input) the row with a line break exit 1, empty stdout select --multi (<script>alert(1)</script> ...) rows 1 and 3 the original lines, unchanged

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/output-formats.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Page structure
items.text:
The CLI generates the HTML page for each window. --css (all commands) and --html (form) are inserted into it as trusted content, so it helps to know what is there. This is the 0.1.2 page; ids and classes are not a stable API across versions, but the custom properties and the nhk-* ids below are what the CLI itself relies on.

<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset='utf-8'>
<style> built-in style sheet, then the contents of --css </style></head>
<body><main>
  <h1>escaped --title</h1>

  <!-- select -->
  <form id="nhk-selection-form"><div class="scroll">
    <table><thead><tr><th>Pick</th><th>column...</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody><tr><td><input type="checkbox|radio" id="nhk-row-0" name="selection" value="0"
                     aria-label="Select row 1"></td><td>escaped cell...</td></tr>...</tbody></table>
  </div></form>
  <div class="error" id="nhk-error"></div>
  <footer><button id="nhk-cancel">Cancel</button><button class="primary" id="nhk-submit">Submit selection</button></footer>

  <!-- view, lines input -->
  <section class="scroll"><pre>escaped lines</pre></section>
  <!-- view, other formats: the same <table> without the Pick column -->
  <footer><button class="primary" id="nhk-done">Close</button></footer>

  <!-- form -->
  your --html fragment (must contain <form id="nhk-form">)
  <div class="error" id="nhk-error"></div>
  <footer><button id="nhk-cancel">Cancel</button><button id="nhk-submit" class="primary">Submit</button></footer>
</main></body></html>

The window is created 900 x 610 and can be resized; the table area scrolls, the heading and footer stay visible.

items.title: Built-in style sheet
items.text:
Colours are custom properties on :root, so a theme only has to override them:

:root{color-scheme:dark;--background:#202734;--panel:#2b3444;--border:#4e5b70;--text:#edf2f7;--accent:#6798d5}
body{margin:0;background:var(--background);color:var(--text);font:14px sans-serif}
main{padding:20px;height:100%;display:flex;flex-direction:column}
h1{font-size:20px;margin:0 0 8px;font-weight:600;flex:none}
.scroll{flex:0 1 auto;min-height:0;overflow:auto;border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:8px}
table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:13px}
td,th{padding:9px 12px;border-bottom:1px solid #415068;text-align:left}
th{position:sticky;top:0;background:#344258;z-index:1}  tr:hover{background:#34435a}
footer{display:flex;gap:10px;justify-content:flex-end;margin-top:14px;flex:none}
button{border:1px solid #66768c;border-radius:7px;color:var(--text);padding:9px 18px;background:#39465b;cursor:pointer}
button.primary{background:#2867b4;border-color:#4384d1}
pre{white-space:pre-wrap;overflow-wrap:anywhere;line-height:1.45;padding:12px;margin:0}
.error{color:#ffaeae;min-height:22px;flex:none}
input[type=checkbox],input[type=radio]{accent-color:var(--accent)}

(abridged; the exact text is CSS in src/render.rs). --css comes after it, so equal selectors in your file win. examples/css/light.css is a complete light theme; examples/css/form.css lays out a form.

items.title: Rules for trusted content
items.text:
• --css and --html are inserted verbatim. Treat them like code: write them yourself, and escape every dynamic value you put into a generated --html file.
  • Core runs no JavaScript; <script> does nothing. Do not reference remote resources (fonts, images, @import URLs): the page is meant to be self-contained.
  • Keep the CLI's ids (nhk-form, nhk-error, nhk-cancel, nhk-submit, nhk-done, nhk-selection-form, nhk-row-N) unique: do not reuse them in your fragment.
  • Do not hide the footer: the CLI's buttons are the only way to submit.
  • Layout that relies on viewport units (vh) follows a resize with Core 1.0.3.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/page-structure.md · edit the page there.

items.title: nativehtmlkit select
items.text:
Show piped records as a table with a pick column and return the rows the user submits.

nativehtmlkit select [OPTIONS]
Option Default Meaning --input-format <FORMAT> lines how stdin is parsed: lines, csv, tsv, json, ndjson (input formats) --no-headers off csv/tsv: the first record is data; columns are named column_1 ... column_N. Accepted but without effect for the other formats. --multi off checkboxes, any number of rows; without it, radio buttons and exactly one row --allow-empty off Submit with nothing ticked is accepted and returns an empty result --output-format <FORMAT> same same, lines, csv, tsv, json, ndjson (output formats) --title <TITLE> Select an item window title and page heading; 1-128 characters, no control characters, shown as text --css <PATH> none trusted UTF-8 CSS file, at most 256 KiB, appended to the built-in style sheet (page structure) global options --host, --diagnostics, --timeout, --rpc-timeout, --liveness-interval, --startup-timeout (global options)

items.title: Behaviour
items.text:
1. stdin must not be a terminal. A terminal stdin is refused at once: nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: stdin is a terminal; pipe records in, e.g. ..., exit 1.
  2. stdin is read to the end (at most 8 MiB), decoded as UTF-8 and parsed. Every parse or limit problem exits 1 with error[input.invalid] before any window opens.
  3. At least one record is required: error[input.invalid]: no selectable input rows; stdin was empty or contained no records.
  4. The window shows the title as a heading, a scrolling table (a Pick column, then one column per input column), an error line, and the buttons Cancel and Submit selection. Every cell and the title are HTML-escaped: input is always shown as text.
  5. Submit selection:
  6. nothing ticked and no --allow-empty: the window stays open and shows select at least one row before submitting;
  7. otherwise the window closes and the chosen rows are written to stdout in input order (not click order), exit 0.
  8. Cancel, or closing the window: exit 2, empty stdout. If Submit and a close arrive at the same instant, the close wins (exit 2).
  9. --timeout expired: the window is closed, exit 124, empty stdout.

Keyboard: the pick controls and buttons are ordinary focusable controls (Tab moves, Space toggles, Enter or Space activates a focused button).

items.title: Examples
items.text:
Every option of select with a verified example: Linux (bash), Windows (PowerShell).

Related: exit statuses in scripts (Linux, Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/select.md · edit the page there.

items.title: nativehtmlkit view
items.text:
Show piped records read-only. There is no result: stdout stays empty.

nativehtmlkit view [OPTIONS]
Option Default Meaning --input-format <FORMAT> lines lines, csv, tsv, json, ndjson (input formats) --no-headers off csv/tsv: the first record is data (column_1 ... column_N) --title <TITLE> Output viewer 1-128 characters, no control characters, shown as text --css <PATH> none trusted UTF-8 CSS file, at most 256 KiB global options global options

view has no --multi, --allow-empty or --output-format; passing one is a usage error (exit 1).

items.title: Behaviour
items.text:
• stdin must not be a terminal and is parsed exactly as for select; parse and limit errors exit 1 with error[input.invalid].
  • Unlike select, no records is fine: empty stdin, [], or a CSV header without data rows opens an empty viewer. (Completely empty stdin with --input-format csv/tsv is still an error: expected at least one header column.)
  • lines input is shown as one wrapped, scrolling text block (<pre>), so the 65,536-node limit does not apply; only the 1 MiB page limit does (limits). Every other format is shown as a table, one column per input column.
  • The only button is Close. Close, or closing the window: exit 0, empty stdout.
  • --timeout expired: exit 124, empty stdout.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
Every option of view with a verified example: Linux (bash), Windows (PowerShell).

view returns only when the window is closed (or the deadline passes), so a script waits at that line. Related: viewing logs (Linux, Windows).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/reference/view.md · edit the page there.

items.title: NativeHTMLKit CLI on Windows
items.text:
nativehtmlkit.exe (alias nhk.exe) puts a native window into a PowerShell or cmd.exe pipeline: pipe records in, let a person pick, view or fill in something, and read the result from stdout. This section documents CLI 0.1.2 (bundled with Core host 1.0.3) for Windows x86-64, with examples for Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7. For bash on Linux see the Linux section.

Get-ChildItem -Directory | Select-Object Name, @{ n = 'Modified'; e = { $_.LastWriteTime.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } } |
    ConvertTo-Json | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --title 'Open folder'

items.title: Install
items.text:
Download the Windows archive and the checksum file from the v0.1.2 release (in the browser, or with the GitHub CLI as below) and compare the hash:

gh release download v0.1.2 -R nativehtmlkit/nativehtmlkit-cli -p '*windows-x64*' -p SHA256SUMS
$want = ((Get-Content SHA256SUMS | Select-String 'windows-x64.zip').Line -split '\s+')[0]
$got = (Get-FileHash .\nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
if ($got -eq $want) { 'checksum OK' } else { throw 'checksum mismatch' }

Without gh: Invoke-WebRequest -OutFile with https://github.com/nativehtmlkit/nativehtmlkit-cli/releases/download/v0.1.2/nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-windows-x64.zip (and the same for SHA256SUMS). -eq compares strings case-insensitively, so the upper-case hash of Get-FileHash matches the lower-case one in the file.

Extract it to a permanent place and add that folder to your PATH:

Expand-Archive .\nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-windows-x64.zip -DestinationPath "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs"
$dir = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-windows-x64"
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path', 'User') + ";$dir", 'User')
$env:Path += ";$dir"     # this session too

The folder contains:

File What it is nativehtmlkit.exe the CLI nhk.exe an identical copy under the short name nativehtmlkit-host.exe Core host 1.0.3, the program that draws the window; keep it beside the CLI manifest.json, SHA256SUMS versions, source commits, protocol version and hashes examples\sample-form.html the smallest form for nativehtmlkit form LICENSE, licenses\ licences of the CLI, Core and third-party components

Check it:

nativehtmlkit doctor

NativeHTMLKit CLI 0.1.2
Core host: C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\Programs\nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-windows-x64\nativehtmlkit-host.exe
nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3

The CLI writes no configuration files and needs no installer; to uninstall, delete the folder and remove it from PATH.

items.title: Set up UTF-8 once
items.text:
The CLI reads and writes UTF-8. Windows PowerShell 5.1 sends text to native programs as us-ascii by default ($OutputEncoding) and decodes their output with the console code page, so non-ASCII text would arrive as ? and come back garbled. Put this at the top of every script (or in your $PROFILE); it is harmless in PowerShell 7, which already uses UTF-8:

[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
'Příliš žluťoučký kůň', 'naïve café 😀' | nativehtmlkit select

Příliš žluťoučký kůň

Use [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false), not [Text.Encoding]::UTF8: the latter makes Windows PowerShell 5.1 send a byte-order mark first, which the json input format rejects (input formats). The example scripts also restore the console encoding when they finish.

items.title: First command
items.text:
'alpha', 'beta', 'gamma' | nativehtmlkit select --multi

A window lists the three lines with a checkbox each. Tick some and click Submit selection: they are printed, one per line, and $LASTEXITCODE is 0. Click Cancel: nothing is printed and $LASTEXITCODE is 2.

alpha
gamma

items.title: The four commands
items.text:
Command Reads stdin stdout on success Page select records the chosen rows select view records nothing (read-only) view form no one JSON line with the form values form doctor no which host is used, and its version doctor, help, version

Global options (--timeout, --host, --diagnostics, --rpc-timeout, --liveness-interval, --startup-timeout) work with every command, before or after its name. Each command page shows each of them with that command.

items.title: Pages in this section
items.text:
Page Contents select, view, form, doctor every option of every command, with a verified PowerShell example Input formats lines, csv, tsv, json, ndjson, --no-headers; objects as JSON Output formats same, lines, csv, tsv, json, ndjson: the exact text, read back as objects Exit codes and scripting 0, 1, 2, 124, 130 with $LASTEXITCODE; helper functions; cmd.exe Environment and diagnostics environment variables, --diagnostics levels, reading the records CSS and forms --css themes, writing and generating --html forms safely Troubleshooting every error line and what to do, encoding pitfalls Recipes Git branches, files, processes, services, Docker, JSON APIs, CSV, logs and events, pipelines, a deployment form, time zones, headless tests Tutorial: a project picker build proj.ps1, a bookmark tool using all three window commands Tutorial: a Git branch picker build git-pick.ps1 with select, JSON and --multi

The exact, OS-neutral specification is the reference; runnable scripts are listed in the example catalogue.

items.title: How the examples are verified
items.text:
The examples on these pages run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository:

git clone https://github.com/nativehtmlkit/nativehtmlkit-cli.git
Set-Location nativehtmlkit-cli\examples

Every PowerShell (and cmd.exe) block that calls the CLI is run by scripts/test-docs.ps1 against the released Windows archive (CLI 0.1.2, Core host 1.0.3) in Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows Server 2022, and the portable ones also in PowerShell 7 on Linux, with the real host in headless mode (no window and nobody to click). That proves the input and options are accepted, the page renders, and the documented exit status and output follow; since nobody clicks, each window ends by its deadline. Three kinds of results are shown:

  • stdout / stderr blocks: the text the example printed in that run.
  • "Submit prints" blocks: what the CLI writes when the user ticks the named rows. They are checked by running the release's own parsing, selection and output code on the exact bytes and options PowerShell gave the CLI.
  • Replayed results: a recorded Submit result, in the exact output format, handed to the script after the real CLI call was accepted, to show what the script does with it.

What a person sees and clicks (layout, keyboard, Cancel, closing the window, Ctrl+C) is covered by the release's GUI qualification on Windows Server 2022 and KDE Plasma.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/index.md · edit the page there.

items.title: CSS and forms (Windows)
items.text:
Two options insert your own trusted content into the page the CLI generates: --css FILE (every window command) adds a style sheet, and --html FILE (form) is the form itself. This page shows how to write both, and how to generate them from data safely in PowerShell. The generated page, its element ids and the built-in style sheet are documented in page structure.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how). How the windows look is checked by the release's GUI qualification, not here.

items.title: Trusted means: written by you
items.text:
• --css and --html are inserted verbatim. Write them yourself; never paste data into them without encoding it (below).
  • Core runs no JavaScript: <script> does nothing. Keep the files self-contained: no remote fonts, images or @import URLs.
  • Each file is UTF-8 and at most 256 KiB. Write generated files with [IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $text, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)): Set-Content in Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes the ANSI code page by default, and -Encoding UTF8 adds a byte-order mark.
  • Do not hide the footer or reuse the CLI's ids (nhk-form, nhk-error, nhk-cancel, nhk-submit, nhk-done, nhk-selection-form, nhk-row-N).

Data piped into select and view, and the --title, are always escaped by the CLI: they can never become markup.

items.title: --css: themes
items.text:
The built-in style sheet takes its colours from custom properties on :root (--background, --panel, --border, --text, --accent); your file comes after it, so overriding them is enough for most themes. The repository's css/light.css:

:root {
  color-scheme: light;
  --background: #f6f7f9; --panel: #ffffff; --border: #c9d1dc; --text: #1d2430; --accent: #2f6fd0;
}
th { background: #e8edf4; }
tr:hover { background: #eef3fb; }
button.primary { background: #2f6fd0; border-color: #2f6fd0; color: #ffffff; }
.error { color: #b3261e; }

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --css css/light.css

The same file works for view and form:

Get-Content data\app.log | nativehtmlkit view --css css/light.css

A small accent change, written on the fly:

$css = @'
:root { --accent: #3fa37a; }
h1 { font-size: 18px; letter-spacing: .02em; }
button.primary { background: #2f8a63; border-color: #3fa37a; }
'@
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path (Get-Location) 'accent.css'), $css, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
'keep', 'remove' | nativehtmlkit select --css accent.css --title 'Green'

Files over 256 KiB, unreadable files and non-UTF-8 files are refused before a window opens:

[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path (Get-Location) 'huge.css'), (' ' * 300000))
'a' | nativehtmlkit select --css huge.css

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: custom HTML or CSS file exceeds 256 KiB

items.title: --html: writing a form
items.text:
The fragment must contain <form id="nhk-form">. Put every control inside it and give each a name. Do not add a submit button; the CLI adds Cancel and Submit below your fragment. Core validates these constraints when the user clicks Submit and keeps an invalid form open with Some required fields are invalid:

Attribute / type Checked required text, select, checkbox, radio group minlength, maxlength text, textarea pattern the whole value must match type="number" with min, max, step number range type="email", type="url" format date/time types with min, max range

A deployment form using most of them (the repository's deploy-form.ps1 generates this):

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

$html = @'
<form id="nhk-form">
  <label>Service <select name="service" required>
    <option value="">Choose...</option><option value="api">api</option><option value="web">web</option>
  </select></label>
  <fieldset><legend>Environment</legend>
    <label><input type="radio" name="environment" value="staging" required checked> Staging</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="environment" value="production"> Production</label>
  </fieldset>
  <label>Version <input name="version" required value="v1.0.0"
         pattern="v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" title="a version such as v1.4.2"></label>
  <label>Replicas <input name="replicas" type="number" min="1" max="20" value="2" required></label>
  <label>Notify <input name="notify" type="email" placeholder="team@example.com"></label>
  <label>Change notes <textarea name="notes" maxlength="500" rows="3"></textarea></label>
  <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" name="dry_run" value="yes" checked> Dry run only</label>
</form>
'@
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path (Get-Location) 'deploy.html'), $html, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
nativehtmlkit form --html deploy.html --css css/form.css --title 'Deploy'

css/form.css lays it out as a grid of labelled fields using the page's colour variables:

#nhk-form { display: grid; gap: 12px; max-width: 520px; }
#nhk-form label { display: grid; gap: 4px; }
#nhk-form input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]), #nhk-form select, #nhk-form textarea {
  background: var(--panel); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 6px; padding: 7px 9px; font: inherit;
}

items.title: Reading the result
items.text:
Submit prints one line {"entries":[...]}: one entry per named control that has a value, in document order. All values are strings; an unticked checkbox has no entry; an empty text field is "". Turn it into a hashtable:

$json = nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
$values = @{}
foreach ($e in (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n")).entries) {
    if (-not $values.ContainsKey($e.name)) { $values[$e.name] = $e.value }
}
if ($values.confirm -ne 'yes') { Write-Warning 'not confirmed'; exit 1 }
"creating $($values.project) for $($values.environment)"

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"project","value":"Demo App"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"production"}]}

WARNING: not confirmed

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"project","value":"Demo App"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"production"},{"kind":"text","name":"confirm","value":"yes"}]}

creating Demo App for production

Rules HTML cannot express (for example "production needs change notes") are checked by the script after Submit; see the deployment form recipe.

items.title: Generating a form from data
items.text:
Anything that comes from outside the script (file names, Git tags, user names, API data) must be HTML-encoded before it goes into the fragment, or a value such as <b> or " would change the markup. [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode encodes & < > " ':

function Enc([string] $s) { [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($s) }
$items = ('a <b>.txt', 'notes & "more".log' | ForEach-Object { "<li>$(Enc $_)</li>" }) -join "`n"
$html = @"
<form id="nhk-form"><p>These files will be deleted:</p><ul>
$items
</ul><label><input type="checkbox" name="sure" value="yes" required> I understand</label></form>
"@
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path (Get-Location) 'confirm.html'), $html, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
[Console]::Error.WriteLine($items)
nativehtmlkit form --html confirm.html --title 'Confirm deletion' | Out-Null

<li>a <b>.txt</li>
<li>notes & "more".log</li>

Options for a select built from data need no encoding: pipe the data in and the CLI escapes it.
