Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/css-and-forms.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Environment and diagnostics (Windows)
items.text:
This page shows the environment variables the CLI reads, how it finds the Core host, and how to get a timeline of a session with --diagnostics. Specifications: environment, diagnostics, host discovery.

The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how). In PowerShell an environment variable is set for the session with $env:NAME = 'value' and removed with Remove-Item Env:NAME; in cmd.exe with set NAME=value.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
Variable Effect NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY the Core host to use when --host is not given (an empty value is ignored) NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS default for --diagnostics: off, normal, debug, trace; the host reads it too NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID correlation id put into every CLI and host record (1-128 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -) PATH the last place the CLI looks for nativehtmlkit-host.exe TMP / TEMP where the private, per-session folder nativehtmlkit-cli-* is created and removed again

The CLI reads no configuration files and no registry keys.

items.title: Which host is used
items.text:
The first match wins: --host PATH, then NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY, then nativehtmlkit-host.exe in the folder of the CLI executable, then each PATH folder. doctor shows the result:

$coreHost = (nativehtmlkit doctor | Select-String '^Core host: (.+)$').Matches[0].Groups[1].Value
$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY = $coreHost
nativehtmlkit doctor | Select-Object -Last 1
Remove-Item Env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY

nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3

A variable that names no file is an error; --host wins over it:

$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY = 'C:\missing\nativehtmlkit-host.exe'
'a' | nativehtmlkit select

nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: C:\missing\nativehtmlkit-host.exe

$coreHost = (nativehtmlkit doctor | Select-String '^Core host: (.+)$').Matches[0].Groups[1].Value
$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY = 'C:\missing\nativehtmlkit-host.exe'
'a' | nativehtmlkit select --host $coreHost

The CLI 0.1.2 is qualified with Core host 1.0.3, the one in its release archive; use the override for development builds only.

items.title: --diagnostics levels
items.text:
The CLI writes structured records, one JSON object per line, to stderr; stdout only ever carries the result. The Core host writes its own JSON log records to the same stderr ("target":"nativehtmlkit_host..."); the CLI's carry "component":"nativehtmlkit-cli".

Level CLI records off none normal (default) failures only debug the session's lifecycle with timings trace also every request, host event and liveness probe

A small helper collects the CLI's records from stderr (2>&1 turns each stderr line into an error record; "$_" is its text):

function Get-CliRecords { process { $line = "$_"; if ($line.StartsWith('{')) { $r = ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $line; if ($r.component -eq 'nativehtmlkit-cli') { $r } } } }
@('a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --diagnostics off 2>&1 | Get-CliRecords).Count
exit 0

0

function Get-CliRecords { process { $line = "$_"; if ($line.StartsWith('{')) { $r = ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $line; if ($r.component -eq 'nativehtmlkit-cli') { $r } } } }
@('a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --diagnostics normal 2>&1 | Get-CliRecords).Count
exit 0

A deadline is not a failure, so normal writes nothing here either:

0

function Get-CliRecords { process { $line = "$_"; if ($line.StartsWith('{')) { $r = ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $line; if ($r.component -eq 'nativehtmlkit-cli') { $r } } } }
$records = @('a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --diagnostics debug 2>&1 | Get-CliRecords)
@($records | ForEach-Object { $_.event } | Sort-Object -Unique).Count
$done = $records | Where-Object { $_.event -eq 'session.completed' }
"$($done.context.outcome) $($done.context.exit_code)"
exit 0

11
deadline 124

function Get-CliRecords { process { $line = "$_"; if ($line.StartsWith('{')) { $r = ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $line; if ($r.component -eq 'nativehtmlkit-cli') { $r } } } }
$records = @('a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --diagnostics trace 2>&1 | Get-CliRecords)
($records | Where-Object { $_.event -eq 'rpc.started' } | Select-Object -First 1).event
exit 0

rpc.started

NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS sets the default; the flag wins:

$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS = 'debug'
$log = 'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
[bool] ($log | Where-Object { $_ -like '*"event":"window.ready"*' })
exit 0

True

items.title: A timeline of one session
items.text:
Keep the result and the log apart: with 2>&1 the stderr lines arrive as error records and the result lines as strings, so they can be split again:

$all = 'one', 'two', 'three' | nativehtmlkit --diagnostics debug select 2>&1
$result = $all | Where-Object { $_ -isnot [System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord] }
$log = $all | Where-Object { $_ -is [System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord] } | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
$log | Where-Object { $_.StartsWith('{') } | ForEach-Object { ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_ } |
    Where-Object { $_.component -eq 'nativehtmlkit-cli' -and $_.event -ne 'rpc.completed' } |
    ForEach-Object { '{0,-8} {1}' -f $_.role, $_.event }
exit 0

launcher session.started
launcher host.spawned
backend  backend.started
backend  handshake.completed
backend  window.ready
backend  deadline.expired
backend  host.request
backend  session.shutdown
launcher host.exited
launcher session.completed

With a Submit instead of a deadline you would see submit.accepted where deadline.expired is. rpc.completed records carry the protocol operation and duration_ms of each request. Records never contain your data, titles, paths or form values; the host's records are a separate log, so review those before sharing one.

Avoid 2> file for these logs in Windows PowerShell 5.1: it writes the first stderr line as a formatted error record and wraps long lines, so the JSON records no longer parse. PowerShell 7 and cmd.exe (2> session.log) write the lines unchanged.

items.title: Correlate with your own logs
items.text:
NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID puts your id into every CLI record (session_id) and every host record (diagnostic_session_id):

$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID = 'nightly-42'
$log = 'build ok' | nativehtmlkit --diagnostics debug view 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
$log | Where-Object { $_.StartsWith('{') } | ForEach-Object { $r = ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_; if ($r.session_id) { $r.session_id } else { $r.diagnostic_session_id } } |
    Sort-Object -Unique
exit 0

nightly-42

An id with other characters is replaced by a generated one, and a session_id.replaced record says so:

$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID = 'my id/1'
$log = 'x' | nativehtmlkit view --diagnostics normal 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
$log | Where-Object { $_ -like '*"component":"nativehtmlkit-cli"*' } | ForEach-Object { (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_).event }
exit 0

session_id.replaced

items.title: Temporary files
items.text:
Each session uses a private folder nativehtmlkit-cli-* under TMP and removes it when the command ends, whatever the outcome:

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path session-tmp | Out-Null
$env:TMP = (Resolve-Path session-tmp).ProviderPath; $env:TEMP = $env:TMP; $env:TMPDIR = $env:TMP
'x' | nativehtmlkit view
@(Get-ChildItem -Force -Directory session-tmp -Filter 'nativehtmlkit-cli-*').Count
exit 0

0

On Windows the Core host also creates a folder nativehtmlkit-bitmaps in TMP and leaves it there (empty) after the session; it is the host's, not the CLI's, and can be deleted.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/environment-and-diagnostics.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Exit codes and scripting (Windows)
items.text:
Every nativehtmlkit command reports what happened through its exit status, and only a successful Submit writes anything to stdout. In PowerShell the status is in $LASTEXITCODE, in cmd.exe in %ERRORLEVEL%. This page shows how to use it. The complete specification, including every error[<code>], is the exit status reference.

Status Meaning stdout Typical reaction 0 submitted (select, form), closed (view), done (doctor, --help, --version) the result use it 1 error: usage, input, host missing or failed; one nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: ... line on stderr empty fail 2 Cancel, or the window was closed without submitting empty stop quietly, change nothing 124 --timeout expired empty stop, maybe say so 130 Ctrl+C in the console empty stop

Usage errors exit 1 (not 2), so 2 always means the user said no. (143 and 129 are the Unix SIGTERM and SIGHUP statuses; they do not occur on Windows.)

The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how). Headless, nobody clicks, so windows end with 124; replayed results show the other paths.

items.title: $LASTEXITCODE right after the call
items.text:
A native program's non-zero status is not an exception: branch on $LASTEXITCODE immediately, before another native command overwrites it.

$size = 'small', 'medium', 'large' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Size' --timeout 60
switch ($LASTEXITCODE) {
    0       { "size: $size" }
    2       { Write-Warning 'cancelled'; exit 2 }
    124     { Write-Warning 'no answer within 60 s'; exit 124 }
    default { exit $LASTEXITCODE }    # the CLI already explained the error on stderr
}

When the user clicks Cancel:



WARNING: cancelled

When the user picks large:

large

size: large

(Write-Warning goes to the warning stream; with the script's output redirected, as in these runs, PowerShell prints it to stdout with the WARNING: prefix.)

items.title: A helper that ends the script on anything but Submit
items.text:
Inside a function, exit ends the whole script, with the CLI's status. $input passes the pipeline on to the CLI:

function Invoke-Picker {
    $out = $input | nativehtmlkit @args
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Warning 'nothing chosen'; exit $LASTEXITCODE }
    $out -join "`n"
}
$colour = 'red', 'green' | Invoke-Picker select --title 'Colour'
"colour: $colour"



WARNING: nothing chosen

green

colour: green

items.title: Hand the status on to the caller
items.text:
exit $LASTEXITCODE makes a script return the CLI's status, so whoever started it can tell Cancel from success. The example scripts do this:

$ps = (Get-Process -Id $PID).Path
& $ps -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\pick-git-branch.ps1 *> $null
"pick-git-branch.ps1 exited with $LASTEXITCODE"
exit 0

pick-git-branch.ps1 exited with 124

items.title: PowerShell 7: native errors as exceptions
items.text:
PowerShell 7.4 and later can turn a non-zero native status into an error with $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference. Then Cancel throws under $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop', so catch it where 2 or 124 are normal answers:

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true
try {
    $choice = 'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select
    "chose $choice"
} catch {
    "no choice (status $LASTEXITCODE)"
}
exit 0

no choice (status 124)

items.title: Errors: status 1 and the error code
items.text:
Each failure writes exactly one line nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: <message> to stderr. stderr also carries the Core host's log records, so match the line; never parse stderr for results. With 2>&1 each stderr line arrives as an error record; "$_" gives its text:

$err = 'a,b', '1,2,3' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
$status = $LASTEXITCODE
$code = ($err | Select-String -Pattern 'error\[[a-z_.]+\]' | Select-Object -First 1).Matches[0].Value
"status $status, $code"
exit 0

status 1, error[input.invalid]

A usage error from the argument parser has no code but also exits 1:

'a' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format xml

error: invalid value 'xml' for '--input-format <INPUT_FORMAT>'

With $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop', Windows PowerShell 5.1 turns the first redirected stderr line of a native program into a terminating error. Redirect stderr only while 'Continue' is in effect, as pick-container.ps1 does around docker logs 2>&1.

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

items.title: Write files only after success
items.text:
Check the status first, then write. [IO.File]::WriteAllText with UTF8Encoding($false) writes UTF-8 without a BOM in both editions (Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 adds one in 5.1):

$csv = Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format csv
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { "out.csv exists: $(Test-Path out.csv)"; exit $LASTEXITCODE }
$target = Join-Path (Get-Location) 'out.csv'
[IO.File]::WriteAllText($target, ($csv -join "`n") + "`n", [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))

out.csv exists: False

items.title: --timeout is for people, not for hangs
items.text:
Without --timeout a window waits as long as the person needs. Add it when an unattended window must not block a job forever:

'deploy', 'skip' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Nightly deploy?' --timeout 900

nativehtmlkit: no decision before the --timeout deadline; the window was closed

You do not need --timeout against a hung host: the CLI notices that itself (liveness probes) and exits 1 with error[host.unresponsive] (environment and diagnostics).

items.title: Ctrl+C: 130
items.text:
Ctrl+C in the console window closes the CLI's window and exits 130; stdout stays empty, even if the user had just clicked Submit. A script sees it like any other status (here the 130 is replayed; scripts/test-docs.ps1 separately sends a real Ctrl+C to the released CLI on Windows and checks for 130):

$choice = 'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 130) { Write-Warning 'interrupted'; exit 130 }
exit $LASTEXITCODE



WARNING: interrupted

items.title: view and doctor
items.text:
view has no Cancel: closing it is 0, and 124 is "the deadline closed it". Treat both as done:

Get-Content data\app.log | nativehtmlkit view --timeout 120
if ($LASTEXITCODE -notin 0, 124) { exit 1 }
'carry on'
exit 0

carry on

-notin needs PowerShell 3 or later (both editions have it). doctor exits 0 or 1 and suits a start-of-script check:

nativehtmlkit doctor | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'NativeHTMLKit CLI is not installed correctly' }
'ready'

ready

items.title: cmd.exe and batch files
items.text:
The CLI works the same from cmd.exe: < and | feed stdin, %ERRORLEVEL% holds the status. cmd.exe passes bytes unchanged, so save input files as UTF-8.

(echo small& echo medium& echo large) > sizes.txt
nativehtmlkit select --title "Size" < sizes.txt > choice.txt
if %ERRORLEVEL% equ 0 (
  set /p CHOICE=<choice.txt
) else (
  echo no choice: %ERRORLEVEL%
)
exit /b 0

no choice: 124

medium

if errorlevel N means "N or greater", so test the higher statuses first, or compare %ERRORLEVEL% with equ as above:

type data\app.log | nativehtmlkit view --title "app.log"
if errorlevel 124 (echo closed by the deadline) else if errorlevel 1 (echo failed) else (echo closed)
exit /b 0

closed by the deadline

nativehtmlkit doctor > nul || echo the CLI is not installed correctly
echo doctor: %ERRORLEVEL%

doctor: 0

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/exit-codes-and-scripting.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Input formats (Windows)
items.text:
select and view read all of stdin, then parse it as --input-format lines (default), csv, tsv, json or ndjson. PowerShell sends each object of the pipeline to a native program as one line of text, so strings become lines, and objects are best sent as json. This page shows each format with PowerShell examples; the complete rules are in the input formats reference.

Common rules:

  • stdin must be piped (not the console), UTF-8, at most 8 MiB (set up UTF-8).
  • At most 2,000 rows and 32 columns.
  • Any problem exits 1 with nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: ... before a window opens.
  • Every cell is shown as text: markup in the data is never interpreted.

The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how); "Submit prints" blocks are the exact output of the released code for the bytes PowerShell sent and the rows named.

items.title: lines (default)
items.text:
One row per line, one column named Value. PowerShell ends each line with CR LF on Windows; the \r is removed. Empty strings are rows too.

'first', '', 'third', 'fourth' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format lines --multi

Submit prints, after ticking rows 1 and 4:

first
fourth

Lines are kept exactly, including leading spaces and markup:

[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
'  indented', '<b>not bold</b>', 'Příliš žluťoučký kůň 😀' | nativehtmlkit select --multi

  indented
<b>not bold</b>
Příliš žluťoučký kůň 😀

Without the UTF-8 setup Windows PowerShell 5.1 sends us-ascii: every non-ASCII character silently becomes ? before the CLI sees it. The same happens in any edition with an ASCII $OutputEncoding:

$OutputEncoding = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII
'café' | nativehtmlkit select

caf?

No input at all is refused by select (an empty view is fine):

@() | nativehtmlkit select

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: no selectable input rows; stdin was empty or contained no records

items.title: csv
items.text:
Comma-separated values with a header row, RFC 4180 quoting: inside "..." commas and line breaks are data and "" is one ". Blank lines are skipped; a byte-order mark before the header is ignored. Get-Content sends a file line by line, which keeps quoted line breaks intact:

@'
name,comment,n
plain,"has, comma",1

quote,"say ""hi""",2
'@ | Set-Content -Path notes.csv
Get-Content notes.csv | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --multi

Two rows (the blank line is skipped). Submit prints, after ticking both (CSV output is re-quoted where needed):

name,comment,n
plain,"has, comma",1
quote,"say ""hi""",2

A quoted field may also contain a line break. PowerShell sends lines with CR LF on Windows, so such a field keeps the CR LF as data, and the csv output writes it back unchanged.

ConvertTo-Csv produces input the CLI reads directly. Windows PowerShell 5.1 needs -NoTypeInformation (otherwise the first line is #TYPE ...) and quotes every field, which is fine:

[pscustomobject]@{ Host = 'web-01'; Status = 'healthy' }, [pscustomobject]@{ Host = 'web-02'; Status = 'degraded' } |
    ConvertTo-Csv -NoTypeInformation | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --output-format json

[{"Host":"web-02","Status":"degraded"}]

Every record must have as many fields as the header, and header names must be unique:

'host,role', 'web-01,frontend,extra' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv

found record with 3 fields, but the previous record has 2 fields

'name,name', 'a,b' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: duplicate CSV/TSV column names cannot be represented as JSON objects

Only , is a delimiter. Convert semicolon files (a common Excel export in many locales) with Import-Csv -Delimiter ';':

'host;status', 'web-01;healthy', 'web-02;degraded' | Set-Content -Path semicolons.csv
Import-Csv -Path semicolons.csv -Delimiter ';' | ConvertTo-Csv -NoTypeInformation |
    nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv

A header without data rows: select refuses it, view shows an empty table:

'host,status' | nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv

items.title: tsv
items.text:
Tab-separated values, otherwise like csv (same header and quoting rules). In PowerShell `t is a tab:

"branch`tupdated`tsubject", "main`t2 hours ago`tMerge fix/typo", "feature/login`t3 days ago`tAdd login form" |
    nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv

branch  updated subject
feature/login   3 days ago  Add login form

Pitfall: TSV uses CSV quoting, so a field that starts with " is read as a quoted field: the quotes are removed, and a quote that is never closed swallows the following tabs and lines. Two data lines, but one row:

"branch`tsubject", "main`t`"unclosed quote", "feature`tsecond row" | nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv

For free text such as commit subjects send JSON instead (below).

items.title: --no-headers
items.text:
For csv and tsv: the first record is data; columns are named column_1 ... column_N. (Accepted, without effect, for the other formats.)

"web-01`thealthy", "web-02`tdegraded", "db-01`thealthy" |
    nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv --no-headers --multi --output-format json

[{"column_1":"web-01","column_2":"healthy"},{"column_1":"web-02","column_2":"degraded"}]

items.title: json: PowerShell objects
items.text:
The natural way to send objects. Exactly one JSON document: an array gives one row per element, any other value is one row. Columns are the union of the objects' properties; cells show strings as they are, $null as empty, numbers and booleans as JSON text, nested values as compact JSON.

$rows = [pscustomobject]@{ id = 1; name = 'web'; tags = @('a', 'b') },
        [pscustomobject]@{ id = 2; name = 'db'; owner = $null }
ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $rows -Compress | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

Columns id, name, tags, owner. The result is the original element, unchanged:

[{"id":2,"name":"db","owner":null}]

Rules that keep this working:

  • Choose the properties first with Select-Object: raw objects have many properties (the CLI accepts 32 columns) and nested objects would be shown as JSON text.
  • Turn enums and dates into strings yourself: ConvertTo-Json writes enums as numbers, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes dates as "\/Date(...)\/".
  • One object is serialised as an object, not an array; the CLI accepts both (one row).
  • Zero objects produce no input at all, which select refuses: check the count first.
Get-ChildItem -File | Select-Object Name,
    @{ n = 'Size (KiB)'; e = { [math]::Ceiling($_.Length / 1KB) } },
    @{ n = 'Modified'; e = { $_.LastWriteTime.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') } } |
    ConvertTo-Json -Compress | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json

Too many properties:

$wide = [ordered]@{}; 1..33 | ForEach-Object { $wide["p$_"] = $_ }
[pscustomobject] $wide | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: 33 columns exceeds the 32-column limit

An array of strings is a one-column table:

ConvertTo-Json -InputObject @('red', 'green', 'blue') -Compress |
    nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --output-format lines

green

A file that already holds JSON: send it as one string with Get-Content -Raw:

Get-Content -Raw data\issues.json | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json

Only one document is accepted, and no byte-order mark. Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes one when $OutputEncoding is [Text.Encoding]::UTF8 (PowerShell 7 does not):

$OutputEncoding = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8
'[1]' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: invalid JSON input: expected value at line 1 column 1

$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
'[1]' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

items.title: ndjson
items.text:
One JSON value per line. Blank lines are skipped; a line holding an array is one row. Convert objects one at a time with -Compress:

1..3 | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ n = $_; square = $_ * $_ } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress } |
    nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson --multi

{"n":2,"square":4}
{"n":3,"square":9}

JSON Lines files and tools that print one JSON object per line feed it directly:

Get-Content data\app.ndjson | nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson

docker ps --all --format '{{json .}}' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson

Pretty-printed JSON is not NDJSON (ConvertTo-Json without -Compress spans lines):

[pscustomobject]@{ a = 1 } | ConvertTo-Json | nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: invalid NDJSON line 1: EOF while parsing an object at line 1 column 1

items.title: Limits
items.text:
1..2000 | nativehtmlkit select --multi

1..2001 | nativehtmlkit select

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: 2001 rows exceeds the 2000-row initial GUI limit

Also refused: more than 8 MiB, and a page over 1 MiB or 65,536 elements (the message says how many rows would fit). See the limits reference.

items.title: Which format to use
items.text:
Your data Format strings, names, paths lines PowerShell objects json via Select-Object ... \| ConvertTo-Json a CSV file, ConvertTo-Csv -NoTypeInformation output csv docker ps --format '{{json .}}', JSON Lines log files ndjson text that may contain tabs, quotes or newlines json/ndjson (not tsv)

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/input-formats.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Output formats (Windows)
items.text:
After Submit selection, select writes the chosen rows to stdout in the format named by --output-format: same (default), lines, csv, tsv, json or ndjson. view never writes to stdout; form always writes one JSON line (form). The complete rules are in the output formats reference.

Common rules:

  • Rows are written in input order, whatever order they were ticked in.
  • The result is written in one piece after the window has closed, and only when $LASTEXITCODE is 0. On Cancel (2), timeout (124), error (1) or Ctrl+C (130) nothing is written, so a variable assigned from the CLI is $null then.
  • UTF-8, \n line ends, a newline at the end. PowerShell receives several lines as an array of strings: -join "n"makes one string beforeConvertFrom-Json`.

Every "Submit prints" block below is the exact output of the released code for the bytes of the example above it and the rows named, checked by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how). The examples read the sample file data\servers.csv from the repository's examples folder:

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes
web-01,frontend,eu-west,4,8,healthy,
web-02,frontend,eu-west,4,8,degraded,"disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled"
api-01,backend,eu-west,8,32,healthy,
api-02,backend,us-east,8,32,healthy,"canary for ""v2"" API"
db-01,database,eu-west,16,128,healthy,primary
db-02,database,us-east,16,128,maintenance,"replica, patching until 18:00"
cache-01,cache,eu-west,2,16,healthy,

items.title: same (default)
items.text:
The format of the input: lines in, lines out; csv in, csv out; and so on.

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format same

Submit prints, after ticking api-02 and web-02:

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes
web-02,frontend,eu-west,4,8,degraded,"disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled"
api-02,backend,us-east,8,32,healthy,"canary for ""v2"" API"

items.title: lines
items.text:
One line per chosen row. A lines row is written as it was read; a row whose value is a JSON string is written as that string; any other row is written as its cells joined by a tab.

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format lines

web-01  frontend    eu-west 4   8   healthy 
db-01   database    eu-west 16  128 healthy primary

Split a line into its cells with -split "t"`:

$chosen = Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format lines
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { $chosen | ForEach-Object { 'checking ' + ($_ -split "`t")[0] } }
exit 0

web-01  frontend    eu-west 4   8   healthy 
db-01   database    eu-west 16  128 healthy primary

checking web-01
checking db-01

A lines result can never turn one row into two: if a chosen value contains a line break, nothing is written and the command fails with exit 1. Use json or ndjson for such data:

'name,comment', 'plain,ok', 'multi,"line one', 'line two"' |
    nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --output-format lines

Submit after picking multi:

nativehtmlkit: error[output.failed]: selected value contains newline: use --output-format json or ndjson

JSON strings come back as plain lines:

ConvertTo-Json -InputObject @('red', 'green', 'blue') -Compress |
    nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json --output-format lines

red
blue

items.title: csv
items.text:
The header line, then each chosen row's cells, quoted where needed. ConvertFrom-Csv reads it back as objects:

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format csv

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes
db-02,database,us-east,16,128,maintenance,"replica, patching until 18:00"

$csv = Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format csv
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { $csv | ConvertFrom-Csv | ForEach-Object { "$($_.host): $($_.notes)" } }
exit 0

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes
db-02,database,us-east,16,128,maintenance,"replica, patching until 18:00"

db-02: replica, patching until 18:00

From json or ndjson input the columns are the union of the keys; nested values are written as compact JSON and null as an empty field:

Get-Content data\app.ndjson | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format ndjson --output-format csv

time,level,msg,port,duration_ms,retry,upstream
2026-11-16T09:00:01Z,info,server listening,8080,,,
2026-11-16T09:02:40Z,error,upstream timeout,,,1,"{""host"":""api-01""}"

Write a result file only after a successful Submit (exit codes and scripting).

items.title: tsv
items.text:
Like csv with a tab as delimiter (and the same quoting):

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format tsv

host    role    region  cpu_cores   memory_gib  status  notes
web-02  frontend    eu-west 4   8   degraded    disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled
api-01  backend eu-west 8   32  healthy

items.title: json
items.text:
One JSON array with the chosen rows' values on one line. A lines row is a string, a csv/tsv row an object of strings keyed by the header, a json/ndjson row the original value unchanged. Read it back with ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject and enumerate it with foreach or a pipeline. Do not wrap it in @(...) to count the rows: Windows PowerShell 5.1 returns a JSON array as one object, so @(ConvertFrom-Json ...) holds a single item there; ConvertFrom-Json ... | ForEach-Object { $_ } gives the rows in both editions:

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json

[{"host":"api-01","role":"backend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"8","memory_gib":"32","status":"healthy","notes":""}]

$json = Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit 0 }
$rows = @(ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n") | ForEach-Object { $_ })
"$($rows.Count) row(s)"
foreach ($row in $rows) { "$($row.host) has $($row.memory_gib) GiB" }

[{"host":"api-01","role":"backend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"8","memory_gib":"32","status":"healthy","notes":""},{"host":"db-01","role":"database","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"16","memory_gib":"128","status":"healthy","notes":"primary"}]

2 row(s)
api-01 has 32 GiB
db-01 has 128 GiB

lines input as JSON keeps every character of each line:

'a.txt', 'b c.txt', "it's.txt" | nativehtmlkit select --multi --output-format json

["b c.txt","it's.txt"]

items.title: ndjson
items.text:
The same values as json, one per line; each line is a complete JSON document:

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format ndjson

{"host":"web-01","role":"frontend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"4","memory_gib":"8","status":"healthy","notes":""}
{"host":"db-01","role":"database","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"16","memory_gib":"128","status":"healthy","notes":"primary"}

$lines = Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format ndjson
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
    $lines | ForEach-Object { $r = ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_; "would restart $($r.role) on $($r.host)" }
}
exit 0

{"host":"web-01","role":"frontend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"4","memory_gib":"8","status":"healthy","notes":""}
{"host":"db-01","role":"database","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"16","memory_gib":"128","status":"healthy","notes":"primary"}

would restart frontend on web-01
would restart database on db-01

items.title: Nothing chosen (--allow-empty)
items.text:
With --allow-empty, Submit with nothing ticked is a valid answer (exit 0). lines and ndjson print nothing, json prints [], csv/tsv print the header line only:

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --allow-empty --input-format csv --output-format csv

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --allow-empty --input-format csv --output-format ndjson

items.title: Which one to use
items.text:
You need Output format strings for ForEach-Object lines (single-column input) objects json + ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ... \| ForEach-Object { $_ } a spreadsheet file, or objects via ConvertFrom-Csv csv exactly the records you put in same values that may contain line breaks json or ndjson

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/output-formats.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Troubleshooting (Windows)
items.text:
On failure the CLI exits 1 and writes one line to stderr:

nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: <message> (<details>)

Find the line in the table, or reproduce the error with the example below it. Every code is listed in the exit status reference. The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

You see Cause Fix nativehtmlkit : The term 'nativehtmlkit' is not recognized ... the folder is not on PATH add it (install) or call it by full path error[host.not_found]: NativeHTMLKit Core host not found... nativehtmlkit-host.exe is not beside the CLI keep the extracted archive together; run nativehtmlkit doctor error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: <path> --host or NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY points nowhere correct or remove it error[host.not_found]: cannot start the Core host (...) the file is not a working program (blocked, damaged) extract the archive again non-ASCII text shows as ? Windows PowerShell 5.1 sends us-ascii set up UTF-8 error[input.invalid]: invalid JSON input: expected value at line 1 column 1 a byte-order mark from $OutputEncoding = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8 (5.1) use [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false) error[input.invalid]: no selectable input rows... the pipeline before the CLI produced nothing check the count first error[input.invalid]: ... 33 columns exceeds the 32-column limit a raw object with many properties Select-Object the properties first error[input.invalid]: malformed CSV/TSV record: ... ragged rows, #TYPE line from ConvertTo-Csv in 5.1, a TSV field starting with " -NoTypeInformation; send JSON error[input.invalid]: input is too large to display: ... over the 1 MiB page or 65,536-node limit the message says how many rows fit; filter first error[usage.invalid]: --title must be nonempty... over 128 characters, or a tab/newline $title.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(128, $title.Length)) error[output.failed]: selected value contains newline... lines output of a value with a line break --output-format json or ndjson error[host.startup_timeout] no window within --startup-timeout (+5 s) slow first start on a busy machine: raise --startup-timeout error[host.unresponsive] the host stopped answering while the window was open it has been stopped; report it with a --diagnostics debug log error: unexpected argument ... (no code) a typo in an option nativehtmlkit <command> --help

items.title: Check the installation
items.text:
nativehtmlkit doctor

If that fails with host.not_found, the host is not beside the CLI. Copying only nativehtmlkit.exe somewhere else is the usual cause:

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path lonely | Out-Null
Copy-Item -Path (Get-Command nativehtmlkit).Source -Destination lonely\
$env:PATH = "$env:SystemRoot\System32"
.\lonely\nativehtmlkit.exe doctor

nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: NativeHTMLKit Core host not found. Install a qualified release beside the CLI or set NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY.

Which nativehtmlkit PowerShell runs, if there are several:

@(Get-Command nativehtmlkit -All | ForEach-Object { $_.CommandType }) | Select-Object -First 1

Application

items.title: Encoding problems
items.text:
Symptoms: ? instead of letters, or invalid JSON input for JSON that looks fine. After the UTF-8 setup the session sends UTF-8 without a byte-order mark:

[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
"sending: $($OutputEncoding.WebName), BOM: $($OutputEncoding.GetPreamble().Length -gt 0)"

sending: utf-8, BOM: False

Without it, Windows PowerShell 5.1 sends us-ascii (PowerShell 7 sends UTF-8):

"default: $($OutputEncoding.WebName)"

default: us-ascii

items.title: Input problems
items.text:
An empty pipeline (the previous command found nothing). Check before calling select:

$files = @(Get-ChildItem -Filter *.nothing-here)
if ($files.Count -eq 0) { 'no files to choose from'; exit 0 }
$files | ForEach-Object Name | nativehtmlkit select

no files to choose from

Too large to display. The message says how many rows fit at this width:

$row = [ordered]@{}; 0..15 | ForEach-Object { $row["c$_"] = 'v' }
$rows = 1..1871 | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject] $row }
ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $rows -Compress | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --multi

at most 1870 rows fit

Long lines push a page over 1 MiB; shorten them first:

1..2000 | ForEach-Object { "$_".PadLeft(600, '0') } | nativehtmlkit view

the host accepts 1048576 (1 MiB)

1..2000 | ForEach-Object { "$_".PadLeft(600, '0') } |
    ForEach-Object { if ($_.Length -gt 400) { $_.Substring(0, 400) + '...' } else { $_ } } | nativehtmlkit view

items.title: "Nothing happens when I click Submit"
items.text:
• select: something must be ticked, unless --allow-empty is given. The window says select at least one row before submitting.
  • form: a constraint failed; the window says Some required fields are invalid. Check required, pattern (it must match the whole value), min/max.
  • With --diagnostics debug the stderr log shows submit.rejected with the reason (empty_selection, invalid_form).

items.title: The script stops at the CLI
items.text: That is by design: the window waits for the person. Add --timeout for unattended runs (exit codes and scripting).

items.title: Get a log to report a problem
items.text:
$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID = 'report-1'
$log = 'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit --diagnostics trace select 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
[IO.File]::WriteAllLines((Join-Path (Get-Location) 'report.log'), [string[]] $log)
$log | Where-Object { $_ -like '*"component":"nativehtmlkit-cli"*' } | Select-Object -First 3 |
    ForEach-Object { $r = ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_; "$($r.role) $($r.event)" }
exit 0

launcher session.started
launcher host.spawned
backend backend.started

The CLI's records contain no data from your input; the host's records (also in the file) are a separate log, review them before you share it. More in environment and diagnostics.

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/troubleshooting.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Tutorial: a Git branch picker (Windows)
items.text:
You will write git-pick.ps1, a PowerShell script that lists your local Git branches in a native window, switches to the one you pick, and can delete merged branches in a multi-select list. It shows how to use nativehtmlkit select safely in scripts: objects as JSON, reading the result back, $LASTEXITCODE and timeouts. It works in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.

Time: about 20 minutes. You need: Git and nativehtmlkit on your PATH (install). Final code: examples/tutorial-branch-picker/git-pick.ps1. The same tutorial for bash: Linux. The bash version sends TSV; PowerShell builds objects, so this version sends JSON, which needs no clean-up of commit subjects.

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

The runs below were made in the examples folder of a clone of this repository (a Git work tree with the branches main, feature/login, fix/typo and release/1.4) against the released CLI 0.1.2 by scripts/test-docs.ps1, headless and with replayed results (how).

items.title: Step 1: pick a branch
items.text:
step1-pick.ps1:

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

<#
Branch picker tutorial, step 1: offer the local branches in a native list and report the choice.

Teaches: piping lines into `nativehtmlkit select`, capturing stdout, and the exit statuses
0 (chosen), 2 (cancelled), 124 (-Timeout expired) and anything else (error) through
$LASTEXITCODE. The PowerShell counterpart of step1-pick.sh.

Run:   .\step1-pick.ps1 [-Timeout SECONDS]     (inside a Git work tree)
Guide: docs/windows/tutorial-branch-picker.md (step 1 of 2)
#>
param([double] $Timeout = 0)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
try {
    $extra = @()
    if ($Timeout -gt 0) { $extra = '--timeout', [string] $Timeout }

    $choice = git for-each-ref '--format=%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ |
        nativehtmlkit select --title 'Pick a branch' @extra
    $status = $LASTEXITCODE
    switch ($status) {
        0       { "You chose: $choice" }
        2       { Write-Warning 'Cancelled' }
        124     { Write-Warning 'No choice made in time' }
        default { Write-Warning "nativehtmlkit select failed with exit status $status" }
    }
    exit $status
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}
  • git for-each-ref '--format=%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ prints one branch per line, which is the default lines input format.
  • nativehtmlkit select opens the window and blocks. On success it prints the chosen line and $LASTEXITCODE is 0.
  • $LASTEXITCODE is read once, right after the call, into $status.
  • -Timeout passes --timeout through only when given.

Run it inside any Git work tree:

.\tutorial-branch-picker\step1-pick.ps1 -Timeout 30

Nobody chose within the deadline:

WARNING: No choice made in time

After picking release/1.4:

release/1.4

You chose: release/1.4

After Cancel:



WARNING: Cancelled

items.title: Step 2: a table, switching, and deleting merged branches
items.text:
git-pick.ps1:

<#
git-pick.ps1: choose a local Git branch in a native window and switch to it (CLI tutorial final code).

Teaches: objects -> ConvertTo-Json -> `select --input-format json`, reading the chosen records
back, handling every exit status (0 chosen, 2 cancelled, 124 timed out, anything else an
error), multi-select with --multi, and stopping the script cleanly from a helper function.
The PowerShell counterpart of git-pick.sh.

Run:   .\git-pick.ps1 [-Timeout SECONDS]                 switch to the chosen branch
       .\git-pick.ps1 -DeleteMerged [-Timeout SECONDS]   delete chosen branches already merged
       .\git-pick.ps1 -Print                             show the table that would be offered
       (inside a Git work tree; needs `nativehtmlkit` on PATH)
Guide: docs/windows/tutorial-branch-picker.md
#>
param([double] $Timeout = 0, [switch] $DeleteMerged, [switch] $Print)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)

# One object per branch, most recently committed first. JSON carries any character safely,
# so commit subjects need no clean-up.
function Get-BranchTable([string[]] $Filter) {
    git for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate '--format=%(refname:short)%09%(committerdate:relative)%09%(subject)' @Filter refs/heads/ |
        ForEach-Object {
            $f = $_ -split "`t", 3
            [pscustomobject]@{ branch = $f[0]; updated = $f[1]; 'last commit' = $f[2] }
        }
}

# Runs `nativehtmlkit select` on the rows and returns the chosen branch names. On anything
# but a submit it explains the status and ends the script with it.
function Select-Branch([object[]] $Rows, [string] $Title, [string[]] $More = @()) {
    $extra = @()
    if ($Timeout -gt 0) { $extra = '--timeout', [string] $Timeout }
    $json = ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $Rows -Compress |
        nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --output-format json --title $Title @extra @More
    $status = $LASTEXITCODE
    switch ($status) {
        0       { return ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n") | ForEach-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { $_.branch } }
        2       { Write-Warning 'git-pick: cancelled; nothing changed' }
        124     { Write-Warning 'git-pick: no choice made in time; nothing changed' }
        default { Write-Warning "git-pick: nativehtmlkit select failed with exit status $status" }
    }
    exit $status
}

try {
    git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree *> $null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Warning 'git-pick: not inside a Git repository'; exit 1 }
    $current = git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD
    if (-not $current) { $current = '(detached HEAD)' }

    if ($Print) {
        Get-BranchTable | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Stream -Width 200
        exit 0
    }
    if (-not $DeleteMerged) {
        $branch = Select-Branch @(Get-BranchTable) "Switch branch (current: $current)"
        if ($branch -eq $current) { "Already on $branch"; exit 0 }
        git switch --quiet $branch
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit 1 }
        "Switched to $branch"
        exit 0
    }

    # Offer every merged branch except the one you are on.
    $merged = @(Get-BranchTable '--merged', 'HEAD' | Where-Object { $_.branch -ne $current })
    if ($merged.Count -eq 0) { 'No merged branches to delete'; exit 0 }
    foreach ($branch in (Select-Branch $merged 'Delete merged branches' '--multi')) {
        git branch --quiet -d $branch
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit 1 }
        "Deleted $branch"
    }
    exit 0
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}
  • Get-BranchTable turns each git for-each-ref line into an object with branch, updated and last commit; ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $Rows sends them as one JSON array (also when there is only one).
  • --output-format json returns the chosen objects exactly as they went in; the script keeps their branch property.
  • Select-Branch turns every exit status into a clear message and ends the script with it: 2 when cancelled, 124 when -Timeout expired.
  • -DeleteMerged offers only branches merged into HEAD (minus the current one) and passes --multi, so the user can tick several rows. Each is deleted with git branch -d, which refuses anything not merged.
  • -Print shows the table without opening a window.

items.title: Try it
items.text:
The table that would be offered (no window):

.\tutorial-branch-picker\git-pick.ps1 -Print | Select-String -Pattern '^(main|fix/typo|feature/login|release/1\.4) ' |
    ForEach-Object { ($_.Line -split ' ')[0] }

main
fix/typo
feature/login
release/1.4

Switch branch, giving up after 20 seconds (exit 124):

.\tutorial-branch-picker\git-pick.ps1 -Timeout 20

WARNING: git-pick: no choice made in time; nothing changed

With feature/login picked, the CLI returns that object and the script switches:

[{"branch":"feature/login","updated":"6 days ago","last commit":"Add the example scripts"}]

Switched to feature/login

Tidy up merged branches (-DeleteMerged, --multi):

.\tutorial-branch-picker\git-pick.ps1 -DeleteMerged

[{"branch":"fix/typo","updated":"4 days ago","last commit":"Fix the \"quick start\" typo"},{"branch":"release/1.4","updated":"6 days ago","last commit":"Add the example scripts"}]

Deleted fix/typo
Deleted release/1.4

Save it as git-pick.ps1 in a folder on your PATH to run it from any repository.

items.title: What you learned
items.text:
• Send objects as JSON and read the chosen objects back with ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject.
  • Check $LASTEXITCODE right after the call and hand it on with exit.
  • Use --multi and --timeout.

items.title: Where next
items.text:
• form collects several values at once from trusted HTML; the project picker tutorial uses select, form and view together.
  • Recipes, and every option on select.
  • For anything more interactive than one decision, use the PowerShell or Python SDK (see nativehtmlkit.github.io).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/tutorial-branch-picker.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Tutorial: build a project picker (Windows)
items.text:
In this tutorial you build proj.ps1, a small PowerShell tool that remembers project folders and lets you jump to one by picking it in a native window:

.\proj.ps1 add C:\src\website       # a form asks for name and tags
Set-Location (.\proj.ps1 pick)      # a table of projects; pick one, Submit
.\proj.ps1 list                     # a read-only table
.\proj.ps1 remove                   # tick projects, confirm

On the way you use all three interactive commands (select, form, view), two input formats, the exit contract, encoding for trusted HTML, and a stylesheet. The finished script is examples/tutorial/proj.ps1 (about 120 lines, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7); every step below is a part of it. The same tutorial for bash: Linux.

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

You need: the CLI release extracted and on PATH (install).

items.title: Step 1: a first picker
items.text:
select reads records from stdin, one per line by default, and prints the chosen one:

'C:\src\website', 'C:\src\cli', 'C:\notes' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Open project'

A window lists the three paths with a radio button each. Pick one and press Submit selection: the path is printed and $LASTEXITCODE is 0. Press Cancel: nothing is printed and $LASTEXITCODE is 2.

That is already a usable tool, but a path alone is a poor label, and we want to store more (a name, tags, the date added).

items.title: Step 2: store projects as JSON lines
items.text:
Keep one JSON object per line in a file. NDJSON is both easy to append to and an input format of the CLI, so the file can be piped straight into select:

{"name":"website","path":"C:\\src\\website","tags":"work, web","added":"2026-11-16"}
{"name":"cli","path":"C:\\src\\cli","tags":"rust","added":"2026-11-16"}

The store lives in %APPDATA%\proj\projects.ndjson unless $env:PROJ_FILE says otherwise, and is always read and written as UTF-8 without BOM:

$store = $env:PROJ_FILE
if (-not $store) {
    $base = if ($env:APPDATA) { $env:APPDATA } else { Join-Path $HOME '.config' }
    $store = Join-Path $base 'proj/projects.ndjson'
}

With --input-format ndjson the window shows a table with the columns name, path, tags, added. With --output-format json the result is a JSON array holding the chosen record exactly as stored:

function Invoke-Pick {
    Assert-Projects
    $picked = Get-StoreText | ui select --input-format ndjson --output-format json --title 'Open project'
    (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $picked)[0].path
}

select refuses empty input (exit 1, no selectable input rows), so check first:

function Stop-Proj([string] $Message) { Write-Warning "proj: $Message"; exit 1 }
function Assert-Projects { if ((Get-Records).Count -eq 0) { Stop-Proj 'no projects yet; add one with: proj add [DIR]' } }

items.title: Step 3: one place for the exit contract
items.text:
Every call of the CLI can end in four ways: 0 (a result on stdout), 2 (Cancel), 124 (--timeout), or 1 and others (an error already explained on stderr). Handle that once. Inside a function, exit ends the whole script, with that status:

function ui {
    $out = $input | nativehtmlkit @args @style
    switch ($LASTEXITCODE) {
        0       { return ($out -join "`n") }
        2       { exit 2 }
        124     { Write-Warning 'proj: no answer in time'; exit 124 }
        default { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
    }
}

$input passes the pipeline on to the CLI, @args the arguments, and @style the stylesheet from step 7. A cancelled proj.ps1 pick exits 2 and prints nothing, so the caller can tell.

items.title: Step 4: add projects with a form
items.text:
form --html FILE shows your own HTML form and prints {"entries":[...]} on Submit. The fragment is trusted HTML, so the folder name and path, which come from the file system, must be encoded before they go into it:

function Enc([string] $s) { [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($s) }

    $form = @"
<form id="nhk-form">
  <p><label>Name <input name="name" required maxlength="60" value="$(Enc (Split-Path -Leaf $dir))"></label></p>
  <p><label>Directory <input name="path" required value="$(Enc $dir)"></label></p>
  <p><label>Tags <input name="tags" placeholder="work, rust" pattern="[A-Za-z0-9 ,_-]*"
         title="letters, digits, spaces, commas, - and _"></label></p>
</form>
"@
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($html, $form, $Utf8)
    try { $result = ui form --html $html --title 'Add project' }
    finally { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $html -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }

The form element must have id="nhk-form". Core checks required, maxlength and pattern when the user presses Submit; an invalid form stays open with a message. The result looks like this:

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"name","value":"website"},{"kind":"text","name":"path","value":"C:\\src\\website"},{"kind":"text","name":"tags","value":"work, web"}]}

The entries become one ordered record, which is checked and appended:

    $values = @{}
    foreach ($e in (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $result).entries) { $values[$e.name] = $e.value }
    $record = [ordered]@{ name = $values.name; path = $values.path; tags = "$($values.tags)"; added = (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd') }
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $record.path -PathType Container)) { Stop-Proj "not a directory: $($record.path)" }
    if (@(Get-Records | Where-Object { $_.path -eq $record.path }).Count) { Stop-Proj "already bookmarked: $($record.path)" }

Messages go to the warning stream; the success output is reserved for results (that is what makes Set-Location (.\proj.ps1 pick) work).

items.title: Step 5: list them
items.text:
view shows the same file read-only. It has no result; closing it exits 0:

function Invoke-List {
    Assert-Projects
    Get-StoreText | ui view --input-format ndjson --title "Projects ($((Get-Records).Count))" | Out-Null
}

items.title: Step 6: remove with confirmation
items.text:
--multi turns the radio buttons into checkboxes. --output-format ndjson returns the chosen records one per line, exactly as stored. A second select asks for confirmation; its safe answer is first and nothing is preselected:

    $count = $picked.Count
    $answer = 'Keep them', "Remove $count project(s)" | ui select --title "Remove $count project(s)?"
    if (-not $answer.StartsWith('Remove')) { Write-Warning 'proj: nothing removed'; return }

The store is rewritten through a temporary file and Move-Item, so an interrupted run never leaves half a file.

items.title: Step 7: give it a look
items.text:
--css adds a stylesheet after the built-in one. The page's colours are CSS custom properties, so small overrides go a long way (examples/tutorial/proj.css):

:root { --accent: #3fa37a; }
h1 { font-size: 18px; letter-spacing: .02em; }
td { color: #dfe7f1; }
button.primary { background: #2f8a63; border-color: #3fa37a; }

ui passes it on every call:

$style = '--css', (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'proj.css')

items.title: Step 8: the command dispatcher
items.text:
A validated parameter chooses the command; the console encoding is restored at the end:

param(
    [ValidateSet('pick', 'add', 'list', 'remove')] [string] $Command = 'pick',
    [string] $Directory = '.'
)

A script cannot change its caller's location by itself, so add a function to your $PROFILE:

function p { $dir = & "$HOME\tools\proj.ps1" pick; if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { Set-Location -LiteralPath $dir } }

After Cancel, proj.ps1 pick exits 2 with no output and p stays where it is.

items.title: Step 9: try it
items.text:
The examples below run proj.ps1 from the repository's examples folder with a store in the current folder. They were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1, headless and with replayed results (how).

Add a project. The form opens with the folder's name and path filled in:

$env:PROJ_FILE = Join-Path (Get-Location) 'projects.ndjson'
.\tutorial\proj.ps1 add data

When the user submits it, the record is stored:

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"name","value":"sample data"},{"kind":"text","name":"path","value":"data"},{"kind":"text","name":"tags","value":"demo"}]}

WARNING: proj: added data

Pick one (the store here has two projects):

$env:PROJ_FILE = Join-Path (Get-Location) 'projects.ndjson'
$lines = '{"name":"sample data","path":"data","tags":"demo","added":"2026-11-16"}',
         '{"name":"styles","path":"css","tags":"","added":"2026-11-16"}'
[IO.File]::WriteAllText($env:PROJ_FILE, ($lines -join "`n") + "`n")
.\tutorial\proj.ps1 pick

[{"name":"styles","path":"css","tags":"","added":"2026-11-16"}]

css

After Cancel, proj.ps1 pick prints nothing and exits 2:

List and remove:

$env:PROJ_FILE = Join-Path (Get-Location) 'projects.ndjson'
$lines = '{"name":"sample data","path":"data","tags":"demo","added":"2026-11-16"}',
         '{"name":"styles","path":"css","tags":"","added":"2026-11-16"}'
[IO.File]::WriteAllText($env:PROJ_FILE, ($lines -join "`n") + "`n")
.\tutorial\proj.ps1 list

$env:PROJ_FILE = Join-Path (Get-Location) 'projects.ndjson'
$lines = '{"name":"sample data","path":"data","tags":"demo","added":"2026-11-16"}',
         '{"name":"styles","path":"css","tags":"","added":"2026-11-16"}'
[IO.File]::WriteAllText($env:PROJ_FILE, ($lines -join "`n") + "`n")
.\tutorial\proj.ps1 remove 3> $null
$status = $LASTEXITCODE
@(Get-Content $env:PROJ_FILE).Count
exit $status

2

Tick sample data, then confirm with Remove 1 project(s):

{"name":"sample data","path":"data","tags":"demo","added":"2026-11-16"}

Remove 1 project(s)

1

To test your own tools like this, see test your scripts without a desktop.

items.title: Command reference (Windows)
items.text: Every command and option with a runnable PowerShell example. The exact, system-independent rules are in the reference for both systems.

items.title: Commands
items.text:
• select: choose rows
  • view: show records read-only
  • form: collect values with an HTML form
  • doctor, help and version

items.title: Formats
items.text:
• Input formats
  • Output formats

items.title: doctor, help and version (Windows)
items.text:
nativehtmlkit doctor reports which Core host executable the CLI would use and checks that it starts. help, --help and --version print information. None of them opens a window or reads stdin. Exact rules: OS-neutral reference.

The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

items.title: doctor
items.text:
nativehtmlkit doctor

prints three lines, for example:

NativeHTMLKit CLI 0.1.2
Core host: C:\Tools\nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-windows-x64\nativehtmlkit-host.exe
nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3

The third line is the host's own --version output. Check it in a script:

if ((nativehtmlkit doctor) -contains 'nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3') {
    'qualified host found'
} else {
    Write-Error 'install the release archive, or set NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY'
}

qualified host found
Situation Exit stderr host found and it answered --version 0 no host anywhere 1 error[host.not_found]: NativeHTMLKit Core host not found. ... --host/NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY names no file 1 error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: <path> the file cannot be started 1 error[host.not_found]: cannot start the Core host (<reason>) it failed, printed nothing, or took over 10 s 1 error[host.failed]: ...

items.title: doctor --host PATH
items.text:
Check a specific host executable:

nativehtmlkit doctor --host C:\missing\nativehtmlkit-host.exe

nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: C:\missing\nativehtmlkit-host.exe

A file that is not a program cannot be started:

Set-Content -Path fake-host.exe -Value 'not a program'
nativehtmlkit doctor --host .\fake-host.exe

nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: cannot start the Core host

items.title: doctor --diagnostics LEVEL
items.text:
doctor writes no diagnostic records of its own at any level; the option is accepted so that the same global options work for every command:

$err = nativehtmlkit doctor --diagnostics trace 2>&1 | Where-Object { $_ -is [System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord] }
@($err).Count

0

items.title: doctor --timeout, --rpc-timeout, --liveness-interval, --startup-timeout
items.text:
Accepted and ignored by doctor: it never opens a window, and its version check has its own fixed 10-second limit. They are useful when one array of options is splatted into every command:

$opts = '--timeout', '120', '--rpc-timeout', '10', '--liveness-interval', '2', '--startup-timeout', '30'
nativehtmlkit doctor @opts | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { 'doctor ok' }
'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select @opts
"select ended with $LASTEXITCODE"

doctor ok
select ended with 124

items.title: --version, -V
items.text:
nativehtmlkit --version
nhk -V

nativehtmlkit 0.1.2
nativehtmlkit 0.1.2

items.title: --help, -h, help COMMAND
items.text:
--help prints the full help, -h a summary; after a command they describe that command. help COMMAND is the same as COMMAND --help:

nativehtmlkit --help | Select-Object -Last 1

Exit status: 0 submitted/viewed, 1 error, 2 cancelled, 124 --timeout expired, 130 Ctrl+C/SIGINT, 143 SIGTERM, 129 SIGHUP.

(143 and 129 are Unix signals; on Windows the interruption is Ctrl+C, 130.)

(nativehtmlkit doctor --help | Select-String -SimpleMatch -- '--host <HOST>' | Select-Object -First 1).Line
nativehtmlkit -h | Select-Object -First 1
(nativehtmlkit help select | Select-String -SimpleMatch -- '--allow-empty').Line

      --host <HOST>
Native HTML/CSS windows for shell pipelines (alias: nhk)
      --allow-empty

help takes a command name, not options: nativehtmlkit help --help is a usage error (exit 1).

items.title: The nhk.exe alias
items.text:
The release archive contains nhk.exe, an identical copy of nativehtmlkit.exe; it finds the host beside itself the same way:

nhk doctor | Select-Object -First 1

NativeHTMLKit CLI 0.1.2

items.title: form: collect values with an HTML form (Windows)
items.text:
nativehtmlkit form --html FILE shows your own HTML form with the CLI's Cancel and Submit buttons below it. When the user submits a valid form, one line of JSON with the values is written to stdout. stdin is not read. Exact rules: OS-neutral reference.

nativehtmlkit form [OPTIONS] --html FILE
Outcome $LASTEXITCODE stdout Submit, every constraint satisfied 0 {"entries":[...]} Cancel, or the window closed 2 empty --timeout expired 124 empty error (missing file, no nhk-form, ...) 1 empty

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how). How to write and style forms: CSS and forms.
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --html FILE (required)
items.text:
A trusted UTF-8 HTML fragment (at most 256 KiB) that contains <form id="nhk-form">. Give every control a name; do not add a submit button of your own. sample-form.html (also in the release archive) is the smallest useful one:

<form id="nhk-form">
  <label>Project name <input id="project" name="project" required placeholder="My NativeHTMLKit App"></label>
  <p><label>Environment
    <select name="environment"><option value="development">Development</option><option value="production">Production</option></select>
  </label></p>
  <p><label><input type="checkbox" name="confirm" value="yes"> I confirm the details</label></p>
</form>

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html

After typing Demo App, keeping Development and ticking the checkbox, Submit prints this line (the exact result the release's GUI qualification asserts on Windows and Linux):

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"project","value":"Demo App"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"development"},{"kind":"text","name":"confirm","value":"yes"}]}

Turn the entries into a hashtable. A checkbox that is not ticked has no entry:

$json = nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
$values = @{}
foreach ($e in (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n")).entries) { $values[$e.name] = $e.value }
"project=$($values.project) environment=$($values.environment) confirm=$($values.confirm)"

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"project","value":"Demo App"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"development"}]}

With that result (checkbox not ticked) the script prints:

project=Demo App environment=development confirm=

The fragment must contain the form element nhk-form; otherwise nothing opens:

Set-Content -Path no-id.html -Value '<form><input name="a"></form>'
nativehtmlkit form --html no-id.html

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: --html must contain <form id="nhk-form"> with the controls to submit

--html is required:

nativehtmlkit form

error: the following required arguments were not provided:
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: Generated forms: encode every value
items.text:
The fragment is trusted markup. Anything that comes from data (file names, Git tags, user names) must be HTML-encoded before it goes in, with [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode. Write the file as UTF-8 without BOM:

function Enc([string] $s) { [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($s) }
$version = 'v1.2.3 <rc> & "beta"'
$html = @"
<form id="nhk-form">
  <label>Version <input name="version" required value="$(Enc $version)"></label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="publish" value="yes"> Publish now</label>
</form>
"@
$path = Join-Path (Get-Location) 'release.html'
[IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $html, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
[Console]::Error.WriteLine(([regex]::Match($html, 'value="[^"]*"')).Value)
nativehtmlkit form --html $path

value="v1.2.3 <rc> & "beta""
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --title TITLE
items.text:
Window title and heading (default Input form), 1-128 characters, shown as text:

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --title 'New project'
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --css FILE
items.text:
A trusted style sheet added after the built-in one. css/form.css lays the form out as a grid of labelled fields:

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --css css/form.css --title 'New project'
path: form: collect values with an HTML form

items.title: --timeout SECONDS
items.text:
A form left open is closed after the deadline, with exit 124 and no output:

$json = nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --timeout 600
switch ($LASTEXITCODE) {
    0       { $json }
    2       { Write-Warning 'cancelled'; exit 2 }
    124     { Write-Warning 'the form was left open for 10 minutes'; exit 124 }
    default { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
}

WARNING: the form was left open for 10 minutes

Write-Warning text goes to the warning stream; when a script's output is redirected, as here, PowerShell writes it to stdout with the WARNING: prefix.

items.title: --host PATH
items.text:
$coreHost = (nativehtmlkit doctor | Select-String '^Core host: (.+)$').Matches[0].Groups[1].Value
nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --host $coreHost

exit 0

nativehtmlkit form --html sample-form.html --rpc-timeout 15

items.title: What the result contains
items.text: entries are the form's successful controls in document order, as HTML form submission defines them: one {"kind":"text","name":...,"value":...} per named, enabled control that has a value. All values are strings. Unticked checkboxes and radio groups have no entry; a <select multiple> has one entry per chosen option; names may repeat; a file input gives {"kind":"file","name":...,"path":...,"filename":...}. Core checks required, pattern, min/max/step, minlength/maxlength and type="email"/"url" when the user clicks Submit; an invalid form stays open with Some required fields are invalid. Details: form reference.

items.title: select: choose rows (Windows)
items.text:
nativehtmlkit select shows the records piped into it as a table with a pick column and writes the rows the user submits to stdout. This page shows every option of the command with a PowerShell example; each one works in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7. The exact rules are in the OS-neutral reference.

nativehtmlkit select [OPTIONS] < records
Outcome $LASTEXITCODE stdout Submit selection 0 the chosen rows, in input order Cancel, or the window closed 2 empty --timeout expired 124 empty error (bad input or option, no host) 1 empty; nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: ... on stderr

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository, which has the sample files data\servers.csv, data\issues.json and css\light.css. They were run against the released Windows CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 (and in PowerShell 7) by scripts/test-docs.ps1; a "Submit prints" block shows the exact text the released code writes when the user ticks the rows named above it (how the examples are verified). Set up UTF-8 first when your data is not plain ASCII (why).

items.title: Without options: one line
items.text:
Each string piped in is one row (--input-format lines). The window has one radio button per row; the chosen line is printed.

'small', 'medium', 'large' | nativehtmlkit select

Submit prints, after picking medium:

medium

Capture it in a variable and check $LASTEXITCODE right after the call. A non-zero status is not an exception:

$size = 'small', 'medium', 'large' | nativehtmlkit select
switch ($LASTEXITCODE) {
    0       { "size: $size" }
    2       { 'cancelled' }
    124     { 'no answer in time' }
    default { Write-Error "failed with $LASTEXITCODE" }
}

medium

After the user picks medium the script prints:

size: medium

items.title: --multi
items.text:
Checkboxes instead of radio buttons: any number of rows. The chosen rows come back in input order, whatever order they were ticked in; several lines arrive in PowerShell as an array of strings.

'alpha', 'beta', 'gamma', 'delta' | nativehtmlkit select --multi

Submit prints, after ticking delta, then alpha:

alpha
delta

Submit with nothing ticked is refused: the window stays open and says select at least one row before submitting:

'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --multi

items.title: --allow-empty
items.text:
Accept Submit with nothing ticked. stdout is then empty for lines (and ndjson), [] for json, the header line for csv/tsv:

$extras = @('clear cache', 'rotate logs', 'vacuum database' |
    nativehtmlkit select --multi --allow-empty --title 'Also run')
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
"$($extras.Count) extra task(s)"

Submit with nothing ticked prints nothing and exits 0:



'name,size', 'a.txt,1', 'b.txt,2' |
    nativehtmlkit select --multi --allow-empty --input-format csv --output-format json

[]

items.title: --input-format FORMAT
items.text:
How stdin is parsed: lines (default), csv, tsv, json, ndjson. In PowerShell the most useful one is json: choose the properties with Select-Object, then ConvertTo-Json (input formats):

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv

Get-ChildItem -File | Select-Object Name, Length, @{ n = 'Modified'; e = { $_.LastWriteTime.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') } } |
    ConvertTo-Json | nativehtmlkit select --input-format json

items.title: --no-headers
items.text:
For csv and tsv: the first record is data, and the columns are named column_1 ... column_N:

'web-01,healthy', 'web-02,degraded', 'db-01,healthy' |
    nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --no-headers --output-format json

Submit prints, after picking web-02:

[{"column_1":"web-02","column_2":"degraded"}]

items.title: --output-format FORMAT
items.text:
What Submit writes: same (default: the input format), lines, csv, tsv, json, ndjson (output formats). JSON out, read back as objects:

$json = Get-Content data\servers.csv |
    nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
(ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n")) | ForEach-Object { $_.host }

[{"host":"web-02","role":"frontend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"4","memory_gib":"8","status":"degraded","notes":"disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled"},{"host":"db-02","role":"database","region":"us-east","cpu_cores":"16","memory_gib":"128","status":"maintenance","notes":"replica, patching until 18:00"}]

The replayed result above is what Submit prints after ticking web-02 and db-02; the script then prints:

web-02
db-02

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json

[{"host":"web-02","role":"frontend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"4","memory_gib":"8","status":"degraded","notes":"disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled"},{"host":"db-02","role":"database","region":"us-east","cpu_cores":"16","memory_gib":"128","status":"maintenance","notes":"replica, patching until 18:00"}]

items.title: --title TITLE
items.text:
The window title and the heading of the page (default Select an item). 1 to 128 characters, no control characters; it is shown as text, never as markup:

'main', 'feature/login' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Switch to <branch> & pull'

A title that is too long (or empty) is refused before any window opens:

'a' | nativehtmlkit select --title ('x' * 129)

nativehtmlkit: error[usage.invalid]: --title must be nonempty, at most 128 characters, with no control characters

Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not pass an empty string argument ('') to a native program at all, so --title '' there is a usage error of the argument parser instead (also exit 1).

items.title: --css FILE
items.text:
A trusted UTF-8 style sheet (at most 256 KiB) added after the built-in one (CSS and forms):

'Europe/Prague', 'America/New_York', 'Asia/Tokyo' |
    nativehtmlkit select --title 'Time zone' --css css/light.css

items.title: --timeout SECONDS
items.text:
Give the user a deadline. Without it the window waits as long as it takes. When the deadline passes the window is closed, stderr says so, stdout stays empty and $LASTEXITCODE is 124:

'deploy', 'skip' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Deploy now?' --timeout 60
"exit status: $LASTEXITCODE"

Nobody answered within the deadline (60 s here; the test uses a shorter one):

exit status: 124

nativehtmlkit: no decision before the --timeout deadline; the window was closed

items.title: --host PATH
items.text:
Use this Core host executable instead of the one beside the CLI. The release archive has the qualified host next to nativehtmlkit.exe, so you only need this for development builds:

$coreHost = (nativehtmlkit doctor | Select-String '^Core host: (.+)$').Matches[0].Groups[1].Value
'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --host $coreHost

($host is a built-in variable in PowerShell, hence $coreHost.) A path that does not exist is an error, before anything else happens:

'a' | nativehtmlkit select --host C:\missing\nativehtmlkit-host.exe

nativehtmlkit: error[host.not_found]: Core host binary does not exist: C:\missing\nativehtmlkit-host.exe

items.title: --diagnostics LEVEL
items.text:
off, normal (default), debug, trace: structured JSON records about the session on stderr, separate from the result on stdout (environment and diagnostics):

$log = 'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --diagnostics debug 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
$events = $log | Where-Object { $_.StartsWith('{') } | ForEach-Object { ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_ } |
    Where-Object { $_.component -eq 'nativehtmlkit-cli' } | ForEach-Object { $_.event }
$events -contains 'window.ready'

True

items.title: --rpc-timeout SECONDS
items.text:
How long the CLI waits for the host to answer one request before it treats the host as hung (default 30). The person in front of the window is never affected by it:

'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --rpc-timeout 10

items.title: --liveness-interval SECONDS
items.text:
Idle time between the CLI's "are you alive?" probes to the host while the window is open (default 5; 0 turns probing off):

'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --liveness-interval 2 --rpc-timeout 5

'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --liveness-interval 0

items.title: --startup-timeout SECONDS
items.text:
How long the host may take to open the window (default 15). Raise it on a slow, loaded machine:

'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --startup-timeout 60

items.title: -h, --help
items.text:
(nativehtmlkit select --help | Select-String -SimpleMatch -- '--multi').Line

      --multi

The usage line names the program nativehtmlkit.exe select [OPTIONS]. -h prints the same options in one line each.

items.title: Options in any order
items.text:
Options can come before or after the command name; each may be given once:

'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit --rpc-timeout 10 select --multi --allow-empty

A repeated or unknown option is a usage error, exit 1:

'a' | nativehtmlkit select --multi --multi
