items.title: view: show records read-only (Windows)
items.text:
nativehtmlkit view shows the records piped into it in a window with a single Close button. It never writes to stdout. Plain lines are shown as one wrapping, scrolling text block; every other input format as a table. Exact rules: OS-neutral reference.

nativehtmlkit view [OPTIONS] < records
Outcome $LASTEXITCODE stdout Close, or the window closed 0 empty --timeout expired 124 empty error 1 empty; nativehtmlkit: error[<code>]: ... on stderr

view blocks until the window is closed. Unlike select it accepts no records: an empty viewer is fine. It has no --multi, --allow-empty or --output-format.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

items.title: Without options: text
items.text:
Get-Content data\app.log | nativehtmlkit view

Markup in the text is shown literally: the <script> in that log stays text. Any command output works; Out-String -Stream turns formatted objects into lines first:

Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 30 |
    Format-Table Id, ProcessName, CPU -AutoSize | Out-String -Stream -Width 200 | nativehtmlkit view

Nothing to show is not an error:

@() | nativehtmlkit view

items.title: --input-format FORMAT
items.text:
lines (default), csv, tsv, json, ndjson; every format except lines is shown as a table (input formats):

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv

Get-Content data\app.ndjson | nativehtmlkit view --input-format ndjson

Get-Content -Raw data\issues.json | nativehtmlkit view --input-format json

issues.json has nested values (user, labels): they appear as compact JSON in their cells. Reshape the objects first for a readable table:

Get-Content -Raw data\issues.json | ConvertFrom-Json | ForEach-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object {
    [pscustomobject]@{ '#' = $_.number; Title = $_.title; Author = $_.user.login; Labels = ($_.labels.name -join ', ') }
} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | nativehtmlkit view --input-format json

(ForEach-Object { $_ } unrolls the array: Windows PowerShell 5.1 passes a parsed JSON array down the pipeline as one object.)

"name`tsize`tmodified", "report.pdf`t120 KiB`t2026-11-14", "notes.txt`t2 KiB`t2026-11-16" |
    nativehtmlkit view --input-format tsv

items.title: --no-headers
items.text:
For csv/tsv without a header row; columns are named column_1 ... column_N:

'alice,admin,2026-01-04', 'bob,dev,2026-03-17', 'carol,ops,2026-06-30' |
    nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --no-headers

items.title: --title TITLE
items.text:
Window title and heading (default Output viewer), 1-128 characters, shown as text:

$lines = Get-Content data\app.log
$lines | nativehtmlkit view --title "app.log ($($lines.Count) lines)"

items.title: --css FILE
items.text:
A trusted style sheet added after the built-in one (CSS and forms):

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --css css/light.css

items.title: --timeout SECONDS
items.text:
Close the viewer by itself after a while. Exit 0 (closed) and 124 (deadline) both mean "done looking", so a script can carry on after either:

Get-Content data\app.log | nativehtmlkit view --timeout 300 --title 'Build log'
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -and $LASTEXITCODE -ne 124) { exit 1 }
'continuing'
exit 0

continuing

items.title: --host PATH
items.text:
$coreHost = (nativehtmlkit doctor | Select-String '^Core host: (.+)$').Matches[0].Groups[1].Value
'pinned host' | nativehtmlkit view --host $coreHost

items.title: --diagnostics LEVEL
items.text:
$log = 'hello' | nativehtmlkit view --diagnostics debug 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
$started = $log | Where-Object { $_ -like '*"event":"session.started"*' } | ForEach-Object { ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_ }
"$($started.context.mode) $($started.context.rows)x$($started.context.columns)"
exit 0

view 1x1

items.title: --rpc-timeout SECONDS, --liveness-interval SECONDS, --startup-timeout SECONDS
items.text:
The host watchdogs (defaults 30, 5 and 15 seconds). They limit how long the CLI waits for a host that stopped working, never the person reading (global options):

Get-Content data\app.log | nativehtmlkit view --rpc-timeout 10

Get-Content data\app.log | nativehtmlkit view --liveness-interval 10

Get-Content data\app.log | nativehtmlkit view --startup-timeout 45

items.title: -h, --help
items.text:
(nativehtmlkit view --help | Select-String -SimpleMatch -- '--no-headers').Line

      --no-headers

items.title: Options that view does not have
items.text:
'a' | nativehtmlkit view --multi

error: unexpected argument '--multi' found

items.title: Limits
items.text:
At most 2,000 lines or records, 32 columns and an 8 MiB stdin; the generated page must stay under 1 MiB. More is an error, never a silent truncation, so cut first:

1..100000 | Select-Object -Last 2000 | nativehtmlkit view --title 'last 2000'

1..2001 | nativehtmlkit view

nativehtmlkit: error[input.invalid]: 2001 rows exceeds the 2000-row initial GUI limit

See view logs for long lines and the Windows event log, and the limits reference.

items.title: Windows examples
items.text:
Every example is a complete program, verified against the real NativeHTMLKit host. Open one to see a screenshot, how to run it and its full source.

Example What it does Pick a Git branch Switch to a branch chosen from a table of recent branches with their last commit. Delete files with confirmation Tick files, confirm in a second window, then delete exactly the ticked files. Choose processes to stop Pick processes in a table and stop or signal exactly those. Choose a Docker container Pick a container, then show its logs, restart, stop it or open a shell. Choose from JSON API output Reshape a REST response, pick issues and print their URLs. Review and export CSV reports View a CSV report, or export the rows you tick to a new CSV file. View logs Show the end of a text or JSON-lines log (Windows: also the event log). Search only the files you tick Tick files in a window, then search only those for a pattern. A deployment form Collect validated deployment parameters, confirm production, return them typed. Choose a time zone in a light theme Pick one time zone from a long list in a window restyled with --css. Restart, stop or start Windows services Pick Windows services, then the action to apply to them. Project picker (tutorial) Bookmark project directories, pick one to jump to, list and remove them. Branch picker, step 1 (tutorial) Offer the local branches in a list and report the choice and exit status. git-pick: switch and delete branches (tutorial) Switch to a branch from a table, or delete merged branches ticked in a list.

items.title: Branch picker, step 1 (tutorial)
items.text:
Offer the local branches in a list and report the choice and exit status.

Same example in Linux: Branch picker, step 1 (tutorial)

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: lines input; capturing stdout; exit statuses 0, 2, 124.

items.title: Run it
items.text: .\tutorial-branch-picker\step1-pick.ps1 [-Timeout SECONDS]

items.title: Source: tutorial-branch-picker/step1-pick.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
Branch picker tutorial, step 1: offer the local branches in a native list and report the choice.

Teaches: piping lines into `nativehtmlkit select`, capturing stdout, and the exit statuses
0 (chosen), 2 (cancelled), 124 (-Timeout expired) and anything else (error) through
$LASTEXITCODE. The PowerShell counterpart of step1-pick.sh.

Run:   .\step1-pick.ps1 [-Timeout SECONDS]     (inside a Git work tree)
Guide: docs/windows/tutorial-branch-picker.md (step 1 of 2)
#>
param([double] $Timeout = 0)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
try {
    $extra = @()

    $choice = git for-each-ref '--format=%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ |
        nativehtmlkit select --title 'Pick a branch' @extra
    $status = $LASTEXITCODE
    switch ($status) {
        0       { "You chose: $choice" }
        2       { Write-Warning 'Cancelled' }
        124     { Write-Warning 'No choice made in time' }

items.title: git-pick: switch and delete branches (tutorial)
items.text:
Switch to a branch from a table, or delete merged branches ticked in a list.

Same example in Linux: git-pick: switch and delete branches (tutorial)

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: TSV or JSON tables; lines output; --multi; every exit status.

items.title: Run it
items.text: .\tutorial-branch-picker\git-pick.ps1 [-DeleteMerged | -Print] [-Timeout SECONDS]

items.title: Source: tutorial-branch-picker/git-pick.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
git-pick.ps1: choose a local Git branch in a native window and switch to it (CLI tutorial final code).

Teaches: objects -> ConvertTo-Json -> `select --input-format json`, reading the chosen records
back, handling every exit status (0 chosen, 2 cancelled, 124 timed out, anything else an
error), multi-select with --multi, and stopping the script cleanly from a helper function.
The PowerShell counterpart of git-pick.sh.

Run:   .\git-pick.ps1 [-Timeout SECONDS]                 switch to the chosen branch
       .\git-pick.ps1 -DeleteMerged [-Timeout SECONDS]   delete chosen branches already merged
       .\git-pick.ps1 -Print                             show the table that would be offered
       (inside a Git work tree; needs `nativehtmlkit` on PATH)
Guide: docs/windows/tutorial-branch-picker.md
#>
param([double] $Timeout = 0, [switch] $DeleteMerged, [switch] $Print)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)

# One object per branch, most recently committed first. JSON carries any character safely,
# so commit subjects need no clean-up.
function Get-BranchTable([string[]] $Filter) {
    git for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate '--format=%(refname:short)%09%(committerdate:relative)%09%(subject)' @Filter refs/heads/ |
        ForEach-Object {
            $f = $_ -split "`t", 3
            [pscustomobject]@{ branch = $f[0]; updated = $f[1]; 'last commit' = $f[2] }
        }
}

# Runs `nativehtmlkit select` on the rows and returns the chosen branch names. On anything
# but a submit it explains the status and ends the script with it.
function Select-Branch([object[]] $Rows, [string] $Title, [string[]] $More = @()) {
    $extra = @()
    if ($Timeout -gt 0) { $extra = '--timeout', [string] $Timeout }
    $json = ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $Rows -Compress |
        nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --output-format json --title $Title @extra @More
    $status = $LASTEXITCODE
    switch ($status) {
        0       { return ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n") | ForEach-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { $_.branch } }
        2       { Write-Warning 'git-pick: cancelled; nothing changed' }
        124     { Write-Warning 'git-pick: no choice made in time; nothing changed' }
        default { Write-Warning "git-pick: nativehtmlkit select failed with exit status $status" }
    }
    exit $status
}

try {
    git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree *> $null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Warning 'git-pick: not inside a Git repository'; exit 1 }
    $current = git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD
    if (-not $current) { $current = '(detached HEAD)' }

    if ($Print) {
        Get-BranchTable | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Stream -Width 200
        exit 0
    }
    if (-not $DeleteMerged) {
        $branch = Select-Branch @(Get-BranchTable) "Switch branch (current: $current)"
        if ($branch -eq $current) { "Already on $branch"; exit 0 }
        git switch --quiet $branch
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit 1 }
        "Switched to $branch"
        exit 0
    }

    # Offer every merged branch except the one you are on.
    $merged = @(Get-BranchTable '--merged', 'HEAD' | Where-Object { $_.branch -ne $current })
    if ($merged.Count -eq 0) { 'No merged branches to delete'; exit 0 }
    foreach ($branch in (Select-Branch $merged 'Delete merged branches' '--multi')) {
        git branch --quiet -d $branch
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit 1 }
        "Deleted $branch"
    }
    exit 0
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.title: Review and export CSV reports
items.text:
View a CSV report, or export the rows you tick to a new CSV file.

Same example in Linux: Review and export CSV reports

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: view; CSV in and out; writing output only after Submit.

items.text: .\csv-report.ps1 -Report data\servers.csv [-Output OUTPUT.csv]

items.title: Source: csv-report.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
csv-report.ps1 - review a CSV report in a native table, then export only the rows you tick.

Teaches: sending a file's text unchanged to `view`/`select --input-format csv`, getting
correctly re-quoted CSV back (`--output-format csv`), and writing the export as UTF-8
without a BOM only after the user submitted, so Cancel never leaves a half-written file.

Run:   .\csv-report.ps1 -Report data\servers.csv [-Output subset.csv]
Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH.
Exit:  0 viewed / exported, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
#>
param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Report, [string] $Output)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
try {
    $text = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Report).ProviderPath, [Text.Encoding]::UTF8)
    $title = "Report: $(Split-Path -Leaf $Report)"
    if (-not $Output) {
        $text | nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --title $title
        exit $LASTEXITCODE
    }

    $csv = $text | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format csv --title 'Rows to export'
    switch ($LASTEXITCODE) {
        0       { }
        2       { Write-Warning "Cancelled; $Output not written."; exit 2 }
        124     { Write-Warning "No decision in time; $Output not written."; exit 124 }
        default { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
    }
    $target = $ExecutionContext.SessionState.Path.GetUnresolvedProviderPathFromPSPath($Output)
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($target, (($csv -join "`n") + "`n"), [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
    Write-Host "Wrote $(@($csv).Count - 1) row(s) to $Output"
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.title: Delete files with confirmation
items.text:
Tick files, confirm in a second window, then delete exactly the ticked files.

Same example in Linux: Delete files with confirmation

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: NUL-safe or literal paths; a confirmation select; nothing changes unless submitted.

items.title: Run it
items.text: .\delete-files.ps1 -Path DIRECTORY [-Filter GLOB] [-WhatIf]

items.title: Source: delete-files.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
delete-files.ps1 - tick files in a folder, confirm, and delete exactly those files.

Teaches: Get-ChildItem objects as JSON rows, multi-select, a second `select` as the
confirmation dialog (nothing is preselected, so the safe answer needs no click), and
SupportsShouldProcess so -WhatIf shows what would be deleted.

Run:   .\delete-files.ps1 -Path C:\Temp\logs [-Filter *.log] [-WhatIf]
Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH.
Exit:  0 deleted or nothing to do, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
#>
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path,
    [string] $Filter = '*'
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)

# Run the CLI on pipeline input; return its stdout. Cancel, timeout and errors end the
# script with the CLI's exit status (`exit` inside a function ends the whole script).
function Invoke-Picker {
    $out = $input | nativehtmlkit @args
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        Write-Warning 'Nothing deleted.'
        exit $LASTEXITCODE
    }
    $out -join "`n"
}

try {
    $files = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Path -File -Filter $Filter | Sort-Object LastWriteTime |
        Select-Object -First 2000)              # the CLI shows at most 2,000 rows
    if ($files.Count -eq 0) { Write-Host "Nothing in $Path matches $Filter."; exit 0 }

    $rows = $files | ForEach-Object {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Name         = $_.Name
            'Size (KiB)' = [math]::Ceiling($_.Length / 1KB)
            Modified     = $_.LastWriteTime.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')
            Path         = $_.FullName
        }
    }
    $json = $rows | ConvertTo-Json -Compress |
        Invoke-Picker select --multi --input-format json --output-format json --title "Files to delete in $(Split-Path -Leaf $Path)"
    # ForEach-Object unrolls the array: Windows PowerShell 5.1 returns a JSON array as one object.
    $picked = @(ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $json | ForEach-Object { $_ })

    $answer = "No, keep them", "Yes, delete $($picked.Count) file(s)" |
        Invoke-Picker select --title "Delete $($picked.Count) file(s)?"
    if (-not $answer.StartsWith('Yes')) { Write-Host 'Kept all files.'; exit 0 }

    foreach ($file in $picked) {
        if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($file.Path, 'Delete file')) {
            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $file.Path
            Write-Host "deleted $($file.Path)"
        }
    }
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.title: A deployment form
items.text:
Collect validated deployment parameters, confirm production, return them typed.

Same example in Linux: A deployment form

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: generated and escaped --html; Core form validation; parsing entries; a confirmation step.

items.title: Run it
items.text: .\deploy-form.ps1 [-Service NAME, ...]

items.title: Source: deploy-form.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
deploy-form.ps1 - collect deployment parameters in a native form and return them as an object.

Teaches: building a trusted `--html` form in PowerShell with every dynamic value encoded by
[System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode, Core's HTML constraint validation (required, pattern,
min/max, type=email, maxlength), turning {"entries":[...]} into a hashtable, an extra rule
checked by the script, and a production confirmation.

Run:   .\deploy-form.ps1 [-Service api, web, worker]
       $p = .\deploy-form.ps1 -Service api; $p.replicas
Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH; git (optional, to prefill the version).
Exit:  0 parameters returned, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
#>
param([string[]] $Service = @('api', 'web', 'worker'))
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)

function Enc([string] $s) { [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($s) }   # & < > " '

$form = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "deploy-form-$PID.html"
try {
    $version = 'v1.0.0'
    if (Get-Command git -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $described = & { $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'; git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>$null }
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0 -and $described) { $version = "$described".Trim() }
    }
    $options = ($Service | ForEach-Object { "<option value=`"$(Enc $_)`">$(Enc $_)</option>" }) -join ''
    $html = @"
<form id="nhk-form">
<label>Service <select name="service" required><option value="">Choose...</option>$options</select></label>
<fieldset><legend>Environment</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="environment" value="staging" required checked> Staging</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="environment" value="production"> Production</label>
</fieldset>
<label>Version <input name="version" required value="$(Enc $version)" pattern="v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" title="a version such as v1.4.2"></label>
<label>Replicas <input name="replicas" type="number" min="1" max="20" value="2" required></label>
<label>Notify <input name="notify" type="email" placeholder="team@example.com"></label>
<label>Change notes <textarea name="notes" maxlength="500" rows="3"></textarea></label>
<label class="check"><input type="checkbox" name="dry_run" value="yes" checked> Dry run only</label>
</form>
"@
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($form, $html, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))

    $json = nativehtmlkit form --html $form --css (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'css/form.css') --title 'Deploy' --timeout 600
    switch ($LASTEXITCODE) {
        0       { }
        2       { Write-Warning 'Cancelled.'; exit 2 }
        124     { Write-Warning 'The form was left open for 10 minutes; closed.'; exit 124 }
        default { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
    }

    # One entry per successful control, in document order; an unchecked checkbox has none.
    $values = @{}
    foreach ($entry in (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n")).entries) {
        if (-not $values.ContainsKey($entry.name)) { $values[$entry.name] = $entry.value }
    }

    if ($values.environment -eq 'production' -and -not "$($values.notes)".Trim()) {
        Write-Error 'Production deploys need change notes.'    # ends the script with exit 1
    }
    $dryRun = $values.dry_run -eq 'yes'
    if ($values.environment -eq 'production' -and -not $dryRun) {
        $answer = 'No, stop here', "Yes, deploy $($values.service) $($values.version) to production" |
            nativehtmlkit select --title 'Really deploy to production?'
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not "$answer".StartsWith('Yes')) { Write-Warning 'Not confirmed.'; exit 2 }
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        service     = $values.service
        environment = $values.environment
        version     = $values.version
        replicas    = [int] $values.replicas
        notify      = if ($values.notify) { $values.notify } else { $null }
        notes       = "$($values.notes)"
        dry_run     = $dryRun
    }
}
finally {
    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $form -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.title: Choose a Docker container
items.text:
Pick a container, then show its logs, restart, stop it or open a shell.

Same example in Linux: Choose a Docker container

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: NDJSON from docker ps; chained selections; view for logs.

items.title: Run it
items.text: .\pick-container.ps1

items.title: Source: pick-container.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
pick-container.ps1 - choose a Docker container, then choose what to do with it.

Teaches: NDJSON straight from `docker ps --format '{{json .}}'` reshaped into fewer columns,
two chained selections, and `view` for command output.

Run:   .\pick-container.ps1
Needs: nativehtmlkit and docker on PATH.
Exit:  0 action done, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
#>
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)

function Invoke-Picker {
    $out = $input | nativehtmlkit @args
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Warning 'No action taken.'; exit $LASTEXITCODE }
    $out -join "`n"
}

try {
    $rows = @(docker ps --all --format '{{json .}}' | ForEach-Object {
        $c = $_ | ConvertFrom-Json
        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $c.Names; Image = $c.Image; State = $c.State; Status = $c.Status; Ports = $c.Ports; ID = $c.ID } |
            ConvertTo-Json -Compress
    })
    if ($rows.Count -eq 0) { Write-Host 'No containers.'; exit 0 }

    $container = (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($rows | Invoke-Picker select --input-format ndjson --output-format json --title 'Containers'))[0]
    $label = $container.Name.Substring(0, [math]::Min(80, $container.Name.Length))   # --title: at most 128 characters
    $action = 'logs', 'restart', 'stop' | Invoke-Picker select --title "Container $label"

    switch ($action) {
        'logs'    {
            # 2>&1 turns docker's stderr lines into error records; with 'Stop' Windows
            # PowerShell 5.1 would end the script on the first one.
            $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
            docker logs --tail 1000 --timestamps $container.ID 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" } |
                nativehtmlkit view --title "Logs: $label"
            exit $LASTEXITCODE
        }
        'restart' { docker restart $container.ID }
        'stop'    { docker stop $container.ID }
    }
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.title: Choose from JSON API output
items.text:
Reshape a REST response, pick issues and print their URLs.

Same example in Linux: Choose from JSON API output

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: flattening nested JSON; records returned unchanged; multi-select.

items.title: Run it
items.text: .\pick-from-api.ps1 -Path data\issues.json

items.title: Source: pick-from-api.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
pick-from-api.ps1 - choose issues from a JSON API response and output their URLs.

Teaches: Invoke-RestMethod (or a saved response) -> flat objects -> JSON rows, keeping a
`url` column for the follow-up step, multi-select, and emitting plain strings so the script
can feed another command.

Run:   .\pick-from-api.ps1 -Uri 'https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/issues?per_page=100'
       .\pick-from-api.ps1 -Path data\issues.json      (the sample response in this folder)
Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH.
Exit:  0 printed the chosen URLs, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
#>
param([string] $Uri, [string] $Path)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
try {
    $response = if ($Path) {
        ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ([IO.File]::ReadAllText((Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Path).ProviderPath, [Text.Encoding]::UTF8))
    } else {
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $Uri -Headers @{ Accept = 'application/vnd.github+json' }
    }
    # GitHub lists pull requests as issues too; they carry a pull_request property.
    $rows = @($response | Where-Object { -not $_.PSObject.Properties['pull_request'] } | ForEach-Object {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            '#'     = $_.number
            Title   = $_.title
            Author  = $_.user.login
            Labels  = ($_.labels.name -join ', ')
            # PowerShell 7 turns ISO dates into [datetime]; Windows PowerShell keeps the text.
            Updated = if ($_.updated_at -is [datetime]) { $_.updated_at.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { "$($_.updated_at)".Substring(0, 10) }
            url     = $_.html_url
        }
    })
    if ($rows.Count -eq 0) { Write-Host 'The response contains no issues.'; exit 0 }

    $json = $rows | ConvertTo-Json -Compress |
        nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json --output-format json --title 'Open issues'
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }

    (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n")) | ForEach-Object { $_.url }
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.title: Pick a Git branch
items.text:
Switch to a branch chosen from a table of recent branches with their last commit.

Same example in Linux: Pick a Git branch

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: JSON rows built from tab-separated tool output; single choice; reading a field of the chosen record.

items.title: Run it
items.text: .\pick-git-branch.ps1 [-Repository PATH]

items.title: Source: pick-git-branch.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
pick-git-branch.ps1 - choose a local Git branch in a native window and switch to it.

Teaches: objects -> ConvertTo-Json -> `select --input-format json`, reading the JSON result
back with ConvertFrom-Json, and handling Cancel (2) and --timeout (124) through
$LASTEXITCODE. Works in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.

Run:   .\pick-git-branch.ps1 [-Repository <dir>]
Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH, git.
Exit:  0 switched, 2 cancelled, 124 no choice before the deadline, 1 error.
#>
param([string] $Repository = '.')
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# The CLI reads and writes UTF-8. Windows PowerShell 5.1 would otherwise send ASCII to it
# and decode its output with the console code page. Restored at the end.
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
try {
    $format = '%(HEAD)%09%(refname:short)%09%(committerdate:relative)%09%(upstream:short)%09%(subject)'
    $rows = @(git -C $Repository for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate "--format=$format" refs/heads |
        ForEach-Object {
            $f = $_ -split "`t", 5
            [pscustomobject]@{ Current = $f[0]; Branch = $f[1]; Updated = $f[2]; Upstream = $f[3]; 'Last commit' = $f[4] }
        })
    if ($rows.Count -eq 0) { Write-Error "no local branches in $Repository" }

    $picked = $rows | ConvertTo-Json -Compress |
        nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --output-format json --title 'Switch branch' --timeout 120
    switch ($LASTEXITCODE) {
        0       { }
        2       { Write-Warning 'Cancelled; staying on the current branch.'; exit 2 }
        124     { Write-Warning 'No branch chosen within 120 s.'; exit 124 }
        default { exit $LASTEXITCODE }    # the CLI already printed "nativehtmlkit: error[...]"
    }

    # [0] is the first record in both editions (5.1 returns the array as one object, 7 enumerates it).
    $branch = (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($picked -join "`n"))[0].Branch
    git -C $Repository switch $branch
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

<#
pick-service.ps1 - choose Windows services and start, stop or restart them.

Teaches: a Windows-only workflow: Get-Service -> JSON table, multi-select, an action chosen
in a second window, and -WhatIf through SupportsShouldProcess. Changing services needs an
elevated session.

Run:   .\pick-service.ps1 [-Name 'w*'] [-WhatIf]
Needs: Windows, nativehtmlkit on PATH.
Exit:  0 done, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
#>
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
param([string] $Name = '*')
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)

function Invoke-Picker {
    $out = $input | nativehtmlkit @args
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Warning 'Nothing changed.'; exit $LASTEXITCODE }
    $out -join "`n"
}

try {
    $rows = @(Get-Service -Name $Name | Sort-Object DisplayName | Select-Object -First 2000 |
        Select-Object Name, DisplayName, @{ n = 'Status'; e = { "$($_.Status)" } }, @{ n = 'Start type'; e = { "$($_.StartType)" } })
    if ($rows.Count -eq 0) { Write-Host "No service matches $Name."; exit 0 }

    # ForEach-Object unrolls the array: Windows PowerShell 5.1 returns a JSON array as one object.
    $picked = @(ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($rows | ConvertTo-Json -Compress |
        Invoke-Picker select --multi --input-format json --output-format json --title 'Services') | ForEach-Object { $_ })
    $action = 'Restart', 'Stop', 'Start' | Invoke-Picker select --title "Action for $($picked.Count) service(s)"

    foreach ($service in $picked) {
        if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($service.DisplayName, "$action service")) {
            switch ($action) {
                'Restart' { Restart-Service -Name $service.Name }
                'Stop'    { Stop-Service -Name $service.Name }
                'Start'   { Start-Service -Name $service.Name }
            }
        }
    }
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

<#
pick-timezone.ps1 - choose a time zone from a long list in a light-themed window.

Teaches: restyling the CLI's window with a trusted --css file (css/light.css overrides the
page's colour custom properties), a table built from .NET objects, and returning one field
of the chosen row. The PowerShell counterpart of pick-timezone.sh.

Run:   .\pick-timezone.ps1                       prints the zone id, e.g. Tokyo Standard Time
       $zone = .\pick-timezone.ps1; [TimeZoneInfo]::ConvertTimeBySystemTimeZoneId([DateTime]::UtcNow, $zone)
Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH.
Exit:  0 printed the zone, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
#>
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
try {
    $rows = @([TimeZoneInfo]::GetSystemTimeZones() | Select-Object -First 2000 | ForEach-Object {
        $offset = $_.BaseUtcOffset
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Id     = $_.Id
            Offset = '{0}{1:hh\:mm}' -f $(if ($offset -lt [TimeSpan]::Zero) { '-' } else { '+' }), $offset
            Name   = $_.DisplayName
        }
    })
    $json = $rows | ConvertTo-Json -Compress |
        nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --output-format json --title 'Time zone' `
            --css (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'css/light.css')
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
    (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n"))[0].Id
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.title: Choose processes to stop
items.text:
Pick processes in a table and stop or signal exactly those.

Same example in Linux: Choose processes to stop

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: process lists as CSV or JSON; CSV/JSON in, JSON out; a second choice for the action.

items.title: Run it
items.text: .\stop-process.ps1 [-Name PATTERN] [-WhatIf]

items.title: Source: stop-process.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
stop-process.ps1 - pick processes from a table and stop them.

Teaches: Get-Process -> Select-Object -> ConvertTo-Json as CLI input (choose the columns:
a raw Process object has far more than the 32 columns the CLI accepts), multi-select, and
reading the Id property back from the JSON result.

Run:   .\stop-process.ps1 [-Name notepad*] [-WhatIf]
Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH. Works on Windows and, with PowerShell 7, on Linux.
Exit:  0 stopped, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time, 1 error.
#>
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
param([string] $Name = '*')
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
try {
    $rows = @(Get-Process -Name $Name -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object Id -ne $PID |
        Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 500 |
        Select-Object Id, ProcessName,
            @{ n = 'CPU (s)'; e = { [math]::Round($_.CPU, 1) } },
            @{ n = 'Memory (MiB)'; e = { [math]::Round($_.WorkingSet64 / 1MB) } })
    if ($rows.Count -eq 0) { Write-Host "No process matches $Name."; exit 0 }

    $json = $rows | ConvertTo-Json -Compress |
        nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json --output-format json --title 'Processes to stop'
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Warning 'Nothing stopped.'; exit $LASTEXITCODE }

    # ForEach-Object unrolls the array: Windows PowerShell 5.1 returns a JSON array as one object.
    foreach ($process in @(ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n") | ForEach-Object { $_ })) {
        if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess("$($process.ProcessName) ($($process.Id))", 'Stop process')) {
            Stop-Process -Id $process.Id
        }
    }
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.title: Project picker (tutorial)
items.text:
Bookmark project directories, pick one to jump to, list and remove them.

Same example in Linux: Project picker (tutorial)

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: select, form and view in one tool; NDJSON as storage and CLI format; one wrapper for the exit contract; escaped generated forms; --css.

items.title: Run it
items.text: .\tutorial\proj.ps1 [pick | add [DIR] | list | remove]

items.title: Source: tutorial/proj.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
proj.ps1 - a small project-directory bookmark tool, built step by step in
docs/windows/tutorial.md. The PowerShell counterpart of proj.sh.

Teaches: one storage format (NDJSON) used directly as CLI input and output, a shared
wrapper for the exit contract, a generated and encoded form, multi-select with
confirmation, a read-only table, and a custom stylesheet.

Run:   .\proj.ps1 add [DIR]                  bookmark DIR (default: the current directory)
       Set-Location (.\proj.ps1 pick)        jump to a bookmarked project
       .\proj.ps1 list                       show all bookmarks
       .\proj.ps1 remove                     tick bookmarks to remove, then confirm
Store: $env:PROJ_FILE, default %APPDATA%\proj\projects.ndjson (~/.config/proj on Linux)
Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH.
Exit:  0 done, 2 cancelled, 124 no answer in time, 1 error.
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('pick', 'add', 'list', 'remove')] [string] $Command = 'pick',
    [string] $Directory = '.'
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
$Utf8 = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)

$store = $env:PROJ_FILE
if (-not $store) {
    $base = if ($env:APPDATA) { $env:APPDATA } else { Join-Path $HOME '.config' }
    $store = Join-Path $base 'proj/projects.ndjson'
}
$style = '--css', (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'proj.css')

function Stop-Proj([string] $Message) { Write-Warning "proj: $Message"; exit 1 }
function Enc([string] $s) { [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($s) }

# ui ARGS... - run the CLI with ARGS (and the pipeline input) and return its stdout as one
# string. Cancel, timeout and errors end the whole script with the CLI's status.
function ui {
    $out = $input | nativehtmlkit @args @style
    switch ($LASTEXITCODE) {
        0       { return ($out -join "`n") }
        2       { exit 2 }
        124     { Write-Warning 'proj: no answer in time'; exit 124 }
        default { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
    }
}

function Get-Records {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $store)) { return @() }
    @([IO.File]::ReadAllLines($store, $Utf8) | Where-Object { $_.Trim() } | ForEach-Object { ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_ })
}
function Assert-Projects { if ((Get-Records).Count -eq 0) { Stop-Proj 'no projects yet; add one with: proj add [DIR]' } }
function Get-StoreText { [IO.File]::ReadAllText($store, $Utf8) }

function Invoke-Pick {
    Assert-Projects
    $picked = Get-StoreText | ui select --input-format ndjson --output-format json --title 'Open project'
    (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $picked)[0].path
}

function Invoke-Add {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Directory -PathType Container)) { Stop-Proj "no such directory: $Directory" }
    $dir = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Directory).ProviderPath
    $html = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "proj-add-$PID.html"
    $form = @"
<form id="nhk-form">
  <p><label>Name <input name="name" required maxlength="60" value="$(Enc (Split-Path -Leaf $dir))"></label></p>
  <p><label>Directory <input name="path" required value="$(Enc $dir)"></label></p>
  <p><label>Tags <input name="tags" placeholder="work, rust" pattern="[A-Za-z0-9 ,_-]*"
         title="letters, digits, spaces, commas, - and _"></label></p>
</form>
"@
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($html, $form, $Utf8)
    try { $result = ui form --html $html --title 'Add project' }
    finally { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $html -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }

    # {"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"name","value":"..."},...]} -> one ordered record
    $values = @{}
    foreach ($e in (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $result).entries) { $values[$e.name] = $e.value }
    $record = [ordered]@{ name = $values.name; path = $values.path; tags = "$($values.tags)"; added = (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd') }
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $record.path -PathType Container)) { Stop-Proj "not a directory: $($record.path)" }
    if (@(Get-Records | Where-Object { $_.path -eq $record.path }).Count) { Stop-Proj "already bookmarked: $($record.path)" }
    $parent = Split-Path -Parent $store
    if ($parent -and -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $parent)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $parent | Out-Null }
    [IO.File]::AppendAllText($store, (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $record -Compress) + "`n", $Utf8)
    Write-Warning "proj: added $($record.path)"
}

function Invoke-List {
    Assert-Projects
    Get-StoreText | ui view --input-format ndjson --title "Projects ($((Get-Records).Count))" | Out-Null
}

function Invoke-Remove {
    Assert-Projects
    $picked = @((Get-StoreText | ui select --multi --input-format ndjson --output-format ndjson --title 'Remove projects') -split "`n" |
        Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_).path })
    $count = $picked.Count
    $answer = 'Keep them', "Remove $count project(s)" | ui select --title "Remove $count project(s)?"
    if (-not $answer.StartsWith('Remove')) { Write-Warning 'proj: nothing removed'; return }
    $keep = @([IO.File]::ReadAllLines($store, $Utf8) | Where-Object { $_.Trim() -and $picked -notcontains (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_).path })
    $tmp = "$store.$PID.tmp"
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($tmp, $(if ($keep.Count) { ($keep -join "`n") + "`n" } else { '' }), $Utf8)
    Move-Item -LiteralPath $tmp -Destination $store -Force
    Write-Warning "proj: removed $count project(s)"
}

try {
    switch ($Command) {
        'pick'   { Invoke-Pick }
        'add'    { Invoke-Add }
        'list'   { Invoke-List }
        'remove' { Invoke-Remove }
    }
    exit 0
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.title: Run it
items.text: .\search-selected.ps1 -Pattern PATTERN [-Path DIRECTORY]
path: Search only the files you tick

items.title: Source: search-selected.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
search-selected.ps1 - tick files in a window, then search only those files for a pattern.

Teaches: `select --multi` as one stage between PowerShell commands: paths go in as lines,
the ticked paths come back as lines, and $LASTEXITCODE says whether the user submitted
before anything is searched. The PowerShell counterpart of grep-selected.sh.

Run:   .\search-selected.ps1 -Pattern TODO [-Path src]
Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH.
Exit:  0 matches found, 1 no match or error, 2 cancelled, 124 no decision in time.
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Pattern,
    [string] $Path = '.'
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
try {
    # Relative paths, sorted, without .git, at most 2,000 (more would be an error, not a cut).
    $root = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Path).ProviderPath
    $files = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $root -File -Recurse |
        Where-Object { $_.FullName -notmatch '[\\/]\.git[\\/]' -and $_.Length -lt 2MB } |
        ForEach-Object { $_.FullName.Substring($root.Length).TrimStart('\', '/') } |
        Sort-Object | Select-Object -First 2000)
    if ($files.Count -eq 0) { Write-Warning "search-selected: no files in $Path"; exit 1 }

    $title = 'Search for: ' + $Pattern.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(100, $Pattern.Length))
    $chosen = @($files | nativehtmlkit select --multi --title $title)
    switch ($LASTEXITCODE) {
        0       { }
        2       { Write-Warning 'search-selected: cancelled'; exit 2 }
        124     { Write-Warning 'search-selected: no files chosen in time'; exit 124 }
        default { exit 1 }
    }

    $hits = @(Select-String -LiteralPath ($chosen | ForEach-Object { Join-Path $root $_ }) -Pattern $Pattern)
    foreach ($hit in $hits) {
        '{0}:{1}:{2}' -f $hit.Path.Substring($root.Length).TrimStart('\', '/'), $hit.LineNumber, $hit.Line
    }
    exit $(if ($hits.Count) { 0 } else { 1 })
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.text:
Show the end of a text or JSON-lines log (Windows: also the event log).

Same example in Linux: View logs

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

What it teaches: view for text and NDJSON; staying inside the page limit.

items.title: Source: view-logs.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

<#
view-logs.ps1 - show the end of a log file, or recent Windows events, in a native viewer.

Teaches: `view` for plain text (Get-Content -Tail, lines shortened to stay inside the 1 MiB
page limit) and for structured records (Get-WinEvent -> Select-Object -> JSON table).

Run:   .\view-logs.ps1 -Path data\app.log
       .\view-logs.ps1 -LogName System            (Windows: the newest 200 events)
Needs: nativehtmlkit on PATH.
Exit:  0 viewer closed, 124 closed by the deadline, 1 error.
#>
[CmdletBinding(DefaultParameterSetName = 'File')]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory, ParameterSetName = 'File')] [string] $Path,
    [Parameter(Mandatory, ParameterSetName = 'Event')] [string] $LogName,
    [int] $Lines = 1000
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$previousEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
try {
    if ($PSCmdlet.ParameterSetName -eq 'File') {
        Get-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Tail $Lines -Encoding UTF8 |
            ForEach-Object { if ($_.Length -gt 400) { $_.Substring(0, 400) + '...' } else { $_ } } |
            nativehtmlkit view --title "Log: $(Split-Path -Leaf $Path)"
    } else {
        Get-WinEvent -LogName $LogName -MaxEvents 200 |
            Select-Object @{ n = 'Time'; e = { $_.TimeCreated.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') } },
                @{ n = 'Level'; e = { $_.LevelDisplayName } }, Id, ProviderName,
                @{ n = 'Message'; e = { ("$($_.Message)" -split "`r?`n")[0] } } |
            ConvertTo-Json -Compress |
            nativehtmlkit view --input-format json --title "Events: $LogName"
    }
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}
finally {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = $previousEncoding
}

items.title: Recipes (Windows)

Task-oriented PowerShell recipes for CLI 0.1.2. Each one runs a complete script from the repository's examples and explains the parts that matter. Every script works in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, and every example was run against the released CLI by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

Recipe You want to Script Pick a Git branch switch branches from a table of recent branches pick-git-branch.ps1 Delete files with confirmation tick files, confirm, delete exactly those (-WhatIf) delete-files.ps1 Choose processes to stop pick processes and stop them (-WhatIf) stop-process.ps1 Restart, stop or start Windows services pick services, then the action (Windows only) pick-service.ps1 Choose a Docker container pick a container, then logs, restart or stop pick-container.ps1 Choose from JSON API output reshape a REST response and use the chosen records pick-from-api.ps1 Review and export CSV reports view a CSV, export the rows you tick csv-report.ps1 View logs and events show a text log or the Windows event log view-logs.ps1 Multi-select in pipelines use select between PowerShell commands search-selected.ps1 A deployment form collect validated parameters, confirm, return an object deploy-form.ps1 Choose a time zone in a light theme one value from a long list, restyled with --css pick-timezone.ps1 Test your scripts without a desktop run your own scripts in CI

items.title: Review and export CSV reports (Windows)
items.text:
Look at a CSV file in a table, or tick rows and export them as a new CSV file. Script: examples/csv-report.ps1, sample examples/data/servers.csv.

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

items.title: Look at it
items.text:
.\csv-report.ps1 -Report data\servers.csv

The first record is the header; quoted fields are shown unquoted. Without the script:

Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --title 'Servers'

items.title: Export the rows you tick
items.text:
.\csv-report.ps1 -Report data\servers.csv -Output degraded.csv
"degraded.csv exists: $(Test-Path degraded.csv)"
exit $LASTEXITCODE

On Cancel or a timeout no file is written:

WARNING: No decision in time; degraded.csv not written.
degraded.csv exists: False

After ticking web-02 and Submit:

host,role,region,cpu_cores,memory_gib,status,notes
web-02,frontend,eu-west,4,8,degraded,"disk 91% full, cleanup scheduled"

Wrote 1 row(s) to degraded.csv
degraded.csv exists: True

The script sends the file's text unchanged and writes the result as UTF-8 without a BOM:

$text = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Report).ProviderPath, [Text.Encoding]::UTF8)
$csv = $text | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format csv --title 'Rows to export'
$target = $ExecutionContext.SessionState.Path.GetUnresolvedProviderPathFromPSPath($Output)
[IO.File]::WriteAllText($target, (($csv -join "`n") + "`n"), [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))

items.title: Other shapes of the same rows
items.text:
Objects instead of text: ask for JSON, or read the CSV result with ConvertFrom-Csv:

$json = Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n")) | ForEach-Object { $_.host } }
exit 0

A file without a header row needs --no-headers (columns column_1, ...):

Get-Content data\servers.csv | Select-Object -Skip 1 | nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --no-headers

Semicolon-separated files: convert with Import-Csv -Delimiter ';' | ConvertTo-Csv -NoTypeInformation (input formats).

items.title: Delete files with confirmation (Windows)
items.text:
Tick files in a window, confirm in a second window, then delete exactly the ticked files. Cancel, closing a window or the deadline delete nothing. Script: examples/delete-files.ps1; it supports -WhatIf and -Confirm.

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

items.title: Run it
items.text:
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path scratch | Out-Null
'one' | Set-Content -LiteralPath 'scratch/a b.txt'
'two' | Set-Content -LiteralPath "scratch/it's [quoted].log"
'three' | Set-Content -LiteralPath 'scratch/notes.md'
'four' | Set-Content -LiteralPath 'scratch/-rf.txt'
.\delete-files.ps1 -Path scratch

A table of the four files (Name, Size (KiB), Modified, Path) opens. Suppose the user ticks a b.txt and it's [quoted].log:

[{"Name":"a b.txt","Size (KiB)":1,"Modified":"2026-11-16 09:00","Path":"scratch/a b.txt"},{"Name":"it's [quoted].log","Size (KiB)":1,"Modified":"2026-11-16 09:00","Path":"scratch/it's [quoted].log"}]

The script then asks in a second window (here nobody answers, so it ends with 124 and deletes nothing):

WARNING: Nothing deleted.

With Yes, delete 2 file(s) picked in the second window, exactly those two files go:

Yes, delete 2 file(s)

deleted scratch/a b.txt
deleted scratch/it's [quoted].log

With No, keep them nothing is deleted:

No, keep them

Kept all files.

-WhatIf shows what would be deleted and deletes nothing:

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path scratch | Out-Null
'x' | Set-Content -LiteralPath 'scratch/old.iso'
.\delete-files.ps1 -Path scratch -Filter *.iso -WhatIf

[{"Name":"old.iso","Size (KiB)":1,"Modified":"2026-11-16 09:00","Path":"scratch/old.iso"}]

Yes, delete 1 file(s)

What if: Performing the operation "Delete file" on target "scratch/old.iso".

Nothing matches: the script says so and exits 0 without opening a window:

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path empty-dir | Out-Null
.\delete-files.ps1 -Path empty-dir

Nothing in empty-dir matches *.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
1. List the files as objects, newest last, at most 2,000 (the CLI's row limit), and send them as JSON.
  2. Pick, then confirm with Invoke-Picker, a helper that ends the script on anything but a Submit. The confirmation is a single-choice select whose safe answer comes first:
$answer = "No, keep them", "Yes, delete $($picked.Count) file(s)" |
    Invoke-Picker select --title "Delete $($picked.Count) file(s)?"
  1. Delete exactly what was chosen with -LiteralPath (names with [ ] are wildcards for -Path) and ShouldProcess, which gives -WhatIf and -Confirm:
if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($file.Path, 'Delete file')) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $file.Path }

items.title: A form as the confirmation
items.text:
For a stronger confirmation use form with a required checkbox; Submit is only accepted with the box ticked. Encode the names you put into the HTML:

function Enc([string] $s) { [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($s) }
$items = ('scratch/a <b>.txt', 'scratch/notes & more.md' | ForEach-Object { "<li>$(Enc $_)</li>" }) -join ''
$html = "<form id=`"nhk-form`"><p>These files will be deleted:</p><ul>$items</ul>" +
        '<label><input type="checkbox" name="sure" value="yes" required> I understand</label></form>'
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path (Get-Location) 'confirm.html'), $html, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
nativehtmlkit form --html confirm.html --title 'Confirm deletion' | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
'confirmed'

Linux: Delete files with confirmation (Linux).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/recipes/delete-files.md · edit the page there.

items.title: A deployment form (Windows)
items.text:
Collect deployment parameters in a form with validation, check a rule HTML cannot express, ask for confirmation before production, and return the parameters as an object. Script: examples/deploy-form.ps1 with css/form.css (git optional, to prefill the version).

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how). Writing forms in general: CSS and forms.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
.\deploy-form.ps1 -Service api, web, worker

The form offers the services given, Staging or Production, a version (prefilled from git describe, checked with a pattern), replicas (1-20), an optional e-mail address, change notes and a Dry run only checkbox. Service names are HTML-encoded into the form, so hostile names are harmless:

.\deploy-form.ps1 -Service '<script>x</script>', 'a"b', "it's&more"

After a staging Submit the script returns an object (shown here as JSON):

$params = .\deploy-form.ps1 -Service api, web
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
$params | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
"deploying $($params.service) $($params.version) x$($params.replicas) to $($params.environment)"

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"service","value":"api"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"staging"},{"kind":"text","name":"version","value":"v1.4.2"},{"kind":"text","name":"replicas","value":"3"},{"kind":"text","name":"notify","value":""},{"kind":"text","name":"notes","value":""},{"kind":"text","name":"dry_run","value":"yes"}]}

{"service":"api","environment":"staging","version":"v1.4.2","replicas":3,"notify":null,"notes":"","dry_run":true}
deploying api v1.4.2 x3 to staging

Production without change notes is refused by the script (Write-Error, exit 1):

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"service","value":"api"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"production"},{"kind":"text","name":"version","value":"v1.4.2"},{"kind":"text","name":"replicas","value":"3"},{"kind":"text","name":"notify","value":""},{"kind":"text","name":"notes","value":"  "}]}

Production deploys need change notes.

A real production deploy (no dry run) asks once more in a select. Anything but Yes (here: nobody answered in time) stops with exit 2:

{"entries":[{"kind":"text","name":"service","value":"web"},{"kind":"text","name":"environment","value":"production"},{"kind":"text","name":"version","value":"2.0.0"},{"kind":"text","name":"replicas","value":"4"},{"kind":"text","name":"notify","value":"ops@example.com"},{"kind":"text","name":"notes","value":"Rollout of the new login"}]}

WARNING: Not confirmed.

Answering Yes, deploy web 2.0.0 to production:

Yes, deploy web 2.0.0 to production

{"service":"web","environment":"production","version":"2.0.0","replicas":4,"notify":"ops@example.com","notes":"Rollout of the new login","dry_run":false}
deploying web 2.0.0 x4 to production

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Every dynamic value is encoded with HtmlEncode while the form is built:

function Enc([string] $s) { [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($s) }   # & < > " '
$options = ($Service | ForEach-Object { "<option value=`"$(Enc $_)`">$(Enc $_)</option>" }) -join ''

Core validates required, pattern, min/max and type="email" before it accepts Submit. The script turns the entries into a hashtable (an unticked checkbox has no entry) and builds a typed object:

$values = @{}
foreach ($entry in (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n")).entries) {
    if (-not $values.ContainsKey($entry.name)) { $values[$entry.name] = $entry.value }
}
$dryRun = $values.dry_run -eq 'yes'

Linux: A deployment form (Linux).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/recipes/deploy-form.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Choose a Docker container (Windows)
items.text:
Pick a container, then an action: show its logs, restart or stop it. Script: examples/pick-container.ps1 (needs docker).

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how) with a stand-in docker that lists two containers (web, and db <primary>), so no real Docker engine was touched.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
.\pick-container.ps1

After the user picks web, a second window asks for the action (here nobody answers, so nothing is done):

[{"Name":"web","Image":"nginx:1.27","State":"running","Status":"Up 2 hours","Ports":"0.0.0.0:8080->80/tcp","ID":"3f2a9c1d7b44"}]

WARNING: No action taken.

With restart chosen the script runs docker restart 3f2a9c1d7b44:

restart

With logs chosen a third window shows the last 1,000 log lines:

logs

items.title: How it works
items.text:
docker ps --format '{{json .}}' prints one JSON object per container per line. The script keeps six properties and sends the objects as NDJSON:

docker ps --all --format '{{json .}}' | ForEach-Object {
    $c = $_ | ConvertFrom-Json
    [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $c.Names; Image = $c.Image; State = $c.State; Status = $c.Status; Ports = $c.Ports; ID = $c.ID } |
        ConvertTo-Json -Compress
} | nativehtmlkit select --input-format ndjson --output-format json --title 'Containers'

[{"Name":"db <primary>","Image":"postgres:17","State":"exited","Status":"Exited (0) 3 minutes ago","Ports":"5432/tcp","ID":"9b8e7d6c5a43"}]

The name db <primary> is shown as text, never as markup. Logs go to view; docker writes some of them to stderr, so the script merges the streams with 2>&1 while $ErrorActionPreference is 'Continue' (with 'Stop', Windows PowerShell 5.1 would end the script at the first stderr line):

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
docker logs --tail 1000 --timestamps $container.ID 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" } |
    nativehtmlkit view --title "Logs: $label"

items.title: Pick a Git branch (Windows)
items.text:
Show the local branches, newest first, with their last commit, and switch to the one the user picks. Script: examples/pick-git-branch.ps1 (needs git). For a step-by-step version that can also delete merged branches, see the branch picker tutorial.

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository (a Git work tree) and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

items.title: Quick version
items.text:
$branch = git branch '--format=%(refname:short)' | nativehtmlkit select --title 'Switch branch'
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { git switch $branch }

git switch runs only after a Submit; on Cancel (2) or a timeout (124) nothing happens. ('--format=...' in quotes keeps PowerShell from interpreting the parentheses.)

items.title: With columns
items.text:
.\pick-git-branch.ps1

The window shows Current, Branch, Updated, Upstream and Last commit. When the user picks feature/login, the CLI returns that record as a JSON array (the record exactly as it went in) and the script switches:

[{"Current":" ","Branch":"feature/login","Updated":"2 minutes ago","Upstream":"","Last commit":"Add the example scripts"}]

Switched to branch 'feature/login'

After Cancel nothing changes and the script exits 2:



WARNING: Cancelled; staying on the current branch.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
git for-each-ref prints tab-separated fields; the script turns each line into an object and sends the objects as JSON, which no character in a commit subject can break:

$format = '%(HEAD)%09%(refname:short)%09%(committerdate:relative)%09%(upstream:short)%09%(subject)'
$rows = @(git -C $Repository for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate "--format=$format" refs/heads |
    ForEach-Object {
        $f = $_ -split "`t", 5
        [pscustomobject]@{ Current = $f[0]; Branch = $f[1]; Updated = $f[2]; Upstream = $f[3]; 'Last commit' = $f[4] }
    })
$picked = $rows | ConvertTo-Json -Compress |
    nativehtmlkit select --input-format json --output-format json --title 'Switch branch' --timeout 120

After checking $LASTEXITCODE, the branch is read back with (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($picked -join "n"))[0].Branch.[0]is the first record in both editions: Windows PowerShell 5.1 returns the JSON array as one object, PowerShell 7 enumerates it (and[0]` of a single object is that object).

items.title: Variations
items.text:
Remote branches as well:

git for-each-ref '--format=%(refname:short)' refs/heads refs/remotes |
    nativehtmlkit select --title 'Check out' --timeout 120

Delete merged branches: tick several with --multi; git branch -d refuses anything that is not merged:

$merged = git branch --merged main '--format=%(refname:short)' | Where-Object { $_ -ne 'main' }
$chosen = $merged | nativehtmlkit select --multi --title 'Delete merged branches'
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { $chosen | ForEach-Object { git branch -d $_ } }

Here feature/login, fix/typo and release/1.4 are merged into main. Submit prints, after ticking fix/typo:

fix/typo

items.title: Test your scripts without a desktop
path: Test your scripts without a desktop

items.title: Test your scripts without a desktop (Windows)
items.text:
A script that opens a window is hard to test in CI: nobody clicks. This repository tests its examples and these pages headless; you can do the same for your own PowerShell scripts.

NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS is a test-only switch, not part of the user contract of CLI 0.1.2, and may change in a later release. Never set it for real use.

The examples were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).
path: Test your scripts without a desktop

items.title: What headless mode proves
items.text:
With NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1 the CLI starts the real Core host with --headless: the host runs the whole protocol (handshake, window, document, events, shutdown) without showing anything. With no input, every session ends by --timeout:

$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS = '1'
'a', 'b' | nativehtmlkit select --timeout 0.5 2>$null
"exit $LASTEXITCODE"
exit 0

exit 124

Exit 124 with empty stdout shows that the input was parsed, the page was accepted by the host and the exit contract held. --diagnostics debug shows how the input was understood:

$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS = '1'
$log = 'a,b', '1,2', '3,4' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --timeout 0.5 --diagnostics debug 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
$started = $log | Where-Object { $_ -like '*"event":"session.started"*' } | ForEach-Object { ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_ }
"rows $($started.context.rows), columns $($started.context.columns)"
exit 0

rows 2, columns 2

Input errors still fail at once with exit 1, so a headless run also proves your data is acceptable (UTF-8, valid JSON, row, column and page limits).
path: Test your scripts without a desktop

items.title: Testing a whole script
items.text:
Your script probably sets its own --timeout (or none). PowerShell resolves functions before executables, so a function named nativehtmlkit defined before the script runs can replace the deadline with a short one, and hand the script a recorded result to test what happens after a Submit:

$real = (Get-Command nativehtmlkit -CommandType Application | Select-Object -First 1).Source
function global:nativehtmlkit {
    $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'     # the tested script may use 'Stop'
    $keep = @(); $skip = $false
    foreach ($a in $args) {
        if ($skip) { $skip = $false; continue }
        if ($a -eq '--timeout') { $skip = $true; continue }
        $keep += $a
    }
    $env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS = '1'
    $out = $input | & $real @keep --timeout 0.5 2>$null
    $global:calls += "$($keep[0]) -> $LASTEXITCODE"
    if ($global:replay) { $global:replay; $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0 } else { $out; $global:LASTEXITCODE = $LASTEXITCODE }
}
$global:calls = @()
$global:replay = $null
& .\tutorial-branch-picker\step1-pick.ps1 3> $null
"headless: $LASTEXITCODE"
$global:replay = 'release/1.4'
& .\tutorial-branch-picker\step1-pick.ps1
"replayed: $LASTEXITCODE"
$global:calls
exit 0

headless: 124
You chose: release/1.4
replayed: 0
select -> 124
select -> 124

The first run proves the script's window opened and that it passes 124 on (3> $null hides its warning); the second, with a recorded result in the exact output format (output formats), what it does after a Submit.

This repository's harnesses do the same with more checks (rows x columns per call, document ready, no stdout on a non-zero status, no leftover processes):

powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\test-examples.ps1 -Cli C:\Tools\nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-windows-x64\nativehtmlkit.exe -Shell powershell.exe
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\test-docs.ps1 -Cli C:\Tools\nativehtmlkit-cli-v0.1.2-windows-x64\nativehtmlkit.exe -Shell powershell.exe

What this does not prove: anything that needs a person or a real screen (clicking, keyboard focus, layout, colours). The CLI release's GUI qualification covers those.

Linux: Test your scripts without a desktop (Linux).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/recipes/headless-testing.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Choose from JSON API output (Windows)
items.text:
Reshape a REST response, let the user pick records, and use fields of the chosen records. Script: examples/pick-from-api.ps1 with Invoke-RestMethod, or the sample response examples/data/issues.json (GitHub's issue list format).

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

items.title: Run it
items.text:
With the saved response, or live with .\pick-from-api.ps1 -Uri 'https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/issues?per_page=100':

.\pick-from-api.ps1 -Path data\issues.json

The response has four entries; one is a pull request, so three issues are offered. The script prints the URLs of the chosen issues:

[{"#":42,"Title":"Window opens off-screen on a second monitor","Author":"ada","Labels":"bug, windows","Updated":"2026-11-12","url":"https://example.invalid/issues/42"},{"#":39,"Title":"Unicode in titles","Author":"zoe","Labels":"i18n","Updated":"2026-11-01","url":"https://example.invalid/issues/39"}]

https://example.invalid/issues/42
https://example.invalid/issues/39

items.title: How it works
items.text:
The CLI shows one column per top-level property and nested values as compact JSON, so flatten first, and keep the property you need afterwards (url):

$response = Get-Content -Raw data\issues.json | ConvertFrom-Json
$rows = @($response | ForEach-Object { $_ } | Where-Object { -not $_.PSObject.Properties['pull_request'] } | ForEach-Object {
    [pscustomobject]@{
        '#' = $_.number; Title = $_.title; Author = $_.user.login
        Labels = ($_.labels.name -join ', ')
        Updated = if ($_.updated_at -is [datetime]) { $_.updated_at.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { "$($_.updated_at)".Substring(0, 10) }
        url = $_.html_url
    }
})
ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $rows -Compress |
    nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json --output-format json --title 'Open issues'

[{"#":41,"Title":"Document the <form> limits","Author":"grace","Labels":"docs","Updated":"2026-11-10","url":"https://example.invalid/issues/41"}]

Two edition differences the script handles: PowerShell 7 turns ISO date strings into [datetime] while Windows PowerShell keeps the text (hence the -is [datetime] test), and a parsed JSON array goes down the pipeline as one object in 5.1 (ForEach-Object { $_ } unrolls it). What comes back is the array of the chosen records exactly as they went in.

Linux: Choose from JSON API output (Linux).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/recipes/json-api.md · edit the page there.

items.title: View logs and events (Windows)
items.text:
Show a text log in a scrolling, wrapping pane, or the newest Windows events as a table. view has no result: closing it exits 0. Script: examples/view-logs.ps1, samples data/app.log and data/app.ndjson.

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

items.title: Text files
items.text:
.\view-logs.ps1 -Path data\app.log

The script shows the last 1,000 lines (-Lines changes that), each cut to 400 characters. Markup in log lines is shown literally. The same without the script:

Get-Content -LiteralPath data\app.log -Tail 1000 -Encoding UTF8 |
    ForEach-Object { if ($_.Length -gt 400) { $_.Substring(0, 400) + '...' } else { $_ } } |
    nativehtmlkit view --title 'app.log'

Two limits matter for logs (limits): at most 2,000 lines (more is an error, so use -Tail), and the page must stay under 1 MiB (2,000 lines of 500 characters fit, 600 do not):

$long = Join-Path (Get-Location) 'long.log'
[IO.File]::WriteAllLines($long, [string[]] (1..3000 | ForEach-Object { 'line {0}: {1}' -f $_, ('x' * 700) }))
.\view-logs.ps1 -Path $long

items.title: The Windows event log
items.text:
.\view-logs.ps1 -LogName System

The newest 200 events with Time, Level, Id, ProviderName and the first line of the Message:

Get-WinEvent -LogName $LogName -MaxEvents 200 |
    Select-Object @{ n = 'Time'; e = { $_.TimeCreated.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') } },
        @{ n = 'Level'; e = { $_.LevelDisplayName } }, Id, ProviderName,
        @{ n = 'Message'; e = { ("$($_.Message)" -split "`r?`n")[0] } } |
    ConvertTo-Json -Compress |
    nativehtmlkit view --input-format json --title "Events: $LogName"

Only errors and warnings of the last day:

$events = @(Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName = 'System'; Level = 1, 2, 3; StartTime = (Get-Date).AddDays(-1) } -MaxEvents 500 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object @{ n = 'Time'; e = { $_.TimeCreated.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') } },
        @{ n = 'Level'; e = { $_.LevelDisplayName } }, Id, ProviderName)
if ($events.Count -eq 0) { $events = @([pscustomobject]@{ Time = ''; Level = ''; Id = ''; ProviderName = 'no errors or warnings' }) }
ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $events -Compress | nativehtmlkit view --input-format json --title 'System: errors and warnings'

items.title: JSON lines
items.text:
Get-Content data\app.ndjson | ForEach-Object {
    $r = ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $_
    [pscustomobject]@{ time = $r.time; level = $r.level; msg = $r.msg } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
} | nativehtmlkit view --input-format ndjson --title 'app.ndjson'

items.title: Keep the script going
items.text:
view blocks until the window is closed. Exit 0 (closed) and 124 (--timeout) both mean "done looking":

Get-Content data\app.log | nativehtmlkit view --timeout 300 --title 'Build log'
if ($LASTEXITCODE -notin 0, 124) { exit 1 }
'next step'
exit 0

next step

Linux: View logs (Linux).

Source: nativehtmlkit-cli/docs/windows/recipes/logs.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Multi-select in pipelines (Windows)
items.text:
select --multi writes one line per chosen row, in input order, and nothing at all on Cancel or a timeout. In PowerShell it sits between commands as a filter; check $LASTEXITCODE before acting on what came out. Script: examples/search-selected.ps1 (the counterpart of grep-selected.sh).

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

items.title: Search only the files you tick
items.text:
.\search-selected.ps1 -Pattern 'nativehtmlkit view' -Path .

The window lists the files under . as relative paths (at most 2,000). Suppose the user ticks two scripts:

csv-report.ps1
view-logs.ps1

csv-report.ps1:20:        $text | nativehtmlkit view --input-format csv --title $title
view-logs.ps1:25:            nativehtmlkit view --title "Log: $(Split-Path -Leaf $Path)"
view-logs.ps1:32:            nativehtmlkit view --input-format json --title "Events: $LogName"

After Cancel the script exits 2 and nothing is searched:



WARNING: search-selected: cancelled

items.title: The pattern
items.text:
'first' | Set-Content one.log; 'second' | Set-Content two.log
$chosen = Get-ChildItem *.log | ForEach-Object Name | nativehtmlkit select --multi --title 'Compress'
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { $chosen | ForEach-Object { Compress-Archive -LiteralPath $_ -DestinationPath "$_.zip" } }
@(Get-ChildItem *.zip).Count
exit 0

0
  • Check $LASTEXITCODE first: after Cancel or a timeout the variable is $null, and $null | ForEach-Object would still run once in Windows PowerShell 5.1 with $_ empty.
  • Use -LiteralPath with the chosen names, so [ and ] are not wildcards.
  • Send at most 2,000 rows (Select-Object -First 2000): more is an error, not a cut.
  • Names containing line breaks cannot be represented in lines; use JSON.

items.title: Rows with several fields
items.text:
Choose an output format that keeps the fields apart, then work with objects:

$json = Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit 0 }
foreach ($server in @(ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n") | ForEach-Object { $_ })) {
    "would restart $($server.role) on $($server.host)"
}

[{"host":"api-01","role":"backend","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"8","memory_gib":"32","status":"healthy","notes":""},{"host":"cache-01","role":"cache","region":"eu-west","cpu_cores":"2","memory_gib":"16","status":"healthy","notes":""}]

would restart backend on api-01
would restart cache on cache-01

One Test-Connection (or any command) per chosen host:

$json = Get-Content data\servers.csv | nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format csv --output-format json
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
    (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject ($json -join "`n")) | ForEach-Object { "checking $($_.host)" }
}
exit 0

items.title: Choose processes to stop (Windows)
items.text:
Pick processes in a table and stop exactly those. Script: examples/stop-process.ps1; it supports -WhatIf and -Confirm and also runs in PowerShell 7 on Linux.

Real capture on Windows Server 2022 with the released packages.

The examples run in the examples folder of a clone of this repository and were run against the released CLI 0.1.2 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 by scripts/test-docs.ps1 (how).

items.title: Run it
items.text:
Offer the processes of the PowerShell you are using (the script leaves itself out):

.\stop-process.ps1 -Name (Get-Process -Id $PID).ProcessName

The table shows Id, ProcessName, CPU (s) and Memory (MiB). With -WhatIf, a Submit shows what would be stopped and stops nothing:

.\stop-process.ps1 -Name (Get-Process -Id $PID).ProcessName -WhatIf

[{"Id":4242,"ProcessName":"demo","CPU (s)":0.4,"Memory (MiB)":35}]

What if: Performing the operation "Stop process" on target "demo (4242)".

After Cancel nothing is stopped:



WARNING: Nothing stopped.

No match: the script exits 0 without a window:

.\stop-process.ps1 -Name no-such-process-42

No process matches no-such-process-42.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
A raw Process object has far more properties than the 32 columns the CLI accepts, and converting it is slow; Select-Object keeps the table small and readable:

$rows = @(Get-Process -Name $Name -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object Id -ne $PID |
    Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 500 |
    Select-Object Id, ProcessName,
        @{ n = 'CPU (s)'; e = { [math]::Round($_.CPU, 1) } },
        @{ n = 'Memory (MiB)'; e = { [math]::Round($_.WorkingSet64 / 1MB) } })
$json = $rows | ConvertTo-Json -Compress |
    nativehtmlkit select --multi --input-format json --output-format json --title 'Processes to stop'
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Warning 'Nothing stopped.'; exit $LASTEXITCODE }

Each chosen object then goes through $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess(...) and Stop-Process -Id.
