items.title: HTML and CSS support
items.text:
NativeHTMLKit Core renders HTML and CSS with its own native engine: an HTML5 parser (html5ever), the Stylo CSS engine for selectors and the cascade, Taffy plus Core layout code for block, inline, flex, grid and tables, Parley for text, and a CPU rasterizer (vello_cpu). It is built for desktop application interfaces, not for browsing: there is no JavaScript, no network and no navigation. All application logic runs in your backend, which receives events and changes the page through document commands (directly over wire v1 or through an SDK).

This guide describes Core 1.0.3 (CSS profile ui4me-desktop-1.0). It has two companions:

  • Generated HTML/CSS profile — tables produced by asking a live host: the CSS feature profile, ~250 CSS properties, units, selectors, media queries, accepted markup, <input type> values and accessibility roles. Prefer it over this page for "is X supported?" questions.
  • Runtime introspection — the css_profile, get_computed_style, explain, get_diagnostics and get_accessibility_tree ops answer the same questions for your document.

Statements on this page were checked against the 1.0.3 source and, where headless mode allows, against a running host. Native painting, input, IME and screen-reader behaviour need a real desktop; those statements come from the source and the platform qualification record, not from this run.

items.title: Debugging a page that looks wrong
items.text:
1. get_diagnostics lists what the engine dropped or refused: UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE (with the CSS feature id and a reason such as profile-disabled or not-consumed-by-stage), RESOURCE_DENIED (a URL outside the allowed sources), RESOURCE_PENDING, parse problems.
  2. explain {element, property} says why a declaration has no effect: not_applicable (for example a display: none ancestor, width on an inline box, top on a static element, flex-grow on a child of a non-flex container), overridden, unsupported (profile), unknown_property.
  3. get_computed_style {element, properties} shows the values the engine computed.
  4. add_stylesheet returns parse diagnostics for the CSS you add (unknown properties with line and column).
  5. nativehtmlkit-host render --html page.html --output page.png [--width --height --scale] renders a file to a PNG without a desktop and prints the diagnostics as JSON.

items.title: Markup the host refuses
items.text:
A document or inserted fragment containing any of these fails to load with -32602, and the previous document stays in place (verified, see profile §6):

  • <script>, <iframe>, <object>, <embed>;
  • any on… attribute (event-handler attributes) and srcdoc;
  • contenteditable with any value other than false — use <input> or <textarea>;
  • <input type> color, date, time, month, week, datetime-local (no native picker);
  • duplicate id values, an id containing whitespace or longer than 256 bytes;
  • more than 65,536 nodes, nesting deeper than 256, or more than 1 MiB of HTML.

Accepted but inert: <noscript> is ordinary content (scripting is off), <template> content is not rendered, custom elements behave as plain elements and declarative shadow roots are not attached. <canvas>, <video> and <audio controls> produce empty boxes (300x150 px; 300x54 px for audio) with no drawing API or playback — use a live bitmap for custom pixels.

items.title: Elements and links
items.text:
Flow, sectioning, heading, list, table, phrasing, quotation and bidi elements get WHATWG default styles. <details>/<summary> toggle (including exclusive accordions with a shared name), and <dialog> and popovers are described below.

Activating an <a href> never navigates. The backend receives a link_activated event with href and the resolved url and decides what to do (for example desktop.open_external). :visited never matches.

items.title: Forms and controls
items.text:
Control Support <input> text, search, tel, url, email, password, number, range, checkbox, radio, button, submit, reset, image, hidden, file (native picker; the backend gets paths, never contents; ≤1024 files). <textarea> Multi-line editing; field-sizing is supported. <select> Drop-down, list box (size > 1), multiple, <optgroup>. <button>, <label> Activation and label forwarding. <progress>, <meter> Painted, with accessibility roles. <output> Plain text. <datalist> Loads, but no suggestion popup is shown.

Editing in text controls: caret and selection, IME composition, plain-text clipboard and per-control undo/redo (100 steps). The edit_command op exposes undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, select_all and delete; set_control_selection and replace_control_range give precise programmatic editing.

Constraint validation: required, minlength/maxlength, pattern (anchored), type=email, type=url, type=number with min/max/step, and custom messages (set_custom_validity), with the standard validity flags and :valid/:invalid. As in browsers, minlength is only checked after the value changed (a too-short initial value attribute is valid). Messages are fixed English strings (for example Please enter a URL.) and no validation bubble is shown — display your own, typically from the invalid event.

Submission never navigates or sends anything. A valid submission fires a cancelable submit event (with the submitter); invalid controls get invalid events and the first one is focused. get_form_data returns entries in document order ({name, kind, value}, file entries with path/filename); request_submit and reset_form drive forms from the backend. Programmatic set_value/set_checked/set_selected_values do not fire input or change.

items.title: Dialogs, popovers, focus and selection
items.text:
• <dialog>: non-modal and modal (top layer, ::backdrop, :modal, the rest of the page inert). Escape on a modal dialog sends a cancelable cancel, then close with return_value. Ops: show_dialog, close_dialog, get_dialog.
  • Popovers: popover / popover="auto" (light dismiss and Escape) and popover="manual", popovertarget on <button> elements, beforetoggle/toggle events, :popover-open. Any other value, including popover="hint", is treated as manual (get_popover reports kind: "manual"). Anchor positioning works with anchor-name, position-anchor and anchor(); position-try and anchor-size() are off.
  • Focus: sequential Tab navigation, :focus, :focus-visible and :focus-within, an outline-style: auto focus ring; ops focus, blur, get_focused_element.
  • Text selection of read-only document text with the pointer and keyboard; ops select_text, get_selection, copy_selection, clear_selection. Selection highlight colours are the engine's own.
  • In-page drag and drop: an element with draggable="true" produces dragstart, dragover, drop and dragend events (no DataTransfer, no dragging out to other applications).

items.title: CSS
items.text:
The profile enables nearly everything Stylo parses; profile §1 lists the features that are switched off, unavailable or filtered.

Selectors (verified in profile §4): type, class, id, attribute, combinators, :is(), :where(), :not(), :has(), :nth-child(An+B of S), :dir(), :lang(), :empty, :root, :defined, form-state pseudo-classes (:checked, :disabled, :enabled, :required, :optional, :placeholder-shown, :valid, :invalid), interaction states (:hover, :active, :focus, :focus-visible, :focus-within), :modal, :popover-open, :open, :link/:any-link, CSS nesting and @scope with an explicit root. Pseudo-elements: ::before, ::after, ::marker, ::first-line, ::first-letter, ::backdrop. Not matching in 1.0.3: :read-only, :read-write, progress:indeterminate and :visited; :host, ::part, ::slotted do not apply (no Shadow DOM); ::placeholder and ::selection use fixed theme colours.

At-rules: @media, @supports, @import (local files), @layer, @container (size queries), @font-face, @keyframes, @property, @namespace, @scope, @starting-style. Not available: @counter-style, @custom-media, @font-palette-values, @view-transition, @page (parsed, no effect), container style queries.

Media queries (profile §5): viewport size, orientation, aspect-ratio, resolution, hover, pointer, screen, and prefers-color-scheme / prefers-reduced-motion, which follow the desktop settings or an application override (set_environment {color_scheme: "dark"|"light"|"system", reduced_motion: "reduce"|"no-preference"|"system"}). prefers-contrast and forced-colors never match: high contrast is observed and reported to the backend (desktop.preferences), but no forced-colours palette is applied. print never matches.

Values and units (profile §3): absolute and font-relative units, viewport units including svh/lvh/dvh, container query units (cq*), custom properties and var(), calc(), min(), max(), clamp(), color-mix(), oklch() and other modern colour syntax, light-dark(), fit-content(), stretch, counters. Note: lh and rlh resolve to 0 while line-height is normal (feature css.unit.lh-normal is off) — set an explicit line-height when you use them. Off: random(), cross-fade(), shape(), anchor-size(), zoom, font-size-adjust, initial-letter, standard line-clamp.

items.title: Layout
items.text: Feature Status block, inline, inline-block, flow-root, list-item, contents, none Supported Flexbox Supported: wrapping, gap, order, alignment; also flex-wrap: balance Grid Supported: templates and named areas, auto-placement, subgrid Tables Supported (table, inline-table and table elements) Positioning relative, absolute, fixed, sticky; floats (no shape-outside) Overflow and scrolling Scroll containers, smooth scroll-behavior, scroll snap, scroll-margin/scroll-padding, overscroll-behavior, scrollbar-color/-width/-gutter Multi-column Supported, with column breaks Writing modes and bidi Vertical writing modes, text-orientation, text-combine-upright, RTL and bidi isolation Containment contain, content-visibility: hidden, contain-intrinsic-size, size container queries resize Supported, with a painted grip display: -webkit-box + -webkit-line-clamp Supported Ruby, masonry (grid-lanes) Not supported

items.title: Visual effects
items.text:
Supported: backgrounds and multiple layers, borders and border-radius, border-image, box-shadow (outer and inset), outlines, linear, radial and conic gradients, opacity, 2D transforms, filter functions and drop-shadow, backdrop-filter, mix-blend-mode, masks, clip-path basic shapes and path() (no url() references), background-clip: text, accent-color, appearance. Transitions and @keyframes animations run on the document clock with cubic-bezier(), steps() and linear() easing, and fire transition/animation events; scroll-driven animations (animation-timeline) and view transitions are not supported. prefers-reduced-motion is yours to honour in CSS. Cursors map to the native standard set; url() cursors fall back to the default.

Known rendering gaps in 1.0.3:

  • A dashed or dotted border on a box with border-radius is not drawn (the host reports UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE css.property.border-*-style). Use a solid rounded border, or a dashed border without rounding.
  • option:checked colours in a <select multiple> list are ignored; selected rows use the engine's highlight.

items.title: Text and fonts
items.text:
• System fonts with generic families (sans-serif, serif, monospace, system-ui, …) and per-character fallback. Noto Sans Regular is built in as the last resort, so text always renders.
  • @font-face loads TTF, OTF, TTC, WOFF and WOFF2 (≤32 MiB per font) from local files under the asset root, data: URLs or registered resources; local() names system fonts; unicode-range and feature/variation descriptors work. size-adjust and the metric overrides are parsed but ignored (reported as UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE). Fonts load asynchronously and text re-lays out when they arrive.
  • Shaping: complex scripts, bidi, vertical text, variable fonts, OpenType features (font-variant-*, font-feature-settings), kerning, synthesis, colour emoji.
  • Wrapping: text-overflow: ellipsis, text-wrap: balance, word-break, overflow-wrap, hyphens: auto for English, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Dutch (requires lang). text-wrap: pretty and standard line-clamp are off.

items.title: Images and resources
items.text:
Resources load only from three places; everything else, including http: and https:, is refused (RESOURCE_DENIED, and an <img> shows its alt box):

Source Rules Local files (relative URL or file:) Must be inside the document's asset root: the directory of the HTML file loaded with path, or the asset_root passed to document.load. A path that leaves it (for example ../x.png) is refused. Inline HTML without asset_root cannot reference local files. Relative paths in document.load resolve against the backend's working directory. data: URLs Up to 4 MiB. nativehtmlkit-res://<bundle>/<path> (alias ui4me-res://) In-memory bundles registered with register_resource_bundle (≤256 entries and 1 MiB decoded per registration; ≤64 bundles, 16 MiB in total).
  • Raster formats: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and BMP (detected by content). Animated images show their first frame. AVIF, TIFF and ICO are not supported.
  • <img>: srcset, sizes, <picture>, object-fit, object-position, alt text for broken images. The same loader serves CSS background-image, <link rel="stylesheet"> and @import. Images decode asynchronously: right after document.load an image may still have no natural size (get_rect reports 0x0 until it arrives, and pending_resources in the load result is not a reliable "all images decoded" signal). An image may decode to at most 16,777,216 pixels.
  • SVG is static: as <img>/CSS image and as inline <svg> (≤2,000 elements, ≤512 KiB of markup).
  • Live bitmaps: <img src="nativehtmlkit-bitmap://<id>"> shows RGBA frames the backend streams through shared memory (bitmap.create/present/close; ≤4096x4096, 8 bitmaps and 64 MiB per document). See examples/wire-v1/live_bitmap.py and your SDK's live-bitmap API.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Desktop attributes
items.text: Attribute (alias data-ui4me-*) Effect data-nativehtmlkit-drop="files text" Opt-in target for drops from other applications. Tokens files, text, none; the nearest element carrying the attribute decides; none, or a disabled or inert ancestor, refuses. Without it nothing accepts drops. The backend gets drag_feedback and drop events. data-nativehtmlkit-drag Pressing on this region moves the native window (custom title bars, typically with decorations: false). data-nativehtmlkit-resize="north-west" Pressing resizes the window from that edge: n/north, s, e, w, ne/north-east, nw, se, sw. data-nativehtmlkit-no-drag Excludes a subtree. Buttons, links, form controls and <summary> are never drag regions.

items.title: Accessibility
items.text:
The host builds a native accessibility tree from the document and publishes it through AccessKit (AT-SPI on Linux, UI Automation on Windows). HTML semantics map to roles, plus the ARIA role values listed in profile §8 and the common ARIA states and properties (aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-expanded, aria-checked, aria-selected, aria-live, aria-busy, aria-hidden, aria-invalid, …). Names come from a simplified accessible-name computation (aria-labelledby, aria-label, <label>, content, title, placeholder). Hidden, display: none, aria-hidden and inert content is excluded; elements without a role of their own (a plain <div>, an unnamed <section> or <form>, <label>) have no node. get_accessibility_tree returns exactly what is published, which makes it the tool for automated accessibility checks.

Screen-reader behaviour must be qualified on the real desktop. Known limitation in 1.0.3: NHK-CROSS-0010 (Linux, Orca does not announce a collapsed drop-down's value change by arrow key; the value does change).

items.title: Untrusted text
items.text: There is no script execution, but markup injection still changes what users see and submit. Put user-provided text in with text operations (set_text, append_text, set_value), which never parse markup. Ops that take HTML (insert_html, replace_children_html, document.load) must only receive trusted HTML, with user values escaped (html.escape() in Python, [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode() in PowerShell).

items.title: Limits
items.text: Item Limit HTML per document load, file or inserted fragment 1 MiB, UTF-8 Nodes / nesting depth 65,536 / 256 Text per set_text/set_value/append_text 16 KiB Runtime stylesheets 64, each ≤1 MiB Properties per get_computed_style 64 Batch operations 1024 per batch/node_batch Default-action rules 256 per document Undelivered events per document 1024 Live documents per host / windows per host 16 / max_windows (≤64, default 16) Any protocol message (results and events included) 2 MiB after JSON encoding

items.title: Not supported
items.text:
JavaScript and inline event handlers; frames and embedded objects; network loading and link navigation; audio and video playback; a canvas drawing API; GPU rendering; printing and PDF export (printing capability is false); Shadow DOM and custom-element behaviour; contenteditable rich-text editing; colour and date/time pickers; datalist suggestions; HTML or image clipboard formats; dragging content out to other applications; browser storage, cookies and Web APIs.

Source: nativehtmlkit-core/docs/guides/html-css-support.md · edit the page there.

items.title: NativeHTMLKit wire protocol v1 — reference
items.text:
Status: public-stable since Core 1.0.3. Changes within v1 are additive only (COMPATIBILITY.md); anything else needs protocol version 2.

This page is for authors of SDKs and other independent clients. Application developers should use the Python SDK, the PowerShell SDK or the CLI; UI libraries never speak the protocol.

You want to… Read Learn the protocol by building a working client Tutorial: your first wire-v1 client and examples/wire-v1/ Implement or review an SDK SDK authoring guide Look up a method, op, parameter or result member Generated wire tables, then the schemas below Understand what each document op does Document command reference Know which events arrive and what they carry Events guide Know which HTML/CSS the host renders HTML and CSS support

items.title: Source of truth
items.text:
The generated contract in v1/ is authoritative; this page explains it and never overrides it.

Artifact What it is Authority v1/method-matrix.json Every message: direction, kind, Rust parameter type, unknown-member policy; the 81 op names scripts/generate-protocol-contract.py (parameter types parsed from Rust; the method list is checked against the host's dispatch arms) v1/schemas/methods/ JSON Schema (2020-12) of the params of each decoding client→host method Generated from the serde types v1/schemas/document-command.schema.json All 81 document.command ops (oneOf, tag op) with Rust defaults (x-rust-defaults) Generated from DocumentCommand v1/conformance/golden.json 342 runtime cases: error code, or the JSON kind of each top-level result member, boolean values and array lengths crates/nativehtmlkit-host/tests/protocol_conformance.rs against the compiled host (Linux socket and Windows pipe) reference/wire-tables.md Readable tables of all of the above scripts/docs/generate-wire-tables.py (generated, --checked)

python3 scripts/generate-protocol-contract.py --check fails when the Rust types change without regenerating the schemas, or when dispatch arms and the method list diverge. The golden does not compare string or number values, nested contents or notification payloads beyond member names.

items.title: 1. Launch and transport
items.text:
A launcher (an SDK, the CLI or your own tool) writes an application manifest and runs:

nativehtmlkit-host run --app <app.toml> [--headless] [--allow-unsupervised]

--headless runs the whole protocol and document engine without a desktop (no native windows, input, clipboard, dialogs, external open or accessibility; those methods return -32001). The SDKs select it when NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1. --allow-unsupervised is a Linux diagnostic mode without systemd --user containment. Other subcommands: render --html F --output F.png (diagnostic PNG, no backend), doctor (environment facts as JSON), probe (native probe window), --version --verbose (embedded source identity as JSON).

items.title: Manifest (app.toml)
items.text:
Paths are relative to the manifest's directory; {app_dir} is substituted in program, args, cwd, env values and icon. Unknown keys are rejected; the file is at most 256 KiB of UTF-8 TOML.

[app]
id = "org.example.Notes"        # dot-separated ASCII identity, components start with a letter, ≤128 bytes
name = "Notes"                  # ≤128 characters, used as the default window title
version = "1.2.0"               # optional
icon = "{app_dir}/icon.png"     # optional, must exist

[backend]
program = "/usr/bin/python3"    # absolute, relative to the manifest, or a bare name looked up on PATH
args = ["app.py", "--backend"]  # ≤256 arguments
cwd = "."                       # default: the manifest directory
[backend.env]                   # ≤128 entries; may not set UI4ME_*/NATIVEHTMLKIT_* transport names
PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1"

[host]                          # all optional
startup_timeout_ms = 15000      # 1000..300000: hello + app.ready must happen within it
shutdown_timeout_ms = 5000      # 100..120000: the deadline_ms sent with app.shutdown
max_windows = 16                # 1..64
instance = "single"             # "single" (default) forwards a second launch; "multiple"

items.title: Endpoint and launch variables
items.text:
The host creates a private endpoint and spawns the backend (stdin closed, stdout/stderr captured) with its own environment plus [backend.env] plus exactly these variables:

Variable Meaning UI4ME_ENDPOINT Linux: path of a Unix stream socket in a 0700 runtime directory ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nativehtmlkit-host/). Windows: \\.\pipe\nativehtmlkit-host-<key>, a byte-mode pipe whose DACL grants only the current logon session, remote clients rejected UI4ME_TOKEN 64 hexadecimal characters, the single-use credential for host.hello UI4ME_APP_ID The manifest app.id UI4ME_PROTOCOL_VERSION 1

These v1 names are permanent. A client must read them, remove them from its own environment and never log them or pass them to child processes (the host redacts the token from relayed output). The backend's stdout/stderr lines are relayed to the host's stderr as JSON records with fields.source = "backend" (see §10); they are never protocol traffic.

items.title: Containment
items.text: On Linux the host re-executes itself under a transient systemd --user unit (KillMode=control-group) unless it is headless or --allow-unsupervised; the backend gets PR_SET_PDEATHSIG. On Windows the backend runs in a kill-on-close Job Object. A launcher that must not be outlived by the host should bind the host to itself (Linux PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, Windows Job Object with kill-on-close), as the SDKs and the CLI do. On Linux, when the launcher exits, the host begins a normal bounded shutdown; if its event loop has not started that shutdown within max(shutdown_timeout_ms + 1 s, 2 s), a watchdog kills the backend process group and exits with status 1. host.capabilities.containment describes the mode in use.

items.title: Host exit status
items.text: 0 after a normal shutdown. 1 when the application failed (backend exited or lost its connection while running, missed the startup deadline, exceeded the shutdown deadline) or was force-quit. A second launch of a single-instance app forwards app.activate to the first one and exits 0.

items.title: 2. Framing
items.text: Each frame is a 4-byte unsigned big-endian length followed by exactly that many bytes of one UTF-8 JSON object. Length 0 and lengths above 2,097,152 bytes are fatal. A frame that is not valid UTF-8 or JSON, or a truncated header or body, ends the connection without a response (no -32700 is ever sent); for the authenticated backend this fails the application. The host never writes a partial frame. Results and notifications that would exceed the limit are refused: document.command returns -32002 asking for a smaller query, and an oversize document.event is replaced by a document.error.

items.title: 3. Envelope (JSON-RPC 2.0 subset)
items.text:
Requests: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":<string>,"method":<string>,"params":<object>}. Notifications omit id. Responses carry exactly one of result or error {code, message, data?}. Locked behaviour:

Input Outcome id not a string, empty, longer than 128 bytes or containing control characters (including id: null) -32600, response id: null jsonrpc missing or not "2.0"; an unknown top-level member; method not a string, empty, longer than 128 bytes, outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] or starting with rpc. -32600, id: null params omitted treated as {} params an array or null -32602, id: null Unknown method -32601 with the request id and data.method A batch (top-level array) or an object without method on the authenticated connection treated as a response to a host request; if it is not one, logged and dropped (no reply) A notification (no id) that fails no response Duplicate object keys last occurrence wins A request id reused while the first is pending fatal: the session fails

Send unique string ids and never batches. At most 128 requests may be pending. Correlate responses by id only: a document.load with path or asset_root is answered when its file read finishes on a worker thread, so later requests can be answered first. Requests with inline html and all other methods are answered in order.

items.title: 4. Authentication and handshake
items.text:
The first request on a connection must be host.hello:

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"c1","method":"host.hello","params":{"token":"<UI4ME_TOKEN>","protocol_version":1}}

Other members (for example client) are ignored. Result: {protocol_version: 1, host_version, app_id, capabilities} where capabilities equals the host.capabilities result (§7). Errors: wrong protocol_version -32010; wrong or missing token -32011; any other method first -32011; a second hello, or a hello with a valid token on a second connection, -32005. Only one authenticated connection exists. Other connections may only call app.activate (the secondary-instance hand-off) and get -32011 otherwise; a malformed frame closes only that connection.

items.title: 5. Error codes
items.text:
Code Name Typical cause -32600 invalid request envelope violation (§3) -32601 method not found unknown method -32602 invalid params decode failure, unknown member on a decoding method or op, semantic argument error (unknown element id, rejected markup, out-of-range value) -32603 internal unexpected host failure -32001 unsupported not available here: headless clipboard/dialogs/external open/attention, hidden windows on Wayland, document features outside the profile -32002 unavailable a service or file missing at run time; a result too large for one frame -32003 denied policy refusal -32004 closed window, document, node or bitmap no longer exists (stale handle) -32005 busy a limit reached (windows, documents, pending operations, HTML over 1 MiB), duplicate hello, window creation during quit preflight -32006 cancelled request cancelled by request.cancel -32007 disconnected -32008 invalid state wrong lifecycle phase: app.ready without a window or twice; any call after shutdown begins except host.capabilities, host.diagnostics, request.cancel, app.force_quit -32009 timeout -32010 version mismatch host.hello protocol_version ≠ 1 -32011 unauthenticated before or without a valid host.hello

Errors raised by the document engine carry data.engine_code. Treat every code, including unknown ones, as failure, and never parse message.

items.title: 6. Parameters and unknown members
items.text:
Every decoding method and every op with parameters rejects unknown members with -32602. Locked v1 exceptions: methods that do not decode params (host.capabilities, host.diagnostics, app.ready, app.request_quit, app.force_quit, window.list, desktop.paths, desktop.preferences, clipboard.read_text) ignore them, and so do the 11 parameterless ops (clear_selection, copy_selection, css_profile, get_accessibility_tree, get_diagnostics, get_environment, get_focused_element, get_pointer_capture, get_resource_stats, get_selection, list_stylesheets). Ops whose element and node are both optional in the schema may still require one of them at run time (focus, explain, get_computed_style, get_control_selection, set_control_selection, replace_control_range, set_custom_validity, get_form_data, reset_form, request_submit, edit_command without a focused control).

host.hello validates token and protocol_version by hand. In headless mode the dialog methods return -32001 before decoding, so an unknown member there is also -32001.

items.title: 7. Methods
items.text: Exact parameters, defaults and observed result members of every method are in the wire tables. Summary:

items.title: Host and application
items.text:
Method Purpose host.hello Authenticate (§4). host.capabilities Capability snapshot: platform, headless, native, renderer ("cpu"), css_profile, max_windows, max_documents (16), limits {frame_bytes, pending_requests, probe_text_bytes}, legacy booleans (clipboard_text, file_dialogs, external_open, accessibility, ime, drag_drop, printing, tray, window_positioning, …) and the authoritative features map (below). Callable at any phase. host.diagnostics {phase, windows, pending_jobs, pending_transfers, pid, backend_pid, containment, logging, dropped_notifications}. Callable at any phase. app.ready The backend finished startup. Requires at least one window (-32008 otherwise or when repeated). Must happen before host.startup_timeout_ms. app.request_quit Start the quit preflight: the host asks app.before_quit {reason: "backend_request"}. Returns {requested: true}. app.force_quit End the session at once without asking; the backend is killed and the host exits with status 1. request.cancel {id} Cancel a pending asynchronous request of this connection (dialogs, external open/reveal, clipboard read, path loads). The cancelled request is answered -32006; the result is {cancelled: bool}.

capabilities.features maps a feature name to {implemented, available, qualification, scope}. available is whether this host, OS session and mode can use it now; qualification is requires_current_native_evidence or out_of_scope. Feature names in 1.0.3: accessibility, attention, clipboard_text, external_open, file_dialogs, ime, ime_purpose_hints, incoming_drop, native_preferences, printing, reveal_file, tray, window_constraints, window_focus, window_observation, window_position, window_restore, window_visibility. Probe features.<name>.available instead of assuming a platform, and ignore unknown keys.

items.title: Windows
items.text:
Method Purpose window.create Create a top-level window (title defaults to the app name, 900x560 CSS px, visible, resizable, decorations, paired min_/max_ size constraints 1..8192). Returns the window description with window_id ("w1", "w2", …, never reused). -32005 beyond max_windows or during quit preflight. On Linux (Wayland) visible: false is -32001. window.get / window.list Describe one / all windows: title, width, height (requested CSS px), visible, closing, native, scale_factor, physical_size, requested {decorations, resizable, visible, size_constraints}, observed {…} (native state, null when unknown or headless). window.set Change title, size, visibility, resizable, decorations, minimized/maximized/fullscreen, focus, position (x, y) and size constraints (null clears a constraint; update both dimensions together). What the OS honours is reported in observed. window.request_attention {kind?} Ask the window manager for attention (-32001 headless or where unavailable). window.request_close Ask to close a window: after app.ready the host sends window.event close_requested and the window.before_close decision; see §8.

A window is first presented when its first document.load succeeds, or at most 750 ms after creation (then a placeholder page is shown). On Windows a new window is fitted into the monitor work area; on Wayland the compositor places windows and the surface is clamped to the smallest output.

items.title: Documents
items.text:
Method Purpose document.load {window_id, html \| path, asset_root?} Replace the window's document. Exactly one of html (inline, ≤1 MiB UTF-8) or path (a regular file ≤1 MiB, resolved against the backend cwd); asset_root (a directory) bounds local resource loading, default: the HTML file's directory, none for inline HTML. Returns {window_id, document_id, loaded, source, asset_root, renderer, pending_resources}. Markup the profile rejects fails the load (-32602) and the previous document stays. At most 16 live documents per host. document.get {window_id} Describe the current document, or {document_id: null, loaded: false}. document.unload {window_id, document_id} Remove the document; the window shows nothing. document.command {window_id, document_id, command} Run one op on the document (§7a).

Document ids ("d1", "d2", …) are never reused. Every command names both window and document, so a command meant for a replaced document fails with -32004 instead of touching the new one.

items.title: 7a. document.command ops
items.text:
81 ops in nine groups; see the document command reference for semantics and the wire tables for fields.

Group Ops DOM content set_text, append_text, get_text, get_html, insert_html, replace_children_html, remove_element, move_element, trim_children, batch Attributes and classes get_attribute, get_attributes, set_attribute, remove_attribute, add_class, remove_class, has_element Query and node handles query, query_nodes, node_of, get_node, node_children, node_batch, element_at_point, text_at_point Form controls and validation get_value, set_value, get_checked, set_checked, get_options, set_selected_values, get_files, get_form_data, request_submit, reset_form, check_validity, get_validity, set_custom_validity Focus, selection and editing focus, blur, get_focused_element, get_control_selection, set_control_selection, replace_control_range, edit_command, select_text, get_selection, clear_selection, copy_selection, set_pointer_capture, get_pointer_capture Dialogs and popovers show_dialog, close_dialog, get_dialog, show_popover, hide_popover, toggle_popover, get_popover Scrolling and geometry scroll_to, scroll_by, scroll_into_view, get_scroll, set_scroll_follow, get_rect, text_rects Styles, environment and behaviour add_stylesheet, replace_stylesheet, remove_stylesheet, list_stylesheets, get_computed_style, set_environment, get_environment, set_default_action Resources and diagnostics register_resource_bundle, unregister_resource_bundle, get_resource_stats, purge_unused_resources, get_accessibility_tree, get_diagnostics, css_profile, explain

items.title: Bitmaps (live pixels)
items.text:
Method Purpose bitmap.create {window_id, document_id, bitmap_id, width, height, slots?, pixel_format?} Register a live bitmap (bitmap_id 1..64 of [A-Za-z0-9_-], 1..4096 px per side, 2..3 slots, only "RGBA8"). Returns {bitmap_id, width, height, stride, pixel_format, slots, slot_bytes, path, owner}. bitmap.present {…, bitmap_id, slot, sequence} The backend finished writing slot; the host copies it once. sequence must be positive and increasing; an old one is acknowledged with presented_to_engine: false. bitmap.close {…, bitmap_id} Remove it: {closed: bool}.

Map the returned path (a private file of slots × slot_bytes bytes) before the first present and write straight-alpha sRGB RGBA8 rows of stride bytes into a slot. Reuse a slot only after its bitmap.present was acknowledged. The host unlinks the file after the first present. Markup shows it as <img src="nativehtmlkit-bitmap://<bitmap_id>"> (ui4me-bitmap:// also works). Limits: 8 bitmaps and 64 MiB per document, 256 MiB per host. Files live in the private runtime directory on Linux and in %TEMP%\nativehtmlkit-bitmaps\ on Windows; use the returned path, never a guessed one. Worked example: examples/wire-v1/live_bitmap.py.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Desktop services
items.text:
Method Purpose dialog.open_files / dialog.save_file / dialog.choose_folder Parented native dialogs (window_id, title, directory, file_name, filters [{name, extensions}], multiple). Answered when the user closes the dialog; cancellable. Linux needs the desktop portal. clipboard.read_text / clipboard.write_text {text} Plain-text clipboard (≤1 MiB written). read_text is answered asynchronously. desktop.open_external {target, window_id?} Open a URL or file with the default application; "accepted" is not proof that an app appeared. desktop.reveal_file {path, window_id?} Show an absolute local path in the file manager. desktop.paths Per-app config, data, cache, state, runtime directories. desktop.preferences {available, source, color_scheme, reduced_motion, high_contrast, revision, scope}; null = not observed. probe.get_text / probe.set_text Text of the built-in probe surface of a window without a document (host self-tests).

All of these except desktop.paths, desktop.preferences and probe.* return -32001 in headless mode.

items.title: 8. Lifecycle, host requests and notifications
items.text:
flowchart LR
  Hello["host.hello"] --> Window["window.create (≥1)"] --> Load["document.load"] --> Ready["app.ready"]
  Ready --> Run["events, commands, services"] --> Quit["before_quit allowed"] --> Shutdown["app.shutdown {deadline_ms}"]

Host phases (host.diagnostics.phase): starting, connecting, initializing (after hello), running (after app.ready), quit_pending, quitting, failed, stopped.

Host → client requests must be answered with {"allow": true} or {"allow": false}; a missing, false or non-boolean allow vetoes:

Request When window.before_close {window_id, reason} the user or window.request_close asks to close a window (preceded by window.event close_requested). Allowed → the window closes (window.event closed). app.before_quit {reason} app.request_quit (reason: "backend_request") or closing the last window ("last_window"). Allowed → app.shutdown.

Answer any other host request with an error (-32601). There is no host-side deadline for these decisions: a backend that never answers keeps the window or app open until app.force_quit or the user's Ctrl+Shift+Q in a document window.

Notifications (host → client): document.event, document.error, window.event, app.shutdown {deadline_ms}, request.cancelled {id, reason} (a pending close decision superseded by an app-wide quit), app.activated (a second launch: {args, cwd, activation_token}), and desktop.preferences_changed (a new preferences snapshot). Payloads are described in the events guide. Ignore unknown notifications and unknown members.

Closing before app.ready: a backend window.request_close of one window while another usable window remains closes it without a decision; closing the last usable window, or any native close by the user during startup, cancels startup (app.shutdown).

No closed event for the last window: when an allowed close of the last window starts shutdown, no window.event closed is sent for it. app.shutdown means every window and document handle is stale; later window calls fail with -32008. Release resources and exit before deadline_ms, or the backend is killed and the host exits with status 1.

Output backpressure: a backend that stops reading is not disconnected because of input events. When its outbound queue reaches three quarters of its bound (96 messages or 6 MiB), further window.event and document.event notifications are dropped and counted in host.diagnostics.dropped_notifications. Responses, host requests and all other notifications are never dropped; a backend that leaves even those unread past the full bound fails the session. Keep reading while you work.

items.title: 9. Markup and resource names
items.text: ui4me-res://, ui4me-bitmap:// and data-ui4me-{drag,no-drag,resize,drop} remain valid in v1; nativehtmlkit-res://, nativehtmlkit-bitmap:// and data-nativehtmlkit-* are additive aliases of the same objects. Wire-visible identifiers keep their v1 values: CSS profile ui4me-desktop-1.0, profile id ui4me-css/1, diagnostics schema ui4me-diagnostics. There is no JavaScript, no HTTP loading and no browser engine; see HTML and CSS support.

items.title: Known limitations of v1
items.text:
• Close/quit decisions have no host-side deadline (§8).
  • A Linux host whose whole process is stopped (SIGSTOP, a debugger) cannot bound itself; the watchdog thread does not run. A launcher that must survive this kills the host itself (its pid is in host.diagnostics).

items.title: 10. Host diagnostics output (not part of the wire contract)
items.text: The host writes one JSON record per line to stderr ({"timestamp","level","fields":{…},"target"}). Backend stdout/stderr lines appear as records with fields.source = "backend", fields.stream and fields.text at every level, launch token redacted. NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS=off|normal|debug|trace selects the host's own detail (off keeps errors and backend output); at trace it records request receipt and completion (method, id, duration, error code) and notification types, never params, results or values. The sink is bounded and lossy; host.diagnostics.logging reports the drop counters. Record shapes may gain members: parse them defensively.

items.title: Compatibility and change ownership
items.text:
See COMPATIBILITY.md for the v1 stability rules and CONFORMANCE-ROADMAP.md for the qualification evidence. Native capabilities vary by OS and session; Core 1.0.3 has recorded accessibility and platform qualification limits (for example NHK-CROSS-0010) that the stable protocol declaration does not hide.

Source: nativehtmlkit-core/protocol/README.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Protocol versioning and compatibility policy
items.text: Applies to the NativeHTMLKit host wire protocol. Host releases, CLI releases and SDK releases are versioned independently of the protocol version.

items.title: Protocol version 1
items.text:
• Status: public-stable since host 1.0.3 (2026-11-16). Every rule below is binding for all later 1.x hosts; the behaviours host 1.0.3 introduced (protocol README.md §3, §7, §8, §10: id-correlated document.load responses, output backpressure, deferred first presentation, initial placement, the Windows bitmap directory, backend-output relay) are part of the stable contract.
  • protocol_version is the integer in host.hello. Hosts in the 1.x line speak exactly 1.
  • Never changed within v1: framing (§2 of README.md), envelope rules (§3), authentication and launch variables (UI4ME_ENDPOINT, UI4ME_TOKEN, UI4ME_APP_ID, UI4ME_PROTOCOL_VERSION), error codes and their meaning, existing method/op names, existing parameter names and types, existing result members, lifecycle ordering and the {allow} decision contract, and the legacy markup/resource spellings (ui4me-res://, ui4me-bitmap://, data-ui4me-*) and wire-visible identifiers (ui4me-desktop-1.0, ui4me-css/1, ui4me-diagnostics).
  • Allowed additive changes in a v1 host: new methods, new document ops, new optional parameters, new result members, new notification types, new capabilities/features keys, new aliases (as done for nativehtmlkit-*). Clients MUST ignore unknown result members, unknown notifications and unknown capability keys, and MUST answer unknown host requests with an error.
  • Every additive change regenerates v1/method-matrix.json and schemas and re-blesses v1/conformance/golden.json; a review must confirm the golden diff only adds cases or members. A removed case, a changed error code or a removed member is a breaking change.
  • Quirks locked as v1 behaviour (they are documented, not bugs to silently "fix"): no -32700 responses; dropped method-less frames on the authenticated connection; last-key-wins duplicates; parameterless ops ignoring extra members; document.load oversize returning -32005.

items.title: Breaking changes → protocol version 2
items.text: A v2 must be negotiated (a v2 host keeps accepting protocol_version: 1 for at least one major host release, or the host refuses with -32010 and the release notes say so). Candidate v2 items: NATIVEHTMLKIT_* launch variables (never exported alongside the UI4ME_* ones, so a credential is not duplicated into children), strict unknown-member rejection for parameterless ops, -32700 responses before closing, and removal of legacy spellings.

items.title: Host / client compatibility matrix
items.text: Each consumer release records the exact host version, host SHA-256 and protocol version it was qualified with (CLI: manifest.json in its archive; workspace: nativehtmlkit-project compatibility record). A consumer may run with a newer 1.x host of the same protocol version, but only the recorded host is "qualified".

items.title: Platforms
items.text:
Qualified targets: Linux x86-64 KDE Plasma Wayland, Windows x86-64 interactive desktop (Server 2022 tested). Other Unix targets compile only as best effort and are not qualified.

Source: nativehtmlkit-core/protocol/COMPATIBILITY.md · edit the page there.

items.title: document.command op reference (wire v1)
items.text:
A document.command request runs one op on one document:

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"c7","method":"document.command",
 "params":{"window_id":"w1","document_id":"d1","command":{"op":"set_text","element":"status","text":"Saved"}}}

This page explains what each of the 81 ops does and what it returns. Exact field types, defaults and observed result members are generated in the wire tables; the JSON Schema ../v1/schemas/document-command.schema.json is authoritative. Result examples below were captured from a headless Core 1.0.3 host.

items.title: Addressing elements and nodes
items.text:
• element is the value of an element's id attribute. Ids must be unique and contain no whitespace (≤256 bytes); a document violating that does not load. An unknown id is -32602 (Unknown element ID: …).
  • node is an opaque, generation-checked reference such as "node:1:13:1", returned by query_nodes, node_of, get_node, node_children, element_at_point, get_focused_element and by every document.event (event.node). It lets you address elements without an id. A node that was removed is never reused: using it fails with -32004 (or a stale_reference answer from explain). Do not parse node references.
  • Ops that accept element or node take exactly one of them.
  • Mutating ops answer {"updated": true} unless stated otherwise.
  • Ops may emit document.event notifications before their response (for example focus emits focus/focusin, request_submit emits submit or invalid). Programmatic value changes (set_value, set_checked, set_selected_values) do not emit input/change.
  • Text arguments are limited to 16 KiB per update (set_text, set_value, append_text); inserted HTML and whole documents to 1 MiB; a document to 65,536 nodes and nesting depth 256.
  • A result larger than one 2 MiB frame fails with -32002; page with offset/limit.

items.title: DOM content
items.text: Op What it does Result set_text {element, text} Replace the element's children with one text node. Text is never parsed as markup. Not for form controls (use set_value). updated append_text {element, text} Append text (extends the last text node while small, so streaming logs stay cheap). updated get_text {element} Text content. {text} get_html {element? \| node?, outer?, offset?, limit?} Serialized inner (or outer) HTML of an element, or of the whole document when neither is given; paged by byte offset/limit. {html, offset, next_offset, total_bytes, truncated} insert_html {element, position, html} Parse trusted HTML and insert it at beforebegin, afterbegin, beforeend or afterend. The fragment is validated like a document (no scripts, unique ids). Escape untrusted text. updated replace_children_html {element, html} Replace the children with parsed HTML. updated remove_element {element} Remove an element (not html, head, body). updated move_element {element, target, position} Move an element relative to target (same positions). updated trim_children {element, keep, from?} Keep only keep children; from: "start" (default) removes the oldest children first, "end" the newest. Typical for bounded logs. updated batch {ops} Apply up to 1024 BatchOps (set_text, set_attribute, remove_attribute, add_class, remove_class, insert_html, replace_children_html, remove_element, move_element, append_text, trim_children) as one update. updated

items.title: Attributes and classes
items.text: Op What it does Result get_attribute {element, name} One attribute. {value} get_attributes {element} All attributes. {attributes: {name: value}} set_attribute {element, name, value} / remove_attribute {element, name} Change an attribute; on* and srcdoc are rejected. Setting open on <details> emits toggle. updated add_class / remove_class {element, name} Edit class. updated has_element {element} Whether an id exists. {exists}

items.title: Query and node handles
items.text: Op What it does Result query {selector, offset?, limit?} CSS selector query returning only matches that have an id. {ids, total, matched_nodes, offset, limit, truncated} query_nodes {selector, offset?, limit?} Selector query returning node references for every match (limit default 1024). {nodes: [{node, element}], total, offset} node_of {element?} Node reference of an id (or of the document). {node} get_node {node} Describe a node: type (element, text, …), name, id, attributes, text, parent, previous, next, child_count. object node_children {node, offset?, limit?} Child references (limit default 256, max 4096). {children, total} node_batch {ops} Like batch, but every op addresses a node (MoveElement uses target_node). Stale nodes fail the batch. updated element_at_point {x, y} Hit test in viewport CSS px (null outside the viewport). {node, element} or null text_at_point {x, y} Text position under a point. {hit: {block, element, offset}}

items.title: Form controls and validation
items.text: Op What it does Result get_value / set_value {element, value?} Value of input, textarea, select. {value} / updated get_checked / set_checked {element, checked?} Checkbox/radio state. {checked} / updated get_options {element} Options of a select. {options: [{value, label, selected, disabled}]} set_selected_values {element, values} Select options by value (several for multiple). updated get_files {element} Files chosen in an <input type=file> (paths only, never contents). {files} get_form_data {element \| node, submitter?, submitter_node?} Form entries in document order, as a submission would build them. {entries: [{name, kind, value}], submitter} (file entries carry path/filename) request_submit {element \| node, submitter?, submitter_node?} Run constraint validation; if valid fire a cancelable submit event, otherwise invalid events and focus the first invalid control. Never navigates. {submitted, default_prevented} reset_form {element \| node} Fire reset and restore defaults. {reset, default_prevented} check_validity {element} Validate a control or a whole form; fires invalid on failures. {valid, count, invalid: [ids]} get_validity {element} Validity state with the standard flags (valueMissing, typeMismatch, patternMismatch, tooLong, tooShort, rangeUnderflow, rangeOverflow, stepMismatch, badInput, customError) and an English message. {valid, will_validate, flags, message} set_custom_validity {element \| node, message} Set (non-empty) or clear ("") a custom error. validity state

items.title: Focus, selection and editing
items.text: Op What it does Result focus {element \| node} / blur {element? \| node?} Move focus (emits focus/focusin, and blur/focusout on the old element). blur without a target blurs the focused element. updated get_focused_element Focused element. {element, node} or null get_control_selection {element \| node} Caret/selection inside a text control (UTF-16 offsets). {start, end, direction, length, node} set_control_selection {…, start, end, direction?} Select in a control (forward, backward, none); emits select/selectionchange. selection replace_control_range {…, replacement, start?, end?, selection_mode?} Replace a range (default: the selection) as user editing would (emits beforeinput, input); selection_mode preserve (default), select, start, end. selection + changed edit_command {command, element? \| node?} undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, select_all, delete on a text control (copy/cut/paste also on the document selection). {accepted, clipboard_pending} select_text {element?} Select an element's text (or the whole document). updated get_selection / copy_selection / clear_selection Document text selection (not control selections); copy_selection returns the text it copies. {text} / {text} / updated set_pointer_capture {element, pointer_id?, capture?} / get_pointer_capture Capture the active pointer for drag interactions; only accepted while that pointer is pressed. {accepted} / {element}

items.title: Dialogs and popovers
items.text: Op What it does Result show_dialog {element, modal?} Open a <dialog> (modal by default: top layer, rest inert). Emits beforetoggle, focus events, toggle. updated close_dialog {element, return_value?} Close it; emits close with return_value. updated get_dialog {element} {open, modal, return_value}. object show_popover / hide_popover / toggle_popover {element} Popover state of an element with popover. Emits beforetoggle/toggle. updated / {open} get_popover {element} {open, kind} (auto or manual). object

items.title: Scrolling and geometry
items.text: Op What it does Result scroll_to {element?, x?, y?, behavior?} Scroll a container (or the viewport) to a position; behavior auto, instant or smooth. Emits scroll. scroll state scroll_by {element?, dx?, dy?, behavior?} Relative scroll. scroll state scroll_into_view {element, block?, inline?, behavior?} Align start, center, end or nearest (default). updated get_scroll {element?} {x, y, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y, width, height, scrollable, animating}. object set_scroll_follow {element?, follow?} Keep a container pinned to its end while content is appended (log views). updated get_rect {element} Border box in viewport CSS px. {rect: {x, y, width, height}} text_rects {element? \| node?, start?, end?} Line boxes of an element's text. {text, length, rects: [{x, y, width, height, visible}]}

items.title: Styles, environment and behaviour
items.text:
Op What it does Result add_stylesheet {css} Add a runtime stylesheet (≤1 MiB, ≤64 sheets). {sheet, diagnostics} (parse problems such as unknown properties, with line/column) replace_stylesheet {sheet, css} / remove_stylesheet {sheet} Change a runtime sheet. {sheet, diagnostics} / updated list_stylesheets Document <style>/<link> and runtime sheets. {sheets: [{sheet, kind, node, element, href, media, length}]} get_computed_style {element \| node, properties} 1..64 property names (custom properties allowed): {status: "supported", value, inherited}, {status: "unsupported", feature} (profile-excluded) or {status: "invalid", reason}. {schema: 1, properties} set_environment {color_scheme?, reduced_motion?} App override for prefers-color-scheme (light, dark, system) and prefers-reduced-motion (reduce, no-preference, system). environment get_environment {color_scheme, reduced_motion, high_contrast, scale, …_source, system_…}; sources are app, system or default. object set_default_action {element, event, key?, shift?, ctrl?, alt?, meta?, prevent?} Declare ahead of time that the host prevents an event's default action on that element (and descendants), optionally only for one key and modifier combination. Events: keydown, click, dblclick, auxclick, contextmenu, beforeinput, copy, cut, paste, mousedown, pointerdown, wheel, submit, reset, cancel, beforetoggle. prevent: false removes the rule. ≤256 rules. The delivered event then has default_prevented: true. updated

There is no way to prevent a default action from an event handler: events reach the backend after the host handled the input. Declare rules with set_default_action instead.

items.title: Resources and diagnostics
items.text:
Op What it does Result register_resource_bundle {name, entries: [{path, data_url}]} In-memory files served as nativehtmlkit-res://<name>/<path> (≤256 entries and 1 MiB decoded per request; at most 64 bundles and 16 MiB of registered data in total). Re-registering replaces the bundle. {name, replaced} unregister_resource_bundle {name} Remove a bundle. {name, removed} get_resource_stats / purge_unused_resources {url?} Cache, bundle and SVG raster counters / drop unreferenced cache entries. stats / {purged, stats} get_accessibility_tree The semantic tree the native bridge publishes: nodes with id, role, name, html_id, bounds, states, relations, structure, actions, children, and the tree focus. {tree} get_diagnostics Bounded engine diagnostics (code, stage, feature, reason, message), e.g. UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE for dropped CSS or RESOURCE_DENIED for refused URLs. {css_profile_version, diagnostics} css_profile The CSS feature profile: {version, features: [{id, state}]}; see the generated profile. object explain {element \| node, property?} Why a property has (no) effect: status applied, not_applicable (e.g. display: none ancestor, inline box, static position, not a flex/grid item), overridden, unsupported (profile), unknown_property or stale_reference, with a human reason. Without property, explains the element and its inline-style declarations. {schema: 1, status, reason, …}

Source: nativehtmlkit-core/protocol/reference/document-commands.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Tutorial: your first wire-v1 client
items.text:
In this tutorial you run, read and extend a complete NativeHTMLKit application that talks to the native host without an SDK, using only the Python standard library. By the end you will know every step a client performs: launch, handshake, window and document, events, commands, quit.

You need Python 3.10+ and a nativehtmlkit-host 1.0.3 binary (from a Core release archive, or the one bundled in the nativehtmlkit Python wheel under nativehtmlkit/_bin/). The tutorial uses headless mode, so no desktop is required; drop --headless to see the real window.

The code lives in examples/wire-v1/:

  • wire_client.py — ~200 lines: framing, handshake, correlation, host requests, notifications.
  • notes_app.py — a "Quick notes" app built on it.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: 1. Run it
items.text:
export NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY=/path/to/nativehtmlkit-host
uv run examples/wire-v1/notes_app.py --headless --self-test --transcript session.jsonl

Expected output (Core 1.0.3, Linux):

PASS empty form is not submitted
PASS invalid event shows an error
PASS valid form is submitted
PASS note is escaped
PASS no <b> element was injected
PASS input was cleared
PASS whitespace note rejected
PASS counter reads 2 notes
SELF-TEST PASS

Headless mode has no synthetic input, so --self-test makes the backend play the user: it fills the field with set_value and presses "Add" with request_submit, which fires the same submit (or invalid) events a real click would. session.jsonl now holds every frame (token redacted).

items.title: 2. Two processes, one script
items.text:
notes_app.py runs twice. You start it as the launcher: it writes an app.toml manifest whose backend is the same script with --backend, then runs nativehtmlkit-host run --app app.toml --headless. The host starts that backend with four variables in its environment:

UI4ME_ENDPOINT=/run/user/1000/nativehtmlkit-host/<key>.sock   (Windows: \\.\pipe\nativehtmlkit-host-<key>)
UI4ME_TOKEN=<64 hex characters>
UI4ME_APP_ID=org.example.QuickNotes
UI4ME_PROTOCOL_VERSION=1

The backend's print() output goes to a pipe the host owns; the host relays each line to its own stderr as a JSON record with fields.source = "backend", and the launcher turns those back into plain lines (wire_client.relay_host_stderr). That is why the PASS lines appear on your terminal.

items.title: 3. Connect and say hello
items.text:
wire_client.connect_from_environment() pops the four variables (so they cannot leak into child processes), checks the token shape, connects to the socket or pipe and sends the first request. From session.jsonl:

{"dir":"send","frame":{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"c1","method":"host.hello","params":{"token":"<redacted-token>","protocol_version":1}}}
{"dir":"receive","frame":{"id":"c1","jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"app_id":"org.example.QuickNotes","capabilities":{"headless":true,"css_profile":"ui4me-desktop-1.0","features":{…},…},"host_version":"1.0.3","protocol_version":1}}}

On the wire each JSON object is preceded by its length as a 4-byte big-endian integer (struct.pack(">I", len(body))). Ids are strings you choose; correlate responses by id.

items.title: 4. Window, document, ready
items.text:
{"dir":"send","frame":{"id":"c2","method":"window.create","params":{"title":"Quick notes","width":520,"height":420},…}}
{"dir":"receive","frame":{"id":"c2","result":{"window_id":"w1","width":520,"height":420,"native":false,…}}}
{"dir":"send","frame":{"id":"c3","method":"document.load","params":{"window_id":"w1","html":"<!doctype html>…"},…}}
{"dir":"receive","frame":{"id":"c3","result":{"document_id":"d1","loaded":true,"renderer":"cpu",…}}}
{"dir":"send","frame":{"id":"c4","method":"app.ready","params":{},…}}
{"dir":"receive","frame":{"id":"c4","result":{"ready":true}}}

app.ready tells the host startup is complete; it must arrive within startup_timeout_ms (15 s by default) or the host fails the application. Keep the window_id and document_id: every document.command names both, so a command can never hit a newer document by accident.

items.title: 5. React to events
items.text:
The page contains <form id="add"> with a required input. When the form is submitted the host sends a notification:

{"dir":"receive","frame":{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"document.event","params":{"window_id":"w1","document_id":"d1",
  "event":{"type":"submit","element":"add","path":["add"],"cancelable":true,"default_prevented":false,…}}}}

NotesBackend.handle matches on type and on element or path, then reads the value, escapes it and inserts it:

{"dir":"send","frame":{"id":"c10","method":"document.command","params":{…,"command":{"op":"get_value","element":"note"}}}}
{"dir":"receive","frame":{"id":"c10","result":{"value":"<b>milk</b> & eggs"}}}
{"dir":"send","frame":{"id":"c11","method":"document.command","params":{…,"command":{"op":"insert_html","element":"notes","position":"beforeend","html":"<li><b>milk</b> & eggs</li>"}}}}

insert_html parses markup, so the text is passed through html.escape() first; set_text (used for the counter and the error line) never parses markup and needs no escaping.

When the field is empty, request_submit runs constraint validation instead: the host sends an invalid event for the field (with a validity object), focuses it, and answers {"submitted": false}. The app shows its own message, because the host draws no validation bubble.

items.title: 6. Quit
items.text:
{"dir":"send","frame":{"id":"c31","method":"app.request_quit","params":{}}}
{"dir":"receive","frame":{"id":"host:decision:1","method":"app.before_quit","params":{"reason":"backend_request"}}}
{"dir":"send","frame":{"id":"host:decision:1","result":{"allow":true}}}
{"dir":"receive","frame":{"id":"c31","result":{"requested":true}}}
{"dir":"receive","frame":{"method":"app.shutdown","params":{"deadline_ms":5000}}}

app.before_quit is a request from the host: it has an id and expects {"allow": bool}. Session._dispatch_one answers it (through the decide callback) while waiting for the c31 response — a client must keep reading and answering at all times. After app.shutdown the backend exits; the host exits with status 0.

The same request arrives with reason: "last_window" when the user closes the window, so this is also where an app would ask about unsaved notes (answer {"allow": false} to keep running).

items.title: 7. Extend it
items.text:
Try these changes, then rerun the self-test (and add a check for each):

  1. Delete a note. Render each note as <li><span></span><button class="del">×</button></li> and, on a click whose path contains no id, use the event's node with get_node to find the <li> and remove it with node_batch [{op: "remove_element", node}].
  2. Persist notes. Ask desktop.paths for the data directory and store the notes as JSON there.
  3. Confirm quit. Answer app.before_quit with allow: false when there are unsaved notes, show a <dialog> with show_dialog, and call app.request_quit again from its "Quit" button.
  4. Dark mode. Add @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) rules and switch them with set_environment {color_scheme: "dark"}.

Next: live_bitmap.py streams pixels into an <img>; the SDK authoring guide lists what a production client must add (Windows overlapped I/O for concurrent readers, cancellation, backpressure, lifetime binding).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

Source: nativehtmlkit-core/docs/tutorials/first-wire-client.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Writing an independent NativeHTMLKit client (SDK authoring guide)
items.text:
A client is a backend process launched by the host; the host owns windows, rendering, input and accessibility. Use only the published contract — this directory, README.md and v1/ — never Core's private Rust crates.

New to the protocol? Work through the tutorial first; its dependency-free client examples/wire-v1/wire_client.py is a compact, verified implementation of the steps below.

items.title: 1. Launcher
items.text:
1. Locate a pinned host binary and verify it (the Python SDK checks the SHA-256 recorded next to its bundled host). nativehtmlkit-host --version --verbose prints the embedded source identity (version, source_commit, source_tree, source_dirty) as JSON.
  2. Write an app.toml (reference §1) into a private temporary directory. Quote every string safely (a JSON string is a valid TOML basic string, except that DEL must be escaped); {app_dir} is substituted everywhere and has no escape, so reject arguments that contain it.
  3. Run nativehtmlkit-host run --app <manifest>; add --headless only when the user asked for test mode (the SDKs use NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1). Never select headless silently because no desktop was found.
  4. Bind the host's lifetime to the launcher: Linux PR_SET_PDEATHSIG in the child, Windows a Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (plus SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK so applications the host opens for the user survive). Otherwise a killed launcher leaves an orphaned window.
  5. Read the host's stderr continuously: it is JSON lines. Relay fields.source == "backend" records as the app's stdout/stderr (fields.stream), show WARN/ERROR records, and hide the rest unless the user asked for verbose output. Return the host's exit status.
  6. Delete the manifest directory afterwards; keep any result/session files in 0700 directories.

items.title: 2. Backend connection
items.text:
1. Read and remove UI4ME_ENDPOINT, UI4ME_TOKEN, UI4ME_APP_ID, UI4ME_PROTOCOL_VERSION. Validate the token (64 hex characters) and the version (1). Never log the token or pass it to child processes.
  2. Connect: Linux AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM to the path. Windows: open the named pipe for read and write, retrying briefly while it is busy. If one thread reads while another writes, open the pipe for overlapped I/O (FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, one OVERLAPPED/event per operation): on a synchronous handle a pending ReadFile blocks every WriteFile. A single-threaded client (read only while waiting for something, as in wire_client.py) can use a plain synchronous handle.
  3. Framing: write a u32 big-endian length followed by the UTF-8 JSON; read the same. Reject length 0 or more than 2,097,152 before allocating. Never interleave two writers on one stream.
  4. Send host.hello {token, protocol_version: 1} first; require result.protocol_version == 1. Keep result.capabilities.

items.title: 3. Requests and the reader loop
items.text:
• Use unique, non-empty string ids (≤128 bytes, no control characters); keep at most 128 requests pending, and refuse locally beyond that.
  • Dispatch every incoming frame:
  • method and id → host request. Answer window.before_close / app.before_quit with {"allow": bool} (missing or non-boolean is a veto); answer any other method with error -32601. Answer promptly — the host has no deadline and waits.
  • method without id → notification. Deliver it; ignore unknown methods and members.
  • otherwise → response; correlate by id, never by order. An error response with id: null belongs to no request: treat it as a defect in your client (log it, fail loudly in tests).
  • Keep reading at all times. Run the reader on its own thread or task (or read whenever you wait, as the example does). A backend that stops reading loses document.event/window.event notifications (counted in host.diagnostics.dropped_notifications) and, if it leaves responses unread, fails the session. Hand slow application work to another thread; never run user callbacks on the reader thread if they may block on a request.
  • Give long-running requests (dialogs, clipboard reads, path loads) a cancellation path: request.cancel {id}; the original request is then answered -32006.
  • Map error codes to typed exceptions and never parse message; treat unknown codes as failure. Distinguish -32004 (stale window/document/node: retire the handle) and -32008 (lifecycle phase).

items.title: 4. Application model
items.text:
1. window.create → document.load {window_id, html|path} → app.ready (within startup_timeout_ms).
  2. Expose handles that carry both window_id and document_id. Retire the old document handle only after a successful document.load (a refused load keeps the old document). After window.event closed retire the window; after app.shutdown retire everything (no closed arrives for the last window).
  3. Wrap document.command generically (command(op, **fields)) so new additive ops work without an SDK release, then add typed helpers. Generate them from v1/schemas/document-command.schema.json if your language allows.
  4. Events: deliver document.event with the documented members (events guide). Let users match a target on event.element or event.path. Ignore members beginning with _.
  5. Default actions cannot be cancelled from a callback; expose set_default_action as a declarative API ("prevent Enter in #search", "prevent submit on #form").
  6. Validate what document.command returns before trusting it (form entries are {name, kind, value}, file entries carry path/filename).
  7. Make HTML insertion APIs obviously "trusted HTML" and offer text APIs (set_text, set_value) for user data. Provide an escaping helper.
  8. Live bitmaps: map the returned path before the first bitmap.present, write straight-alpha RGBA8 rows of stride bytes into a slot, present it with an increasing sequence, and reuse the slot only after the acknowledgement. On Windows open the file with delete sharing so the host can unlink it after the first present.
  9. On app.shutdown {deadline_ms} release resources (close bitmaps' mappings, flush files) and exit before the deadline; otherwise the backend is killed and the host exits with status 1.

items.title: 5. Verifying a new client
items.text:
1. Run it against the pinned host in headless mode and compare every method and op you wrap with v1/conformance/golden.json (error codes, result member kinds); the wire tables show the same data per method.
  2. Exercise the edge cases the golden locks: stale documents (-32004), app.ready twice (-32008), unknown members (-32602), oversize HTML (-32005), a host request arriving while you wait for a response, quit vetoed and then allowed.
  3. Check for orphans: after a normal exit, a crash of your backend and a killed launcher, no host or backend process may remain.
  4. Then qualify real windows on Linux KDE Plasma Wayland and an interactive Windows desktop (input, focus, resize, close decisions, file dialogs, clipboard). Headless mode proves the protocol and document state, not native behaviour.

The Rust CLI (nativehtmlkit-cli), the Python SDK and the PowerShell SDK are independent v1 clients qualified against the same host and are useful references.

Source: nativehtmlkit-core/protocol/SDK-AUTHORING.md · edit the page there.

items.title: SDK
items.text:
Plain HTML and CSS driven from your program: open windows, load pages, react to events, update the page, use native dialogs, the clipboard and live bitmaps. Full control, no extra layer. The UI library is built on it.

It works the same on Linux and Windows; the few real differences are listed in Linux and Windows.

  • Python

    Python 3.10+ with uv. Same API on Linux (KDE Plasma Wayland) and Windows.

    Getting started · Tutorials · Guides · Examples · API

  • PowerShell

    PowerShell 7.2+, or Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows. Same API on Linux (KDE Plasma Wayland) and Windows.

items.title: PowerShell SDK architecture
items.text: This page explains how the NativeHTMLKit module turns a PowerShell script into a native desktop app, so that the rules in the guides (side effects below Start-NativeHTMLKitScript, callbacks on one runspace, plain data for background work) make sense. It describes module 0.1.2 with Core 1.0.3 and wire protocol v1.

items.title: Two processes
items.text:
+---------------------------+        private local channel         +---------------------------+
 | nativehtmlkit-host (Rust) |  <--- length-prefixed JSON-RPC  --->  | PowerShell backend        |
 | windows, input, layout,   |       Unix socket / named pipe       | your script + this module |
 | rendering, accessibility, |                                      | state, logic, callbacks   |
 | native dialogs, clipboard |                                      |                           |
 +---------------------------+                                      +---------------------------+
  • The host is the native NativeHTMLKit Core executable bundled in the module (runtimes/linux-x64, runtimes/win-x64). It owns everything the user sees and touches: the windows, the HTML/CSS engine (no browser and no JavaScript), input methods, accessibility trees and operating-system services.
  • The backend is a PowerShell process running your script. It holds your data and logic and tells the host what to show. The module is the backend half of the protocol: a C# transport compiled at import (Private/NativeHTMLKit.Transport.cs), the cmdlets (NativeHTMLKit.psm1), background tasks and diagnostics.
  • They talk over a private, authenticated local channel: a Unix-domain socket (Linux) or a restricted named pipe (Windows), never TCP or HTTP. The host creates it, starts the backend with UI4ME_ENDPOINT and a one-time UI4ME_TOKEN, and the backend proves the token in host.hello. Messages are 4-byte length prefixes plus UTF-8 JSON-RPC 2.0, at most 2 MiB each.

The host supervises the backend: it enforces startup and shutdown deadlines, stops it when the app quits, and reports a backend that disappears without an accepted quit as an application failure.

items.title: How a script becomes a backend
items.text:
Start-NativeHTMLKitScript makes a normal .ps1 file both launcher and backend:

pwsh -File app.ps1 args            (launcher run)
  Start-NativeHTMLKitScript
    writes private app.toml  ->  starts nativehtmlkit-host run --app app.toml
                                   host starts: pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File app.ps1 args   (backend run)
                                     Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -> Connect -> returns $app
                                     ... your code: windows, documents, handlers, ready, wait ...
    waits for the host; exit <host exit code>

The launcher role is chosen when the UI4ME_* variables are absent; it validates the options, resolves and verifies the host binary (SHA-256 against HOST-MANIFEST.json), writes the manifest into a folder only the current user can access, starts the host (on Linux through setpriv --pdeathsig so the host stops if the launcher is killed), relays the host's records to the console as plain text, and finally exits with the host's exit code. The backend role connects and removes the launch secrets from its environment so programs it starts cannot inherit them.

Everything above the call therefore runs twice, which is why side effects belong below it. Manifest-based deployments skip the launcher: the host is started with an explicit app.toml and the backend only connects.

items.title: One owner runspace, one event pump
items.text:
The transport's reader is a .NET thread that parses frames into a bounded queue; it never runs PowerShell code. PowerShell code runs only on the owner runspace, the one that created the application, when it pumps the queue:

  • Wait-NativeHTMLKit pumps explicitly;
  • every SDK command that needs a reply pumps while it waits, so events can be handled in the middle of, for example, Get-NativeHTMLKitValue.

Messages are handled in host order. Replies complete waiting requests; host requests (window.before_close, app.before_quit) run your policy scriptblock and are answered at once, even inside a nested wait, so the host is never left waiting on a decision; host notifications (document.event, window.event, desktop.preferences_changed, ...) run your callbacks one at a time. While a callback runs, further notifications are deferred until it returns (bounded at 128; extra ones are dropped and counted). A failing callback is isolated: logged, counted, and the app continues.

This single-threaded model is why SDK objects must not be shared with other runspaces, why long work in a callback freezes the window, and why Start-NativeHTMLKitTask exists.

items.title: Handles and their lifetime
items.text: The SDK mirrors host objects as small handle objects: application, window, document, node, live bitmap, request, subscription, task. Each handle knows its owner and whether it is still current. The host's lifecycle events retire them: a closed window retires its document; loading a new document retires the previous one together with its subscriptions, nodes and bitmaps; app.shutdown retires every window (the host sends no separate closed event for the last window); Close-NativeHTMLKit retires everything and removes all callbacks. A retired handle throws NativeHTMLKit.StaleObjectException locally instead of sending a request the host would reject.

items.title: Documents and commands
items.text:
A document is HTML and CSS rendered by the host. The backend changes it with document commands (document.command with an op such as set_text, insert_html, batch, get_form_data); the typed cmdlets are thin wrappers that build these commands, and Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand reaches the rest of the 81 operations. Elements are addressed by id, or by generation-bound node references for elements without ids. Events travel the other way as document.event notifications that carry the element id, the id path, the target node reference and event-specific fields; the SDK matches them against subscriptions (type plus id on the path) after native dispatch.

Live bitmaps bypass the message channel for pixels: the host creates a file mapping with two or three frame slots, the backend writes a frame into the next slot and sends a small bitmap.present request.

items.title: Background work
items.text: Start-NativeHTMLKitTask runs a scriptblock in a fresh runspace (its text is re-parsed there, so no variables, functions or modules carry over) and refuses SDK objects among its arguments. The pump checks for finished tasks between messages and runs -OnCompleted/-OnFailed on the owner runspace, never inside another callback.
