items.title: NativeHTMLKit PowerShell SDK: cmdlet reference
items.text:
Module NativeHTMLKit 0.1.2, bundling NativeHTMLKit Core 1.0.3 (public wire protocol v1). PowerShell 7.2+ on Linux and Windows, Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows.

This page is the entry point of the reference: every exported command, grouped by task, with a link to its full description (syntax, parameters with types and defaults, output, errors, examples). 88 functions are exported, each with one short -NHK alias (alias table). Run Get-Command -Module NativeHTMLKit and Get-Help <command> for the installed copy.

New here? Start with getting started, the tutorials (todo app, process dashboard, bulk rename) or the examples. Concepts: architecture.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• Handles (NativeHTMLKit.Application, .Window, .Document, .Node, ...) belong to the runspace that created the application. Callbacks run on that runspace while it pumps events. Objects, errors, threading and limits.
  • Parameter tables name the expected handle type (NativeHTMLKit.Document, ...). Those parameters are declared as [object] (see the syntax blocks) and checked when the command runs; passing the wrong handle throws, for example, Expected a NativeHTMLKit.Window from New-NativeHTMLKitWindow.
  • -Element always means an element id. Elements without ids are reached through nodes.
  • Text you show is safe with Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText; HTML you build must encode untrusted values. Security guide.
  • Failures are terminating errors; host refusals are NativeHTMLKit.RpcException with a Code.

items.title: Reference: live bitmaps
items.text:
Live bitmaps show pixels you compute in PowerShell (charts, previews, simple animations) inside the document. Frames travel through a shared memory file mapping that the host creates, not over the message channel. How-to: Live bitmaps.

A NativeHTMLKit.LiveBitmap has read-only properties Id, Width, Height, Stride (Width * 4), SlotBytes (Width * Height * 4), Slots, Sequence (frames presented), Closed and Document. It belongs to its document: it is released when the document is retired or the window or application closes.

items.title: New-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap
items.text:
Alias: New-NHKLiveBitmap

Creates a live image (bitmap.create, pixel format RGBA8) that any <img src="nativehtmlkit-bitmap://ID"> in the document shows. The <img> can exist before or after the bitmap.

New-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap [-Document] <Object> [-Id] <string> [-Width] <int> [-Height] <int> [[-Slots] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Id string yes - Bitmap id: 1-64 ASCII letters, digits, _ or -. -Width int yes - Width in pixels. Range 1 to 4096. -Height int yes - Height in pixels. Range 1 to 4096. -Slots int no 2 Number of frame buffers (2 or 3). One of: 2, 3.

Returns NativeHTMLKit.LiveBitmap. Errors an invalid id; The host returned invalid bitmap geometry (the host's bitmap is closed again); NativeHTMLKit.RpcException from the host.

items.title: Send-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap
items.text:
Alias: Send-NHKLiveBitmap

Writes one complete frame into the next slot and presents it (bitmap.present). Pixels are straight (not premultiplied) alpha RGBA8, row by row from the top-left, exactly SlotBytes bytes. The call returns after the host has taken its copy of the slot (synchronous backpressure), so the same byte[] can be reused for the next frame.

Send-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap [-Bitmap] <Object> [-Pixels] <Object> [-Try] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Bitmap NativeHTMLKit.LiveBitmap yes - The live bitmap. -Pixels byte[] yes - byte[] of Width * Height * 4 bytes (an object array of byte values is converted, slower). -Try switch no off Return $null instead of throwing when a present of this bitmap is already in progress (for example from a callback that runs during that present).

Returns @{ sequence; presented_to_engine; slot_released }. Errors wrong length (Expected N RGBA8 bytes, received M); a present already in progress (without -Try); a closed bitmap or retired document (NativeHTMLKit.StaleObjectException).

$bitmap = New-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap -Document $doc -Id preview -Width 64 -Height 64
$pixels = New-Object byte[] (64 * 64 * 4)
for ($i = 0; $i -lt $pixels.Length; $i += 4) { $pixels[$i] = 255; $pixels[$i + 3] = 255 }   # opaque red
$null = Send-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap -Bitmap $bitmap -Pixels $pixels

items.title: Remove-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap
items.text:
Alias: Remove-NHKLiveBitmap

Unmaps the shared memory and releases the host bitmap (bitmap.close). Idempotent; $null is accepted. When the document, window or application is already gone, only local resources are released. Errors for a bitmap the host already closed are ignored; -Quiet ignores all host errors.

Remove-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap [-Bitmap] <Object> [-Quiet] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Bitmap NativeHTMLKit.LiveBitmap yes - The live bitmap, or $null. Accepts $null. -Quiet switch no off Suppress host errors.

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/bitmaps.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Reference: desktop services
items.text:
Capabilities, desktop preferences, clipboard, opening URLs and files, and native file dialogs. How-to: File dialogs, Clipboard.

Desktop services depend on the operating system and session. In the host's headless test mode (NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1) clipboard, file dialogs, external open and attention requests are refused with NativeHTMLKit.RpcException (code -32001, unsupported). Check Get-NativeHTMLKitCapabilities and handle RpcException instead of assuming a service exists.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitCapabilities
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKCapabilities

Returns what the running host offers (host.capabilities).

Get-NativeHTMLKitCapabilities [-Application] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application.

Returns an object. Top-level fields for Core 1.0.3 include native and headless, platform (linux, windows), max_windows, max_documents, renderer (cpu), css_profile, window_positioning, limits (frame_bytes, pending_requests, ...), the service booleans clipboard_text, file_dialogs, external_open, drag_drop, ime, accessibility (enabled API surfaces; $false in headless mode), features (per-feature implemented/available detail; null means not observed) and native_preferences.

$caps = Get-NativeHTMLKitCapabilities -Application $app
if (-not $caps.file_dialogs) { Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute -Document $doc -Element browse -Name disabled }

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitPreferences
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKPreferences

Returns the observed desktop preferences (desktop.preferences): color_scheme, reduced_motion, high_contrast (each $null when not observed), available, source (headless in test mode), revision and scope. Changes are announced by the desktop.preferences_changed notification (see Register-NativeHTMLKitNotification). Documents follow the observed preferences in CSS media queries unless overridden with Set-NativeHTMLKitEnvironment.

Get-NativeHTMLKitPreferences [-Application] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitClipboard
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKClipboard

Reads plain text from the system clipboard (clipboard.read_text).

Get-NativeHTMLKitClipboard [-Application] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application.

Returns [string] (empty when the clipboard holds no text). Errors NativeHTMLKit.RpcException when the clipboard is unavailable (headless: Clipboard requires a native event loop).

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitClipboard
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKClipboard

Writes plain text to the system clipboard (clipboard.write_text).

Set-NativeHTMLKitClipboard [-Application] <Object> [-Text] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application. -Text string yes - Text to copy. May be empty.

Errors as for Get-NativeHTMLKitClipboard.

items.title: Open-NativeHTMLKitExternal
items.text:
Alias: Open-NHKExternal

Opens a URL or a document with the desktop's default handler (desktop.open_external), or with -Reveal shows a file in the file manager (desktop.reveal_file; the path is resolved against the PowerShell location). Accepted targets are http, https, mailto and file URIs and absolute local paths; a relative path fails with code -32602, other schemes and executable file types (programs, scripts, shortcuts) are denied with code -32003. -Window names the parent window for any desktop prompt. Waits up to 60 seconds.

Open-NativeHTMLKitExternal [-Application] <Object> [-Target] <string> [[-Window] <Object>] [-Reveal] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application. -Target string yes - URI or absolute path; with -Reveal a file path (relative paths are resolved against the PowerShell location). -Window NativeHTMLKit.Window no - Parent window; must belong to -Application. -Reveal switch no off Show the file in the file manager instead of opening it.

Returns the host result (accepted, cancelled, ...).

items.title: Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog
items.text:
Alias: Show-NHKFileDialog

Shows a native Open, Save or Choose-folder dialog attached to a window (dialog.open_files, dialog.save_file, dialog.choose_folder) and waits without a deadline while the user decides, pumping events meanwhile. Only one native dialog per window can be open at a time (a second one fails with code -32005, busy).

Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog [-Window] <Object> [[-Kind] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [[-Directory] <string>] [[-FileName] <string>] [[-Filters] <Object[]>] [[-Multiple] <bool>] [-NoWait] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Window NativeHTMLKit.Window yes - Parent window. -Kind string no 'OpenFiles' OpenFiles, SaveFile or ChooseFolder. One of: OpenFiles, SaveFile, ChooseFolder. -Title string no - Dialog title. -Directory string no - Initial folder (resolved against the PowerShell location). -FileName string no - Suggested file name; only with -Kind SaveFile. -Filters object[] no @() Array of @{ name = 'Images'; extensions = @('png', 'jpg') } (extensions without dot). Ignored for ChooseFolder. -Multiple bool no $false OpenFiles only: allow several files. -NoWait switch no off Return a NativeHTMLKit.Request immediately instead of waiting.

Returns @{ cancelled; paths }: cancelled is $true and paths empty when the user cancelled. With -NoWait, a NativeHTMLKit.Request: Wait-NativeHTMLKitRpc returns the same result later, Stop-NativeHTMLKitRpc closes the dialog. Errors NativeHTMLKit.RpcException when dialogs are unavailable (headless: code -32001 Native file dialogs are unavailable in headless mode).

try {
    $pick = Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog -Window $window -Kind OpenFiles -Multiple $true -Title 'Import logs' -Filters @(@{ name = 'Logs'; extensions = @('log', 'txt') })
    if (-not $pick.cancelled) { foreach ($path in $pick.paths) { Import-Log $path } }
} catch [NativeHTMLKit.RpcException] {
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text $_.Exception.RpcMessage
}

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/desktop.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Reference: diagnostics and support
items.text: Local diagnostics only: nothing is sent anywhere. How-to: Diagnostics and support bundles.

items.title: Levels and records
items.text:
One switch controls the SDK, the host and the backend: NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS = off, normal (default when unset), debug or trace; Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Diagnostics sets it for the host and backend. The SDK keeps the last 2048 records in memory (older ones are dropped and counted). Records hold fixed event names, identifiers, numbers and allow-listed short tokens only: never RPC parameters or results, form values, HTML, text, paths, URLs, tokens or exception messages ([REDACTED]).

Level SDK records off Nothing. normal Errors and warnings (callback.failed, rpc.rejected, rpc.timeout, transport.disconnected, task.failed, ...). debug Also lifecycle (host.authenticated, host.request, task.started, task.completed, application.closed, ...). trace Also every request (rpc.started, rpc.completed with duration), notification (host.notification) and callback (callback.started, callback.completed).

A diagnostic session ID (NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID, generated as nhk-ps-<32 hex> when unset) is shared by the launcher, the host's records (diagnostic_session_id) and the backend.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnosticReport
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKDiagnosticReport

Returns the SDK's diagnostic counters. With -Application, adds that connection's counters and, when connected, the host's own loss counters (host.diagnostics).

Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnosticReport [[-Application] <Object>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application no - Optional application to include.

Returns SchemaVersion, SessionId, Level, RecordCount, RecordLimit, DroppedRecords, SessionReplaced; with -Application also Connection (Closed, Disconnected, ShutdownRequested, ReceivedMessages, PendingRequests, QueuedMessages, DroppedNotifications, RejectedHostRequests, DeferredDropped, CallbackFailures, ActiveTasks, CancellationPendingTasks), HostCounters (dropped_notifications, sink_dropped_records, backend_omitted_records, sink_capacity_records, backend_records_per_pump) and HostCountersError (NotConnected or an exception type name).

items.title: Export-NativeHTMLKitSupportBundle
items.text:
Alias: Export-NHKSupportBundle

Writes a sanitized ZIP with manifest.json (versions, counters, level, whether records were dropped) and timeline.jsonl (the redacted SDK records), only when called. It contains no RPC parameters or results, form values, tokens, file paths, screenshots, or raw host/backend output.

Export-NativeHTMLKitSupportBundle [-Path] <string> [[-Application] <Object>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Path string yes - Destination .zip path; the file must not exist and its folder must. -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application no - Optional application whose counters to include.

Returns the System.IO.FileInfo of the bundle. Errors Support bundle already exists; The support bundle path must end with .zip; Destination directory missing.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnostics
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKDiagnostics

Returns the document's renderer diagnostics (get_diagnostics): css_profile_version and diagnostics, a list of @{ code; stage; message } notes such as unsupported CSS features or pending resources.

Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnostics [-Document] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitResourceStats
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKResourceStats

Returns the document's resource cache statistics (get_resource_stats): bundles (count, entries, bytes), cache (entries, bytes, hits, misses, evictions, ...) and svg_rasters.

Get-NativeHTMLKitResourceStats [-Document] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document.

items.title: Clear-NativeHTMLKitUnusedResources
items.text:
Alias: Clear-NHKUnusedResources

Releases cached resources that no element references (purge_unused_resources), or only the given URL.

Clear-NativeHTMLKitUnusedResources [-Document] <Object> [[-Url] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Url string no - Purge only this resource URL.

Returns @{ purged; stats } (stats as from Get-NativeHTMLKitResourceStats).

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/diagnostics.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Reference: documents and DOM updates
items.text:
Loading HTML, reading and changing elements by id, stylesheets, computed style, environment, scrolling, focus and text selection. How-to: DOM updates.

A NativeHTMLKit.Document has read-only properties Id (such as d1), Window and Retired. A window has at most one document. Loading another document into the window (or Remove-NativeHTMLKitDocument, a fatal document.error, closing the window) retires the old one: its handlers, nodes and bitmaps are released and every later use throws NativeHTMLKit.StaleObjectException (This NativeHTMLKit document was replaced, unloaded, or its window closed).

Commands that take -Element address an element by its id attribute. An unknown id, invalid arguments or an operation the element does not support make the host answer with an error, which surfaces as NativeHTMLKit.RpcException (for example code -32602, invalid parameters). Every command in this page waits for the host's reply and pumps events while waiting (see events).

items.title: Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml
items.text:
Alias: Open-NHKHtml

Loads an HTML string into the window (document.load), atomically replacing any current document. Use a full document (<!doctype html><html>...) or a fragment. Relative URLs (stylesheets, images, fonts) resolve against -AssetRoot. Scripts are not executed: NativeHTMLKit has no JavaScript; all behaviour is PowerShell callbacks.

Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml [-Window] <Object> [-Html] <string> [[-AssetRoot] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Window NativeHTMLKit.Window yes - The window to load into. -Html string yes - HTML text. May be empty. -AssetRoot string no - Folder that relative resource URLs resolve against. Resolved against the PowerShell location.

Returns NativeHTMLKit.Document. Waits up to 30 seconds for the host.

items.title: Open-NativeHTMLKitFile
items.text:
Alias: Open-NHKFile

Loads an HTML file into the window, atomically replacing any current document. Relative URLs in the file (<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">) resolve against the file's folder unless -AssetRoot is given. The path is resolved against the PowerShell location (Set-Location), not the process working directory.

Open-NativeHTMLKitFile [-Window] <Object> [-Path] <string> [[-AssetRoot] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Window NativeHTMLKit.Window yes - The window to load into. -Path string yes - HTML file path. -AssetRoot string no - Folder that relative resource URLs resolve against.

Returns NativeHTMLKit.Document. Waits up to 30 seconds.

$doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitFile -Window $window -Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'index.html')

items.title: Remove-NativeHTMLKitDocument
items.text:
Alias: Remove-NHKDocument

Unloads the document (document.unload); the window stays open and empty, and the document handle is retired.

Remove-NativeHTMLKitDocument [-Document] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKDocumentText

Returns an element's text content (get_text) as [string].

Get-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKDocumentText

Replaces an element's children with a single text node (set_text). The text is never parsed as HTML, so it is the safe way to show user input, file content or command output.

Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [-Text] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id. -Text string yes - New text. May be empty.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitValue
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKValue

Returns the current value of a form control (get_value): text of an <input> or <textarea>, the selected value of a <select>.

Get-NativeHTMLKitValue [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id of the control.

Returns [string].

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKDocumentValue

Sets a control's current value (set_value). This changes the value the user sees, not the value attribute, and it does not dispatch input or change events. After setting a text control's value the caret is at its end.

Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [-Value] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id of the control. -Value string yes - New value. May be empty.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitChecked
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKChecked

Returns whether a checkbox or radio button is checked (get_checked), as [bool].

Get-NativeHTMLKitChecked [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id of the checkbox or radio button.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitChecked
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKChecked

Checks or unchecks a checkbox or radio button (set_checked). Does not dispatch events.

Set-NativeHTMLKitChecked [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [-Checked] <bool> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id. -Checked bool yes - New state.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKDocumentAttribute

Sets an attribute (set_attribute) or, with -Remove, removes it (remove_attribute). Use an empty value for boolean attributes: -Name disabled disables a button, -Name disabled -Remove enables it.

Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [-Name] <string> [[-Value] <string>] [-Remove] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id. -Name string yes - Attribute name. -Value string no '' Attribute value (ignored with -Remove). -Remove switch no off Remove the attribute instead of setting it.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitClass
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKClass

Adds a class (add_class) or, with -Remove, removes it (remove_class).

Set-NativeHTMLKitClass [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [-Name] <string> [-Remove] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id. -Name string yes - Class name. -Remove switch no off Remove the class instead of adding it. 
Set-NativeHTMLKitClass -Document $doc -Element status -Name error -Remove:(-not $failed)

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKDocumentHtml

Replaces an element's children with HTML (replace_children_html, the default -Position replace) or inserts HTML relative to it (insert_html with beforebegin, afterbegin, beforeend or afterend). The HTML is parsed: only pass trusted markup and encode every untrusted value with [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode(); see security.

Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [-Html] <string> [[-Position] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id. -Html string yes - HTML to insert. May be empty (clears the element with replace). -Position string no 'replace' Where to put the HTML. One of: replace, beforebegin, afterbegin, beforeend, afterend. 
$row = '<li>' + [Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($line) + '</li>'
Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml -Document $doc -Element log -Html $row -Position beforeend

items.title: Remove-NativeHTMLKitElement
items.text:
Alias: Remove-NHKElement

Removes an element and its subtree (remove_element).

Remove-NativeHTMLKitElement [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id.

items.title: Find-NativeHTMLKitElement
items.text:
Alias: Find-NHKElement

Runs a CSS selector query (query). The result counts every matching element but lists only the ids of matches that have one; use Get-NativeHTMLKitNodes to address matches without ids.

Find-NativeHTMLKitElement [-Document] <Object> [-Selector] <string> [[-Offset] <int>] [[-Limit] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Selector string yes - CSS selector. -Offset int no 0 Index of the first id to return. Range 0 to 2147483647. -Limit int no 1024 Maximum number of ids to return. Range 1 to 4096.

Returns an object: ids (array of id strings), matched_nodes (number of matching elements), total (number of matching elements that have an id), offset, limit, truncated.

$rows = (Find-NativeHTMLKitElement -Document $doc -Selector '#rows tr').matched_nodes

items.title: Invoke-NativeHTMLKitBatch
items.text:
Alias: Invoke-NHKBatch

Applies several id-addressed DOM operations as one atomic transaction (batch): either all of them apply or none does, and they are painted together. Each operation is a hashtable with op and its fields:

op Fields set_text element, text append_text element, text set_attribute element, name, value remove_attribute element, name add_class, remove_class element, name insert_html element, position (beforebegin, afterbegin, beforeend, afterend), html replace_children_html element, html remove_element element move_element element, target, position trim_children element, keep, optional from (start (default) removes the first children, end removes the last) 
Invoke-NativeHTMLKitBatch [-Document] <Object> [-Operations] <Object[]> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Operations object[] yes - Array of operation hashtables.

Returns nothing.

Invoke-NativeHTMLKitBatch -Document $doc -Operations @(
    @{ op = 'set_text'; element = 'count'; text = '42' }
    @{ op = 'add_class'; element = 'count'; name = 'changed' }
    @{ op = 'insert_html'; element = 'history'; position = 'afterbegin'; html = '<li>42</li>' }
    @{ op = 'trim_children'; element = 'history'; keep = 10; from = 'end' }
)

items.title: Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand
items.text:
Alias: Invoke-NHKDocumentCommand

Runs any document command of the Core wire protocol (document.command) and returns its result. The typed cmdlets cover the common commands; this one gives access to the rest, for example get_html, get_attribute, get_attributes, has_element, get_rect, get_dialog, get_popover, check_validity, get_validity, set_custom_validity, scroll_into_view, scroll_by, set_scroll_follow, replace_control_range, select_text and get_accessibility_tree. The exact fields of all 81 operations are in the Core protocol contract (protocol/v1/schemas/document-command.schema.json).

Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand [-Document] <Object> [-Operation] <string> [[-Parameters] <IDictionary>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Operation string yes - The command name (the protocol's op). -Parameters System.Collections.IDictionary no @{} Command fields. op is not allowed here; use -Operation.

Commands used in this repository's examples (verified with Core 1.0.3):

Operation Parameters Result get_html element or node, optional outer (bool), offset, limit html, total_bytes, truncated, offset, next_offset get_attribute element, name value get_dialog element open, modal, return_value get_popover element open set_scroll_follow element, follow (default $true) keeps a scroll container pinned to its end while content is appended replace_control_range element or node, replacement, optional start, end (UTF-16), selection_mode replaces the given range, or the current selection, of a text control 
$outer = (Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Document $doc -Operation get_html -Parameters @{ element = 'status'; outer = $true }).html

items.title: Add-NativeHTMLKitStylesheet
items.text:
Alias: Add-NHKStylesheet

Adds an author stylesheet to the document (add_stylesheet).

Add-NativeHTMLKitStylesheet [-Document] <Object> [-Css] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Css string yes - CSS text. May be empty (useful as a placeholder sheet to replace later).

Returns an object with sheet (the sheet handle, a number) and diagnostics (CSS parse notes).

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitStylesheets
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKStylesheets

Lists the document's stylesheets (list_stylesheets). Returned as one array object (assign it and use the variable). Each entry has sheet, kind (attached for sheets added with Add-NativeHTMLKitStylesheet), length, href, media, element, node.

Get-NativeHTMLKitStylesheets [-Document] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitStylesheet
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKStylesheet

Replaces the CSS of a sheet (replace_stylesheet, parameter set Replace) or removes it (remove_stylesheet, set Remove).

Set-NativeHTMLKitStylesheet -Document <Object> -Sheet <long> -Css <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Set-NativeHTMLKitStylesheet -Document <Object> -Sheet <long> -Remove [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Sheet long yes - Sheet handle from Add-NativeHTMLKitStylesheet or Get-NativeHTMLKitStylesheets. -Css string yes (Replace) - New CSS text. Parameter set: Replace. -Remove switch yes (Remove) off Remove the sheet. Parameter set: Remove. 
$sheet = (Add-NativeHTMLKitStylesheet -Document $doc -Css '').sheet
$null = Set-NativeHTMLKitStylesheet -Document $doc -Sheet $sheet -Css 'body { font-size: 18px; }'

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitComputedStyle
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKComputedStyle

Returns computed CSS values (get_computed_style) for an element (by id or node) or, without a target, for the document root.

Get-NativeHTMLKitComputedStyle [-Document] <Object> [-Properties] <string[]> [[-Element] <string>] [[-Node] <Object>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Properties string[] yes - CSS property names, for example @('color', 'font-size'). -Element string no - Element id. Use -Element or -Node, not both. -Node NativeHTMLKit.Node no - A NativeHTMLKit.Node from Get-NativeHTMLKitNode.

Returns @{ schema = 1; properties = @{ <name> = @{ value; status; inherited } } }, for example (...).properties.'font-size'.value is '18px'. status is supported for properties the CSS profile implements.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitEnvironment
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKEnvironment

Returns the document's media environment (get_environment): color_scheme, reduced_motion, high_contrast, each with a *_source (default, app for an override, or the observed system value), plus system_color_scheme, system_reduced_motion and scale.

Get-NativeHTMLKitEnvironment [-Document] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitEnvironment
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKEnvironment

Overrides prefers-color-scheme and/or prefers-reduced-motion for this document (set_environment). Only the parameters you pass change. Allowed values: color scheme light, dark or system (removes the override); reduced motion reduce, no-preference or system. Other values fail with NativeHTMLKit.RpcException (-32602).

Set-NativeHTMLKitEnvironment [-Document] <Object> [[-ColorScheme] <string>] [[-ReducedMotion] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -ColorScheme string no - light, dark or system. -ReducedMotion string no - reduce, no-preference or system.

Returns the new environment (same shape as Get-NativeHTMLKitEnvironment).

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitScroll
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKScroll

Returns the scroll state of the document or of a scroll container (get_scroll): x, y, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y, width, height, scrollable, animating.

Get-NativeHTMLKitScroll [-Document] <Object> [[-Element] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string no - Element id of a scroll container. Default: the document.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitScroll
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKScroll

Scrolls the document or an element (scroll_to) to -X/-Y in CSS pixels. Only the given coordinates change. Returns the new scroll state.

Set-NativeHTMLKitScroll [-Document] <Object> [[-Element] <string>] [[-X] <double>] [[-Y] <double>] [[-Behavior] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string no - Element id of a scroll container. Default: the document. -X double no - Horizontal scroll position. -Y double no - Vertical scroll position. -Behavior string no 'auto' Scroll behaviour. One of: auto, instant, smooth.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitFocusedElement
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKFocusedElement

Returns the focused element (get_focused_element): element (its id or $null) and node.

Get-NativeHTMLKitFocusedElement [-Document] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitFocus
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKFocus

Focuses an element or node (focus), or with -Blur removes focus (blur). Without -Blur a target is required.

Set-NativeHTMLKitFocus [-Document] <Object> [[-Element] <string>] [[-Node] <Object>] [-Blur] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string no - Element id. -Node NativeHTMLKit.Node no - A NativeHTMLKit.Node. -Blur switch no off Remove focus (from the given element, or from the focused element).

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitSelection
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKSelection

Returns a text control's selection (get_control_selection): start and end (UTF-16 offsets), direction (none, forward, backward), node, and length, which is the length of the control's whole value, not of the selection (use end - start).

Get-NativeHTMLKitSelection [-Document] <Object> [[-Element] <string>] [[-Node] <Object>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string no - Element id of an <input> or <textarea>. -Node NativeHTMLKit.Node no - A NativeHTMLKit.Node.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitSelection
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKSelection

Sets a text control's selection (set_control_selection); -Start equal to -End places the caret.

Set-NativeHTMLKitSelection [-Document] <Object> [[-Element] <string>] [[-Node] <Object>] [-Start] <int> [-End] <int> [[-Direction] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string no - Element id of an <input> or <textarea>. -Node NativeHTMLKit.Node no - A NativeHTMLKit.Node. -Start int yes - Selection start (UTF-16 offset). Range 0 to 2147483647. -End int yes - Selection end (UTF-16 offset). Range 0 to 2147483647. -Direction string no 'none' Selection direction. One of: none, forward, backward.

Returns the new selection (same shape as Get-NativeHTMLKitSelection).

items.title: Invoke-NativeHTMLKitEditCommand
items.text:
Alias: Invoke-NHKEditCommand

Runs an editing command through the native editor (edit_command) on the given element or the focused one. Core 1.0.3 accepts exactly undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, select_all and delete (other names fail with code -32602; note select_all, not selectAll as the module's built-in help says). Commands that change the value dispatch input events. Clipboard commands complete asynchronously: acceptance does not mean the operating-system transfer succeeded.

Invoke-NativeHTMLKitEditCommand [-Document] <Object> [-Command] <string> [[-Element] <string>] [[-Node] <Object>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Command string yes - undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, select_all or delete. -Element string no - Element id. Default: the focused element. -Node NativeHTMLKit.Node no - A NativeHTMLKit.Node.

Returns @{ accepted; clipboard_pending }.

items.title: Register-NativeHTMLKitResources
items.text:
Alias: Register-NHKResources

Atomically registers or replaces one document-local resource bundle that HTML and CSS can reference as nativehtmlkit-res://NAME/<path> (register_resource_bundle): icons, images or fonts generated in memory, without temporary files. -Entries maps relative paths to byte[], or to @{ Bytes = [byte[]]; Mime = 'image/png' } (default MIME application/octet-stream). At most 256 entries and 1 MiB of decoded bytes per registration.

Register-NativeHTMLKitResources [-Document] <Object> [-Name] <string> [-Entries] <IDictionary> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Name string yes - Bundle name (the host part of the URL). -Entries System.Collections.IDictionary yes - Hashtable of relative path to bytes or @{ Bytes; Mime }.

Returns @{ name; replaced } (replaced is $true when a bundle of that name existed).

$png = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'logo.png'))
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitResources -Document $doc -Name brand -Entries @{ 'logo.png' = @{ Bytes = $png; Mime = 'image/png' } }
# <img src="nativehtmlkit-res://brand/logo.png">

items.title: Unregister-NativeHTMLKitResources
items.text:
Alias: Unregister-NHKResources

Removes a resource bundle (unregister_resource_bundle).

Unregister-NativeHTMLKitResources [-Document] <Object> [-Name] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Name string yes - Bundle name.

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/documents.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Reference: document events
items.text: Subscribing PowerShell scriptblocks to DOM events and controlling native default actions. How-to: Events and callbacks.

items.title: When callbacks run
items.text:
The host delivers events as notifications. The SDK queues them on a reader thread and runs your scriptblocks on the runspace that pumps the queue, one at a time, in host order:

  • inside Wait-NativeHTMLKit (the normal case), and
  • inside any command that waits for a host reply (every document, window and desktop command). An event can therefore run in the middle of, for example, Submit-NativeHTMLKitForm or Get-NativeHTMLKitValue called from your script's top level.

While a callback runs, nested waits still answer replies and host decisions (close/quit policies), but further notifications and task completions are deferred until the callback returns (at most 128 deferred notifications; beyond that they are dropped and counted in Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnosticReport as DeferredDropped). Callbacks can nest at most 32 deep.

A callback that throws does not stop the app: the error is written to stderr as NativeHTMLKit: document_event callback failed: <type>: <message> (<script>:<line>), recorded as a callback.failed diagnostic and counted in CallbackFailures. break or continue outside a loop inside a callback stops only that callback.

Events are delivered after native dispatch: the native default action (typing, focus movement, checkbox toggling, form submission) has already happened when your scriptblock runs. To cancel a default action, register it beforehand with Set-NativeHTMLKitPreventDefault.

items.title: The event object
items.text:
The callback receives one argument, a PSCustomObject. Fields present for Core 1.0.3:

Field Present Meaning type always Event type, such as click, input, submit. element always Id of the nearest element with an id, starting at the target and walking up; empty string if none. path always Ids of the elements with ids along the event route, target first. node always Node reference of the actual target (use with Get-NativeHTMLKitNode -Reference). window_id, document_id always Added by the SDK. ctrl, shift, alt, meta always Modifier keys. cancelable, default_prevented cancelable events Whether the default action could be / was prevented. detail always Click count for mouse events. value target is a text control or <select> The control's current value (no extra request needed). checked checkbox/radio Current checked state. selection text control start, end, direction. key, code, repeat keyboard events DOM key name (a, Enter, Tab, Escape, F1, ArrowUp, ...), physical key code, auto-repeat. x, y, button, buttons pointer/mouse events Position in CSS pixels and buttons. delta_x, delta_y wheel Scroll amounts. data, input_type, is_composing input, beforeinput, composition Inserted text and input kind. submitter submit Id of the submit button, when it has one. old_state, new_state toggle (popover, <details>) Open state change. return_value close of a <dialog> The dialog's return value. validity invalid flags (valueMissing, typeMismatch, patternMismatch, tooShort, tooLong, rangeUnderflow, rangeOverflow, stepMismatch, badInput, customError), message, valid. files file input Selected file metadata.

Fields whose names start with _ are internal. Use $evt or $e as the parameter name: $event is a PowerShell automatic variable.

Typical event types: click, dblclick, auxclick, contextmenu, input, beforeinput, change, submit, reset, invalid, keydown, keyup, focus, blur, focusin, focusout, pointerdown/up/move/over/out/enter/leave/cancel, mousedown/up/move/..., wheel, scroll, compositionstart/update/end, dragstart/drag/dragenter/dragover/ dragleave/dragend/drop, toggle, close, cancel, select, selectionchange, copy, cut, paste, load, and error (see below).

items.title: Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent
items.text:
Alias: Register-NHKDocumentEvent

Subscribes a scriptblock to events of one type in a document. With -Element, the callback runs only when that id is the event's element or appears in its path, so one handler on a container (a list, a toolbar, a table) receives events from all its descendants: delegation. Without -Element, every event of that type in the document is delivered. At most 256 subscriptions per document; they are released when the document is retired.

Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent [-Document] <Object> [-Type] <string> [-Callback] <scriptblock> [[-Element] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Type string yes - Event type, for example click. -Callback scriptblock yes - Scriptblock; receives the event object as its single argument. -Element string no - Element id to filter on (target or ancestor).

Returns a NativeHTMLKit.Subscription (Type, Element, Document) for Unregister-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent. Use $null = Register-... to discard it.

# Delegation: one handler for every button in #toolbar.
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element toolbar -Callback {
    param($evt)
    switch ($evt.element) {
        'save'   { Save-Report }
        'export' { Export-Report }
    }
}

Variable lookup inside the scriptblock happens when it runs, not when it was registered. A scriptblock written at script level sees script variables ($doc, $app) and functions; a scriptblock created inside a function needs .GetNewClosure() to keep that function's locals. See closures and scope.

items.title: Document errors
items.text: The host reports document failures as document.error. The SDK writes the message to stderr and delivers it to handlers registered for type error as @{ type = 'error'; message; fatal }. When fatal is $true the host has already unloaded the document: it is retired, and an error handler may load a replacement.

items.title: Unregister-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent
items.text:
Alias: Unregister-NHKDocumentEvent

Removes a subscription.

Unregister-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent [-Subscription] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Subscription NativeHTMLKit.Subscription yes - The NativeHTMLKit.Subscription returned by Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitPreventDefault
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKPreventDefault

Registers, before input happens, that the native default action of an event on an element (and its descendants) is prevented (set_default_action). Because callbacks run after native dispatch, this is the only way to stop, for example, Tab moving focus out of an editor or Enter submitting a form. -Key and the modifier switches narrow the rule; a modifier you do not pass matches either state. -Prevent $false registers a rule that allows the default action again.

Set-NativeHTMLKitPreventDefault [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [-EventType] <string> [[-Prevent] <bool>] [[-Key] <string>] [[-Shift] <bool>] [[-Ctrl] <bool>] [[-Alt] <bool>] [[-Meta] <bool>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Element id; the rule applies to events whose route contains it. -EventType string yes - Event type, for example keydown or submit. Alias: -Event. -Prevent bool no $true $true prevents the default action; $false allows it. -Key string no - DOM key name to match, case-sensitive (Tab, Enter, s). -Shift bool no - Match only when Shift is ($true) or is not ($false) pressed. -Ctrl bool no - Match the Ctrl state. -Alt bool no - Match the Alt state. -Meta bool no - Match the Meta (Windows/Super) state. 
# Tab indents in the editor instead of moving focus; the keydown handler inserts spaces.
Set-NativeHTMLKitPreventDefault -Document $doc -Element editor -EventType keydown -Key Tab -Shift $false

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/events.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers
path: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers

items.title: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers
items.text:
How-to guides: Forms, HTML dialogs and popovers.

Form commands take the form by id (-Form) or as a node (-FormNode), and an optional submit button by id (-Submitter) or node (-SubmitterNode). Exactly one form target is required.
path: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitFormData
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKFormData

Returns the form's entries as the HTML form-submission algorithm builds them (get_form_data): in document order, with repeated names preserved, unchecked checkboxes and radio buttons omitted, a checked checkbox without value reported as on, and file inputs reported as metadata. The submitter's name/value is included when -Submitter is given.

Get-NativeHTMLKitFormData [-Document] <Object> [[-Form] <string>] [[-FormNode] <Object>] [[-Submitter] <string>] [[-SubmitterNode] <Object>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Form string no - Form element id. -FormNode NativeHTMLKit.Node no - Form as a NativeHTMLKit.Node. -Submitter string no - Id of the submit button to include. -SubmitterNode NativeHTMLKit.Node no - Submit button as a node.

Returns @{ entries = @(@{ name; value; kind }); submitter }. kind is text for ordinary fields; submitter is @{ element; node } when -Submitter/-SubmitterNode was given, else $null.

$values = @{}
foreach ($entry in (Get-NativeHTMLKitFormData -Document $doc -Form signup).entries) { $values[$entry.name] = $entry.value }
path: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers

items.title: Submit-NativeHTMLKitForm
items.text:
Alias: Submit-NHKForm

Requests submission exactly as a submit button would (request_submit): native constraint validation runs first (required, type=email, min/max, minlength, pattern, ...). If the form is invalid nothing is submitted and an invalid event is dispatched for each invalid control (with validity.flags such as valueMissing, validity.message and validity.valid); otherwise a submit event is dispatched to your handlers, with submitter set to the submit button's id. No navigation happens: NativeHTMLKit forms never load a URL.

Submit-NativeHTMLKitForm [-Document] <Object> [[-Form] <string>] [[-FormNode] <Object>] [[-Submitter] <string>] [[-SubmitterNode] <Object>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Form string no - Form element id. -FormNode NativeHTMLKit.Node no - Form as a node. -Submitter string no - Id of the button that "submits". -SubmitterNode NativeHTMLKit.Node no - Submit button as a node.

Returns @{ submitted; default_prevented }. submitted is $false when validation blocked the submission.
path: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers

items.title: Reset-NativeHTMLKitForm
items.text:
Alias: Reset-NHKForm

Resets every control of the form to its initial value (reset_form), like a reset button.

Reset-NativeHTMLKitForm [-Document] <Object> [[-Form] <string>] [[-FormNode] <Object>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Form string no - Form element id. -FormNode NativeHTMLKit.Node no - Form as a node.

Returns @{ reset; default_prevented }.
path: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitSelectOptions
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKSelectOptions

Returns a <select> element's options (get_options), each with value, label, selected and disabled. Returned as one array object (assign it and use the variable).

Get-NativeHTMLKitSelectOptions [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Id of the <select>.
path: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitSelectedValues
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKSelectedValues

Selects the options whose values are given and deselects the others (set_selected_values). For a single-selection <select> pass one value; an empty array clears a multiple selection. Does not dispatch events.

Set-NativeHTMLKitSelectedValues [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [-Values] <string[]> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Id of the <select>. -Values string[] yes - Option values to select. May be empty.
path: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers

items.title: Show-NativeHTMLKitHtmlDialog
items.text:
Alias: Show-NHKHtmlDialog

Opens an HTML <dialog> element (show_dialog), modal by default: a modal dialog enters the top layer, makes the rest of the document inert and focuses its first focusable element; Escape asks it to close (cancel, then close events). With -Close it closes the dialog with a return value (close_dialog); the dialog's close event carries it as return_value. As in HTML, the return value persists: showing the dialog again or closing it with Escape keeps the previous value, so decide in your button handlers rather than in the close event. This is an in-window HTML dialog, not a native operating-system dialog (for those see Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog).

Show-NativeHTMLKitHtmlDialog [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [[-Modal] <bool>] [[-ReturnValue] <string>] [-Close] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Id of the <dialog> element. -Close switch no off Close the dialog instead of opening it. -Modal bool no $true $false opens it non-modally (show() instead of showModal()). -ReturnValue string no '' With -Close: the return value.

Returns nothing. Inspect state with Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Operation get_dialog -Parameters @{ element = 'id' } (open, modal, return_value).

Show-NativeHTMLKitHtmlDialog -Document $doc -Element confirm
# ... in the OK button's click handler:
Show-NativeHTMLKitHtmlDialog -Document $doc -Element confirm -Close -ReturnValue 'ok'
path: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers

items.title: Show-NativeHTMLKitPopover
items.text:
Alias: Show-NHKPopover

Shows, hides or toggles an element with the popover attribute (show_popover, hide_popover, toggle_popover).

Show-NativeHTMLKitPopover [-Document] <Object> [-Element] <string> [[-Action] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string yes - Id of the popover element. -Action string no 'show' What to do. One of: show, hide, toggle.

Returns [bool] (new open state) for -Action toggle; nothing otherwise. Inspect state with the get_popover document command (open).

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/forms.md · edit the page there.
path: Reference: forms, select lists, HTML dialogs and popovers

items.title: Reference: application lifecycle
items.text:
Module NativeHTMLKit 0.1.2 (Core 1.0.3, wire protocol v1). Starting the host, connecting, signalling readiness, pumping events, quitting and closing. Task-oriented explanation: Script lifecycle guide.

All commands in this module are advanced functions: parameters bind by name or by position in the order shown in the syntax blocks, and common parameters (-Verbose, -ErrorAction, ...) are accepted. The module sets $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' internally, so every failure described below is a terminating error that try/catch can handle.

items.title: Typical order
items.text:
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'My tool'          # 1. host + backend connection
try {
    $window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app    # 2. at least one window
    $doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml -Window $window -Html '<p id="s">Ready</p>'
    # 3. register events, policies, notifications
    Set-NativeHTMLKitReady -Application $app               # 4. startup finished
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown    # 5. run callbacks until quit
} finally {
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app                  # 6. retire every handle
}

items.title: Start-NativeHTMLKitScript
items.text:
Alias: Start-NHKScript

Runs an ordinary .ps1 file as a NativeHTMLKit app and returns the connected NativeHTMLKit.Application. It has two roles, chosen from the process environment:

  • Launcher role (you ran the script with pwsh -File app.ps1 or powershell.exe -File app.ps1): writes a private temporary app.toml, starts the native host (run --app, plus --headless when NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1), and waits. The host runs the same script again with the same PowerShell edition (-NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File) and the same arguments, as its supervised backend. When the host exits, the launcher calls exit <host exit code>: code below this call never runs in the launcher process.
  • Backend role (UI4ME_ENDPOINT and UI4ME_TOKEN are set by the host): connects like Connect-NativeHTMLKit, removes the launch variables from the process environment so child processes cannot see them, and returns the application.

Everything above the call runs twice. Keep side effects (files, prompts, network calls) below it. On Linux the launcher starts the host through setpriv --pdeathsig TERM when available, so the host stops even if the launcher is killed. The temporary manifest folder is created with mode 0700 (Linux) or in the per-user %TEMP% (Windows) and removed afterwards; folders left by a killed launcher are removed after one day.

Start-NativeHTMLKitScript [[-Name] <string>] [[-AppId] <string>] [[-Version] <string>] [[-Icon] <string>] [[-Instance] <string>] [[-StartupTimeoutMilliseconds] <int>] [[-ShutdownTimeoutMilliseconds] <int>] [[-MaxWindows] <int>] [[-ArgumentList] <string[]>] [[-ScriptPath] <string>] [[-Diagnostics] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Name string no - Application name shown by the desktop (1-128 characters, no control characters). Default: the script file name without extension. -AppId string no - Reverse-DNS identity such as org.example.MyTool (letters, digits, _, -, dot-separated, at most 128). Default: local.nativehtmlkit.<name-slug>.h<12 hex digits of the script path hash>, stable per script path. -Version string no - Application version string (1-128 characters). -Icon string no - Path of an application icon file; must exist. -Instance string no 'single' single forwards a second launch of the same AppId to the running app; multiple allows several instances. One of: single, multiple. -StartupTimeoutMilliseconds int no 30000 Host limit for the backend to connect and call Set-NativeHTMLKitReady. Range 1000 to 300000. -ShutdownTimeoutMilliseconds int no 5000 Host limit for the backend to exit after shutdown. Range 100 to 120000. -MaxWindows int no 16 Maximum number of windows the host allows for this app. Range 1 to 64. -ArgumentList string[] no - Arguments for the backend run. Default: the arguments that followed the script on the pwsh/powershell.exe command line. -ScriptPath string no - Script to run as the backend. Default: the calling script ($MyInvocation.PSCommandPath). Required when called outside a script file. -Diagnostics string no 'Normal' Sets NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS for the host and backend when not Normal (Off, Debug, Trace). See diagnostics. One of: Off, Normal, Debug, Trace.

Returns NativeHTMLKit.Application (backend role only).

Errors

  • Invalid -Name, -Version or -AppId: Name must be 1-128 characters..., AppId must be a dot-separated ASCII identity....
  • Called from the console instead of a file: Start-NativeHTMLKitScript must be called from a .ps1 script file.
  • Only one of UI4ME_ENDPOINT/UI4ME_TOKEN set, or a backend started by a launcher without a connection: refuses to start a second host.
  • Host binary missing or failing its integrity check: see Get-NativeHTMLKitHostPath.
  • Connection failure in the backend role: as for Connect-NativeHTMLKit.
param([string]$Folder)                       # parameters are forwarded to the backend run
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Folder report' -AppId 'org.example.FolderReport' -Instance multiple

items.title: Connect-NativeHTMLKit
items.text:
Alias: Connect-NHK

Connects a backend that a manifest-based launch started (Start-NativeHTMLKitHost, or nativehtmlkit-host run --app app.toml). It reads the endpoint and token, clears the four UI4ME_* launch variables from the process environment before anything can fail, opens the Unix socket or Windows named pipe and authenticates with host.hello (protocol version 1). Most scripts use Start-NativeHTMLKitScript, which calls this in its backend role.

Connect-NativeHTMLKit [[-Endpoint] <string>] [[-Token] <string>] [[-ConnectTimeoutMilliseconds] <int>] [-SkipTokenValidation] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Endpoint string no $env:UI4ME_ENDPOINT Socket path or pipe name. Default: $env:UI4ME_ENDPOINT. -Token string no $env:UI4ME_TOKEN Launch token (64 hexadecimal digits). Default: $env:UI4ME_TOKEN. -ConnectTimeoutMilliseconds int no 15000 How long to wait for the endpoint. Range 1 to 120000. -SkipTokenValidation switch no off For test peers only: accept a token that is not 64 hexadecimal digits.

Returns NativeHTMLKit.Application. Its Hello property holds the host's host.hello result.

Errors missing endpoint/token (message explains to use Start-NativeHTMLKitScript); System.ArgumentException for a malformed token; NativeHTMLKit.DisconnectedException (Cannot connect to the native host endpoint (...)) when the endpoint does not answer; NativeHTMLKit.RpcException when authentication fails; Unsupported NativeHTMLKit Core protocol version.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitReady
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKReady

Tells the host that startup finished (app.ready). Call it once, after creating at least one window and registering the event handlers the first frame needs. Repeated calls do nothing. Until ready, the host treats closing the last window as cancelling startup, and closes extra windows without asking their close policy.

Set-NativeHTMLKitReady [-Application] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application.

Returns nothing. Errors NativeHTMLKit.RpcException from the host (for example when no window exists).

items.title: Wait-NativeHTMLKit
items.text:
Alias: Wait-NHK

Pumps host messages on the calling runspace: every document event, notification, close/quit decision and background-task completion callback runs inside this call (or inside any other command that waits for a host reply). Two parameter sets:

  • Run (-UntilShutdown): pumps until the host requests shutdown or Close-NativeHTMLKit is called (for example from a callback). Returns no output. Throws NativeHTMLKit.DisconnectedException if the host disappears first.
  • Pump (default): waits up to -TimeoutMilliseconds for the first message, then handles up to 64 queued messages without waiting, and returns how many it handled (0 on timeout or after close). -Once handles at most one message. Use this for your own loop with periodic work.
Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application <Object> [-TimeoutMilliseconds <int>] [-Once] [<CommonParameters>]
Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application <Object> [-UntilShutdown] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application. -TimeoutMilliseconds int no 100 How long to wait for the first message; -1 waits indefinitely. Range -1 to 2147483647. Parameter set: Pump. -Once switch no off Handle at most one message. Parameter set: Pump. -UntilShutdown switch no off Pump until shutdown or close. Parameter set: Run.

Returns [int] (Pump set) or nothing (Run set).

# A custom loop: do periodic work between pumps (prefer a background task for real work).
while (-not $done) {
    $handled = Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -TimeoutMilliseconds 250
    if ($handled -eq 0) { Update-Clock }
}

items.title: Request-NativeHTMLKitQuit
items.text:
Alias: Request-NHKQuit

Asks the host for an orderly quit (app.request_quit). The host asks the Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeQuit policy (if any); when allowed it sends app.shutdown, which makes Wait-NativeHTMLKit -UntilShutdown return. Use it for a Quit button or menu item.

Request-NativeHTMLKitQuit [-Application] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application.

Returns the host result, @{ requested = $true } when the request was accepted. The quit itself happens later, while events are pumped.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeQuit
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKBeforeQuit

Sets the application's quit policy. The host asks it (request app.before_quit) when a quit is requested, for example by Request-NativeHTMLKitQuit (reason = 'backend_request'). The scriptblock receives the host parameters (with a reason property); its last output value decides: truthy allows the quit, $false or no output vetoes it. A throwing policy is reported as a callback failure and the host receives an error reply. Pass $null to remove the policy.

Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeQuit [-Application] <Object> [-Callback] <scriptblock> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application. -Callback scriptblock yes - Policy scriptblock, or $null to remove it. Accepts $null. 
Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeQuit -Application $app -Callback {
    param($request)
    if ($script:unsaved) { Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text 'Save first.'; $false; return }
    $true
}

items.title: Register-NativeHTMLKitNotification
items.text:
Alias: Register-NHKNotification

Runs a scriptblock for every host notification with the given method, for example window.event (window state changes, including type = 'closed') or desktop.preferences_changed. One callback per method; registering again replaces it; $null removes it. The SDK's own bookkeeping (closing window handles, retiring documents, dispatching document events) always runs before your callback. The callback receives the notification's params object.

Register-NativeHTMLKitNotification [-Application] <Object> [-Method] <string> [-Callback] <scriptblock> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application. -Method string yes - Notification method name, for example window.event. -Callback scriptblock yes - Scriptblock receiving the notification parameters, or $null to remove it. Accepts $null.

window.event parameters observed with Core 1.0.3: window_id, type (for example closed, close_requested, focused, resized, moved, dropped_files, theme_changed) and data.

Register-NativeHTMLKitNotification -Application $app -Method 'window.event' -Callback {
    param($params)
    if ($params.type -eq 'closed') { Write-Verbose "window $($params.window_id) closed" }
}

items.title: Close-NativeHTMLKit
items.text:
Alias: Close-NHK

Closes the application connection and retires every window, document, node and bitmap handle (later use throws NativeHTMLKit.StaleObjectException). It removes all callbacks, requests cancellation of unfinished background tasks without waiting for them, and is idempotent; $null is accepted, so it is safe in a finally block even when startup failed. In a backend started by Start-NativeHTMLKitScript before shutdown, the connection is left for process exit to close, so an error that is unwinding through finally is still reported by PowerShell before the host stops the process. Calling it inside a callback ends Wait-NativeHTMLKit -UntilShutdown normally.

Close-NativeHTMLKit [-Application] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application, or $null. Accepts $null.

items.title: Start-NativeHTMLKitHost
items.text:
Alias: Start-NHKHost

Runs an app manifest (app.toml) through the native host and waits for it to exit (throws NativeHTMLKit host exited with code N on a nonzero exit). With -NoWait it starts the host and returns its System.Diagnostics.Process. The manifest's backend must call Connect-NativeHTMLKit or Start-NativeHTMLKitScript (which only connects in that case). New-NativeHTMLKitProject writes a suitable app.toml.

Start-NativeHTMLKitHost [-Manifest] <string> [-NoWait] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Manifest string yes - Path of the app.toml manifest; must exist. -NoWait switch no off Start the host and return its process object instead of waiting.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitHostPath
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKHostPath

Returns the full path of the native host this module will run: NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY (or the legacy UI4ME_HOST_BINARY) when set, otherwise the bundled runtimes/linux-x64/nativehtmlkit-host or runtimes/win-x64/nativehtmlkit-host.exe. A bundled host is checked against the SHA-256 in HOST-MANIFEST.json on every call (fail closed), and on Linux made executable if a package extraction dropped the execute bit.

Get-NativeHTMLKitHostPath [<CommonParameters>]

No parameters (common parameters only).

Errors NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY does not exist: <path>; NativeHTMLKit ships x64 hosts only; NativeHTMLKit supports Linux and Windows only; The native NativeHTMLKit host is missing (a source checkout without hosts: set NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY); a missing or mismatching HOST-MANIFEST.json.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
Variable Used by Effect NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY Get-NativeHTMLKitHostPath, launcher Use this host binary instead of the bundled one. NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 Start-NativeHTMLKitScript Start the host with --headless: the full protocol runs without windows on screen. No native input, clipboard, file dialogs, external open or attention requests. NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS SDK, host, backend off, normal (default), debug or trace. NATIVEHTMLKIT_VERBOSE launcher Any value other than empty, 0, false, no relays the host's informational records to stderr. NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID SDK, host Correlation ID shared by launcher, host and backend; generated when absent. UI4ME_ENDPOINT, UI4ME_TOKEN, UI4ME_APP_ID, UI4ME_PROTOCOL_VERSION backend Set by the host for its backend (wire v1 names). Removed from the environment on connect.

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/lifecycle.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Reference: nodes (elements without ids)
items.text:
Id-based commands cover most apps. Node references address elements that have no id, for example the rows of a generated table, the target of an event ($evt.node) or the results of a selector query. A node reference is a string such as node:1:18:1, bound to one document generation: after the element is removed or replaced, the old reference no longer resolves (NativeHTMLKit.RpcException code -32004, Stale node reference: ...), and every node of a retired document throws NativeHTMLKit.StaleObjectException in the SDK.

A NativeHTMLKit.Node has read-only properties Id (the reference string) and Document. Commands that accept -Node (Get-NativeHTMLKitComputedStyle, Set-NativeHTMLKitFocus, the selection and edit commands, form commands via -FormNode) refuse a node of another document. Raw reference strings (for example in $evt.node or Get-NativeHTMLKitNodes results) can be passed to Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand as node = '<ref>', or wrapped with Get-NativeHTMLKitNode -Reference.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitNode
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKNode

Resolves an element id to a node (node_of), returns the document root's node when neither parameter is given, or wraps an existing reference string without a host round trip.

Get-NativeHTMLKitNode [-Document] <Object> [[-Element] <string>] [[-Reference] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Element string no - Element id to resolve. Use -Element or -Reference, not both. -Reference string no - An existing node reference string, for example $evt.node.

Returns NativeHTMLKit.Node.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitNodes
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKNodes

Runs a CSS selector query and returns node references for matches, including elements without ids (query_nodes).

Get-NativeHTMLKitNodes [-Document] <Object> [-Selector] <string> [[-Offset] <int>] [[-Limit] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Selector string yes - CSS selector. -Offset int no 0 Index of the first match to return. Range 0 to 2147483647. -Limit int no 1024 Maximum number of matches to return. Range 1 to 4096.

Returns @{ nodes = @(@{ node; element }); total; offset } where element is the match's id or $null.

$third = (Get-NativeHTMLKitNodes -Document $doc -Selector '#log li' -Offset 2 -Limit 1).nodes[0].node
$html = (Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Document $doc -Operation get_html -Parameters @{ node = $third }).html

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitNodeInfo
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKNodeInfo

Describes a node (get_node).

Get-NativeHTMLKitNodeInfo [-Node] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Node NativeHTMLKit.Node yes - The node.

Returns @{ node; type; child_count; parent; ... }. For an element also name (tag name), id, attributes and the previous/next sibling references, for example type = 'element', name = 'ul', attributes = @{ id = 'list' }. The root node has type = 'document'.

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitNodeChildren
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKNodeChildren

Lists a node's children (node_children), paginated.

Get-NativeHTMLKitNodeChildren [-Node] <Object> [[-Offset] <int>] [[-Limit] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Node NativeHTMLKit.Node yes - The node. -Offset int no 0 Index of the first child. Range 0 to 2147483647. -Limit int no 256 Maximum number of children. Range 1 to 4096.

Returns @{ children = @(@{ node; type; name; id }); total }.

items.title: Invoke-NativeHTMLKitNodeOperation
items.text:
Alias: Invoke-NHKNodeOperation

Applies one node-addressed operation (sent as a one-element node_batch). Operations and their extra parameters: set_text/append_text (text), set_attribute (name, value), remove_attribute/add_class/remove_class (name), insert_html (position, html), replace_children_html (html), trim_children (keep, optional from), move_element (target_node, position), remove_element. A NativeHTMLKit.Node given as a parameter value (for example target_node) is converted to its reference; nodes of another document are refused.

Invoke-NativeHTMLKitNodeOperation [-Node] <Object> [-Operation] <string> [[-Parameters] <IDictionary>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Node NativeHTMLKit.Node yes - The node to operate on. -Operation string yes - Operation name. -Parameters System.Collections.IDictionary no @{} Operation fields; op and node are reserved. 
$list = Get-NativeHTMLKitNode -Document $doc -Element log
Invoke-NativeHTMLKitNodeOperation -Node $list -Operation trim_children -Parameters @{ keep = 200 }

items.title: Invoke-NativeHTMLKitNodeBatch
items.text:
Alias: Invoke-NHKNodeBatch

Applies several node-addressed operations as one atomic transaction (node_batch). Each operation is a hashtable with op, node (a reference string) and the fields listed for Invoke-NativeHTMLKitNodeOperation.

Invoke-NativeHTMLKitNodeBatch [-Document] <Object> [-Operations] <Object[]> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Document NativeHTMLKit.Document yes - The document. -Operations object[] yes - Array of operation hashtables. 
$rows = (Get-NativeHTMLKitNodes -Document $doc -Selector '#rows tr').nodes
Invoke-NativeHTMLKitNodeBatch -Document $doc -Operations @($rows | ForEach-Object { @{ op = 'add_class'; node = $_.node; name = 'stale' } })

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/nodes.md · edit the page there.
