items.title: Reference: objects, errors, threading and limits
items.text: Applies to NativeHTMLKit 0.1.2 with Core 1.0.3 (wire protocol v1).
path: Reference: objects, errors, threading and limits

items.title: Handle objects
items.text:
The SDK returns PSCustomObject handles whose first type name identifies them ($x.PSObject.TypeNames[0]). Use the documented read-only properties; other properties are SDK internals and may change.

Type name Returned by Documented properties Becomes stale when NativeHTMLKit.Application Start-NativeHTMLKitScript, Connect-NativeHTMLKit Hello (host.hello result) Close-NativeHTMLKit; the host disconnects (DisconnectedException) NativeHTMLKit.Window New-NativeHTMLKitWindow Id, Closed, Application, Document the window closes, app.shutdown, application close NativeHTMLKit.Document Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml, Open-NativeHTMLKitFile Id, Window, Retired another document is loaded into the window, Remove-NativeHTMLKitDocument, a fatal document.error, window close NativeHTMLKit.Node Get-NativeHTMLKitNode Id (reference string), Document its document is retired (SDK); the element is removed or replaced (host, code -32004) NativeHTMLKit.Subscription Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent Type, Element, Document its document is retired NativeHTMLKit.LiveBitmap New-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap Id, Width, Height, Stride, SlotBytes, Slots, Sequence, Closed, Document Remove-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap, its document is retired NativeHTMLKit.Request Start-NativeHTMLKitRpc, Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog -NoWait Id, Method, Completed, Cancelled, Failed awaited once, or stopped NativeHTMLKit.Task Start-NativeHTMLKitTask Id - (inspect with Receive-NativeHTMLKitTask)

Results of host queries (Get-NativeHTMLKitWindow, Get-NativeHTMLKitCapabilities, document commands, ...) are plain PSCustomObjects parsed from the host's JSON: field names are the protocol's snake_case names, JSON arrays become object[], numbers become [long] or [double].

One-array results. Get-NativeHTMLKitWindowList, Get-NativeHTMLKitStylesheets and Get-NativeHTMLKitSelectOptions return their list as one array object (return ,@(...)). Assign the result to a variable and use it; @(Get-NativeHTMLKitWindowList ...) or piping produces a single element that contains the whole array.
path: Reference: objects, errors, threading and limits

items.title: Exceptions
items.text:
All failures are terminating errors. The SDK's own exception types live in the NativeHTMLKit namespace and are available after the first connection (Start-NativeHTMLKitScript loads them), so catch [NativeHTMLKit.RpcException] { } works in scripts.

Exception Base type Thrown when NativeHTMLKit.RpcException System.Exception The host answered a request with an error. Properties: Method, Code, RpcMessage, RpcData. NativeHTMLKit.StaleObjectException InvalidOperationException A window, document, node, bitmap or request handle is no longer current. NativeHTMLKit.DisconnectedException System.IO.IOException The connection is closed or the host went away; a waiting request's outcome is unknown. NativeHTMLKit.RpcTimeoutException TimeoutException A request wait expired (cancellation was requested; the host may still complete it). NativeHTMLKit.BusyException InvalidOperationException 128 requests are outstanding; await or stop earlier ones. NativeHTMLKit.ProtocolException System.Exception The peer sent a malformed or unexpected message; fatal to the connection. System.TimeoutException Receive-NativeHTMLKitTask -Wait -TimeoutMilliseconds expired; a task deadline (-OnFailed). System.OperationCanceledException A stopped task (-OnFailed). System.Management.Automation.RuntimeException Parameter misuse detected by the SDK, for example Expected a NativeHTMLKit.Window from New-NativeHTMLKitWindow, Use -Element or -Node, not both.
path: Reference: objects, errors, threading and limits

items.title: Host error codes (RpcException.Code)
items.text: Code Name Typical cause -32601 method not found Unknown method in Invoke-NativeHTMLKitRpc. -32602 invalid params Unknown element id (Unknown element ID: x), invalid value (color_scheme must be light, dark or system). -32603 internal error Host-side failure. -32001 unsupported The service is not available in this session (headless: clipboard, file dialogs, external open, attention). -32002 unavailable A resource or service is temporarily unavailable. -32003 denied Refused by host policy (for example an executable as open target). -32004 closed The window, document, bitmap or node no longer exists (Stale node reference). -32005 busy A limit was reached, for example a second native dialog on one window. -32006 cancelled The request was cancelled. -32008 invalid state Not allowed in the current lifecycle phase, for example Set-NativeHTMLKitReady without a window. -32009 timeout A host-side deadline expired.
path: Reference: objects, errors, threading and limits

items.title: Threading and runspaces
items.text:
• Every SDK object belongs to the runspace that created the application. Use it only from that runspace: your script and the callbacks the SDK runs for it.
  • A .NET reader thread receives frames; it never runs PowerShell code.
  • Callbacks (document events, notifications, close/quit policies, task completions) run one at a time on the owning runspace while it pumps: inside Wait-NativeHTMLKit or inside any command that waits for a host reply. See events.
  • Background work runs in separate runspaces through Start-NativeHTMLKitTask and communicates by plain data and completion callbacks. Do not use Start-Job, Start-ThreadJob, ForEach-Object -Parallel or your own runspaces to call SDK commands.
path: Reference: objects, errors, threading and limits

items.title: Limits
items.text:
Limit Value Message frame 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes) of JSON per request or reply Outstanding requests per application 128 Deferred notifications while a callback runs 128 (more are dropped and counted) Callback nesting depth 32 Subscriptions per document 256 Background tasks 8 unfinished per application, 32 per process Windows Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -MaxWindows (1-64, default 16) Live bitmap size 1-4096 x 1-4096 pixels, 2 or 3 slots Resource bundle 256 entries, 1 MiB decoded per registration SDK diagnostic history 2048 records Default request timeout 15 s; document loads 30 s; external open 60 s; dialogs unlimited

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/objects-and-errors.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Reference: raw host requests
items.text:
Low-level access to the Core wire protocol v1 for methods without a dedicated cmdlet. Normal applications do not need these commands. The method list and parameter schemas are in the Core protocol contract. Do not send host.hello or lifecycle replies yourself; the SDK owns them.

A NativeHTMLKit.Request has read-only properties Id (ps-<n>), Method, Completed, Cancelled and Failed. At most 128 requests may be outstanding per application; more fail with NativeHTMLKit.BusyException.

items.title: Invoke-NativeHTMLKitRpc
items.text:
Alias: Invoke-NHKRpc

Sends a request and waits for its result, pumping events meanwhile.

Invoke-NativeHTMLKitRpc [-Application] <Object> [-Method] <string> [[-Parameters] <IDictionary>] [[-TimeoutMilliseconds] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application. -Method string yes - Host method, for example host.capabilities or desktop.paths. -Parameters System.Collections.IDictionary no @{} Request parameters. -TimeoutMilliseconds int no 15000 How long to wait; -1 waits indefinitely. When not given, dialog.* methods wait indefinitely. Range -1 to 2147483647.

Returns the host's result object. Errors NativeHTMLKit.RpcException (properties Method, Code, RpcMessage, RpcData) when the host answers with an error; NativeHTMLKit.RpcTimeoutException after the timeout (cancellation is requested; the outcome is unknown); NativeHTMLKit.DisconnectedException when the connection is lost or closed meanwhile.

$paths = Invoke-NativeHTMLKitRpc -Application $app -Method 'desktop.paths'

items.title: Start-NativeHTMLKitRpc
items.text:
Alias: Start-NHKRpc

Sends a request without waiting and returns a NativeHTMLKit.Request.

Start-NativeHTMLKitRpc [-Application] <Object> [-Method] <string> [[-Parameters] <IDictionary>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application. -Method string yes - Host method. -Parameters System.Collections.IDictionary no @{} Request parameters.

items.title: Wait-NativeHTMLKitRpc
items.text:
Alias: Wait-NHKRpc

Waits for a request started with Start-NativeHTMLKitRpc (or Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog -NoWait), pumping events. Each request can be awaited once. Errors as for Invoke-NativeHTMLKitRpc; a cancelled request throws NativeHTMLKit.StaleObjectException.

Wait-NativeHTMLKitRpc [-Request] <Object> [[-TimeoutMilliseconds] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Request NativeHTMLKit.Request yes - The request. -TimeoutMilliseconds int no 15000 How long to wait; -1 waits indefinitely. Range -1 to 2147483647.

items.title: Stop-NativeHTMLKitRpc
items.text:
Alias: Stop-NHKRpc

Requests cancellation of an outstanding request (request.cancel), for example to close a native dialog. It is not a rollback: the host may already have acted. Does nothing for a completed or cancelled request.

Stop-NativeHTMLKitRpc [-Request] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Request NativeHTMLKit.Request yes - The request.

items.title: Send-NativeHTMLKitNotification
items.text:
Alias: Send-NHKNotification

Sends a JSON-RPC notification (no reply) to the host.

Send-NativeHTMLKitNotification [-Application] <Object> [-Method] <string> [[-Parameters] <IDictionary>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application. -Method string yes - Notification method. -Parameters System.Collections.IDictionary no @{} Notification parameters.

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/rpc.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Reference: background tasks
items.text: Run slow PowerShell work (file scans, hashing, web requests, Get-WinEvent queries) without freezing the window. How-to: Background tasks.

items.title: Rules
items.text:
• The -ScriptBlock runs in a new, isolated runspace: none of the caller's variables, functions or imported modules exist there (import what it needs inside the block). Its text is re-parsed in that runspace, so a closure's captured variables do not travel either.
  • Pass inputs with -ArgumentList as plain data. NativeHTMLKit objects (application, window, document, node, bitmap, request, task, subscription) are refused anywhere inside the arguments (checked 8 levels deep) because they belong to the owning runspace.
  • The task's output becomes the result. -OnCompleted and -OnFailed run later on the owning runspace, while it pumps events (Wait-NativeHTMLKit or any waiting command), never inside another callback, and never after Close-NativeHTMLKit. Update the UI there.
  • At most 8 unfinished tasks per application and 32 per process. A worker whose cancellation was requested still occupies its slot until its thread really ends.
  • -TimeoutMilliseconds and Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask only request cancellation (PowerShell BeginStop). Interruptible commands such as Start-Sleep stop; a worker blocked in .NET or native code may keep running. Its eventual result is discarded.

items.title: Start-NativeHTMLKitTask
items.text:
Alias: Start-NHKTask

Starts the scriptblock in an isolated runspace and returns a task handle.

Start-NativeHTMLKitTask [-Application] <Object> [-ScriptBlock] <scriptblock> [[-ArgumentList] <Object[]>] [[-OnCompleted] <scriptblock>] [[-OnFailed] <scriptblock>] [[-TimeoutMilliseconds] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application that owns the task and runs its callbacks. -ScriptBlock scriptblock yes - Work to run. Receives the -ArgumentList values as positional arguments. -ArgumentList object[] no @() Plain-data arguments. Pass one array argument as @(, $array). -OnCompleted scriptblock no - Runs on the owning runspace after success; receives the task output as one array (param($result); $result[0] is the first output object). -OnFailed scriptblock no - Runs on the owning runspace after a terminating error, a timeout (System.TimeoutException) or a stop (System.OperationCanceledException); receives the exception. Without it, a failure is written as a warning. -TimeoutMilliseconds int no 0 Deadline after which cancellation is requested and the task fails with TimeoutException; 0 means no deadline. Range 0 to 3600000.

Returns NativeHTMLKit.Task (property Id; use the cmdlets below to inspect it). Errors a refused argument (A NativeHTMLKit.Window belongs to the owning runspace...); the task limit (NativeHTMLKit background task limit (8 per application) reached...).

Non-terminating errors written by the worker (Write-Error) do not fail the task; they are available as Errors from Receive-NativeHTMLKitTask. Exceptions thrown by -OnCompleted or -OnFailed are isolated like event callbacks (stderr message, CallbackFailures counter).

$null = Start-NativeHTMLKitTask -Application $app -ArgumentList @($computer) -TimeoutMilliseconds 30000 -ScriptBlock {
    param([string]$Name)
    Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Service -ComputerName $Name | Select-Object Name, State, StartMode
} -OnCompleted {
    param($services)
    Show-Services $services          # runs on the UI runspace
} -OnFailed {
    param($failure)
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text ('Query failed: ' + $failure.Message)
}

items.title: Receive-NativeHTMLKitTask
items.text:
Alias: Receive-NHKTask

Reports a task's state and, with -Wait, pumps host messages until it completes. Calling it also delivers any due completion callbacks (when not called from inside a callback).

Receive-NativeHTMLKitTask [-Task] <Object> [[-TimeoutMilliseconds] <int>] [-Wait] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Task NativeHTMLKit.Task yes - The task. -Wait switch no off Wait (pumping events) until the task completes. -TimeoutMilliseconds int no -1 With -Wait: give up after this time with System.TimeoutException (the task is not cancelled); -1 waits indefinitely. Range -1 to 2147483647.

Returns @{ Id; Completed; Result; Failure; Errors; CancellationPending }. CancellationPending is $true while a stopped or timed-out worker is still running.

items.title: Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask
items.text:
Alias: Stop-NHKTask

Requests cancellation. The task is marked completed with an OperationCanceledException, which -OnFailed receives; does nothing for a completed task.

Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask [-Task] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Task NativeHTMLKit.Task yes - The task.

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/tasks.md · edit the page there.

items.title: New-NativeHTMLKitProject
items.text:
Alias: New-NHKProject

Generates a runnable app folder: app.ps1 (UTF-8 with BOM, so Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads it correctly), index.html, style.css and an optional app.toml manifest. Refuses to overwrite any of these files without -Force. Run the app with pwsh -File ./app.ps1 (or powershell.exe -File .\app.ps1); app.toml is for launchers that start the host explicitly with Start-NativeHTMLKitHost and names pwsh, or powershell.exe with -WindowsPowerShell.

New-NativeHTMLKitProject [-Path] <string> [[-Name] <string>] [[-AppId] <string>] [-WindowsPowerShell] [-Force] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Path string yes - Destination folder; created when missing. Must not be a file. -Name string no 'NativeHTMLKit PowerShell App' App name (1-128 characters, no quotes, backslashes or control characters). -AppId string no 'org.example.PowerShellApp' Reverse-DNS identity written to app.ps1 and app.toml. -WindowsPowerShell switch no off Make app.toml start powershell.exe instead of pwsh. Alias: -WindowsPowerShell51. -Force switch no off Overwrite existing generated files.

Returns the folder's System.IO.DirectoryInfo.

New-NativeHTMLKitProject -Path ./InventoryTool -Name 'Inventory tool' -AppId 'org.example.InventoryTool'
pwsh -File ./InventoryTool/app.ps1
path: Reference: project scaffolding and agent skills

items.title: Install-NativeHTMLKitSkill
items.text:
Alias: Install-NHKSkill

Installs, inspects or removes the nativehtmlkit-powershell coding-agent skill (bundled in the module under skills/) for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, Cursor and Gemini CLI. User scope writes below your home folder; project scope below -ProjectPath:

Agent User scope Project scope claude ~/.claude/skills .claude/skills codex ~/.agents/skills .agents/skills opencode ~/.config/opencode/skills .opencode/skills copilot ~/.copilot/skills .github/skills cursor ~/.cursor/skills .cursor/skills gemini ~/.gemini/skills .gemini/skills

An installed folder carries a .nativehtmlkit-managed.json record of its file hashes. Folders not installed by this command (unmanaged) or edited since (modified) are never replaced or removed without -Force; links and junctions in the destination path are refused.

Install-NativeHTMLKitSkill [[-Action] <string>] [[-Agents] <string[]>] [[-Scope] <string>] [[-ProjectPath] <string>] [-Force] [-DryRun] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Action string no 'install' install, status or uninstall. One of: install, status, uninstall. -Agents string[] no @('all') Agent names (also comma-separated) or all. -Scope string no 'user' user or project. One of: user, project. -ProjectPath string no - Existing project folder; required with -Scope project, not allowed with user. -Force switch no off Replace or remove unmanaged or modified skill folders. -DryRun switch no off Report what would happen without changing anything.

Returns one object per agent: Agent, Scope, State (missing, installed, modified, unmanaged), Path, Action (installed, removed, none, status, would-<action>).

Install-NativeHTMLKitSkill -Action status -Agents claude,codex -Scope project -ProjectPath .

items.title: Reference: windows
items.text:
Creating, changing, listing and closing native windows, and the close policy. How-to: Multiple windows.

A NativeHTMLKit.Window has read-only properties Id (host window id such as w1), Closed, Application and Document (the current NativeHTMLKit.Document or $null). After the window closes (user close, Close-NativeHTMLKitWindow, shutdown or Close-NativeHTMLKit) Closed is $true and every command that takes the window throws NativeHTMLKit.StaleObjectException.

items.title: New-NativeHTMLKitWindow
items.text:
Alias: New-NHKWindow

Creates a native window (window.create). It is empty until you load a document with Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml or Open-NativeHTMLKitFile. The number of windows is limited by Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -MaxWindows (default 16).

New-NativeHTMLKitWindow [-Application] <Object> [[-Title] <string>] [[-Width] <int>] [[-Height] <int>] [[-Visible] <bool>] [[-Resizable] <bool>] [[-Decorations] <bool>] [[-MinWidth] <int>] [[-MinHeight] <int>] [[-MaxWidth] <int>] [[-MaxHeight] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application. -Title string no '' Window title. -Width int no 900 Initial width in logical pixels. Range 1 to 8192. -Height int no 600 Initial height in logical pixels. Range 1 to 8192. -Visible bool no $true Show the window when created. -Resizable bool no $true Allow the user to resize the window. -Decorations bool no $true Show the title bar and frame. -MinWidth int no - Minimum width; sent only when given. Range 1 to 8192. -MinHeight int no - Minimum height; sent only when given. Range 1 to 8192. -MaxWidth int no - Maximum width; sent only when given. Range 1 to 8192. -MaxHeight int no - Maximum height; sent only when given. Range 1 to 8192.

Returns NativeHTMLKit.Window.

$window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app -Title 'Inventory' -Width 1000 -Height 700 -MinWidth 640 -MinHeight 400

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitWindow
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKWindow

Changes window state (window.set): only the parameters you pass are sent. -Properties passes host field names directly (title, width, height, visible, resizable, decorations, minimized, maximized, fullscreen, focus, x, y, min_width, min_height, max_width, max_height); typed parameters override the same field. Size constraints are set in pairs; pass $null values in -Properties, for example @{ min_width = $null; min_height = $null }, to clear them. Window positioning (-X/-Y) is honoured only where the platform allows it (reported by window_positioning in Get-NativeHTMLKitCapabilities; Wayland does not let applications position windows).

Set-NativeHTMLKitWindow [-Window] <Object> [[-Properties] <IDictionary>] [[-Title] <string>] [[-Width] <int>] [[-Height] <int>] [[-Visible] <bool>] [[-Resizable] <bool>] [[-Decorations] <bool>] [[-Minimized] <bool>] [[-Maximized] <bool>] [[-Fullscreen] <bool>] [[-Focus] <bool>] [[-X] <int>] [[-Y] <int>] [[-MinWidth] <int>] [[-MinHeight] <int>] [[-MaxWidth] <int>] [[-MaxHeight] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Window NativeHTMLKit.Window yes - The window. -Properties System.Collections.IDictionary no @{} Hashtable of host field names and values. -Title string no - New title. -Width int no - New width. Range 1 to 8192. -Height int no - New height. Range 1 to 8192. -Visible bool no - Show or hide. -Resizable bool no - Allow resizing. -Decorations bool no - Show or hide the frame. -Minimized bool no - Minimize or restore. -Maximized bool no - Maximize or restore. -Fullscreen bool no - Enter or leave full screen. -Focus bool no - $true asks the desktop to focus the window. -X int no - Horizontal position. -Y int no - Vertical position. -MinWidth int no - Minimum width. Range 1 to 8192. -MinHeight int no - Minimum height. Range 1 to 8192. -MaxWidth int no - Maximum width. Range 1 to 8192. -MaxHeight int no - Maximum height. Range 1 to 8192.

Returns the host's window description (same shape as Get-NativeHTMLKitWindow).

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitWindow
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKWindow

Returns the host's description of the window (window.get).

Get-NativeHTMLKitWindow [-Window] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Window NativeHTMLKit.Window yes - The window.

Returns an object with, for Core 1.0.3: window_id, title, width, height, visible, closing, native (false in headless mode), scale_factor, physical_size, requested (decorations, resizable, visible, size_constraints) and observed (what the desktop reported: focused, minimized, maximized, fullscreen, position, theme, ...; null means not observed).

items.title: Get-NativeHTMLKitWindowList
items.text:
Alias: Get-NHKWindowList

Lists the application's open windows (window.list), each with the same shape as Get-NativeHTMLKitWindow.

The list is returned as one array object: assign it and use the variable ($list = Get-NativeHTMLKitWindowList -Application $app; $list.Count). Wrapping the call in @() or piping it yields a single item that contains the array.

Get-NativeHTMLKitWindowList [-Application] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Application NativeHTMLKit.Application yes - The application.

items.title: Close-NativeHTMLKitWindow
items.text:
Alias: Close-NHKWindow

Requests a graceful close (window.request_close, reason backend_request). After Set-NativeHTMLKitReady, the host first asks the window's Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeClose policy, which can veto; without a policy the window closes. The close completes while events are pumped: the handle's Closed becomes $true when the host reports window.event closed. Before ready, closing one of several windows closes it without asking the policy, and closing the last window cancels startup (the app shuts down).

Close-NativeHTMLKitWindow [-Window] <Object> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Window NativeHTMLKit.Window yes - The window.

Returns nothing.

items.title: Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeClose
items.text:
Alias: Set-NHKBeforeClose

Sets the window's close policy. The host asks it (request window.before_close, parameters window_id and reason: native_close for the title-bar button or window manager, backend_request for Close-NativeHTMLKitWindow). The last output value of the scriptblock decides: truthy closes, $false or no output keeps the window open. A policy that throws is reported as a callback failure and the host receives an error reply. Keep policies fast: the host waits for the answer. Pass $null to remove the policy.

Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeClose [-Window] <Object> [-Callback] <scriptblock> [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Window NativeHTMLKit.Window yes - The window. -Callback scriptblock yes - Policy scriptblock, or $null to remove it. Accepts $null. 
Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeClose -Window $window -Callback {
    param($request)              # $request.reason: native_close or backend_request
    -not $script:dirty           # last output decides
}

items.title: Request-NativeHTMLKitAttention
items.text:
Alias: Request-NHKAttention

Asks the desktop to flag the window, for example by flashing its taskbar entry (window.request_attention). none clears a previous request. Not available in headless mode (NativeHTMLKit.RpcException, code -32001 Attention requires a native desktop window).

Request-NativeHTMLKitAttention [-Window] <Object> [[-Kind] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
Parameter Type Required Default Description -Window NativeHTMLKit.Window yes - The window. -Kind string no 'informational' informational, critical, or none to clear. One of: informational, critical, none.

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/reference/windows.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview
items.text:
In this tutorial you build a small admin tool with the NativeHTMLKit PowerShell SDK: pick a folder, type a find/replace rule (plain text or regular expression), see a live preview of the new names with conflicts flagged, confirm in a dialog, rename, and undo. It takes about 30 minutes.

You will learn the whole app lifecycle, loading HTML and CSS from files, live updates from input events, safe rendering of file names, a native folder picker with a fallback, an HTML confirmation dialog, error handling per file and an automated self-test.

The finished app is examples/bulk-rename: app.ps1, index.html and style.css. Every app.ps1 excerpt below is copied from that file, which the repository's test suite runs on Linux (PowerShell 7) and Windows (PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1).

You need PowerShell 7.2+ (Linux or Windows) or Windows PowerShell 5.1, a desktop session, and the module: Install-Module NativeHTMLKit -Scope CurrentUser.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 1: create the project
items.text:
New-NativeHTMLKitProject -Path ./BulkRename -Name 'Bulk rename' -AppId 'org.example.BulkRename'
pwsh -File ./BulkRename/app.ps1        # Windows PowerShell 5.1: powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\BulkRename\app.ps1

A window with a greeting form opens. Close it. You now have app.ps1, index.html, style.css and app.toml in BulkRename. Read script lifecycle if you want to know why the script runs twice.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 2: the page
items.text:
Replace index.html and style.css with the files from examples/bulk-rename. The page has four parts, each addressed by element ids that the script will use:

  • a header with the folder box (folder), Browse... (browse) and Load (load);
  • the rule form rule with find, replace and the checkboxes regex and case;
  • the preview table body preview;
  • a footer with the summary line summary, Undo (undo) and Rename (apply), plus a <dialog id="confirm"> with confirm-text, confirm-no and confirm-yes.

All behaviour lives in PowerShell; the page has no scripts. style.css uses prefers-color-scheme, so the tool follows the desktop's light or dark mode.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 3: the skeleton
items.text:
Replace app.ps1 with this skeleton. It loads the page from the script's folder; relative URLs in index.html (the stylesheet) resolve against that folder.

app.ps1 (step 3)
param([string]$Folder, [switch]$SelfTest)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit

$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Bulk rename'
try {
    $window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app -Title 'Bulk rename' -Width 900 -Height 620 -MinWidth 640 -MinHeight 400
    $doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitFile -Window $window -Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'index.html')

    # Steps 5-8 add state, functions and event handlers here.

    Set-NativeHTMLKitReady -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

Run it: the window shows the empty tool. param() is declared above Start-NativeHTMLKitScript, and the launcher passes your command-line arguments to the backend run, so pwsh -File ./app.ps1 -Folder ~/Pictures will reach $Folder in step 5.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 4: plan the renames without any UI
items.text:
Keep the logic that decides new names separate from the window. A pure function is easy to reason about and to test. Add it above Start-NativeHTMLKitScript (defining a function there is not a side effect, so running it twice is harmless):

app.ps1
function Get-RenamePlan {
    # Returns one row per file: Old, New, Status (unchanged | rename | conflict | invalid | error), Note.
    param([string[]]$Names, [string]$Find, [string]$Replace, [bool]$Regex, [bool]$MatchCase)
    $options = [Text.RegularExpressions.RegexOptions]::None
    if (-not $MatchCase) { $options = [Text.RegularExpressions.RegexOptions]::IgnoreCase }
    $pattern = $Find
    $replacement = $Replace
    if (-not $Regex) {
        $pattern = [regex]::Escape($Find)
        $replacement = $Replace.Replace('$', '$$')   # literal text, not $1 group references
    }
    $matcher = $null
    $patternError = $null
    if ($Find) {
        try { $matcher = New-Object Text.RegularExpressions.Regex($pattern, $options) }
        catch {
            $reason = $_.Exception
            if ($null -ne $reason.InnerException) { $reason = $reason.InnerException }
            $patternError = 'Invalid pattern: ' + $reason.Message
        }
    }
    $comparer = [StringComparer]::Ordinal
    if ([Environment]::OSVersion.Platform -eq [PlatformID]::Win32NT) { $comparer = [StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase }
    $existing = New-Object 'System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]' -ArgumentList @(, $comparer)
    foreach ($name in $Names) { [void]$existing.Add($name) }
    $claimed = New-Object 'System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]' -ArgumentList @(, $comparer)
    $invalid = [IO.Path]::GetInvalidFileNameChars()

    foreach ($name in $Names) {
        $row = [pscustomobject]@{ Old = $name; New = $name; Status = 'unchanged'; Note = '' }
        if ($patternError) { $row.Status = 'error'; $row.Note = $patternError }
        elseif ($null -ne $matcher) {
            $new = $matcher.Replace($name, $replacement)
            $row.New = $new
            if ($new -cne $name) {
                if (-not $new -or $new.IndexOfAny($invalid) -ge 0 -or $new -eq '.' -or $new -eq '..') { $row.Status = 'invalid'; $row.Note = 'Not a valid file name' }
                elseif (($existing.Contains($new) -and -not $comparer.Equals($new, $name)) -or -not $claimed.Add($new)) { $row.Status = 'conflict'; $row.Note = 'Name already used' }
                else { $row.Status = 'rename' }
            }
        }
        $row
    }
}

It escapes the find text and the $ in the replacement in plain-text mode, reports an invalid regular expression on every row instead of throwing, refuses names with characters the file system does not allow, and flags a conflict when the new name already exists or two files would get the same name (case-insensitively on Windows).

Try it in a console (paste the function first):

Get-RenamePlan -Names 'IMG_0001.jpg', 'IMG_0002.jpg', 'notes.txt' -Find 'IMG_' -Replace 'photo-' -Regex $false -MatchCase $false | Format-Table
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 5: list files and preview live
items.text:
Add the state and the functions that read the rule, render the preview, load a folder, rename and undo, inside try below Open-NativeHTMLKitFile (the rename and undo functions are used in steps 7 and 8):

app.ps1
$state = @{ Folder = $null; Names = @(); Plan = @(); Undo = @() }
app.ps1
function Read-Rule {
    return @{
        Find = Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element find
        Replace = Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element replace
        Regex = Get-NativeHTMLKitChecked -Document $doc -Element regex
        MatchCase = Get-NativeHTMLKitChecked -Document $doc -Element case
    }
}

function Update-Preview {
    $rule = Read-Rule
    $state.Plan = @(Get-RenamePlan -Names $state.Names -Find $rule.Find -Replace $rule.Replace -Regex $rule.Regex -MatchCase $rule.MatchCase)
    $html = New-Object System.Text.StringBuilder
    foreach ($row in $state.Plan) {
        $status = $row.Status
        if ($row.Note) { $status = $row.Note }
        [void]$html.Append("<tr class=`"$($row.Status)`"><td>" + [Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($row.Old) + '</td><td>' +
            [Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($row.New) + '</td><td>' + [Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($status) + '</td></tr>')
    }
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml -Document $doc -Element preview -Html $html.ToString()
    $count = @($state.Plan | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq 'rename' }).Count
    $blocked = @($state.Plan | Where-Object { $_.Status -in 'conflict', 'invalid', 'error' }).Count
    $summary = "$($state.Names.Count) file(s), $count to rename"
    if ($blocked) { $summary += ", $blocked skipped" }
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element summary -Text $summary
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element apply -Text "Rename $count"
    if ($count -gt 0) { Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute -Document $doc -Element apply -Name disabled -Remove }
    else { Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute -Document $doc -Element apply -Name disabled }
}

function Update-FileList {
    $state.Names = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $state.Folder -File | Sort-Object Name | ForEach-Object { $_.Name })
    Update-Preview
}

function Open-Folder([string]$Path) {
    if (-not $Path -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path -PathType Container)) {
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element summary -Text 'That folder does not exist.'
        return
    }
    $state.Folder = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Path).ProviderPath
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue -Document $doc -Element folder -Value $state.Folder
    Set-Undo @()
    Update-FileList
}

function Set-Undo($Steps) {
    $state.Undo = @($Steps)
    if ($state.Undo.Count -gt 0) { Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute -Document $doc -Element undo -Name disabled -Remove }
    else { Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute -Document $doc -Element undo -Name disabled }
}

function Invoke-Rename {
    $done = New-Object System.Collections.ArrayList
    $failed = 0
    foreach ($row in @($state.Plan | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq 'rename' })) {
        try {
            Rename-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $state.Folder $row.Old) -NewName $row.New
            [void]$done.Add(@{ From = $row.Old; To = $row.New })
        } catch { $failed++ }   # in use, permission denied, or changed since the preview
    }
    Set-Undo $done.ToArray()
    Update-FileList
    $message = "Renamed $($done.Count) file(s)."
    if ($failed) { $message += " $failed failed (in use, permission denied or changed)." }
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element summary -Text $message
}

function Undo-Rename {
    if ($state.Undo.Count -eq 0) { return }
    $restored = 0
    # Reverse order, so chains such as a->b, b->c are undone correctly.
    foreach ($step in $state.Undo[($state.Undo.Count - 1)..0]) {
        try { Rename-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $state.Folder $step.To) -NewName $step.From; $restored++ } catch { $null = $_ }
    }
    Set-Undo @()
    Update-FileList
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element summary -Text "Restored $restored file name(s)."
}

Everything shown in the table is a file name, which is untrusted text, so each cell is encoded with [Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode. The status class (rename, conflict, ...) comes from a fixed set and styles the row. $state is a hashtable at script level: the functions and every callback read and change the same object.

Now connect the events. input fires on every keystroke in the rule form (the handler sits on the form and receives events from all its fields), change when a checkbox toggles, and submit when the user presses Enter in a field:

app.ps1
# Live preview: every keystroke or checkbox change in the rule form.
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type input -Element rule -Callback { Update-Preview }
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type change -Element rule -Callback { Update-Preview }
# Enter in a rule field submits the form: treat it as "update preview", nothing else.
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type submit -Element rule -Callback { Update-Preview }
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element load -Callback { Open-Folder (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element folder) }

Finally, open the folder passed on the command line, just before Set-NativeHTMLKitReady:

app.ps1
if ($Folder) { Open-Folder $Folder }

Run pwsh -File ./app.ps1 -Folder <a folder with some files>. Type IMG_ in Find and photo- in Replace with: the preview updates while you type, and the summary counts the files that would be renamed.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 6: choose the folder with the native dialog
items.text:
Add the capability check after $state, so the Browse... button is disabled where the host cannot show native dialogs (for example in headless test runs):

app.ps1
$caps = Get-NativeHTMLKitCapabilities -Application $app
if (-not $caps.file_dialogs) { Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute -Document $doc -Element browse -Name disabled }

and the button's handler next to the other registrations:

app.ps1
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element browse -Callback {
    try { $picked = Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog -Window $window -Kind ChooseFolder -Title 'Folder with files to rename' }
    catch [NativeHTMLKit.RpcException] { Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element summary -Text $_.Exception.RpcMessage; return }
    if (-not $picked.cancelled) { Open-Folder @($picked.paths)[0] }
}

Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog waits until the user decides while the window keeps handling events; a cancelled dialog returns cancelled = $true. See file dialogs.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 7: confirm and rename
items.text:
Renaming is destructive, so ask first in an HTML <dialog>. The Rename button fills the dialog text and opens it modally; the dialog's buttons close it and decide. Escape closes the dialog without a click, which counts as "no".

app.ps1
function Confirm-Rename([bool]$Yes) {
    Show-NativeHTMLKitHtmlDialog -Document $doc -Element confirm -Close -ReturnValue ''
    if ($Yes) { Invoke-Rename }
}
app.ps1
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element apply -Callback {
    $count = @($state.Plan | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq 'rename' }).Count
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element confirm-text -Text "Rename $count file(s) in $($state.Folder)?"
    Show-NativeHTMLKitHtmlDialog -Document $doc -Element confirm
}
# Decide in the button handlers, not in the dialog's close event: a <dialog> keeps its
# previous return value when the user dismisses it with Escape.
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element confirm-no -Callback { Confirm-Rename $false }
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element confirm-yes -Callback { Confirm-Rename $true }

The decision is made in the button handlers rather than in the dialog's close event because a <dialog> keeps its previous return value when it is dismissed with Escape (see HTML dialogs).

Invoke-Rename (added in step 5) renames each planned file on its own: one locked file does not stop the others, and the summary reports how many failed. Each success is recorded for undo.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 8: undo
items.text:
Undo-Rename (also added in step 5) renames the recorded files back in reverse order. Connect the Undo button:

app.ps1
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element undo -Callback { Undo-Rename }

Your app now matches examples/bulk-rename/app.ps1 except for the self-test.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 9: test it without a screen
items.text:
The finished example has a -SelfTest switch. It creates a temporary folder with sample files, fills the rule form through the SDK (Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue, Set-NativeHTMLKitChecked), checks the preview summary and the conflict detection, opens the confirmation dialog and calls Confirm-Rename $true (what the dialog's Rename button does), checks the files on disk, undoes, and finally requests a quit:

$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE = '1'      # the host runs without windows on screen
pwsh -File ./app.ps1 -SelfTest          # prints: SELFTEST PASS bulk-rename

Headless mode has no mouse or keyboard input, so the self-test calls the same functions the handlers call. This catches mistakes in your logic and in the SDK calls; check the real clicks once in a desktop session.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Where next
items.text:
• Ship it: project scaffolding explains app.toml, app identity and distribution.
  • Make it faster on big folders: move Get-ChildItem into a background task.
  • Browse the other examples and the cmdlet reference.

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/tutorials/bulk-rename.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Tutorial: a live process dashboard
items.text:
You will build Process Dashboard: a native window with a table of running processes that refreshes itself in the background, can be filtered and sorted, paused, and copied to the clipboard. It works the same on Linux (PowerShell 7) and Windows (PowerShell 7 or Windows PowerShell 5.1).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and PowerShell SDK 0.1.2 on PowerShell 7.7.

Time: about 30 minutes. You need: the NativeHTMLKit module and the first window from getting started. The three scripts are in examples/process-dashboard/; the final app is app.ps1. All three are run against the real host by this repository's tests.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 1: a table from Get-Process
Step 2: filter and sort
Step 3: background refresh, pause and copy
items.text:
Calling Get-Process inside a callback blocks the window while it runs. The final version collects processes in a background task and refreshes every few seconds. The page gains a status line, a Pause checkbox and a Copy table button (see app.ps1 for the full markup). The script now takes a parameter, and -SelfTest lets the test suite drive it headless:

app.ps1
param([ValidateRange(1, 3600)][int]$RefreshSeconds = 3, [switch]$SelfTest)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Process Dashboard'

The data collection runs in a separate runspace:

app.ps1
# Runs in a separate runspace: no access to $app, $doc or this script's variables and functions.
$collect = {
    param([int]$DelayMilliseconds)
    if ($DelayMilliseconds -gt 0) { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds $DelayMilliseconds }
    Get-Process | ForEach-Object {
        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $_.ProcessName; Id = $_.Id
            MemoryMB = [Math]::Round($_.WorkingSet64 / 1MB, 1); Cpu = [Math]::Round([double]$_.CPU, 1) }
    }
}

Everything the callbacks change lives in one object, and Update-View now renders the cached snapshot instead of calling Get-Process:

app.ps1
# Everything the callbacks change lives in one object, so they never need to assign script variables.
$view = [pscustomobject]@{ Rows = @(); Refreshes = 0; Task = $null; Shown = @() }

function ConvertTo-HtmlText([string]$Text) { return [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($Text) }

function Update-View {
    $filter = (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element filter).Trim()
    $shown = @($view.Rows | Where-Object { $filter -eq '' -or $_.Name.IndexOf($filter, [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) -ge 0 })
    $sorted = switch (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element sort) {
        'cpu'  { $shown | Sort-Object Cpu -Descending }
        'name' { $shown | Sort-Object Name }
        default { $shown | Sort-Object MemoryMB -Descending }
    }
    $view.Shown = @($sorted | Select-Object -First 25)
    $html = @($view.Shown | ForEach-Object {
        '<tr><td>{0}</td><td class="num">{1}</td><td class="num">{2:N1}</td><td class="num">{3:N1}</td></tr>' -f `
            (ConvertTo-HtmlText $_.Name), $_.Id, $_.MemoryMB, $_.Cpu
    }) -join ''
    $total = ($view.Rows | Measure-Object MemoryMB -Sum).Sum
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml -Document $doc -Element rows -Html $html
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element summary -Text ("Showing {0} of {1} processes, {2:N0} MB in total" -f $view.Shown.Count, $view.Rows.Count, $total)
}

Start-Refresh starts the task and schedules the next one when it completes:

app.ps1
function Start-Refresh([int]$DelayMilliseconds) {
    $view.Task = Start-NativeHTMLKitTask -Application $app -ScriptBlock $collect -ArgumentList @($DelayMilliseconds) -OnCompleted {
        param($rows)
        $view.Task = $null
        $view.Rows = @($rows)
        $view.Refreshes++
        Update-View
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text ("Updated {0:HH:mm:ss} (refresh #{1})" -f (Get-Date), $view.Refreshes)
        if (-not (Get-NativeHTMLKitChecked -Document $doc -Element paused)) { Start-Refresh ($RefreshSeconds * 1000) }
    } -OnFailed {
        param($failure)
        $view.Task = $null
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text ('Refresh failed: ' + $failure.Message)
    }
}

Copying the visible rows as tab-separated text:

app.ps1
function Copy-Table {
    $lines = @("Name`tId`tMemoryMB`tCpu") + @($view.Shown | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name)`t$($_.Id)`t$($_.MemoryMB)`t$($_.Cpu)" })
    try {
        Set-NativeHTMLKitClipboard -Application $app -Text ($lines -join [Environment]::NewLine)
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text "Copied $($view.Shown.Count) rows"
    } catch {
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text 'The clipboard is not available in this session'
    }
}

Finally the window, the subscriptions and the first refresh:

app.ps1
try {
    $window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app -Title 'Process Dashboard' -Width 760 -Height 640
    $doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml -Window $window -Html $page
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type input -Element filter -Callback { param($eventObject) Update-View }
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type change -Element sort -Callback { param($eventObject) Update-View }
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type submit -Element 'view-form' -Callback { param($eventObject) Update-View }
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type change -Element paused -Callback {
        param($eventObject)
        if ([bool]$eventObject.checked) {
            Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text 'Paused'
        } elseif ($null -eq $view.Task) {
            Start-Refresh 0
        }
    }
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element copy -Callback { param($eventObject) Copy-Table }
    Start-Refresh 0
    Set-NativeHTMLKitReady -Application $app

In the file, the -SelfTest block comes next; the script ends with the event loop:

app.ps1
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}
  • Start-NativeHTMLKitTask -ScriptBlock $collect -ArgumentList @($delay) runs $collect in a separate runspace. It cannot see $app, $doc or your functions, and it must not receive SDK objects; pass plain data in and return plain objects (here [pscustomobject] rows).
  • -OnCompleted { param($rows) ... } runs back on the main runspace, during Wait-NativeHTMLKit, where it is safe to update the page. It stores the rows, re-renders and starts the next task: a self-scheduling timer that never blocks the window.
  • -OnFailed receives the exception if the task throws, times out or is stopped.
  • Everything the callbacks change lives in one object, $view. Assigning $x = ... inside a scriptblock would only create a local variable; setting $view.Rows changes the shared object.
  • The pause checkbox reads $eventObject.checked from the change event. Unpausing starts a new refresh immediately if none is pending.
  • Copy table uses Set-NativeHTMLKitClipboard inside try/catch: some sessions (for example headless test runs) have no clipboard.
  • -RefreshSeconds is a normal script parameter: pwsh -File app.ps1 -RefreshSeconds 10. The host re-runs the script with the same arguments.
  • Close-NativeHTMLKit in finally also requests cancellation of a task that is still sleeping; no callback runs after it.

Test it headless: $env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE = '1'; pwsh -File app.ps1 -SelfTest waits for two refreshes, filters, sorts, pauses, copies (or reports that there is no clipboard) and prints SELFTEST PASS process-dashboard.

items.title: What you learned
items.text:
• Render tables from objects with encoded values; subscribe to input, change and submit.
  • Keep slow work off the event loop with Start-NativeHTMLKitTask, and update the page in -OnCompleted.
  • Share state between callbacks through one object; pass parameters through the re-executed script.

items.title: Where next
items.text:
• Background work: cancellation with Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask, timeouts and several jobs at once.
  • Live bitmaps: draw a memory chart next to the table.
  • Cmdlet reference.

Source: nativehtmlkit-powershell/docs/tutorials/process-dashboard.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Tutorial: build a todo app
items.text:
In five steps you build a complete desktop todo list with the NativeHTMLKit PowerShell SDK: a native window with HTML and CSS, adding items with a form, completing and deleting them, editing in place with keyboard support, and saving everything to a JSON file.

Every step is a complete script in examples/todo-tutorial/; the final result is examples/04-todo-list.ps1. All of them are started and checked by this repository's test suite against the real native host, with PowerShell 7 on Linux and Windows and with Windows PowerShell 5.1.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

You need PowerShell 7.2+ (Linux x64 or Windows x64) or Windows PowerShell 5.1, and about 30 minutes.

Install-Module NativeHTMLKit -Scope CurrentUser
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit; (Get-Module NativeHTMLKit).Version     # 0.1.2

items.title: Step 1: a window with HTML and CSS
items.text:
Create todo.ps1 (the tested copy in the repository is step1-window.ps1):

step1-window.ps1
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit

$page = @'
<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; background:#f6f7fb; color:#1d2433; font:15px/1.4 sans-serif; }
  main { max-width:560px; margin:32px auto; padding:0 20px; }
  ul { list-style:none; padding:0; background:#fff; border-radius:8px; }
  li { padding:10px 12px; border-bottom:1px solid #e3e6ee; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <h1>Todo</h1>
  <ul id="todos"><li>Learn NativeHTMLKit</li><li>Build an app</li></ul>
</main></body></html>
'@

$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Todo'
try {
    $window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app -Title 'Todo' -Width 640 -Height 480
    $doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml -Window $window -Html $page
    Set-NativeHTMLKitReady -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown     # returns when the user closes the window
} finally {
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

Run it with pwsh -File ./todo.ps1 (Windows PowerShell: powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\todo.ps1). A native window appears; the HTML and CSS are rendered by the native host. There is no browser and no JavaScript.

What happened:

  • Start-NativeHTMLKitScript started the native host, and the host ran todo.ps1 a second time as its supervised backend. In that second run the call returned a connected application. That is why side effects (files, prompts) belong below this line: anything above it runs twice. Assigning the page to $page above it is harmless. (Lifecycle explains the details.)
  • The page is a single-quoted here-string (@' ... '@): PowerShell does not expand $ or backticks inside it.
  • New-NativeHTMLKitWindow and Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml created the window and loaded the page.
  • Set-NativeHTMLKitReady told the host the app is ready; Wait-NativeHTMLKit -UntilShutdown runs the event loop until the window is closed. Close-NativeHTMLKit in finally cleans up.

Full file: step1-window.ps1.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 2: add items with a form
items.text:
Replace the static list with a form and an empty list:

<form id="new-form">
  <input id="new-title" type="text" placeholder="What needs doing?" required>
  <button id="add" type="submit">Add</button>
</form>
<ul id="todos"></ul>
<p id="count">0 items</p>

and handle the form's submit event below Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml:

step2-add.ps1
$titles = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]

function Update-Todos {
    # HtmlEncode: a title such as "<b>" is shown as text, never parsed as markup.
    $html = ($titles | ForEach-Object { '<li>' + [Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($_) + '</li>' }) -join ''
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml -Document $doc -Element todos -Html $html
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element count -Text "$($titles.Count) items"   # never parses markup
}

# Clicking Add, or pressing Enter in the field, submits the form.
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type submit -Element new-form -Callback {
    $title = (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element new-title).Trim()
    if ($title) {
        $titles.Add($title)
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue -Document $doc -Element new-title -Value ''
        Update-Todos
    }
}

New ideas:

  • Events. Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Type submit -Element new-form runs the scriptblock whenever that form is submitted: by clicking Add or by pressing Enter in the field (HTML implicit submission). required makes the host refuse an empty submission before PowerShell sees it.
  • Callbacks run later. The scriptblock runs inside Wait-NativeHTMLKit, on this runspace. It can read script variables ($doc, $titles) and call script functions (Update-Todos).
  • Reading and writing controls. Get-NativeHTMLKitValue reads what the user typed; Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue clears it.
  • Rendering. The PowerShell list is the source of truth; Update-Todos rebuilds the <ul> from it with Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml.
  • Escaping. Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml parses HTML, so every piece of user text goes through [Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode. Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText and Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue never parse markup and need no escaping. (Security)

Full file: step2-add.ps1.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 3: complete and delete items
items.text:
Each item becomes a small structure with a checkbox and a Delete button. The ids encode the item number and the action:

step3-complete-delete.ps1
function Get-TodoRow($Todo) {
    $n = $Todo.Id; $class = ''; $checked = ''
    if ($Todo.Done) { $class = 'done'; $checked = ' checked' }
    return ('<li id="todo-{0}" class="{1}"><input id="todo-{0}-done" type="checkbox"{2}>' -f $n, $class, $checked) +
        ('<span class="text">{0}</span><button id="todo-{1}-delete" class="plain">Delete</button></li>' -f [Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($Todo.Title), $n)
}

The handlers now change more than one value, so the state moves into one hashtable. A callback that assigned $nextId++ would only change a local copy; changing an entry of a shared hashtable changes it for everybody:

step3-complete-delete.ps1
$state = @{ Todos = New-Object System.Collections.ArrayList; NextId = 1 }

Instead of subscribing to every checkbox and button, subscribe once to the list:

step3-complete-delete.ps1
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type change -Element todos -Callback {
    param($evt)
    if ($evt.element -match '^todo-(\d+)-done$') {
        (Find-Todo ([int]$Matches[1])).Done = [bool]$evt.checked
        Update-Todos
    }
}
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element todos -Callback {
    param($evt)
    if ($evt.element -match '^todo-(\d+)-delete$') {
        $state.Todos.Remove((Find-Todo ([int]$Matches[1])))
        Update-Todos
    }
}

-Element todos also matches events whose target is inside the list. Every event names the nearest element with an id in $evt.element and lists all identified ancestors in $evt.path, so a click on the Delete button of item 7 arrives with element = 'todo-7-delete'. The checkbox reports its new state in $evt.checked. Because the subscription lives on the list, re-rendering the items never requires subscribing again. Name the parameter $evt: $event is a PowerShell automatic variable.

A little CSS strikes through completed items:

li.done .text { text-decoration:line-through; color:#6b7385; }

Full file: step3-complete-delete.ps1. More on delegation in events and callbacks.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 4: edit in place, with the keyboard
items.text:
An Edit button switches one row into an inline form. The state gets an Editing entry, and the row function renders the form for that row:

step4-edit-keyboard.ps1
$title = [Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($Todo.Title)    # also escapes quotes for value="..."
if ($n -eq $state.Editing) {
    # Enter in this field submits its form; Escape is handled by the keydown handler.
    return '<li id="todo-{0}"><form id="edit-form-{0}"><input id="edit-title" type="text" value="{1}"></form></li>' -f $n, $title
}

HtmlEncode also protects the value="..." attribute, because it escapes quotes. One submit handler, registered without -Element, serves both forms; $evt.element says which one was submitted:

step4-edit-keyboard.ps1
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type submit -Callback {
    param($evt)
    if ($evt.element -eq 'new-form') {
        $title = (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element new-title).Trim()
        if ($title) {
            [void]$state.Todos.Add(@{ Id = $state.NextId; Title = $title; Done = $false })
            $state.NextId++
            Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue -Document $doc -Element new-title -Value ''
        }
    } elseif ($evt.element -like 'edit-form-*') {
        $title = (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element edit-title).Trim()
        if ($title) { (Find-Todo $state.Editing).Title = $title }
        $state.Editing = $null
    }
    Update-Todos
}

Starting an edit renders the input and moves the keyboard focus into it:

step4-edit-keyboard.ps1
$state.Editing = $id
Update-Todos
Set-NativeHTMLKitFocus -Document $doc -Element edit-title

And Escape cancels, via a keydown subscription on the list:

step4-edit-keyboard.ps1
# keydown events carry `key` (for example "Enter", "Escape", "a") and modifier flags.
$null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type keydown -Element todos -Callback {
    param($evt)
    if ($evt.key -eq 'Escape' -and $null -ne $state.Editing) {
        $state.Editing = $null
        Update-Todos
    }
}

Full file: step4-edit-keyboard.ps1. More in keyboard and focus.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 5: save to a JSON file and polish
items.text:
The finished app, examples/04-todo-list.ps1, adds persistence, filters, "Clear completed", an empty state and a theme that follows the desktop's dark mode.

Where to store data. The host knows per-application folders. Give the app a stable id, then ask for its data folder:

04-todo-list.ps1
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Todo' -AppId 'org.nativehtmlkit.examples.powershell.todo'
04-todo-list.ps1
# desktop.paths is a public Core v1 method: per-application config/data/cache folders.
$DataPath = Join-Path (Invoke-NativeHTMLKitRpc -Application $app -Method 'desktop.paths').data 'todos.json'

desktop.paths returns XDG folders on Linux and AppData folders on Windows, named after the app id. The host does not create them.

Load and save safely. A missing or broken file starts an empty list; writes go to a temporary file first, which then replaces the old one, so a crash never leaves half a file:

04-todo-list.ps1
# Write atomically: a crash mid-write never leaves a truncated file.
function Save-Todos([string]$Path, $Todos) {
    $folder = Split-Path -Parent $Path
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $folder)) { $null = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $folder }
    $json = ConvertTo-Json -InputObject @($Todos | ForEach-Object { [ordered]@{ id = $_.Id; title = $_.Title; done = $_.Done } })
    $temporary = $Path + '.tmp'
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($temporary, $json, (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path) { [IO.File]::Replace($temporary, $Path, [NullString]::Value) } else { [IO.File]::Move($temporary, $Path) }
}

ConvertTo-Json -InputObject @(...) writes an array even for one item, and [NullString]::Value tells File.Replace "no backup file" (a plain $null would arrive as an empty string). Every action ends in Complete-Change, which saves and re-renders.

Testable actions. The handlers only translate events into calls such as Add-Todo, Set-TodoDone, Rename-Todo and Remove-Todo. Those functions can be called directly, which is how the app's -SelfTest drives it headless: it submits the form with Submit-NativeHTMLKitForm, calls the actions, and reads the result back with Get-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText, Find-NativeHTMLKitElement and the saved JSON file.

Styling with the desktop theme. CSS custom properties plus a media query switch the palette when the desktop is in dark mode:

:root { --bg:#f6f7fb; --card:#fff; --text:#1d2433; --accent:#3a6ff7; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root { --bg:#141923; --card:#1d2433; --text:#e8ecf5; --accent:#7aa2ff; }
}
body { background:var(--bg); color:var(--text); }

Run the finished app:

pwsh -File ./04-todo-list.ps1                 # Windows PowerShell: powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\04-todo-list.ps1

items.title: Test it without a desktop
items.text:
The host has a headless mode for automated tests. It runs the whole protocol without native windows (and without user input):

$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE = '1'
pwsh -File ./04-todo-list.ps1 -SelfTest       # prints SELFTEST PASS 04-todo-list

Combine it with Submit-NativeHTMLKitForm, Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue and the read-back cmdlets to test behaviour in CI.
