items.title: Python SDK
items.text:
Plain HTML and CSS driven from your program: open windows, load pages, react to events, update the page, use native dialogs, the clipboard and live bitmaps. Full control, no extra layer. The UI library is built on it.

  • Getting started
  • Tutorials
  • How-to guides
  • Examples
  • API reference

Same section in PowerShell: PowerShell SDK. Differences between Linux and Windows: Linux and Windows.

items.title: Python SDK architecture
items.text: How nativehtmlkit 0.1.2 runs an application: which processes exist, how they find and trust each other, which threads run your code, and why handles become stale. For the API itself see the reference.

items.title: Process model
items.text:
flowchart LR
  L["Launcher<br/>uv run app.py: python app.py<br/>(Application.start)"] -- "starts, relays output,<br/>exits with its status" --> H["Native host<br/>nativehtmlkit-host run --app"]
  H -- "starts and supervises" --> B["Backend<br/>python app.py (again, same interpreter)<br/>Application returned here"]
  B <-- "authenticated local socket / named pipe<br/>length-prefixed JSON-RPC (wire v1)" --> H

Three roles cooperate:

Process Owns Launcher: the command you ran Writing a private manifest, starting the host, relaying output, propagating the exit status and signals Native host (Rust, bundled in the wheel) Windows, rendering, input, IME, accessibility, native dialogs and services, the event loop, start-up/shutdown policy, supervising the backend Backend: your Python code Application logic; the Application/Window/Document objects

There is no browser, JavaScript engine or HTTP server. The backend never draws; it sends commands and receives events.

items.title: Start-up: re-executing the script
items.text:
Application.start() decides its role from the environment:

  1. No host connection variables: this is the launcher. It reconstructs the current command line from sys.orig_argv (interpreter options and -m module form preserved; a script path made absolute), writes app.toml into a fresh private temporary directory (prefix nativehtmlkit-start-, removed afterwards; leftovers older than a day are swept), resolves and verifies the host, and runs nativehtmlkit-host run --app <manifest> (plus --headless when NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1). It marks the environment with UI4ME_DIRECT_START so that a backend that somehow lacks a connection refuses to start yet another host.
  2. Connection variables present: this is the backend. start() validates the options, connects with from_environment() and returns the Application.

Consequently code before start() runs in both processes. uv run -m nativehtmlkit run module:func avoids that: its launcher never imports your module, and its backend imports it once, after connecting.

items.title: Host resolution and verification
items.text: nativehtmlkit.host_binary() picks the host: NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY (explicit development override), else the wheel's bundled _bin/nativehtmlkit-host[.exe], whose SHA-256 must match _bin/HOST-MANIFEST.json on every launch (HostVerificationError otherwise), else, only with NATIVEHTMLKIT_ALLOW_PATH_HOST=1, an absolute PATH entry (unverified, with a warning). uv run nativehtmlkit-python version reports which one is used and whether the build identity matches.

items.title: Lifetime binding
items.text:
The host must not outlive the launcher, and the backend must not outlive the host:

  • Linux: the host is started with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (SIGTERM if the launcher dies); the host runs the backend under its own containment.
  • Windows: the host is placed in a kill-on-close Job Object held by the launcher; the host puts the backend in its own job.
  • Ctrl+C, SIGTERM or SIGHUP to the launcher terminate the host (forcefully after 10 s); the launcher exits with 128 + signal number.

items.title: Output relay
items.text: The host captures the backend's standard output and error and writes them, with its own structured records, to its standard error as JSON lines. The launcher turns backend lines back into plain text on the matching stream, summarises host warnings and errors, and shows host information records only with NATIVEHTMLKIT_VERBOSE=1. The backend runs with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 and UTF-8 output so print() appears at once.

items.title: Connection
items.text:
• Transport: a Unix domain socket in a private runtime directory (Linux) or a named pipe restricted to the current logon session (Windows; overlapped I/O so reads and writes do not block each other).
  • Authentication: the first request is host.hello with the single-use 64-hex token from UI4ME_TOKEN and protocol_version: 1. The SDK then deletes UI4ME_ENDPOINT, UI4ME_TOKEN, UI4ME_APP_ID and UI4ME_PROTOCOL_VERSION from os.environ.
  • Framing: 4-byte big-endian length + one UTF-8 JSON object, at most 2 MiB. Outgoing requests that cannot be encoded or are too large are refused locally (LocalRequestError); a malformed frame from the host is fatal (ProtocolError).
  • Messages: a JSON-RPC 2.0 subset. Request ids are strings (py-1, py-2, …), responses are matched by id, never by order. At most 128 requests may be pending and 8 MiB queued for writing (ClientBusyError beyond that, nothing sent).
  • Deadlines: synchronous calls default to 15 s (none for native dialogs). A timeout sends request.cancel and raises RpcTimeoutError with outcome_unknown=True: the SDK never claims a rollback.

items.title: Threads
items.text:
flowchart TB
  subgraph Transport
    R[receiver thread] --> Q1[(ordered notification queue, 128)]
    R --> Q2[(request queue, 128)]
    W[writer thread]
  end
  Q1 --> E[application events thread<br/>document.on, on_window_event, on_desktop_preferences]
  Q2 --> P[4 worker threads<br/>on_before_close, on_before_quit, app.shutdown]
  R -. "responses complete futures" .-> C[completion thread per call_async result]
  M[your thread: app.run] --> S[on_shutdown callbacks]
  • The receiver reads frames, completes pending requests and sorts host messages into queues. The writer drains the outgoing queue. Neither ever runs application code, so a callback may make blocking SDK calls without deadlocking the connection.
  • Notifications (document.event, window.event, document.error, preference changes) go to one ordered queue served by a single application events thread: your event callbacks run one at a time, in the order the host sent them.
  • Host requests (window.before_close, app.before_quit) and app.shutdown go to a pool of four workers. Close and quit decisions are therefore answered even while an event callback waits, for example on a blocking file dialog. Every host request is answered; an exception counts as a denial.
  • Futures from call_async (and wait=False dialogs) are completed on a short-lived completion thread each, so their done-callbacks may call the synchronous SDK.
  • Both queues hold 128 messages. When callbacks fall that far behind, further notifications are dropped and counted (rpc.dropped_notifications); further host requests are answered with -32005. The host separately drops window/document events when the backend stops reading its socket and reports them in host.diagnostics dropped_notifications.

All public methods are safe to call from any thread: requests from several threads are multiplexed over the one connection.

items.title: Callback dispatch
items.text:
For each document.event the application looks up the window and checks that the event's document_id is the window's current document; events of a retired document are dropped silently. The document then matches subscriptions: same type, and either no element filter or the filter equals the event's element (nearest identified target) or appears in its path (identified bubbling route). Matching handlers run in subscription order; one raising does not stop the others. Each dispatch writes a document.dispatch trace record with the number of registered and matched handlers.

window.event first updates bookkeeping (a closed window is marked closed and its document retired) and then calls on_window_event listeners.

items.title: Document generations
items.text:
Every successful document.load returns a new document id. The Window swaps its document attribute only after the load succeeded, then retires the previous Document:

  • its subscriptions are cleared and its live bitmaps closed;
  • every method on it, and on Nodes that reference it, raises StaleDocumentError locally;
  • the host independently rejects the old id (RpcError -32004) if it ever receives it.

Node references (node:…) embed the document generation, so they cannot address the replacement document either. The same retirement happens on unload(), on the window's closed event, after a fatal document.error and, for everything, on app.shutdown.

items.title: Lifecycle state machine
items.text:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Connecting: backend started
  Connecting --> Initializing: host.hello
  Initializing --> Running: app.ready (Application.run)
  Initializing --> Stopped: a window closed before app.ready
  Initializing --> Failed: start-up timeout
  Running --> QuitPending: last window closed or request_quit
  QuitPending --> Running: on_before_quit returned False
  QuitPending --> ShuttingDown: allowed
  ShuttingDown --> Stopped: backend exits before shutdown_timeout_ms
  Running --> Failed: backend disconnect or crash

On app.shutdown the SDK sets rpc.shutdown_requested, waits up to two seconds for already received events to be handled, records the host's drop counter, retires every window and document, runs on_shutdown callbacks on the thread of run(), and run() returns. Core v1 sends no closed event for the last window; app.shutdown implies it. During shutdown the host refuses most methods (RpcError -32008), so on-shutdown code should only touch Python state and files.

If the connection drops instead, pending requests fail with DisconnectedError (their outcome is unknown) and run() raises DisconnectedError. A deliberate close() ends run() normally on the Python side, but the host sees a lost backend and exits with status 1.

items.title: asyncio layer
items.text: AsyncApplication adds no second connection. AsyncRpcClient.call wraps the transport future with asyncio.wrap_future; EventDispatcher moves events from the application events thread onto your loop with call_soon_threadsafe into a bounded FIFO and runs callbacks (sync or async) there one at a time. AsyncApplication.run() runs the blocking Application.run() in a worker thread.

items.title: Diagnostics
items.text: Each layer records structured, privacy-filtered events: the SDK into memory (and, at debug/trace, JSON Lines files), the host into its standard error. One session id (NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID) is shared by launcher, host and backend, and RPC records carry cause_seq, the notification whose callback issued them, so a timeline links "user clicked" to "handler ran" to "host answered". See diagnostics.

items.title: Packaging
items.text: A platform wheel bundles exactly one Core host for its OS (_bin/), its HOST-MANIFEST.json with the pinned SHA-256 and build identity, and the Core licence notices; a source-only build has no host. See BUILD.md.

items.title: Boundaries
items.text:
The SDK speaks only the public Core wire protocol v1; it imports no Core internals. Reusable components, layouts and reactive state belong to the separate Python UI library, which uses only this SDK's public API.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Getting started with the Python SDK
items.text: Build a native desktop window from Python, HTML and CSS in about ten minutes. This page covers installing nativehtmlkit 0.1.2, writing and running a first application, testing it without a screen, and where to go next.

items.title: What you get
items.text: NativeHTMLKit draws windows with a native host written in Rust (Core 1.0.3). Your page is local HTML and CSS; your logic is ordinary Python that reacts to events and changes the page. There is no browser, no JavaScript and no web server. The host and your Python code run as two processes that talk over a private local connection.

items.title: Install
items.text:
You need uv on Linux x64 (glibc 2.39 or newer) or Windows x64, and a desktop session to see windows. uv provides a CPython 3.10 to 3.14 for the project if you have none.

uv init --app hello && cd hello         # a project for your app
uv add nativehtmlkit
uv run nativehtmlkit-python version     # prints the SDK, protocol and bundled host versions

The platform wheels bundle the native host and check its SHA-256 on every start. The source distribution has no host; use a published wheel. uv run nativehtmlkit-python doctor prints the host's view of your desktop session (display server, paths, renderer) without opening a window.

items.title: Your first window
items.text:
Save this as hello.py in the project folder. It is the repository's hello.py example:

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Document

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 32px; }
  input { padding: 6px 8px; font-size: 15px; }
  button { padding: 6px 14px; font-size: 15px; }
  #greeting { margin-top: 18px; font-size: 20px; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <label for="name">Your name</label>
  <input id="name" autofocus>
  <button id="greet">Greet</button>
  <p id="greeting">Type a name and press Greet.</p>
</body></html>"""


def greet(document: Document) -> None:
    name = document.get_value("name").strip() or "world"
    # Text is never parsed as HTML: '<b>' typed by the user stays visible as '<b>'.
    document.set_text("greeting", f"Hello, {name}!")


def build(app: Application) -> Document:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Hello", width=520, height=300)
    document = window.document
    document.on("click", lambda _event: greet(document), element="greet")
    return document


def main() -> None:
    # Application.start() runs this script a second time as the host's backend.
    # Keep side effects inside main(), after start().
    with Application.start(name="Hello NativeHTMLKit") as app:
        build(app)
        app.run()   # until the user closes the last window


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run it:

uv run hello.py

A window titled Hello opens. Type a name and press Greet. Close the window to end the program.

items.title: What happened
items.text:
1. Application.start() started the native host. The host ran hello.py a second time as its backend; in that run start() connected and returned the Application. Code before start() runs in both processes, so keep it free of side effects and put your work in main().
  2. app.open_html(PAGE, title=..., width=..., height=...) opened a window and loaded the page. It returns a Window; window.document is the loaded Document.
  3. document.on("click", callback, element="greet") subscribed to clicks on the element with id="greet" (and anything inside it). Callbacks receive the event as a dict.
  4. get_value read the input field; set_text replaced the paragraph's text. set_text never interprets HTML, which makes it safe for anything the user typed.
  5. app.run() told the host the application is ready, then dispatched events until the last window closed.

Every element your Python code touches has an id. That is how you address the page.

items.title: Other ways to run
items.text:
• uv run -m nativehtmlkit run hello:build imports hello.py only in the backend and calls build(app); the runner then calls app.run() for you. Use it when module-level code must run only once (see lifecycle).
  • nativehtmlkit-new myapp --name "My App" creates a project with app.py, index.html and style.css (see project scaffolding).

items.title: Run it without a screen
items.text:
NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 runs the real host headless, which is how you test an application in CI. Native services (file dialogs, clipboard, opening links) are not available there and raise RpcError with code -32001. A test drives the same functions the handlers call and reads the page back:

# check_hello.py, next to hello.py
import threading

import hello


def check(app):
    document = hello.build(app)
    document.set_value("name", "<b>Ada</b>")
    hello.greet(document)
    assert document.get_text("greeting") == "Hello, <b>Ada</b>!"
    print("hello works")
    threading.Timer(0.5, app.request_quit).start()

NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 uv run -m nativehtmlkit run check_hello:check     # prints: hello works

items.title: When something does not work
items.text:
• uv run nativehtmlkit-python version exits with status 1 when no usable host is found: install a platform wheel for Linux x64 or Windows x64.
  • Nothing happens on a click: check that the id in element= matches the HTML. Run with uv run nativehtmlkit-python --diagnostics trace run hello:build and look for document.dispatch records with matched: 0.
  • More in diagnostics and troubleshooting.

  • Solve a task: the how-to guides, for example events, updating the page and styling and layout.
  • Look something up: the API reference.
  • Read working code: the examples, 21 small applications listed in examples/catalog.toml.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/getting-started.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Python examples
items.text:
Every example is a complete program, verified against the real NativeHTMLKit host. Open one to see a screenshot, how to run it and its full source.

Example What it does Hello The smallest complete app: a greeting form that writes untrusted text safely. Counter A counter with a step selector, limits and a bounded change history. Todo list Add, edit, complete, filter and delete tasks, saved to a JSON file. Sign-up form Sign-up form with native constraint validation, a password-match rule, an error summary and a result. Inventory data table Searchable, sortable, paged table rendered from data, with a details pane. Process viewer Sortable, filterable table of running processes. Log viewer Follows a growing log file with highlighting, pause, clear and auto-scroll. File viewer Text file viewer and editor with native Open, Save As and Choose Folder dialogs. Multiple windows Note windows managed from a main window, with a close veto for unsaved notes. Settings dialog Settings in a modal HTML dialog, saved to JSON: colour scheme, text size and reduced motion. Clipboard tool Text transforms, copy and paste, a documentation link and the desktop colour scheme. Checksums SHA-256 of every file in a folder, computed in the background with progress, cancel and a quit warning. Live chart A live line chart of memory use drawn into an RGBA bitmap. Snippet editor A snippet editor with keyboard shortcuts, Tab indentation and a help popover. About and support An About/Support window: capabilities, preferences, counters and a support bundle. DOM explorer Tree view of a live DOM with selecting, editing, moving and deleting nodes. Focus timer A countdown timer that asks before quitting while it runs. Background jobs Concurrent jobs with progress bars and cancel buttons. Bulk rename Rename many files with find/replace, a live preview, a confirmation dialog and undo. Process dashboard Live process monitor that refreshes in the background, with filter, sort, pause and copy. Async counter A counter whose callback is an async function (asyncio basics).

items.title: Async counter
items.text:
A counter whose callback is an async function (asyncio basics).

Python only

This example has no counterpart in the other language.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

What it teaches: async_adapter; awaitable document.command.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
uv init --app myapp && cd myapp    # once: a uv project for your app
uv add nativehtmlkit
# save the example file(s) in the project folder, then:
uv run async_counter.py

Related guide: asyncio

items.title: Source: async_counter.py
items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Async counter: async callbacks on the owning event loop, awaitable RPC, clean shutdown.

What it teaches (Python-specific: asyncio basics)
  * ``app.async_adapter()``: the same host connection, with callbacks that run on YOUR loop
  * ``async def`` event handlers registered with ``adapter.on_document_event``
  * awaitable RPC (``await adapter.rpc.call(...)``) that keeps the loop responsive
  * ``await adapter.run()``, which returns when the window is closed or the app quits

Run:  uv run async_counter.py   (or: uv run -m nativehtmlkit run async_counter:amain)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Window

HTML = """<main style="padding:20px;font-family:sans-serif">
<h1>Async counter</h1>
<button id="inc">Add one</button> <span id="count">0</span>
<p id="status">Ready</p></main>"""


class AsyncCounter:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, window: Window):
        self.window, self.document = window, window.document
        self.adapter = app.async_adapter()   # callbacks registered here run on the current loop
        self.count = 0
        self.adapter.on_document_event(self.document, "click", self.increment, element="inc")

    async def increment(self, _event: dict) -> None:
        self.count += 1
        # Awaitable RPC: the loop keeps running while the host answers.
        await self.adapter.rpc.call("document.command", {
            "window_id": self.window.id, "document_id": self.document.id,
            "command": {"op": "set_text", "element": "count", "text": str(self.count)}})


async def amain(app: Application) -> None:
    # Blocking SDK calls go through a thread so they never stall the loop.
    window = await asyncio.to_thread(app.open_html, HTML, title="NativeHTMLKit async counter", width=420, height=260)
    counter = AsyncCounter(app, window)
    await counter.adapter.run()   # returns after the window is closed / the app quits


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Async counter") as app:
        asyncio.run(amain(app))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.title: Background jobs
items.text:
Concurrent jobs with progress bars and cancel buttons.

Same example in PowerShell: Background jobs

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

What it teaches: asyncio tasks; async callbacks; AsyncRpcClient; cancellation.

items.title: Run it

uv init --app myapp && cd myapp    # once: a uv project for your app
uv add nativehtmlkit
# save the example file(s) in the project folder, then:

items.title: Source: async_jobs.py
items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Async job runner: start, watch and cancel concurrent asyncio tasks from the UI.

What it teaches
  * ``app.async_adapter()``: async event callbacks that run on YOUR asyncio loop
  * awaitable document updates with ``adapter.rpc.call("document.command", ...)``
  * one asyncio task per job, progress updates, cancellation with ``task.cancel()``
  * ``asyncio.to_thread`` for synchronous SDK calls (never block the loop)
  * ``await adapter.run()`` waits for shutdown; remaining tasks are cancelled afterwards

Run:  uv run async_jobs.py      (or: uv run -m nativehtmlkit run async_jobs:amain)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import random

from nativehtmlkit import Application, NativeHTMLKitError

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; padding:18px 22px; font:14px sans-serif; background:#f3f5f9; color:#1f2430; }
  h1 { font-size:20px; margin:0 0 12px; }
  form { display:flex; gap:8px; margin-bottom:14px; }
  input { width:80px; padding:6px; }
  button { padding:6px 12px; border:1px solid #a9b2c3; border-radius:5px; background:#fff; cursor:pointer; }
  .job { background:#fff; border-radius:8px; padding:10px 12px; margin-bottom:8px; display:flex; gap:12px; align-items:center; }
  .job .name { width:70px; font-weight:bold; }
  .track { flex:1; height:8px; background:#e2e6ee; border-radius:4px; }
  .fill { height:8px; width:0%; background:#3b74e8; border-radius:4px; }
  .job.done .fill { background:#2f9e5b; } .job.cancelled .fill { background:#c4573a; }
  .state { width:90px; color:#5d6678; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <h1>Background jobs</h1>
  <form id="new-job"><label>Duration (s) <input id="seconds" type="number" min="1" max="30" value="4"></label>
    <button id="start" type="submit">Start job</button></form>
  <div id="jobs"></div>
  <p id="summary">No jobs yet.</p>
</body></html>"""


class JobRunner:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, window):
        self.app, self.window, self.document = app, window, window.document
        self.adapter = app.async_adapter()   # must be created inside the running loop
        self.tasks: dict[int, asyncio.Task] = {}
        self.states: dict[int, str] = {}
        self.next_id = 1
        self.adapter.on_document_event(self.document, "submit", self.on_submit, element="new-job")
        self.adapter.on_document_event(self.document, "click", self.on_click, element="jobs")

    async def command(self, op: str, **fields):
        """Awaitable Document.command(): the loop keeps running while the host answers."""
        return await self.adapter.rpc.call("document.command", {
            "window_id": self.window.id, "document_id": self.document.id,
            "command": {"op": op, **fields}})

    async def on_submit(self, _event: dict) -> None:
        seconds = (await self.command("get_value", element="seconds"))["value"]
        self.start_job(float(seconds) if seconds.replace(".", "", 1).isdigit() else 4.0)

    async def on_click(self, event: dict) -> None:
        parts = event["element"].split("-")          # "job-3-cancel"
        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[2] == "cancel" and parts[1].isdigit():
            task = self.tasks.get(int(parts[1]))
            if task and not task.done():
                task.cancel()

    def start_job(self, seconds: float) -> int:
        job_id, self.next_id = self.next_id, self.next_id + 1
        self.states[job_id] = "queued"
        self.tasks[job_id] = asyncio.create_task(self.run_job(job_id, seconds), name=f"job-{job_id}")
        return job_id

    async def run_job(self, job_id: int, seconds: float) -> None:
        await self.command("insert_html", element="jobs", position="beforeend", html=(
            f'<div class="job" id="job-{job_id}"><span class="name">Job {job_id}</span>'
            f'<div class="track"><div class="fill" id="job-{job_id}-fill"></div></div>'
            f'<span class="state" id="job-{job_id}-state">running</span>'
            f'<button id="job-{job_id}-cancel">Cancel</button></div>'))
        self.states[job_id] = "running"
        await self.summary()
        steps = 20
        try:
            for step in range(1, steps + 1):
                await asyncio.sleep(seconds / steps * random.uniform(0.6, 1.4))   # simulated work
                await self.command("set_attribute", element=f"job-{job_id}-fill", name="style",
                                   value=f"width:{step * 100 // steps}%")
            outcome = "done"
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            outcome = "cancelled"
        self.states[job_id] = outcome
        try:
            await self.command("batch", ops=[
                {"op": "add_class", "element": f"job-{job_id}", "name": outcome},
                {"op": "set_text", "element": f"job-{job_id}-state", "text": outcome},
                {"op": "remove_element", "element": f"job-{job_id}-cancel"}])
            await self.summary()
        except NativeHTMLKitError:
            pass                                   # the window is gone (application quitting)

    async def summary(self) -> None:
        counts = {s: list(self.states.values()).count(s) for s in ("running", "done", "cancelled")}
        await self.command("set_text", element="summary", text=", ".join(f"{n} {s}" for s, n in counts.items()))


async def amain(app: Application) -> None:
    window = await asyncio.to_thread(app.open_html, PAGE, title="Background jobs", width=620, height=480)
    runner = JobRunner(app, window)
    try:
        await runner.adapter.run()                 # until the window is closed / the app quits
    finally:
        for task in runner.tasks.values():
            task.cancel()


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Background jobs") as app:
        asyncio.run(amain(app))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Bulk rename: rename many files with find/replace, a live preview and undo.

This is the finished app of the tutorial docs/tutorials/bulk-rename.md.

What it teaches
  * an app split into index.html + style.css + app.py (``Application.open_file``)
  * a pure planning function that is easy to test without a window
  * live preview on ``input``/``change`` events of a whole form
  * the native folder picker with a capability check and an ``RpcError`` fallback
  * a confirmation ``<dialog>``, per-file error handling, and undo

Run:  uv run bulk_rename/app.py [FOLDER]
In regular-expression mode the replacement uses Python syntax: ``\\1`` or ``\\g<1>`` for groups.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import os
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Document, RpcError

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
WINDOWS = sys.platform == "win32"
INVALID_CHARACTERS = set('<>:"/\\|?*' + "".join(map(chr, range(32)))) if WINDOWS else {"/", "\0"}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- planning (no UI)

@dataclass
class Row:
    old: str
    new: str
    status: str = "unchanged"     # unchanged | rename | conflict | invalid | error
    note: str = ""


def plan_renames(names: list[str], find: str, replace: str, *, regex: bool, match_case: bool) -> list[Row]:
    """One row per file name; never touches the disk."""
    rows = [Row(name, name) for name in names]
    if not find:
        return rows
    try:
        pattern = re.compile(find if regex else re.escape(find), 0 if match_case else re.IGNORECASE)
        # Plain-text mode: the replacement is literal text (a function bypasses \1 processing).
        replacement = replace if regex else (lambda _match: replace)
        new_names = [pattern.sub(replacement, name) for name in names]
    except (re.error, IndexError) as error:          # bad pattern, or \3 with only two groups
        for row in rows:
            row.status, row.note = "error", f"Invalid pattern: {error}"
        return rows

    def key(name: str) -> str:                       # Windows file names are case-insensitive
        return name.casefold() if WINDOWS else name

    existing = {key(name) for name in names}
    claimed: set[str] = set()
    for row, new in zip(rows, new_names):
        row.new = new
        if new == row.old:
            continue
        if not new or new in (".", "..") or INVALID_CHARACTERS & set(new):
            row.status, row.note = "invalid", "Not a valid file name"
        elif (key(new) in existing and key(new) != key(row.old)) or key(new) in claimed:
            row.status, row.note = "conflict", "Name already used"
        else:
            row.status = "rename"
            claimed.add(key(new))
    return rows


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- the app

class BulkRename:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, window):
        self.app, self.window, self.document = app, window, window.document
        self.folder: Path | None = None
        self.names: list[str] = []
        self.plan: list[Row] = []
        self.undo_steps: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        doc = self.document
        # The top-level flag says whether the host offers native dialogs in this session.
        # (features["file_dialogs"]["available"] is None, "not observed", on a native desktop.)
        if not app.capabilities().get("file_dialogs"):
            doc.set_attribute("browse", "disabled", "")
        # Live preview: every keystroke or checkbox change in the rule form.
        doc.on("input", lambda _event: self.update_preview(), element="rule")
        doc.on("change", lambda _event: self.update_preview(), element="rule")
        # Enter in a rule field submits the form: treat it as "update preview", nothing else.
        doc.on("submit", lambda _event: self.update_preview(), element="rule")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.open_folder(doc.get_value("folder")), element="load")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.browse(), element="browse")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.ask_confirmation(), element="apply")
        # Decide in the button handlers, not in the dialog's close event: a <dialog> keeps its
        # previous return value when the user dismisses it with Escape.
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.confirm(False), element="confirm-no")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.confirm(True), element="confirm-yes")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.undo(), element="undo")

    def set_summary(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.document.set_text("summary", text)

    def set_enabled(self, element: str, enabled: bool) -> None:
        if enabled:
            self.document.remove_attribute(element, "disabled")
        else:
            self.document.set_attribute(element, "disabled", "")

    def update_preview(self) -> None:
        doc = self.document
        self.plan = plan_renames(self.names, doc.get_value("find"), doc.get_value("replace"),
                                 regex=doc.get_checked("regex"), match_case=doc.get_checked("case"))
        # File names are untrusted text: escape every cell. The status class comes from a fixed set.
        cells = "".join(f'<tr class="{row.status}"><td>{html.escape(row.old)}</td><td>{html.escape(row.new)}</td>'
                        f'<td>{html.escape(row.note or row.status)}</td></tr>' for row in self.plan)
        count = sum(row.status == "rename" for row in self.plan)
        blocked = sum(row.status in ("conflict", "invalid", "error") for row in self.plan)
        summary = f"{len(self.names)} file(s), {count} to rename" + (f", {blocked} skipped" if blocked else "")
        doc.batch([
            {"op": "replace_children_html", "element": "preview", "html": cells},
            {"op": "set_text", "element": "summary", "text": summary},
            {"op": "set_text", "element": "apply", "text": f"Rename {count}"},
        ])
        self.set_enabled("apply", count > 0)

    def update_file_list(self) -> None:
        self.names = sorted(entry.name for entry in self.folder.iterdir() if entry.is_file())
        self.update_preview()

    def open_folder(self, path: str) -> None:
        if not path or not Path(path).is_dir():
            self.set_summary("That folder does not exist.")
            return
        self.folder = Path(path).resolve()
        self.document.set_value("folder", str(self.folder))
        self.set_undo([])
        self.update_file_list()

    def browse(self) -> None:
        def done(future) -> None:
            try:
                result = future.result()
            except RpcError as error:        # -32001: no dialog service in this session
                self.set_summary("Native file dialogs are not available in this session."
                                 if error.code == -32001 else f"The folder dialog failed (error {error.code}).")
                return
            if not result["cancelled"]:
                self.open_folder(result["paths"][0])
        # wait=False keeps the event thread free while the dialog is open.
        self.window.choose_folder(title="Folder with files to rename", wait=False).add_done_callback(done)

    def set_undo(self, steps: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
        self.undo_steps = steps
        self.set_enabled("undo", bool(steps))

    def ask_confirmation(self) -> None:
        count = sum(row.status == "rename" for row in self.plan)
        self.document.set_text("confirm-text", f"Rename {count} file(s) in {self.folder}?")
        self.document.show_dialog("confirm")

    def confirm(self, yes: bool) -> None:
        self.document.close_dialog("confirm", "")
        if yes:
            self.rename()

    def rename(self) -> None:
        done, failed = [], 0
        for row in (r for r in self.plan if r.status == "rename"):
            source, target = self.folder / row.old, self.folder / row.new
            try:
                # os.rename silently replaces an existing file on Linux: refuse that ourselves.
                if target.exists() and not (WINDOWS and row.old.casefold() == row.new.casefold()):
                    raise FileExistsError(target)
                os.rename(source, target)
                done.append((row.old, row.new))
            except OSError:                   # in use, permission denied, or changed since the preview
                failed += 1
        self.set_undo(done)
        self.update_file_list()
        message = f"Renamed {len(done)} file(s)."
        if failed:
            message += f" {failed} failed (in use, permission denied or changed)."
        self.set_summary(message)

    def undo(self) -> None:
        if not self.undo_steps:
            return
        restored = 0
        # Reverse order, so chains such as a->b, b->c are undone correctly.
        for old, new in reversed(self.undo_steps):
            try:
                os.rename(self.folder / new, self.folder / old)
                restored += 1
            except OSError:
                pass
        self.set_undo([])
        self.update_file_list()
        self.set_summary(f"Restored {restored} file name(s).")


def build(app: Application, folder: str | None = None) -> BulkRename:
    # Relative URLs in index.html (style.css) resolve against the file's folder.
    window = app.open_file(HERE / "index.html", title="Bulk rename", width=900, height=620,
                           min_width=640, min_height=400)
    tool = BulkRename(app, window)
    if folder:
        tool.open_folder(folder)
    return tool


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Bulk rename") as app:
        build(app, sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Folder checksums: hash every file of a folder on a worker thread, with progress and cancel.

What it teaches
  * keeping slow work OFF the event callback: callbacks run one at a time, so a long job
    there would delay every later event; a worker thread keeps the window responsive
  * updating the document from the worker (the SDK is thread-safe), throttled to a few
    updates per second
  * cancelling cooperatively with ``threading.Event``
  * ``on_before_quit``: ask before quitting while a job is running
  * file names are untrusted text: escaped with ``html.escape``

Run:  uv run checksum.py [FOLDER]      (default: the current directory)
Type or browse to a folder, then press Start.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import sys
import html
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application, NativeHTMLKitError, RpcError, Window

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; padding:16px 20px; font:14px sans-serif; background:#f5f6f9; color:#1d2230; }
  h1 { font-size:20px; margin:0 0 10px; }
  form { display:flex; gap:8px; }
  input[type=text] { flex:1; padding:7px; font-family:monospace; }
  button { padding:6px 12px; }
  .progress { height:8px; background:#e0e4ec; border-radius:4px; margin:12px 0 6px; }
  #bar { height:8px; width:0%; background:#3b74e8; border-radius:4px; }
  #warning { display:none; background:#fff0c9; padding:8px 12px; border-radius:6px; }
  #warning.shown { display:block; }
  table { width:100%; border-collapse:collapse; background:#fff; font-size:12px; }
  td { padding:4px 8px; border-bottom:1px solid #e6e8ee; font-family:monospace; }
  td.size { text-align:right; color:#5f6879; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <h1>Folder checksums (SHA-256)</h1>
  <form id="job"><input id="folder" type="text" placeholder="Folder path" required>
    <button id="browse" type="button">Browse…</button>
    <button id="start" type="submit">Start</button><button id="cancel" type="button">Cancel</button></form>
  <div class="progress"><div id="bar"></div></div>
  <p id="status">Idle.</p>
  <p id="warning">A job is still running. Cancel it, or quit again to stop it.</p>
  <table><tbody id="results"></tbody></table>
</body></html>"""


def sha256(path: Path, cancel: threading.Event) -> str | None:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            if cancel.is_set():
                return None
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


class ChecksumApp:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, window: Window):
        self.app, self.window, self.document = app, window, window.document
        self.cancel = threading.Event()
        self.worker: threading.Thread | None = None
        self.results: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.quit_warned = False
        doc = self.document
        doc.on("submit", lambda _e: self.start(Path(doc.get_value("folder").strip())), element="job")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.cancel.set(), element="cancel")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.browse(), element="browse")
        app.on_before_quit(self.may_quit)
        app.on_shutdown(self.cancel.set)

    @property
    def busy(self) -> bool:
        return self.worker is not None and self.worker.is_alive()

    def browse(self) -> None:
        def done(future):
            try:
                result = future.result()
            except RpcError as error:
                self.status(f"Folder dialog unavailable (code {error.code}); type a path instead.")
                return
            if not result["cancelled"] and result["paths"]:
                self.document.set_value("folder", result["paths"][0])
        self.window.choose_folder(title="Choose a folder to hash", wait=False).add_done_callback(done)

    def start(self, folder: Path) -> threading.Thread | None:
        if self.busy:
            self.status("A job is already running.")
            return None
        if not folder.is_dir():
            self.status(f"Not a folder: {folder}")
            return None
        self.cancel.clear()
        self.results.clear()
        self.quit_warned = False
        self.document.replace_html("results", "")
        self.worker = threading.Thread(target=self._run, args=(folder,), name="checksum-worker", daemon=True)
        self.worker.start()
        return self.worker

    def _run(self, folder: Path) -> None:
        files = sorted(p for p in folder.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
        pending_rows: list[str] = []
        last_update = 0.0
        try:
            for index, path in enumerate(files, 1):
                try:
                    digest = sha256(path, self.cancel)
                except OSError as error:
                    digest = f"unreadable ({error.strerror})"
                if digest is None:
                    break                                   # cancelled
                name = path.relative_to(folder).as_posix()
                self.results[name] = digest
                pending_rows.append(f"<tr><td>{html.escape(digest)}</td><td>{html.escape(name)}</td>"
                                    f'<td class="size">{path.stat().st_size:,}</td></tr>')
                now = time.monotonic()
                if now - last_update > 0.2 or index == len(files):   # throttle UI updates
                    self._flush(pending_rows, index, len(files))
                    pending_rows, last_update = [], now
            self._flush(pending_rows, len(self.results), len(files))
            word = "Cancelled after" if self.cancel.is_set() else "Done:"
            self.status(f"{word} {len(self.results)} of {len(files)} file(s).")
            self.document.remove_class("warning", "shown")
        except NativeHTMLKitError:
            return                                          # window closed while hashing

    def _flush(self, rows: list[str], done: int, total: int) -> None:
        operations = [{"op": "set_attribute", "element": "bar", "name": "style",
                       "value": f"width:{done * 100 // max(total, 1)}%"},
                      {"op": "set_text", "element": "status", "text": f"Hashing… {done}/{total}"}]
        if rows:
            operations.insert(0, {"op": "insert_html", "element": "results", "position": "beforeend",
                                  "html": "".join(rows)})
        self.document.batch(operations)

    def may_quit(self) -> bool:
        """Answer the host's quit request. Runs on an SDK worker; must return promptly."""
        if self.busy and not self.quit_warned:
            self.quit_warned = True
            self.document.add_class("warning", "shown")
            return False                                    # keep running; a second quit is allowed
        self.cancel.set()
        return True

    def status(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.document.set_text("status", text)


def build(app: Application) -> ChecksumApp:
    return ChecksumApp(app, app.open_html(PAGE, title="Checksums", width=760, height=560))


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Checksums") as app:
        checksum = build(app)
        checksum.document.set_value("folder", sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else str(Path.cwd()))
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Clipboard tool: transform text and move it through the system clipboard.

What it teaches
  * ``Application.clipboard_text`` / ``set_clipboard_text`` (plain text only)
  * the ``link_activated`` event and ``Application.open_external`` to open a link in the browser
  * ``desktop_preferences`` / ``on_desktop_preferences`` and ``capabilities``
  * checking capabilities and handling RpcError -32001 ("unsupported here") gracefully
  * one delegated click handler for a toolbar of buttons
  * ``get_value`` / ``set_value`` and the UTF-16 based ``control_selection`` offsets

Run:  uv run text_toolbox.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

from nativehtmlkit import Application, RpcError, Window

DOCS_URL = "https://github.com/nativehtmlkit/nativehtmlkit-python"


def _sorted_lines(text: str) -> str:
    return "\n".join(sorted(text.splitlines(), key=str.casefold))


def _unique_lines(text: str) -> str:
    return "\n".join(dict.fromkeys(text.splitlines()))


def _pretty_json(text: str) -> str:
    return json.dumps(json.loads(text), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)


TRANSFORMS = {
    "upper": str.upper, "lower": str.lower, "title": str.title,
    "trim": lambda t: "\n".join(line.strip() for line in t.splitlines()),
    "sort": _sorted_lines, "unique": _unique_lines, "json": _pretty_json,
}

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; padding:16px 20px; font:14px sans-serif; background:#f7f7fa; color:#22252d; }
  h1 { font-size:20px; margin:0 0 10px; }
  .toolbar { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:6px; margin-bottom:8px; }
  button { padding:6px 10px; border:1px solid #b9bfcc; border-radius:5px; background:#fff; cursor:pointer; }
  button.primary { background:#2d6be0; color:#fff; border-color:#2d6be0; }
  textarea { width:100%; height:260px; box-sizing:border-box; padding:10px; font:13px monospace; }
  footer { display:flex; justify-content:space-between; color:#61697a; margin-top:8px; }
  a { color:#2d6be0; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <h1>Clipboard tool</h1>
  <div class="toolbar" id="toolbar">
    <button id="t-upper">UPPER</button><button id="t-lower">lower</button><button id="t-title">Title</button>
    <button id="t-trim">Trim lines</button><button id="t-sort">Sort lines</button>
    <button id="t-unique">Unique lines</button><button id="t-json">Format JSON</button>
    <button id="paste" class="primary">Paste</button><button id="copy" class="primary">Copy</button>
  </div>
  <textarea id="text" spellcheck="false">  banana
Apple
cherry
apple
  {"name": "NativeHTMLKit", "native": true}</textarea>
  <footer><span id="stats"></span><span id="status"></span></footer>
  <p>Theme reported by the desktop: <b id="scheme">unknown</b> ·
     <a id="docs" href="https://github.com/nativehtmlkit/nativehtmlkit-python">Open the SDK documentation</a></p>
</body></html>"""


class Toolbox:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, window: Window):
        self.app, self.window, self.document = app, window, window.document
        features = app.capabilities().get("features", {})
        # "available" is True/False once observed and None when not known yet.
        self.clipboard_known_unavailable = features.get("clipboard_text", {}).get("available") is False
        doc = self.document
        doc.on("click", self._on_toolbar, element="toolbar")
        # Links never navigate the document: activating one sends a "link_activated" event
        # (with "href" and the resolved "url") and the application decides what to do.
        doc.on("link_activated", lambda event: self.open_link(event.get("url") or DOCS_URL))
        doc.on("input", lambda _e: self.update_stats(), element="text")
        self.show_preferences(app.desktop_preferences())
        app.on_desktop_preferences(self.show_preferences)   # live updates when the desktop changes
        self.update_stats()

    def transform(self, name: str) -> None:
        text = self.document.get_value("text")
        try:
            self.document.set_value("text", TRANSFORMS[name](text))
            self.status(f"Applied “{name}”.")
        except ValueError as error:                         # e.g. invalid JSON
            self.status(f"Cannot apply “{name}”: {error}")
        self.update_stats()

    def copy(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.app.set_clipboard_text(self.document.get_value("text"))
            self.status("Copied to the clipboard.")
        except RpcError as error:
            self.status(self._unsupported("Clipboard", error))

    def paste(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.document.set_value("text", self.app.clipboard_text())
            self.status("Pasted from the clipboard.")
        except RpcError as error:
            self.status(self._unsupported("Clipboard", error))
        self.update_stats()

    def open_link(self, url: str) -> None:
        if not url.startswith("https://"):
            self.status("Only https links are opened.")
            return
        try:
            result = self.app.open_external(url, window=self.window)
            self.status("Opened the documentation." if result.get("accepted") else "Opening was cancelled.")
        except RpcError as error:
            self.status(self._unsupported("Opening links", error))

    def update_stats(self) -> None:
        text = self.document.get_value("text")
        selection = self.document.control_selection("text")    # offsets are UTF-16 code units
        self.document.set_text("stats", f"{len(text)} characters · {len(text.split())} words · "
                                        f"{len(text.splitlines())} lines · cursor at {selection['start']}")

    def show_preferences(self, preferences: dict) -> None:
        self.document.set_text("scheme", preferences.get("color_scheme") or "unknown")

    def status(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.document.set_text("status", text)

    def _unsupported(self, what: str, error: RpcError) -> str:
        if error.code == -32001 or self.clipboard_known_unavailable:
            return f"{what} is not available in this session."
        return f"{what} failed (code {error.code})."

    def _on_toolbar(self, event: dict) -> None:
        element = event["element"]
        if element.startswith("t-"):
            self.transform(element[2:])
        elif element == "copy":
            self.copy()
        elif element == "paste":
            self.paste()


def build(app: Application) -> Toolbox:
    return Toolbox(app, app.open_html(PAGE, title="Clipboard tool", width=720, height=560))


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Clipboard tool") as app:
        build(app)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

View on GitHub

"""Counter: a counter with a step selector, limits and a change history.

What it teaches
  * application state in one object that every callback shares
  * one click handler for several buttons (event delegation: ``event["element"]`` is the id of
    the clicked button)
  * reading a ``<select>`` with ``get_value``
  * atomic multi-element updates with ``Document.batch`` (one host transaction)
  * a bounded list: ``insert_html`` at the top plus ``trim_children``

Run:  uv run counter.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Document

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 28px; }
  #value { font-size: 56px; font-weight: 600; margin: 8px 0 16px; }
  #value.negative { color: #b3261e; }
  #value.at-limit { text-decoration: underline; }
  .row { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; }
  button { min-width: 44px; padding: 6px 12px; font-size: 16px; }
  #history { color: #555; font-size: 13px; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <div id="value" aria-live="polite">0</div>
  <div class="row" id="buttons">
    <button id="dec" aria-label="Decrease">-</button>
    <button id="inc" aria-label="Increase">+</button>
    <button id="reset">Reset</button>
    <label for="step">Step</label>
    <select id="step"><option>1</option><option>5</option><option>10</option></select>
  </div>
  <p id="limits">Range -50 to 50.</p>
  <ol id="history" reversed></ol>
</body></html>"""

MINIMUM, MAXIMUM, HISTORY = -50, 50, 8


class Counter:
    def __init__(self, document: Document):
        self.document = document
        self.count = 0
        # One handler on the button row: event["element"] is the id of the clicked element.
        document.on("click", self.on_click, element="buttons")

    def step(self) -> int:
        return int(self.document.get_value("step"))

    def set_count(self, value: int, reason: str) -> None:
        value = max(MINIMUM, min(MAXIMUM, value))
        self.count = value
        # One transaction: the value, its classes and the history entry change together.
        self.document.batch([
            {"op": "set_text", "element": "value", "text": str(value)},
            {"op": "add_class" if value < 0 else "remove_class", "element": "value", "name": "negative"},
            {"op": "add_class" if value in (MINIMUM, MAXIMUM) else "remove_class", "element": "value",
             "name": "at-limit"},
            {"op": "insert_html", "element": "history", "position": "afterbegin",
             "html": f"<li>{html.escape(f'{reason} -> {value}')}</li>"},
            {"op": "trim_children", "element": "history", "keep": HISTORY, "from": "end"},
        ])

    def on_click(self, event: dict) -> None:
        step = self.step()
        if event["element"] == "inc":
            self.set_count(self.count + step, f"+{step}")
        elif event["element"] == "dec":
            self.set_count(self.count - step, f"-{step}")
        elif event["element"] == "reset":
            self.set_count(0, "reset")


def build(app: Application) -> Counter:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Counter", width=460, height=420, min_width=360, min_height=320)
    return Counter(window.document)


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Counter") as app:
        build(app)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Data table: search, sort, page through and inspect a list of records.

What it teaches
  * re-rendering a region with ``replace_html`` built from escaped data
  * live search with the ``input`` event (the event carries the control's current ``value``)
  * a ``<select>`` ``change`` event, sortable column headers and pagination buttons
  * a details pane updated with ``set_text`` (always plain text)
  * splitting state (Python) from presentation (HTML/CSS)

Run:  uv run data_table.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import random

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Window

COLUMNS = [("sku", "SKU"), ("name", "Product"), ("category", "Category"), ("stock", "Stock"), ("price", "Price")]


def sample_inventory(count: int = 240, seed: int = 7) -> list[dict]:
    rng = random.Random(seed)          # deterministic: the same rows on every start
    adjectives = ["Compact", "Deluxe", "Eco", "Heavy-duty", "Mini", "Smart", "Travel", "Ultra"]
    things = {"Kitchen": ["kettle", "blender", "toaster"], "Office": ["stapler", "lamp", "chair"],
              "Garden": ["hose", "rake", "planter"], "Audio": ["speaker", "headset", "radio"]}
    rows = []
    for n in range(1, count + 1):
        category = rng.choice(sorted(things))
        rows.append({"sku": f"SKU-{n:04d}", "name": f"{rng.choice(adjectives)} {rng.choice(things[category])}",
                     "category": category, "stock": rng.randint(0, 500), "price": round(rng.uniform(3, 400), 2)})
    return rows


PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; font:13px sans-serif; background:#f4f5f8; color:#1e2330; display:flex; height:100vh; }
  .main { flex:1; display:flex; flex-direction:column; padding:14px 16px; min-width:0; }
  .tools { display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:center; margin-bottom:10px; }
  input[type=search] { flex:1; padding:7px; border:1px solid #c3c9d6; border-radius:5px; }
  .scroll { flex:1; overflow:auto; background:#fff; border-radius:6px; }
  table { width:100%; border-collapse:collapse; }
  th { position:sticky; top:0; background:#e9ecf2; text-align:left; padding:7px 8px; cursor:pointer; }
  th.sorted-asc::after { content:" ▲"; } th.sorted-desc::after { content:" ▼"; }
  td { padding:6px 8px; border-bottom:1px solid #eceef3; }
  td.num { text-align:right; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; }
  tr.low td { color:#b03a2e; }
  tr.selected td { background:#dce7fd; }
  .pager { display:flex; gap:8px; align-items:center; margin-top:8px; }
  button { padding:4px 10px; }
  aside { width:240px; padding:16px; background:#fff; border-left:1px solid #dde1e8; }
  aside dt { color:#6a7284; margin-top:8px; } aside dd { margin:2px 0 0; font-weight:bold; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <div class="main">
    <div class="tools">
      <input id="search" type="search" placeholder="Search name, SKU or category">
      <label>Category <select id="category"><option value="">All</option>
        <option>Audio</option><option>Garden</option><option>Kitchen</option><option>Office</option></select></label>
    </div>
    <div class="scroll"><table>
      <thead><tr id="headers">%HEADERS%</tr></thead><tbody id="rows"></tbody></table></div>
    <div class="pager"><button id="prev">‹ Previous</button><span id="page">-</span>
      <button id="next">Next ›</button><span id="matches"></span></div>
  </div>
  <aside><h2>Details</h2><dl>
    <dt>SKU</dt><dd id="d-sku">-</dd><dt>Product</dt><dd id="d-name">-</dd>
    <dt>Category</dt><dd id="d-category">-</dd><dt>Stock</dt><dd id="d-stock">-</dd><dt>Price</dt><dd id="d-price">-</dd>
  </dl></aside>
</body></html>""".replace("%HEADERS%", "".join(f'<th id="col-{key}">{label}</th>' for key, label in COLUMNS))


class DataTable:
    PAGE_SIZE = 25

    def __init__(self, window: Window, records: list[dict]):
        self.document = doc = window.document
        self.records = records
        self.query, self.category = "", ""
        self.sort_key, self.descending = "sku", False
        self.page = 0
        self.selected: str | None = None
        doc.on("input", lambda e: self.set_query(e.get("value", "")), element="search")
        doc.on("change", lambda e: self.set_category(e.get("value", "")), element="category")
        doc.on("click", self._on_header, element="headers")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.go(-1), element="prev")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.go(+1), element="next")
        doc.on("click", self._on_row, element="rows")
        self.render()

    def visible(self) -> list[dict]:
        needle = self.query.casefold()
        rows = [r for r in self.records
                if (not self.category or r["category"] == self.category)
                and (not needle or any(needle in str(r[k]).casefold() for k in ("sku", "name", "category")))]
        return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r[self.sort_key], reverse=self.descending)

    def set_query(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.query, self.page = text.strip(), 0
        self.render()

    def set_category(self, category: str) -> None:
        self.category, self.page = category, 0
        self.render()

    def sort_by(self, key: str) -> None:
        self.descending = not self.descending if key == self.sort_key else False
        self.sort_key, self.page = key, 0
        self.render()

    def go(self, delta: int) -> None:
        self.page += delta
        self.render()

    def select(self, sku: str) -> None:
        record = next(r for r in self.records if r["sku"] == sku)
        self.selected = sku
        for key, _label in COLUMNS:
            self.document.set_text(f"d-{key}", str(record[key]))
        self.render()

    def render(self) -> None:
        rows = self.visible()
        pages = max(1, -(-len(rows) // self.PAGE_SIZE))
        self.page = max(0, min(self.page, pages - 1))
        start = self.page * self.PAGE_SIZE
        body = []
        for r in rows[start:start + self.PAGE_SIZE]:
            classes = " ".join(c for c, on in (("low", r["stock"] < 20), ("selected", r["sku"] == self.selected)) if on)
            sku = html.escape(r["sku"])
            body.append(f'<tr id="row-{sku}" class="{classes}"><td>{sku}</td><td>{html.escape(r["name"])}</td>'
                        f'<td>{html.escape(r["category"])}</td><td class="num">{r["stock"]}</td>'
                        f'<td class="num">{r["price"]:.2f}</td></tr>')
        # One batch = one round trip and one atomic document update (all or nothing).
        ops = [{"op": "replace_children_html", "element": "rows",
                "html": "".join(body) or '<tr><td colspan="5">No matching records.</td></tr>'}]
        for key, _label in COLUMNS:
            ops += [{"op": "remove_class", "element": f"col-{key}", "name": "sorted-asc"},
                    {"op": "remove_class", "element": f"col-{key}", "name": "sorted-desc"}]
        ops += [{"op": "add_class", "element": f"col-{self.sort_key}",
                 "name": "sorted-desc" if self.descending else "sorted-asc"},
                {"op": "set_text", "element": "page", "text": f"Page {self.page + 1} of {pages}"},
                {"op": "set_text", "element": "matches", "text": f"{len(rows)} of {len(self.records)} records"}]
        self.document.batch(ops)

    def _on_header(self, event: dict) -> None:
        if event["element"].startswith("col-"):
            self.sort_by(event["element"][4:])

    def _on_row(self, event: dict) -> None:
        # A click on a <td> (no id) reports the nearest identified ancestor: the row.
        if event["element"].startswith("row-"):
            self.select(event["element"][4:])


def build(app: Application, records: list[dict] | None = None) -> DataTable:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Inventory", width=980, height=640)
    return DataTable(window, sample_inventory() if records is None else records)


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Inventory") as app:
        build(app)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Diagnostics: an "About / Support" window with capabilities, counters and a support bundle.

What it teaches
  * ``Application.capabilities()`` for feature detection: the top-level flags say which APIs the
    host offers; ``features[name]["available"]`` is True/False when observed and None otherwise
  * ``Application.desktop_preferences()`` (colour scheme, reduced motion, high contrast)
  * ``Application.host_diagnostics()`` and the SDK recorder (``nativehtmlkit.diagnostics``):
    loss and failure counters
  * ``Document.diagnostics()`` (CSS/resource notes for one document)
  * ``export_support_bundle`` (a local, redacted ZIP; nothing is uploaded)

Run:  uv run diagnostics.py [OUTPUT_FOLDER]      (default: the temporary folder)
Tip:  set NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS=trace (or run ``uv run nativehtmlkit-python --diagnostics trace ...``)
      to record callback and request timing in the bundle.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import platform
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path

import nativehtmlkit
from nativehtmlkit import Application, Document, diagnostics, export_support_bundle

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 18px; font-size: 14px; }
  h2 { font-size: 16px; margin: 18px 0 6px; }
  table { border-collapse: collapse; }
  td, th { text-align: left; padding: 2px 12px 2px 0; vertical-align: top; }
  td.yes { color: #2e7d32; } td.no { color: #8a1c1c; }
  #bundle { font-family: monospace; font-size: 12px; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <h2>Host</h2><table id="host"></table>
  <h2>Features</h2><table id="features"></table>
  <h2>Desktop preferences</h2><table id="prefs"></table>
  <h2>Connection counters</h2><table id="counters"></table>
  <h2>Support</h2>
  <p><button id="refresh">Refresh</button> <button id="export">Save support bundle</button></p>
  <p id="bundle" role="status"></p>
</body></html>"""

# Top-level capability flag -> its entry in capabilities()["features"] (the host names drops differently).
FEATURES = {"clipboard_text": "clipboard_text", "file_dialogs": "file_dialogs", "external_open": "external_open",
            "drag_drop": "incoming_drop", "ime": "ime", "accessibility": "accessibility"}


def feature_state(caps: dict, flag: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """(text, usable) for one feature.

    The top-level flag says whether the host offers the API in this session. The feature entry's
    ``available`` is True/False when the host has observed the native service and None ("not
    observed") otherwise; on a native desktop Core 1.0.3 reports None for these services.
    None is not False.
    """
    if not caps.get(flag):
        return "not available", False
    available = caps.get("features", {}).get(FEATURES[flag], {}).get("available")
    if available is None:
        return "enabled (not observed)", True
    return ("available", True) if available else ("unavailable", False)


def rows(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> str:
    """Values from the host are data: always escaped, never trusted as markup."""
    out = []
    for name, value in pairs:
        css = (' class="yes"' if value else ' class="no"') if isinstance(value, bool) else ""
        text = "unknown" if value is None else str(value)
        out.append(f"<tr><th>{html.escape(name)}</th><td{css}>{html.escape(text)}</td></tr>")
    return "".join(out)


class SupportWindow:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, document: Document, output: Path):
        self.app, self.document, self.output = app, document, output
        document.on("click", lambda _event: self.refresh(), element="refresh")
        document.on("click", lambda _event: self.export(), element="export")
        self.refresh()

    def refresh(self) -> dict:
        caps = self.app.capabilities()
        prefs = self.app.desktop_preferences()
        host = self.app.host_diagnostics()
        recorder = diagnostics.recorder()
        summary = recorder.summary()
        failures = sum(1 for r in recorder.history() if r.get("event") == "callback.failed")
        counters = {
            "Host dropped notifications": host.get("dropped_notifications"),
            "SDK dropped notifications": self.app.rpc.dropped_notifications,
            "Pending host jobs": host.get("pending_jobs"),
            "Callback failures": failures,
            "SDK records (dropped)": f"{summary['records']} ({summary['dropped']})",
            "Document diagnostics": len(self.document.diagnostics().get("diagnostics", [])),
        }
        self.document.batch([
            {"op": "replace_children_html", "element": "host", "html": rows([
                ("Platform", caps.get("platform")), ("Native session", caps.get("native")),
                ("Headless", caps.get("headless")), ("Renderer", caps.get("renderer")),
                ("CSS profile", caps.get("css_profile")), ("Max windows", caps.get("max_windows")),
                ("Python", f"{platform.python_implementation()} {platform.python_version()}"),
                ("SDK", nativehtmlkit.__version__)])},
            {"op": "replace_children_html", "element": "features", "html": "".join(
                f'<tr><th>{html.escape(flag)}</th><td class="{"yes" if usable else "no"}">{html.escape(text)}</td></tr>'
                for flag, (text, usable) in ((flag, feature_state(caps, flag)) for flag in FEATURES))},
            {"op": "replace_children_html", "element": "prefs", "html": rows([
                ("Source", prefs.get("source")), ("Colour scheme", prefs.get("color_scheme")),
                ("Reduced motion", prefs.get("reduced_motion")), ("High contrast", prefs.get("high_contrast"))])},
            {"op": "replace_children_html", "element": "counters", "html": rows(list(counters.items()))},
        ])
        return counters

    def export(self) -> Path | None:
        target = self.output / f"nativehtmlkit-support-{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}.zip"
        try:
            path = export_support_bundle(target, overwrite=True)
        except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
            self.document.set_text("bundle", f"Could not save the bundle: {error}")
            return None
        self.document.set_text("bundle", f"Saved {path} ({path.stat().st_size} bytes). Attach it to a bug report.")
        return path


def build(app: Application, output: Path) -> SupportWindow:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="About and support", width=760, height=640)
    return SupportWindow(app, window.document, output)


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Diagnostics") as app:
        output = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path(tempfile.gettempdir())
        build(app, output)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.text:
View on GitHub

"""DOM explorer: browse the live element tree and edit nodes that have no HTML id.

What it teaches
  * ``Document.node()`` / ``query_nodes()``: opaque node references, also for elements without an id
  * ``Node.inspect()`` and ``Node.children()`` (paginated) to walk the tree
  * ``Node`` mutations: ``add_class``, ``set_text``, ``move_to`` and ``remove``
  * node references belong to ONE document generation: after a reload they are stale

Run:  uv run dom_explorer.py
Click a node in the tree on the left; the matching element in the sample is highlighted.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html

from nativehtmlkit import Application, NativeHTMLKitError, Node, Window

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; font:13px sans-serif; display:flex; height:100vh; color:#1d2230; }
  #tree { width:320px; overflow:auto; background:#f3f4f8; border-right:1px solid #d9dde6; padding:8px 0; font-family:monospace; }
  .item { padding:2px 8px; cursor:pointer; white-space:nowrap; }
  .item:hover { background:#e1e8fa; } .item.current { background:#c9d8fb; }
  .tag { color:#7c3aa8; } .attr { color:#9a6a00; } .text { color:#4a7a2a; }
  .right { flex:1; display:flex; flex-direction:column; }
  .tools { padding:8px 12px; display:flex; gap:6px; border-bottom:1px solid #d9dde6; align-items:center; }
  #info { color:#5c6577; margin-left:8px; font-family:monospace; }
  #sample { padding:16px 20px; overflow:auto; }
  .highlight { outline:2px solid #e8590c; background:#fff4e6; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <div id="tree"></div>
  <div class="right">
    <div class="tools"><button id="up">Move up</button><button id="shout">UPPERCASE text</button>
      <button id="delete">Delete</button><button id="reset">Reset sample</button><span id="info">Nothing selected</span></div>
    <div id="sample"></div>
  </div>
</body></html>"""

SAMPLE = """<article><h2>Release notes</h2>
<p>Elements in this sample have <em>no</em> id attributes.</p>
<ul><li>Faster layout</li><li>Smaller binaries</li><li>Better <code>dialog</code> support</li></ul>
<blockquote>Node references work without ids.</blockquote></article>"""


class Explorer:
    def __init__(self, window: Window):
        self.document = doc = window.document
        self.items: list[Node] = []          # tree row index -> node reference
        self.current: Node | None = None
        doc.on("click", self._on_tree_click, element="tree")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.move_up(), element="up")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.uppercase(), element="shout")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.delete(), element="delete")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.reset(), element="reset")
        self.reset()

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.document.replace_html("sample", SAMPLE)
        self.current = None
        self.document.set_text("info", "Nothing selected")
        self.refresh()

    def refresh(self) -> None:
        """Walk the sample subtree with Node.children() and render one row per node."""
        self.items, rows = [], []

        def walk(node: Node, depth: int) -> None:
            listing = node.children(limit=256)
            for child in listing["children"]:
                ref = self.document.node(reference=child["node"])
                info = ref.inspect()
                if info["type"] == "text":
                    text = info.get("text", "").strip()      # text nodes report their text
                    if not text:
                        continue                              # skip whitespace between tags
                    label = f'<span class="text">"{html.escape(text[:40])}"</span>'
                elif info["type"] == "element":
                    attrs = "".join(f' <span class="attr">{html.escape(k)}="{html.escape(v)}"</span>'
                                    for k, v in info.get("attributes", {}).items())
                    label = f'<span class="tag"><{html.escape(info["name"])}></span>{attrs}'
                else:
                    continue
                current = " current" if self.current and self.current.id == ref.id else ""
                rows.append(f'<div id="item-{len(self.items)}" class="item{current}" '
                            f'style="padding-left:{8 + depth * 14}px">{label}</div>')
                self.items.append(ref)
                if info["type"] == "element":
                    walk(ref, depth + 1)

        walk(self.document.node("sample"), 0)
        self.document.replace_html("tree", "".join(rows))

    def select(self, index: int) -> None:
        if self.current is not None:
            try:
                self.current.remove_class("highlight")
            except NativeHTMLKitError:
                pass                          # the previous node may have been deleted
        self.current = self.items[index]
        info = self.current.inspect()
        if info["type"] == "element":
            self.current.add_class("highlight")
        self.document.set_text("info", f"{info.get('name') or info['type']} · {info['node']}")
        self.refresh()

    def move_up(self) -> None:
        if self.current is None:
            return
        previous = self.current.inspect().get("previous")
        # Skip whitespace text nodes; move before the previous ELEMENT sibling.
        while previous and self.document.node(reference=previous).inspect()["type"] != "element":
            previous = self.document.node(reference=previous).inspect().get("previous")
        if previous:
            self.current.move_to(self.document.node(reference=previous), position="beforebegin")
            self.refresh()

    def uppercase(self) -> None:
        """Uppercase an element whose only child is text (set_text replaces ALL children)."""
        if self.current is None or self.current.inspect()["type"] != "element":
            return
        children = self.current.children()["children"]
        if len(children) == 1 and children[0]["type"] == "text":
            text = self.document.node(reference=children[0]["node"]).inspect()["text"]
            self.current.set_text(text.upper())
            self.refresh()

    def delete(self) -> None:
        if self.current is not None:
            self.current.remove()
            self.current = None
            self.document.set_text("info", "Deleted")
            self.refresh()

    def _on_tree_click(self, event: dict) -> None:
        element = event["element"]
        if element.startswith("item-") and element[5:].isdigit():
            self.select(int(element[5:]))


def build(app: Application) -> Explorer:
    return Explorer(app.open_html(PAGE, title="DOM explorer", width=900, height=560))


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="DOM explorer") as app:
        build(app)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
