items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Text file viewer and editor with native Open, Save As and Choose Folder dialogs.

What it teaches
  * ``Window.open_files`` / ``save_file`` / ``choose_folder`` with filters and a start directory
  * ``wait=False``: the dialog returns a Future, so the event callback returns at once and other
    events keep flowing while the dialog is open; the result arrives in a done-callback
  * the dialog result shape ``{"cancelled": bool, "paths": [...]}``
  * graceful degradation: without a desktop session (headless/CI) dialogs fail with RpcError -32001
  * showing file content safely with ``set_value`` (plain text) and escaping file names

Run:  uv run file_viewer.py [FILE]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import sys
from concurrent.futures import Future
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application, RpcError, Window

MAX_BYTES = 512 * 1024
TEXT_SUFFIXES = ["txt", "md", "py", "json", "csv", "log", "toml"]
TEXT_FILTERS = [{"name": "Text files", "extensions": TEXT_SUFFIXES}]   # extensions without the dot

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; font:14px sans-serif; background:#f3f4f7; color:#20242c; display:flex; flex-direction:column; height:100vh; }
  header { display:flex; gap:8px; align-items:center; padding:10px 12px; background:#fff; border-bottom:1px solid #d9dce3; }
  button { padding:6px 12px; border:1px solid #b8bfcc; border-radius:5px; background:#fff; cursor:pointer; }
  #path { margin-left:12px; color:#5b6474; font-family:monospace; }
  .body { flex:1; display:flex; min-height:0; }
  aside { width:220px; overflow:auto; background:#fbfbfd; border-right:1px solid #d9dce3; }
  aside ul { list-style:none; margin:0; padding:6px 0; }
  aside li { padding:4px 12px; cursor:pointer; font-family:monospace; }
  aside li:hover { background:#e8eefc; }
  textarea { flex:1; border:0; padding:12px; font:13px monospace; resize:none; }
  footer { padding:6px 12px; background:#fff; border-top:1px solid #d9dce3; color:#5b6474; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <header>
    <button id="open">Open…</button><button id="save-as">Save As…</button><button id="folder">Folder…</button>
    <span id="path">No file</span>
  </header>
  <div class="body">
    <aside><ul id="files"></ul></aside>
    <textarea id="editor" spellcheck="false" placeholder="Open a text file"></textarea>
  </div>
  <footer id="status">Ready.</footer>
</body></html>"""


class FileViewer:
    def __init__(self, window: Window):
        self.window, self.document = window, window.document
        self.current: Path | None = None
        self.folder_files: list[Path] = []
        doc = self.document
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.ask_open(), element="open")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.ask_save_as(), element="save-as")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.ask_folder(), element="folder")
        doc.on("click", self._on_file_click, element="files")

    # ----- native dialogs (non-blocking) -----
    def ask_open(self) -> Future:
        start = self.current.parent if self.current else Path.home()
        future = self.window.open_files(title="Open a text file", directory=start, filters=TEXT_FILTERS,
                                        multiple=False, wait=False)
        future.add_done_callback(lambda f: self._dialog_done(f, self.load))
        return future

    def ask_save_as(self) -> Future:
        name = self.current.name if self.current else "untitled.txt"
        future = self.window.save_file(title="Save as", file_name=name, filters=TEXT_FILTERS, wait=False)
        future.add_done_callback(lambda f: self._dialog_done(f, self.save))
        return future

    def ask_folder(self) -> Future:
        future = self.window.choose_folder(title="Show the text files of a folder", wait=False)
        future.add_done_callback(lambda f: self._dialog_done(f, self.show_folder))
        return future

    def _dialog_done(self, future: Future, action) -> None:
        # Runs on an SDK completion thread; calling the synchronous SDK from here is fine.
        try:
            result = future.result()
        except RpcError as error:
            if error.code == -32001:   # unsupported here, e.g. no desktop session (headless)
                self.status("Native file dialogs are not available in this session.")
            else:
                self.status(f"Dialog failed (code {error.code}).")
            return
        except Exception as error:     # window closed, application shutting down, ...
            print("dialog ended:", type(error).__name__)
            return
        if result["cancelled"] or not result["paths"]:
            self.status("Cancelled.")
            return
        action(Path(result["paths"][0]))

    # ----- file operations (also used directly by the tests) -----
    def load(self, path: Path) -> None:
        try:
            if path.stat().st_size > MAX_BYTES:
                self.status(f"{path.name} is larger than {MAX_BYTES // 1024} KiB.")
                return
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            self.status(f"{path.name} is not UTF-8 text.")
            return
        except OSError as error:
            self.status(f"Cannot read {path.name}: {error.strerror}")
            return
        self.current = path
        self.document.set_value("editor", text)          # plain text: never parsed as HTML
        self.document.set_text("path", str(path))
        self.window.set(title=f"{path.name} — File viewer")
        self.status(f"Opened {path.name} ({len(text)} characters).")

    def save(self, path: Path) -> None:
        try:
            path.write_text(self.document.get_value("editor"), encoding="utf-8")
        except OSError as error:
            self.status(f"Cannot save {path.name}: {error.strerror}")
            return
        self.current = path
        self.document.set_text("path", str(path))
        self.status(f"Saved {path.name}.")

    def show_folder(self, folder: Path) -> None:
        suffixes = {"." + e for e in TEXT_SUFFIXES}
        self.folder_files = sorted(p for p in folder.iterdir() if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in suffixes)[:200]
        items = "".join(f'<li id="file-{i}">{html.escape(p.name)}</li>' for i, p in enumerate(self.folder_files))
        self.document.replace_html("files", items or "<li>(no text files)</li>")
        self.status(f"{len(self.folder_files)} text file(s) in {folder.name or folder}.")

    def _on_file_click(self, event: dict) -> None:
        element = event["element"]
        if element.startswith("file-") and element[5:].isdigit():
            self.load(self.folder_files[int(element[5:])])

    def status(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.document.set_text("status", text)


def build(app: Application) -> FileViewer:
    return FileViewer(app.open_html(PAGE, title="File viewer", width=900, height=600))


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="File viewer") as app:
        viewer = build(app)
        if len(sys.argv) > 1:              # optional: open a file at start, without a dialog
            viewer.load(Path(sys.argv[1]))
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Focus timer: application lifecycle, quit confirmation and saving state on shutdown.

What it teaches
  * a ``setup(app)`` entry point that works with BOTH launch styles:
      uv run focus_timer.py                         (Application.start)
      uv run -m nativehtmlkit run focus_timer:setup   (host-first runner)
  * ``on_before_quit``: veto a quit while the timer runs and ask with an HTML <dialog>
  * ``on_shutdown``: save statistics after the host shut down (no more RPC is possible then)
  * ``Window.request_attention`` (where the platform supports it) and ``Window.set(title=...)``
  * a ticking background thread that stops with the application
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application, NativeHTMLKitError, RpcError, Window

APP_ID = "org.nativehtmlkit.examples.focus_timer"

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; font:15px sans-serif; background:#1e2233; color:#eef0f7; text-align:center; }
  main { padding:28px 20px; }
  #clock { font-size:64px; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; margin:12px 0; }
  form { display:flex; gap:8px; justify-content:center; align-items:center; }
  input { width:60px; padding:6px; }
  button { padding:7px 14px; border:0; border-radius:6px; background:#5b7cfa; color:#fff; cursor:pointer; }
  button.secondary { background:#3a4058; }
  #sessions { color:#a8afc6; margin-top:14px; }
  dialog { border:0; border-radius:10px; padding:20px; background:#2b3047; color:#eef0f7; }
  .running #clock { color:#8ef0b6; }
</style></head>
<body id="body"><main>
  <h1>Focus timer</h1>
  <div id="clock">25:00</div>
  <form id="controls">
    <label>Minutes <input id="minutes" type="number" min="1" max="120" value="25"></label>
    <button id="start" type="submit">Start</button>
    <button id="pause" type="button" class="secondary">Pause</button>
    <button id="reset" type="button" class="secondary">Reset</button>
  </form>
  <p id="sessions">Completed sessions: 0</p>
  <dialog id="confirm-quit"><p>The timer is still running. Quit anyway?</p>
    <button id="quit-anyway">Quit</button> <button id="keep" class="secondary">Keep running</button></dialog>
</main></body></html>"""


class FocusTimer:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, window: Window, stats_file: Path):
        self.app, self.window, self.document = app, window, window.document
        self.stats_file = stats_file
        self.stats = self._load_stats()
        self.saved_stats = dict(self.stats)
        self.remaining = 25 * 60.0
        self.deadline: float | None = None          # monotonic time when the timer ends
        self.allow_quit = False
        self.stopped = threading.Event()
        doc = self.document
        doc.on("submit", lambda _e: self.start(self._minutes() * 60), element="controls")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.pause(), element="pause")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.reset(), element="reset")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.quit_anyway(), element="quit-anyway")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: doc.close_dialog("confirm-quit", "keep"), element="keep")
        app.on_before_quit(self.may_quit)
        app.on_shutdown(self.on_shutdown)
        threading.Thread(target=self._tick, name="timer-tick", daemon=True).start()
        self.show()

    @property
    def running(self) -> bool:
        return self.deadline is not None

    def start(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        self.remaining = float(seconds)
        self.deadline = time.monotonic() + self.remaining
        self.document.add_class("body", "running")
        self.show()

    def pause(self) -> None:
        if self.running:
            self.remaining = max(0.0, self.deadline - time.monotonic())
            self.deadline = None
            self.document.remove_class("body", "running")

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.deadline = None
        self.remaining = self._minutes() * 60.0
        self.document.remove_class("body", "running")
        self.show()

    def show(self) -> None:
        left = max(0.0, self.deadline - time.monotonic()) if self.running else self.remaining
        minutes, seconds = divmod(int(round(left)), 60)
        self.document.set_text("clock", f"{minutes:02d}:{seconds:02d}")
        self.window.set(title=f"{minutes:02d}:{seconds:02d} — Focus timer" if self.running else "Focus timer")

    def finish(self) -> None:
        self.deadline, self.remaining = None, 0.0
        self.stats["completed"] += 1
        self.document.remove_class("body", "running")
        self.document.set_text("sessions", f"Completed sessions: {self.stats['completed']}")
        self.show()
        try:
            self.window.request_attention("informational")
        except RpcError:
            pass                                   # not available (headless, some compositors)

    def _tick(self) -> None:
        while not self.stopped.wait(0.25):
            if not self.running:
                continue
            try:
                if time.monotonic() >= self.deadline:
                    self.finish()
                else:
                    self.show()
            except NativeHTMLKitError:
                return                             # window gone / shutting down

    # ----- lifecycle -----
    def may_quit(self) -> bool:
        """The host asks before quitting (last window closed, or request_quit())."""
        if self.running and not self.allow_quit:
            self.document.show_dialog("confirm-quit")
            return False
        return True

    def quit_anyway(self) -> None:
        self.allow_quit = True
        self.document.close_dialog("confirm-quit", "quit")
        self.app.request_quit()                    # asks may_quit() again, which now allows it

    def on_shutdown(self) -> None:
        # Runs in the thread that called app.run(), after the host shut down: plain Python only.
        self.stopped.set()
        if self.stats == self.saved_stats:
            return                                 # nothing new to save
        self.stats_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.stats_file.write_text(json.dumps(self.stats), encoding="utf-8")

    def _load_stats(self) -> dict:
        try:
            return {"completed": int(json.loads(self.stats_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["completed"])}
        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
            return {"completed": 0}

    def _minutes(self) -> int:
        value = self.document.get_value("minutes")
        return min(120, max(1, int(value))) if value.isdigit() else 25


def build(app: Application, stats_file: Path) -> FocusTimer:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Focus timer", width=420, height=360)
    timer = FocusTimer(app, window, stats_file)
    timer.document.set_text("sessions", f"Completed sessions: {timer.stats['completed']}")
    return timer


def setup(app: Application) -> None:
    """Entry point for ``uv run -m nativehtmlkit run focus_timer:setup``; the runner calls app.run()."""
    stats = Path(app.rpc.call("desktop.paths")["state"]) / "focus-timer.json"
    build(app, stats)


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Focus timer", app_id=APP_ID) as app:
        setup(app)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Hello: the smallest complete NativeHTMLKit app, a greeting form.

What it teaches
  * the application lifecycle: ``Application.start`` -> window -> document -> events ->
    ``app.run()`` (which announces readiness and waits until the last window closes)
  * reading an input value with ``get_value``
  * writing untrusted text safely with ``set_text`` (it never parses HTML)

Run:  uv run hello.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Document

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 32px; }
  input { padding: 6px 8px; font-size: 15px; }
  button { padding: 6px 14px; font-size: 15px; }
  #greeting { margin-top: 18px; font-size: 20px; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <label for="name">Your name</label>
  <input id="name" autofocus>
  <button id="greet">Greet</button>
  <p id="greeting">Type a name and press Greet.</p>
</body></html>"""


def greet(document: Document) -> None:
    name = document.get_value("name").strip() or "world"
    # Text is never parsed as HTML: '<b>' typed by the user stays visible as '<b>'.
    document.set_text("greeting", f"Hello, {name}!")


def build(app: Application) -> Document:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Hello", width=520, height=300)
    document = window.document
    document.on("click", lambda _event: greet(document), element="greet")
    return document


def main() -> None:
    # Application.start() runs this script a second time as the host's backend.
    # Keep side effects inside main(), after start().
    with Application.start(name="Hello NativeHTMLKit") as app:
        build(app)
        app.run()   # until the user closes the last window


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.title: Source: keyboard_shortcuts.py
items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Keyboard shortcuts: a snippet editor with keyboard shortcuts.

What it teaches
  * ``keydown`` events (``key``, ``ctrl``, ``shift``, ``alt``, ``meta``) and a shortcut table that
    maps chords such as ``"ctrl+s"`` to actions
  * ``Document.prevent_default`` registered BEFORE the key is pressed (callbacks run after native
    dispatch), so Tab indents instead of moving focus
  * inserting text at the caret with ``replace_control_range``
  * ``control_selection`` / ``set_control_selection`` (UTF-16 offsets)
  * a ``popover`` used as a help panel

Shortcuts: Tab indent, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+L insert timestamp, Ctrl+Shift+U upper-case the
selection, F1 show/hide help, Escape hide help.

Run:  uv run keyboard_shortcuts.py [FILE]
Default file: ~/Documents/nativehtmlkit-snippet.txt (or ~/nativehtmlkit-snippet.txt without a Documents folder).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Document

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100vh; }
  #editor { flex: 1; margin: 10px; font: 14px/1.45 monospace; padding: 8px; tab-size: 4; }
  footer { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 4px 10px 8px; font-size: 12px; color: #555; }
  #help { padding: 12px 16px; font-size: 13px; }
  #help kbd { border: 1px solid #aaa; border-radius: 3px; padding: 0 4px; font-family: monospace; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <textarea id="editor" aria-label="Snippet" autofocus></textarea>
  <footer><span id="status" role="status">Press F1 for shortcuts.</span><span id="file"></span></footer>
  <div id="help" popover>
    <strong>Shortcuts</strong><br>
    <kbd>Tab</kbd> indent - <kbd>Ctrl+S</kbd> save - <kbd>Ctrl+L</kbd> timestamp<br>
    <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+U</kbd> upper-case selection - <kbd>F1</kbd>/<kbd>Esc</kbd> help
  </div>
</body></html>"""


def chord(event: dict) -> str:
    """{'key': 'U', 'ctrl': True, 'shift': True} -> 'ctrl+shift+u'."""
    parts = [name for name in ("ctrl", "alt", "shift", "meta") if event.get(name)]
    return "+".join(parts + [str(event.get("key", "")).lower()])


class SnippetEditor:
    def __init__(self, document: Document, path: Path):
        self.document, self.path = document, path
        self.shortcuts = {
            "tab": lambda: self.insert("    "),
            "ctrl+s": self.save,
            "ctrl+l": lambda: self.insert(time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")),
            "ctrl+shift+u": self.upper_case_selection,
            "f1": lambda: self.document.toggle_popover("help"),
            "escape": lambda: self.document.hide_popover("help"),
        }
        document.set_text("file", str(path))
        if path.is_file():
            document.set_value("editor", path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        # Default actions must be cancelled before the key arrives: callbacks only run after
        # native dispatch. Tab (without Shift) in the editor no longer moves focus.
        document.prevent_default("editor", "keydown", key="Tab", shift=False)
        # Without element=, the handler receives every keydown in the document.
        document.on("keydown", self.on_key)

    def on_key(self, event: dict) -> None:
        action = self.shortcuts.get(chord(event))
        if action:
            action()

    def status(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.document.set_text("status", text)

    def insert(self, text: str) -> None:
        # Without start/end, replace_control_range replaces the selection (or inserts at the caret).
        self.document.replace_control_range("editor", text, selection_mode="end")

    def save(self) -> None:
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.path.write_text(self.document.get_value("editor"), encoding="utf-8")
        self.status("Saved " + time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"))

    def upper_case_selection(self) -> None:
        # start/end are UTF-16 offsets, so slice the UTF-16 encoding, not the Python str.
        selection = self.document.control_selection("editor")
        start, end = selection["start"], selection["end"]
        if end <= start:
            self.status("Select some text first.")
            return
        units = self.document.get_value("editor").encode("utf-16-le")
        selected = units[start * 2:end * 2].decode("utf-16-le")
        self.insert(selected.upper())


def default_path() -> Path:
    documents = Path.home() / "Documents"
    return (documents if documents.is_dir() else Path.home()) / "nativehtmlkit-snippet.txt"


def build(app: Application, path: Path) -> SnippetEditor:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Snippet editor", width=720, height=500)
    return SnippetEditor(window.document, path)


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Snippet editor") as app:
        path = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else default_path()
        build(app, path)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Live chart: a live line chart drawn into an RGBA bitmap.

What it teaches
  * ``Document.create_bitmap`` + ``<img src="nativehtmlkit-bitmap://ID">`` for pixels you render
  * the frame format: straight-alpha RGBA8, row-major, ``width * 4`` bytes per row
  * cheap rendering in pure Python: copy a prepared background, then draw short vertical spans
  * presenting frames from a background thread (``present``), sampling twice per second
  * pausing, and closing the bitmap (``close`` is idempotent)

The chart shows this Python process's working set (resident memory), sampled twice per second.

Run:  uv run live_chart.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
import threading

from nativehtmlkit import Application, NativeHTMLKitError, Window

WIDTH, HEIGHT = 360, 120
LINE = bytes((50, 104, 216, 255))

PAGE = f"""<!doctype html>
<html><head><style>
  body {{ font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 20px; }}
  img {{ width: {WIDTH}px; height: {HEIGHT}px; border: 1px solid #ccc; display: block; }}
  #legend {{ font-size: 13px; color: #444; margin-top: 8px; }}
</style></head>
<body>
  <h3>Working set of this backend process</h3>
  <img id="chart" src="nativehtmlkit-bitmap://memory" alt="Memory use over time">
  <p id="legend" role="status">Starting...</p>
  <button id="pause">Pause</button>
</body></html>"""


def working_set_mb() -> float:
    """Resident memory of this process in MB (Linux: /proc/self/statm; Windows: Win32 API)."""
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        import ctypes
        from ctypes import wintypes

        class Counters(ctypes.Structure):
            _fields_ = [("cb", wintypes.DWORD), ("PageFaultCount", wintypes.DWORD),
                        ("PeakWorkingSetSize", ctypes.c_size_t), ("WorkingSetSize", ctypes.c_size_t)] + [
                (name, ctypes.c_size_t) for name in ("QuotaPeakPagedPoolUsage", "QuotaPagedPoolUsage",
                                                     "QuotaPeakNonPagedPoolUsage", "QuotaNonPagedPoolUsage",
                                                     "PagefileUsage", "PeakPagefileUsage")]
        kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32")
        kernel32.GetCurrentProcess.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
        counters = Counters(cb=ctypes.sizeof(Counters))
        process = wintypes.HANDLE(kernel32.GetCurrentProcess())       # a pseudo-handle, no need to close
        kernel32.K32GetProcessMemoryInfo(process, ctypes.byref(counters), counters.cb)
        return counters.WorkingSetSize / 2**20
    with open("/proc/self/statm", encoding="ascii") as handle:
        return int(handle.read().split()[1]) * os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE") / 2**20


def draw_background() -> bytes:
    """White with grid lines at rows 30, 60 and 90; every frame starts as a copy of it."""
    frame = bytearray(b"\xff" * (WIDTH * HEIGHT * 4))
    grid = bytes((225, 229, 236, 255)) * WIDTH
    for y in (30, 60, 90):
        frame[y * WIDTH * 4:(y + 1) * WIDTH * 4] = grid
    return bytes(frame)


def render(samples: list[float], background: bytes) -> bytearray:
    """Newest sample at the right edge; the line is scaled to the visible minimum and maximum."""
    frame = bytearray(background)
    if not samples:
        return frame
    low, high = min(samples), max(samples)
    span = max(1.0, high - low)
    previous = None
    for i, value in enumerate(samples):
        x = WIDTH - len(samples) + i
        y = int((HEIGHT - 6) - ((value - low) / span) * (HEIGHT - 12))
        if previous is None:
            previous = y
        # A vertical span from the previous point keeps the line connected.
        for row in range(min(previous, y), max(previous, y) + 1):
            offset = (row * WIDTH + x) * 4
            frame[offset:offset + 4] = LINE
        previous = y
    return frame


class LiveChart:
    def __init__(self, window: Window):
        self.document = window.document
        # The bitmap belongs to this document; it is released with the document or by close().
        self.bitmap = self.document.create_bitmap("memory", WIDTH, HEIGHT)
        self.background = draw_background()
        self.samples: list[float] = []
        self.frames = 0
        self.paused = False
        self.stopped = threading.Event()
        self.document.on("click", lambda _event: self.toggle_pause(), element="pause")

    def add_sample(self) -> None:
        mb = working_set_mb()
        self.samples.append(mb)
        del self.samples[:-WIDTH]                         # at most one sample per pixel column
        self.document.set_text("legend", f"{mb:,.1f} MB now, {len(self.samples)} samples")

    def write_frame(self) -> dict:
        result = self.bitmap.present(render(self.samples, self.background))
        self.frames += 1
        return result

    def toggle_pause(self) -> None:
        self.paused = not self.paused
        self.document.set_text("pause", "Resume" if self.paused else "Pause")

    def start(self) -> threading.Thread:
        def tick() -> None:
            while not self.stopped.wait(0.5):
                if self.paused:
                    continue
                try:
                    self.add_sample()
                    self.write_frame()
                except (NativeHTMLKitError, RuntimeError):
                    return            # window closed / shutting down (a closed bitmap raises RuntimeError)
        thread = threading.Thread(target=tick, name="chart-tick", daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        return thread


def build(app: Application) -> LiveChart:
    chart = LiveChart(app.open_html(PAGE, title="Live chart", width=440, height=300))
    app.on_shutdown(chart.stopped.set)
    chart.add_sample()
    chart.write_frame()
    return chart


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Live chart") as app:
        build(app).start()
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Log viewer: follow a growing log file and highlight warnings and errors.

What it teaches
  * polling without blocking the window: a background thread reads the new bytes of the file
    every half second and appends complete lines (every SDK method is thread-safe)
  * handling a file that is truncated or rotated, and partial last lines
  * appending with ``insert_html`` and bounding the view with ``trim_children``
  * keeping the view scrolled to the end with ``set_scroll_follow``
  * escaping every log line, and stopping the thread cleanly on shutdown (``on_shutdown``)

Run:  uv run log_viewer.py FILE        (for example /var/log/syslog or C:\\Logs\\app.log)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import re
import sys
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application, NativeHTMLKitError, Window

MAX_LINES = 500
ERROR = re.compile(r"\b(ERROR|FATAL|FAIL(ED)?)\b")
WARNING = re.compile(r"\bWARN(ING)?\b")

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><style>
  body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100vh; }
  header { display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: center; padding: 8px 12px; background: #eef1f6; }
  #file { flex: 1; font-size: 13px; color: #444; overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; }
  #log { flex: 1; overflow: auto; margin: 0; padding: 8px 12px; list-style: none; font: 12px/1.45 monospace; }
  #log li { white-space: pre-wrap; }
  #log li.warn { background: #fff4ce; }
  #log li.error { background: #fde7e9; color: #8a1c1c; }
  footer { padding: 4px 12px; font-size: 12px; color: #555; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <header><span id="file"></span><label><input type="checkbox" id="paused"> Pause</label><button id="clear">Clear</button></header>
  <ul id="log"></ul>
  <footer id="status">Waiting for data...</footer>
</body></html>"""


def read_new_text(path: Path, offset: int) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Return (new offset, complete new lines) from ``offset``; a partial last line is read again later."""
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        size = handle.seek(0, 2)
        if size < offset:            # the file was truncated or rotated
            offset = 0
        handle.seek(offset)
        data = handle.read()
    end = data.rfind(b"\n")
    if end < 0:
        return offset, ""
    return offset + end + 1, data[:end + 1].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


class LogViewer:
    def __init__(self, window: Window, path: Path):
        self.document = doc = window.document
        self.path = path
        self.offset = 0
        self.line_count = 0
        self.lock = threading.Lock()           # the poll thread and the Clear button both change the list
        self.stopped = threading.Event()
        doc.set_text("file", str(path))
        # Keep the list pinned to its end while new lines arrive (unless the user scrolls up).
        doc.command("set_scroll_follow", element="log", follow=True)
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.clear(), element="clear")

    def add_lines(self, text: str) -> None:
        rows = []
        for line in re.split(r"\r?\n", text):
            if not line:
                continue
            css = ' class="error"' if ERROR.search(line) else ' class="warn"' if WARNING.search(line) else ""
            rows.append(f"<li{css}>{html.escape(line)}</li>")
        if not rows:
            return
        with self.lock:
            operations = [{"op": "insert_html", "element": "log", "position": "beforeend", "html": "".join(rows)}]
            self.line_count += len(rows)
            if self.line_count > MAX_LINES:
                # Drop the oldest lines (from the start) and keep the newest.
                operations.append({"op": "trim_children", "element": "log", "keep": MAX_LINES, "from": "start"})
                self.line_count = MAX_LINES
            self.document.batch(operations)

    def clear(self) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            self.document.replace_html("log", "")
            self.line_count = 0

    def poll_once(self) -> float:
        """Read and show new lines; return the delay before the next poll."""
        try:
            offset, text = read_new_text(self.path, self.offset)
        except OSError as error:
            self.document.set_text("status", f"Cannot read the file: {error.strerror or error} Retrying...")
            return 2.0
        if not self.document.get_checked("paused"):
            self.add_lines(text)
            self.offset = offset
        self.document.set_text("status", f"{self.line_count} lines shown. Last check {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}.")
        return 0.5

    def start(self) -> threading.Thread:
        def loop() -> None:
            delay = 0.0
            while not self.stopped.wait(delay):
                try:
                    delay = self.poll_once()
                except NativeHTMLKitError:      # window closed or application shutting down
                    return
        thread = threading.Thread(target=loop, name="log-poll", daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        return thread


def build(app: Application, path: Path) -> LogViewer:
    path = path.resolve()
    viewer = LogViewer(app.open_html(PAGE, title=f"Log - {path.name}", width=900, height=560), path)
    app.on_shutdown(viewer.stopped.set)
    return viewer


def main() -> None:
    # Validate arguments before starting the host, so a usage error is a plain console error.
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        sys.exit("Pass the log file to follow: uv run log_viewer.py FILE")
    with Application.start(name="Log tail") as app:
        build(app, Path(sys.argv[1])).start()
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

View on GitHub

"""Window manager: open note windows and inspect, rename, resize and close them from a main window.

What it teaches
  * several windows in one application, each with its own document and handlers
  * ``Window.state()`` / ``Window.set(...)`` and the live window list
  * ``Application.on_window_event`` (close_requested, closed, resized, focused, ...)
  * ``Window.on_before_close``: veto closing a note with unsaved changes
  * "closing the main window quits the app" even while other windows are open

Run:  uv run window_manager.py
Platform note: Wayland compositors own window placement and focus, so position/focus requests
are refused there (RpcError -32001); size, title, maximize and close work everywhere.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import itertools

from nativehtmlkit import Application, NativeHTMLKitError, RpcError, Window

INSPECTOR = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; padding:18px 22px; font:14px sans-serif; background:#f4f5f8; color:#1e2430; }
  h1 { font-size:20px; margin:0 0 12px; }
  .bar { display:flex; gap:8px; margin-bottom:12px; }
  input { padding:6px; border:1px solid #c2c8d4; border-radius:5px; }
  button { padding:6px 10px; border:1px solid #aab3c3; border-radius:5px; background:#fff; cursor:pointer; }
  table { width:100%; border-collapse:collapse; background:#fff; }
  th, td { text-align:left; padding:6px 8px; border-bottom:1px solid #e1e4ea; }
  td.actions button { padding:3px 7px; font-size:12px; }
  #events { font:12px monospace; color:#596273; max-height:120px; overflow:auto; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <h1>Windows</h1>
  <div class="bar">
    <button id="new-note">New note window</button>
    <input id="rename-to" type="text" placeholder="New title for Rename">
  </div>
  <table><thead><tr><th>ID</th><th>Title</th><th>Size</th><th>State</th><th></th></tr></thead>
    <tbody id="rows"></tbody></table>
  <h2>Window events</h2>
  <div id="events"></div>
  <p id="status"></p>
</body></html>"""

NOTE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; font:14px sans-serif; display:flex; flex-direction:column; height:100vh; background:#fffbea; }
  #warning { display:none; padding:8px 12px; background:#ffe2b8; }
  #warning.shown { display:block; }
  textarea { flex:1; border:0; padding:12px; background:transparent; font:14px sans-serif; resize:none; }
  footer { padding:6px 12px; display:flex; gap:8px; align-items:center; color:#6f6440; }
  button { padding:4px 10px; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <div id="warning">Unsaved changes. <button id="discard">Discard and close</button></div>
  <textarea id="text" placeholder="Type a note…"></textarea>
  <footer><button id="save">Save</button><span id="note-status">Saved</span></footer>
</body></html>"""


class Note:
    def __init__(self, window: Window):
        self.window, self.document = window, window.document
        self.dirty = False
        self.saved_text = ""
        self.document.on("input", lambda _e: self.mark_dirty(), element="text")
        self.document.on("click", lambda _e: self.save(), element="save")
        self.document.on("click", lambda _e: self.discard_and_close(), element="discard")
        window.on_before_close(self.allow_close)

    def mark_dirty(self) -> None:
        self.dirty = True
        self.document.set_text("note-status", "Edited")

    def save(self) -> None:
        self.saved_text = self.document.get_value("text")
        self.dirty = False
        self.document.remove_class("warning", "shown")
        self.document.set_text("note-status", "Saved")

    def allow_close(self) -> bool:
        """Called by the host before the window closes; return False to keep it open."""
        if self.dirty:
            self.document.add_class("warning", "shown")
            return False
        return True

    def discard_and_close(self) -> None:
        self.dirty = False
        self.window.request_close()


class WindowManager:
    def __init__(self, app: Application):
        self.app = app
        self.notes: dict[str, Note] = {}
        self.numbers = itertools.count(1)
        self.main = app.open_html(INSPECTOR, title="Window manager", width=760, height=520)
        self.document = doc = self.main.document
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: self.new_note(), element="new-note")
        doc.on("click", self._on_row_click, element="rows")
        self.main.on_before_close(self._main_may_close)
        app.on_window_event(self._on_window_event)
        self.refresh()

    def new_note(self) -> Note:
        number = next(self.numbers)
        window = self.app.open_html(NOTE, title=f"Note {number}", width=360, height=300)
        note = self.notes[window.id] = Note(window)
        self.refresh()
        return note

    def windows(self) -> list[Window]:
        return [self.main] + [n.window for n in self.notes.values()]

    def refresh(self) -> None:
        rows = []
        for window in self.windows():
            try:
                state = window.state()
            except NativeHTMLKitError:
                continue                       # closed meanwhile
            observed = state.get("observed") or {}
            flags = [name for name in ("maximized", "minimized", "fullscreen", "focused") if observed.get(name)]
            if state.get("closing"):
                flags.append("closing")
            wid = html.escape(window.id)
            actions = "" if window is self.main else (
                f'<button id="row-{wid}-rename">Rename</button>'
                f'<button id="row-{wid}-grow">640×480</button>'
                f'<button id="row-{wid}-max">Maximize</button>'
                f'<button id="row-{wid}-close">Close</button>')
            rows.append(f"<tr><td>{wid}</td><td>{html.escape(state['title'])}</td>"
                        f"<td>{state['width']}×{state['height']}</td><td>{', '.join(flags) or '-'}</td>"
                        f'<td class="actions">{actions}</td></tr>')
        self.document.replace_html("rows", "".join(rows))

    def _on_row_click(self, event: dict) -> None:
        parts = event["element"].split("-")
        if len(parts) != 3 or parts[1] not in self.notes:
            return
        window, action = self.notes[parts[1]].window, parts[2]
        try:
            if action == "rename":
                title = self.document.get_value("rename-to").strip()
                if title:
                    window.set(title=title)
            elif action == "grow":
                window.set(width=640, height=480)
            elif action == "max":
                maximized = bool((window.state().get("observed") or {}).get("maximized"))
                window.set(maximized=not maximized)
            elif action == "close":
                window.request_close()       # the note may veto (unsaved changes)
        except RpcError as error:
            self.document.set_text("status", f"{action} refused by the platform (code {error.code}).")
        self.refresh()

    def _main_may_close(self) -> bool:
        dirty = [n for n in self.notes.values() if n.dirty]
        if dirty:
            self.document.set_text("status", f"{len(dirty)} note(s) have unsaved changes; save or close them first.")
            return False
        return True

    def _on_window_event(self, params: dict) -> None:
        kind, wid = params.get("type"), params.get("window_id")
        if kind == "closed" and wid == self.main.id:
            # The SDK has already retired the main window's handles; just quit, which
            # closes the remaining note windows too.
            self.app.request_quit()
            return
        if kind == "closed":
            self.notes.pop(wid, None)
        try:
            self.document.insert_html("events", f"<div>{html.escape(str(wid))}: {html.escape(str(kind))}</div>")
            self.document.node("events").trim_children(30)        # keep the 30 newest entries
            if kind in ("closed", "resized", "close_requested", "focused"):
                self.refresh()
        except NativeHTMLKitError:
            pass                                  # the application is shutting down


def build(app: Application) -> WindowManager:
    return WindowManager(app)


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Window manager") as app:
        build(app)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Process dashboard: a live process monitor (final code of the process dashboard tutorial).

What it teaches
  * collecting data in a background thread and updating the page from it (SDK calls are
    thread-safe), so slow work never blocks the window's event callbacks
  * a refresh loop that waits on a ``threading.Event`` (wakes early to resume or to quit)
  * pausing with a checkbox (the ``change`` event carries ``checked``)
  * filtering and sorting a cached snapshot under a lock
  * copying the table to the clipboard with ``set_clipboard_text`` (and a fallback without one)
  * stopping the thread from ``app.on_shutdown``

Run:    uv run process_dashboard/dashboard.py [--refresh-seconds 3]
Guide:  docs/tutorials/process-dashboard.md (step 3 of 3)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import html
import threading
import time

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Document, NativeHTMLKitError, RpcError
from processes import list_processes

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 14px sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #11161f; color: #e6ebf3; }
  main { padding: 18px 22px; }
  header { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px; }
  h1 { font-size: 20px; margin: 0 0 12px; }
  #status { color: #9fb0c8; }
  form { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 10px; }
  input, select { background: #1b2331; color: #e6ebf3; border: 1px solid #3a475c; border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px; }
  #filter { flex: 1; }
  button { background: #3574c6; color: white; border: 0; border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px 12px; }
  table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; }
  th, td { text-align: left; padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #2a3445; }
  th { color: #9fb0c8; font-weight: 600; }
  td.num, th.num { text-align: right; }
  #summary { color: #9fb0c8; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <header><h1>Processes</h1><span id="status" role="status">Collecting...</span></header>
  <form id="view-form">
    <input id="filter" type="search" placeholder="Filter by name" aria-label="Filter by name">
    <select id="sort" aria-label="Sort by">
      <option value="memory">Memory</option><option value="cpu">CPU time</option><option value="name">Name</option>
    </select>
    <label><input type="checkbox" id="paused"> Pause</label>
    <button id="copy" type="button">Copy table</button>
  </form>
  <p id="summary"></p>
  <table>
    <thead><tr><th>Name</th><th class="num">Id</th><th class="num">Memory (MB)</th><th class="num">CPU (s)</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody id="rows"></tbody>
  </table>
</main></body></html>"""

SORT_KEYS = {
    "memory": (lambda p: p.memory_mb, True),
    "cpu": (lambda p: p.cpu_seconds, True),
    "name": (lambda p: p.name.lower(), False),
}
SHOWN = 25


class Dashboard:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, document: Document, refresh_seconds: float):
        self.app, self.document, self.refresh_seconds = app, document, refresh_seconds
        self.lock = threading.Lock()          # rows/shown are read by callbacks and the worker
        self.rows: list = []
        self.shown: list = []
        self.refreshes = 0
        self.paused = False
        self.wake = threading.Event()         # set to refresh now (resume) or to stop
        self.stopped = threading.Event()
        doc = document
        doc.on("input", lambda _event: self.update_view(), element="filter")
        doc.on("change", lambda _event: self.update_view(), element="sort")
        doc.on("submit", lambda _event: self.update_view(), element="view-form")
        doc.on("change", self.on_pause, element="paused")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.copy(), element="copy")
        app.on_shutdown(self.stop)

    # ----- the background refresh loop -----
    def start(self) -> threading.Thread:
        thread = threading.Thread(target=self._loop, name="process-refresh", daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        return thread

    def _loop(self) -> None:
        while not self.stopped.is_set():
            if not self.paused:
                try:
                    self.refresh()
                except NativeHTMLKitError:    # the window closed or the app is shutting down
                    return
            self.wake.wait(self.refresh_seconds)
            self.wake.clear()

    def refresh(self) -> None:
        rows = list_processes()               # the slow part: runs on this worker thread
        with self.lock:
            self.rows = rows
            self.refreshes += 1
            count = self.refreshes
        self.update_view()
        if not self.paused:                   # paused while collecting: keep showing "Paused"
            self.document.set_text("status", f"Updated {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} (refresh #{count})")

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self.stopped.set()
        self.wake.set()

    # ----- the view -----
    def update_view(self) -> None:
        needle = self.document.get_value("filter").strip().lower()
        key, descending = SORT_KEYS.get(self.document.get_value("sort"), SORT_KEYS["memory"])
        with self.lock:
            matching = [p for p in self.rows if needle in p.name.lower()]
            self.shown = sorted(matching, key=key, reverse=descending)[:SHOWN]
            shown, total = list(self.shown), len(self.rows)
            memory = sum(p.memory_mb for p in self.rows)
        cells = "".join(f'<tr><td>{html.escape(p.name)}</td><td class="num">{p.pid}</td>'
                        f'<td class="num">{p.memory_mb:,.1f}</td><td class="num">{p.cpu_seconds:,.1f}</td></tr>'
                        for p in shown)
        self.document.batch([
            {"op": "replace_children_html", "element": "rows", "html": cells},
            {"op": "set_text", "element": "summary",
             "text": f"Showing {len(shown)} of {total} processes, {memory:,.0f} MB in total"},
        ])

    def on_pause(self, event: dict) -> None:
        self.paused = bool(event.get("checked"))
        if self.paused:
            self.document.set_text("status", "Paused")
        else:
            self.wake.set()                   # refresh at once instead of after the interval

    def copy(self) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            lines = ["Name\tId\tMemoryMB\tCpu"] + [f"{p.name}\t{p.pid}\t{p.memory_mb}\t{p.cpu_seconds}"
                                                  for p in self.shown]
        try:
            self.app.set_clipboard_text("\n".join(lines))
            self.document.set_text("status", f"Copied {len(lines) - 1} rows")
        except RpcError:                      # -32001: no clipboard (for example headless runs)
            self.document.set_text("status", "The clipboard is not available in this session")


def build(app: Application, refresh_seconds: float = 3) -> Dashboard:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Process Dashboard", width=760, height=640)
    return Dashboard(app, window.document, refresh_seconds)


def main() -> None:
    # Parse inside main(): the host re-runs this script with the same arguments.
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Live process dashboard")
    parser.add_argument("--refresh-seconds", type=float, default=3, help="refresh interval (1-3600)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not 1 <= args.refresh_seconds <= 3600:
        parser.error("--refresh-seconds must be between 1 and 3600")
    with Application.start(name="Process Dashboard") as app:
        build(app, args.refresh_seconds).start()
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Process viewer: a sortable, filterable table of running processes.

What it teaches
  * rendering plain Python data as an HTML table with escaped cells (``html.escape``)
  * the ``input`` event's ``value`` member (no extra round trip while typing)
  * sorting by clicking column headers, with ``aria-sort`` kept up to date
  * a status line with counts

The process list uses only the standard library: ``/proc`` on Linux and the Win32 API (through
``ctypes``) on Windows. In your own code, ``psutil`` is a good alternative.

Run:  uv run process_viewer.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import os
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Document


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Process:
    name: str
    pid: int
    memory_mb: float
    cpu_seconds: float


def list_processes() -> list[Process]:
    """A snapshot of running processes: name, id, resident memory (MB) and CPU time (s)."""
    return _windows_processes() if sys.platform == "win32" else _linux_processes()


def _linux_processes() -> list[Process]:
    tick, page = os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK"), os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE")
    result = []
    for entry in os.listdir("/proc"):
        if not entry.isdigit():
            continue
        try:
            with open(f"/proc/{entry}/stat", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
                stat = handle.read()
        except OSError:          # the process ended, or access is denied
            continue
        # The name is in parentheses and may itself contain spaces or ')'.
        name = _full_name(entry, stat[stat.index("(") + 1:stat.rindex(")")])
        fields = stat[stat.rindex(")") + 2:].split()
        cpu = (int(fields[11]) + int(fields[12])) / tick       # utime + stime
        memory = int(fields[21]) * page / 2**20                 # rss pages
        result.append(Process(name, int(entry), round(memory, 1), round(cpu, 1)))
    return result


def _full_name(pid: str, comm: str) -> str:
    """The kernel truncates comm to 15 characters; take the full name from argv[0] or the executable."""
    if len(comm) < 15:
        return comm
    candidates = []
    try:
        with open(f"/proc/{pid}/cmdline", "rb") as handle:
            candidates.append(handle.read().split(b"\0", 1)[0].decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    except OSError:
        pass
    try:
        candidates.append(os.readlink(f"/proc/{pid}/exe"))
    except OSError:                      # other users' processes: no access
        pass
    for candidate in candidates:
        base = os.path.basename(candidate)
        if base.startswith(comm):
            return base
    return comm


def _windows_processes() -> list[Process]:
    import ctypes
    from ctypes import wintypes

    class ProcessEntry(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [("dwSize", wintypes.DWORD), ("cntUsage", wintypes.DWORD), ("th32ProcessID", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("th32DefaultHeapID", ctypes.c_size_t), ("th32ModuleID", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("cntThreads", wintypes.DWORD), ("th32ParentProcessID", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("pcPriClassBase", wintypes.LONG), ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("szExeFile", wintypes.WCHAR * 260)]

    class MemoryCounters(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [("cb", wintypes.DWORD), ("PageFaultCount", wintypes.DWORD)] + [
            (name, ctypes.c_size_t) for name in ("PeakWorkingSetSize", "WorkingSetSize", "QuotaPeakPagedPoolUsage",
                                                 "QuotaPagedPoolUsage", "QuotaPeakNonPagedPoolUsage",
                                                 "QuotaNonPagedPoolUsage", "PagefileUsage", "PeakPagefileUsage")]

    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
    kernel32.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
    kernel32.OpenProcess.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
    snapshot = kernel32.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(0x2, 0)        # TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS
    if snapshot in (None, wintypes.HANDLE(-1).value):
        return []
    result = []
    try:
        entry = ProcessEntry(dwSize=ctypes.sizeof(ProcessEntry))
        more = kernel32.Process32FirstW(wintypes.HANDLE(snapshot), ctypes.byref(entry))
        while more:
            memory = cpu = 0.0
            handle = kernel32.OpenProcess(0x1000, False, entry.th32ProcessID)   # QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION
            if handle:                                                      # None: access denied
                counters = MemoryCounters(cb=ctypes.sizeof(MemoryCounters))
                if kernel32.K32GetProcessMemoryInfo(wintypes.HANDLE(handle), ctypes.byref(counters), counters.cb):
                    memory = counters.WorkingSetSize / 2**20
                times = [wintypes.FILETIME() for _ in range(4)]            # creation, exit, kernel, user
                if kernel32.GetProcessTimes(wintypes.HANDLE(handle), *map(ctypes.byref, times)):
                    cpu = sum((t.dwHighDateTime << 32 | t.dwLowDateTime) for t in times[2:]) / 1e7
                kernel32.CloseHandle(wintypes.HANDLE(handle))
            name = entry.szExeFile.removesuffix(".exe")
            result.append(Process(name, entry.th32ProcessID, round(memory, 1), round(cpu, 1)))
            more = kernel32.Process32NextW(wintypes.HANDLE(snapshot), ctypes.byref(entry))
    finally:
        kernel32.CloseHandle(wintypes.HANDLE(snapshot))
    return result


PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 16px; }
  .bar { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 10px; }
  #filter { flex: 1; padding: 6px 8px; font-size: 14px; }
  table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 13px; }
  th, td { text-align: left; padding: 4px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd; }
  th { background: #eef1f6; }
  th button { all: unset; cursor: default; font-weight: 700; }
  td.num, th.num { text-align: right; }
  #status { color: #555; font-size: 13px; margin-top: 8px; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <div class="bar">
    <input id="filter" placeholder="Filter by name or id" aria-label="Filter">
    <button id="refresh">Refresh</button>
  </div>
  <table>
    <thead><tr id="headers">
      <th aria-sort="none" id="col-Name"><button id="sort-Name">Name</button></th>
      <th class="num" aria-sort="none" id="col-Id"><button id="sort-Id">PID</button></th>
      <th class="num" aria-sort="descending" id="col-MemoryMB"><button id="sort-MemoryMB">Memory (MB)</button></th>
      <th class="num" aria-sort="none" id="col-CpuSeconds"><button id="sort-CpuSeconds">CPU (s)</button></th>
    </tr></thead>
    <tbody id="rows"></tbody>
  </table>
  <p id="status"></p>
</body></html>"""

# Column id in the page -> Process attribute.
COLUMNS = {"Name": "name", "Id": "pid", "MemoryMB": "memory_mb", "CpuSeconds": "cpu_seconds"}
MAX_ROWS = 200


class ProcessViewer:
    def __init__(self, document: Document):
        self.document = document
        self.snapshot: list[Process] = []
        self.filter_text = ""
        self.sort_by, self.descending = "MemoryMB", True
        # The input event carries the control's current value: no get_value needed.
        document.on("input", self.on_filter, element="filter")
        document.on("click", self.on_header, element="headers")
        document.on("click", lambda _event: self.refresh(), element="refresh")
        self.refresh()

    def refresh(self) -> None:
        # Plain data only: the view never keeps OS handles.
        self.snapshot = list_processes()
        self.render()

    def visible(self) -> list[Process]:
        rows = self.snapshot
        needle = self.filter_text.lower()
        if needle:
            rows = [p for p in rows if needle in p.name.lower() or str(p.pid) == needle]
        attribute = COLUMNS[self.sort_by]
        key = (lambda p: p.name.lower()) if attribute == "name" else (lambda p: getattr(p, attribute))
        return sorted(rows, key=key, reverse=self.descending)[:MAX_ROWS]

    def render(self) -> None:
        rows = self.visible()
        cells = "".join(
            f'<tr><td>{html.escape(p.name)}</td><td class="num">{p.pid}</td>'
            f'<td class="num">{p.memory_mb:,.1f}</td><td class="num">{p.cpu_seconds:,.1f}</td></tr>' for p in rows)
        operations = [{"op": "replace_children_html", "element": "rows", "html": cells}]
        for column in COLUMNS:
            sort = "none" if column != self.sort_by else ("descending" if self.descending else "ascending")
            operations.append({"op": "set_attribute", "element": f"col-{column}", "name": "aria-sort", "value": sort})
        operations.append({"op": "set_text", "element": "status",
                           "text": f"Showing {len(rows)} of {len(self.snapshot)} processes. "
                                   f"Updated {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}."})
        self.document.batch(operations)

    def on_filter(self, event: dict) -> None:
        self.filter_text = str(event.get("value", "")).strip()
        self.render()

    def on_header(self, event: dict) -> None:
        column = event["element"].removeprefix("sort-")
        if column not in COLUMNS:
            return
        self.sort_by, self.descending = self.sort_column(column)
        self.render()

    def sort_column(self, column: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:
        """Clicking the sorted column flips the order; a new column starts descending (Name ascending)."""
        if column == self.sort_by:
            return column, not self.descending
        return column, column != "Name"


def build(app: Application) -> ProcessViewer:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Processes", width=760, height=620)
    return ProcessViewer(window.document)


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Process viewer") as app:
        build(app)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Settings dialog: a settings dialog that applies and remembers preferences.

What it teaches
  * an HTML ``<dialog>`` opened modally with ``show_dialog`` and closed with a return value
    (``close_dialog``)
  * a popover help tip (``toggle_popover``)
  * reading a form inside the dialog with ``form_data``; native validation (``min``/``max``/
    ``required``) runs before the ``submit`` event is dispatched
  * applying a colour scheme and reduced motion with ``set_environment``
  * replacing one stylesheet in place (``add_stylesheet`` once, then ``replace_stylesheet``)
  * saving settings as JSON

Run:  uv run settings_dialog.py [SETTINGS_FILE]
Default settings file: <config folder>/NativeHTMLKit-Examples/settings.json
(%APPDATA% on Windows, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config on Linux).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Window

DEFAULTS = {"theme": "system", "size": 15, "motion": False}

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><style>
  :root { color-scheme: light dark; }
  body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 24px; background: Canvas; color: CanvasText; }
  @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { body { background: #1d222b; color: #e7ebf3; } }
  dialog { padding: 20px 24px; border-radius: 10px; min-width: 320px; }
  dialog label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; }
  .actions { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 8px; margin-top: 18px; }
  #help-tip { max-width: 260px; padding: 10px; font-size: 13px; }
  #saved { color: #2e7d32; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <h1>Report viewer</h1>
  <p id="sample">This paragraph follows the chosen text size.</p>
  <p><button id="open-settings">Settings...</button> <span id="saved" role="status"></span></p>

  <dialog id="settings" aria-labelledby="settings-title">
    <h2 id="settings-title">Settings</h2>
    <form id="settings-form">
      <label for="theme">Colour scheme <button type="button" id="help" aria-label="Help">?</button></label>
      <select id="theme" name="theme"><option value="system">Follow the system</option><option value="light">Light</option><option value="dark">Dark</option></select>
      <label for="size">Text size (px)</label>
      <input id="size" name="size" type="number" min="11" max="24" required>
      <label><input type="checkbox" id="motion" name="motion" value="reduce"> Reduce motion</label>
      <div class="actions"><button type="button" id="cancel">Cancel</button><button type="submit" id="apply">Save</button></div>
    </form>
  </dialog>
  <div id="help-tip" popover>"Follow the system" uses the desktop colour preference when the host can observe it.</div>
</body></html>"""


def default_settings_path() -> Path:
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        base = Path(os.environ.get("APPDATA") or Path.home() / "AppData" / "Roaming")
    else:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME") or Path.home() / ".config")
    return base / "NativeHTMLKit-Examples" / "settings.json"


def read_settings(path: Path) -> dict:
    """Saved values over the defaults; an unreadable file is ignored."""
    settings = dict(DEFAULTS)
    try:
        saved = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return settings
    if isinstance(saved, dict):
        settings.update({name: saved[name] for name in DEFAULTS if name in saved})
    return settings


class SettingsDialog:
    def __init__(self, window: Window, path: Path):
        self.document = doc = window.document
        self.path = path
        self.settings = read_settings(path)
        self.size_sheet = doc.add_stylesheet("")["sheet"]
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.show(), element="open-settings")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.cancel(), element="cancel")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: doc.toggle_popover("help-tip"), element="help")
        # Native validation (min/max/required) runs before this submit event is dispatched.
        doc.on("submit", lambda _event: self.save(), element="settings-form")
        self.apply(self.settings)

    def apply(self, settings: dict) -> None:
        # "system" removes the app override so the observed desktop preference applies again.
        self.document.set_environment(color_scheme=settings["theme"],
                                      reduced_motion="reduce" if settings["motion"] else "system")
        # Replace one app stylesheet in place instead of adding a new one each time.
        self.document.replace_stylesheet(self.size_sheet, f"body {{ font-size: {int(settings['size'])}px; }}")

    def show(self) -> None:
        doc, s = self.document, self.settings
        doc.set_selected_values("theme", [str(s["theme"])])
        doc.set_value("size", str(s["size"]))
        doc.set_checked("motion", bool(s["motion"]))
        doc.show_dialog("settings")              # modal by default

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        self.document.close_dialog("settings", "cancelled")
        self.document.set_text("saved", "Settings unchanged.")

    def save(self) -> None:
        entries = {e["name"]: e.get("value", "") for e in self.document.form_data("settings-form")["entries"]}
        self.settings = {"theme": entries.get("theme", "system"), "size": int(entries.get("size") or 15),
                         "motion": "motion" in entries}       # unchecked boxes are absent from form data
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.path.write_text(json.dumps(self.settings, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
        self.apply(self.settings)
        self.document.close_dialog("settings", "saved")
        # Report here, not in the dialog's close event: a <dialog> keeps its previous return
        # value when the user dismisses it with Escape, so "saved" would be reported again.
        self.document.set_text("saved", f"Settings saved to {self.path}")


def build(app: Application, path: Path) -> SettingsDialog:
    return SettingsDialog(app.open_html(PAGE, title="Settings dialog", width=640, height=480), path)


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Settings dialog") as app:
        path = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else default_settings_path()
        build(app, path)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Sign-up form: native HTML constraint validation plus a cross-field rule.

What it teaches
  * built-in validation (required, minlength, type=email, min/max) runs on submit;
    an invalid form fires one ``invalid`` event per failing control and no ``submit``
  * ``set_custom_validity`` for a rule HTML cannot express (passwords must match)
  * reading the submitted values with ``form_data`` (ordered entries, repeated names kept)
  * showing an error summary and a result with escaped user text

Run:  uv run signup_form.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Window

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; background:#eef1f6; color:#1f2633; font:14px/1.45 sans-serif; }
  main { max-width:520px; margin:28px auto; padding:24px; background:#fff; border-radius:10px; }
  h1 { margin:0 0 4px; font-size:24px; }
  .hint { color:#68708a; margin:0 0 18px; }
  label { display:block; margin:12px 0 4px; font-weight:bold; }
  input[type=text], input[type=email], input[type=password], input[type=number], select {
    width:100%; box-sizing:border-box; padding:8px; border:1px solid #c7cddb; border-radius:6px; }
  .check { font-weight:normal; display:flex; gap:8px; align-items:center; }
  fieldset { border:1px solid #d8dce6; border-radius:6px; margin-top:12px; }
  button { margin-top:18px; padding:10px 18px; border:0; border-radius:6px; background:#2f6fec; color:#fff; }
  #errors { color:#b3261e; }
  #errors:empty, #result:empty { display:none; }
  #result { background:#e9f6ec; border-radius:6px; padding:10px 14px; margin-top:16px; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <h1>Create an account</h1>
  <p class="hint">All fields except the newsletter are required.</p>
  <ul id="errors" role="alert"></ul>
  <form id="signup">
    <label for="name">Name</label>
    <input id="name" name="name" type="text" required minlength="2" maxlength="80">
    <label for="email">Email</label>
    <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>
    <label for="password">Password (8+ characters)</label>
    <input id="password" name="password" type="password" required minlength="8">
    <label for="confirm">Repeat password</label>
    <input id="confirm" name="confirm" type="password" required>
    <label for="age">Age</label>
    <input id="age" name="age" type="number" required min="13" max="120">
    <label for="country">Country</label>
    <select id="country" name="country" required>
      <option value="">Choose…</option><option value="de">Germany</option>
      <option value="fr">France</option><option value="jp">Japan</option><option value="us">United States</option>
    </select>
    <fieldset><legend>Interests</legend>
      <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" name="topic" value="news"> News</label>
      <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" name="topic" value="releases"> Releases</label>
      <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" name="topic" value="events"> Events</label>
    </fieldset>
    <label class="check"><input id="terms" name="terms" type="checkbox" required> I accept the terms</label>
    <button id="submit" type="submit">Sign up</button>
  </form>
  <div id="result"></div>
</main></body></html>"""

LABELS = {"name": "Name", "email": "Email", "password": "Password", "confirm": "Repeat password",
          "age": "Age", "country": "Country", "terms": "Terms"}


class SignupForm:
    def __init__(self, window: Window):
        self.document = doc = window.document
        self.errors: list[str] = []
        self.accounts: list[dict] = []
        # "invalid" does not bubble: its path holds only the control itself, so subscribe
        # document-wide and keep the controls of this form.
        doc.on("invalid", self._on_invalid)
        doc.on("submit", self._on_submit, element="signup")
        # Re-check the cross-field rule whenever either password changes.
        doc.on("input", lambda _e: self.check_passwords(), element="password")
        doc.on("input", lambda _e: self.check_passwords(), element="confirm")

    def check_passwords(self) -> None:
        """A custom validity message makes the control invalid until it is cleared again."""
        same = self.document.get_value("password") == self.document.get_value("confirm")
        self.document.set_custom_validity("confirm", "" if same else "The passwords do not match.")

    def submit(self) -> dict:
        """Run the same path as clicking "Sign up" (also used by the tests)."""
        self.check_passwords()
        self.errors.clear()
        self.document.replace_html("errors", "")
        return self.document.request_submit("signup", submitter="submit")

    def _on_invalid(self, event: dict) -> None:
        # One event per invalid control, in document order, before (instead of) "submit".
        if event["element"] not in LABELS:
            return
        message = event.get("validity", {}).get("message", "Invalid value")
        self.errors.append(f"{LABELS.get(event['element'], event['element'])}: {message}")
        self.document.replace_html("errors", "".join(f"<li>{html.escape(e)}</li>" for e in self.errors))
        self.document.set_text("result", "")

    def _on_submit(self, _event: dict) -> None:
        # Events reach Python after native dispatch, so a fast typist can submit before the
        # last "input" event updated the custom validity. Validate again here.
        if self.document.get_value("password") != self.document.get_value("confirm"):
            self.check_passwords()
            self.errors[:] = ["Repeat password: The passwords do not match."]
            self.document.replace_html("errors", "<li>Repeat password: The passwords do not match.</li>")
            return
        entries = self.document.form_data("signup")["entries"]
        values: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for entry in entries:                   # ordered; checkboxes may repeat a name
            values.setdefault(entry["name"], []).append(entry.get("value", ""))
        account = {"name": values["name"][0], "email": values["email"][0],
                   "country": values["country"][0], "topics": values.get("topic", [])}
        self.accounts.append(account)
        self.errors.clear()
        self.document.replace_html("errors", "")
        topics = ", ".join(account["topics"]) or "none"
        self.document.replace_html("result", (
            f"<strong>Welcome, {html.escape(account['name'])}!</strong><br>"
            f"We will write to {html.escape(account['email'])}. Interests: {html.escape(topics)}."))
        self.document.reset_form("signup")


def build(app: Application) -> SignupForm:
    return SignupForm(app.open_html(PAGE, title="Sign up", width=600, height=820))


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Sign-up form") as app:
        build(app)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.text:
Add, edit, complete, filter and delete tasks, saved to a JSON file.

Same example in PowerShell: Todo list

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

What it teaches: form submit; delegated list events; escaping user text; keyboard editing; atomic JSON persistence.
