items.title: Application
items.text:
from nativehtmlkit import Application

One Application is one connection to one NativeHTMLKit Core host. The host owns the native windows, rendering and the event loop; the Application object owns the Python side: windows, documents, callbacks and lifecycle hooks. Everything on this page is in nativehtmlkit 0.1.2 (bundled Core 1.0.3, wire protocol v1).

  • Creating an application: start, from_environment, the context manager
  • Windows: create_window, open_html, open_file
  • Running and stopping: ready, run, request_quit, close
  • Lifecycle hooks: on_window_event, on_before_quit, on_shutdown
  • Desktop services: clipboard, open_external, reveal_file, preferences
  • Host information: capabilities, host_diagnostics
  • asyncio: async_adapter
  • Attributes

items.title: Application.start(...) (classmethod)
items.text:
Application.start(*, name=None, app_id=None, version=None, icon=None, instance="single",
                  startup_timeout_ms=30_000, shutdown_timeout_ms=5_000, max_windows=16) -> Application

The normal entry point for uv run app.py and uv run -m package.app.

The call has two roles:

  1. Launcher (the process you started). It validates the options, writes a private temporary manifest naming the same interpreter and command line, starts the bundled native host and relays the backend's print() output and errors to your console. When the host exits, this process exits with the host's status: start() never returns here (it raises SystemExit).
  2. Backend (the same script, started again by the host). The host provided a connection; the call validates the options, connects, removes the connection secret from os.environ and returns the Application.

Everything before Application.start() therefore runs twice. Keep side effects (files, network, print) after it and guard the entry point with if __name__ == "__main__":.

Parameter Default Meaning and accepted values name script file stem (or the last module component) Application/window name. 1–128 characters, no control characters. app_id local.nativehtmlkit.<name-slug>.h<hash> derived from the script path (or module and working directory) Reverse-DNS identity, e.g. org.example.Notes: ASCII, at most 128 bytes, at least two dot-separated components, each starting with a letter and containing letters, digits, _ or -. It also names the per-application directories returned by the host's desktop.paths. version None Optional version string, same rules as name. icon None Path to an icon file. It must exist (StartupError otherwise). instance "single" "single": a second launch of the same app is handed to the running one; "multiple": every launch is independent. startup_timeout_ms 30000 1000–300000. Time the host allows for connecting and reaching app.ready. shutdown_timeout_ms 5000 100–120000. Deadline for the backend to exit after app.shutdown. max_windows 16 1–64. Window limit enforced by the host (window.create then fails with RpcError -32005).

Raises:

  • ValueError: an option is out of range (raised in both roles, before anything starts).
  • StartupError: started from an interactive interpreter, python -c or standard input; no native host found (NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY missing file, wheel without host); the icon does not exist; the host could not be executed; an incomplete or recursive host environment.
  • HostVerificationError (a FileNotFoundError): the wheel's bundled host does not match the SHA-256 pinned in its HOST-MANIFEST.json.
  • SystemExit(status): in the launcher role, always, with the host's exit status.
  • In the backend role, connection errors from from_environment.

With NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 the launcher adds the host's --headless flag (no native windows; see environment variables).

from nativehtmlkit import Application

def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Notes", app_id="org.example.Notes") as app:
        app.open_html("<h1>Hello</h1>", title="Notes")
        app.run()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.title: Application.from_environment() (classmethod)
items.text:
Application.from_environment() -> Application

Connect to the host that launched this process. The host passes UI4ME_ENDPOINT, UI4ME_TOKEN, UI4ME_APP_ID and UI4ME_PROTOCOL_VERSION; the call authenticates with host.hello, requires protocol v1 and removes those four variables from os.environ (also when it fails), so child processes never inherit the credential. Use it in a backend started from your own manifest (nativehtmlkit-python-host run --app app.toml); Application.start() and uv run -m nativehtmlkit run call it for you.

Raises StartupError when the endpoint or token variable is missing, ProtocolError for a token that is not 64 hexadecimal characters or a host that did not negotiate protocol v1, RpcError if the host refuses authentication, and OSError if the endpoint cannot be opened.

items.title: Context manager
items.text: with Application.start(...) as app: returns the application and calls close() on exit. If the block raises (other than SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt) the traceback is printed before the connection closes, so it reaches your console through the host.

items.title: create_window
items.text:
app.create_window(*, title="NativeHTMLKit", width=900, height=600, visible=True, decorations=True,
                  min_width=None, min_height=None, max_width=None, max_height=None) -> Window

Create an empty native window and return its Window. Sizes are logical (CSS) pixels. Size constraints must be given in pairs (min_width with min_height, max_width with max_height); a single value fails with RpcError -32602. resizable is not a creation option here: call window.set(resizable=False) afterwards.

Raises ApplicationShutdownError once the host has begun shutting down, RpcError -32005 when the window limit (max_windows) is reached or a quit decision is pending, and -32001 for options the platform refuses (for example a hidden window on Wayland).

A window without a document shows a built-in placeholder; load a document right away (or use open_html / open_file).

items.title: open_html
items.text:
app.open_html(html: str, *, asset_root=None, **window_options) -> Window

create_window(**window_options) followed by window.load_html(html, asset_root=asset_root). html is at most 1 MiB (UTF-8); larger documents fail with RpcError -32005. asset_root is a directory used to resolve relative URLs (images, stylesheets). If loading fails, the new window is closed and the error re-raised.

items.title: open_file
items.text:
app.open_file(path: str | Path, **window_options) -> Window

create_window(**window_options) followed by window.load_file(path). The path is resolved to an absolute path; relative resources resolve against the file's directory. A missing file fails with RpcError -32002. open_file does not take asset_root; use app.create_window(...) and window.load_file(path, asset_root=...) for that.

from pathlib import Path
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
window = app.open_file(HERE / "index.html", title="Viewer", width=800, height=600)

items.title: ready
items.text: app.ready() -> None. Tell the host that start-up is complete (app.ready). Called once by run(); calling it again does nothing. Raises RpcError -32008 if no window exists yet. Until the application is ready the host cancels start-up when the user closes any window or when the last window is closed from Python.

items.title: run
items.text:
app.run() -> None. Announce readiness and block until the host shuts the application down. Before it returns, events the host sent ahead of app.shutdown are delivered (for up to two seconds), every window and document handle is retired, and the on_shutdown callbacks run in the calling thread.

Returns normally after an orderly shutdown (the user closed the last window, request_quit() was allowed) or after this process called close(). Raises DisconnectedError if the host connection was lost instead. Calling run() again after it returned does nothing.

items.title: request_quit
items.text: app.request_quit() -> None. Ask the host to quit. The host then asks on_before_quit (reason backend_request); if that allows it, the host sends app.shutdown and run() returns. Safe to call from callbacks and other threads. This is the orderly way to end an application.

items.title: close
items.text: app.close() -> None. Retire every handle and close the connection immediately. run() then returns, but for the host this is a lost backend connection: it records an application failure and exits with status 1. Prefer request_quit(); close() is for tear-down after run() returned (the context manager calls it) or for abandoning a session.

items.title: on_window_event
items.text:
app.on_window_event(callback: Callable[[dict], Any]) -> Callable[[], None]

Call callback(params) for every native window event of this application; returns a function that unsubscribes. Several callbacks may be registered. params is {"window_id": "w2", "type": ..., "data": {...}}:

type data close_requested reason: "native_close" (user) or "backend_request" (Window.request_close) closed {}. The SDK has already marked the window closed and retired its document. resized physical_width, physical_height, scale_factor scale_changed scale_factor focused focused (bool) key key, state ("pressed"/"released"), repeat, physical_key

When closing the last window ends the application, no closed event is sent for it: the host goes straight to app.shutdown, after which all handles are stale. Callbacks run on the application event thread, in order; an exception is printed and does not stop other callbacks.

def log(params):
    print(params["window_id"], params["type"], params.get("data"))
stop = app.on_window_event(log)

items.title: on_before_quit
items.text:
app.on_before_quit(callback: Callable[[], bool]) -> None

Install the quit policy. Before the application quits (last window closed, request_quit()), the host asks; callback() returns True to allow and False to keep running. Only one policy is active; a new call replaces the previous one. Without a policy every quit is allowed.

The callback runs on an SDK worker thread, not the event thread, and must answer promptly: the host waits for the answer without a deadline. It may call the SDK (for example to show a confirmation <dialog>). An exception counts as deny; SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt count as allow.

def may_quit() -> bool:
    if unsaved_changes():
        document.show_dialog("confirm-quit")
        return False
    return True
app.on_before_quit(may_quit)

items.title: on_shutdown
items.text:
app.on_shutdown(callback: Callable[[], Any]) -> None

Run callback() once the host has shut the application down, in the thread that called run(), after the final events were delivered. Several callbacks run in registration order; one failing callback does not skip the others. The host connection is shutting down at this point: save files and stop your threads here, but do not call window or document methods.

Window-level close policies are on Window.on_before_close.

items.title: Desktop services
items.text:
These call native services. In headless mode, and where the platform lacks the service, they raise RpcError with code -32001 (unsupported). Check capabilities()["features"] or catch the error.

Method Returns Notes app.clipboard_text() -> str Clipboard text Text only. app.set_clipboard_text(text: str) -> None At most 1 MiB. app.open_external(target, *, window=None) -> dict {"accepted", "cancelled", "parent_forwarded", "presented"} target: an http/https/mailto/file URI or an absolute path; opened with the desktop's default application. window parents the request. accepted is not proof that an application appeared. Other URI schemes are refused with RpcError -32003; on Windows so are executable file types. Waits up to 60 s. app.reveal_file(path, *, window=None) -> dict same shape Show a local file in the file manager. The path is resolved to an absolute path. app.desktop_preferences() -> dict {"color_scheme", "reduced_motion", "high_contrast", "available", "source", "revision", "scope"} Values are None when the platform does not report them. Works headless (available: False, source: "headless"). app.on_desktop_preferences(callback) callback(preferences) with the same object whenever the desktop preferences change. One callback; a new call replaces it.

open_external and reveal_file raise ValueError for a window of another application and StaleDocumentError for a closed window.

from nativehtmlkit import RpcError
try:
    app.set_clipboard_text("copied")
except RpcError as error:
    if error.code != -32001:
        raise
    print("No clipboard in this session")

items.title: capabilities
items.text:
app.capabilities() -> dict: the host's capability report (host.capabilities, schema 2). Useful members: headless, native, platform, max_windows, max_documents, limits, css_profile, and features, a map of feature name to {"implemented": bool, "available": True | False | None, "qualification": str, "scope": str} (available: None means "not observed yet"). Feature names include clipboard_text, file_dialogs, external_open, reveal_file, attention, native_preferences, ime, accessibility, incoming_drop, window_constraints, window_focus, window_position and printing/tray (not implemented). Prefer features over the legacy top-level booleans.

features = app.capabilities()["features"]
can_pick_files = features["file_dialogs"]["available"] is not False

items.title: host_diagnostics
items.text: app.host_diagnostics(*, timeout=5.0) -> dict: the host's own counters (host.diagnostics): phase, windows, pending_jobs, pending_transfers, pid, backend_pid, containment, logging and dropped_notifications (window/document events the host dropped because this process stopped reading). Allowed even while shutting down. See diagnostics.

items.title: async_adapter
items.text: app.async_adapter(*, loop=None) -> AsyncApplication. An asyncio facade over the same connection. Create it inside the running loop (or pass loop). See asyncio reference.

items.title: Attributes
items.text:
Attribute Type Meaning rpc RpcClient The authenticated connection. rpc.hello holds the host.hello result (protocol_version, host_version, app_id, capabilities). host_dropped_notifications int \| None Set by run() at shutdown from host.diagnostics (None if unavailable).

Application(rpc) can be constructed around an existing RpcClient; applications normally use start() or from_environment().

items.title: Threading summary
items.text:
All methods may be called from any thread. Where your code is called:

Callback Thread Document.on, on_window_event, on_desktop_preferences the single application event thread, in event order on_before_quit, Window.on_before_close an SDK worker thread (independent of the event thread) Future done-callbacks from wait=False / rpc.call_async a short-lived completion thread per result on_shutdown the thread that called run()

A callback that blocks (for example a wait=True file dialog) delays later events, but close/quit decisions are still answered. See events and callbacks.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/application.md · edit the page there.

items.title: asyncio: AsyncApplication, AsyncRpcClient, EventDispatcher
items.text:
from nativehtmlkit import AsyncApplication, AsyncRpcClient, EventDispatcher
adapter = app.async_adapter()          # inside a running event loop

The asyncio layer uses the same host connection as the synchronous API; there is no second connection or event loop. Event callbacks run on your loop, and RPCs are awaitable.

items.title: Application.async_adapter
items.text: app.async_adapter(*, loop=None) -> AsyncApplication. Create it inside the running loop (it calls asyncio.get_running_loop() when loop is None, so outside a loop it raises RuntimeError).

items.title: AsyncApplication
items.text:
AsyncApplication(app, *, loop=None).

Attribute Meaning app The synchronous Application rpc An AsyncRpcClient over app.rpc dispatcher The EventDispatcher that runs callbacks on the loop

items.title: on_document_event
items.text:
adapter.on_document_event(document, event_type: str, callback, *, element: str | None = None) -> Callable[[], None]

Like Document.on, but callback(event) runs on the owning loop. It may be a plain function or an async def coroutine function; a coroutine is awaited before the next event is dispatched (callbacks are strictly FIFO). Start an asyncio.create_task inside the callback for work that should not hold up later events. Returns a function that disposes the subscription: once it returned, no new invocation starts, including for queued events.

items.title: run
items.text: await adapter.run() -> None. Run app.run() in a worker thread and wait for an orderly shutdown. Afterwards every subscription is disposed and the dispatcher drains and stops. Cancelling the awaiting task closes the connection (app.close()) and re-raises CancelledError.

items.title: close
items.text: await adapter.close() -> None. Dispose subscriptions, close the connection, stop the dispatcher. Like Application.close() this is an abrupt end for the host (exit status 1); prefer await asyncio.to_thread(app.request_quit) for an orderly quit.

items.title: AsyncRpcClient
items.text:
AsyncRpcClient(rpc: RpcClient).

await adapter.rpc.call(method: str, params: dict | None = None, *, timeout: float | None = 15.0)

Send a request and await its result without blocking the loop. timeout in seconds; None waits indefinitely (use it for native dialogs). On expiry it asks the host to cancel and raises RpcTimeoutError (outcome_unknown=True). Cancelling the awaiting task also asks the host to cancel and re-raises CancelledError. Neither is a rollback. Errors are the same as for RpcClient.call.

Document operations through the async client name the window and document explicitly:

async def command(op, **fields):
    return await adapter.rpc.call("document.command", {
        "window_id": window.id, "document_id": window.document.id,
        "command": {"op": op, **fields}})

await command("set_text", element="status", text="Working…")
value = (await command("get_value", element="name"))["value"]

Synchronous SDK methods block; call them off the loop with await asyncio.to_thread(...). A blocking SDK RPC made directly on a running loop triggers a one-time RuntimeWarning ("Blocking NativeHTMLKit RPC on a running asyncio event loop").

items.title: EventDispatcher
items.text:
EventDispatcher(loop=None, *, capacity=128): a bounded FIFO that runs callbacks on loop. Normally used through AsyncApplication.

Member Meaning submit(callback, event, *, active=None) Thread-safe: queue callback(event); active() is re-checked on the loop right before running. await stop() Run the already queued callbacks, then end. Called from inside a dispatched callback it only marks the dispatcher to finish (it cannot wait for itself). dropped Events dropped because the queue was full or the loop was closed (also recorded as callback.queue_overflow). loop, queue The owning loop and its asyncio.Queue

Callback failures, including a callback that raises CancelledError, are passed to the loop's exception handler (loop.call_exception_handler) and do not stop later events.

items.title: Two ways to start an async application
items.text:
import asyncio
from nativehtmlkit import Application

async def amain(app: Application) -> None:
    window = await asyncio.to_thread(app.open_html, "<button id='go'>Go</button><p id='out'></p>")
    adapter = app.async_adapter()

    async def go(_event):
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)                       # the loop stays responsive
        await adapter.rpc.call("document.command", {"window_id": window.id,
            "document_id": window.document.id, "command": {"op": "set_text", "element": "out", "text": "Done"}})

    adapter.on_document_event(window.document, "click", go, element="go")
    await adapter.run()

def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Async demo") as app:   # uv run app.py
        asyncio.run(amain(app))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

uv run -m nativehtmlkit run app:amain also works: the runner awaits a coroutine returned by the entry point (asyncio.run) and then calls app.run(), which returns at once when amain already waited for shutdown.

See the asyncio guide and the examples async_counter.py and async_jobs.py.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/asyncio.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Command-line tools
items.text:
Installing nativehtmlkit adds four commands. In a uv project, start them with uv run (for example uv run nativehtmlkit-python version). uv run -m nativehtmlkit is the same as nativehtmlkit-python. nativehtmlkit-new also works before you have a project: uvx --from nativehtmlkit nativehtmlkit-new DIRECTORY.

Command Purpose nativehtmlkit-python Run an entry point in a managed backend, check the installation, export support bundles nativehtmlkit-python-host The bundled native host's own command line (run a manifest, doctor) nativehtmlkit-new Create a new application project nativehtmlkit-skill Install the bundled coding-agent skill

items.title: nativehtmlkit-python
items.text:
nativehtmlkit-python [--diagnostics {off,normal,debug,trace}] {run,doctor,version,support} ...

--diagnostics LEVEL sets NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS for this process, the host and the backend (trace also sets NATIVEHTMLKIT_VERBOSE=1). Errors print nativehtmlkit: <Type>: <message> and exit with status 1.

items.title: run
items.text:
nativehtmlkit-python run MODULE:CALLABLE [--name NAME] [--host-log FILE]

The host-first runner. It starts the native host, which starts a backend process that imports MODULE (from the current directory / PYTHONPATH), calls CALLABLE(app) with a connected Application and then app.run(). Your module is imported only in the backend, once, after the launch credential was removed from the environment, so module-level code does not run twice.

  • CALLABLE may be a dotted attribute path (pkg.app:App.main) that does not start with _. It receives the Application and should create at least one window and register callbacks; it should not call app.run() itself (if it does, the runner's call returns at once).
  • If CALLABLE returns a coroutine, the runner runs it with asyncio.run(...) before app.run().
  • --name (default "NativeHTMLKit App") is the application name. The application id is derived from the entry point and name; every launch is independent (instance = "multiple"), the window limit is 16, start-up and shutdown timeouts are 30 s and 5 s.
  • --host-log FILE appends the host's raw JSON log records to FILE (mode 0600). Sensitive: the records include backend output and therefore application data.
  • NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 runs the host headless.

The exit status is the host's: 0 after an orderly quit, 1 when the application failed (for example an unhandled exception in CALLABLE, or a lost backend connection), 128+N after signal N.

cd examples
uv run -m nativehtmlkit run focus_timer:setup --name "Focus timer"
uv run -m nativehtmlkit run async_jobs:amain

items.title: doctor
items.text: uv run nativehtmlkit-python doctor runs the host's own environment report (JSON: host version, build identity, OS, desktop session variables, per-app paths, renderer, containment). It does not open windows. Times out after 15 s.

items.title: version
items.text: uv run nativehtmlkit-python version prints JSON: sdk_version, client_version, protocol_version, python and host (source: bundled/environment/path, path, sha256, the bundled manifest, manifest_match, the host's source_identity and source_identity_match). It starts no application. Exit status 1 when no host is found or the bundled host does not match its pinned manifest.

items.title: support
items.text:
nativehtmlkit-python support OUTPUT.zip [--session ID] [--force]

Export a redacted support bundle of the most recently recorded diagnostics session (or --session). --force replaces an existing file.

items.title: nativehtmlkit-python-host
items.text:
Forwards its arguments to the bundled (SHA-256-verified) native host. On Linux the Python wrapper replaces itself with the host process, so signals reach the host directly.

nativehtmlkit-python-host run --app app.toml     # start an application from a manifest
nativehtmlkit-python-host doctor
nativehtmlkit-python-host --version

A manifest names the backend program to start. A minimal one, as written by nativehtmlkit-new:

[app]
id = "org.example.notes"
name = "Notes"
version = "1.0.0"

[backend]
program = "/path/to/python"          # the interpreter; pin your virtual environment's python
args = ["{app_dir}/app.py"]          # {app_dir} is the manifest's directory
cwd = "{app_dir}"

[host]
startup_timeout_ms = 30000
shutdown_timeout_ms = 5000
max_windows = 4
instance = "single"

[backend.env] may add environment variables (not the UI4ME_*/NATIVEHTMLKIT_* transport names or *_HOST_* keys, which the host rejects). The backend connects with Application.start() (which only connects when started by a host) or Application.from_environment().

items.title: nativehtmlkit-new
items.text:
nativehtmlkit-new DIRECTORY [--name NAME] [--python INTERPRETER]

Create a project in a new or empty directory: app.py (an Application.start() app with a form handler), index.html, style.css, pyproject.toml (depends on nativehtmlkit>=0.1.1) and an optional app.toml manifest that pins --python (default: the current interpreter; under uvx that is a temporary interpreter in uv's cache, so point program at your project's .venv interpreter before using the manifest). The app id is org.nativehtmlkit.examples.<slug>; change it for your own application. Refuses to overwrite a non-empty directory (exit status 2). Then:

cd DIRECTORY
uv run app.py

items.title: nativehtmlkit-skill
items.text:
nativehtmlkit-skill {install,status,uninstall} [--agents all|claude,codex,opencode,copilot,cursor,gemini]
                    [--scope user|project] [--project PATH] [--force] [--dry-run]

Install the nativehtmlkit-python agent skill bundled in the wheel into the skill folders of coding agents, per user (default) or per project (--scope project --project PATH). Only this skill is managed: a modified or foreign directory is replaced or removed only with --force. No network access. Exit status 1 if any target failed.

Agent User folder Project folder claude ~/.claude/skills .claude/skills codex ~/.agents/skills .agents/skills opencode ~/.config/opencode/skills .opencode/skills copilot ~/.copilot/skills .github/skills cursor ~/.cursor/skills .cursor/skills gemini ~/.gemini/skills .gemini/skills

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/cli-runner.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Diagnostics
items.text:
The SDK records privacy-safe structured diagnostics: event names, ids, counters, durations and error codes, never RPC parameters or results, document text, form values, file paths, titles or credentials. Recording never raises into your code and never blocks the transport.

from nativehtmlkit import diagnostics_session_id, export_support_bundle

items.title: Levels
items.text:
Set with NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS (or uv run nativehtmlkit-python --diagnostics LEVEL ...):

Level Recorded Written to disk off nothing no normal (default) ERROR and WARN records, kept in memory (last 256) no debug also INFO/DEBUG yes, JSON Lines trace also TRACE (every RPC, notification, callback and dispatch) yes

The same variable controls the host's own records, which it writes to its standard error. The launcher relays the backend's output at every level and summarises host warnings and errors; informational host records are shown with NATIVEHTMLKIT_VERBOSE=1 (set automatically by --diagnostics trace).

items.title: Files
items.text:
At debug/trace each process writes python-<session>-<pid>.jsonl (mode 0600, at most 16 MiB) into the diagnostics directory:

Platform Directory any NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR if set Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\NativeHTMLKit\diagnostics Linux ~/.local/state/nativehtmlkit/diagnostics

Each line is one record:

{"schema_version": 1, "timestamp": "2026-11-16T09:12:03.120511+00:00", "session_id": "py-3f…",
 "component": "python-sdk", "pid": 41872, "level": "TRACE", "event": "rpc.completed",
 "context": {"request_id": "py-12", "method": "document.command", "duration_ms": 1, "failed": false, "error_code": null}}

Context values that are not short identifiers are replaced by "[REDACTED]"; method and op names outside the published Core contract become "unknown-method"/"unknown-op".

Useful record names:

Event Meaning host.authenticated Connected with protocol v1 rpc.started, rpc.completed, rpc.timeout, rpc.cancel_requested Requests (method, op, duration_ms, error_code, cause_seq: the event whose callback made the call) host.notification A notification arrived (method, event_type, element, event_seq) document.dispatch An event reached a document: handlers registered, matched for this event. matched: 0 explains "my handler never ran". callback.started, callback.completed, callback.failed Your callbacks (exception_type on failure) rpc.notification_dropped, host.notifications_dropped, callback.queue_overflow Events lost because callbacks were too slow transport.disconnected, transport.closed Connection ended by the host / by close() document.error, application.shutdown_received Document failures and orderly shutdown

items.title: Session id
items.text: diagnostics_session_id (also nativehtmlkit.diagnostics.SESSION_ID) identifies this run. It is taken from NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID if that holds 1–128 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -, else generated (py-<hex>), and exported again in the environment, so the launcher, the host and the backend share one id. Every NativeHTMLKitError carries it as session_id.

items.title: Support bundles
items.text:
export_support_bundle(path, *, capture_environment=False, session=None, directory=None, overwrite=False) -> Path

Write a local ZIP with manifest.json (counts, losses, SDK version, optionally OS/architecture/ Python version) and timeline.jsonl (the re-sanitised records of one session; default: this process's session, from its files or, without files, its in-memory history). Raises FileExistsError unless overwrite=True, ValueError for an invalid session id. Never included: RPC payloads, form values, credentials, environment variables, raw host output, screenshots.

From the command line (uses the most recently recorded session unless --session is given):

NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS=trace uv run app.py          # reproduce the problem
uv run nativehtmlkit-python support bundle.zip                # then export it

items.title: Host counters
items.text: app.host_diagnostics() returns the host's view (phase, windows, pending_jobs, dropped_notifications, logging counters); app.host_dropped_notifications holds the final count after run(). document.diagnostics() lists render/layout diagnostics of a document (unsupported CSS, pending resources).

items.title: In-process access
items.text:
nativehtmlkit.diagnostics.recorder() returns the process recorder: summary() (level, record count, drops, file name) and history() (the in-memory records). nativehtmlkit.diagnostics.record(event, level=..., **fields) adds a record with the same sanitisation.

See diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/diagnostics.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Document
items.text:
document = window.document          # or the return value of window.load_html(...)

A Document is a handle to the HTML document currently loaded in a Window. It reads and changes the live DOM, subscribes to events and owns live bitmaps. There is no JavaScript: Python changes the document through these methods, and the host parses, lays out and renders it.

Contents: attributes · generations and stale handles · events · text, values and attributes · markup and structure · batches · queries and nodes · focus, selection and editing · forms · dialogs and popovers · styles and environment · scrolling and geometry · resources · bitmaps · inspection · low-level command · errors

items.title: Attributes
items.text: Attribute Type Meaning window Window The window that shows this document. id str Opaque host document ID such as "d3". Never reused within a session. MAX_HANDLERS int (class attribute) 256: the most event callbacks one document accepts.

items.title: Generations and stale handles
items.text:
Each load creates a new document generation with a new id. The previous Document, its Node references, its event subscriptions and its bitmaps are retired at that moment. A document is also retired by unload(), when its window closes, when the application shuts down, and after a fatal document.error.

Every method of a retired document raises StaleDocumentError locally, before anything is sent. Events queued for a retired document are discarded, so a late callback can never change its replacement. Always reach the live document through window.document in long-lived code.

old = window.document
window.load_html("<p id='x'>new</p>")
old.set_text("x", "...")     # raises StaleDocumentError
window.document.get_text("x")   # "new"

element arguments are HTML id values. An unknown id fails with RpcError -32602 ("Unknown element ID"). Methods that also accept a Node say so; a node of another document raises ValueError, any other type TypeError.

items.title: on
items.text:
document.on(event_type: str, callback: Callable[[dict], Any], *, element: str | None = None) -> Callable[[], None]

Call callback(event) for every event_type event of this document. With element, only events whose target is that element or inside it are delivered: the event's element (nearest identified target) or one of the ids in its path (the identified bubbling route) must equal element. Returns a function that removes the subscription; once it returned, the callback is not called again, even for events already queued.

  • Callbacks run on the application event thread, one at a time, in event order. They may call any SDK method, including other documents and windows.
  • An exception in a callback is printed with its traceback to standard error and does not stop the other callbacks of the same event.
  • Notifications arrive after native dispatch: a callback cannot cancel a default action retroactively. Use prevent_default in advance.
  • Raises ValueError once 256 callbacks are registered on the document.
  • Non-bubbling events (focus, blur, invalid, toggle, close, ...) have a path with only their target. Subscribe to the target itself, or without element and filter on event["element"].

The event object and all event types are described in the events reference. The special type "error" receives {"type": "error", "message", "fatal"} for asynchronous document failures (see errors).

def on_list_click(event):
    if event["element"].startswith("delete-"):
        remove_item(event["element"].removeprefix("delete-"))

unsubscribe = document.on("click", on_list_click, element="items")   # every click inside #items

items.title: prevent_default
items.text:
document.prevent_default(element: str, event: str, *, prevent: bool = True, **key_modifiers) -> None

Register (or with prevent=False remove) a rule that cancels the native default action of event on element and its descendants before it happens. key_modifiers narrows keyboard rules: key="Enter", shift=, ctrl=, alt=, meta= (booleans). Preventable events: keydown, click, dblclick, auxclick, contextmenu, beforeinput, copy, cut, paste, mousedown, pointerdown, wheel, submit, reset, cancel, beforetoggle. Matching events report default_prevented: True. At most 256 rules per document (op set_default_action).

document.prevent_default("editor", "keydown", key="Tab")   # keep Tab inside the editor

items.title: Text, values and attributes
items.text:
Method Returns Op Notes set_text(element, text) None set_text Replace the element's children with one text node. Plain text: <b> stays literally visible. get_text(element) str get_text Concatenated text of the element and its descendants (no separators between elements). set_value(element, value) None set_value Value of an input/textarea/select. Plain text. Does not fire input/change events. get_value(element) str get_value Current control value. set_checked(element, checked) None set_checked Checkbox/radio state; no events. get_checked(element) bool get_checked set_attribute(element, name, value) None set_attribute E.g. ("bar", "style", "width:40%"), ("save", "disabled", ""). remove_attribute(element, name) None remove_attribute add_class(element, name) None add_class One class name. remove_class(element, name) None remove_class

Reading attributes has no convenience method: document.command("get_attribute", element=..., name=...) returns {"value": str | None} and document.command("get_attributes", element=...) returns {"attributes": {...}}. document.command("has_element", element=...) returns {"exists": bool}.

document.set_text("greeting", f"Hello, {user_name}")       # safe for any user_name
document.set_attribute("progress", "style", f"width:{percent}%")
document.add_class("row-3", "selected")

items.title: Markup and structure
items.text:
These methods parse trusted HTML. Escape untrusted text with html.escape() first (see the security guide).

Method Op Notes replace_html(element, html) replace_children_html Replace the element's children. insert_html(element, html, *, position="beforeend") insert_html position: "beforebegin", "afterbegin", "beforeend", "afterend". remove(element) remove_element Remove the element and its subtree.

All return None. Moving an element is available through Node.move_to or document.command("move_element", element=..., target=..., position=...); appending text through document.command("append_text", element=..., text=...) or Node.append_text; keeping only the newest children through document.command("trim_children", element=..., keep=N, **{"from": "start"}) ("start" removes the oldest children, "end" the newest).

import html
document.insert_html("log", f"<li>{html.escape(message)}</li>")
document.replace_html("results", "".join(f"<tr><td>{html.escape(n)}</td></tr>" for n in names))

items.title: batch
items.text:
document.batch(operations: Iterable[dict]) -> None

Apply up to 1024 operations as one transaction: either all succeed or none is applied (an error names the failing index, e.g. batch operation 1: Unknown element ID). Each operation is a dict with op and the op's fields, addressed by element. Allowed ops: set_text, set_attribute, remove_attribute, add_class, remove_class, insert_html (position, html), replace_children_html (html), remove_element, move_element (target, position), append_text (text), trim_children (keep, from).

node_batch is the same for Node references.

document.batch([
    {"op": "insert_html", "element": "log", "position": "beforeend", "html": rows},
    {"op": "trim_children", "element": "log", "keep": 500, "from": "start"},
    {"op": "set_text", "element": "count", "text": f"{total} records"},
])

items.title: query
items.text:
document.query(selector: str, *, offset: int = 0, limit: int = 1024) -> dict

CSS selector query. Returns {"ids", "total", "matched_nodes", "offset", "limit", "truncated"}: matched_nodes counts every match; ids lists the ids of the matches that have an id (and total counts those). limit is 1–4096.

items.title: query_nodes
items.text:
document.query_nodes(selector: str, *, offset: int = 0, limit: int = 1024) -> dict

Returns {"nodes": [{"node": ref, "element": id | None}, ...], "total", "offset"} for all matches, including elements without an id. Use this to count matches and to get node references.

rows = document.query_nodes("#results tr")["total"]
first = document.node(reference=document.query_nodes("li")["nodes"][0]["node"])

items.title: node
items.text:
document.node(element: str | None = None, *, reference: str | None = None) -> Node

node("list") resolves an element id; node() returns the document node; node(reference=ref) wraps a reference string returned by query_nodes, children, inspect or an event's node member. Passing both raises ValueError. See Node.

items.title: node_batch
items.text: document.node_batch(operations: Iterable[dict]) -> None: like batch but each operation names a node reference (and target_node for move_element).

items.title: Other queries
items.text:
Method Returns element_at_point(x, y) {"element": id \| None, "node": ref} or None; x/y in CSS pixels of the viewport focused_element() {"element", "node"} or None

Through command: text_at_point(x=, y=) → {"hit": {...}}; get_rect(element=) → {"rect": {"x", "y", "width", "height"}}; text_rects(element=|node=, start=, end=); get_html(element=|node=, outer=False, offset=0, limit=None) → {"html", "total_bytes", "offset", "next_offset", "truncated"} (byte-paged serialisation).

items.title: Focus, selection and editing
items.text:
Method Returns Notes focus(element) None element is an id or a Node. blur(element=None) None Without an argument blurs the focused element. control_selection(element) {"start", "end", "direction", "length", "node"} Text-control selection. Offsets are UTF-16 code units, not Python string indices. set_control_selection(element, start, end, *, direction="none") same shape direction: "forward", "backward", "none". replace_control_range(element, replacement, *, start=None, end=None, selection_mode="preserve") same shape plus changed Replace a range of a control's value (default: the selection). edit(command, element=None) {"accepted", "clipboard_pending"} Run an editing command through the native editor and its undo history: "undo", "redo", "cut", "copy", "paste", "select_all", "delete". Clipboard commands complete later; accepted does not mean the OS transfer succeeded.

Document text selection through command: select_text(element=), get_selection() → {"text"}, clear_selection(), copy_selection().

document.set_value("notes", "hello world")
document.set_control_selection("notes", 0, 5)
document.replace_control_range("notes", "HELLO")      # "HELLO world"
document.edit("undo", "notes")                        # back to "hello world"

items.title: Forms
Dialogs and popovers
items.text:
Method Returns Notes show_dialog(element, *, modal=True) None Open a <dialog> (modal=False for a non-modal dialog). close_dialog(element, return_value="") None Close it; fires close with return_value. show_popover(element) / hide_popover(element) None For elements with the popover attribute. toggle_popover(element) bool The new open state.

State through command: get_dialog(element=) → {"open", "modal", "return_value"} and get_popover(element=) → {"open", "kind"}. Opening and closing fire beforetoggle and toggle (with old_state/new_state); dialogs fire close, and cancel for a native close request such as Escape. See the dialogs guide.

items.title: Styles and environment
items.text:
Method Returns Notes add_stylesheet(css) {"sheet": int, "diagnostics": [...]} Attach a stylesheet after the document's own; sheet identifies it. replace_stylesheet(sheet, css) same shape Replace an attached sheet. remove_stylesheet(sheet) None stylesheets() [{"sheet", "kind", "href", "media", "length", "element", "node"}] Document <style>/<link> sheets have sheet: None; attached sheets have their number. computed_style(properties, element=None) {"schema": 1, "properties": {name: {"value", "status", "inherited"}}} element is an id, a Node or None (document element). environment() {"color_scheme", "reduced_motion", "high_contrast", "scale", "*_source", "system_*"} Effective media environment of this document. set_environment(*, color_scheme=None, reduced_motion=None) the new environment Override what @media (prefers-color-scheme) and (prefers-reduced-motion) see. color_scheme: "light", "dark", or "system" to remove the override; reduced_motion: "reduce", "no-preference" or "system". None leaves a value unchanged.

Through command: css_profile() (the supported CSS feature set) and explain(element=, property=) (why a property has its value).

sheet = document.add_stylesheet(".card { border-radius: 12px; }")["sheet"]
document.replace_stylesheet(sheet, ".card { border-radius: 4px; }")
document.set_environment(color_scheme="dark")
document.computed_style(["background-color"], "body")["properties"]["background-color"]["value"]

items.title: Scrolling and geometry
items.text:
Method Returns Notes scroll(element=None) {"x", "y", "min_x", "min_y", "max_x", "max_y", "width", "height", "scrollable", "animating"} Viewport or an element's scroll state. scroll_to(*, x=None, y=None, element=None, behavior="auto") same shape behavior: "auto", "instant", "smooth". scroll_into_view(element, *, block="nearest", inline="nearest") None block/inline like CSS: "start", "center", "end", "nearest".

Through command: scroll_by(dx=, dy=, element=) and set_scroll_follow(element=, follow=True) (keep a growing container scrolled to its end, as in a log view).

items.title: Resources
items.text:
register_resources(name, entries) -> dict atomically replaces a named in-memory bundle for this document, addressable as ui4me-res://NAME/PATH (or nativehtmlkit-res://NAME/PATH). entries maps a path to bytes or (bytes, mime_type) (default application/octet-stream). At most 256 entries and 1 MiB per registration (ValueError locally), 16 MiB across all bundles. Returns {"name", "replaced"}.

Method Returns unregister_resources(name) {"name", "removed"} resource_stats() {"bundles", "cache", "svg_rasters"} counters purge_unused_resources(url=None) {"purged", "stats"} 
document.register_resources("icons", {"ok.svg": (svg_bytes, "image/svg+xml")})
document.set_attribute("status-icon", "src", "ui4me-res://icons/ok.svg")

items.title: Bitmaps
items.text: create_bitmap(bitmap_id, width, height, *, slots=2) -> LiveBitmap: a live RGBA surface shown by <img src="ui4me-bitmap://BITMAP_ID">. See LiveBitmap.

items.title: Inspection
items.text:
Method Returns diagnostics() {"diagnostics": [{"code", "message", "stage"}], "css_profile_version"}: render/layout diagnostics such as unsupported CSS or pending resources unload() None. Unload the document: the window shows no document, this handle and its nodes become stale and window.document is None.

Through command: get_accessibility_tree() (the tree exposed to assistive technology), get_pointer_capture(), set_pointer_capture(element=, pointer_id=1, capture=True).

items.title: Low-level command
items.text:
document.command(op: str, **fields) -> Any

Send one document.command operation of the Core v1 protocol and return its result. Every method above is a thin wrapper over an op. The full op list (81 ops) and parameter schemas are part of the Core protocol release (protocol/v1/schemas/document-command.schema.json); unknown ops and unknown fields fail with RpcError -32602. Passing op twice raises TypeError.

Ops without a convenience method: append_text, clear_selection, copy_selection, css_profile, explain, get_accessibility_tree, get_attribute, get_attributes, get_dialog, get_html, get_pointer_capture, get_popover, get_rect, get_selection, has_element, move_element, node_children, get_node, scroll_by, select_text, set_pointer_capture, set_scroll_follow, text_at_point, text_rects, trim_children.

items.title: Errors
items.text:
• StaleDocumentError: the document was replaced, unloaded or closed (local, nothing sent).
  • ApplicationShutdownError: window.load_* after shutdown began.
  • RpcError codes: -32602 invalid argument (unknown id, bad op field), -32004 the host no longer knows this document, -32005 limits (for example the bitmap budget), -32008 wrong lifecycle phase (after shutdown began).
  • Asynchronous failures arrive as document.error: the SDK prints the message to standard error and calls handlers registered with document.on("error", ...) with {"type": "error", "message": str, "fatal": bool}. After a fatal error the host has unloaded the document: it is retired and window.document becomes None (an error handler may load a replacement).

See errors for the exception classes.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/document.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Variables you may set
items.text:
Variable Effect NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 Application.start() and nativehtmlkit-python run start the host with --headless: the whole protocol runs without native windows (for CI and tests). Native services (dialogs, clipboard, external open, attention) then fail with RpcError -32001 and there is no user input. NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS off, normal (default), debug, trace: SDK and host diagnostics level. NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR Directory for the SDK's diagnostics files (debug/trace). NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID Correlation id shared by launcher, host and backend; generated when unset or invalid. NATIVEHTMLKIT_VERBOSE=1 The launcher also shows the host's informational records. NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_LOG=FILE Append the host's raw JSON log records to FILE (0600). Sensitive: includes backend output. Same as run --host-log. NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY=PATH Use this host executable instead of the bundled one (development override; it is not hash-verified). UI4ME_HOST_BINARY is an accepted older spelling. NATIVEHTMLKIT_ALLOW_PATH_HOST=1 If the wheel has no bundled host, allow an unpinned nativehtmlkit-host found in an absolute PATH entry (a warning is printed).

Host resolution order: NATIVEHTMLKIT_HOST_BINARY, then the bundled host (verified against HOST-MANIFEST.json on every launch), then (only with NATIVEHTMLKIT_ALLOW_PATH_HOST=1) PATH. nativehtmlkit.host_binary() returns the path that would be used, applying the same checks.

items.title: Variables the SDK sets
items.text: Variable Where Meaning PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 backend Added by Application.start() and the runner unless you set them, so print() output reaches your console immediately and as UTF-8. NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_ID every process Exported with the effective session id. UI4ME_DIRECT_START host and backend Internal marker of Application.start(); prevents a backend without a host connection from starting another host. Removed in the backend after connecting.

items.title: Variables the host sets for the backend
items.text:
UI4ME_ENDPOINT (socket path or pipe name), UI4ME_TOKEN (single-use 64-hex launch credential), UI4ME_APP_ID and UI4ME_PROTOCOL_VERSION (1). These are the permanent names of protocol v1. The SDK reads them once and removes them from os.environ when it connects (also when connecting fails), so child processes of your application never inherit the credential. Never set them yourself; having only one of the two connection variables raises StartupError.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/environment-variables.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Errors
items.text:
from nativehtmlkit import (NativeHTMLKitError, RpcError, RpcTimeoutError, HostDisconnectedError,
                           DisconnectedError, HostProtocolError, ProtocolError, StaleDocumentError,
                           StartupError)

Every SDK error derives from NativeHTMLKitError. Catch it to handle "anything NativeHTMLKit"; catch the subclasses to react precisely. Never parse str(error): use the attributes.

items.title: Hierarchy
items.text:
NativeHTMLKitError (Exception)
├── RpcError                          code = numeric wire error code
│   └── ClientBusyError               local back-pressure, nothing sent       (nativehtmlkit.client)
├── RpcTimeoutError (TimeoutError)    local deadline expired, outcome unknown
├── HostDisconnectedError (ConnectionError)
│   └── DisconnectedError             connection lost or closed, outcome unknown
├── HostProtocolError
│   └── ProtocolError                 the host broke wire v1 (fatal)
├── LocalRequestError (ValueError)    request not encodable / > 2 MiB, nothing sent (nativehtmlkit.errors)
├── StaleHandleError                                                         (nativehtmlkit.errors)
│   ├── StaleDocumentError (RuntimeError)   window/document/node no longer live
│   └── ApplicationShutdownError (RuntimeError)   shutdown began, no new windows/documents
├── StartupError (RuntimeError)       host could not be started or reached
├── HostVerificationError (FileNotFoundError)   bundled host fails its SHA-256 pin (nativehtmlkit.errors)
└── UnsupportedFeatureError                                                  (nativehtmlkit.errors)

Classes without a module note are exported by nativehtmlkit. StaleDocumentError and ApplicationShutdownError share the base StaleHandleError; StartupError is in nativehtmlkit._bootstrap and re-exported.

items.title: Common attributes
items.text: Attribute Meaning classification Stable category string, e.g. "NHK-HOST-RPC", "NHK-HANDLE-STALE" code Same as classification, except on RpcError, where it is the numeric wire code operation The RPC method involved, if any (e.g. "document.command") request_id The SDK's wire request id, if any session_id The diagnostics session id of this process data Extra error data from the host (RpcError) retryable False for all current classes outcome_unknown True when the host may or may not have applied the operation (RpcTimeoutError, disconnects). The SDK never claims a rollback. Class classification RpcError NHK-HOST-RPC ClientBusyError NHK-CLIENT-BUSY (code -32005, local=True) RpcTimeoutError NHK-TRANSPORT-TIMEOUT HostDisconnectedError, DisconnectedError NHK-HOST-DISCONNECTED (plus pending_failed: requests failed by the same event) HostProtocolError, ProtocolError NHK-PROTOCOL-MALFORMED LocalRequestError NHK-REQUEST-INVALID StaleHandleError, StaleDocumentError NHK-HANDLE-STALE ApplicationShutdownError NHK-APP-SHUTDOWN StartupError NHK-STARTUP HostVerificationError NHK-HOST-UNVERIFIED UnsupportedFeatureError NHK-FEATURE-UNSUPPORTED

items.title: RpcError
items.text:
RpcError(code, message, data=None, *, operation=None, request_id=None); members code (int), message (host text, for logs only), data, local (False for host errors) and error_id (same as classification). Wire codes:

Code Name Typical cause -32600 invalid request malformed envelope -32601 method not found unknown method -32602 invalid params unknown element id, unknown member, bad argument -32603 internal unexpected host failure -32001 unsupported not available here: headless mode, no desktop service, platform policy (e.g. Wayland placement) -32002 unavailable a service or file is missing at run time (e.g. load_file of a missing file) -32003 denied policy refusal (e.g. open_external with an unsupported URI scheme) -32004 closed window or document no longer exists in the host -32005 busy a limit was reached (windows, 1 MiB HTML, bitmap budget, one dialog per window, pending requests) -32006 cancelled request cancelled -32007 disconnected -32008 invalid state wrong lifecycle phase: app.ready without a window or most calls after shutdown began -32009 timeout -32010 version mismatch protocol version is not 1 -32011 unauthenticated wrong or missing launch token

Treat unknown codes as failures.

items.title: StaleDocumentError
items.text: Raised locally, before anything is sent, when you use a Window that is closed, or a Document/Node that was replaced, unloaded, closed or retired by shutdown. It is a RuntimeError. (If the host itself receives a stale id, it answers RpcError -32004 instead.)

items.title: Patterns
items.text:
from nativehtmlkit import NativeHTMLKitError, RpcError, StaleDocumentError

try:
    window.document.set_text("status", "Saved")
except StaleDocumentError:
    pass                         # the window was closed meanwhile; nothing to update
except RpcError as error:
    if error.code == -32602:
        print("No element with that id")
    else:
        raise

In background threads that update the UI, catch NativeHTMLKitError around each update and stop the thread when it occurs: it covers stale handles, shutdown and disconnects.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/errors.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Event objects
items.text: Callbacks registered with Document.on receive one dict per event. The host creates it after native dispatch; the SDK adds window_id and document_id.

items.title: Common members
items.text:
Member Type Meaning type str Event type, e.g. "click". element str id of the nearest element with an id, starting at the target ("" if none). path list[str] Ids of the identified elements on the bubbling route, innermost first. For non-bubbling events only the target's entry. node str Node reference of the actual target, usable with document.node(reference=...). window_id, document_id str Where the event happened. detail int Click count for pointer events, else 0. cancelable bool Whether the event has a cancelable default action. default_prevented bool Present when cancelable: whether a prevent_default rule cancelled it. shift, ctrl, alt, meta bool Modifier state.

Members beginning with _ are internal and may change.

items.title: Control state (when the target is a form control)
items.text: Member Meaning value Current value of an input, textarea or select checked Checkbox/radio state selection {"start", "end", "direction"} for text controls (UTF-16 offsets) files Selected files of an <input type="file">

items.title: Type-specific members (present when they apply)
items.text: Member Events key, code, repeat, is_composing keydown, keyup: key is the logical key: the character for printable keys ("a", "A"), otherwise a key name such as "Enter", "Escape", "Tab", "ArrowDown", "Space"; code names the physical key ("KeyA", "Enter") data, input_type beforeinput, input, composition events x, y, button, buttons pointer, mouse and wheel events (x/y in CSS pixels) delta_x, delta_y wheel pointer_id, pointer_type, is_primary, pressure pointer events related_node, related_element mouseover/mouseout/focusin/focusout and similar submitter submit: id of the button that submitted (if it has one) validity invalid: {"valid", "message", "flags"} as from Document.validity old_state, new_state beforetoggle, toggle ("open"/"closed") return_value close of a <dialog> property_name, elapsed_time, pseudo_element transition* animation_name, elapsed_time, pseudo_element animation*

items.title: Event types
items.text:
The host listens for these types on every document and forwards each one; subscribe to the ones you need:

Group Types Pointer and mouse click, dblclick, auxclick, contextmenu, mousedown, mouseup, mousemove, mouseover, mouseout, mouseenter, mouseleave, pointerdown, pointerup, pointermove, pointercancel, gotpointercapture, lostpointercapture, wheel Keyboard and text keydown, keyup, beforeinput, input, compositionstart, compositionupdate, compositionend Focus focus, blur, focusin, focusout Forms change, submit, reset, invalid, select Selection and clipboard selectionchange, copy, cut, paste Dialogs and popovers toggle, beforetoggle, cancel, close Scrolling scroll Transitions and animations transitionrun, transitionstart, transitionend, transitioncancel, animationstart, animationiteration, animationend, animationcancel

Two further types come from the host rather than the DOM:

Type Members When link_activated element, href, url (resolved, or None), node A link (<a href>) was activated. Documents never navigate; handle this event, e.g. with Application.open_external. environment_changed environment The desktop preferences changed the document's media environment.

And the SDK's own error type: {"type": "error", "message", "fatal"} for document.error notifications (see Document errors).

items.title: Programmatic changes do not fire events
items.text: set_value, set_checked, set_text and the other mutation methods change the DOM without firing input, change or similar events; they model a script assignment, not user input. request_submit, reset_form, show_dialog/close_dialog and the popover methods do fire their events (submit/invalid, reset, beforetoggle/toggle/close). If your handler must also run after a programmatic change, call it yourself.

items.title: Delegation example
items.text:
# <ul id="todos"><li id="todo-3"><input id="todo-3-done" type="checkbox"> ...
#   <button id="todo-3-delete">Delete</button></li></ul>

def on_click(event):
    # A click on the Delete button: element == "todo-3-delete",
    # path == ["todo-3-delete", "todo-3", "todos", ...]
    if event["element"].endswith("-delete"):
        delete(int(event["element"].split("-")[1]))

def on_change(event):
    if event["element"].endswith("-done"):
        set_done(int(event["element"].split("-")[1]), event["checked"])

document.on("click", on_click, element="todos")
document.on("change", on_change, element="todos")

See events and callbacks for threading and ordering.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/events.md · edit the page there.

items.title: LiveBitmap
items.text:
from nativehtmlkit import LiveBitmap   # type; create with Document.create_bitmap
bitmap = document.create_bitmap("chart", 480, 200)

A live bitmap shows pixels that Python renders, for charts, previews, plots or video-like surfaces, in an <img> of the document:

<img id="chart" src="ui4me-bitmap://chart" width="480" height="200" alt="Live chart">

(nativehtmlkit-bitmap://chart is an equivalent spelling.) Frames travel through a private shared-memory file the host creates in its runtime directory; nothing is encoded or sent over the socket except a small bitmap.present request.

items.title: Document.create_bitmap
items.text:
document.create_bitmap(bitmap_id: str, width: int, height: int, *, slots: int = 2) -> LiveBitmap
Parameter Rules bitmap_id 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, _ or - (ValueError otherwise); matches the img URL width, height 1–4096 pixels (ValueError otherwise) slots 2 or 3 frame slots

Raises StaleDocumentError for a retired document and RpcError -32005 when the host's bitmap budget is exhausted (per document: 8 bitmaps and 64 MiB of slots; host-wide: 256 MiB).

items.title: Attributes
items.text: Attribute Meaning id, width, height As created stride Bytes per row: width * 4 slots, slot_bytes Slot count and bytes per frame (width * height * 4) path The host-chosen transport file (informational; the host may unlink it after the first frame)

items.title: Frame format
items.text: Straight (non-premultiplied) alpha RGBA8, row-major, top row first, tightly packed: byte (y * width + x) * 4 is the red value of pixel (x, y). Pass bytes, bytearray or any buffer whose memoryview has exactly slot_bytes bytes.

items.title: present
items.text: bitmap.present(pixels) -> dict. Write one frame and return after the host copied it: {"sequence": int, "presented_to_engine": bool, "slot_released": True}. Raises ValueError for a wrong length, RuntimeError if the bitmap is closed, StaleDocumentError if its document is retired. Thread-safe; concurrent calls are serialised. Do not modify the buffer during the call.

items.title: try_present
items.text: bitmap.try_present(pixels) -> dict | None. Like present, but returns None immediately when another present of this bitmap is still in progress. Use it from a producer loop to drop a frame instead of queueing.

items.title: close
items.text: bitmap.close() -> None. Release the bitmap (idempotent). Bitmaps are also released automatically when their document is retired (reload, unload, window closed, shutdown). Usable as a context manager: with document.create_bitmap(...) as bitmap:.

items.title: Example
items.text:
WIDTH, HEIGHT = 256, 64
bitmap = document.create_bitmap("gradient", WIDTH, HEIGHT)
frame = bytearray(WIDTH * HEIGHT * 4)
for y in range(HEIGHT):
    for x in range(WIDTH):
        i = (y * WIDTH + x) * 4
        frame[i:i + 4] = bytes((x, 64, 255 - x, 255))
bitmap.present(frame)

Pure-Python per-pixel loops are slow; draw a background once and copy it (bytearray(background)), then touch only the pixels that change. The live chart example renders 480×200 at 30 frames per second this way. See also the live bitmaps guide.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/live-bitmap.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Node
items.text:
from nativehtmlkit import Node
node = document.node("list")                               # from an element id
node = document.node(reference=event["node"])              # from an event or a query

A Node is an opaque reference to one node of one document generation: elements (with or without an id), text nodes and the document node. Use nodes to work with elements that have no id, such as rows rendered from data or markup you did not write.

items.title: Attributes
items.text:
Attribute Type Meaning document Document The document the reference belongs to. id str The reference string, e.g. "node:1:43:1". Treat it as opaque.

Node(document, reference) raises ValueError for an empty reference; prefer document.node(...). References never resolve in another document: when the document is replaced, unloaded or closed, every method raises StaleDocumentError locally. A reference to a node that was removed from a live document fails with RpcError.

items.title: inspect
items.text: node.inspect() -> dict: {"node", "type", "name", "id", "attributes", "parent", "previous", "next", "child_count"} for elements; text nodes have "text" instead of name/attributes; the document node has type: "document". parent/previous/next are references or None.

items.title: children
items.text:
node.children(*, offset=0, limit=256) -> dict: {"children": [{"node", "type", "name", "id"}], "total"}, paginated. Whitespace between tags appears as text nodes.

listing = document.node("menu").children()
for child in listing["children"]:
    if child["type"] == "element":
        print(child["name"], child["id"], child["node"])

items.title: Changing
items.text:
Every mutation is a one-operation node_batch.

Method Effect set_text(text) Replace the children with one text node (plain text). append_text(text) Append a text node. set_attribute(name, value) / remove_attribute(name) add_class(name) / remove_class(name) insert_html(html, *, position="beforeend") Trusted markup; position as in Document.insert_html. replace_html(html) Replace the children with trusted markup. trim_children(keep, *, from_start=True) Keep keep children: from_start=True removes the oldest (first) children, False the newest (last). remove() Remove the node and its subtree. focus() / blur() Same as document.focus(node) / document.blur(node).

items.title: move_to
items.text:
node.move_to(target: Node, *, position: str = "beforeend") -> None

Move this node relative to target ("beforebegin", "afterbegin", "beforeend", "afterend"). Both nodes must belong to the same document (ValueError otherwise).

items = document.query_nodes("#playlist li")["nodes"]
second = document.node(reference=items[1]["node"])
first = document.node(reference=items[0]["node"])
second.move_to(first, position="beforebegin")              # swap the first two entries

Document methods that accept element: str | Node (focus, blur, control_selection, set_control_selection, replace_control_range, edit, reset_form, request_submit, form_data, set_custom_validity, computed_style) take nodes too.

The DOM explorer example walks and edits a tree of id-less elements with these methods.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/node.md · edit the page there.

items.title: RpcClient: the host connection
items.text:
from nativehtmlkit import RpcClient
rpc = app.rpc

RpcClient is the authenticated, length-prefixed JSON-RPC connection to the Core host (Unix socket on Linux, named pipe on Windows). Application, Window and Document are built on it. Use it directly for Core v1 methods that have no convenience wrapper, such as desktop.paths, window.list or document.get. Parameters and results are those of the public Core wire protocol v1 (method list and JSON schemas ship with the Core release under protocol/v1/).

items.title: Attributes
items.text: Attribute Meaning hello The host.hello result: protocol_version, host_version, app_id, capabilities (set by from_environment) closed (property) True once the connection ended closed_locally (property) True when close() ended it (not the host or a transport error) shutdown_requested threading.Event, set when the host announced app.shutdown dropped_notifications Notifications the SDK dropped because its callback queue (128) was full

items.title: call
items.text:
rpc.call(method: str, params: dict | None = None, *, timeout=<default>) -> Any

Send a request and wait for the result. The default timeout is 15 s, and none for dialog.* methods (a person is answering). An explicit timeout=None waits forever. On timeout the SDK asks the host to cancel and raises RpcTimeoutError; the remote outcome is unknown. If the reply won the race against the deadline, its result is returned.

Raises RpcError (host error, code is the numeric wire code), ClientBusyError (an RpcError with local=True: more than 128 requests pending or the 8 MiB outgoing buffer is full; nothing was sent), LocalRequestError (ValueError: the request is not JSON-encodable, has non-string keys or exceeds the 2 MiB frame; nothing was sent), DisconnectedError, RpcTimeoutError.

paths = app.rpc.call("desktop.paths")        # {"config", "data", "cache", "state", "runtime"}
for w in app.rpc.call("window.list"):
    print(w["window_id"], w["title"])

desktop.paths returns per-application directories named after the app id (XDG directories on Linux, the AppData folders on Windows). The directories are not created for you.

items.title: call_async
items.text:
rpc.call_async(method: str, params: dict | None = None) -> concurrent.futures.Future

Send a request and return a Future. Done-callbacks run on a short-lived nativehtmlkit-completion thread per result, so they may call synchronous SDK methods. future.cancel() asks the host to cancel (advisory).

future = app.rpc.call_async("window.get", {"window_id": window.id})
future.add_done_callback(lambda f: print(f.result()["title"]))

items.title: notify
items.text: rpc.notify(method: str, params: dict | None = None) -> None: send a notification (no reply), for example request.cancel.

items.title: Host-to-client messages
items.text: Method Meaning on_request(method, callback) Answer host requests (window.before_close, app.before_quit): callback(params) returns the result ({"allow": bool}). One handler per method. Prefer Window.on_before_close / Application.on_before_quit, which Application routes through these. on_notification(method, callback) Handle host notifications: callback(params). One handler per method; Application already uses document.event, document.error, window.event and app.shutdown. Registering one of those replaces the SDK's own handler and breaks the object model; use it for others such as app.activated (a second launch of a single-instance app: {"args", "cwd", "activation_token"}).

items.title: Lifetime
items.text:
Method Meaning wait(timeout=None) -> bool Wait until the connection closed flush(timeout=2.0) Wait until queued outgoing messages were written; TimeoutError otherwise wait_for_notifications(timeout) -> bool Wait until already received ordered notifications were handled close() Close the connection; pending requests fail with DisconnectedError

Construction: RpcClient(stream, *, workers=4, ordered_notifications=False) and RpcClient.from_environment(*, workers=4, ordered_notifications=False) are used by Application.from_environment(); applications rarely construct a client themselves.

items.title: Threads
items.text:
The client runs a reader and a writer thread that never execute application code, four worker threads for host requests (and app.shutdown), and, for an Application, one ordered "application events" thread for notifications. A full callback queue drops further notifications (counted in dropped_notifications) and answers further host requests with error -32005, which the host treats as a denial. See architecture.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/rpc.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Window
items.text:
from nativehtmlkit import Window   # type only; windows come from Application

A Window is a handle to one native top-level window. Create it with Application.create_window, open_html or open_file. Each window holds at most one Document at a time.

items.title: Attributes
items.text: Attribute Type Meaning app Application The owning application. id str Opaque host ID such as "w1". Never reused within a session. document Document \| None The current document, None before the first load or after unload(). closed bool True once the host reported the window closed or the application shut down.

items.title: Stale-handle semantics
items.text: When the window closes (its closed window event, or app.shutdown for the last window) the SDK sets closed = True and retires its document. Every later call on the window, its document or its nodes raises StaleDocumentError locally, without contacting the host. Check window.closed or catch the error in code that may outlive a window (threads, timers, futures).

items.title: load_html
items.text:
window.load_html(html: str, *, asset_root: str | Path | None = None) -> Document

Replace the window's document with html (at most 1 MiB, else RpcError -32005). asset_root is the directory for relative URLs; it is resolved to an absolute path. The previous document is retired only after the new one loaded successfully: a failed load leaves the old document live. Returns the new Document, also available as window.document.

items.title: load_file
items.text:
window.load_file(path: str | Path, *, asset_root: str | Path | None = None) -> Document

Load a UTF-8 HTML file of at most 1 MiB. The path is resolved to an absolute path; asset_root defaults to the file's directory, so <link href="style.css"> and <img src="logo.png"> next to the file work. A missing file fails with RpcError -32002.

Both raise StaleDocumentError if the window is closed and ApplicationShutdownError once the application is shutting down. The host admits at most 16 live documents.

document = window.load_file(Path(__file__).with_name("index.html"))
document.set_text("status", "Loaded")

items.title: state
items.text:
window.state() -> dict returns the window description (window.get):

Member Meaning window_id, title, width, height, visible As requested, logical pixels native False in headless mode scale_factor Display scale physical_size Actual size in physical pixels, or None requested {"visible", "resizable", "decorations", "size_constraints": {"min_width", "min_height", "max_width", "max_height"}} observed {"focused", "minimized", "maximized", "fullscreen", "resizable", "decorations", "visible", "theme", "position"}; each None when the platform cannot report it (always in headless mode) closing True while a close is in progress

app.rpc.call("window.list") returns the same description for every open window.

items.title: set
items.text:
window.set(**properties) -> dict

Change window properties and return the updated description. Accepted keywords (all optional):

Keyword Type title str width, height int, logical pixels visible, resizable, decorations bool minimized, maximized, fullscreen bool focus bool (True asks for focus) x, y int, together; screen position min_width + min_height, max_width + max_height int pairs; None removes the constraint

Unknown keywords, and x without y, fail with RpcError -32602. Platform limits are reported as RpcError -32001. On Linux the Wayland compositor owns placement and focus: x/y and minimized=False are always refused there, and focus=True and visible are refused for an existing native window. On Windows all members are applied. The observed members of the returned description show what the platform actually did.

window.set(title="Report — saved", width=1024, height=720)
window.set(min_width=480, min_height=320)
window.set(maximized=True)

items.title: request_attention
items.text:
window.request_attention(kind: str | None = "informational") -> dict

Ask the desktop to draw attention to the window: "informational", "critical", or None to clear the request. Returns {"requested": True, "kind", "presented": None, "policy"}. Raises RpcError -32001 in headless mode and where the window manager does not support it (Wayland cannot clear a request).

items.title: request_close
items.text: window.request_close() -> None. Ask to close the window as if the user had. The host sends close_requested (reason backend_request), asks the window's on_before_close policy, then closes the window (closed event). Closing the last window quits the application (after on_before_quit). Before app.ready, closing the last usable window cancels start-up.

items.title: on_before_close
items.text:
window.on_before_close(callback: Callable[[], bool]) -> None

Install a close policy for this window: callback() returns True to allow closing and False to keep the window open (for example to show an "unsaved changes" banner). One policy per window; a new call replaces it. Windows without a policy always close. The callback runs on an SDK worker thread and must answer promptly (the host waits indefinitely); it may call the SDK. An exception counts as deny.

def allow_close() -> bool:
    if editor.dirty:
        window.document.add_class("unsaved-banner", "shown")
        return False
    return True
window.on_before_close(allow_close)

items.title: Native file dialogs
items.text:
window.open_files(*, multiple=False, title=None, directory=None, filters=(), wait=True)
window.save_file(*, file_name=None, title=None, directory=None, filters=(), wait=True)
window.choose_folder(*, title=None, directory=None, wait=True)

Show a native dialog parented to this window. filters is a list of {"name": "Images", "extensions": ["png", "jpg"]} (extensions without the dot). directory is the start folder.

The result is a dict: {"cancelled": bool, "paths": [str, ...]}. paths has one entry for save_file and choose_folder, and one or more for open_files(multiple=True); it is empty when the user cancelled.

  • wait=True (default) blocks until the user answers. There is no timeout.
  • wait=False returns a concurrent.futures.Future at once; read it in a done-callback. future.cancel() asks the host to close the native dialog.

Errors: RpcError -32001 in headless mode and without a desktop dialog service (on Linux the desktop portal), -32005 if this window already shows a native dialog or the host's service limit is reached, StaleDocumentError for a closed window. With wait=False the error is set on the future.

def done(future):
    try:
        result = future.result()
    except RpcError as error:
        print("no dialog:", error.code)
        return
    if not result["cancelled"]:
        window.document.set_text("chosen", result["paths"][0])

window.open_files(title="Choose an image", filters=[{"name": "Images", "extensions": ["png", "jpg"]}],
                  wait=False).add_done_callback(done)

A blocking (wait=True) dialog inside an event callback holds up later document and window events until it closes. Prefer wait=False there. See the file dialogs guide.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/reference/window.md · edit the page there.
