items.title: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview
items.text:
In this tutorial you build a small admin tool with the NativeHTMLKit Python SDK: pick a folder, type a find/replace rule (plain text or regular expression), see a live preview of the new names with conflicts flagged, confirm in a dialog, rename, and undo. It takes about 30 minutes.

You will learn how to split an app into index.html, style.css and app.py, keep decisions in a pure function, update a preview live from input events, render file names safely, use the native folder picker with a fallback, confirm with an HTML dialog, handle errors per file, and test the whole thing without a screen.

The finished app is examples/bulk_rename: app.py, index.html and style.css. Every app.py excerpt below is copied from that file, which the repository's test suite runs against the real native host.

You need uv on Linux x64 (glibc 2.39+) or Windows x64, and a desktop session.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 1: create the project
items.text:
uvx --from nativehtmlkit nativehtmlkit-new BulkRename --name "Bulk rename"
cd BulkRename
uv run app.py               # installs nativehtmlkit into the project on first run

A window with a name field and an Add item button opens. Close it. You now have app.py, index.html, style.css, pyproject.toml and app.toml (see project scaffolding). Read lifecycle if you want to know why app.py runs twice.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 2: the page
items.text:
Replace index.html and style.css with the files from examples/bulk_rename. The page has four parts, each addressed by element ids that the Python code uses:

  • a header with the folder box (folder), Browse... (browse) and Load (load);
  • the rule form rule with find, replace and the checkboxes regex and case;
  • the preview table body preview;
  • a footer with the summary line summary, Undo last rename (undo) and Rename (apply), plus a <dialog id="confirm"> with confirm-text, confirm-no and confirm-yes.

All behaviour lives in Python; the page has no scripts. style.css uses prefers-color-scheme, so the tool follows the desktop's light or dark mode, and a flex column layout in which only the table scrolls (see styling and layout).
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 3: the skeleton
items.text:
Replace app.py with this skeleton. It loads the page from the script's folder; relative URLs in index.html (the stylesheet) resolve against that folder.

app.py (step 3)
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


class BulkRename:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, window):
        self.app, self.window, self.document = app, window, window.document
        # Steps 5-8 add state, methods and event handlers here.


def build(app: Application, folder: str | None = None) -> BulkRename:
    window = app.open_file(HERE / "index.html", title="Bulk rename", width=900, height=620,
                           min_width=640, min_height=400)
    return BulkRename(app, window)


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Bulk rename") as app:
        build(app, sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run it: the window shows the empty tool. The launcher passes your command-line arguments to the backend run, so uv run app.py ~/Pictures will reach build() as folder in step 5.

build(app, ...) returns the object that owns the window. main() uses it, and so will the test in step 9.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 4: plan the renames without any UI
items.text:
Keep the logic that decides new names separate from the window. A pure function, with no SDK calls and no file system access, is easy to reason about and to test. The finished file starts with these imports and constants:

app.py
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import os
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Document, RpcError

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
WINDOWS = sys.platform == "win32"
INVALID_CHARACTERS = set('<>:"/\\|?*' + "".join(map(chr, range(32)))) if WINDOWS else {"/", "\0"}

Add the planning code below them:

app.py
@dataclass
class Row:
    old: str
    new: str
    status: str = "unchanged"     # unchanged | rename | conflict | invalid | error
    note: str = ""


def plan_renames(names: list[str], find: str, replace: str, *, regex: bool, match_case: bool) -> list[Row]:
    """One row per file name; never touches the disk."""
    rows = [Row(name, name) for name in names]
    if not find:
        return rows
    try:
        pattern = re.compile(find if regex else re.escape(find), 0 if match_case else re.IGNORECASE)
        # Plain-text mode: the replacement is literal text (a function bypasses \1 processing).
        replacement = replace if regex else (lambda _match: replace)
        new_names = [pattern.sub(replacement, name) for name in names]
    except (re.error, IndexError) as error:          # bad pattern, or \3 with only two groups
        for row in rows:
            row.status, row.note = "error", f"Invalid pattern: {error}"
        return rows

    def key(name: str) -> str:                       # Windows file names are case-insensitive
        return name.casefold() if WINDOWS else name

    existing = {key(name) for name in names}
    claimed: set[str] = set()
    for row, new in zip(rows, new_names):
        row.new = new
        if new == row.old:
            continue
        if not new or new in (".", "..") or INVALID_CHARACTERS & set(new):
            row.status, row.note = "invalid", "Not a valid file name"
        elif (key(new) in existing and key(new) != key(row.old)) or key(new) in claimed:
            row.status, row.note = "conflict", "Name already used"
        else:
            row.status = "rename"
            claimed.add(key(new))
    return rows

It escapes the find text in plain-text mode and uses a function as the replacement, so $, \ and \1 in the replacement stay literal text. It reports an invalid regular expression on every row instead of raising, refuses names with characters the file system does not allow (only / on Linux; <>:"/\|?* and control characters on Windows), and flags a conflict when the new name already exists or two files would get the same name (case-insensitively on Windows).

In regular-expression mode the replacement uses Python's syntax: \1 or \g<1> for groups.

Try it in a Python console (paste the imports and the planning code first):

for row in plan_renames(["IMG_0001.jpg", "IMG_0002.jpg", "notes.txt"], "IMG_", "photo-",
                        regex=False, match_case=False):
    print(row)
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 5: list files and preview live
items.text:
Now fill in the class. Its __init__ holds the state and connects every event of the page; the handlers for Browse..., Rename, the dialog buttons and Undo call methods you add in steps 6 to 8:

app.py
class BulkRename:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, window):
        self.app, self.window, self.document = app, window, window.document
        self.folder: Path | None = None
        self.names: list[str] = []
        self.plan: list[Row] = []
        self.undo_steps: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        doc = self.document
        # The top-level flag says whether the host offers native dialogs in this session.
        # (features["file_dialogs"]["available"] is None, "not observed", on a native desktop.)
        if not app.capabilities().get("file_dialogs"):
            doc.set_attribute("browse", "disabled", "")
        # Live preview: every keystroke or checkbox change in the rule form.
        doc.on("input", lambda _event: self.update_preview(), element="rule")
        doc.on("change", lambda _event: self.update_preview(), element="rule")
        # Enter in a rule field submits the form: treat it as "update preview", nothing else.
        doc.on("submit", lambda _event: self.update_preview(), element="rule")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.open_folder(doc.get_value("folder")), element="load")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.browse(), element="browse")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.ask_confirmation(), element="apply")
        # Decide in the button handlers, not in the dialog's close event: a <dialog> keeps its
        # previous return value when the user dismisses it with Escape.
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.confirm(False), element="confirm-no")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.confirm(True), element="confirm-yes")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.undo(), element="undo")

input fires on every keystroke in the rule form (the handler sits on the form and receives events from all its fields), change when a checkbox toggles, and submit when the user presses Enter in a field. All three only update the preview.

The preview methods read the rule, plan, and render:

app.py
    def set_summary(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.document.set_text("summary", text)

    def set_enabled(self, element: str, enabled: bool) -> None:
        if enabled:
            self.document.remove_attribute(element, "disabled")
        else:
            self.document.set_attribute(element, "disabled", "")

    def update_preview(self) -> None:
        doc = self.document
        self.plan = plan_renames(self.names, doc.get_value("find"), doc.get_value("replace"),
                                 regex=doc.get_checked("regex"), match_case=doc.get_checked("case"))
        # File names are untrusted text: escape every cell. The status class comes from a fixed set.
        cells = "".join(f'<tr class="{row.status}"><td>{html.escape(row.old)}</td><td>{html.escape(row.new)}</td>'
                        f'<td>{html.escape(row.note or row.status)}</td></tr>' for row in self.plan)
        count = sum(row.status == "rename" for row in self.plan)
        blocked = sum(row.status in ("conflict", "invalid", "error") for row in self.plan)
        summary = f"{len(self.names)} file(s), {count} to rename" + (f", {blocked} skipped" if blocked else "")
        doc.batch([
            {"op": "replace_children_html", "element": "preview", "html": cells},
            {"op": "set_text", "element": "summary", "text": summary},
            {"op": "set_text", "element": "apply", "text": f"Rename {count}"},
        ])
        self.set_enabled("apply", count > 0)

    def update_file_list(self) -> None:
        self.names = sorted(entry.name for entry in self.folder.iterdir() if entry.is_file())
        self.update_preview()

    def open_folder(self, path: str) -> None:
        if not path or not Path(path).is_dir():
            self.set_summary("That folder does not exist.")
            return
        self.folder = Path(path).resolve()
        self.document.set_value("folder", str(self.folder))
        self.set_undo([])
        self.update_file_list()
app.py
    def set_undo(self, steps: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
        self.undo_steps = steps
        self.set_enabled("undo", bool(steps))

Everything shown in the table is a file name, which is untrusted text, so each cell goes through html.escape. The status class (rename, conflict, ...) comes from a fixed set and styles the row. The table, the summary and the button label change in one batch, so the user never sees a half-updated view. A disabled button is an HTML attribute: set_attribute(id, "disabled", "") turns it on, remove_attribute turns it off.

Finally, open the folder passed on the command line. Replace build() with the finished version:

app.py
def build(app: Application, folder: str | None = None) -> BulkRename:
    # Relative URLs in index.html (style.css) resolve against the file's folder.
    window = app.open_file(HERE / "index.html", title="Bulk rename", width=900, height=620,
                           min_width=640, min_height=400)
    tool = BulkRename(app, window)
    if folder:
        tool.open_folder(folder)
    return tool


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Bulk rename") as app:
        build(app, sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None)
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run uv run app.py <a folder with some files>. Type IMG_ in Find and photo- in Replace with: the preview updates while you type, and the summary counts the files that would be renamed.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 6: choose the folder with the native dialog
items.text:
The capability check in __init__ disables Browse... where the host cannot show native dialogs (for example in headless test runs):

        # The top-level flag says whether the host offers native dialogs in this session.
        # (features["file_dialogs"]["available"] is None, "not observed", on a native desktop.)
        if not app.capabilities().get("file_dialogs"):
            doc.set_attribute("browse", "disabled", "")

The button's handler opens the folder picker without blocking the event thread (wait=False) and handles the answer in a done-callback:

app.py
    def browse(self) -> None:
        def done(future) -> None:
            try:
                result = future.result()
            except RpcError as error:        # -32001: no dialog service in this session
                self.set_summary("Native file dialogs are not available in this session."
                                 if error.code == -32001 else f"The folder dialog failed (error {error.code}).")
                return
            if not result["cancelled"]:
                self.open_folder(result["paths"][0])
        # wait=False keeps the event thread free while the dialog is open.
        self.window.choose_folder(title="Folder with files to rename", wait=False).add_done_callback(done)

A cancelled dialog returns {"cancelled": True, "paths": []}. Without a dialog service the future raises RpcError -32001 and the summary says so. See file dialogs.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 7: confirm and rename
items.text:
Renaming is destructive, so ask first in an HTML <dialog>. Rename fills the dialog text and opens it modally; the dialog's buttons close it and decide. Escape closes the dialog without a click, which counts as "no".

app.py
    def ask_confirmation(self) -> None:
        count = sum(row.status == "rename" for row in self.plan)
        self.document.set_text("confirm-text", f"Rename {count} file(s) in {self.folder}?")
        self.document.show_dialog("confirm")

    def confirm(self, yes: bool) -> None:
        self.document.close_dialog("confirm", "")
        if yes:
            self.rename()

    def rename(self) -> None:
        done, failed = [], 0
        for row in (r for r in self.plan if r.status == "rename"):
            source, target = self.folder / row.old, self.folder / row.new
            try:
                # os.rename silently replaces an existing file on Linux: refuse that ourselves.
                if target.exists() and not (WINDOWS and row.old.casefold() == row.new.casefold()):
                    raise FileExistsError(target)
                os.rename(source, target)
                done.append((row.old, row.new))
            except OSError:                   # in use, permission denied, or changed since the preview
                failed += 1
        self.set_undo(done)
        self.update_file_list()
        message = f"Renamed {len(done)} file(s)."
        if failed:
            message += f" {failed} failed (in use, permission denied or changed)."
        self.set_summary(message)

The decision is made in the button handlers rather than in the dialog's close event because a <dialog> keeps its previous return value when it is dismissed with Escape (see HTML dialogs).

rename() renames each planned file on its own: one locked file does not stop the others, and the summary reports how many failed. os.rename replaces an existing target silently on Linux, so the method refuses that itself (the file may have appeared after the preview). Each success is recorded for undo.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 8: undo
items.text:
undo() renames the recorded files back in reverse order:

app.py
    def undo(self) -> None:
        if not self.undo_steps:
            return
        restored = 0
        # Reverse order, so chains such as a->b, b->c are undone correctly.
        for old, new in reversed(self.undo_steps):
            try:
                os.rename(self.folder / new, self.folder / old)
                restored += 1
            except OSError:
                pass
        self.set_undo([])
        self.update_file_list()
        self.set_summary(f"Restored {restored} file name(s).")

Your app now matches examples/bulk_rename/app.py.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Step 9: test it without a screen
items.text:
Headless mode (NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1) runs the real host without windows on screen, but it has no mouse or keyboard input. Call the same methods the handlers call and read the page back. Save this as check_rename.py next to app.py:

check_rename.py
import tempfile
import threading
from pathlib import Path

import app as bulk_rename


def check(application):
    folder = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    for name in ("IMG_0001.jpg", "IMG_0002.jpg", "img_0003.JPG", "notes.txt"):
        (folder / name).write_text(name, encoding="utf-8")
    tool = bulk_rename.build(application, str(folder))
    doc = tool.document
    doc.set_value("find", r"^img_(\d+)")
    doc.set_value("replace", r"photo-\1")
    doc.set_checked("regex", True)
    tool.update_preview()                 # set_value does not fire input events
    assert doc.get_text("summary") == "4 file(s), 3 to rename", doc.get_text("summary")
    tool.ask_confirmation()
    tool.confirm(True)                    # what the dialog's Rename button does
    assert (folder / "photo-0003.JPG").is_file()
    tool.undo()
    assert doc.get_text("summary") == "Restored 3 file name(s)."
    assert (folder / "img_0003.JPG").is_file()
    print("check passed")
    threading.Timer(0.5, application.request_quit).start()

NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 uv run -m nativehtmlkit run check_rename:check    # prints: check passed

set_value and set_checked do not fire input/change events, so the test calls update_preview() itself. A failed assert ends the run with exit status 1 and a traceback. The repository's tests/integration/example_checks.py runs a longer version of this check (conflicts, invalid names, a failed rename, the dialog fallback). Try the real clicks once in a desktop session.
path: Tutorial: build a bulk file-rename tool with a live preview

items.title: Tutorial: a live process dashboard
items.text:
You will build Process Dashboard: a native window with a table of running processes that refreshes itself in the background, can be filtered and sorted, paused, and copied to the clipboard. It works the same on Linux and Windows.

Time: about 30 minutes. You need: uv on Linux x64 (glibc 2.39+) or Windows x64, a project with the SDK (uv init --app dashboard && cd dashboard && uv add nativehtmlkit), and the first window from getting started.

The code is in examples/process_dashboard: one program per step plus a small helper module. The repository's test suite runs all of them against the real native host.

items.title: Step 0: a process snapshot helper
items.text:
The dashboard needs a list of processes as plain data. processes.py reads it with the standard library only: /proc on Linux (with the full name from the command line or executable, because the kernel truncates its own name to 15 characters) and the Win32 API through ctypes on Windows. It has no user interface, and you can treat it as a black box (in your own projects psutil does the same job). Save it next to your program:

processes.py
"""Process snapshot helper for the process dashboard tutorial (docs/tutorials/process-dashboard.md).

``list_processes()`` returns plain data (name, pid, memory in MB, CPU time in seconds) using only
the standard library: ``/proc`` on Linux and the Win32 API (through ``ctypes``) on Windows. In your
own code, ``psutil`` is a good alternative. This module has no user interface and is imported by
step1_snapshot.py, step2_filter.py and dashboard.py.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Process:
    name: str
    pid: int
    memory_mb: float
    cpu_seconds: float


def list_processes() -> list[Process]:
    """A snapshot of running processes: name, id, resident memory (MB) and CPU time (s)."""
    return _windows_processes() if sys.platform == "win32" else _linux_processes()


def _linux_processes() -> list[Process]:
    tick, page = os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK"), os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE")
    result = []
    for entry in os.listdir("/proc"):
        if not entry.isdigit():
            continue
        try:
            with open(f"/proc/{entry}/stat", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
                stat = handle.read()
        except OSError:          # the process ended, or access is denied
            continue
        # The name is in parentheses and may itself contain spaces or ')'.
        name = _full_name(entry, stat[stat.index("(") + 1:stat.rindex(")")])
        fields = stat[stat.rindex(")") + 2:].split()
        cpu = (int(fields[11]) + int(fields[12])) / tick       # utime + stime
        memory = int(fields[21]) * page / 2**20                 # rss pages
        result.append(Process(name, int(entry), round(memory, 1), round(cpu, 1)))
    return result


def _full_name(pid: str, comm: str) -> str:
    """The kernel truncates comm to 15 characters; take the full name from argv[0] or the executable."""
    if len(comm) < 15:
        return comm
    candidates = []
    try:
        with open(f"/proc/{pid}/cmdline", "rb") as handle:
            candidates.append(handle.read().split(b"\0", 1)[0].decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    except OSError:
        pass
    try:
        candidates.append(os.readlink(f"/proc/{pid}/exe"))
    except OSError:                      # other users' processes: no access
        pass
    for candidate in candidates:
        base = os.path.basename(candidate)
        if base.startswith(comm):
            return base
    return comm


def _windows_processes() -> list[Process]:
    import ctypes
    from ctypes import wintypes

    class ProcessEntry(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [("dwSize", wintypes.DWORD), ("cntUsage", wintypes.DWORD), ("th32ProcessID", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("th32DefaultHeapID", ctypes.c_size_t), ("th32ModuleID", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("cntThreads", wintypes.DWORD), ("th32ParentProcessID", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("pcPriClassBase", wintypes.LONG), ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("szExeFile", wintypes.WCHAR * 260)]

    class MemoryCounters(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [("cb", wintypes.DWORD), ("PageFaultCount", wintypes.DWORD)] + [
            (name, ctypes.c_size_t) for name in ("PeakWorkingSetSize", "WorkingSetSize", "QuotaPeakPagedPoolUsage",
                                                 "QuotaPagedPoolUsage", "QuotaPeakNonPagedPoolUsage",
                                                 "QuotaNonPagedPoolUsage", "PagefileUsage", "PeakPagefileUsage")]

    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
    kernel32.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
    kernel32.OpenProcess.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
    snapshot = kernel32.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(0x2, 0)        # TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS
    if snapshot in (None, wintypes.HANDLE(-1).value):
        return []
    result = []
    try:
        entry = ProcessEntry(dwSize=ctypes.sizeof(ProcessEntry))
        more = kernel32.Process32FirstW(wintypes.HANDLE(snapshot), ctypes.byref(entry))
        while more:
            memory = cpu = 0.0
            handle = kernel32.OpenProcess(0x1000, False, entry.th32ProcessID)   # QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION
            if handle:                                                      # None: access denied
                counters = MemoryCounters(cb=ctypes.sizeof(MemoryCounters))
                if kernel32.K32GetProcessMemoryInfo(wintypes.HANDLE(handle), ctypes.byref(counters), counters.cb):
                    memory = counters.WorkingSetSize / 2**20
                times = [wintypes.FILETIME() for _ in range(4)]            # creation, exit, kernel, user
                if kernel32.GetProcessTimes(wintypes.HANDLE(handle), *map(ctypes.byref, times)):
                    cpu = sum((t.dwHighDateTime << 32 | t.dwLowDateTime) for t in times[2:]) / 1e7
                kernel32.CloseHandle(wintypes.HANDLE(handle))
            name = entry.szExeFile.removesuffix(".exe")
            result.append(Process(name, entry.th32ProcessID, round(memory, 1), round(cpu, 1)))
            more = kernel32.Process32NextW(wintypes.HANDLE(snapshot), ctypes.byref(entry))
    finally:
        kernel32.CloseHandle(wintypes.HANDLE(snapshot))
    return result

list_processes() returns Process(name, pid, memory_mb, cpu_seconds) records. Processes that end while they are read, or that you may not inspect, are skipped or reported with zero memory and CPU time.

items.title: Step 1: a table of the busiest processes
Step 2: filter and sort
Step 3: background refresh, pause and copy
items.text:
list_processes() takes a moment on a busy machine, and calling it in a callback holds up every later event. The final version collects processes in a background thread that refreshes every few seconds, and the callbacks only filter and sort the cached snapshot.

dashboard.py
"""Process dashboard: a live process monitor (final code of the process dashboard tutorial).

What it teaches
  * collecting data in a background thread and updating the page from it (SDK calls are
    thread-safe), so slow work never blocks the window's event callbacks
  * a refresh loop that waits on a ``threading.Event`` (wakes early to resume or to quit)
  * pausing with a checkbox (the ``change`` event carries ``checked``)
  * filtering and sorting a cached snapshot under a lock
  * copying the table to the clipboard with ``set_clipboard_text`` (and a fallback without one)
  * stopping the thread from ``app.on_shutdown``

Run:    uv run process_dashboard/dashboard.py [--refresh-seconds 3]
Guide:  docs/tutorials/process-dashboard.md (step 3 of 3)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import html
import threading
import time

from nativehtmlkit import Application, Document, NativeHTMLKitError, RpcError
from processes import list_processes

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 14px sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #11161f; color: #e6ebf3; }
  main { padding: 18px 22px; }
  header { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px; }
  h1 { font-size: 20px; margin: 0 0 12px; }
  #status { color: #9fb0c8; }
  form { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 10px; }
  input, select { background: #1b2331; color: #e6ebf3; border: 1px solid #3a475c; border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px; }
  #filter { flex: 1; }
  button { background: #3574c6; color: white; border: 0; border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px 12px; }
  table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; }
  th, td { text-align: left; padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #2a3445; }
  th { color: #9fb0c8; font-weight: 600; }
  td.num, th.num { text-align: right; }
  #summary { color: #9fb0c8; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <header><h1>Processes</h1><span id="status" role="status">Collecting...</span></header>
  <form id="view-form">
    <input id="filter" type="search" placeholder="Filter by name" aria-label="Filter by name">
    <select id="sort" aria-label="Sort by">
      <option value="memory">Memory</option><option value="cpu">CPU time</option><option value="name">Name</option>
    </select>
    <label><input type="checkbox" id="paused"> Pause</label>
    <button id="copy" type="button">Copy table</button>
  </form>
  <p id="summary"></p>
  <table>
    <thead><tr><th>Name</th><th class="num">Id</th><th class="num">Memory (MB)</th><th class="num">CPU (s)</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody id="rows"></tbody>
  </table>
</main></body></html>"""

SORT_KEYS = {
    "memory": (lambda p: p.memory_mb, True),
    "cpu": (lambda p: p.cpu_seconds, True),
    "name": (lambda p: p.name.lower(), False),
}
SHOWN = 25


class Dashboard:
    def __init__(self, app: Application, document: Document, refresh_seconds: float):
        self.app, self.document, self.refresh_seconds = app, document, refresh_seconds
        self.lock = threading.Lock()          # rows/shown are read by callbacks and the worker
        self.rows: list = []
        self.shown: list = []
        self.refreshes = 0
        self.paused = False
        self.wake = threading.Event()         # set to refresh now (resume) or to stop
        self.stopped = threading.Event()
        doc = document
        doc.on("input", lambda _event: self.update_view(), element="filter")
        doc.on("change", lambda _event: self.update_view(), element="sort")
        doc.on("submit", lambda _event: self.update_view(), element="view-form")
        doc.on("change", self.on_pause, element="paused")
        doc.on("click", lambda _event: self.copy(), element="copy")
        app.on_shutdown(self.stop)

    # ----- the background refresh loop -----
    def start(self) -> threading.Thread:
        thread = threading.Thread(target=self._loop, name="process-refresh", daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        return thread

    def _loop(self) -> None:
        while not self.stopped.is_set():
            if not self.paused:
                try:
                    self.refresh()
                except NativeHTMLKitError:    # the window closed or the app is shutting down
                    return
            self.wake.wait(self.refresh_seconds)
            self.wake.clear()

    def refresh(self) -> None:
        rows = list_processes()               # the slow part: runs on this worker thread
        with self.lock:
            self.rows = rows
            self.refreshes += 1
            count = self.refreshes
        self.update_view()
        if not self.paused:                   # paused while collecting: keep showing "Paused"
            self.document.set_text("status", f"Updated {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} (refresh #{count})")

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self.stopped.set()
        self.wake.set()

    # ----- the view -----
    def update_view(self) -> None:
        needle = self.document.get_value("filter").strip().lower()
        key, descending = SORT_KEYS.get(self.document.get_value("sort"), SORT_KEYS["memory"])
        with self.lock:
            matching = [p for p in self.rows if needle in p.name.lower()]
            self.shown = sorted(matching, key=key, reverse=descending)[:SHOWN]
            shown, total = list(self.shown), len(self.rows)
            memory = sum(p.memory_mb for p in self.rows)
        cells = "".join(f'<tr><td>{html.escape(p.name)}</td><td class="num">{p.pid}</td>'
                        f'<td class="num">{p.memory_mb:,.1f}</td><td class="num">{p.cpu_seconds:,.1f}</td></tr>'
                        for p in shown)
        self.document.batch([
            {"op": "replace_children_html", "element": "rows", "html": cells},
            {"op": "set_text", "element": "summary",
             "text": f"Showing {len(shown)} of {total} processes, {memory:,.0f} MB in total"},
        ])

    def on_pause(self, event: dict) -> None:
        self.paused = bool(event.get("checked"))
        if self.paused:
            self.document.set_text("status", "Paused")
        else:
            self.wake.set()                   # refresh at once instead of after the interval

    def copy(self) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            lines = ["Name\tId\tMemoryMB\tCpu"] + [f"{p.name}\t{p.pid}\t{p.memory_mb}\t{p.cpu_seconds}"
                                                  for p in self.shown]
        try:
            self.app.set_clipboard_text("\n".join(lines))
            self.document.set_text("status", f"Copied {len(lines) - 1} rows")
        except RpcError:                      # -32001: no clipboard (for example headless runs)
            self.document.set_text("status", "The clipboard is not available in this session")


def build(app: Application, refresh_seconds: float = 3) -> Dashboard:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Process Dashboard", width=760, height=640)
    return Dashboard(app, window.document, refresh_seconds)


def main() -> None:
    # Parse inside main(): the host re-runs this script with the same arguments.
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Live process dashboard")
    parser.add_argument("--refresh-seconds", type=float, default=3, help="refresh interval (1-3600)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not 1 <= args.refresh_seconds <= 3600:
        parser.error("--refresh-seconds must be between 1 and 3600")
    with Application.start(name="Process Dashboard") as app:
        build(app, args.refresh_seconds).start()
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
  • start() runs _loop in a daemon thread. The loop collects, updates the view and then waits on self.wake for refresh_seconds. Every SDK method is thread-safe, so the thread can update the page directly.
  • wake doubles as a doorbell: unpausing sets it to refresh at once, and stop() sets it so the thread notices stopped without waiting for the interval. app.on_shutdown(self.stop) stops the thread when the application ends.
  • self.lock protects rows and shown, which the thread and the event callbacks both use.
  • The pause checkbox reads event["checked"] from the change event.
  • When the window closes during a refresh, the next SDK call raises a NativeHTMLKitError (for example StaleDocumentError); the loop ends quietly.
  • Copy table uses app.set_clipboard_text inside try/except RpcError: some sessions (for example headless test runs) have no clipboard and report error -32001.
  • --refresh-seconds is a normal command-line option: uv run dashboard.py --refresh-seconds 10. The arguments are parsed in main(); the host re-runs the script with the same arguments.

items.title: Test it without a screen
items.text:
The repository checks every step headless. The core of the check for the final app:

dashboard = example.build(app, refresh_seconds=1)
thread = dashboard.start()
# ... wait until dashboard.refreshes >= 1, then read the page back:
assert document.get_text("status").startswith("Updated ")
dashboard.on_pause({"checked": True})          # what the checkbox's change event does
assert document.get_text("status") == "Paused"
dashboard.stop()
thread.join(5)

See process_dashboard in tests/integration/example_checks.py for the complete version, and run a check of your own with NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 uv run -m nativehtmlkit run module:function as shown in project scaffolding.

items.title: What you learned
items.text:
• Render tables from data with escaped values; subscribe to input, change and submit.
  • Keep slow work off the event thread with a worker thread, and update the page from it.
  • Share state between the thread and callbacks under a lock; stop the thread on shutdown.
  • Use a native service (the clipboard) with a fallback where it is unavailable.

items.title: Where next
items.text:

  • Live bitmaps: draw a memory chart next to the table.
  • The bulk rename tutorial: files, dialogs and undo.
  • API reference.

Source: nativehtmlkit-python/docs/tutorials/process-dashboard.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Tutorial: build a todo app
items.text:
In five steps you build a complete desktop todo list with the NativeHTMLKit Python SDK: a native window with HTML and CSS, adding items with a form, completing and deleting them, editing in place with keyboard support, and saving everything to a JSON file.

Every step is a complete program in examples/tutorial/; the final result is examples/todo.py. All of them are started and checked by this repository's test suite against the real native host.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

You need uv on Linux x64 (glibc 2.39+) or Windows x64, and about 30 minutes.

uv init --app todo && cd todo
uv add nativehtmlkit
uv run nativehtmlkit-python version             # prints the SDK and bundled host versions

items.title: Step 1: a window with HTML and CSS
items.text:
Create todo.py in the project folder:

from nativehtmlkit import Application

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; background:#f6f7fb; color:#1d2433; font:15px/1.4 sans-serif; }
  main { max-width:560px; margin:32px auto; padding:0 20px; }
  ul { list-style:none; padding:0; background:#fff; border-radius:8px; }
  li { padding:10px 12px; border-bottom:1px solid #e3e6ee; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <h1>Todo</h1>
  <ul id="todos"><li>Learn NativeHTMLKit</li><li>Build an app</li></ul>
</main></body></html>"""


def main() -> None:
    with Application.start(name="Todo") as app:
        app.open_html(PAGE, title="Todo", width=640, height=480)
        app.run()  # returns when the user closes the window


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run it with uv run todo.py. A native window appears; the HTML and CSS are rendered by the Rust host. There is no browser and no JavaScript.

What happened:

  • Application.start() started the native host, and the host ran todo.py a second time as its supervised backend. In that second run start() returned a connected Application. That is why all work lives in main() behind if __name__ == "__main__":: anything at module level would run twice. (Lifecycle explains the details.)
  • app.open_html(...) created a window and loaded the page into it.
  • app.run() told the host the app is ready and waits until it quits. Closing the window quits.

Full file: step1_window.py.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 2: add items with a form
items.text:
Replace the static list with a form and an empty list:

<form id="new-form">
  <input id="new-title" type="text" placeholder="What needs doing?" required>
  <button id="add" type="submit">Add</button>
</form>
<ul id="todos"></ul>
<p id="count">0 items</p>

and handle the form's submit event in main():

import html

with Application.start(name="Todo") as app:
    window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Todo", width=640, height=480)
    doc = window.document
    titles: list[str] = []

    def render() -> None:
        # html.escape: a title such as "<b>" is shown as text, never parsed as markup.
        doc.replace_html("todos", "".join(f"<li>{html.escape(t)}</li>" for t in titles))
        doc.set_text("count", f"{len(titles)} items")   # set_text never parses markup

    def on_submit(_event: dict) -> None:
        title = doc.get_value("new-title").strip()
        if title:
            titles.append(title)
            doc.set_value("new-title", "")
            render()

    doc.on("submit", on_submit, element="new-form")
    app.run()

New ideas:

  • Events. doc.on("submit", on_submit, element="new-form") calls on_submit whenever that form is submitted: by clicking Add or by pressing Enter in the field (HTML implicit submission). required makes the host refuse an empty submission before Python sees it.
  • Reading and writing controls. get_value reads what the user typed; set_value clears it.
  • Rendering. The Python list is the source of truth; render() rebuilds the <ul> from it with replace_html.
  • Escaping. replace_html parses HTML, so every piece of user text goes through html.escape. set_text and set_value never parse markup and need no escaping. (Security)

Full file: step2_add.py.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 3: complete and delete items
items.text:
Each item becomes a small structure with a checkbox and a Delete button. Ids encode the item number and the action:

def row(todo: dict) -> str:
    n = todo["id"]
    return (f'<li id="todo-{n}" class="{"done" if todo["done"] else ""}">'
            f'<input id="todo-{n}-done" type="checkbox"{" checked" if todo["done"] else ""}>'
            f'<span class="text">{html.escape(todo["title"])}</span>'
            f'<button id="todo-{n}-delete" class="plain">Delete</button></li>')

Instead of subscribing to every button, subscribe once to the list:

def parse(element: str):
    # "todo-7-delete" -> (7, "delete")
    parts = element.split("-")
    return (int(parts[1]), parts[2]) if len(parts) == 3 and parts[1].isdigit() else (None, None)

def on_change(event: dict) -> None:
    todo_id, action = parse(event["element"])
    if action == "done":
        next(t for t in todos if t["id"] == todo_id)["done"] = bool(event.get("checked"))
        render()

def on_click(event: dict) -> None:
    todo_id, action = parse(event["element"])
    if action == "delete":
        todos[:] = [t for t in todos if t["id"] != todo_id]
        render()

doc.on("change", on_change, element="todos")
doc.on("click", on_click, element="todos")

element="todos" also matches events whose target is inside the list. Every event names the nearest element with an id in event["element"] and lists all identified ancestors in event["path"], so a click on the Delete button of item 7 arrives with element == "todo-7-delete". The checkbox reports its new state in event["checked"]. Because the subscription lives on the list, re-rendering the items never requires re-subscribing.

A little CSS strikes through completed items:

li.done .text { text-decoration: line-through; color: #6b7385; }

Full file: step3_complete_delete.py. More on delegation in events and callbacks.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 4: edit in place, with the keyboard
items.text:
The handlers now share state (todos, next_id, the item being edited), so this step moves them into a small class. An Edit button switches one row into an inline form:

def row(self, todo: dict) -> str:
    n, title = todo["id"], html.escape(todo["title"])
    if n == self.editing:
        # Enter in this field submits its form; Escape is handled in on_key.
        return (f'<li id="todo-{n}"><form id="edit-form-{n}">'
                f'<input id="edit-title" type="text" value="{title}"></form></li>')
    ...

html.escape also protects the value="..." attribute (it escapes quotes). One submit handler serves both forms:

def on_submit(self, event: dict) -> None:
    if event["element"] == "new-form":
        ...                                            # add, as before
    elif event["element"].startswith("edit-form-"):
        title = self.doc.get_value("edit-title").strip()
        if title:
            self.find(self.editing)["title"] = title
        self.editing = None
    self.render()

Starting an edit renders the input and moves the keyboard focus into it:

elif action == "edit":
    self.editing = todo_id
    self.render()
    self.doc.focus("edit-title")

And Escape cancels, via a keydown subscription on the list:

def on_key(self, event: dict) -> None:
    # keydown events carry "key" (for example "Enter", "Escape", "a") and modifier flags.
    if event.get("key") == "Escape" and self.editing is not None:
        self.editing = None
        self.render()

self.doc.on("keydown", self.on_key, element="todos")

Full file: step4_edit_keyboard.py.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 5: save to a JSON file and polish
items.text:
The finished app, examples/todo.py, adds persistence, filters, "Clear completed", an empty state and a theme that follows the desktop's dark mode.

Where to store data. The host knows per-application directories. Give the app a stable id, then ask for its data directory:

APP_ID = "org.nativehtmlkit.examples.todo"

with Application.start(name="Todo", app_id=APP_ID) as app:
    store = Path(app.rpc.call("desktop.paths")["data"]) / "todos.json"
    build(app, store)
    app.run()

desktop.paths is a public host method (via the raw RpcClient); on Linux it returns XDG directories, on Windows AppData folders. It does not create them.

Load and save safely. A missing or broken file starts an empty list; writes go to a temporary file first and then replace the old one, so a crash never leaves half a file:

def load_todos(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return []
    return [{"id": int(x["id"]), "title": str(x["title"]), "done": bool(x["done"])}
            for x in data if isinstance(x, dict) and {"id", "title", "done"} <= x.keys()]


def save_todos(path: Path, todos: list[dict]) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")
    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(todos, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    os.replace(temporary, path)

Every action ends in changed(), which saves and re-renders.

Testable actions. The handlers only translate events into calls such as add(title), toggle(id, done), rename(id, title) and delete(id). Those methods can be called directly, which is how tests/integration/example_checks.py drives the app headless: it submits the form with document.request_submit("new-form"), calls the actions, and reads the result back with get_text, query_nodes and the saved JSON file.

Styling with the desktop theme. CSS custom properties plus a media query switch the palette when the desktop is in dark mode:

:root { --bg:#f6f7fb; --card:#fff; --text:#1d2433; --accent:#3a6ff7; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root { --bg:#141923; --card:#1d2433; --text:#e8ecf5; --accent:#7aa2ff; }
}
body { background:var(--bg); color:var(--text); }

Run the finished app:

uv run todo.py

items.title: Test it without a desktop
items.text:
The host has a headless mode for automated tests. It runs the whole protocol without native windows (and without user input):

NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 uv run todo.py      # PowerShell: $env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1

Combine it with request_submit, set_value and read-back methods to test behaviour in CI.

items.title: UI library
items.text:
Reactive state and ready-made components (layouts, buttons, inputs, lists, themes) on top of the SDK. Start here unless you want to write all of the HTML yourself; use the SDK directly for anything the UI library does not wrap.

It works the same on Linux and Windows; the few real differences are listed in Linux and Windows.

  • Python

    Python 3.10+ with uv. Same API on Linux (KDE Plasma Wayland) and Windows.

    Getting started · Tutorials · Guides · Examples · API

  • PowerShell

    PowerShell 7.2+, or Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows. Same API on Linux (KDE Plasma Wayland) and Windows.

    Getting started · Tutorials · Guides · Examples · API

items.title: CSS reference: classes, themes and tokens (UI 0.1.1)
items.text:
Both libraries ship the same stylesheet (shared/css/ui.css, packaged as assets/ui.css). It uses no JavaScript, web fonts or remote assets. The generated document is:

<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>...</title><style>/* ui.css */ /* your extra CSS */</style></head>
<body class="nhk-theme-cobalt nhk-density-compact"><main class="nhk-app" id="nhkui-...-1">...</main></body></html>

Your extra_css (Python) / -ExtraCss (PowerShell) is appended after the built-in rules in the same <style> element, so a rule with equal specificity wins over the built-in one.

items.title: Themes
items.text:
The theme sets custom properties on body.nhk-theme-<name>:

Token cobalt graphite daylight Used for --nhk-bg #101824 #171d25 #f1f5fa Page background --nhk-panel #192536 #222b36 #ffffff Cards --nhk-panel-2 #1d2b3d #28333e #f6f9fd Inputs, secondary buttons, badges, alerts --nhk-border #304255 #3b4b5c #d5deea Borders --nhk-text #ecf3fc #eff2f7 #203047 Text --nhk-muted #a6b9cc #b1becc #5a6d85 Muted text and labels --nhk-accent #69a6f3 #87a7ef #276fca Primary buttons, badge text, alert edge, checkbox --nhk-accent-strong #458bdf #6b8ed6 #2365b8 Primary button hover --nhk-accent-text #0b233f #121d38 #ffffff Text on accent and danger buttons --nhk-danger #ed7f89 #eb9696 #bc424d Danger buttons --nhk-radius 9px 9px 9px Card radius --nhk-focus #69a6f3 #87a7ef #276fca Focus outline color-scheme dark dark light Native control rendering

items.title: Densities
items.text:
Set on body.nhk-density-<name>:

Token compact regular comfortable --nhk-control-h (minimum control height) 30px 36px 42px --nhk-font (base font size) 13px 14px 15px --nhk-gap (row/column/grid gap) 10px 13px 16px --nhk-pad (app padding) 20px 25px 30px

The font stack is Inter, "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif (local fonts only).

items.title: Component classes
items.text:
Class Created by Rules nhk-app root <main> padding: var(--nhk-pad), max-width: 1380px, centred. nhk-row row() / Add-NHKUiRow Flex row, wrap, align-items: center, gap: var(--nhk-gap). nhk-col column() / Add-NHKUiColumn Flex column, gap: var(--nhk-gap), min-width: 0. nhk-stack stack() (Python only) Flex column with gap: 6px. nhk-grid grid() / Add-NHKUiGrid repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); 2 columns at max-width: 1000px; 1 column at max-width: 620px (also nhk-app padding 14 px). nhk-card card() / Add-NHKUiCard --nhk-panel background, border, --nhk-radius, padding: 16px. nhk-heading headings Weight 640; h1 24 px, h2 19 px, h3 16 px, h4 14 px. nhk-text, nhk-muted text No margin, overflow-wrap: anywhere; muted uses --nhk-muted. nhk-badge badge Pill, --nhk-panel-2 background, accent text, 0.85 em. nhk-alert alert Bordered box with a 3 px accent left border; role="status". nhk-button + nhk-primary/nhk-secondary/nhk-danger/nhk-quiet buttons Height --nhk-control-h; primary uses accent; :disabled has opacity 0.45. nhk-input, nhk-select input / select --nhk-panel-2 background; inputs are full width. nhk-field, nhk-label labelled input/select wrapper Field is a flex column (flex: 1 1 200px, min-width: 150px); label is muted, 0.9 em. In a column the 200px basis becomes height (defect B-0014); see limitations for the workaround. nhk-checkrow, nhk-checkbox checkbox Row with 8 px gap; checkbox 16 px with accent-color. nhk-region, nhk-hidden when() / Add-NHKUiWhen nhk-hidden is display: none !important. nhk-list text list Left padding 20 px; items 3 px padding. nhk-custom raw_html() / Add-NHKUiHtml min-width: 0. nhk-hr (style hook only) Top border; apply it yourself, for example ui.element("hr", css_class="nhk-hr").

Focus: .nhk-input:focus, .nhk-select:focus and .nhk-button:focus-visible draw a 2 px --nhk-focus outline with 2 px offset. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables transitions and animations.

items.title: Theming hooks
items.text:
Override tokens for one theme, or for all, in extra CSS:

body.nhk-theme-daylight { --nhk-accent: #0f7b6c; --nhk-accent-strong: #0b6458; --nhk-focus: #0f7b6c; }
/* Tokens are defined on body.nhk-theme-*; a plain `body { }` rule is less specific and loses. */
body.nhk-theme-cobalt, body.nhk-theme-graphite, body.nhk-theme-daylight { --nhk-radius: 4px; }

Style components by their classes (.nhk-card { border-top: 3px solid var(--nhk-accent); }) or add your own classes: Python ui.element("div", css_class="metric", text=value) or ui.container("section", css_class="toolbar"); in PowerShell, which has no generic element function, target structure such as .nhk-card h1.nhk-heading. Do not rely on generated ids in CSS; they change on every run.

The theme and density are fixed when the window is created. For a theme switch at run time, create the UI with the chosen theme (see examples/*/dashboard.*) or restyle through your own classes. The UI does not follow the desktop's light/dark preference automatically; the SDK can read it (Application.desktop_preferences(), Get-NativeHTMLKitPreferences) before you choose a theme.

Source: nativehtmlkit_ui/docs/css.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Getting started with the PowerShell UI module
items.text: NativeHTMLKit.UI builds native desktop windows from PowerShell with components (headings, inputs, buttons, lists, cards, a grid) bound to reactive state. It runs on the NativeHTMLKit native host, without a browser engine or JavaScript, and uses only the public cmdlets of the PowerShell SDK. This page covers version 0.1.1. The same page for Python: getting started.

items.title: Install
items.text:
You need PowerShell 7.2 or later on Linux x64 (KDE Plasma Wayland is the primary desktop) or Windows x64, or Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows.

Install-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI -Scope CurrentUser      # also installs the NativeHTMLKit SDK
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI
(Get-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI).Version                    # 0.1.1

items.title: Your first window
items.text:
Save this as hello.ps1 (it is the hello example):

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Hello UI'

$name = New-NHKUiState -Value 'world'
$greeting = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($name) -Data $name -Compute { param($n) "Hello, $($n.Value)!" }

$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Hello UI' -Width 480 -Height 320
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Bind $greeting -Level 1
    $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $name -Label 'Your name'
        $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Reset' -Variant secondary -Data $name -OnClick {
            param($eventObject, $n)
            $n.Set('world')
        }
    }
}

try {
    $null = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Stop-NHKUi -UI $ui
    $greeting.Dispose()
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

Run it:

pwsh -File ./hello.ps1                        # PowerShell 7
powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\hello.ps1    # Windows PowerShell 5.1

Type a name: the heading follows every keystroke. Reset sets the state back, and the input follows too.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
• New-NHKUiState is an observable value. Add-NHKUiInput -Bind $name binds it both ways: typing sets the state, .Set() changes the field.
  • New-NHKUiComputed derives a value. List the states it reads in -DependsOn; it receives -Data as its parameter. Dispose computed states in finally.
  • Containers such as Add-NHKUiColumn take a -Content scriptblock; components added inside it become children. Assign every result to $null. You build the whole tree first; Start-NHKUi opens the window. After that you only change state.
  • Button callbacks receive param($eventObject, $data), where $data is the -Data argument, and change state, never the window.
  • Start-NativeHTMLKitScript starts the native host, which runs this same script again as its backend. Everything above that line runs twice; keep side effects below it.
  • Wait-NativeHTMLKit -UntilShutdown processes events until the window is closed; finally stops the UI and closes the connection.

items.title: UI limitations and qualification
items.text:
UI 0.1.1 is an early (pre-1.0) release. Its 0.1.1 packages passed the real-input GUI suite (state, input, keyboard focus, select, disabled bindings, responsive widths, two windows, 1000-update load, 100 mount/close cycles) at 100% scaling against Python SDK 0.1.2 / PowerShell SDK 0.1.2 / Core 1.0.3 on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland (Python, PowerShell 7) and Windows Server 2022 (Python, PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell 5.1). IME, 125%/150% scaling and theme checks were last run with UI 0.1.0 on SDK 0.1.0 / Core 1.0.2. Screen-reader validation is incomplete and Core's select/Orca announcement issue remains open.

Known UI bugs recorded in the Project register: Python Computed can falsely raise a circular dependency error and retain a stale value during concurrent updates; disposing many UI windows can accumulate SDK shutdown callbacks. Until fixed, serialize writes affecting the same computed state, use background worker handoff via ui.post, and avoid rapidly creating/discarding many UIs in long-lived applications.

Inputs placed directly in a column are 200px tall (0.1.1 stylesheet defect B-0014). The built-in rule .nhk-field { flex: 1 1 200px } is meant for fields in a row, but in a column (ui.column(), ui.stack(), Add-NHKUiColumn) the 200px basis applies to the field's height, so a single input followed by more content leaves a large empty gap. Inputs inside a row or directly inside a card (a plain block) are not affected. Workaround: pass

.nhk-col > .nhk-field { flex: 0 0 auto; }

as extra_css= (Python; add .nhk-stack > .nhk-field for ui.stack()) or -ExtraCss (PowerShell). The signup_form and multi_window examples do this. Guides: Python layouts, PowerShell layouts.

There is no UI modal wrapper, router, plugin system, arbitrary widget gallery, virtualized data grid, video/audio player, JS runtime, or HTTP server. The SDK may expose underlying HTML dialogs and bitmap surfaces; do not claim them as UI components.

Source: nativehtmlkit_ui/docs/LIMITATIONS.md · edit the page there.

items.title: PowerShell reference: NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1
items.text:
This page is the complete reference for the PowerShell module NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1, derived from the released source (powershell/NativeHTMLKit.UI). The module requires the NativeHTMLKit SDK module (manifest: ModuleVersion 0.1.0 or later; qualified with 0.1.2 and Core 1.0.3) and uses only its public cmdlets. The Python package is documented in the Python reference; themes and classes in the CSS reference. It runs on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (Windows) and PowerShell 7.2+ (Linux and Windows).

Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI    # also imports the NativeHTMLKit SDK

Exported functions (24, no cmdlets, aliases or variables):

Group Functions State New-NHKUiState, New-NHKUiComputed UI lifecycle New-NHKUi, Start-NHKUi, Stop-NHKUi, Sync-NHKUi, Invoke-NHKUiBatch, Get-NHKUiHtml, Get-NHKUiDiagnostics Layout Add-NHKUiColumn, Add-NHKUiRow, Add-NHKUiGrid, Add-NHKUiCard Display Add-NHKUiHeading, Add-NHKUiText, Add-NHKUiBadge, Add-NHKUiAlert Controls Add-NHKUiButton, Add-NHKUiInput, Add-NHKUiCheckbox, Add-NHKUiSelect Dynamic Add-NHKUiWhen, Add-NHKUiTextList Trusted markup Add-NHKUiHtml

Every Add-NHKUi* function takes the UI explicitly with -UI and returns the created node (see Nodes). Assign the result to $null (or keep the node to read its .Id) so it does not end up in your script's output.

items.title: New-NHKUiState
items.text:
$count = New-NHKUiState -Value 0
$count.Value              # read
$count.Set(5)             # change and notify
$sub = $count.Subscribe({ param($newValue, $context) ... }, $context)
$count.Unsubscribe($sub)
Parameter Description -Value Initial value of any type; $null allowed.

Returns a [pscustomobject] whose first type name is NativeHTMLKit.UI.State, with:

Member Description .Value The current value. Assigning .Value directly does not notify anyone; always use .Set(). .Set($next) If [object]::Equals($current, $next) it does nothing. Otherwise stores $next and calls every active subscription with ($next, $context). No return value. .Subscribe([scriptblock]$Callback, $Context) Registers a callback that receives param($newValue, $context); returns a subscription object. .Unsubscribe($subscription) Deactivates and removes a subscription ($null is ignored). .Listeners The subscription list (for diagnostics; do not edit).

Semantics:

  • Equality is [object]::Equals. Numbers and strings compare by value; arrays, hashtables and objects compare by reference. Build a new array to signal a change: $items.Set(@($items.Value) + @($new)). Changing an element in place and setting the same array again is ignored.
  • Notification is synchronous. Subscribers run inside .Set(), in registration order.
  • Batching depth: the module counts nested .Set() calls. Outside a UI callback or Invoke-NHKUiBatch, the UIs affected by a change are written once, when the outermost .Set() returns. One external change that cascades through several computed states is therefore one document write.
  • UI-bound states must only be changed on the runspace that started the UI; see the owner runspace.

items.title: New-NHKUiComputed
items.text:
$total = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($items, $filter) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s)
    , @($s.Items.Value | Where-Object { $_.Kind -eq $s.Filter.Value })
}
...
$total.Dispose()
Parameter Description -Compute (mandatory) Scriptblock that returns the value. It is invoked as & $Compute $Data, so its first parameter receives -Data. -DependsOn (mandatory) Array of states (or other computed states). Anything else throws DependsOn must contain only NativeHTMLKit.UI.State objects. -Data Any object passed to -Compute on every run (typically a hashtable of states).

Returns a state object (type name NativeHTMLKit.UI.State) with an extra .Dispose() method and a DependencyTokens list. It can be bound and used as a dependency like any state.

Semantics:

  • Dependencies are explicit and static: the module does not inspect the scriptblock. Every state the computation reads must be listed in -DependsOn.
  • -Compute runs once immediately and again, synchronously, every time a dependency's .Set() notifies. The result is stored with .Set(), so subscribers (and bound UI elements) are notified only when it differs by [object]::Equals.
  • Return arrays with a leading comma (, @(...)). PowerShell unrolls pipeline output: an empty result would otherwise become $null and a one-element result a scalar.
  • A computation that triggers itself again while it is running throws Circular computed-state dependency. Errors in -Compute propagate to the .Set() call that caused the recomputation.
  • .Dispose() unsubscribes from every dependency. Computed states are not disposed by Stop-NHKUi; dispose them yourself (all examples do this in finally).
  • Do not call .Set() on a computed state yourself; the next dependency change overwrites it.

items.title: New-NHKUi
items.text:
$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Expenses' -Width 760 -Height 640 -Theme cobalt -Density compact -ExtraCss $css
Parameter Default Validation / meaning -Title 'NativeHTMLKit UI' Window title and HTML <title>. -Width, -Height 940, 660 100-8192; requested window size in CSS pixels. -Theme cobalt cobalt, graphite, daylight. -Density compact compact, regular, comfortable. -ExtraCss '' Trusted CSS appended after the built-in stylesheet. See CSS reference.

Returns a [pscustomobject] with type name NativeHTMLKit.UI.App. Properties you may read:

Property Description Title, Width, Height, Theme, Density, ExtraCss Constructor values (no effect when changed after start). Prefix 'nhkui-' + 12 hex digits; every generated element id is "$Prefix-<n>". Root Root node (<main class="nhk-app">). Window, Document, Application $null until Start-NHKUi; then the SDK window, document and application objects, for direct SDK calls.

Other properties (Stack, Bindings, Handlers, Pending, Subscriptions, counters, ...) are internal state; read them through Get-NHKUiDiagnostics.

items.title: Start-NHKUi
items.text:
$window = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app [-NoReady]
Parameter Description -UI (mandatory) The UI built with New-NHKUi and Add-NHKUi*. -Application (mandatory) The SDK application, from Start-NativeHTMLKitScript or Connect-NativeHTMLKit. -NoReady Do not call Set-NativeHTMLKitReady. Use it when you start further UIs later, or when you announce readiness yourself.

Steps: records the current runspace as the UI's owner, renders the document (Get-NHKUiHtml), creates the window with New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Title -Width -Height, loads it with Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml, writes the live value of every input/select and checkbox, writes any state that changed after its component was built, registers one Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent subscription per used event kind and finally calls Set-NativeHTMLKitReady (the SDK ignores repeated calls). Returns the SDK window object.

Throws UI already started, UI contains an unclosed container, and anything the SDK throws. On failure it records the message in LastError, calls Stop-NHKUi and rethrows; a window that was already created is left to the SDK lifecycle.

items.title: Stop-NHKUi
items.text:
Stop-NHKUi -UI $ui

Idempotent. Unregisters the UI's document event subscriptions, unsubscribes every binding from its state (later .Set() calls no longer touch this UI) and clears pending writes. It does not close the window, the application or computed states. Call it in finally, and when you close a secondary window yourself.

If the window was closed, its document replaced or the application shut down, the next write fails with the SDK's stale-object error (or host code -32004/-32008); the module then calls Stop-NHKUi itself and counts it in DiscardedAfterClose. To react to a user closing a window immediately, handle the SDK's window.event notification (see examples/powershell/multi_window.ps1).

items.title: Sync-NHKUi
items.text:
Sync-NHKUi -UI $ui

Writes all pending binding changes now. Normally not needed: UI callbacks, Invoke-NHKUiBatch and outermost .Set() calls already sync. Does nothing before start or after stop. Throws UI DOM state is uncertain after a failed operation; do not continue managed updates once DomUncertain is set. Re-entrant calls (an event that runs while an SDK request inside a write is waiting) only queue their changes; the outer call writes them afterwards, so an older value never overwrites a newer one.

items.title: Invoke-NHKUiBatch
items.text:
Invoke-NHKUiBatch -UI $ui -ScriptBlock {
    for ($i = 1; $i -le 1000; $i++) { $count.Set($i) }
}

Runs the scriptblock and writes the resulting changes once, at the end (only the final value of each binding is written). Use it for several .Set() calls made outside a UI callback, for example in a task -OnCompleted callback, a notification callback or a custom loop. UI button/input callbacks are batched automatically. Calls may be nested; the write happens when the outermost batch ends. The scriptblock's output is returned.

items.title: Get-NHKUiHtml
items.text: Returns the complete HTML document: doctype, charset and viewport metas, <title>, one <style> with the built-in CSS followed by -ExtraCss, and <body class="nhk-theme-<theme> nhk-density-<density>"> containing the root. Throws UI contains an unclosed container if called from inside a -Content block. Needs no host; useful in tests.

items.title: Get-NHKUiDiagnostics
items.text:
Returns a [pscustomobject]:

Property Type Meaning DomUncertain bool A document write failed with an unknown outcome (for example a timeout or disconnect). Managed updates stop; Sync-NHKUi throws. Not set when the window simply closed. LastError string Message of the last callback or write failure (or start failure). Errors long Number of failed UI callbacks and writes. PendingUpdates int Bindings waiting to be written. Updates long Write rounds that produced at least one operation. Operations long Document operations written. Subscriptions int Active SDK document event subscriptions (one per event kind); 0 after stop. DiscardedAfterClose long Writes dropped because the window/document/application was gone. Disposed bool True after Stop-NHKUi.

Combine with the SDK's Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnosticReport -Application $app (connection counters such as CallbackFailures) when diagnosing an app; the example harness checks both.

items.title: The owner runspace
items.text: Start-NHKUi records [runspace]::DefaultRunspace.InstanceId. After that, starting, syncing, batching, building and every write caused by a bound state's .Set() must happen on that runspace; otherwise the module throws UI updates must run on the SDK owning runspace (use SDK task completion callbacks). A .Set() from another runspace stores the value and then throws, leaving the UI out of date, so never share UI states with Start-NativeHTMLKitTask workers, ForEach-Object -Parallel, thread jobs or raw runspaces. Pass plain data to the worker and set states in the SDK's -OnCompleted/-OnFailed callbacks, which run on the owner during Wait-NativeHTMLKit. See the background work guide.

items.title: Layout containers
items.text:
$null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Disk' -Level 3
}
Function Element and class Layout Add-NHKUiColumn -UI -Content div.nhk-col Vertical flex column, gap --nhk-gap. Add-NHKUiRow -UI -Content div.nhk-row Horizontal flex row that wraps; items centred vertically. Add-NHKUiGrid -UI -Content div.nhk-grid 3 equal columns; 2 at most 1000 px wide; 1 at most 620 px. Add-NHKUiCard -UI -Content div.nhk-card Panel with background, border, radius and padding.

-Content is invoked immediately; components added inside it become children of the container. Output of the block is discarded. All parameters are mandatory. There is no PowerShell equivalent of Python's stack() or generic element().

items.title: Display components
items.text:
Function Parameters Renders Add-NHKUiHeading -UI, -Text (default ''), -Level (1-4, default 2), -Bind <hN class="nhk-heading"> Add-NHKUiText -UI, -Text (empty allowed), -Bind, -Muted <p class="nhk-text"> (+ nhk-muted) Add-NHKUiBadge -UI, -Text, -Bind <span class="nhk-badge"> Add-NHKUiAlert -UI, -Text, -Bind <div class="nhk-alert" role="status">

With -Bind <state> the element shows [string]$state.Value (replacing -Text) and is updated with one set_text operation when the state changes. Text is HTML-encoded with [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode. A -Bind argument that is not a state throws A -Bind argument must be created with New-NHKUiState or New-NHKUiComputed.

items.title: Add-NHKUiButton
items.text:
$null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Save' -Variant primary -DisabledState $cannotSave -Data $s -OnClick {
    param($eventObject, $s)
    ...
}
Parameter Description -UI (mandatory) The UI. -Text Static label. Either -Text or -Bind is required (Add-NHKUiButton needs -Text or a bound -Bind label). -Bind State whose value is the label (for example 'Pause'/'Resume'). -Variant primary (default), secondary, danger, quiet. -OnClick Scriptblock run on the owner runspace with param($eventObject, $data). -Data Any object (often a hashtable of states) passed as the callback's second argument. -DisabledState State interpreted with [bool]; adds/removes the disabled attribute.

Renders <button type="button" class="nhk-button nhk-<variant>">.

items.title: Add-NHKUiInput
items.text:
Parameter Description -UI, -Bind (mandatory) -Bind is the state that holds the text. -Label Visible <label class="nhk-label" for> placed before the input inside div.nhk-field. Without a label there is no wrapper. -Placeholder Placeholder attribute. -Type text (default), search, email, password, number. The state always receives a [string].

Every native input event sets the state to the control's text. Setting the state writes the control with Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue; the value received from the control is remembered first, so typing never triggers an echo write that would reset the caret, selection or IME composition.

items.title: Add-NHKUiCheckbox
items.text: -UI, -Bind, -Label (all mandatory). Renders div.nhk-checkrow with <input type="checkbox" class="nhk-checkbox"> followed by its <label for>. A change event sets the state to [bool]; setting the state writes Set-NativeHTMLKitChecked.

items.title: Add-NHKUiSelect
items.text:
$null = Add-NHKUiSelect -UI $ui -Bind $plan -Label 'Plan' -Options @(
    @{ Value = 'free'; Label = 'Free' }, @{ Value = 'team'; Label = 'Team' })
Parameter Description -UI, -Bind, -Options (mandatory) -Options is an array of hashtables or objects with Value and Label; both are converted to strings. The list is fixed at build time. -Label Optional visible label.

The option whose Value equals [string]$state.Value is marked selected. A change event sets the state to the selected value string; setting the state writes Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue.

All three two-way controls return the control node; its .Id is the element id for SDK calls such as Set-NativeHTMLKitFocus -Document $ui.Document -Element $node.Id.

items.title: Add-NHKUiWhen
items.text: -UI, -Bind, -Content (all mandatory). Creates div.nhk-region around the content. When [bool]$state.Value is false the class nhk-hidden (display: none !important) is added; when true it is removed. The content is always present, so controls keep their values while hidden. Note PowerShell truthiness: '', $null, 0, $false and empty arrays are false, but the string 'False' is true.

items.title: Add-NHKUiTextList
items.text: -UI, -Bind (mandatory). Renders <ul class="nhk-list"> with one encoded <li> per element of @($state.Value) ($null gives an empty list, a scalar one item). A change replaces the list's children with one replace_children_html operation. Text only, not virtualized; format the strings in a computed state.

items.title: Add-NHKUiHtml
items.text: -UI, -Markup (mandatory; empty allowed). Adds div.nhk-custom containing -Markup verbatim. Only pass static markup that you wrote. Never pass user input, file contents or data from the network; bind those to text components, which encode them. See the trusted content guide.

items.title: Nodes
items.text:
Each Add-NHKUi* call returns a node object with Tag, Id, Attrs, Children, Text and Raw. Use .Id for SDK document calls (Get-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText, Get-NativeHTMLKitValue, Set-NativeHTMLKitFocus, ...). Editing node properties after Start-NHKUi does not change the window; adding components after start throws The UI tree is already mounted; change State rather than adding components.

Rendering rules: attribute names must match ^[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_:.-]*$ and may not start with on; attribute values and text are encoded; $false/$null attributes are omitted, $true renders a boolean attribute; attributes are written in sorted order.

items.title: Events and callbacks
items.text:
• Start-NHKUi registers one SDK document subscription per event kind in use (click for buttons with -OnClick, input for inputs, change for checkboxes and selects).
  • For each event the module walks element and then path (the bubbling route) and invokes the handler of the nearest element that has one.
  • Callbacks run on the owner runspace while Wait-NativeHTMLKit (or another waiting SDK call) pumps host messages. State changes made inside them are written once, after the callback returns.
  • A callback that throws increments Errors, sets LastError and rethrows into the SDK, which isolates it as a callback failure (counted in Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnosticReport as CallbackFailures, described on stderr). Catch expected errors such as an unavailable clipboard inside the callback (see examples/powershell/clipboard_tool.ps1).
  • Event objects come from the SDK's JSON reader (type, element, path, window_id, document_id and type-specific members such as value and checked).
  • Unlike raw Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent callbacks (which receive only the event), UI callbacks receive ($eventObject, $data). Pass state through -Data instead of relying on variable capture.

items.title: Known limitations specific to PowerShell
items.text:
• Only buttons have a public event parameter (-OnClick); there is no public keydown, submit or context-menu hook in the UI module. Use SDK events on $ui.Document if you need them.
  • There is no event queue: a long callback delays the next event (the SDK keeps pumping host requests while it waits).
  • B-0014, fields directly in a column are 200 px tall. The stylesheet rule .nhk-field { flex: 1 1 200px } is meant for rows; in Add-NHKUiColumn the 200 px basis becomes the field's height. Fields in rows and cards are not affected. Workaround: -ExtraCss '.nhk-col > .nhk-field { flex: 0 0 auto; }' (see the layouts guide).
  • The Python defects B-0002 and B-0003 do not apply: computed values are synchronous on the owner runspace and Start-NHKUi registers no application shutdown callback.

See limitations for qualification status.

Source: nativehtmlkit_ui/docs/powershell/reference.md · edit the page there.

Every example is a complete program, verified against the real NativeHTMLKit host. Open one to see a screenshot, how to run it and its full source.

Example What it does Hello UI The first window: a greeting that follows a text field, and a Reset button. Counter gallery The smallest tour of state, computed text, buttons, an input, a checkbox and a list. Expense tracker Add expenses, remove the last one, filter by category and see totals (expense-tracker tutorial app). Task list Tasks with Done/Remove buttons per row and an All/Open/Done filter. Sign-up form Live validation, a guarded submit button, a confirmation screen and reset. Settings panel Save, Revert and Restore defaults with an unsaved-changes indicator. Settings editor Edit, validate and save a JSON settings file; the saved theme applies on the next start (settings-editor tutorial app).
