items.title: Source: powershell/theme_preview.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

# Theme preview: try the UI module's themes, densities and a custom accent colour.
#
# Teaches: New-NHKUi -Theme/-Density/-ExtraCss, overriding the module's CSS custom properties
#          (--nhk-accent and friends) for one theme, and the main components side by side.
#          -Instance multiple lets you start several previews at once and compare them.
# Run:     pwsh -File ./theme_preview.ps1 [cobalt|graphite|daylight] [compact|regular|comfortable] [#RRGGBB]
#          powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\theme_preview.ps1 daylight comfortable '#0f7b6c'
# Guide:   docs/powershell/guides/theming-and-custom-css.md
param([string]$Theme = 'cobalt', [string]$Density = 'compact', [string]$Accent = '')
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Theme preview' -Instance multiple

if (@('cobalt', 'graphite', 'daylight') -notcontains $Theme) { $Theme = 'cobalt' }
if (@('compact', 'regular', 'comfortable') -notcontains $Density) { $Density = 'compact' }
if ($Accent -notmatch '^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$') { $Accent = '' }
# -ExtraCss is appended after the module stylesheet, so the same selector wins.
$css = ''
if ($Accent) { $css = "body.nhk-theme-$Theme { --nhk-accent: $Accent; --nhk-accent-strong: $Accent; --nhk-focus: $Accent; }" }

$s = @{ Name = (New-NHKUiState -Value 'Ada'); Enabled = (New-NHKUiState -Value $true)
        Size = (New-NHKUiState -Value 'm'); Always = (New-NHKUiState -Value $true) }
$s.Hello = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Name) -Data $s -Compute { param($s) 'Hello ' + $s.Name.Value }
$accentText = if ($Accent) { $Accent } else { 'default' }
$themeTitle = $Theme.Substring(0, 1).ToUpperInvariant() + $Theme.Substring(1)

$ui = New-NHKUi -Title "Theme preview: $Theme/$Density" -Theme $Theme -Density $Density -ExtraCss $css -Width 720 -Height 560
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text "$themeTitle theme, $Density density" -Level 1
    $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiBadge -UI $ui -Text 'Badge'
        $null = Add-NHKUiBadge -UI $ui -Bind $s.Hello
        $null = Add-NHKUiBadge -UI $ui -Text "accent $accentText"
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiGrid -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
            $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Controls' -Level 2
            $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $s.Name -Label 'Name'
            $null = Add-NHKUiSelect -UI $ui -Bind $s.Size -Label 'Size' -Options @(
                @{ Value = 's'; Label = 'Small' }, @{ Value = 'm'; Label = 'Medium' }, @{ Value = 'l'; Label = 'Large' })
            $null = Add-NHKUiCheckbox -UI $ui -Bind $s.Enabled -Label 'Enabled'
        }
        $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
            $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Buttons' -Level 2
            $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
                $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Primary'
                $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Secondary' -Variant secondary
                $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Danger' -Variant danger
                $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Quiet' -Variant quiet
                $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Disabled' -DisabledState $s.Always
            }
        }
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiAlert -UI $ui -Text 'Alerts use role=status, so screen readers announce changes.'
    $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Text 'Muted text for secondary information.' -Muted
}

try {
    $null = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Stop-NHKUi -UI $ui
    $s.Hello.Dispose()
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

items.title: Task list
items.text:
Tasks with Done/Remove buttons per row and an All/Open/Done filter.

Same example in Python: Task list

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

What it teaches: slot pool for rows with buttons; bound button labels; computed counts.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
pwsh -File ./todo.ps1

Related guide: lists and conditional content

items.title: Source: powershell/todo.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

# Task list with per-row Done/Remove buttons and an All/Open/Done filter.
#
# Teaches: the "slot pool" pattern. The UI tree is fixed once started, so the script creates
# $maxTasks rows up front and shows, hides and relabels them from state (Add-NHKUiWhen, bound
# text, bound button labels via -Bind). Each row gets its own -Data object with its index.
# Also: computed counts, a disabled Add button and "Clear done".
#
# Run:  pwsh -File ./todo.ps1   |   powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\todo.ps1
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Tasks'

$maxTasks = 8
$s = @{
    Tasks = (New-NHKUiState -Value @())   # objects with Id, Title, Done
    Title = (New-NHKUiState -Value ''); Show = (New-NHKUiState -Value 'all'); NextId = 1; Max = $maxTasks
}
$s.Visible = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Tasks, $s.Show) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s)
    , @($s.Tasks.Value | Where-Object { $s.Show.Value -eq 'all' -or [bool]$_.Done -eq ($s.Show.Value -eq 'done') })
}
$s.Counts = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Tasks) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s)
    $all = @($s.Tasks.Value); $done = @($all | Where-Object { $_.Done }).Count
    '{0} open, {1} done' -f ($all.Count - $done), $done
}
$s.Full = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Tasks) -Data $s -Compute { param($s) @($s.Tasks.Value).Count -ge $s.Max }
$s.CannotAdd = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Tasks, $s.Title) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s) (@($s.Tasks.Value).Count -ge $s.Max) -or (-not $s.Title.Value.Trim())
}
$s.NoneDone = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Tasks) -Data $s -Compute { param($s) @($s.Tasks.Value | Where-Object { $_.Done }).Count -eq 0 }
$s.Empty = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Visible) -Data $s -Compute { param($s) @($s.Visible.Value).Count -eq 0 }
$computeds = New-Object System.Collections.ArrayList
foreach ($c in @($s.Visible, $s.Counts, $s.Full, $s.CannotAdd, $s.NoneDone, $s.Empty)) { [void]$computeds.Add($c) }

# Per-row computed values: is the row used, its text and its toggle label.
$rows = for ($row = 0; $row -lt $maxTasks; $row++) {
    $slot = @{ S = $s; Row = $row }
    $slot.Present = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Visible) -Data $slot -Compute { param($t) $t.Row -lt @($t.S.Visible.Value).Count }
    $slot.Text = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Visible) -Data $slot -Compute {
        param($t)
        $items = @($t.S.Visible.Value)
        if ($t.Row -ge $items.Count) { return '' }
        $mark = if ($items[$t.Row].Done) { '[x] ' } else { '[ ] ' }
        $mark + $items[$t.Row].Title
    }
    $slot.Toggle = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Visible) -Data $slot -Compute {
        param($t)
        $items = @($t.S.Visible.Value)
        if ($t.Row -lt $items.Count -and $items[$t.Row].Done) { 'Reopen' } else { 'Done' }
    }
    foreach ($c in @($slot.Present, $slot.Text, $slot.Toggle)) { [void]$computeds.Add($c) }
    $slot
}

$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Tasks' -Width 640 -Height 620
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Tasks' -Level 1
    $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $s.Title -Label 'New task' -Placeholder 'Water the plants'
        $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Add' -DisabledState $s.CannotAdd -Data $s -OnClick {
            param($eventObject, $s)
            $text = $s.Title.Value.Trim()
            if (-not $text -or @($s.Tasks.Value).Count -ge $s.Max) { return }
            $s.Tasks.Set(@($s.Tasks.Value) + @([pscustomobject]@{ Id = $s.NextId; Title = $text; Done = $false }))
            $s.NextId = $s.NextId + 1
            $s.Title.Set('')
        }
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiWhen -UI $ui -Bind $s.Full -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiAlert -UI $ui -Text "The list is full ($maxTasks tasks). Remove or clear some first."
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiSelect -UI $ui -Bind $s.Show -Label 'Show' -Options @(
            @{ Value = 'all'; Label = 'All' }, @{ Value = 'open'; Label = 'Open' }, @{ Value = 'done'; Label = 'Done' })
        $null = Add-NHKUiBadge -UI $ui -Bind $s.Counts
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiWhen -UI $ui -Bind $s.Empty -Content { $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Text 'Nothing here.' -Muted }
        foreach ($slot in $rows) {
            $null = Add-NHKUiWhen -UI $ui -Bind $slot.Present -Content {
                $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
                    $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Bind $slot.Text
                    $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Bind $slot.Toggle -Variant secondary -Data $slot -OnClick {
                        param($eventObject, $t)
                        $items = @($t.S.Visible.Value)
                        if ($t.Row -ge $items.Count) { return }
                        $id = $items[$t.Row].Id
                        $t.S.Tasks.Set(@($t.S.Tasks.Value | ForEach-Object {
                            if ($_.Id -eq $id) { [pscustomobject]@{ Id = $_.Id; Title = $_.Title; Done = -not $_.Done } } else { $_ }
                        }))
                    }
                    $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Remove' -Variant quiet -Data $slot -OnClick {
                        param($eventObject, $t)
                        $items = @($t.S.Visible.Value)
                        if ($t.Row -ge $items.Count) { return }
                        $id = $items[$t.Row].Id
                        $t.S.Tasks.Set(@($t.S.Tasks.Value | Where-Object { $_.Id -ne $id }))
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Clear done' -Variant danger -DisabledState $s.NoneDone -Data $s -OnClick {
        param($eventObject, $s)
        $s.Tasks.Set(@($s.Tasks.Value | Where-Object { -not $_.Done }))
    }
}

try {
    $null = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Stop-NHKUi -UI $ui
    foreach ($c in $computeds) { $c.Dispose() }
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

items.title: Word counter
items.text:
Count words in a text file in the background with progress, Cancel and a top-ten list.

Same example in Python: Word counter

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

What it teaches: background work with progress; cancellation; merging partial results; throttled updates.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
pwsh -File ./word_counter.ps1 [FILE]

Related guide: background work

items.title: Source: powershell/word_counter.ps1
items.text:
View on GitHub

# Word counter: count words in a text file with SDK background tasks, with progress and Cancel.
#
# Teaches: splitting work into chunks that each run in Start-NativeHTMLKitTask (a separate
#          runspace that receives plain data only), merging each chunk's result and reporting
#          progress in -OnCompleted on the owner runspace, starting the next chunk from there,
#          Cancel via a flag plus Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask, Invoke-NHKUiBatch for several .Set()
#          calls in one write, and a busy state that disables Count while work runs.
# Run:     pwsh -File ./word_counter.ps1 [FILE]   |   powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\word_counter.ps1 [FILE]
#          (without FILE it counts 20,000 lines of generated text)
# Guide:   docs/powershell/guides/background-work.md
param([string]$Path)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Word counter'

$culture = [Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture
$s = @{ App = $app; Path = $Path; Lines = @(); Next = 0; Counts = @{}; Task = $null; Cancel = $false
        Progress = (New-NHKUiState -Value 'Press Count to start.'); TopWords = (New-NHKUiState -Value @())
        Running = (New-NHKUiState -Value $false) }
$s.Idle = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Running) -Data $s -Compute { param($s) -not $s.Running.Value }
$chunkSize = 2000

function Format-Number([long]$Value) { return [string]::Format($culture, '{0:N0}', $Value) }

function Read-Lines {
    if ($s.Path) { return , [IO.File]::ReadAllLines([IO.Path]::GetFullPath($s.Path)) }
    # Generated sample: line i is nine consecutive words of a fixed list, starting at word i.
    $words = 'the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog while native windows render html'.Split(' ')
    $distinct = @(for ($i = 0; $i -lt $words.Count; $i++) { (@(for ($j = 0; $j -lt 9; $j++) { $words[($i + $j) % $words.Count] })) -join ' ' })
    return , [string[]]@(for ($i = 0; $i -lt 20000; $i++) { $distinct[$i % $words.Count] })
}

function Complete-Count([string]$Message, [object[]]$Words) {
    Invoke-NHKUiBatch -UI $ui -ScriptBlock {
        $s.Progress.Set($Message)
        $s.TopWords.Set($Words)
        $s.Running.Set($false)
    }
}

function Start-Chunk {
    if ($s.Cancel) { Complete-Count 'Cancelled.' @(); return }
    $total = $s.Lines.Count
    if ($s.Next -ge $total) {
        $sum = [long]0
        foreach ($value in $s.Counts.Values) { $sum += $value }
        $top = @($s.Counts.GetEnumerator() | Sort-Object @{ Expression = 'Value'; Descending = $true }, @{ Expression = 'Name'; Descending = $false } |
            Select-Object -First 10 | ForEach-Object { '{0}: {1}' -f $_.Name, (Format-Number $_.Value) })
        Complete-Count ('Done: {0} words, {1} different, {2} lines.' -f (Format-Number $sum), (Format-Number $s.Counts.Count), (Format-Number $total)) $top
        return
    }
    $count = [Math]::Min($chunkSize, $total - $s.Next)
    $chunk = [string[]]$s.Lines[$s.Next..($s.Next + $count - 1)]
    $s.Next += $count
    # The worker sees only its argument (an array of strings) and returns a plain hashtable.
    $s.Task = Start-NativeHTMLKitTask -Application $s.App -ArgumentList (, $chunk) -TimeoutMilliseconds 60000 -ScriptBlock {
        param([string[]]$lines)
        $pattern = New-Object Text.RegularExpressions.Regex("[^\W\d_]+(?:'[^\W\d_]+)?")
        $counts = @{}
        foreach ($line in $lines) {
            foreach ($match in $pattern.Matches($line)) {
                $word = $match.Value.ToLowerInvariant()
                if ($counts.ContainsKey($word)) { $counts[$word]++ } else { $counts[$word] = 1 }
            }
        }
        $counts
    } -OnCompleted {
        param($result)
        foreach ($entry in $result[0].GetEnumerator()) {
            if ($s.Counts.ContainsKey($entry.Key)) { $s.Counts[$entry.Key] += $entry.Value } else { $s.Counts[$entry.Key] = $entry.Value }
        }
        $s.Progress.Set(('{0}% - {1} lines' -f [Math]::Round(100.0 * $s.Next / [Math]::Max(1, $s.Lines.Count)), (Format-Number $s.Next)))
        Start-Chunk
    } -OnFailed {
        param($failure)
        if ($s.Cancel) { Complete-Count 'Cancelled.' @() } else { Complete-Count ('Failed: ' + $failure.Message) @() }
    }
}

$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Word counter' -Theme daylight -Density regular -Width 560 -Height 560
$source = if ($Path) { [IO.Path]::GetFileName($Path) } else { 'generated sample text' }
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Word counter' -Level 1
    $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Text "Source: $source" -Muted
    $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Count' -DisabledState $s.Running -Data $s -OnClick {
            param($eventObject, $s)
            if ($s.Running.Value) { return }
            try { $s.Lines = Read-Lines }
            catch { $s.Progress.Set('Cannot read the file: ' + $_.Exception.Message); return }
            $s.Next = 0; $s.Counts = @{}; $s.Cancel = $false
            $s.Running.Set($true)
            $s.TopWords.Set(@())
            $s.Progress.Set('Starting...')
            Start-Chunk
        }
        $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Cancel' -Variant secondary -DisabledState $s.Idle -Data $s -OnClick {
            param($eventObject, $s)
            $s.Cancel = $true
            if ($null -ne $s.Task) { Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask -Task $s.Task }
        }
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiAlert -UI $ui -Bind $s.Progress
    $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Most frequent words' -Level 2
        $null = Add-NHKUiTextList -UI $ui -Bind $s.TopWords
    }
}

try {
    $null = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Stop-NHKUi -UI $ui
    $s.Idle.Dispose()
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app      # also stops a task that is still running
}

items.title: Background work
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same guide for Python: background work.

Goal: run slow or periodic work without freezing the window, report progress, cancel it, and get the results into the UI safely.

items.title: The rule
items.text:
The UI may only be changed on the runspace that started it (the owner runspace). Work in another runspace (Start-NativeHTMLKitTask) cannot touch UI states; it receives plain data and returns plain data. The SDK runs -OnCompleted / -OnFailed later on the owner runspace, while Wait-NativeHTMLKit pumps, and those callbacks may set states.

Never call .Set() on a UI state from ForEach-Object -Parallel, thread jobs, raw runspaces or .NET event handlers: the module throws UI updates must run on the SDK owning runspace.

items.title: Run one job and report the result
items.text:
From the background example:

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

$s.Task = Start-NativeHTMLKitTask -Application $s.App -ArgumentList @(500000) -TimeoutMilliseconds 60000 -ScriptBlock {
    param([int]$n)                   # runs in another runspace; sees only its arguments
    $sum = [long]0
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $n; $i++) { $sum += $i }
    $sum
} -OnCompleted {
    param($result)                   # the worker's output as an array; runs on the owner
    $s.Status.Set('Done: ' + $result[0])
    $s.Busy.Set($false)
} -OnFailed {
    param($failure)                  # an exception; OperationCanceledException after Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask
    if ($failure -is [OperationCanceledException]) { $s.Status.Set('Cancelled') }
    else { $s.Status.Set('Failed: ' + $failure.GetType().Name) }
    $s.Busy.Set($false)
}
  • Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask -Task $s.Task requests cancellation; -OnFailed then receives an OperationCanceledException (verified by the example harness).
  • The SDK allows 8 running tasks per application; Close-NativeHTMLKit stops tasks that are still running.
  • Several .Set() calls in a task callback are separate window writes; wrap them in Invoke-NHKUiBatch -UI $ui -ScriptBlock { ... } to write once.

items.title: Report progress and cancel
items.text:
A task cannot report progress while it runs. Split the work into chunks instead: each chunk is one task, its -OnCompleted merges the partial result, updates the progress state and starts the next chunk. Cancel sets a flag that the next chunk checks and stops the running task. From the word_counter example:

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

function Start-Chunk {
    if ($s.Cancel) { Complete-Count 'Cancelled.' @(); return }
    if ($s.Next -ge $s.Lines.Count) { <# all chunks done: report the totals #> return }
    $count = [Math]::Min($chunkSize, $s.Lines.Count - $s.Next)
    $chunk = [string[]]$s.Lines[$s.Next..($s.Next + $count - 1)]
    $s.Next += $count
    $s.Task = Start-NativeHTMLKitTask -Application $s.App -ArgumentList (, $chunk) -ScriptBlock {
        param([string[]]$lines)
        $counts = @{}
        # ... count the words of this chunk ...
        $counts                              # a plain hashtable goes back to the owner
    } -OnCompleted {
        param($result)
        foreach ($entry in $result[0].GetEnumerator()) { <# merge into $s.Counts #> }
        $s.Progress.Set(('{0}% - {1} lines' -f [Math]::Round(100.0 * $s.Next / $s.Lines.Count), $s.Next))
        Start-Chunk
    } -OnFailed {
        param($failure)
        if ($s.Cancel) { Complete-Count 'Cancelled.' @() } else { Complete-Count ('Failed: ' + $failure.Message) @() }
    }
}

, $chunk passes the array as one argument; without the comma every line would become a separate argument. Complete-Count sets three states inside Invoke-NHKUiBatch.

items.title: Streams and timers
items.text:
There is no timer cmdlet. A task that only sleeps, whose completion callback does the work and starts the next task, gives a periodic tick on the owner runspace (the log_viewer example and the dashboard example):

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

function Start-Tick {
    $null = Start-NativeHTMLKitTask -Application $app -ScriptBlock { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 200 } -OnCompleted {
        param($result)
        Add-LogLine $s
        Start-Tick
    }
}
$null = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app
Start-Tick
Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown

Each tick creates a runspace, which is fine for a few ticks per second, not for animation.

items.title: SDK calls that wait
items.text: Calls such as Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog wait inside the button callback while the SDK keeps processing host messages; their result is available when they return (the SDK calls guide).

items.title: Forms, inputs and validation
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same guide for Python: forms and inputs.

Goal: bind inputs, checkboxes and selects to state, validate as the user types, and only allow submitting a valid form.

items.title: Two-way binding
items.text:
Control PowerShell State holds Text input Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $name -Label 'Name' -Type text [string] Checkbox Add-NHKUiCheckbox -UI $ui -Bind $terms -Label 'I accept' [bool] Select Add-NHKUiSelect -UI $ui -Bind $plan -Label 'Plan' -Options @(@{ Value = 'free'; Label = 'Free' }, @{ Value = 'team'; Label = 'Team' }) the option value as [string]
  • Input types: text, search, email, password, number. A number input still gives a string; convert and validate it yourself.
  • Each keystroke updates the state; there is no "on blur" mode.
  • Setting the state from code updates the control ($s.Description.Set('') clears the field after "Add"). Typing never triggers a write-back, so the caret and IME stay intact.
  • -Options is fixed at build time; build it from an ordered dictionary with @($categories.Keys | ForEach-Object { @{ Value = $_; Label = $categories[$_] } }).

items.title: Validation as derived state
items.text:
Do not read values from the DOM. Compute the problems from the states (the signup_form example):

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

$s.Errors = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn $fields -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s)
    $found = New-Object System.Collections.ArrayList
    if ($s.Email.Value -and $s.Email.Value.Trim() -notmatch '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$') { [void]$found.Add('Enter a valid email address.') }
    if ($s.Confirm.Value -and $s.Confirm.Value -cne $s.Password.Value) { [void]$found.Add('Passwords do not match.') }
    , @($found)
}
$s.HasErrors = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Errors) -Data $s -Compute { param($s) @($s.Errors.Value).Count -gt 0 }
$null = Add-NHKUiWhen -UI $ui -Bind $s.HasErrors -Content { $null = Add-NHKUiTextList -UI $ui -Bind $s.Errors }
$null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Create account' -DisabledState $s.CannotSubmit -Data $s -OnClick { <# ... #> }

A single message works the same way (the settings editor): $problem is a computed string that is '' when everything is valid, $hasProblem a computed boolean, and Add-NHKUiWhen -Bind $hasProblem shows the message only when there is one. Bind Add-NHKUiWhen to a boolean: the string 'False' is true in PowerShell.

items.title: Patterns that make forms pleasant
items.text:
• Only complain about fields the user touched. Each rule starts with "if the field is not empty"; a separate muted hint says "Fill in every field" until the form is complete.
  • Disable, then re-check. The submit callback checks the condition again before acting.
  • Parse at the boundary. The expense tracker keeps the amount as text in state and converts it with [decimal]::TryParse(..., InvariantCulture, ...) only when adding; an invalid amount sets an error state shown in an alert inside Add-NHKUiWhen.
  • Reset by setting states. "Start over" sets every state back to its initial value; the controls follow.
  • Show results instead of the form. Two Add-NHKUiWhen regions (form / confirmation) switch on a Welcome state.

items.title: Loading and saving form data
items.text:
Create the states from the loaded data, keep a text snapshot of the last saved values and compare (the settings-editor tutorial builds this step by step):

$loaded = Read-Settings
$name = New-NHKUiState -Value ([string]$loaded.DisplayName)
...
$saved = New-NHKUiState -Value (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject (Get-Snapshot) -Compress)
$changes = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn $all -Compute {
    if ((ConvertTo-Json -InputObject (Get-Snapshot) -Compress) -eq $saved.Value) { 'All changes saved' } else { 'Unsaved changes' }
}

Write files atomically (a temporary file in the same folder, then [IO.File]::Replace or [IO.File]::Move), so a crash never leaves half a settings file. Build paths with [IO.Path]::Combine rather than Join-Path: on Windows the backend runs with an extended-length working directory (\\?\C:\...), relative paths resolve to such paths, and Windows PowerShell 5.1's Join-Path rejects them.

items.title: Keyboard events
items.text: The module only has -OnClick for buttons; there is no keydown or submit parameter. Use buttons, or register SDK document events on $ui.Document yourself (Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent) for other event kinds, and do not register input or change events for bound controls.

items.title: Native form features
items.text: The UI does not wrap <form>, HTML constraint validation (required, pattern) or form data. They are SDK document features (Get-NativeHTMLKitFormData, Submit-NativeHTMLKitForm) for apps that build their own markup.

items.title: Layouts and the responsive grid
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same guide for Python: layouts.

Goal: arrange components with rows, columns, cards and a grid that adapts to the window.

items.title: Containers
items.text:
PowerShell Element Use for Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content { } div.nhk-col The main vertical flow of a window. Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content { } div.nhk-row Toolbars, a field next to its button, badges next to a heading. Wraps when narrow. Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content { } div.nhk-card Grouping related content on a panel. Add-NHKUiGrid -UI $ui -Content { } div.nhk-grid Dashboards and settings pages: equal-width cells.

-Content runs immediately; components added inside it become children of the container. The module has no equivalent of Python's stack() or generic container()/element(); style the structure above with -ExtraCss instead.

items.title: A typical window
items.text:
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Settings' -Level 1
        $null = Add-NHKUiBadge -UI $ui -Bind $s.Badge
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiGrid -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
            $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Profile' -Level 3
            $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $s.Fields.DisplayName -Label 'Display name'
        }
        $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
            $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Editor' -Level 3
            $null = Add-NHKUiSelect -UI $ui -Bind $s.Fields.FontSize -Label 'Font size' -Options $fontSizes
        }
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Save' -Data $s -OnClick { param($eventObject, $s) <# ... #> }
        $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Revert' -Variant secondary -Data $s -OnClick { param($eventObject, $s) <# ... #> }
    }
}

Assign every Add-NHKUi* result to $null so the nodes do not end up in the script's output. The full version is the settings example.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: How the grid responds
items.text:
nhk-grid uses three equal columns. When the window's viewport is at most 1000 px wide it switches to two columns, at most 620 px to one column (and the app padding shrinks to 14 px). Cells keep min-width: 0, so long text wraps instead of widening the grid. There is no column-span API; put wide content outside the grid.

Rows wrap: a labelled input or select is a flex item of at least 150 px that grows (flex: 1 1 200px), so a row of three fields becomes two lines in a narrow window. The dashboard example shows six cards that reflow as you resize.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Fields directly in a column (known defect B-0014)
items.text:
The 0.1.1 stylesheet applies the row rule flex: 1 1 200px to fields placed directly in a column too, where the 200 px basis becomes the field's height: a labelled input followed by more content leaves a large gap. Fields inside a row or a card are not affected. Until it is fixed, add this extra CSS when you put labelled inputs directly in Add-NHKUiColumn:

$fieldFix = '.nhk-col > .nhk-field { flex: 0 0 auto; }'
$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Create account' -ExtraCss $fieldFix

The signup_form and multi_window examples do this.

items.title: Density and window size
items.text:
New-NHKUi -Density changes control height, font size, gaps and padding for the whole window (compact 30 px controls / 13 px font, regular 36 / 14, comfortable 42 / 15). -Width and -Height (100-8192) are the requested initial window size in CSS pixels (the host may clamp it to the screen). Use comfortable for touch screens and forms that are read more than written, compact for tool windows. The theme_preview example shows every density.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Rules of thumb
items.text:
• Exactly one outer Add-NHKUiColumn per window keeps spacing consistent.
  • Put a label on every input and select (-Label); placeholders disappear.
  • Headings: one -Level 1 per window, -Level 2 or -Level 3 inside cards.
  • The tree is fixed after Start-NHKUi; adding components later throws. Plan every region you need up front and toggle it with Add-NHKUiWhen.

items.text:
PowerShell reference: layout containers · CSS reference · theming

Source: nativehtmlkit_ui/docs/powershell/guides/layouts.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Lists and conditional content
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same guide for Python: lists and conditional content.

Goal: show collections and optional parts of a window, given that the component tree is fixed once the window opens.

items.title: Conditional regions
items.text:
$null = Add-NHKUiWhen -UI $ui -Bind $s.Error -Content { $null = Add-NHKUiAlert -UI $ui -Bind $s.Error }
$s.NothingVisible = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Visible) -Data $s -Compute { param($s) @($s.Visible.Value).Count -eq 0 }
$null = Add-NHKUiWhen -UI $ui -Bind $s.NothingVisible -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Text 'No expenses to show yet.' -Muted
}

A region is always in the document and only toggles display: none (class nhk-hidden). Hidden inputs keep their values; showing the region again is instant. Regions nest (the settings example hides the "autosave interval" field, and inside it an error alert). Typical uses: empty states, validation messages, "paused" banners, swapping a form for a confirmation (two regions with opposite conditions). The condition uses [bool]: '', $null, 0, $false and empty arrays hide the region, but the string 'False' is true; bind booleans or a computed -not ....

items.title: Text lists
items.text:
$s.Lines = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Visible) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s) , @($s.Visible.Value | ForEach-Object { '{0}: {1}' -f $_.Description, $_.Amount })
}
$null = Add-NHKUiTextList -UI $ui -Bind $s.Lines
  • Items are always encoded text; markup in data is shown literally.
  • The list shows @($state.Value); format the strings in a computed state.
  • A change replaces all <li> children at once. Show a bounded window of data (the log viewer shows the newest 14 of up to 500 lines) rather than thousands of rows.
  • Filtering and sorting belong in a computed state, not in the list.

items.title: Interactive rows: the slot pool
items.text:
A text list cannot hold buttons. When each row needs actions, create a fixed number of row "slots" at build time and bind each slot to "the item at position i of the visible list" (the todo example). Each slot gets its own hashtable with the row index and small computed states (present, text, button label), and passes itself to the buttons with -Data:

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

for ($row = 0; $row -lt $maxTasks; $row++) {
    $slot = @{ S = $s; Row = $row }
    $slot.Present = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Visible) -Data $slot -Compute { param($t) $t.Row -lt @($t.S.Visible.Value).Count }
    $null = Add-NHKUiWhen -UI $ui -Bind $slot.Present -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Remove' -Variant quiet -Data $slot -OnClick {
            param($eventObject, $t)
            $items = @($t.S.Visible.Value)
            if ($t.Row -ge $items.Count) { return }
            $id = $items[$t.Row].Id
            $t.S.Tasks.Set(@($t.S.Tasks.Value | Where-Object { $_.Id -ne $id }))
        }
    }
}
  • Pass the slot with -Data instead of relying on the loop variable inside the callback.
  • Callbacks look the item up at click time and act on its id, so they stay correct when the filter or order changes.
  • Cap the model at the number of slots and say so in the UI.
  • Keep every slot's computed states in your disposal list.

items.title: When you outgrow this
items.text: For large tables, rich per-row markup or virtual scrolling, render that part yourself with the SDK's document API (Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml, with your own encoding via [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode) inside an Add-NHKUiHtml container that you own completely. The UI module deliberately has no data grid.

items.title: Mixing the UI with direct SDK calls
path: Mixing the UI with direct SDK calls

items.title: Mixing the UI with direct SDK calls
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same guide for Python: mixing the UI with SDK calls.

Goal: use SDK services (dialogs, clipboard, window control, DOM queries) from a UI app.
path: Mixing the UI with direct SDK calls

items.title: The handles
items.text:
The UI module covers components and state. Everything else belongs to the PowerShell SDK, and a UI app calls it directly. The handles you need are on the UI object after Start-NHKUi:

PowerShell Use $ui.Application (or the $app you passed) Clipboard, quit, preferences, window events $ui.Window (also returned by Start-NHKUi) Dialogs, Close-NativeHTMLKitWindow, window state $ui.Document Reading DOM state, focus, scrolling, stylesheets $node.Id Target id for document calls (every Add-NHKUi* returns its node)
path: Mixing the UI with direct SDK calls

items.title: Clipboard
items.text:
try {
    Set-NativeHTMLKitClipboard -Application $s.App -Text ([string]$s.Result.Value)
    $s.Status.Set(('Copied {0} characters to the clipboard.' -f ([string]$s.Result.Value).Length))
} catch { $s.Status.Set('Clipboard unavailable: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }

Always handle the error: the clipboard is not available everywhere. In the host's headless test mode it fails with code -32001 ("Clipboard requires a native event loop"), which is the path the example harness verifies (the clipboard_tool example). An exception that escapes a UI callback is counted as a callback failure; catch expected errors inside the callback.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.
path: Mixing the UI with direct SDK calls

items.title: File dialogs
items.text:
Call the dialog from the button callback; the call waits (while the SDK keeps processing host messages) until the user closes it, and the callback's state changes are written when it returns (the file_picker example):

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

try {
    $result = Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog -Window $s.UI.Window -Kind OpenFiles -Multiple $true -Title 'Choose files to inspect'
} catch { $s.Status.Set('File dialogs are unavailable here: ' + $_.Exception.Message); return }
if ($result.cancelled -or @($result.paths).Count -eq 0) { $s.Status.Set('No files chosen.'); return }

Dialogs are unavailable in headless mode (-32001), so the harness verifies the error path; the interactive dialog path was not part of the automated run.
path: Mixing the UI with direct SDK calls

items.title: Reading the DOM
items.text:
The UI's states are the source of truth, but SDK reads are useful for focus management and tests:

$node = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $name -Label 'Name'
...
Set-NativeHTMLKitFocus -Document $ui.Document -Element $node.Id      # after Start-NHKUi
Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $ui.Document -Element $node.Id      # what the native control holds
path: Mixing the UI with direct SDK calls

items.title: Rules
items.text:
• Do not change bound properties behind the UI's back (Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText on an element whose text is bound): the next write may overwrite it, and the UI cannot know. Change the state.
  • Do not add elements into managed containers with raw document calls; the UI's tree would no longer describe the document. Use an Add-NHKUiHtml container you own, or a separate window.
  • A callback that waits for an SDK call delays the next UI event (there is no event queue).
  • Window and application lifecycle (Close-NativeHTMLKitWindow, Request-NativeHTMLKitQuit, Close-NativeHTMLKit) always belongs to your code.
path: Mixing the UI with direct SDK calls

items.title: Multiple windows and multiple UIs
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same guide for Python: multiple windows.

Goal: open more than one window, share state between them, and handle closing.

items.title: One UI per window
items.text:
Each New-NHKUi object is one window. Create as many as you need from one SDK application; they may bind the same states, and every window updates when a shared state changes (the multi_window example). All UIs live on the same owner runspace.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Open a window from a callback
items.text:
$inspector = New-NHKUi -Title 'Inspector 1' -Width 420 -Height 320 -Theme graphite
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $inspector -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $inspector -Bind $s.NoteText        # same state as the main window
}
$window = Start-NHKUi -UI $inspector -Application $s.App -NoReady
[void]$s.Inspectors.Add([pscustomobject]@{ UI = $inspector; WindowId = $window.Id })

Start later UIs with -NoReady (readiness was announced by the first one; the SDK would ignore a second call anyway). Close-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Window $inspector.Window asks the host to close a window from code.

items.title: Notice closed windows
items.text:
The UI module does not watch window events itself: without a handler, a closed window's UI is stopped on its next write (DiscardedAfterClose). To react immediately, handle the SDK's window.event notification:

Register-NativeHTMLKitNotification -Application $app -Method 'window.event' -Callback {
    param($notification)
    if ($notification.type -ne 'closed') { return }
    foreach ($entry in @($s.Inspectors)) {
        if ($entry.WindowId -eq $notification.window_id) {
            Stop-NHKUi -UI $entry.UI
            $s.Inspectors.Remove($entry)
            $s.Open.Set($s.Inspectors.Count)
        }
    }
}
  • Register-NativeHTMLKitNotification holds one callback per method; combine all window-event handling in that one callback.
  • Closing the last window ends the application (Core asks for quit with reason last_window).

items.title: Limits
items.text: The Python shutdown-callback defect B-0003 does not apply: Start-NHKUi registers no application shutdown callback. Still keep the number of windows bounded; the example allows three inspectors at a time.

items.title: Clean up
items.text: In finally, call Stop-NHKUi for every UI you started (it is idempotent) and dispose shared computed states once, then Close-NativeHTMLKit.

items.text:
PowerShell reference: Start-NHKUi · SDK calls

Source: nativehtmlkit_ui/docs/powershell/guides/multiple-windows.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Reactive state and computed values
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same guide for Python: reactive state.

Goal: keep application data in states, derive everything else, and let the window follow.

Every example in this module follows one rule: the window shows state; button callbacks change state; nothing writes to the window directly.

items.title: Model data as state
items.text:
$s = @{
    Expenses = (New-NHKUiState -Value @())    # source data
    Show     = (New-NHKUiState -Value 'all')  # a choice the user makes
}

New-NHKUiState returns a state object. Read it with .Value, change it with .Set($new). Components bound to it (-Bind $s.Show) update themselves. Assigning .Value directly notifies nobody; always call .Set(). Keeping all states in one hashtable ($s) makes it easy to pass them to callbacks with -Data.

items.title: Derive values with computed
items.text:
$s.Visible = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Expenses, $s.Show) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s)
    , @($s.Expenses.Value | Where-Object { $s.Show.Value -eq 'all' -or $_.Category -eq $s.Show.Value })
}
$s.Count = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Visible, $s.Expenses) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s) '{0} of {1} expenses' -f @($s.Visible.Value).Count, @($s.Expenses.Value).Count
}
$null = Add-NHKUiBadge -UI $ui -Bind $s.Count
  • List every state the scriptblock reads in -DependsOn; there is no automatic tracking.
  • Pass states with -Data (one hashtable is convenient); the scriptblock receives it as its first parameter.
  • Return arrays with a leading comma (, @(...)), or an empty result becomes $null and a one-element result a scalar.
  • There are no bound expressions: anything formatted is a computed state. Keep a list of them and call .Dispose() on each in finally; Stop-NHKUi does not dispose them.
  • Computed states can depend on computed states (Count depends on Visible).

items.title: Change data by replacing it
items.text:
Change detection uses [object]::Equals, which is reference equality for arrays, hashtables and objects. Changing them in place is invisible:

$s.Tasks.Value += $item                         # WRONG: assignment bypasses notification
$s.Tasks.Set(@($s.Tasks.Value) + @($item))      # right: a new array

Store records as [pscustomobject]s that you replace instead of edit, and give list items an id when rows can be toggled or removed (the todo example).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Side effects: subscribe
items.text:
When a change should trigger something that is not display (a counter, saving, logging), use .Subscribe(). It runs synchronously inside .Set():

$null = $s.Note.Subscribe({ param($value, $ctx) $ctx.Edits.Set([int]$ctx.Edits.Value + 1) }, $s)

The callback receives the new value and the context object you passed as the second argument. Keep subscribers short and remove them with .Unsubscribe($subscription) when no longer needed.

items.title: Dirty tracking and snapshots
items.text:
Hashtables compare by reference, so compare a text key of the fields instead (the settings example; the settings-editor tutorial uses compressed JSON the same way):

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

$s.Key = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Fields.Values) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s) (@($s.Fields.Keys | ForEach-Object { $_ + '=' + [string]$s.Fields[$_].Value }) -join ';')
}
$s.SavedKey = New-NHKUiState -Value $s.Key.Value
$s.Dirty = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Key, $s.SavedKey) -Data $s -Compute { param($s) $s.Key.Value -ne $s.SavedKey.Value }

items.title: Where states may be changed
items.text: A state bound to a UI may only be set on the runspace that started the UI (the owner runspace): in button callbacks, in SDK task -OnCompleted/-OnFailed callbacks, in notification callbacks, or in the script itself. From any other runspace the module throws UI updates must run on the SDK owning runspace. See background work. Computed states are synchronous on the owner runspace; the Python defect B-0002 does not apply.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Testing your UI
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same guide for Python: testing.

Goal: test application logic quickly, then prove it against the real native host.

items.title: 1. Logic without a host
items.text:
States and computed states work without any window, so plain Pester tests cover the logic:

Describe 'expense totals' {
    It 'follows the filter' {
        $s = @{ Expenses = (New-NHKUiState -Value @(
                    [pscustomobject]@{ Category = 'food'; Amount = 3 }, [pscustomobject]@{ Category = 'home'; Amount = 5 }))
                Show = (New-NHKUiState -Value 'all') }
        $total = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Expenses, $s.Show) -Data $s -Compute {
            param($s) ($s.Expenses.Value | Where-Object { $s.Show.Value -eq 'all' -or $_.Category -eq $s.Show.Value } |
                Measure-Object Amount -Sum).Sum
        }
        $total.Value | Should -Be 8
        $s.Show.Set('home')
        $total.Value | Should -Be 5
        $total.Dispose()
    }
}

Get-NHKUiHtml renders the full document without a host, which is enough to check structure, labels and escaping:

$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 't'
$null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Text '<b>x</b>'
(Get-NHKUiHtml -UI $ui) | Should -Match '<b>x</b>'

The module's own unit tests do the same with a fake SDK (powershell/tests/Unit.Tests.ps1).

items.title: 2. The real host, headless
items.text:
Set NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 and start the script normally. The SDK launches the real Core host in headless mode: the whole protocol runs (documents load, commands apply, events can be delivered) but no window is shown. Native input does not exist there, and services that need a desktop (clipboard, file dialogs, opening URLs) fail with error -32001, so code paths for those errors get exercised.

In a test you can then:

  • read DOM state through the SDK: Get-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText, Get-NativeHTMLKitValue, Get-NativeHTMLKitChecked, Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Operation get_attribute with $node.Id and $ui.Document;
  • rely on synchronous writes: outside callbacks the window is written when the outermost .Set() returns (Sync-NHKUi writes anything pending);
  • assert health: Get-NHKUiDiagnostics has Errors = 0 and DomUncertain = $false, and Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnosticReport shows no CallbackFailures;
  • end with Request-NativeHTMLKitQuit and check the process exits 0.

items.title: 3. The example harness
items.text:
qualification/examples/run_examples.py (Python 3.11+, standard library only) runs every example and tutorial step listed in examples/catalog.toml this way, in PowerShell and Python, each through its own normal entry point (pwsh -File example.ps1 [args]), unchanged. A small probe records the started UIs, replays the scenario from qualification/examples/scenarios.json on the owner runspace, reads the DOM back, and quits:

"expenses": {"steps": [
  {"op": "type", "label": "Description", "value": "Coffee"},
  {"op": "type", "label": "Amount", "value": "3.50"},
  {"op": "click", "label": "Add expense"},
  {"op": "expect_text", "contains": ["Coffee (Food): 3.50", "Total: 3.50"]},
  {"op": "expect_value", "label": "Description", "value": ""}
]}

Steps: click, type, check, choose (simulated events), expect_text / wait_text (visible text, skipping hidden regions), expect_value, expect_disabled, expect_uis, close_window, sleep. Each step may target another window with "ui": 1 and the n-th matching control with "nth". A scenario may give "args" (positional script arguments) and separate "py"/"ps" step lists.

# PowerShell 7: put the NativeHTMLKit SDK module folder and ./powershell on PSModulePath
python qualification/examples/run_examples.py --lang ps --pwsh pwsh \
    --ps-module-path "/path/to/sdk-modules:$PWD/powershell"

# Windows PowerShell 5.1
python qualification\examples\run_examples.py --lang ps --pwsh powershell.exe --ps-module-path "C:\sdk-modules;$PWD\powershell"

Per example it requires: ready reached, all steps passed, clean UI diagnostics, no SDK callback failures or dropped notifications, exit code 0, no exception on stderr, and no leftover host/backend process. It also fails when a catalogue entry lacks a file in either language, a file has no scenario, or a script under examples/ is not in the catalogue.

What this proves and what not. Events are injected at the UI module's SDK callback entry point after writing the control value with the public SDK, so the app's callbacks, states, computed states and document writes run against the real host exactly as after native input. It does not prove native input, focus, IME, rendering or accessibility.

items.title: 4. On a desktop
items.text: Run the script normally and use it. For repeatable GUI checks, drive real input with your platform's tooling and read state back through the SDK, as the repository's qualification/gui driver does on KDE Plasma Wayland and Windows.

items.title: Theming and custom CSS
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same guide for Python: theming and custom CSS.

Goal: pick a theme and density, adjust colours, and style your own elements.

items.title: Themes and densities
items.text:
$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Dashboard' -Theme graphite -Density regular -ExtraCss $css
  • Themes: cobalt (dark blue, default), graphite (dark grey), daylight (light).
  • Densities: compact (default), regular, comfortable.
  • The CSS reference lists every token and class.

To see them all, run the theme_preview example with different arguments. It uses Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Instance multiple, so several previews can run side by side:

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

pwsh -File ./theme_preview.ps1 cobalt compact
pwsh -File ./theme_preview.ps1 daylight comfortable '#0f7b6c'

items.title: Override design tokens
items.text:
-ExtraCss is appended after the built-in stylesheet, so the same selector wins. Override tokens on body.nhk-theme-<name>; every component follows. From theme_preview.ps1:

$css = ''
if ($Accent) { $css = "body.nhk-theme-$Theme { --nhk-accent: $Accent; --nhk-accent-strong: $Accent; --nhk-focus: $Accent; }" }
$ui = New-NHKUi -Title "Theme preview: $Theme/$Density" -Theme $Theme -Density $Density -ExtraCss $css

Change --nhk-accent, --nhk-accent-strong and --nhk-focus together and check contrast against --nhk-accent-text.

items.title: Style your own elements
items.text:
The module has no generic element function, so style the structure it creates. From the dashboard example:

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

$css = @'
.nhk-card h1.nhk-heading { font-size: 30px; margin: 4px 0; }
.nhk-card { border-top: 3px solid var(--nhk-accent); }
body.nhk-theme-daylight { --nhk-accent: #0f7b6c; --nhk-accent-strong: #0b6458; --nhk-focus: #0f7b6c; }
'@

For your own classes, put static markup you wrote into Add-NHKUiHtml and style it (see trusted and untrusted content).

Guidelines:

  • Use var(--nhk-*) in your own rules so they work in every theme.
  • Target classes, never generated ids (they are random per run).
  • Extra CSS is trusted developer input. Do not build it from user input (the preview only accepts an accent that matches #RRGGBB).
  • Core renders a defined CSS subset natively (no browser engine); test layouts on your target desktops. See Core's HTML/CSS support.

items.title: Choose the theme at start
items.text: Theme and density are fixed when the window opens. Take them from the command line (the dashboard and theme preview), from a saved setting (the settings-editor tutorial starts in the saved theme), or from the desktop: read Get-NativeHTMLKitPreferences -Application $app before building the UI and pick daylight or a dark theme. Inspect the returned object on your systems first; the UI module does not interpret it.

items.title: Trusted and untrusted content
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same guide for Python: trusted and untrusted content.

Goal: show user, file and network data safely, and know when raw HTML is acceptable.

items.title: The rule
items.text:
Content Use Escaped? Anything a user typed, a file contained, a process printed or a server returned Add-NHKUiText, Add-NHKUiHeading, Add-NHKUiBadge, Add-NHKUiAlert, Add-NHKUiTextList, -Bind button labels Yes, always Option values and labels of Add-NHKUiSelect -Options Yes Static markup you wrote and ship with the app Add-NHKUiHtml -Markup No, inserted verbatim Extra CSS New-NHKUi -ExtraCss No (trusted)

Text components never interpret markup. In the message_preview example, typing <b>bold</b> & <i>x</i> into the message field shows exactly those characters in the preview and in the sent list; the harness reads the element text back through the SDK and checks it.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

$null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Bind $s.Preview              # safe for any input
$null = Add-NHKUiHtml -UI $ui -Markup $help                  # $help is a here-string in the script

items.title: Why raw HTML is dangerous even without JavaScript
items.text:
NativeHTMLKit runs no JavaScript, but injected markup can still restyle or hide your interface, fake buttons and labels, add elements whose ids clash with managed ones, or reference images and other resources. Treat Add-NHKUiHtml like code: only constants, reviewed like code.

If you must display structured untrusted data (a table of records), build it from text components or encode every value yourself with [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode before composing markup, and render it into a container you own.

items.title: Other built-in guards
items.text:
• Element ids are generated ($ui.Prefix plus a counter); you cannot choose them.
  • Attribute names must be plain names and may not start with on (no inline handlers).
  • The module has no generic element function; anything beyond its components must go through Add-NHKUiHtml, which makes trusted markup explicit in review.
  • Logs: the examples never log typed values. Keep secrets (passwords) out of Write-Host, logs and diagnostics you export.

items.title: Tutorial (PowerShell): build an expense tracker
items.text:
In about 30 minutes you build a small native desktop app with NativeHTMLKit.UI: enter expenses, validate amounts, remove the last entry, filter by category and see totals that update by themselves. You learn the module's whole model: states, components bound to states, button callbacks that change states, and computed states.

Every step is a complete script in examples/tutorials/powershell/ and the finished app is examples/powershell/expenses.ps1. All of them run in the repository's example harness against the real NativeHTMLKit host, on PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1. The code avoids PowerShell 7-only syntax.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

The Python version of this tutorial is here.

items.title: Step 0: install and check
items.text:
PowerShell 7.2+ (Linux or Windows) or Windows PowerShell 5.1:

Install-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI -Scope CurrentUser      # also installs the NativeHTMLKit SDK
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI
(Get-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI).Version                    # 0.1.1

items.title: Step 1: a window with bound inputs
items.text:
Create expenses.ps1:

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Expenses'

$s = @{ Description = (New-NHKUiState -Value ''); Amount = (New-NHKUiState -Value '') }
$s.Preview = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Description, $s.Amount) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s)
    $d = if ($s.Description.Value) { $s.Description.Value } else { '...' }
    $a = if ($s.Amount.Value) { $s.Amount.Value } else { '0.00' }
    "New expense: $d, $a"
}

$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Expenses' -Width 760 -Height 640
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Expenses' -Level 1
    $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
            $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $s.Description -Label 'Description' -Placeholder 'Coffee with Sam'
            $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $s.Amount -Label 'Amount' -Placeholder '0.00'
        }
        $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Bind $s.Preview -Muted
    }
}

try {
    $null = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Stop-NHKUi -UI $ui
    $s.Preview.Dispose()
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

Run it with pwsh -File ./expenses.ps1 (or powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\expenses.ps1) and type into both fields: the preview follows every keystroke.

What happened:

  • Start-NativeHTMLKitScript starts the native host, which runs this script again as its backend and returns the connected application there. Everything above that line runs twice; keep side effects below it.
  • New-NHKUiState creates an observable value; Add-NHKUiInput -Bind binds it two ways.
  • New-NHKUiComputed derives a value. Unlike Python, PowerShell lists the dependencies explicitly in -DependsOn, and the scriptblock gets its inputs through -Data (here the hashtable $s that holds all states).
  • Containers take a -Content scriptblock; components created inside it become children. Assign results to $null so the nodes do not end up in the script's output.
  • Start-NHKUi opens the window and announces readiness; Wait-NativeHTMLKit -UntilShutdown pumps events until the window closes. finally stops the UI, disposes computed states and closes the connection.

(Complete file: examples/tutorials/powershell/expenses_step1.ps1.)

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 2: a list of expenses
items.text:
Add a list state, a computed list of lines and two buttons:

$s = @{ Expenses = (New-NHKUiState -Value @()); Description = (New-NHKUiState -Value ''); Amount = (New-NHKUiState -Value '') }
$s.Lines = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Expenses) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s) , @($s.Expenses.Value | ForEach-Object { '{0}: {1}' -f $_.Description, $_.Amount })
}
$s.NoExpenses = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Expenses) -Data $s -Compute { param($s) @($s.Expenses.Value).Count -eq 0 }
$computeds = @($s.Lines, $s.NoExpenses)

        $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
            $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Add expense' -Data $s -OnClick {
                param($eventObject, $s)
                $new = [pscustomobject]@{ Description = $s.Description.Value.Trim(); Amount = $s.Amount.Value.Trim() }
                $s.Expenses.Set(@($s.Expenses.Value) + @($new))
                $s.Description.Set('')
                $s.Amount.Set('')
            }
            $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Remove last' -Variant secondary -DisabledState $s.NoExpenses -Data $s -OnClick {
                param($eventObject, $s)
                $items = @($s.Expenses.Value)
                $s.Expenses.Set(@($items | Select-Object -First ([Math]::Max(0, $items.Count - 1))))
            }
        }
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content { $null = Add-NHKUiTextList -UI $ui -Bind $s.Lines }

and dispose every computed state in finally: foreach ($c in $computeds) { $c.Dispose() }.

New ideas:

  • Callbacks change states, nothing else. Setting Description and Amount to '' clears the fields. A button callback receives param($eventObject, $data), where $data is the -Data argument.
  • Always .Set() a new array. States compare with [object]::Equals, which for arrays means "same array object". $s.Expenses.Value += $new would not notify anybody.
  • The leading comma in , @(...) returns the array itself; without it an empty list becomes $null and a one-item list a single string.
  • -DisabledState takes a state (here a computed boolean).
  • All changes made in one callback reach the window in one update.

(Complete file: examples/tutorials/powershell/expenses_step2.ps1.)

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 3: categories and validation
items.text:
Add a category select, an error state and a computed state that disables Add expense while a field is empty. Parse the amount culture-independently:

$categories = [ordered]@{ food = 'Food'; transport = 'Transport'; home = 'Home'; other = 'Other' }
$categoryOptions = @($categories.Keys | ForEach-Object { @{ Value = $_; Label = $categories[$_] } })
# in $s: Category = (New-NHKUiState -Value 'food'); Error = (New-NHKUiState -Value '')
#        Categories = $categories; Culture = [Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture
$s.CannotAdd = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Description, $s.Amount) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s) (-not $s.Description.Value.Trim()) -or (-not $s.Amount.Value.Trim())
}

            $null = Add-NHKUiSelect -UI $ui -Bind $s.Category -Label 'Category' -Options $categoryOptions
        ...
        $null = Add-NHKUiWhen -UI $ui -Bind $s.Error -Content { $null = Add-NHKUiAlert -UI $ui -Bind $s.Error }
        ...
            $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Add expense' -DisabledState $s.CannotAdd -Data $s -OnClick {
                param($eventObject, $s)
                $value = [decimal]0
                $text = $s.Amount.Value.Trim().Replace(',', '.')
                if (-not [decimal]::TryParse($text, [Globalization.NumberStyles]::Number, $s.Culture, [ref]$value)) {
                    $s.Error.Set('Amount must be a number, for example 12.50'); return
                }
                if ($value -le 0) { $s.Error.Set('Amount must be greater than zero'); return }
                $new = [pscustomobject]@{ Description = $s.Description.Value.Trim(); Amount = [Math]::Round($value, 2); Category = $s.Category.Value }
                $s.Expenses.Set(@($s.Expenses.Value) + @($new))
                $s.Description.Set(''); $s.Amount.Set(''); $s.Error.Set('')
            }

New ideas:

  • Add-NHKUiSelect -Options takes @{ Value = ...; Label = ... } entries; the state holds the selected value.
  • Add-NHKUiWhen -Bind $s.Error shows its content while the error text is non-empty; the region is only hidden, never rebuilt.
  • [decimal] with InvariantCulture parses 12.50 the same way on every system locale.

(Complete file: examples/tutorials/powershell/expenses_step3.ps1.)

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 4: filter and totals
items.text:
The finished app adds a Show filter and derives everything else from Expenses and Show:

$s.Visible = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Expenses, $s.Show) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s)
    , @($s.Expenses.Value | Where-Object { $s.Show.Value -eq 'all' -or $_.Category -eq $s.Show.Value })
}
$s.Total = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Visible) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s)
    $sum = [decimal]0
    foreach ($e in $s.Visible.Value) { $sum += $e.Amount }
    'Total: ' + $sum.ToString('#,##0.00', $s.Culture)
}
$s.Count = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($s.Visible, $s.Expenses) -Data $s -Compute {
    param($s) '{0} of {1} expenses' -f @($s.Visible.Value).Count, @($s.Expenses.Value).Count
}

    $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
            $null = Add-NHKUiSelect -UI $ui -Bind $s.Show -Label 'Show' -Options (@(@{ Value = 'all'; Label = 'All categories' }) + $categoryOptions)
            $null = Add-NHKUiBadge -UI $ui -Bind $s.Count
        }
        $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Bind $s.Total -Level 2
        $null = Add-NHKUiWhen -UI $ui -Bind $s.NothingVisible -Content {
            $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Text 'No expenses to show yet.' -Muted
        }
        $null = Add-NHKUiTextList -UI $ui -Bind $s.Lines
        $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Bind $s.ByCategory -Muted
    }

Computed states can depend on computed states (Total depends on Visible). One change to the filter recomputes the chain and updates the list, badge and total in one window update.

The complete script, including Lines, ByCategory, NothingVisible and NoExpenses, is examples/powershell/expenses.ps1.

items.title: Tutorial (PowerShell): build a settings editor
items.text:
PowerShell (NativeHTMLKit.UI 0.1.1; PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The same tutorial for Python: build a settings editor.

You will build Settings editor, a small editor for a JSON settings file: bound inputs, live validation, an "Unsaved changes" badge, Save and Revert buttons, and a theme the app itself uses on the next start.

Time: about 25 minutes. You need: NativeHTMLKit.UI installed and the first window from getting started working. Both steps are complete scripts, verified by the repository's example harness against the real NativeHTMLKit host on PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1: examples/tutorials/powershell/settings_editor_step1.ps1 and the final app examples/powershell/settings_editor.ps1.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

items.title: Step 1: a form bound to state
items.text:
Create settings_editor.ps1:

# Settings editor tutorial, step 1: a form whose controls are bound to UI state.
#
# Teaches: New-NHKUi, New-NHKUiState, two-way Add-NHKUiInput / Add-NHKUiSelect / Add-NHKUiCheckbox,
#          New-NHKUiComputed with explicit -DependsOn, Add-NHKUiText -Bind, Start-NHKUi / Stop-NHKUi.
# Run:     pwsh -File ./settings_editor_step1.ps1   |   powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\settings_editor_step1.ps1
# Guide:   docs/powershell/tutorials/settings-editor.md (step 1 of 2)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Settings editor'

$name = New-NHKUiState -Value 'Ada'
$email = New-NHKUiState -Value 'ada@example.org'
$theme = New-NHKUiState -Value 'cobalt'
$notify = New-NHKUiState -Value $true
$summary = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($name, $email, $theme, $notify) -Data @{ Name = $name; Email = $email; Theme = $theme; Notify = $notify } -Compute {
    param($s)
    $mail = if ($s.Notify.Value) { 'with e-mail notifications' } else { 'without notifications' }
    "$($s.Name.Value) <$($s.Email.Value)>, $($s.Theme.Value) theme, $mail"
}

$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Settings editor' -Theme cobalt -Density regular -Width 560 -Height 520
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Settings' -Level 1
    $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $name -Label 'Display name'
        $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $email -Label 'E-mail' -Type email
        $null = Add-NHKUiSelect -UI $ui -Bind $theme -Label 'Theme' -Options @(
            @{ Value = 'cobalt'; Label = 'Cobalt' }, @{ Value = 'graphite'; Label = 'Graphite' }, @{ Value = 'daylight'; Label = 'Daylight' })
        $null = Add-NHKUiCheckbox -UI $ui -Bind $notify -Label 'Send me e-mail notifications'
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Bind $summary -Muted
}

try {
    $null = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Stop-NHKUi -UI $ui
    $summary.Dispose()
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

Run pwsh -File ./settings_editor.ps1 (or powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\settings_editor.ps1) and edit the fields: the summary below follows every change.

  • Each New-NHKUiState holds one setting. Add-NHKUiInput -Bind $name is two-way; -Type email gives an e-mail field.
  • Add-NHKUiSelect -Options takes hashtables with Value and Label. Add-NHKUiCheckbox binds a Boolean.
  • New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @(...) lists its dependencies explicitly (PowerShell has no automatic dependency tracking), and receives -Data as its parameter.
  • The summary contains < and > around the e-mail address; Add-NHKUiText always encodes text, so this is safe.
  • The inputs are inside a card, so they keep their natural height. Labelled inputs placed directly in a column need the B-0014 workaround from the layouts guide.

items.title: Step 2: load, validate, save and revert
items.text:
Replace the script with the final version:

# Settings editor: edit, validate and save a JSON settings file (settings-editor tutorial, final code).
#
# Teaches: loading initial state from a file, computed validation and "unsaved changes" states,
#          saving JSON atomically, Revert, an Add-NHKUiAlert status line, and starting the UI in
#          the theme the user saved.
# Run:     pwsh -File ./settings_editor.ps1 [PATH]   |   powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\settings_editor.ps1 [PATH]
#          (default file: nativehtmlkit-settings.json in your application-data folder:
#          %APPDATA% on Windows, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config on Linux)
# Guide:   docs/powershell/tutorials/settings-editor.md (step 2 of 2)
param([string]$Path)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Settings editor'

# .NET path methods instead of Join-Path/Test-Path: on Windows the backend's working directory is an
# extended-length path (\\?\C:\...), which Windows PowerShell 5.1's Join-Path rejects.
if (-not $Path) { $Path = [IO.Path]::Combine([Environment]::GetFolderPath([Environment+SpecialFolder]::ApplicationData, [Environment+SpecialFolderOption]::Create), 'nativehtmlkit-settings.json') }
$Path = [IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Path)
$defaults = [ordered]@{ DisplayName = ''; Email = ''; Theme = 'cobalt'; RefreshSeconds = 60; Notifications = $false }
$themes = @('cobalt', 'graphite', 'daylight')

function Read-Settings {
    $result = [ordered]@{}
    foreach ($key in $defaults.Keys) { $result[$key] = $defaults[$key] }
    if ([IO.File]::Exists($Path)) {
        $data = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($Path) | ConvertFrom-Json
        foreach ($key in $defaults.Keys) {
            if ($null -ne $data.PSObject.Properties[$key]) { $result[$key] = $data.$key }
        }
    }
    if ($themes -notcontains $result.Theme) { $result.Theme = 'cobalt' }
    return $result
}

function Get-Snapshot {
    # The values as they would be saved; also used to detect unsaved changes.
    return [ordered]@{ DisplayName = $name.Value.Trim(); Email = $email.Value.Trim(); Theme = $theme.Value
        RefreshSeconds = $interval.Value.Trim(); Notifications = [bool]$notify.Value }
}

function Save-Settings {
    $snapshot = Get-Snapshot
    $snapshot.RefreshSeconds = [int]$snapshot.RefreshSeconds
    $json = ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $snapshot
    $folder = [IO.Path]::GetDirectoryName($Path)
    $null = [IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($folder)
    $temporary = [IO.Path]::Combine($folder, '.settings-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N') + '.tmp')
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($temporary, $json, (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))
    if ([IO.File]::Exists($Path)) { [IO.File]::Replace($temporary, $Path, [NullString]::Value) } else { [IO.File]::Move($temporary, $Path) }
}

$loaded = Read-Settings
$name = New-NHKUiState -Value ([string]$loaded.DisplayName)
$email = New-NHKUiState -Value ([string]$loaded.Email)
$theme = New-NHKUiState -Value ([string]$loaded.Theme)
$interval = New-NHKUiState -Value ([string]$loaded.RefreshSeconds)
$notify = New-NHKUiState -Value ([bool]$loaded.Notifications)
$saved = New-NHKUiState -Value (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject (Get-Snapshot) -Compress)
$status = New-NHKUiState -Value "Editing $Path"
$all = @($name, $email, $theme, $interval, $notify, $saved)

$problem = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn $all -Compute {
    $s = Get-Snapshot
    $seconds = 0
    if ($s.DisplayName -eq '') { 'Enter a display name.' }
    elseif ($s.Email -notmatch '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$') { 'The e-mail address looks invalid.' }
    elseif (-not [int]::TryParse($s.RefreshSeconds, [ref]$seconds) -or $seconds -lt 5 -or $seconds -gt 3600) { 'Refresh interval must be a whole number from 5 to 3600.' }
    else { '' }
}
$changes = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn $all -Compute {
    if ((ConvertTo-Json -InputObject (Get-Snapshot) -Compress) -eq $saved.Value) { 'All changes saved' } else { 'Unsaved changes' }
}
$hasProblem = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($problem) -Compute { $problem.Value -ne '' }

$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Settings editor' -Theme $loaded.Theme -Density regular -Width 600 -Height 640
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Settings' -Level 1
        $null = Add-NHKUiBadge -UI $ui -Bind $changes
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $name -Label 'Display name'
        $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $email -Label 'E-mail' -Type email
        $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $interval -Label 'Refresh interval (seconds)' -Type number
        $null = Add-NHKUiSelect -UI $ui -Bind $theme -Label 'Theme (applies on next start)' -Options @(
            @{ Value = 'cobalt'; Label = 'Cobalt' }, @{ Value = 'graphite'; Label = 'Graphite' }, @{ Value = 'daylight'; Label = 'Daylight' })
        $null = Add-NHKUiCheckbox -UI $ui -Bind $notify -Label 'Send me e-mail notifications'
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiWhen -UI $ui -Bind $hasProblem -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Bind $problem
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiRow -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Save' -OnClick {
            param($eventObject, $data)
            if ($problem.Value -ne '') { $status.Set('Fix the problem above before saving.'); return }
            try {
                Save-Settings
                $saved.Set((ConvertTo-Json -InputObject (Get-Snapshot) -Compress))
                $status.Set("Saved $(Get-Date -Format 'HH:mm:ss')")
            } catch {
                $status.Set('Could not save: ' + $_.Exception.Message)
            }
        }
        $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Revert' -Variant secondary -OnClick {
            param($eventObject, $data)
            $fresh = Read-Settings
            $name.Set([string]$fresh.DisplayName); $email.Set([string]$fresh.Email); $theme.Set([string]$fresh.Theme)
            $interval.Set([string]$fresh.RefreshSeconds); $notify.Set([bool]$fresh.Notifications)
            $status.Set('Reverted to the saved file')
        }
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiAlert -UI $ui -Bind $status
}

try {
    $null = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Stop-NHKUi -UI $ui
    foreach ($c in @($problem, $changes, $hasProblem)) { $c.Dispose() }
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

Run it with pwsh -File ./settings_editor.ps1 or with a file of your choice: pwsh -File ./settings_editor.ps1 ./my-settings.json.

  • param([string]$Path) takes the file as the first argument. Without it, the file is nativehtmlkit-settings.json in your application-data folder ([Environment]::GetFolderPath(...ApplicationData, Create), which creates the folder if it is missing: %APPDATA% on Windows, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config on Linux). The Python version of this tutorial uses the same folder and the same JSON keys, so both apps edit the same file.
  • The script uses .NET methods ([IO.Path]::Combine, [IO.File]::Exists, [IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory) instead of Join-Path, Test-Path and New-Item. On Windows the backend's working directory is an extended-length path (\\?\C:\...), so a relative path argument becomes such a path, and Windows PowerShell 5.1's Join-Path rejects it ("the value of argument "drive" is null"). The .NET methods work in every PowerShell version.
  • Read-Settings starts from defaults and copies known keys from the file, so a partial or older file still works.
  • Get-Snapshot returns the values as they would be saved. Two computed states use it: $problem (a validation message or '') and $changes, which compares the snapshot with $saved, the compressed JSON of the last save (hashtables compare by reference, text by value).
  • These computed states call script functions instead of receiving -Data; that works because the scriptblocks run on the owner runspace in the script's scope. They still list every state they read in -DependsOn ($all).
  • $hasProblem is computed from $problem and drives Add-NHKUiWhen, which shows the message only when there is one.
  • Save refuses to write while there is a problem, writes a temporary file and replaces the real one ([IO.File]::Replace, with [NullString]::Value for "no backup", since a plain $null would be passed as an empty string), then updates $saved, so the badge returns to "All changes saved". Errors become a status message.
  • Revert reads the file again and sets every state; the bound inputs update themselves. All .Set() calls in one callback reach the window as one update.
  • New-NHKUi -Theme $loaded.Theme: the theme is chosen when the UI is built, so a changed theme applies on the next start.

Try it: clear Display name (the message appears and Save refuses), type an e-mail without a dot after the @, set the refresh interval to 2. Fix everything, press Save, change a field and press Revert.

Reactive state and ready-made components (layouts, buttons, inputs, lists, themes) on top of the SDK. Start here unless you want to write all of the HTML yourself; use the SDK directly for anything the UI library does not wrap.

  • Getting started
