Same section in PowerShell: PowerShell UI library. Differences between Linux and Windows: Linux and Windows.

items.title: CSS reference: classes, themes and tokens (UI 0.1.1)
items.text:
Both libraries ship the same stylesheet (shared/css/ui.css, packaged as assets/ui.css). It uses no JavaScript, web fonts or remote assets. The generated document is:

<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>...</title><style>/* ui.css */ /* your extra CSS */</style></head>
<body class="nhk-theme-cobalt nhk-density-compact"><main class="nhk-app" id="nhkui-...-1">...</main></body></html>

Your extra_css (Python) / -ExtraCss (PowerShell) is appended after the built-in rules in the same <style> element, so a rule with equal specificity wins over the built-in one.

items.title: Themes
items.text:
The theme sets custom properties on body.nhk-theme-<name>:

Token cobalt graphite daylight Used for --nhk-bg #101824 #171d25 #f1f5fa Page background --nhk-panel #192536 #222b36 #ffffff Cards --nhk-panel-2 #1d2b3d #28333e #f6f9fd Inputs, secondary buttons, badges, alerts --nhk-border #304255 #3b4b5c #d5deea Borders --nhk-text #ecf3fc #eff2f7 #203047 Text --nhk-muted #a6b9cc #b1becc #5a6d85 Muted text and labels --nhk-accent #69a6f3 #87a7ef #276fca Primary buttons, badge text, alert edge, checkbox --nhk-accent-strong #458bdf #6b8ed6 #2365b8 Primary button hover --nhk-accent-text #0b233f #121d38 #ffffff Text on accent and danger buttons --nhk-danger #ed7f89 #eb9696 #bc424d Danger buttons --nhk-radius 9px 9px 9px Card radius --nhk-focus #69a6f3 #87a7ef #276fca Focus outline color-scheme dark dark light Native control rendering

items.title: Densities
items.text:
Set on body.nhk-density-<name>:

Token compact regular comfortable --nhk-control-h (minimum control height) 30px 36px 42px --nhk-font (base font size) 13px 14px 15px --nhk-gap (row/column/grid gap) 10px 13px 16px --nhk-pad (app padding) 20px 25px 30px

The font stack is Inter, "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif (local fonts only).

items.title: Component classes
items.text:
Class Created by Rules nhk-app root <main> padding: var(--nhk-pad), max-width: 1380px, centred. nhk-row row() / Add-NHKUiRow Flex row, wrap, align-items: center, gap: var(--nhk-gap). nhk-col column() / Add-NHKUiColumn Flex column, gap: var(--nhk-gap), min-width: 0. nhk-stack stack() (Python only) Flex column with gap: 6px. nhk-grid grid() / Add-NHKUiGrid repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); 2 columns at max-width: 1000px; 1 column at max-width: 620px (also nhk-app padding 14 px). nhk-card card() / Add-NHKUiCard --nhk-panel background, border, --nhk-radius, padding: 16px. nhk-heading headings Weight 640; h1 24 px, h2 19 px, h3 16 px, h4 14 px. nhk-text, nhk-muted text No margin, overflow-wrap: anywhere; muted uses --nhk-muted. nhk-badge badge Pill, --nhk-panel-2 background, accent text, 0.85 em. nhk-alert alert Bordered box with a 3 px accent left border; role="status". nhk-button + nhk-primary/nhk-secondary/nhk-danger/nhk-quiet buttons Height --nhk-control-h; primary uses accent; :disabled has opacity 0.45. nhk-input, nhk-select input / select --nhk-panel-2 background; inputs are full width. nhk-field, nhk-label labelled input/select wrapper Field is a flex column (flex: 1 1 200px, min-width: 150px); label is muted, 0.9 em. In a column the 200px basis becomes height (defect B-0014); see limitations for the workaround. nhk-checkrow, nhk-checkbox checkbox Row with 8 px gap; checkbox 16 px with accent-color. nhk-region, nhk-hidden when() / Add-NHKUiWhen nhk-hidden is display: none !important. nhk-list text list Left padding 20 px; items 3 px padding. nhk-custom raw_html() / Add-NHKUiHtml min-width: 0. nhk-hr (style hook only) Top border; apply it yourself, for example ui.element("hr", css_class="nhk-hr").

Focus: .nhk-input:focus, .nhk-select:focus and .nhk-button:focus-visible draw a 2 px --nhk-focus outline with 2 px offset. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables transitions and animations.

items.title: Theming hooks
items.text:
Override tokens for one theme, or for all, in extra CSS:

body.nhk-theme-daylight { --nhk-accent: #0f7b6c; --nhk-accent-strong: #0b6458; --nhk-focus: #0f7b6c; }
/* Tokens are defined on body.nhk-theme-*; a plain `body { }` rule is less specific and loses. */
body.nhk-theme-cobalt, body.nhk-theme-graphite, body.nhk-theme-daylight { --nhk-radius: 4px; }

Style components by their classes (.nhk-card { border-top: 3px solid var(--nhk-accent); }) or add your own classes: Python ui.element("div", css_class="metric", text=value) or ui.container("section", css_class="toolbar"); in PowerShell, which has no generic element function, target structure such as .nhk-card h1.nhk-heading. Do not rely on generated ids in CSS; they change on every run.

The theme and density are fixed when the window is created. For a theme switch at run time, create the UI with the chosen theme (see examples/*/dashboard.*) or restyle through your own classes. The UI does not follow the desktop's light/dark preference automatically; the SDK can read it (Application.desktop_preferences(), Get-NativeHTMLKitPreferences) before you choose a theme.

Source: nativehtmlkit_ui/docs/css.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Getting started with the Python UI library
items.text: nativehtmlkit_ui builds native desktop windows from Python with components (headings, inputs, buttons, lists, cards, a grid) bound to reactive state. It runs on the NativeHTMLKit native host, without a browser engine or JavaScript, and uses only the public API of the Python SDK. This page covers version 0.1.1. The same page for PowerShell: getting started.

items.title: Install
items.text:
You need uv on Linux x64 (KDE Plasma Wayland is the primary desktop) or Windows x64. uv provides Python 3.10 or later for the project if you have none.

uv init --app hello && cd hello              # a project for your app
uv add nativehtmlkit_ui                      # also installs the nativehtmlkit SDK with its native host
uv run python -c "import nativehtmlkit_ui; print(nativehtmlkit_ui.__version__)"    # 0.1.1

items.title: Your first window
items.text:
Save this as hello.py in the project folder (it is the hello example):

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with the released packages.

from nativehtmlkit import Application
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Hello UI") as app:
        name = state("world")
        greeting = computed(lambda: f"Hello, {name.value}!")

        ui = UI(title="Hello UI", width=480, height=320)
        with ui.column():
            ui.heading(greeting, level=1)
            with ui.row():
                ui.input(name, label="Your name")
                ui.button("Reset", variant="secondary", on_click=lambda _event: name.set("world"))
        try:
            ui.mount(app)
            app.run()
        finally:
            ui.dispose()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run it:

uv run hello.py

Type a name: the heading follows every keystroke. Reset sets the state back, and the input follows too.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
• state("world") is an observable value. ui.input(name, ...) binds it both ways: typing sets the state, setting the state changes the field.
  • computed(lambda: ...) derives a value and records which states it read; the heading bound to it updates when name changes.
  • with ui.column(): and with ui.row(): arrange components. You build the whole component tree first; ui.mount(app) opens the window. After that you only change state.
  • Handlers such as on_click run on the UI's own thread and change state, never the window.
  • Application.start() starts the native host, which runs this same script again as its backend. Keep all work inside main() behind if __name__ == "__main__":; code at module level would run twice.
  • app.run() returns when the window is closed; ui.dispose() releases the UI.

  • How-to guides: state, layouts, forms, lists, theming, background work, multiple windows, SDK calls, trusted content, testing.
  • Examples: sixteen small applications, each also available in PowerShell.

items.title: UI limitations and qualification
items.text:
UI 0.1.1 is an early (pre-1.0) release. Its 0.1.1 packages passed the real-input GUI suite (state, input, keyboard focus, select, disabled bindings, responsive widths, two windows, 1000-update load, 100 mount/close cycles) at 100% scaling against Python SDK 0.1.2 / PowerShell SDK 0.1.2 / Core 1.0.3 on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland (Python, PowerShell 7) and Windows Server 2022 (Python, PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell 5.1). IME, 125%/150% scaling and theme checks were last run with UI 0.1.0 on SDK 0.1.0 / Core 1.0.2. Screen-reader validation is incomplete and Core's select/Orca announcement issue remains open.

Known UI bugs recorded in the Project register: Python Computed can falsely raise a circular dependency error and retain a stale value during concurrent updates; disposing many UI windows can accumulate SDK shutdown callbacks. Until fixed, serialize writes affecting the same computed state, use background worker handoff via ui.post, and avoid rapidly creating/discarding many UIs in long-lived applications.

Inputs placed directly in a column are 200px tall (0.1.1 stylesheet defect B-0014). The built-in rule .nhk-field { flex: 1 1 200px } is meant for fields in a row, but in a column (ui.column(), ui.stack(), Add-NHKUiColumn) the 200px basis applies to the field's height, so a single input followed by more content leaves a large empty gap. Inputs inside a row or directly inside a card (a plain block) are not affected. Workaround: pass

.nhk-col > .nhk-field { flex: 0 0 auto; }

as extra_css= (Python; add .nhk-stack > .nhk-field for ui.stack()) or -ExtraCss (PowerShell). The signup_form and multi_window examples do this. Guides: Python layouts, PowerShell layouts.

There is no UI modal wrapper, router, plugin system, arbitrary widget gallery, virtualized data grid, video/audio player, JS runtime, or HTTP server. The SDK may expose underlying HTML dialogs and bitmap surfaces; do not claim them as UI components.

Source: nativehtmlkit_ui/docs/LIMITATIONS.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Python reference: nativehtmlkit_ui 0.1.1
items.text:
This page is the complete reference for the Python package nativehtmlkit_ui 0.1.1. It is derived from the released source (python/src/nativehtmlkit_ui). The package depends only on the public API of the NativeHTMLKit Python SDK (nativehtmlkit 0.1.x; qualified with 0.1.2 and Core 1.0.3). The PowerShell module is documented in the PowerShell reference; themes and classes in the CSS reference.

from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, State, Computed, state, computed

nativehtmlkit_ui.__all__ is exactly ["UI", "State", "Computed", "state", "computed"], and nativehtmlkit_ui.__version__ is "0.1.1".

Contents: Reactive values · UI construction · Layout containers · Display components · Controls · Dynamic regions · Events · Custom and trusted markup · Mounting · Update scheduling · post() and sync() · Diagnostics · Disposal · Errors · Known defects

items.title: state(value) and State
items.text:
count = state(0)            # same as State(0)
count.value                 # read (records a dependency, see below)
count.value = 5             # same as count.set(5)
changed = count.set(6)      # True if the value changed
remove = count.subscribe(lambda: print("changed"))
remove()                    # unsubscribe
Member Description State(value) Observable holder of one value of any type. .value (property) Returns the current value. Reading it inside a computed function or a bound lambda records the state as a dependency of that function. .value = x Calls .set(x). .set(value) -> bool Stores value and notifies subscribers, unless the new value is the same object (is) or compares equal (==) to the current one; then it does nothing and returns False. Returns True when it changed. .subscribe(callback) -> remove Registers callback() (no arguments). Returns a function that removes it. Subscribers are held in a set, so their order is not defined, and the same callable is registered only once.

Semantics:

  • Change detection is by equality. Mutating a list or dict in place and setting the same object again does not notify anyone. Always build a new value: items.set([*items.value, new_item]), items.set(items.value[:-1]).
  • Notification is synchronous on the thread that called set(). Subscribers, computed values that depend on the state, and the UI scheduler run before set() returns. The UI scheduler only marks bindings dirty and queues a flush; it never writes to the window on the calling thread (see Update scheduling).
  • set() may be called from any thread. State itself is protected by a re-entrant lock. See Known defects for computed values updated from several threads.

items.title: computed(fn) and Computed
items.text:
total = computed(lambda: sum(e["amount"] for e in expenses.value))
total.value
total.close()
Member Description Computed(fn) / computed(fn) Calls fn() immediately (eager) and records every State/Computed whose .value it read as a dependency. .value (property) The last computed value. Reading it records the computed as a dependency of an enclosing computed/binding. .subscribe(callback) As for State. .close() Unsubscribes from all dependencies and drops all subscribers. After close() the value no longer changes.

Semantics:

  • When any dependency notifies, fn() runs again synchronously on the notifying thread. Dependencies are re-collected on every run, so conditional reads (a.value if flag.value else b.value) track exactly what the last run read.
  • Subscribers of the computed are notified only when the new result differs (is / ==) from the previous one.
  • A computed that reads itself raises RuntimeError("Computed value depends on itself"); a re-entrant recomputation raises RuntimeError("Circular computed-state dependency").
  • Exceptions raised by fn() propagate to the caller of set() that triggered the recomputation (inside a UI event handler they are recorded in diagnostics["errors"]).
  • A computed is not disposed by UI.dispose(). Call .close() when it should stop following its dependencies (for example a computed created per window).
  • A computed can be used anywhere a State is accepted for display (ui.text(total)), but two-way controls (input, checkbox, select) require a real State.

items.title: Bound expressions
items.text:
Every component argument documented as "text-like" accepts:

  • a plain str (static; escaped once at render time),
  • a State or Computed (shows .value),
  • a zero-argument callable such as lambda: f"Total: {total.value}".

A callable is evaluated once when the component is created, and again on the UI owner thread whenever one of the states it read changes. None is shown as an empty string; any other value is converted with str().

items.title: UI
items.text:
UI(*, title="NativeHTMLKit UI", width=940, height=660, theme="cobalt",
   density="compact", extra_css="")
Parameter Default Meaning title "NativeHTMLKit UI" Native window title and HTML <title>. width, height 940, 660 Requested window size in CSS pixels, passed to Application.open_html. theme "cobalt" "cobalt" (dark blue), "graphite" (dark grey) or "daylight" (light). Anything else raises ValueError. density "compact" "compact", "regular" or "comfortable"; sets control height, font size, gaps and padding. Anything else raises ValueError. extra_css "" CSS appended after the built-in stylesheet inside the same <style> element. It is trusted developer input and is not validated. See CSS reference.

Public attributes:

Attribute Description title, width, height, theme, density, extra_css The constructor values. Changing them after mount() has no effect. prefix "nhkui-" + 12 random hex digits. Every generated element id is f"{prefix}-{n}", so several UIs never collide. root The root Element (<main class="nhk-app">). app, window, document None until mount(); then the SDK Application, Window and Document handles. Use them for SDK calls such as dialogs or reading DOM state. diagnostics Property; see Diagnostics.

Construct the UI and all of its components first, then call mount(app). After mount() (or after disposal) adding components raises RuntimeError; change state instead.

items.title: Element
items.text: Every component method returns an Element (a dataclass). Its fields are tag, id (generated), attrs (dict), children (list of Element or str) and bindings. The most useful field is id: pass it to SDK document methods, for example ui.document.get_text(el.id) or ui.document.focus(el.id). Element.html() renders a standalone, escaped HTML string for the element (used by tests). Treat the other fields as read-only; editing them after mount() does not change the window.

items.title: Layout containers
items.text:
All containers are context managers. Components created inside the with block become their children. Each returns (from __enter__) the container Element.

Method Element and class Layout ui.container(tag="div", *, css_class="", attrs=None) any allowed tag Generic container; the others are shortcuts for it. ui.row() div.nhk-row Horizontal flex row, wraps, centred vertically, gap --nhk-gap. ui.column() div.nhk-col Vertical flex column, gap --nhk-gap. ui.stack() div.nhk-stack Vertical flex column with a tighter 6 px gap. ui.grid() div.nhk-grid CSS grid: 3 equal columns; 2 when the window is at most 1000 px wide; 1 at most 620 px (the app padding also shrinks to 14 px). ui.card() div.nhk-card Panel with background, border, radius and 16 px padding. 
with ui.grid():
    with ui.card():
        ui.heading("Disk", level=3)
        ui.text(disk_text)

ui.html() raises RuntimeError("An open container context is not closed") if a container block is still open.

items.title: Display components
items.text:
Method Renders Notes ui.heading(value, *, level=2) <hN class="nhk-heading"> level 1-4, else ValueError. value is text-like. ui.text(value, *, muted=False) <p class="nhk-text"> (+ nhk-muted) Text-like; long words wrap anywhere. ui.badge(value) <span class="nhk-badge"> Small pill for counts and status. ui.alert(value) <div class="nhk-alert" role="status"> Callout with an accent border. Combine with ui.when() to show it only when needed.

All four escape their text. Updating a bound value sends one set_text document command.

items.title: ui.button(label, *, on_click=None, variant="primary", disabled=False)
items.text:
Renders <button type="button" class="nhk-button nhk-{variant}">.

Parameter Description label Text-like. A bound label (lambda: "Resume" if paused.value else "Pause") is updated with set_text. on_click callback(event: dict), run on the UI owner thread. See Events. variant "primary", "secondary", "danger" or "quiet"; else ValueError. disabled bool, a State, a Computed or a callable returning a truthy value. When bound, the disabled attribute is added or removed as the value changes.

A disabled native button does not deliver clicks, but handlers that perform an irreversible action should still re-check their precondition (the examples do).

items.title: ui.input(value, *, label="", placeholder="", kind="text")
items.text:
Renders <input class="nhk-input"> with a two-way binding to value.

Parameter Description value Must be a State (TypeError otherwise; a Computed is not accepted). Its value is shown with str(); None shows as empty. label When non-empty, the input is wrapped in div.nhk-field and preceded by <label class="nhk-label" for=...>. Without a label there is no wrapper; provide another accessible name. placeholder Placeholder attribute. Not a replacement for a label. kind "text", "password", "search", "email" or "number"; else ValueError. The state always holds a string, also for "number".

Behaviour: every native input event stores the control's text in the state (value.set(str)), so the state follows each keystroke and IME commit. Setting the state from code writes the control with set_value; the binding remembers the value it just received from the control, so typing never causes an echo write that would move the caret or break an IME composition.

items.title: ui.checkbox(value, *, label)
items.text: Renders div.nhk-checkrow containing <input type="checkbox" class="nhk-checkbox"> and a <label for> after it. value must be a State; it receives bool on every change event. label is required (keyword-only). Setting the state writes the control with set_checked.

items.title: ui.select(value, choices, *, label="")
items.text:
Renders div.nhk-field containing an optional <label class="nhk-label"> and <select class="nhk-select">.

Parameter Description value A State holding the selected option's value as a string. choices Iterable of (value, text) pairs, for example [("a", "Alpha"), ("b", "Bravo")], or dict.items(). Values and texts are converted with str(). The option list is fixed at build time. label Optional visible label.

The option whose value equals str(value.value) is marked selected at render time. A change event stores the new value; setting the state from code writes set_value. Setting a value that matches no option is passed to the SDK unchanged; what the native control then shows is up to the host.

All three two-way controls return the control Element (not the wrapper). Its id is the target for SDK calls such as ui.document.focus(el.id).

items.title: ui.when(condition)
items.text:
with ui.when(lambda: not items.value):
    ui.text("Nothing here.", muted=True)

Context manager that creates div.nhk-region around its children. condition is a State, Computed or callable; truthiness uses bool(). The region is always mounted: when the condition becomes false the class nhk-hidden (display: none !important) is added, when it becomes true it is removed. Controls inside keep their value, focus history and native state while hidden; nothing is rebuilt. Regions may be nested.

items.title: ui.text_list(values, *, formatter=str)
items.text: Renders <ul class="nhk-list"> whose <li> items are the escaped results of formatter(item) for each item of values (a State, Computed or callable returning an iterable). When the formatted tuple changes, the list's children are replaced in one replace_children_html command. It is text only and not virtualized; keep it to a few hundred items (the examples show the newest N). For per-row buttons use the slot pool pattern.

items.title: ui.on(element, kind, callback)
items.text:
Registers callback(event: dict) for kind on element (an Element). kind must be one of "click", "input", "change", "keydown", "submit", "auxclick", "contextmenu"; else ValueError. Registration must happen before mount().

  • There is one callback per (kind, element); registering again replaces the previous one. Two-way controls already register "input" (input) or "change" (checkbox, select) on their element, so do not register that kind on them yourself: it would replace the binding. Observe the state instead (value.subscribe(...) or a computed).
  • On mount the UI subscribes once per event kind to the SDK document (Document.on). For each native event it looks at the target event["element"] and then the ids in event["path"] (the bubbling route), and calls the callback of the nearest registered element only, like a delegated handler. A click on a <span> inside a registered card therefore reaches the card's handler.
  • The event dict is the SDK's document event: type, element, path, window_id, document_id, and type-specific members such as value, checked, key, code, button, x, y and modifier flags, as delivered by Core 1.0.3.
  • Callbacks run on the UI owner thread, one at a time, in event order. An exception is logged with logging (logger nativehtmlkit_ui.engine), recorded in diagnostics["errors"] and does not stop the UI.
  • on_click of button() is a shortcut for ui.on(el, "click", on_click).

keydown, submit, auxclick and contextmenu registration is available, but the 0.1.1 GUI qualification exercised click, input and change; verify other kinds in your own app.

items.title: ui.element(tag, *, css_class="", attrs=None, text=None)
items.text:
Adds one element with library-generated id. Use it for styling hooks the components do not cover (for example ui.element("div", css_class="metric", text=clock)).

  • tag must be one of: div section main header footer article nav aside p span h1 h2 h3 h4 small strong em button label input select option textarea form ul li table thead tbody tr th td dialog pre code hr; anything else raises ValueError (use raw_html for other tags).
  • attrs values are escaped. Attribute names must match [A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_:.-]* and must not start with on (no inline event handlers), else ValueError at render time. None/False omit the attribute, True renders a boolean attribute. Passing "id" raises ValueError: ids are always generated.
  • text is text-like and escaped. css_class is appended to any class in attrs.
  • Use it as a container with ui.container(tag, ...).
  • The library does not bind values of textarea, form or dialog created this way; use SDK document methods on el.id if you need them.

items.title: ui.raw_html(markup)
items.text: Adds div.nhk-custom whose content is markup verbatim, without sanitization. Only pass static markup written by the developer. Never pass user input, file contents or network data; show those with text components, which escape them. See the trusted content guide.

items.title: ui.mount(app) -> UI
items.text:
app is a connected SDK Application (from Application.start() or the uv run -m nativehtmlkit run module:main entry point). mount():

  1. Renders the document (ui.html()), and opens one window with app.open_html(markup, title=, width=, height=).
  2. Writes the live value of every input/select (set_value) and checkbox (set_checked).
  3. Subscribes once per used event kind to the document.
  4. Registers app.on_shutdown(...) (holding the UI weakly) and an app.on_window_event listener that disposes the UI when its window is closed.
  5. Starts the UI owner: one daemon thread named nativehtmlkit-ui per UI.
  6. If state changed between building and mounting, queues one flush.

It returns the UI. It does not call app.ready() or app.run(): app.run() announces readiness and waits for shutdown. If any step fails, the UI is disposed, the window is asked to close, and the exception propagates. Calling mount() twice raises RuntimeError("UI already mounted"); after disposal RuntimeError("UI already disposed").

The owner thread runs event callbacks, posted functions and DOM flushes. SDK event worker threads only enqueue events and never block on DOM requests. Mount may be called from any thread, including another UI's event callback (see examples/python/multi_window.py).

items.title: ui.html() -> str
items.text: Returns the complete HTML document: doctype, <meta charset>, viewport meta, <title>, one <style> with the built-in CSS followed by extra_css, and <body class="nhk-theme-{theme} nhk-density-{density}"> containing the root <main>. Useful for tests and snapshots; it does not need a host.

items.title: Update scheduling and batching
items.text:
• When a state read by a binding changes, the binding is marked dirty and one flush is queued on the owner (only one flush is outstanding at a time).
  • The flush re-evaluates each dirty binding on the owner thread, compares the result with the last written value, and skips unchanged ones. It turns the rest into document operations: set_text (text and labels), add_class/remove_class nhk-hidden (when), set_attribute/remove_attribute disabled, replace_children_html (text_list). These are sent through Document.batch in chunks of at most 128 operations (a single operation is sent with Document.command). Control values follow as set_value/set_checked calls.
  • Batching is automatic: all state changes made inside one event callback or posted function are coalesced, because the flush is queued behind the running callback. Many set() calls from a worker thread in quick succession are coalesced the same way. There is no separate batch API in Python.
  • Only the latest value is written: intermediate values that were overwritten before the flush ran are never sent.

items.title: ui.post(fn, *args)
items.text:
Queues fn(*args) to run on the UI owner thread, after work queued earlier. Use it to hand results from worker threads, executors, timers or SDK futures back to the UI:

future.add_done_callback(lambda f: ui.post(show_result, f))
  • Safe from any thread, including the owner itself (it still queues, which preserves batching).
  • After disposal it silently does nothing.
  • The queue holds 4096 items. When it is full, post() raises RuntimeError("NativeHTMLKit UI queue full: event not delivered; inspect diagnostics") and increments diagnostics["event_queue_dropped"]. Producers that can outpace the UI should catch it and drop or merge work (see examples/python/log_viewer.py).
  • Before mount() there is no owner thread yet; queued work runs once the UI is mounted.

items.title: ui.sync(timeout=10.0)
items.text: Blocks until the owner has processed everything queued before the call (including the flush those changes queued). Intended for tests and explicit synchronization from other threads. Called on the owner thread itself it flushes immediately. Raises RuntimeError("UI not mounted"), RuntimeError("UI already disposed"), TimeoutError if the owner did not reach the marker in time, and RuntimeError when the DOM state is uncertain (see below).

items.title: Diagnostics
items.text:
ui.diagnostics returns a new dict:

Key Type Meaning errors tuple[str, ...] The last 64 failures of callbacks, posted functions and flushes, as "TypeName: message". event_queue_dropped int Events and post() calls lost because the 4096-item queue was full. pending_updates int Bindings marked dirty and not yet flushed. dom_uncertain bool A document write failed in a way whose outcome is unknown (for example a timeout). Managed updates stop; sync() raises. Not set when the window simply closed. updates int Flushes that wrote at least one operation. operations int Document operations written in total. subscriptions int Active SDK subscriptions (one per event kind, plus one window-event listener); 0 after disposal. disposed bool True after dispose(). discarded_after_close int Flushes dropped because the window/document was already gone (closed window, replaced document or application shutdown; host codes -32004 and -32008).

A healthy UI has an empty errors, event_queue_dropped == 0 and dom_uncertain == False. The example harness checks exactly these.

items.title: Disposal
items.text:
ui.dispose() (alias ui.close()) is idempotent. It unsubscribes all SDK document event subscriptions and the window-event listener, closes every binding (so later state changes no longer reach this UI), stops the owner thread (joining it for up to 2 s when called from another thread) and discards queued work.

It is called automatically when the UI's window closes and when the application shuts down. It does not close the window, end the application or close Computed objects; the SDK owns the window and application lifecycle (ui.window.request_close(), app.request_quit()). States stay usable after disposal; they simply no longer drive this UI.

items.title: Errors raised by the library
items.text:
Situation Exception Unknown theme, density, button variant, input kind, heading level, event kind or tag ValueError Unsafe attribute name or an id in attrs ValueError Two-way control bound to something that is not a State TypeError Adding components after mount() or disposal RuntimeError mount() twice or after disposal; sync() before mount or after disposal RuntimeError post() with a full queue RuntimeError Self or circular computed dependency RuntimeError

SDK errors (for example nativehtmlkit.RpcError with code -32001 when the clipboard or a dialog is unavailable) come from your own SDK calls and are not wrapped.

items.title: Known defects
items.text:
These are recorded, open defects of 0.1.1 (see limitations):

  • B-0002, Computed under concurrent updates. When dependencies of the same computed are set from several threads at the same time, a recomputation can falsely raise RuntimeError("Circular computed-state dependency") and keep a stale value. Serialize writes that affect the same computed: make them on the UI owner (ui.post(state.set, value)) or from a single worker thread.
  • B-0003, shutdown callback retention. Each mount() registers an Application.on_shutdown callback, and the SDK offers no way to remove it. The callback holds the UI only weakly, but the registrations accumulate. Avoid creating and discarding many UIs in a long-running application; reuse windows or cap their number (as examples/python/multi_window.py does).
  • B-0014, fields directly in a column are 200 px tall. The stylesheet rule .nhk-field { flex: 1 1 200px } is meant for rows; in ui.column() or ui.stack() the 200 px basis becomes the field's height. Fields in rows and cards are not affected. Workaround: extra_css=".nhk-col > .nhk-field, .nhk-stack > .nhk-field { flex: 0 0 auto; }" (see the layouts guide).

Source: nativehtmlkit_ui/docs/python/reference.md · edit the page there.

items.title: Background calculation
items.text:
Run a slow calculation off the UI thread and report the result; cancel it.

Same example in PowerShell: Background calculation

What it teaches: Python executor and ui.post(); PowerShell Start-NativeHTMLKitTask; busy flag; cancel.

uv add nativehtmlkit_ui
# save the example file(s) in the project folder, then:

Related guide: background work

items.title: Source: python/background.py
items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Background calculation: run slow work on a thread pool and report the result with ui.post().

Teaches: never block a UI event handler with slow work; submit it to an executor, then hand the
result (or the error) back to the UI owner with ui.post(); a busy flag that disables the button;
a Cancel button that sets a threading.Event the worker checks; shutting the executor down from
app.on_shutdown().

Run:  uv run background.py      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
"""
import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, state


def main(app):
    status = state("Idle")
    busy = state(False)
    ui = UI(title="Background example")
    executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2, thread_name_prefix="ui-example")
    cancel = threading.Event()

    def calculate(n: int) -> int:               # runs on an executor thread; touches no state
        total = 0
        for start in range(0, n, 10_000):
            if cancel.is_set():
                raise InterruptedError("cancelled")
            total += sum(range(start, min(n, start + 10_000)))
        return total

    def finished(text: str) -> None:            # runs on the UI owner
        status.set(text)
        busy.set(False)

    def run(_event):
        cancel.clear()
        busy.set(True)
        status.set("Running")
        future = executor.submit(calculate, 500_000)

        def completed(f):                       # runs on an executor thread
            try:
                ui.post(finished, f"Done: {f.result()}")
            except InterruptedError:
                ui.post(finished, "Cancelled")
            except Exception as exc:
                ui.post(finished, f"Failed: {type(exc).__name__}")
        future.add_done_callback(completed)

    with ui.column():
        ui.heading("Background work")
        ui.text(status)
        with ui.row():
            ui.button("Calculate", on_click=run, disabled=busy)
            ui.button("Cancel", variant="secondary", on_click=lambda _e: cancel.set(),
                      disabled=lambda: not busy.value)
    ui.mount(app)
    app.on_shutdown(cancel.set)
    app.on_shutdown(lambda: executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="NativeHTMLKit Background") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

items.title: Source: python/clipboard_tool.py
items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Text transformer with copy/paste: mixes UI state with direct SDK clipboard calls.

Teaches: calling public SDK services (app.set_clipboard_text / app.clipboard_text) from a UI
event handler, reporting SDK errors in the UI instead of crashing (the clipboard is
unavailable in headless test mode, error -32001), and a computed live preview.

Run:  uv run clipboard_tool.py      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
"""
import re

from nativehtmlkit import RpcError
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state

TRANSFORMS = {
    "upper": ("UPPER CASE", str.upper),
    "lower": ("lower case", str.lower),
    "title": ("Title Case", str.title),
    "slug": ("slug-for-urls", lambda s: re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", s.lower()).strip("-")),
    "squash": ("Collapse whitespace", lambda s: " ".join(s.split())),
    "reverse": ("Reverse word order", lambda s: " ".join(reversed(s.split()))),
}


def main(app):
    source = state("")
    mode = state("title")
    status = state("")

    result = computed(lambda: TRANSFORMS[mode.value][1](source.value))

    def copy(_event):
        try:
            app.set_clipboard_text(result.value)
            status.set(f"Copied {len(result.value)} characters to the clipboard.")
        except RpcError as error:
            status.set(f"Clipboard unavailable: {error}")

    def paste(_event):
        try:
            source.set(app.clipboard_text())
            status.set("Pasted from the clipboard.")
        except RpcError as error:
            status.set(f"Clipboard unavailable: {error}")

    ui = UI(title="Clipboard tool", width=680, height=520)
    with ui.column():
        ui.heading("Clipboard text tool", level=1)
        with ui.card():
            ui.input(source, label="Text", placeholder="Paste or type something")
            ui.select(mode, [(key, label) for key, (label, _) in TRANSFORMS.items()], label="Transform")
            with ui.row():
                ui.button("Paste", variant="secondary", on_click=paste)
                ui.button("Copy result", on_click=copy, disabled=lambda: not result.value)
        with ui.card():
            ui.heading("Result", level=3)
            ui.text(lambda: result.value or "(empty)")
            ui.text(lambda: f"{len(result.value)} characters", muted=True)
        with ui.when(status):
            ui.alert(status)
    ui.mount(app)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="Clipboard tool") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Counter gallery: the smallest tour of state, computed text, buttons, input, checkbox and list.

Teaches: state() and computed(), text bound to a lambda, a two-way input and checkbox, a reactive
text list shown or hidden with ui.when(), and a responsive card grid.

Run:  uv run counter.py      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
  or: uv run -m nativehtmlkit run counter:main --name Counter   (from this directory)
"""
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, state, computed


def main(app):
    count = state(0)
    name = state("NativeHTMLKit")
    show = state(True)
    history = state(["Ready"])
    message = computed(lambda: f"{name.value}: {count.value} clicks")
    ui = UI(title="NativeHTMLKit UI Gallery", theme="cobalt", density="compact")

    def add(_event):
        count.set(count.value + 1)
        history.set([f"Count became {count.value}", *history.value][:10])

    with ui.column():
        ui.heading("NativeHTMLKit UI", level=1)
        ui.text("Browserless • native HTML/CSS • Python SDK only", muted=True)
        with ui.grid():
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading("State")
                ui.text(message)
                with ui.row():
                    ui.button("Increment", on_click=add)
                    ui.button("Reset", variant="secondary", on_click=lambda e: count.set(0))
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading("Input")
                ui.input(name, label="Your name", placeholder="Enter a name")
                ui.checkbox(show, label="Show recent events")
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading("Lists")
                with ui.when(show):
                    ui.text_list(history)
        ui.alert(lambda: f"Native reactive updates: {count.value}")
    ui.mount(app)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="NativeHTMLKit UI") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

A responsive card grid with a live clock and disk usage, themed with extra CSS.

What it teaches: responsive grid; themes and density; extra CSS; one-second timer.

uv add nativehtmlkit_ui

items.title: Source: python/dashboard.py
items.text:
View on GitHub

"""System dashboard: a responsive card grid with a live clock and disk usage, themed via CSS.

Teaches: ui.grid() (3 columns, 2 below 1000 px, 1 below 620 px), theme and density options,
extra_css with your own classes and token overrides, ui.element() for a custom-styled tag, and
a periodic timer thread that updates state through ui.post().

Run:  uv run dashboard.py [cobalt|graphite|daylight]      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
"""
import os
import platform
import shutil
import sys
import threading
import time
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, state

THEMES = ("cobalt", "graphite", "daylight")
CSS = """
.metric { font-size: 30px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.02em; margin: 4px 0; }
.meter { height: 8px; border-radius: 99px; background: var(--nhk-panel-2); border: 1px solid var(--nhk-border); }
.nhk-card { border-top: 3px solid var(--nhk-accent); }
body.nhk-theme-daylight { --nhk-accent: #0f7b6c; --nhk-accent-strong: #0b6458; --nhk-focus: #0f7b6c; }
"""


def disk_text(path: Path) -> tuple[str, str]:
    usage = shutil.disk_usage(path)
    used = usage.used / usage.total * 100
    return f"{used:.0f} % used", f"{usage.free / 1024**3:.1f} GB free of {usage.total / 1024**3:.0f} GB"


def main(app):
    theme = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] in THEMES else "cobalt"
    started = time.monotonic()
    clock = state("--:--:--")
    uptime = state("0 s")
    disk, disk_detail = state(""), state("")
    refreshed = state(0)

    def refresh() -> None:                        # runs on the UI owner (posted)
        clock.set(f"{datetime.now():%H:%M:%S}")
        seconds = int(time.monotonic() - started)
        uptime.set(f"{seconds // 60} min {seconds % 60} s" if seconds >= 60 else f"{seconds} s")
        used, detail = disk_text(Path.home())
        disk.set(used)
        disk_detail.set(detail)

    ui = UI(title="Dashboard", width=980, height=640, theme=theme, density="regular", extra_css=CSS)
    with ui.column():
        with ui.row():
            ui.heading("System dashboard", level=1)
            ui.badge(f"theme: {theme}")
        with ui.grid():
            with ui.card():
                ui.text("Local time", muted=True)
                ui.element("div", css_class="metric", text=clock)
            with ui.card():
                ui.text("Dashboard uptime", muted=True)
                ui.element("div", css_class="metric", text=uptime)
            with ui.card():
                ui.text("Home drive", muted=True)
                ui.element("div", css_class="metric", text=disk)
                ui.text(disk_detail, muted=True)
            with ui.card():
                ui.text("Processors", muted=True)
                ui.element("div", css_class="metric", text=str(os.cpu_count() or "?"))
            with ui.card():
                ui.text("Platform", muted=True)
                ui.element("div", css_class="metric", text=platform.system())
                ui.text(f"Python {platform.python_version()}", muted=True)
            with ui.card():
                ui.text("Manual refreshes", muted=True)
                ui.element("div", css_class="metric", text=refreshed)
                ui.button("Refresh now", variant="secondary",
                          on_click=lambda _e: (refresh(), refreshed.set(refreshed.value + 1)))
        ui.text("Resize the window: the grid uses 3, 2 or 1 columns.", muted=True)

    stop = threading.Event()

    def tick() -> None:
        while not stop.wait(1.0):
            try:
                ui.post(refresh)
            except RuntimeError:
                pass

    ui.mount(app)
    ui.post(refresh)
    threading.Thread(target=tick, name="dashboard-timer", daemon=True).start()
    app.on_shutdown(stop.set)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="Dashboard") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

"""Expense tracker: add expenses, remove the last one, filter by category, see totals.

Teaches: state + computed values, two-way input/select binding, a disabled button driven by a
computed value, a filtered text list, an empty-state region with ui.when(), and Decimal input
validation. This is the finished app of docs/python/tutorials/expense-tracker.md.

Run:  uv run expenses.py      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
"""
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation

from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state

CATEGORIES = {"food": "Food", "transport": "Transport", "home": "Home", "other": "Other"}


def money(value: Decimal) -> str:
    return f"{value:,.2f}"


def main(app):
    expenses = state([])                 # list of dicts; always replaced, never mutated in place
    description = state("")
    amount = state("")
    category = state("food")
    show = state("all")
    error = state("")

    visible = computed(lambda: [e for e in expenses.value if show.value in ("all", e["category"])])
    total = computed(lambda: sum((e["amount"] for e in visible.value), Decimal("0")))
    by_category = computed(lambda: [
        f"{label}: {money(sum((e['amount'] for e in expenses.value if e['category'] == key), Decimal('0')))}"
        for key, label in CATEGORIES.items() if any(e["category"] == key for e in expenses.value)])
    cannot_add = computed(lambda: not description.value.strip() or not amount.value.strip())

    def add(_event):
        try:
            value = Decimal(amount.value.strip().replace(",", "."))
        except InvalidOperation:
            error.set("Amount must be a number, for example 12.50")
            return
        if value <= 0:
            error.set("Amount must be greater than zero")
            return
        expenses.set([*expenses.value, {"description": description.value.strip(),
                                        "amount": value.quantize(Decimal("0.01")),
                                        "category": category.value}])
        description.set("")          # writes back into the native inputs
        amount.set("")
        error.set("")

    def remove_last(_event):
        expenses.set(expenses.value[:-1])

    ui = UI(title="Expenses", width=760, height=640)
    with ui.column():
        ui.heading("Expenses", level=1)
        with ui.card():
            ui.heading("New expense", level=3)
            with ui.row():
                ui.input(description, label="Description", placeholder="Coffee with Sam")
                ui.input(amount, label="Amount", placeholder="0.00")
                ui.select(category, list(CATEGORIES.items()), label="Category")
            with ui.when(error):
                ui.alert(error)
            with ui.row():
                ui.button("Add expense", on_click=add, disabled=cannot_add)
                ui.button("Remove last", variant="secondary", on_click=remove_last,
                          disabled=lambda: not expenses.value)
        with ui.card():
            with ui.row():
                ui.select(show, [("all", "All categories"), *CATEGORIES.items()], label="Show")
                ui.badge(lambda: f"{len(visible.value)} of {len(expenses.value)} expenses")
            ui.heading(lambda: f"Total: {money(total.value)}", level=2)
            with ui.when(lambda: not visible.value):
                ui.text("No expenses to show yet.", muted=True)
            ui.text_list(visible, formatter=lambda e: (
                f"{e['description']} ({CATEGORIES[e['category']]}): {money(e['amount'])}"))
            ui.text(lambda: " | ".join(by_category.value), muted=True)
    ui.mount(app)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="Expenses") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

"""File inspector: pick files with the native open dialog and list their sizes and a total.

Teaches: an SDK dialog started without blocking the UI (window.open_files(wait=False) returns a
future), handing its result back with ui.post(), a busy flag that disables the button while the
dialog is open, cancel and error handling (dialogs are unavailable in headless test mode).

Run:  uv run file_picker.py      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
"""
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import RpcError
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state


def human(size: int) -> str:
    for unit in ("bytes", "KB", "MB", "GB"):
        if size < 1024 or unit == "GB":
            return f"{size} {unit}" if unit == "bytes" else f"{size:.1f} {unit}"
        size /= 1024
    return str(size)


def main(app):
    files = state([])             # [(name, size_in_bytes)]
    busy = state(False)
    status = state("Choose one or more files to see their sizes.")
    total = computed(lambda: sum(size for _, size in files.value))

    def chosen(future) -> None:                  # posted to the UI owner
        busy.set(False)
        try:
            result = future.result()
        except RpcError as error:
            status.set(f"File dialogs are unavailable here: {error}")
            return
        if result.get("cancelled") or not result.get("paths"):
            status.set("No files chosen.")
            return
        rows = []
        for raw in result["paths"]:
            path = Path(raw)
            try:
                rows.append((path.name, path.stat().st_size))
            except OSError as error:
                rows.append((f"{path.name} (unreadable: {error.strerror})", 0))
        files.set(rows)
        status.set(f"{len(rows)} file(s) chosen.")

    def choose(_event):
        busy.set(True)
        future = ui.window.open_files(multiple=True, title="Choose files to inspect", wait=False)
        future.add_done_callback(lambda f: ui.post(chosen, f))

    ui = UI(title="File inspector", width=720, height=560)
    with ui.column():
        ui.heading("File inspector", level=1)
        with ui.row():
            ui.button(lambda: "Waiting for the dialog..." if busy.value else "Choose files...",
                      on_click=choose, disabled=busy)
            ui.button("Clear", variant="secondary", disabled=lambda: not files.value,
                      on_click=lambda _e: files.set([]))
        ui.text(status, muted=True)
        with ui.when(files):
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading(lambda: f"{len(files.value)} files, {human(total.value)} in total", level=3)
                ui.text_list(files, formatter=lambda row: f"{row[0]}: {human(row[1])}")
    ui.mount(app)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="File inspector") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

"""Live log viewer: a background producer streams lines; filter by level and text, pause, clear.

Teaches: a worker thread that hands every result to the UI owner with ui.post(), bounded
history, a computed filtered view rendered with text_list (all text is escaped), counters,
pausing without losing lines, and stopping the worker from app.on_shutdown().

Run:  uv run log_viewer.py      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
"""
import threading
from datetime import datetime

from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state

KEEP = 500           # lines kept in memory
SHOW = 14            # newest matching lines shown
MESSAGES = ["request served in 12 ms", "cache refreshed", "user signed in", "slow query (420 ms)",
            "disk space below 15 %", "retrying upstream connection", "job finished", "config reloaded"]


def level_for(n: int) -> str:
    return "ERROR" if n % 11 == 0 else "WARN" if n % 4 == 0 else "INFO"


def main(app):
    lines = state([])            # newest last; each line is (level, text)
    paused = state(False)
    held = state([])             # lines that arrived while paused
    level = state("all")
    search = state("")

    def matches(lvl: str, text: str) -> bool:
        return (level.value == "all" or lvl == level.value) and search.value.lower() in text.lower()

    shown = computed(lambda: [text for lvl, text in lines.value if matches(lvl, text)][-SHOW:][::-1])
    errors = computed(lambda: sum(1 for lvl, _ in lines.value if lvl == "ERROR"))

    def receive(entry) -> None:                      # runs on the UI owner (posted)
        if paused.value:
            held.set([*held.value, entry][-KEEP:])
        else:
            lines.set([*lines.value, entry][-KEEP:])

    def toggle_pause(_event):
        if paused.value:
            lines.set([*lines.value, *held.value][-KEEP:])
            held.set([])
        paused.set(not paused.value)

    ui = UI(title="Log viewer", width=820, height=620)
    with ui.column():
        with ui.row():
            ui.heading("Service log", level=1)
            ui.badge(lambda: f"{len(lines.value)} lines")
            ui.badge(lambda: f"{errors.value} errors")
        with ui.row():
            ui.select(level, [("all", "All levels"), ("INFO", "Info"), ("WARN", "Warnings"), ("ERROR", "Errors")],
                      label="Level")
            ui.input(search, label="Contains", kind="search", placeholder="Filter text")
            ui.button(lambda: "Resume" if paused.value else "Pause", variant="secondary", on_click=toggle_pause)
            ui.button("Clear", variant="quiet", on_click=lambda _e: lines.set([]))
        with ui.when(paused):
            ui.alert(lambda: f"Paused: {len(held.value)} new lines are waiting.")
        with ui.card():
            with ui.when(lambda: not shown.value):
                ui.text("No matching lines.", muted=True)
            ui.text_list(shown)

    stop = threading.Event()

    def produce() -> None:                           # worker thread: never touches the UI directly
        n = 0
        while not stop.wait(0.2):
            n += 1
            lvl = level_for(n)
            text = f"#{n:05d} {datetime.now():%H:%M:%S} {lvl:<5} {MESSAGES[n % len(MESSAGES)]}"
            try:
                ui.post(receive, (lvl, text))
            except RuntimeError:                     # queue full: skip a line rather than block
                pass

    ui.mount(app)
    worker = threading.Thread(target=produce, name="log-producer", daemon=True)
    worker.start()
    app.on_shutdown(stop.set)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="Log viewer") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

"""Message composer: untrusted user text is always escaped; only static help uses raw_html().

Teaches: the trust boundary. Everything a user types reaches the window through text bindings
(ui.text, ui.text_list), which escape it, so typing <b>hi</b> shows those characters literally.
ui.raw_html() is used only for a fixed, developer-written snippet. Also: a length limit with a
computed counter and a sent-messages list.

Run:  uv run message_preview.py      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
"""
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state

LIMIT = 140
HELP = """
<table class="help">
  <tr><th>Tip</th><th>Why</th></tr>
  <tr><td>Type <code><b></code> in the message</td><td>It is shown as text, never as markup.</td></tr>
  <tr><td>Keep it under <strong>140</strong> characters</td><td>Longer messages cannot be sent.</td></tr>
</table>
"""
CSS = ".help { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; } .help td, .help th { text-align: left; padding: 4px 8px;" \
      " border-bottom: 1px solid var(--nhk-border); }"


def main(app):
    recipient = state("")
    message = state("")
    sent = state([])
    remaining = computed(lambda: LIMIT - len(message.value))

    def send(_event):
        if message.value.strip() and remaining.value >= 0:
            sent.set([f"To {recipient.value.strip() or 'everyone'}: {message.value.strip()}", *sent.value][:10])
            message.set("")

    ui = UI(title="Message composer", width=700, height=640, extra_css=CSS)
    with ui.column():
        ui.heading("Compose a message", level=1)
        with ui.card():
            ui.input(recipient, label="To", placeholder="Team channel")
            ui.input(message, label="Message", placeholder="Say something")
            with ui.row():
                ui.button("Send", on_click=send, disabled=lambda: not message.value.strip() or remaining.value < 0)
                ui.badge(lambda: f"{remaining.value} characters left")
            with ui.when(lambda: remaining.value < 0):
                ui.alert(lambda: f"Too long by {-remaining.value} characters.")
        with ui.card():
            ui.heading("Preview (escaped text)", level=3)
            ui.text(lambda: message.value or "Nothing typed yet.")
        with ui.card():
            ui.heading("Sent", level=3)
            with ui.when(lambda: not sent.value):
                ui.text("No messages sent yet.", muted=True)
            ui.text_list(sent)
        ui.raw_html(HELP)                       # trusted, static, written by the developer
    ui.mount(app)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="Message composer") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

"""Notes editor with live inspector windows that share the editor's state.

Teaches: several UI objects in one application, each in its own native window; binding two
windows to the same State; opening a window from a button handler; tracking windows the user
closes with app.on_window_event (marshalled to the UI owner with ui.post); closing a window
from code. Each inspector is a new UI; mounting one registers an SDK shutdown callback, so this
example caps the number of inspectors (see the B-0003 limitation).

Run:  uv run multi_window.py      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
"""
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state

MAX_INSPECTORS = 3


# Workaround for a UI 0.1.1 stylesheet defect: a field placed directly in a column gets a
# 200px flex basis (meant for rows) and therefore 200px of height. See docs/LIMITATIONS.md.
FIELD_FIX = ".nhk-col > .nhk-field { flex: 0 0 auto; }"

def main(app):
    note = state("")
    edits = state(0)
    open_inspectors = state(0)
    words = computed(lambda: len(note.value.split()))

    main_ui = UI(title="Notes", width=640, height=480, extra_css=FIELD_FIX)

    def changed() -> None:
        edits.set(edits.value + 1)
    note.subscribe(changed)          # runs on whichever thread set the note (here: the UI owner)

    def open_inspector(_event):
        if open_inspectors.value >= MAX_INSPECTORS:
            return
        number = open_inspectors.value + 1
        inspector = UI(title=f"Inspector {number}", width=420, height=320, theme="graphite")
        with inspector.column():
            inspector.heading(f"Inspector {number}", level=2)
            inspector.text(lambda: f"Note: {note.value}")
            inspector.text(lambda: f"{words.value} words, {len(note.value)} characters")
            inspector.badge(lambda: f"{edits.value} edits")
            inspector.button("Close inspector", variant="secondary",
                             on_click=lambda _e: inspector.window.request_close())
        inspector.mount(app)
        window_id = inspector.window.id
        open_inspectors.set(number)

        def on_window(event: dict) -> None:          # SDK event thread: hand over to the owner
            if event.get("window_id") == window_id and event.get("type") == "closed":
                unsubscribe()
                main_ui.post(lambda: open_inspectors.set(open_inspectors.value - 1))
        unsubscribe = app.on_window_event(on_window)

    with main_ui.column():
        main_ui.heading("Notes", level=1)
        main_ui.input(note, label="Shared note", placeholder="Type here and watch the inspectors")
        with main_ui.row():
            main_ui.button("Open inspector", on_click=open_inspector,
                           disabled=lambda: open_inspectors.value >= MAX_INSPECTORS)
            main_ui.badge(lambda: f"Inspectors open: {open_inspectors.value}")
        main_ui.text(lambda: f"{words.value} words", muted=True)
    main_ui.mount(app)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="Notes") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

"""Settings editor: edit, validate and save a JSON settings file (settings-editor tutorial, final code).

Teaches: loading initial state from a file, a computed validation message and an "unsaved
changes" badge, buttons that save (atomically) and revert, a status alert, and starting the UI
in the theme the user saved.
Run:     uv run settings_editor.py [PATH]
         (default file: nativehtmlkit-settings.json in your application-data folder:
         %APPDATA% on Windows, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config on Linux)
Guide:   docs/python/tutorials/settings-editor.md (step 2 of 2)
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state

DEFAULTS = {"DisplayName": "", "Email": "", "Theme": "cobalt", "RefreshSeconds": 60, "Notifications": False}
THEMES = [("cobalt", "Cobalt"), ("graphite", "Graphite"), ("daylight", "Daylight")]
EMAIL = re.compile(r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$")


def default_path() -> Path:
    if os.name == "nt":
        base = Path(os.environ.get("APPDATA") or Path.home() / "AppData" / "Roaming")
    else:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME") or Path.home() / ".config")
    return base / "nativehtmlkit-settings.json"


def read_settings(path: Path) -> dict:
    """Start from the defaults and copy known keys, so a partial or older file still works."""
    result = dict(DEFAULTS)
    if path.is_file():
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        result.update({key: data[key] for key in DEFAULTS if key in data})
    if result["Theme"] not in dict(THEMES):
        result["Theme"] = "cobalt"
    return result


def write_settings(path: Path, values: dict) -> None:
    """Write a temporary file next to the target and replace the target with it."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".settings-", suffix=".tmp", dir=path.parent)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            json.dump(values, stream, indent=2)
        os.replace(temporary, path)
    except BaseException:
        Path(temporary).unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Settings editor") as app:
        path = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve() if len(sys.argv) > 1 else default_path()
        loaded = read_settings(path)

        name = state(str(loaded["DisplayName"]))
        email = state(str(loaded["Email"]))
        theme = state(str(loaded["Theme"]))
        interval = state(str(loaded["RefreshSeconds"]))
        notify = state(bool(loaded["Notifications"]))
        status = state(f"Editing {path}")

        # The values as they would be saved; also used to detect unsaved changes.
        snapshot = computed(lambda: {"DisplayName": name.value.strip(), "Email": email.value.strip(),
                                     "Theme": theme.value, "RefreshSeconds": interval.value.strip(),
                                     "Notifications": notify.value})
        saved = state(snapshot.value)

        def find_problem(values):
            seconds = values["RefreshSeconds"]
            if not values["DisplayName"]:
                return "Enter a display name."
            if not EMAIL.match(values["Email"]):
                return "The e-mail address looks invalid."
            if not (seconds.isdigit() and 5 <= int(seconds) <= 3600):
                return "Refresh interval must be a whole number from 5 to 3600."
            return ""

        problem = computed(lambda: find_problem(snapshot.value))
        changes = computed(lambda: "All changes saved" if snapshot.value == saved.value else "Unsaved changes")

        def save(_event):
            if problem.value:
                status.set("Fix the problem above before saving.")
                return
            values = dict(snapshot.value, RefreshSeconds=int(snapshot.value["RefreshSeconds"]))
            try:
                write_settings(path, values)
            except OSError as error:
                status.set(f"Could not save: {error.strerror or error}")
                return
            saved.set(snapshot.value)
            status.set(f"Saved {datetime.now():%H:%M:%S}")

        def revert(_event):
            try:
                fresh = read_settings(path)
            except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
                status.set(f"Could not read the file: {error}")
                return
            name.set(str(fresh["DisplayName"]))
            email.set(str(fresh["Email"]))
            theme.set(str(fresh["Theme"]))
            interval.set(str(fresh["RefreshSeconds"]))
            notify.set(bool(fresh["Notifications"]))
            status.set("Reverted to the saved file")

        ui = UI(title="Settings editor", theme=loaded["Theme"], density="regular", width=600, height=640)
        with ui.column():
            with ui.row():
                ui.heading("Settings", level=1)
                ui.badge(changes)
            with ui.card():
                ui.input(name, label="Display name")
                ui.input(email, label="E-mail", kind="email")
                ui.input(interval, label="Refresh interval (seconds)", kind="number")
                ui.select(theme, THEMES, label="Theme (applies on next start)")
                ui.checkbox(notify, label="Send me e-mail notifications")
            with ui.when(problem):
                ui.text(problem)
            with ui.row():
                ui.button("Save", on_click=save)
                ui.button("Revert", variant="secondary", on_click=revert)
            ui.alert(status)
        try:
            ui.mount(app)
            app.run()
        finally:
            ui.dispose()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.text:
View on GitHub

"""Settings panel with Save, Revert and Restore defaults, plus an "unsaved changes" indicator.

Teaches: one computed snapshot of many controls, dirty tracking by comparing it with the last
saved snapshot, writing state back into inputs/selects/checkboxes (Revert, Defaults) and
enabling buttons only when they would do something. Replace save() with your own persistence.

Run:  uv run settings.py      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
"""
from datetime import datetime

from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state

DEFAULTS = {"display_name": "", "language": "en", "font_size": "14", "autosave": True,
            "interval": "5", "telemetry": False}
LANGUAGES = [("en", "English"), ("de", "Deutsch"), ("fr", "Français"), ("ja", "日本語")]
FONT_SIZES = [("12", "Small (12 px)"), ("14", "Normal (14 px)"), ("16", "Large (16 px)")]


def main(app):
    fields = {key: state(value) for key, value in DEFAULTS.items()}
    saved = state(dict(DEFAULTS))
    status = state("Loaded defaults.")

    current = computed(lambda: {key: s.value for key, s in fields.items()})
    dirty = computed(lambda: current.value != saved.value)
    interval_ok = computed(lambda: fields["interval"].value.isdigit() and 1 <= int(fields["interval"].value) <= 60)

    def load(values: dict) -> None:
        for key, value in values.items():
            fields[key].set(value)

    def save(_event):
        if interval_ok.value:
            saved.set(dict(current.value))
            status.set(f"Saved at {datetime.now():%H:%M:%S}.")

    def revert(_event):
        load(saved.value)
        status.set("Reverted to the last saved settings.")

    def defaults(_event):
        load(DEFAULTS)
        status.set("Defaults restored (not saved yet).")

    ui = UI(title="Settings", width=700, height=640, density="regular")
    with ui.column():
        with ui.row():
            ui.heading("Settings", level=1)
            ui.badge(lambda: "Unsaved changes" if dirty.value else "All changes saved")
        with ui.grid():
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading("Profile", level=3)
                ui.input(fields["display_name"], label="Display name", placeholder="Shown in the title bar")
                ui.select(fields["language"], LANGUAGES, label="Language")
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading("Editor", level=3)
                ui.select(fields["font_size"], FONT_SIZES, label="Font size")
                ui.checkbox(fields["autosave"], label="Save documents automatically")
                with ui.when(fields["autosave"]):
                    ui.input(fields["interval"], label="Autosave every (minutes)", kind="number")
                    with ui.when(lambda: not interval_ok.value):
                        ui.alert("Use a whole number of minutes from 1 to 60.")
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading("Privacy", level=3)
                ui.checkbox(fields["telemetry"], label="Send anonymous usage statistics")
                ui.text("Off by default. Nothing is sent by this example.", muted=True)
        with ui.row():
            ui.button("Save", on_click=save, disabled=lambda: not dirty.value or not interval_ok.value)
            ui.button("Revert", variant="secondary", on_click=revert, disabled=lambda: not dirty.value)
            ui.button("Restore defaults", variant="quiet", on_click=defaults)
        ui.text(status, muted=True)
    ui.mount(app)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="Settings") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

"""Sign-up form with live validation, a guarded submit button and a success screen.

Teaches: validation as a computed list of messages (no DOM reads), showing errors only for
fields the user has typed in, a submit button disabled until the form is valid, swapping the
form and a confirmation with ui.when(), and resetting every control by setting its state.

Run:  uv run signup_form.py      (uv add nativehtmlkit_ui)
"""
import re

from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state

EMAIL = re.compile(r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$")
PLANS = [("free", "Free"), ("team", "Team"), ("enterprise", "Enterprise")]


# Workaround for a UI 0.1.1 stylesheet defect: a field placed directly in a column gets a
# 200px flex basis (meant for rows) and therefore 200px of height. See docs/LIMITATIONS.md.
FIELD_FIX = ".nhk-col > .nhk-field { flex: 0 0 auto; }"

def main(app):
    name, email, password, confirm, age = (state("") for _ in range(5))
    plan = state("free")
    terms = state(False)
    welcome = state("")                 # non-empty once the account was "created"

    def problems() -> list[str]:
        found = []
        if name.value and len(name.value.strip()) < 2:
            found.append("Name needs at least 2 characters.")
        if email.value and not EMAIL.match(email.value.strip()):
            found.append("Enter a valid email address.")
        if password.value and len(password.value) < 8:
            found.append("Password needs at least 8 characters.")
        if confirm.value and confirm.value != password.value:
            found.append("Passwords do not match.")
        if age.value and not (age.value.isdigit() and 16 <= int(age.value) <= 120):
            found.append("Age must be a whole number from 16 to 120.")
        return found

    errors = computed(problems)
    complete = computed(lambda: all(s.value for s in (name, email, password, confirm, age)) and terms.value)
    can_submit = computed(lambda: complete.value and not errors.value)

    def submit(_event):
        if can_submit.value:  # re-check: never trust that a disabled button cannot be activated
            welcome.set(f"Welcome, {name.value.strip()}! Your {dict(PLANS)[plan.value]} account is ready.")

    def start_over(_event):
        for field in (name, email, password, confirm, age, welcome):
            field.set("")
        plan.set("free")
        terms.set(False)

    ui = UI(title="Create account", width=620, height=700, theme="daylight", density="regular", extra_css=FIELD_FIX)
    with ui.column():
        ui.heading("Create your account", level=1)
        with ui.when(lambda: not welcome.value):
            with ui.card():
                with ui.column():
                    ui.input(name, label="Name", placeholder="Ada Lovelace")
                    ui.input(email, label="Email", kind="email", placeholder="ada@example.org")
                    with ui.row():
                        ui.input(password, label="Password", kind="password")
                        ui.input(confirm, label="Confirm password", kind="password")
                    with ui.row():
                        ui.input(age, label="Age", kind="number")
                        ui.select(plan, PLANS, label="Plan")
                    ui.checkbox(terms, label="I accept the terms of service")
                    with ui.when(errors):
                        ui.text_list(errors)
                    ui.text(lambda: "" if complete.value else "Fill in every field and accept the terms.",
                            muted=True)
                    ui.button("Create account", on_click=submit, disabled=lambda: not can_submit.value)
        with ui.when(welcome):
            with ui.card():
                ui.alert(welcome)
                ui.button("Start over", variant="secondary", on_click=start_over)
    ui.mount(app)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from nativehtmlkit import Application
    with Application.start(name="Create account") as application:
        main(application)
        application.run()

"""Theme preview: try the UI library's themes, densities and a custom accent colour.

Teaches: UI(theme=..., density=..., extra_css=...), overriding the library's CSS custom properties
(--nhk-accent and friends) for one theme, and the main components side by side.
instance="multiple" lets you start several previews at once and compare them.
Run:     uv run theme_preview.py [cobalt|graphite|daylight] [compact|regular|comfortable] [#RRGGBB]
Guide:   docs/python/guides/theming-and-custom-css.md
"""
import re
import sys

from nativehtmlkit import Application
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, state

THEMES = ("cobalt", "graphite", "daylight")
DENSITIES = ("compact", "regular", "comfortable")


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Theme preview", instance="multiple") as app:
        args = sys.argv[1:]
        theme = args[0] if len(args) > 0 and args[0] in THEMES else "cobalt"
        density = args[1] if len(args) > 1 and args[1] in DENSITIES else "compact"
        accent = args[2] if len(args) > 2 and re.fullmatch(r"#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}", args[2]) else None
        # extra_css is appended after the library stylesheet, so the same selector wins.
        extra = (f"body.nhk-theme-{theme} {{ --nhk-accent: {accent}; --nhk-accent-strong: {accent}; "
                 f"--nhk-focus: {accent}; }}") if accent else ""

        name = state("Ada")
        enabled = state(True)
        size = state("m")
        ui = UI(title=f"Theme preview: {theme}/{density}", theme=theme, density=density, extra_css=extra,
                width=720, height=560)
        with ui.column():
            ui.heading(f"{theme.title()} theme, {density} density", level=1)
            with ui.row():
                ui.badge("Badge")
                ui.badge(lambda: f"Hello {name.value}")
                ui.badge(f"accent {accent or 'default'}")
            with ui.grid():
                with ui.card():
                    ui.heading("Controls", level=2)
                    ui.input(name, label="Name")
                    ui.select(size, [("s", "Small"), ("m", "Medium"), ("l", "Large")], label="Size")
                    ui.checkbox(enabled, label="Enabled")
                with ui.card():
                    ui.heading("Buttons", level=2)
                    with ui.row():
                        ui.button("Primary")
                        ui.button("Secondary", variant="secondary")
                        ui.button("Danger", variant="danger")
                        ui.button("Quiet", variant="quiet")
                        ui.button("Disabled", disabled=True)
            ui.alert("Alerts use role=status, so screen readers announce changes.")
            ui.text("Muted text for secondary information.", muted=True)
        try:
            ui.mount(app)
            app.run()
        finally:
            ui.dispose()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
